## BLOCKER

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue,` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The title shrink ratio is derived via `calc(tan(atan2(var(--type-heading), var(--type-display-1))))`, an identity WebKit does not implement for font-relative (rem/em) lengths. On desktop Safari the stuck title lands at 0.310808 instead of the designed 0.618029 (a 2x error); on iOS Safari, where the ratio must be exactly 1 (display-1 floor-pins at heading on phones), WebKit returns 1.619775 — the title ENLARGES 62% on scroll and occludes three live controls.

**Mechanism.** M-A — a scroll-driven choreography built on unverified engine behaviour: the design reasoned from spec text and from Chromium, and never measured WebKit. The @supports (animation-timeline: scroll()) gate cited at :138-139 as protection ('atan2: Chromium 111+ subset-of SDA engines') does not protect — this WebKit build satisfies that condition, demonstrably runs the animation, and still computes atan2 wrong.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:140-142 (the declaration) and :136-139 (the false rationale). probe-03-atan2-mechanism.mjs, isolated on a bare div at root font-size 16px — webkit: tan(atan2(1rem,1rem)) -> matrix(1.619775,...) [requires 1]; tan(atan2(2rem,1rem)) -> matrix(0.688691,...) [requires 2]; tan(atan2(1.618rem,2.618rem)) -> matrix(0.310808,...) [requires 0.618029]; tan(atan2(10px,10px)) -> matrix(1,...) [correct]. chromium: all five correct. Mechanism confirmed to every serialised digit — tan(deg-magnitude consumed as radians) predicts 1.6197751905438615 / 0.6886911649460621 / 0.310807581296239. probe-04-mobile-inversion.mjs, iPhone 14 (390x664), #/gradient scrolled 200: webkit REST transform matrix(1,...) titleRect {w:324,h:27.2,right:357} -> STUCK matrix(1.619775,...) titleRect {w:524.8,h:44,right:557.8}, headerRect {w:356,h:69} unchanged; chromium(Pixel 7) REST matrix(1,...) -> STUCK matrix(1,...) (the designed no-op). probe-01-structure.mjs desktop 1440x900 #/ scrolled 300: webkit titleTf matrix(1,...) -> matrix(0.310808,...), titleRectH 91.91 -> 28.57; chromium -> matrix(0.618029,...), 91.94 -> 56.82. Screenshot: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/shot-webkit-mobile-gradient-scrolled.png — 'Gradient' at 1.62x overprints the TYPE/SPACE/HUE select row; 'Lin' and 'OK' are cut through by glyph strokes.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-03-atan2-mechanism.mjs  (mechanism, no server needed) ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-04-mobile-inversion.mjs  (live consequence + screenshot, needs http://localhost:9000)

**Proposed cure.** Architectural transposition, not a patch: delete the trigonometric contrivance entirely and use the CSS-values-4 length-divided-by-length form, which yields a <number> directly — `--pane-title-shrink-ratio: calc(var(--type-heading) / var(--type-display-1));`. Measured correct in BOTH engines (probe-03: webkit and chromium both matrix(0.618029,...) for 1.618rem/2.618rem and both matrix(1,...) for 1rem/1rem). This is strictly less machinery than the defect, restores the phone no-op exactly, preserves the fluid-clamp property the closed form was chosen for, and retires the now-groundless @supports-implies-correct-atan2 paragraph in the comment. One-line replacement at PaneHeader.vue:140-142.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (demo/color-picker/` · V-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** A plain network failure on a lazily-imported pane chunk tears down the entire application and leaves a bare "Try again" button on an empty field. usePaneRouter's ten defineAsyncComponent declarations carry no errorComponent, no loadingComponent and no timeout, so the chunk-fetch rejection travels to the single app-wide boundary, which unmounts both panes.

**Mechanism.** async-component load failure treated as an exception to be caught app-wide instead of a pane-local state to be rendered

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:69-78 (ten bare defineAsyncComponent). Measured, probes/challenge-c-verify.mjs V-1: {"hash":"#/browse","paneContainer":false,"boundaryPresent":true,"boundaryText":"This panel hit an unexpected error.Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://localhost:9000/@fs/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/Browse…"}; console log carries `error: Failed to load resource: net::ERR_FAILED`. Screenshot evidence/V1-chunk-abort.png shows the dock plus 1408x804px of empty gradient with one centred pill.
```

**Reproduction.** 1. dev server live at http://localhost:9000. 2. `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/probes/challenge-c-verify.mjs` — its V-1 arm loads #/, then `page.route("**/BrowsePane.vue**", r => r.abort("failed"))`, then sets location.hash = "#/browse". 3. Observe paneContainer false and evidence/V1-chunk-abort.png.

**Proposed cure.** Transpose, do not patch: chunk failure is an expected state, not an exception. Give usePaneRouter's ten declarations a real `errorComponent` (an EmptyState variant="error" whose retry re-triggers the import) and a `loadingComponent`, so the failure is pane-local and retryable and never reaches a boundary whose only move is to unmount the application.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (demo/color-picker/` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The decorative aurora canvas paints over the boundary's icon, headline and detail. The announced error message is never rendered to pixels; only the recovery button paints, and it survives only by accident (glass-ui gives it position:relative + backdrop-filter).

**Mechanism.** CSS 2.1 Appendix E painting order — an unpositioned fallback replaces the very element that carried the z-lift, so a full-viewport absolutely-positioned decorative sibling paints in step 8, over the fallback's step-7 inline content

**Evidence.**

```
Measured by decoding a screenshot in-page and sampling each text node's own bounding box (evidence/probe-live-pixels.mjs, 1440x900, dpr 1), my run: SHIPPED head distinctColours 86, darkestPixel [255,128,176], contrastDarkestVsBg 1.12; detail 42 / [255,142,176] / 1.06. With `.vj-error-boundary{position:relative}` applied at runtime only: head 1323 / [28,25,23] / 8.37; detail 499 / [86,84,83] / 3.70. Stacking, probes/challenge-c-verify.mjs V-4: boundaryPosition "static", boundaryZ "auto", boundaryRect {x:16,y:88,w:1408,h:804}; canvasPosition "absolute", canvasZ "auto". Images: evidence/02-shipped-crop-only-button-paints.png vs evidence/03-runtime-position-relative-restores-text.png. Source: demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:15-22 (no position), demo/color-picker/App.vue:9-17 (canvas), App.vue:50 (boundary mounted OUTSIDE .pane-container, whose .pane-wrapper children carry position:relative;z-index:1).
```

**Reproduction.** 1. `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/evidence/probe-live-pixels.mjs` against http://localhost:9000. 2. Compare the SHIPPED and RUNTIME-LIFTED blocks it prints. 3. Or open evidence/02-shipped-crop-only-button-paints.png beside evidence/03-runtime-position-relative-restores-text.png — same crop, one runtime property changed.

**Proposed cure.** Do not hand-roll a second error plate at all. demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:14-27 already IS the ratified error plate and ErrorBoundary.vue:12-14 admits it is a copy of it. Render <EmptyState variant="error"> inside the existing pane shell so the fallback lands ON the plate every other surface lands on, at the same rung the panes it replaces occupy. That kills C-1, C-6, C-12 and V-5 in one move and deletes ~20 lines of template.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (demo/color-picker/` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `caught` is component-local state with no key, no watcher and no route coupling, so the boundary latches for the rest of the session. Because App.vue:50 wraps the whole two-pane grid in ONE boundary, `v-else` withholds both panes — including a healthy sibling — until someone clicks the button.

**Mechanism.** unkeyed local latch state with no coupling to the route or the slot identity, at a granularity (the whole grid) far wider than the failure

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:55 (`const caught = ref(false)`) and :35 (`<slot v-else />`); demo/color-picker/App.vue:50-140. Live, evidence/probe-live-latching.mjs my run: state1 hash "#/browse" paneContainer false; state2 hash "#/" paneContainer false; state3 hash "#/mix" paneContainer false — mainText identical "This panel hit an unexpected error.INDUCED-AUDIT-THROW Try again" in all three. Unit probe C-E: `error plate still rendered: true`, `healthy pane mounted: false` after the slot content is swapped for a healthy component.
```

**Reproduction.** 1. `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/evidence/probe-live-latching.mjs`. 2. Read state1/state2/state3 in the printed JSON: the hash changes twice, paneContainer stays false, mainText never changes. The dock remains fully operable throughout, so a real user clicks Picker/Mix/Gradient and the pane region simply never responds.

**Proposed cure.** Scope and key: one boundary per PaneSlot, inside demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue, keyed on the pane key. A new route is then a new boundary instance, born un-caught, and one pane's failure cannot take out its sibling or its successor.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/color-picke` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** A cold load / refresh / shared link on any route whose left pane is not the color-picker (10 of 14 routes) permanently stalls the overture beat DAG at B2: overture:b3 and overture:b4 never fire for the life of the session, and the picker's hero-blob ornament (v-if gated on b4) never mounts again on ANY route thereafter.

**Mechanism.** State derived from a source of truth that is not yet true: index.html:205-213 mounts without awaiting router.isReady(), so the first render uses the picker config; PaneSlot then swaps the child (router resolution + the deliberate one-rAF commit at PaneSlot.vue:95), which cancels Vue's `appear` transition so @after-appear never fires. B3 is the one beat in this boot chain with NO state-checked fallback (contrast useDockArrival.ts:63-72 and useOverture.ts:173), so one missed DOM event is terminal.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured with an isolated Chromium probe against localhost:9000. CONTROL cold-load /#/ → marks [b0,b1,b3,b2,b4], `.hero-blob-anchor` present. DEEPLINK /#/generate → marks [b0,b1,b2] only, blob absent; after hash-nav to /#/ still [b0,b1,b2], `.picker-shell` present but blob STILL absent. Identical for /#/browse. First-pane oracle (pre-navigation MutationObserver) on cold /#/generate records `picker-shell` as the FIRST mounted left pane before the GeneratePane. Code: App.vue:90 and App.vue:109 are the ONLY call sites of overture.noteLeftPlateSettled (grep), both via PaneSlot.vue:118 `@after-appear`; useViewManager.ts:43-46 falls back to "picker" while route.name is undefined; PaneSlot.vue:74 seeds liveComponent at setup; useOverture.ts:153-183 gates b4 on b3Complete.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/probe-b3.mjs — launches chromium 1440x900, goto http://localhost:9000/#/generate (or /#/browse), wait 5s, read performance marks + `.hero-blob-anchor`; then set location.hash='#/', wait 7s, re-read. Compare against goto('/#/'). Deep links yield 3 marks and no blob; the control yields 5 marks and a blob.

**Proposed cure.** Take the MT-F012 entry cure and make it the idiomatic vue-router SPA boot: in the new main.ts do `app.use(router); await router.isReady(); app.mount('#app')`. With the route true at first render the first-mounted left pane is the final one, its appear completes, B3 and B4 fire. Second, independent arm: arm B3 on the left pane's MOUNT plus a getAnimations() settle check (the sibling beats' idiom) instead of a single Transition appear event.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/color-sessi` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `data-stops` carries two mutually contradictory referents (truth-function output vs painted output); above the 7-segment cap the component's own documented truth law is false by construction.

**Mechanism.** F-alpha — one attribute overloaded with two referents that the cap makes provably unequal

**Evidence.**

```
PreviewStrip.vue:44 stamps `stampStops(stops)` (ALL stops) while the template at :49-51 paints `visible` = `stops.slice(0,7)` (:32-35). Measured live, both engines: `chromium · count=12 { n: 12, painted: 7 }`, `webkit · count=12 { n: 12, painted: 7 }`, `chromium · count=8 { n: 8, painted: 7 }`. The file's own header at :6-8 asserts "the strip stamps them on `data-stops` and paints them as equal hard segments". o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:33 states the law for the ramp species: "the painted gradient must embed exactly those stops".
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/generate -> focus the "Color count" slider -> ArrowRight to 12 -> open the "Generation preset" combobox -> for any chip: `el.getAttribute("data-stops").split("|").length === 12` while `el.children.length === 7`.

**Proposed cure.** Split the referents at the seam instead of overloading one attribute: the chip stamps WHAT IT PAINTS (`:data-stops="stampStops(visible)"`), and the host — which owns the truth function — stamps the total on the row it owns (`:data-preview-total="stops.length"` on the SelectItem). Then o14's paint-equals-stamp law becomes true for the strip species for the first time and o20's seed-exact law reads the whole truth-function output. Cleaner gestalt: delete the cap from the chip entirely — a chip whose job is "paint the stops you are given" has no business silently discarding five of them; let the host decide how many stops to hand over.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/color-sessi` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The single oracle in the repository that touches PreviewStrip is RED at HEAD, and no CI gate runs it — CI-enforced coverage of this component is exactly zero.

**Mechanism.** F-alpha — non-canonical serialization on one side of the identity, computed canonicalization on the other; plus an un-gated oracle tree

**Evidence.**

```
`npx playwright test --project=smoke e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts -g "seed-exact"` => `1 failed` at o20-generate-plate.spec.ts:105 `expect(live).toEqual(stamped)`; diff: expected `"oklch(80.727303929627% 0.064260062203 230.954823195934deg)"` vs received `"oklch(0.807273 0.0642601 230.955)"` (x5). Mechanism: stampStops (sample.ts:89-91) is a bare join over the host's author-level serialization while the oracle's other side reads computed `backgroundColor`. The ramp leg survives this only because o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:162-168 re-parses to numeric triples. `grep -n "playwright\|e2e" .github/workflows/*.yml` => no output; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs lint, 2x vue-tsc, build, `npm test` (vitest) only.
```

**Reproduction.** `cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && npx playwright test --project=smoke e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts -g "seed-exact" --reporter=line`

**Proposed cure.** Compare at the VALUE level, not the string level — reuse the sibling oracle's existing `parseOklchTriples` (do not mint a second one), or make `stampStops` emit a canonical form once so both sides of every O-14 leg speak the same dialect. The canonicalisation belongs in sample.ts, which calls itself "the ONE serialization, shared by chip + oracle" (:88) and currently is not one serialization at all. Separately: wire the e2e oracle tree into ci.yml, or accept that oracles outside CI are decoration.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt, `demo/color-sessio` · C-2-R · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** CONFIRMED from pass 1 (independently re-measured, and the mechanism proven by direct value comparison). The only oracle that names this component, o20's 'T-17 seed-exact strips' test, is unpassable by construction — and at HEAD it fails even earlier, in the dock fixture, so nobody sees it. e2e is not in CI at all.

**Mechanism.** stampStops is a bare join over the host's AUTHOR-level serialization while the oracle's other side reads getComputedStyle(...).backgroundColor, which every engine canonicalises. The o14 RAMP leg survived this hazard only because someone wrote parseOklchTriples (o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:162-168) and compared numeric triples in a tolerance band; the strip leg never got that treatment.

**Evidence.**

```
I bypassed the failing dock fixture (hash-route navigation) and reproduced o20's exact assertion expect(live).toEqual(stamped): "stamped":["oklch(91.544939436018% 0.08243882705 151.076773675159deg)",...] vs "liveSwatchBg":["oklch(0.915449 0.0824388 151.077)",...] -> "o20WouldPass": false. Same colors, incompatible strings (percent-vs-unit-interval lightness, deg-vs-bare hue, precision). And the spec cannot even reach line 105: `$ npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts --project=smoke --reporter=line` -> `2 failed` — :22:5 fails at locator.click :57 ('element is outside of the viewport' / 'element is not stable'), :63:5 times out at fixtures/dock.ts:78 in openView('Generate'). The o20 header comment at :17-18 claims 'the same rgb() strings' — doubly wrong: not byte-identical, and not rgb().
```

**Reproduction.** npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts --project=smoke (output above), plus node probe-C2-forced-colors.mjs section 1 for the fixture-free value comparison.

**Proposed cure.** Compare at the value level, not the string level — reuse the sibling oracle's existing parseOklchTriples rather than minting a second one — and fix the root by making stampStops emit one canonical dialect (see C-14) so both sides of every O-14 leg speak the same language. Separately, the dock fixture failure and the absence of e2e from CI are their own repairs: a gate nobody runs is not a gate.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/color-session/c` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** PreviewRamp is unreachable in the shipped app: the only UI path that can supply its >=2 operands is a dead <span>. glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot declares `inheritAttrs: !1` and hard-codes `aria-hidden: "true"`, silently discarding the host's `tag="button"`, `aria-label`, `@click` and `:disabled`.

**Mechanism.** Semantics (operability, name, handler, disabled) travel across a package boundary as Vue fall-through attributes into a component that opts out of attribute inheritance. Vue drops them with no type error, no runtime warning, no lint. A producer version bump turned an operable control into decoration and nothing in the build noticed.

**Evidence.**

```
probe-C-ghost.mjs: {"ghost":{"tag":"SPAN","pointerEvents":"none","ariaHidden":"true","tabIndex":-1,"hitIsSelfOrChild":false},"swatchesBefore":0,"swatchesAfterMouse":0,"swatchesAfterSynthetic":0}. probe-C-addslot.mjs: byRoleCount 0, anyAriaLabelMatch 0. probe-C-operands.mjs live option markup contains `<!--v-if-->` where the chip belongs, stopsEls 0 across 9 options. Source: demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:165-175 (declares tag="button" + aria-label + @click); chain demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:111,133 -> MixPane.vue:103 -> useMixingState.ts:42,55-57 -> MixSourceSelector.vue:68-72. Producer: `grep -o 'inheritAttrs[^,}]*' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js` -> `inheritAttrs: !1`.
```

**Reproduction.** node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PreviewRamp/probe-C-ghost.mjs — or by hand: open http://localhost:9000/#/mix, click the dashed ghost in the Selected well; nothing is ever added, and the ghost is not tab-reachable.

**Proposed cure.** Producer-side, not a host patch: WatercolorDot must take an explicit `as`/`tag` prop and `v-bind="$attrs"` (or expose a real <button> wrapper slot) so the operability contract is part of its typed API and breaks the typecheck when it changes. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/color-session/c` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The only oracle for this component is RED, is textually unpassable even if it were reachable, and is not run in CI; the vitest file named for the chip tests only the sampler function.

**Mechanism.** The component's truth is asserted only about its input function (sample.ts) and only in a browser leg that is neither reachable nor runnable. `[\d.]+` in the oracle regex cannot cross the `%`/`deg` units the stamp dialect uses, while the computed background-image canonicalises to unitless — so stamped parses to 0 triples and painted to 17. The gate is vacuous in three independent ways at once.

**Evidence.**

```
`npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o14-preview-truth.spec.ts --project=smoke -g "T-17 chip referent"` -> `2 failed / 1 passed`; both failures are `locator.click: waiting for getByRole('button', { name: 'Add current color to the mix' })` at :355 and :414; the passing test is :334 "honest absence: with <2 operands the rows carry NO chip". probe-C-paint2.mjs, feeding the spec's verbatim parseOklchTriples regex (o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:162-168): {"stampSample":"oklch(62% 0.27 9.8deg)","paintedTriples":17,"stampedTriples":0,"o14Assertion":"expect(painted.length).toBe(stamped.length)"}. `npx vitest run test/preview-chips.test.ts` -> 4 passed, all four call sampleInterpolationRamp, none mounts the SFC. `grep -n "run:" .github/workflows/ci.yml` -> npm ci / lint / vue-tsc x2 / build / npm test only; no playwright job exists.
```

**Reproduction.** Vacuous mutations that keep every gate green: change `linear-gradient(90deg, ...)` to `linear-gradient(180deg, ...)` (PreviewRamp.vue:25); change `stops.join(", ")` to `stops.join(" ")` (invalid gradient, chip paints nothing); change `v-if="stops.length >= 2"` to `>= 99` (PreviewRamp.vue:31); delete the entire <style> block. Run `npx vitest run` and CI after any of them — all green.

**Proposed cure.** Give the SFC a @vue/test-utils mount test in vitest (paint embeds exactly data-stops; <2 stops renders nothing) so CI's existing `npm test` step enforces the chip's own contract without depending on the mix flow being operable. Then make stampStops a genuine canonical serialisation so the browser leg's regex becomes a belt on a canonical form rather than the only thing holding the O-14 law up.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/color-session/c` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The paint violates the module's own SAMPLING LAW: `linear-gradient(90deg, ...stops)` uses POSITIONLESS stops, so the browser interpolates every pixel between library samples — in OKLab, regardless of the row's candidate space. The docblock's claim of "a discrete-stop linear gradient" is false; >=60% of the chip's painted columns are engine fill, and the result is measurably not the library's output.

**Mechanism.** The sampler was built specifically to keep the browser engine out of the interpolation, then its output was handed to the engine as a CONTINUOUS gradient — the one CSS construct that puts the engine back in. The discretisation the docblock describes exists nowhere in the file. The sibling PreviewStrip implements the law correctly (per-segment background-color), which is why the divergence survived review: two chips, one law, only one of them implementing it.

**Evidence.**

```
sample.ts:5-16 forbids it by name ("never CSS `in <space>` gradient interpolation ... no engine divergence") and sample.ts:16-19 says "a chip that approximates the library output is FORBIDDEN"; PreviewRamp.vue:6-7 claims "discrete-stop"; PreviewRamp.vue:24-26 is the positionless gradient. probe-C-paint.mjs interpolation control, endpoints oklch(0.62 0.27 20)/oklch(0.62 0.27 200) 180deg apart, midpoint pixels read from a real screenshot: default `linear-gradient(90deg,A,B)` -> [133,134,134] (OKLab-lerp prediction [135,135,135]); `in oklch shorter hue` -> [148,140,0]; `in srgb` -> [52,65,127]. probe-C-paint2.mjs, chip paint vs per-column library truth at the chip's real 42px width: hsl/longer max 15/255, mean 4.43, 16 of 42 columns >4; oklch/longer max 8/255; hsv max 2; xyz max 1. 17 stops across 42 columns means at most 17 columns can be library truth.
```

**Reproduction.** node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PreviewRamp/probe-C-paint.mjs (interpolation-space control, rows E/F/G) and node .../probe-C-paint2.mjs (chip-vs-library-truth table). Banked image: paint-probe.png.

**Proposed cure.** Emit the hard stops the docblock already claims — `stops.map((s,i) => `${s} ${i/n*100}% ${(i+1)/n*100}%`)` — which deletes the engine from the interpolation, makes the docblock true, collapses data-stops and the paint into one referent, and makes the ramp structurally identical to PreviewStrip. The gestalt version is the rooted chip plate: one primitive taking a stops list and a discrete|continuous intent, instead of two components that disagree about what "discrete" means. (If a genuinely continuous ramp is wanted, the sampling law must be amended and the row must declare its own space, e.g. `linear-gradient(in oklch longer hue ...)`, never silently inherit OKLab — that is a design ruling, not an implementation choice.)

(compiled Vite offsets; sources are picker-color.ts:106/:116 and ColorSpaceSelector.vue:157). ```

booted, triggers: 2  boundary: 0
   after slider 0 -> boundary: 0

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/color-session/C` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The specimen catalog LIES: every preview is computed WITHOUT the value-domain clamp that the write gate applies, so the number the row advertises is not the number the app stores when you click it. RGB promises r=385.30 and delivers 255; HSL promises s=-1295.15% and delivers 0% (a hyper-saturated pink advertised, white delivered); XYZ promises x=1.2667 and delivers 1. The previews are also not valid CSS (negative percentages, out-of-range components).

**Mechanism.** Two code paths compute the same quantity with different laws — the preview reads the raw conversion, the commit reads the clamped conversion. The domain law's own thesis (valueDomain.ts:5-13: 'every color that LANDS on the demo model enters its space's domain … TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION') is not applied to the one surface that promises a landing.

**Evidence.**

```
Preview path: ColorSpaceSelector.vue:157 raw `convertPickerColor`. Write path: useColorPipeline.ts:64-71 `updateModel` applies `clampColorToSpaceDomain(patch.color)` (the T-33a 'ONE write gate'), reached via `updateToColorSpace` -> `setCurrentColor` (useColorPipeline.ts:170-173). MEASURED promise vs result on the shipped default colour `lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)`:
```
CATALOG PROMISE for RGB : rgb(385.302835934518 143.376536829596 199.64311881105 / 82.7%)
URL after select        : #/?space=rgb&color=rgb(255 143.376536829596 199.64311881105 / 82.7%)
HEADER after select     : RGB | 255 | , | 143 | , | 200

PROMISE HSL: hsl(346.045357898758deg -1295.152156124318% 103.662622110611% / 82.7%)
RESULT  URL: #/?space=hsl&color=hsl(346.045357898758deg 0% 100% / 82.7%)
RESULT  HDR: HSL | 346 | deg | , | 0 | % | , | 100 | %

XYZ promised color(xyz 1.266749228777 …) ; delivered color(xyz 1 …)
```
Screenshots: evidence/C-catalog-open-outofgamut.png, evidence/C-after-hsl-select.png.
```

**Reproduction.** Boot `http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(92%25 88.8 20 / 82.7%25)` (the app default). Open `.space-trigger`, read the RGB row's caption, click it, read the URL and the header readout. Then repeat for HSL and XYZ. Outputs pasted above (lie.mjs / hsl.mjs / about.mjs).

**Proposed cure.** Compute the preview through the SAME gate the write goes through: `specimenFor` formats `clampColorToSpaceDomain(converted)` — one call to the already-exported function (valueDomain.ts:44), zero new machinery. This makes the preview definitionally equal to the result, and simultaneously kills the invalid-CSS output, because clamping is what turns `-1295%` into `0%`.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shared/ui/Empty` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Activating the Retry button in EmptyState's `#action` slot permanently annihilates the Browse pane: reactive state still says "error" but the DOM renders nothing at all — no alert, no empty plate, no control, no announcement. Survives SPA navigation; only a hard reload recovers.

**Mechanism.** A control is rendered inside the very conditionally-rendered node its own activation unmounts, and that node lives under `<Transition mode="out-in">`. The state round-trips error→developing→error in 47ms, entirely inside the 200ms out-in leave, and the re-entering vnode shares `key="error"` with the still-leaving vnode, so the pending enter is dropped and nothing is ever mounted.

**Evidence.**

```

AFTER re-nav (/#/browse→/#/palettes→/#/browse, hash-only) byte-identical. probe-deadlock.mjs both engines: "+4s later — alerts=0 retry=0". probe-isolate.mjs: failure latency after Enter = 47ms; durations {fast:"0.2s", normal:"0.3s", springSnappy:"calc(0.44s * 1)"}. Sources: demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:14-27 (error root + #action slot at :26), demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:41 (<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">), :61-78 (EmptyState key="error"), demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:63-88.
```

**Reproduction.** 1. open http://localhost:9000/#/browse (the commons load fails → EmptyState variant="error"). 2. focus the "Retry" button and press Enter. 3. wait 3s. Result: the Browse pane body is empty forever. `node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/probe-state.mjs`

**Proposed cure.** Architectural, not a patch: stop wrapping an aria-live species swap in mode="out-in" (an assertive role="alert" that waits 200ms behind another node's leave already lies about its own semantics), and give EmptyState a STABLE root that never unmounts — swap only the interior (glyph/eyebrow/lines) on `variant`, with the action slot in a persistent footer outside the swap. Then neither the announcement region nor the retry control is a casualty of the retry, and `key="error"`/`key="wall"` plus the whole same-key-during-leave collision class disappear. Do NOT collapse the two v-if/v-else roots into one root with `:role` — see N-4.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shared/ui/PaneH` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The title-shrink ratio is built on the CSS identity tan(atan2(y,x)) === y/x, which WebKit does not implement for font-relative lengths — it feeds atan2's degree magnitude to tan() as radians. Because --type-display-1 is a viewport-fluid clamp, the shipped value is an unbounded, sign-changing, pole-crossing function of viewport width on WebKit. At 1024px the pane title renders at 10.87x and covers the entire pane; at 1280px it renders mirrored and off-screen, taking the About pane's colour-space <button> (slotted inside the <h3>) with it.

**Mechanism.** M-A — a scroll-driven choreography reasoned from spec text and from Chromium, never measured on WebKit; a trigonometric contrivance substituted for plain division, guarded by an @supports condition whose premise (SDA support implies correct atan2) is false by measurement.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:140-142 (declaration) + node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/scale.css:1 (--type-heading: 1.618rem; --type-display-1: clamp(1.618rem, 1.2rem + 1.6vw, 2.618rem)). probe-C2-05-pole-sweep.mjs, isolated AND live arms agreeing to the last digit: webkit 1024 -> 10.868346 (designed 0.727518), 1180 -> -0.363219, 1200 -> -0.642357, 1240 -> -1.587175, 1280 -> -7.39094, 1300 -> 13.171055, 1320 -> 3.42998, 1360 -> 1.205336, 1440+ -> 0.310808 (designed 0.618029); chromium correct at all 20 widths. probe-C2-06-shots.mjs: webkit 1024x900 tf=matrix(10.868346) rect{w:4777.8,h:867.8} in a 1024x900 viewport; webkit 1280x900 tf=matrix(-7.39094) rect{x:-2741.6,y:-215.6}. probe-C2-07-consequences.mjs(b): webkit 1280x900 STUCK button rect {x:-934,y:-523.4}, inViewport:false, hitAtCentre:"OFF-VIEWPORT". Mechanism isolated by probe-03-atan2-mechanism.mjs: tan(atan2(1rem,1rem)) -> 1.619775 == Math.tan(45) exactly; tan(atan2(1.618rem,2.618rem)) -> 0.310808 == Math.tan(31.71726881458922) exactly; px operands correct in both engines. Screenshots committed: shot-C2-webkit-1024-plus10.87x.png, shot-C2-webkit-1280-negative7.39x.png, shot-C2-webkit-1300-plus13.17x.png, shot-C2-webkit-1440-plus0.311x.png.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-C2-05-pole-sweep.mjs ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-C2-06-shots.mjs ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-03-atan2-mechanism.mjs (dev server on :9000)

**Proposed cure.** Replace the trigonometry with the CSS-values-4 length/length division: `--pane-title-shrink-ratio: calc(var(--type-heading) / var(--type-display-1));`. One line at PaneHeader.vue:140-142; verified matrix(0.618029) and matrix(1) on BOTH engines (probe-03 CURE-A / CURE-A' rows). It deletes the contrivance, deletes the @supports-implies-correct-atan2 argument from the comment, restores the phone no-op to exactly 1, and preserves the fluid-clamp property the closed form was chosen for.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (assume the design is flawed)` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The declared F7/F8 inset hairline ring is never painted on PreviewStrip — the component has no boundary of any kind against the translucent menu row it sits on. Its sibling PreviewRamp, sharing the class name and the docblock law, does paint it.

**Mechanism.** CSS paint order: an element's inset box-shadow paints above its own background but BELOW its in-flow descendants. The colour payload lives in opaque child spans that fill the padding box (clipped to the same rounded rect by overflow:hidden), so the shadow is occluded by the component's own content. PreviewRamp escapes only because its payload is a background-image on the element itself.

C2 CONTROL (payload = opaque child filling the box, the PreviewStrip pattern): top rows 0..11 = [(210,121,47) x12] — first row equal to payload y=0 → ZERO ring pixels.
A LIVE /generate light: [(242,228,216)x2 capture bleed, then (0,173,255) payload]. A2 LIVE /generate dark: [(84,71,61)x2 row ground, then (99,101,232)]. D LIVE /atmosphere light: [(255,113,177) x12].

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The boundary root is `position: static` and paints beneath the `position: absolute` full-viewport atmosphere canvas. Three of its four children (alert glyph, Fraunces statement, Fira detail) never render; only the glass-ui Button, which is `position: relative`, survives. The shipped caught state is a wordless pill on an empty field — the exact 'silent dead plate' the component's header comment says it exists to prevent.

**Mechanism.** F1 — the boundary replaced a stage instead of occupying a seat. CSS 2.1 Appendix E painting order: positioned descendants (step 8) paint above in-flow inline content (step 5). The element it displaces, `.pane-container`, carries `position: relative` (demo/styles/shell.css:74) and `.pane-wrapper--left` carries `z-index: 1` (shell.css:94-96); the bare div that replaces them inherits neither. Because the canvas is pointer-events:none, every DOM-level assertion passes while the pixels are blank — which is why the 60-capture visual matrix reports blankOrNearBlank: 0.

**Evidence.**

```
evidence/EB1-caught-desktop-1440-light.png (only 'Try again' visible). evidence/EB-probe2.json → occlusion: canvasStyle {position:absolute, zIndex:auto}, canvasRect {0,0,1440,900}, canvasDomIndexInLayout 0; boundaryStyle {position:static, zIndex:auto}; childStyles svg/msg/detail = static, button = relative. hitTest returns `p.font-display.text-heading` for the invisible message because the canvas is pointer-events:none (App.vue:11). Cure test evidence/EB8-cure-test-position-relative.png: setting only `style.position='relative'` restores all three. Independent prior capture: ../Markdown/evidence/E6-doc-load-failure-whole-route-collapse.png. Source: demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:15-22; demo/color-picker/App.vue:9-17,50.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/eb-probe.mjs — WebKit, viewport 1440x900, `page.route(/\/assets\/docs\/[a-z-]+\.md/, r => r.abort('failed'))`, goto http://localhost:9000/#/, wait 9s. Screenshot shows only the button; DOM reports all four children present with non-zero rects, opacity 1, visibility visible.

**Proposed cure.** Do not bolt `position: relative` onto the div — that patches the symptom. Move the boundary INSIDE `PaneSlot` so the failing pane's own wrapper renders the fallback in place of its child. The seat already owns the stacking layer, the glass material, the `cqi` container and the `vj-enter` grammar, so the bug becomes structurally impossible. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The sole recovery affordance cannot recover. Clicking 'Try again' re-mounts the identical subtree with identical inputs, so a deterministic failure re-throws inside the same tick; the plate returns and focus is dragged back off the button onto the container, re-firing the assertive alert.

**Mechanism.** F2 — the recovery affordance is decorative. `reset()` changes no input to the failing subtree: no remount key bump, no refetch, no attempt counter, no escalated copy, no alternative exit. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.1 requires a recovery article to offer 'diagnosis, preservation/export, then separately confirmed reset'; this offers one verb that provably does nothing.

**Evidence.**

```
evidence/EB-measurements.json → EB5.post: beforeBoundary true → click `.vj-error-boundary button` → afterRetryBoundary true, afterRetryActive {tag: 'div', cls: 'vj-error-boundary flex flex-col items-center justify-center '}. ```

**Reproduction.** node .../eb-probe.mjs (EB5 case) — after the catch, `page.click('.vj-error-boundary button')`, wait 2.5s, re-inspect. Boundary still present, activeElement is the container div again.

**Proposed cure.** A retry must change an input — bump a remount key on the slot, refetch the failed resource, or hand the user a named route escape. After the first failed retry the plate must escalate (say the retry failed and offer the escape) rather than re-arm the same dead verb.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The 'one golden plate' law is false at every viewport and drifts 31%. Measured width/height: 2.9911 at 320px and 390px (+14.25% vs phi^2), 2.8450 at 768px, 2.5548 at 1440px (-2.41%), 2.2886 at 2200px (-12.58%). Never 2.6180. Browser zoom compounds it: 200% zoom halves the CSS viewport, so a 1440px window renders the ~2.85 ratio of a 720px column. Compounding this, the literal 2.618rem is hardcoded in two files while two design tokens already carry that exact value.

**Mechanism.** F-beta — the primitive was never rooted: inline-size is root-relative (rem) while block-size is locally inherited (em) on a vw-clamped token. Two axes on two scales cannot hold a constant ratio, so the declared relation is unexpressible in the code that declares it. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.8 verbatim: 'Real rendered relation wins over token intent... token presence alone cannot close a row.' Owner edict 5 (root-level styling) is breached twice by the hardcoded literal.

**Evidence.**

```
probes-D/ratio-sweep-forced-rtl.mjs SWEEP lines (log probes-D/ratio-sweep.log): 8 measurements, zero equal phi^2, spread 2.2886…2.9911. Source: PreviewStrip.vue:59 `inline-size: 2.618rem; /* one golden plate — phi^2 × 1em (F7) */` against `block-size: 1em` at :60; the local font-size is the vw-clamped `--type-caption: clamp(0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem)`. Unused tokens: demo/styles/foundation.css:462 `--phi-4: 2.618rem` and glass-ui `--space-phi-5: 2.618rem` (grep -rn '2\.618' demo/ = 8 hits).
```

**Reproduction.** `node probes-D/ratio-sweep-forced-rtl.mjs` and read the SWEEP lines; or measure `.preview-strip` getBoundingClientRect() with the Palette harmony menu open at 320px and at 2200px.

**Proposed cure.** One unit system, one token: `block-size: 1em; inline-size: calc(1em * var(--phi-2))`, hoisted to the shared root of D-8 so it is declared once. Then phi^2 is true by construction at every clamp arm and every zoom level. --radius-sm has the same disease in miniature (fixed 4px on a 14→18.3px plate); it must scale with the plate too.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** On Safari the pane title GROWS 1.62x on scroll at the phone band and collides with pane content, in the exact band the file documents as a deliberate no-op.

**Mechanism.** CSS-arithmetic-as-law — WebKit degrades the <angle> returned by atan2() to a bare <number>, so tan() reads it as radians: tan(45 rad)=1.6198 instead of tan(45deg)=1

**Evidence.**

```
probe-shrink-ratio.mjs, 390x844, /#/gradient: webkit ratioVar="1619.765625px" (=1.619766; law demands 1.0), terminal titleTransform=matrix(1.619775,...), titleInkH 27.16->43.99px inside headerH 68.97px (content box 44.97px). chromium ratioVar="1000px" (correct). Frames shots/webkit-phone390-{light,dark}-STUCK.png. Contradicts PaneHeader.vue:137-139.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-shrink-ratio.mjs  (dev server live on :9000). Re-run at verification time; numbers reproduced exactly.

**Proposed cure.** Dissolved by D-16 (no ratio survives the transposition). Interim only, if the jury stages the work: `--pane-title-shrink-ratio: calc(var(--type-heading) / var(--type-display-1))` — measured identical in both engines at both bands. Do NOT add a @supports arm: CSS.supports for atan2 returns true in the engine that computes the wrong answer.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The boundary hand-rolls, at the wrong altitude and worse, a primitive Vue already ships per-pane. defineAsyncComponent's options form supplies errorComponent, loadingComponent, delay, timeout and onError(err, retry, fail, attempts) — i.e. a retry that actually retries, a bounded blast radius, a loading state and a timeout. All ten pane call sites pass a bare loader.

**Mechanism.** F2 — failure handled at the wrong altitude.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:69-78 — ten `defineAsyncComponent(() => import(...))` calls, no options object on any of them. Consequence measured: evidence-r2/R2-retry.json afterRetry.boundaryUp=true, activeIsButton=false — the hand-rolled 'Try again' has no retry() to call. Second consequence: with no `timeout`, a chunk request that hangs rather than rejects produces no error at all, so the boundary never fires and the user sits in front of a permanently empty pane band — a state the boundary's existence conceals.
```

**Reproduction.** grep -n 'defineAsyncComponent' demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts (10 hits, all bare loaders); node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/r2-retry.mjs for the retry consequence. The hanging-chunk arm is a HYPOTHESIS — not reproduced; it follows from the absent `timeout` option but I did not stall a request to witness it.

**Proposed cure.** Move failure handling to the seam that owns the failure: give usePaneRouter's ten async panes the options form with one shared errorComponent and loadingComponent, and back the retry verb with onError's retry(). ErrorBoundary then either dies, or shrinks to the last-resort root boundary above <App/> that it should have been.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The four-arc hue quartet can never render four distinct arcs. In the 4 non-polar spaces of 9 (oklab, lab, rgb, xyz) all four hue ramps are byte-identical; in polar spaces increasing/decreasing collapse onto shorter/longer, capping distinct previews at 2; achromatic operands collapse all four to 1 in every space. The app's default space is oklab, so the shipped default shows four labels over four identical chips with the Hue-method Select still enabled and offering a choice that provably cannot change the result.

**Mechanism.** preview untruth — a differentiating affordance whose differentia is structurally absent; the menu's shape (4 flat rows) does not match the domain (polar-ness of the space × orientation of one operand pair)

**Evidence.**

```
src/color/anchors.ts:360-366 `export const HUE_INDEX = { hsl: 0, hsv: 0, hwb: 0, lch: 2, oklch: 2 }`; src/color/operations.ts:101-111 applies interpolateHue only `if (i === hueIndex)`. demo/color-session/color-space-meta.ts:26-36 offers 9 spaces. demo/workbenches/mix/composables/useMixingState.ts:44 `const colorSpace = ref<PickerSpace>("oklab")` — confirmed visually in both Safari /mix screenshots (trigger reads "OKLab"). MixConfigBar.vue:122-139 has no :disabled binding on the Hue-method Select.
```

**Reproduction.** node /tmp/pr_probe3.mjs (shipped sampler algorithm verbatim vs dist/subpaths/color.js, operands #e11d48→#0ea5e9) → `oklch 2 differ / oklab 1 *** ALL FOUR IDENTICAL *** / lab 1 *** ALL FOUR IDENTICAL *** / lch 2 / hsl 2 / hsv 2 / hwb 2 / rgb 1 *** ALL FOUR IDENTICAL *** / xyz 1 *** ALL FOUR IDENTICAL ***`. node /tmp/pr_probe4.mjs → `oklch #e11d48→#0ea5e9 distinct=2 groups=shorter=decreasing longer=increasing`; `oklch #111111→#eeeeee distinct=1 groups=shorter=longer=increasing=decreasing`.

**Proposed cure.** Transpose the vocabulary, do not patch the chip. (1) INTERPOLATION_SPACES gains `polar: boolean` derived from the library's single source (the HUE_INDEX keyset); when the selected space is non-polar the Hue-method row is disabled with a named reason and leaves the tab order — the lane says why instead of showing four lies. (2) In a polar space, expose the two real trajectories as two, naming the direction for the current pair ("Shorter — counter-clockwise for these colors"), so increasing/decreasing read as the orientation restatement they are rather than as two further arcs. This is a subtraction.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design interrogation of `demo/shared/ui/EmptyS` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The failure species exists only as a content replacement, so a failed refresh over populated data destroys visible truth; and the seven hosts hold two contradictory guard policies for one species.

**Mechanism.** missing state in the species — there is no non-destructive 'failure over retained content' shape, so hosts must choose between hiding the failure and destroying the data

**Evidence.**

```
Unguarded `v-else-if="loadError"` (error branch precedes the data branch with no length guard) at demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:55, AdminTagsPanel.vue:66, AdminAuditPanel.vue:43, AdminNamesPanel.vue:31 and :81, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:23. Guarded at demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:57 (`pm.browseError.value && displayedBrowse.length === 0`). Laws: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:101 "Persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace … never carries the only truth"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:52 PR-08 "Pending/failure/export/recovery truth only transient → ADD-AFFORDANCE … Persistent entity status/recovery".
```

**Reproduction.** Any state with `loadError` truthy AND `items.length > 0` — i.e. press Refresh on a populated Admin roster while the API is down. The template makes rendering both unreachable. (The secondary claim that focus falls to <body> when the focused row control unmounts is labelled a HYPOTHESIS in the report — it needs a forced backend failure with focus parked on a row action.)

**Proposed cure.** `error` is not a variant of *empty*, it is a status on the *field*. Give it two shapes: cold-load failure → plate replacement (keep); refresh failure → a persistent status strip ABOVE the retained field, owning the retry. The tri-state then reduces to `field | field+status | empty-invitation` and the seven divergent guards collapse to one owner.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The condensed title rung is derived by a browser trigonometric function inside a leaf component — `--pane-title-shrink-ratio: calc(tan(atan2(var(--type-heading), var(--type-display-1))))`. A type-scale relationship whose home is the token layer was re-derived in-component, making each engine's math-function implementation a design-system input. WebKit produces 0.310808 where Chromium produces 0.618029: the Safari pane title shrinks to 13.02px effective (below the 25.9px BR-11 floor the repo's own sibling grammar protects), and on Safari mobile the documented "self-neutralizing no-op" inverts to a 43% ENLARGEMENT.

**Mechanism.** wrong-home: a design-system concern (type-scale relationship) re-derived inside a demo leaf component, so engine-dependent CSS math becomes a design input

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:140-142 (the calc); comment claim at :132-139 ("CLOSED-FORM... ≈0.618 (1/φ) at the ≥1440 cap, degenerating to exactly 1 on phones"). MEASURED live, /#/about @1440x900, host scrolled to 200: webkit `matrix(0.310808,…)` title 462px→144px; chromium `matrix(0.618029,…)` title 462px→286px; both report identical `--type-heading: 1.618rem`, `--type-display-1: clamp(1.618rem, 1.2rem + 1.6vw, 2.618rem)` computed 41.888px, `supportsSDA: true`. MOBILE 390x844 /#/gradient: `webkit REST {"tr":"matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)","w":324,"h":27} STUCK {"tr":"matrix(1.433843, 0, 0, 1.433843, 0, 0)","w":465,"h":39}` vs `chromium STUCK {"tr":"matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)","w":324,"h":27}`. MECHANISM isolated to 5 CSS declarations, no app: a=`tan(atan2(1.618rem,2.618rem))` webkit 310.797px / chromium 618.016px; b=`tan(31.71776deg)` 618.031px BOTH; c=`tan(31.71776rad)` 311.344px BOTH; d=`atan2(1.618rem,2.618rem)/1deg` 31717.27 BOTH; e=`tan(atan(0.618))` 618px BOTH. webkit a == c ⇒ atan2() returns a correct angle (row d) but tan() consumes its numeric value as radians. Arithmetic: 31.71727 − 10π = 0.301343 rad; tan(0.301343) = 0.31081 = measured to 5 figures. Floor it violates: demo/picker/header.css:87-93. Only atan2 site in the repo: `grep -rn atan2 demo/ src/` → PaneHeader.vue:141.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-L-structure.mjs (dev server live on :9000) for the app measurement; the 5-declaration isolation and the 390px mobile inversion scripts are pasted verbatim in the report's Reproduction section

**Proposed cure.** ARCHITECTURAL TRANSPOSITION, not a patch: delete the trig and the `transform: scale()` entirely. "One golden rung down from display-1" is a discrete token step and belongs in the design system, where glass-ui already expresses it — dist/components/card/card-scroll.css steps `[data-condensed] > [data-slot=card-title]` from `--type-display-2` to `--type-display-1` with no math function, no @supports gate, and no per-engine evaluation. Under the L-2 cure this defect cannot exist: there is no calc() and no scale() left to get wrong.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Triplicate ownership of one concept, with the canonical home sitting unused in node_modules. glass-ui 7.0.0 — adopted WHOLE at V·W44 — ships `CardHeader shrink` with the veil, the sufficiency-gated threshold crossing, the title token step, the description collapse, and a prefers-reduced-motion arm. The demo carries TWO forks of it (PaneHeader.vue for 9 panes; useHeaderCondense.ts + picker/header.css Row B for 1), and the premise that justifies both — that the producer's grammar is "compositor-only BY ARCHITECTURAL COMMITMENT" and "structurally cannot satisfy §0.8/BR-9" — is FALSE against 7.0.0, which transitions `padding-block-start` and steps `font-size`: real layout channels.

**Mechanism.** wrong-home: a design-system primitive hand-forked into demo/, twice; the forks survived their own supersession when 7.0.0 was adopted whole (edict-2 legacy/dual-path)

**Evidence.**

```
False premise: demo/picker/composables/useHeaderCondense.ts:9-15. Refutation, node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/card-scroll.css (full text): `.card-header--shrink { transition: padding-block-start var(--duration-normal) … }`, `[data-condensed="true"] { padding-block-start: var(--card-header-pad-condensed) }`, `[data-condensed="true"] > [data-slot=card-title] { font-size: var(--type-display-1) }`, `[data-condensed="true"] > [data-slot=card-description] { display: none }`, `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { … transition: none }`. Producer mechanism, dist/card-Bk96VI2R.js `__name: "CardHeader"`: `o.value?.closest(".card-scroll-host")`; gate `e.scrollHeight - e.clientHeight > t.getBoundingClientRect().height/2 + 24`; `triggers: [{at:24,direction:"down",id:"condense"},{…"expand"}]`; `watch(f, g, {immediate:!0, flush:"post"})`. Fork B equivalent: useHeaderCondense.ts:65-73 (overflowY auto|scroll ancestor walk), :80 (`opts.threshold ?? 24`), :94-98 (`overflow <= savings + threshold`, `savings = expandedH - expandedH*0.5`), :75,121 (`{immediate:true, flush:"post"}`) — same algorithm, same constant 24, same flush. Producer has ZERO demo consumers: `grep -rn "card-scroll-host" demo/` → no output; `grep -rn shrink demo/ | grep -i cardheader` → nothing. Dep is `"@mkbabb/glass-ui": "^7.0.0"`; adoption commit 91fa1368. Duplication volume: PaneHeader.vue 224 lines + useHeaderCondense.ts 127 lines + picker/header.css:48-143 ≈ 96 lines ≈ 447 demo-owned lines.
```

**Reproduction.** cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/card-scroll.css; cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/CardHeader.vue.d.ts; node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync("node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/card-Bk96VI2R.js","utf8"); const i=s.indexOf("CardHeader"); console.log(s.slice(i-60,i+900))'; grep -rn "card-scroll-host" demo/

**Proposed cure.** Retire both forks; PaneHeader.vue ceases to exist. Nine panes become `<Card tier="resting" class="card-scroll-host …"><CardHeader shrink><CardTitle as="h2">Title</CardTitle><CardDescription>…</CardDescription></CardHeader><CardContent>…</CardContent></Card>`. Where 7.0.0 is genuinely short of §0.8 the delta goes UPSTREAM to glass-ui as a CardHeader variant/knob via the standing BH relay (edict 4) — it does not come back into demo/. Before landing, two things must be MEASURED not re-quoted: (1) the §0.8/BR-9 claim against 7.0.0's actual padding+font-size grammar; (2) the picker's specific readout line-lock / blob-reservation geometry, which is Fork B's own seat.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Error containment is owned at an altitude that cannot know when the failure is stale: the single App-level ErrorBoundary latches the whole application dead across navigation and across its own Retry, recoverable only by full page reload. Blast radius is the entire pane grid plus every KeepAlive cache.

**Mechanism.** wrong-altitude ownership — state about "which pane is currently failing" is stored on the application, not on the pane; unique semantic ownership violated

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-picker/App.vue:47-50 opens ONE boundary around the whole grid, closes at :139-141 (no @reset listener). `caught` is a bare ref at ErrorBoundary.vue:55; the failing unit is keyed at demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:113-119 (`:key="liveKey"`). Live probe `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/probes/live-latch.mjs` output: instances_with_onErrorCaptured: [{"name":"ErrorBoundary","depth":1}] / after_catch: {"paneContainerPresent":false,"focusTag":"vj-error-boundary flex flex-col items-ce"} / after_navigation_to_/palettes: {"hash":"#/palettes","paneContainerPresent":false,"mainText":"This panel hit an unexpected error.\n\nL-probe induced render throw\n\nTry again"} / after_reload: {"alerts":1,"paneContainerPresent":true}. Unit probes P1+P2 in probes/boundary.test.ts (6/6 pass).
```

**Reproduction.** 1) dev server at localhost:9000; 2) run `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/probes/live-latch.mjs` — it walks the live Vue tree, fires the single onErrorCaptured hook exactly as Vue's handleError does, then sets location.hash='#/palettes'; 3) observe hash changes to #/palettes while .pane-container remains absent and the error plate still renders. Isolated: `npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/probes/vitest.config.ts` P2 — replace the slotted component outright, boundary stays latched, healthy replacement never mounts.

**Proposed cure.** Architectural transposition: move containment INTO demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue where the key already lives — `<PaneErrorBoundary :key="liveKey" @retry="remount"><component :is="liveComponent" :key="liveKey"/></PaneErrorBoundary>` inside the existing KeepAlive. `:key="liveKey"` is the whole fix for the latch: a view change destroys the boundary instance with the pane it guarded, so `caught` cannot outlive its subject. Blast radius drops from the application to one slot. App.vue then holds ZERO boundary markup — the shell owns pane containment, which is what a shell is for.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The condensed type rung is derived by nested browser trigonometry inside a leaf component — `--pane-title-shrink-ratio: calc(tan(atan2(var(--type-heading), var(--type-display-1))))` — and WebKit, the app's primary engine, evaluates it wrong. A type-scale relationship was promoted into a browser math-function implementation detail. CARRIED FROM PASS 1, independently re-verified by this seat.

**Mechanism.** wrong-home: a token-layer proposition ('one golden rung down from display-1') re-derived in a leaf component's calc(), making an engine's math-function implementation a design-system input

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:140-142. My own 5-declaration isolated CSS repro (no app, no framework), written before reading pass 1's probe: webkit {a:310.796875px, b:618.03125px, c:311.34375px, d:31717.265625px, e:618px} vs chromium {a:618.016px, b:618.031px, c:311.344px, d:31717.3px, e:618px} where a=tan(atan2(1.618rem,2.618rem)), b=tan(31.71776deg), c=tan(31.71776rad), d=atan2(...)/1deg, e=tan(atan(0.618)). WebKit's `a` lands exactly on `c` — atan2() returns the correct angle (d matches Chromium to 6 figures) and tan() then consumes its numeric value as RADIANS. In-app, /#/gradient, identical viewport and identical computed fs=41.888px: webkit stuck matrix(0.655404) w=303px vs chromium matrix(0.805831) w=372px at the same scroll offset; at 390x844 webkit matrix(1.433843) w=324->465px vs chromium matrix(1) w=324px — on mobile Safari the title GROWS 43% inside a 390px viewport, the exact inverse of the design. `grep -rn atan2 demo/ src/` → PaneHeader.vue:141 is the only site in the repository depending on it.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/trig-verify.mjs (5 divs, width: calc(1000px * <expr>), webkit + chromium); node <scratchpad>/ratio-verify.mjs against http://localhost:9000/#/gradient at 1440x900 and 390x844

**Proposed cure.** Delete the trig entirely. The condensed rung is a discrete token step taken at the design-system level — glass-ui's card-scroll.css already expresses the identical relationship as `[data-condensed] > [data-slot=card-title] { font-size: var(--type-display-1) }`, no math function, no engine dependence, no @supports gate. This also kills L-3 outright, because a font-size step has no transform-origin.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L2-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `package.json#dependencies` declares two heavyweight runtime dependencies the published artifact never imports, and one of them (`@mkbabb/keyframes.js@6`) hard-pins `@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0` — so the package transitively depends on a registry copy of ITSELF. Every downstream consumer of a 160 KB zero-dependency colour library is forced to install ~6.0 MB, including a duplicate pinned value.js.

**Mechanism.** Demo-only dependencies were declared as runtime `dependencies` instead of `devDependencies` on a package whose `files` ships only `dist`. The reverse edge (keyframes.js → value.js, exact pin) then closes a package-level cycle. In-repo the hazard is masked because vite.config.ts:40-50 aliases the seven specifiers to the local dist before node resolution runs.

**Evidence.**

```
package.json:82-85 declares {"@mkbabb/glass-ui":"^7.0.0","@mkbabb/keyframes.js":"^6.0.0"}. Scan of every emitted ESM file in dist/: `files scanned: 10 / relative imports (internal chunks): 10 / BARE (external) specifiers in the published artifact: 0 []`. vite.library.ts:13 `export const libraryExternal: string[] = [];`. `grep -rn "@mkbabb/" src/` → 2 hits, both doc-comments. `grep -rn "@mkbabb/keyframes" src/ demo/ test/ e2e/` → 0. `npm ls @mkbabb/glass-ui @mkbabb/keyframes.js @mkbabb/value.js` → `@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js ├─┬ @mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 │ ├── @mkbabb/keyframes.js@6.0.0 deduped │ └── @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 └─┬ @mkbabb/keyframes.js@6.0.0 └── @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 deduped`. package-lock.json:1330 `"@mkbabb/value.js": "4.0.0"` (exact pin, hard dependency of keyframes.js). `du -sh`: glass-ui 5.2M, keyframes.js 608K, node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js 168K vs own dist 132K+28K.
```

**Reproduction.** cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && npm ls @mkbabb/glass-ui @mkbabb/keyframes.js @mkbabb/value.js  (shows the self-cycle); du -sh node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui node_modules/@mkbabb/keyframes.js node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js (shows ~6.0 MB); the dist import scan in the report §2 (shows 0 bare specifiers).

**Proposed cure.** `dependencies: {}` — move both entries to `devDependencies`. glass-ui already declares value.js as an OPTIONAL PEER (its peerDependenciesMeta), which is the correct shape; value.js must not re-declare the reverse edge. Cross-repo relay to the keyframes.js inbox: its `dependencies: {"@mkbabb/value.js":"4.0.0"}` should be a `^4`-ranged PEER, which dissolves the cycle at the ecosystem level rather than locally. Gate: `node -p 'JSON.stringify(require("./package.json").dependencies)'` → `{}` and `npm ls @mkbabb/value.js` shows exactly one node.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L2-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Error containment is owned at one fixed altitude that is wrong in BOTH directions: too coarse for the pane (round 1's confirmed latch — one pane's throw unmounts both panes and latches across navigation) and too narrow for the shell — the boundary is a SIBLING of the Dock <nav>, the aurora <canvas>, and the global MigratePalettesDialog, so a throw in any of them is not caught at all.

**Mechanism.** Unique-semantic-ownership violated twice. 'Which unit is currently failing' is a fact about a PANE, stored on the APP (ErrorBoundary.vue:55 `caught` is component-local on a component whose lifetime is the application's). 'Has the shell failed' is a fact about the SHELL, owned by nobody. One component named ErrorBoundary at one fixed depth cannot hold both; holding one at the wrong depth produces the latch and leaves the other uncovered.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-picker/App.vue:24-44 (<nav>, the app's only navigation), :47 (<main>), :50-140 (<ErrorBoundary>), :152-158 (<MigratePalettesDialog>) — grep -n output pasted in report. Live probe `probes-L-r2/live-net.mjs` against localhost:9000: {"app_layout_children":["canvas","nav","main"],"onErrorCaptured_carriers":[{"name":"ErrorBoundary","depth":1,"path":"App"}],"containment_coverage":{"elements_under_app":1695,"elements_inside_main_the_only_guarded_region":1535,"pct":90.6},"uncontained_top_level":["div","div.app-layout","span","div","div","div"]}. Probe R2-A: {"probe":"R2-A","boundary_announced":false,"errors_escaped_to_app_root":["dock render throw"]}.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/probes-L-r2/vitest.config.ts  (R2-A, 3/3 pass) ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/probes-L-r2/live-net.mjs  (dev server on :9000) ; round-1 latch: npx vitest run --config docs/.../ErrorBoundary/probes/vitest.config.ts (13/13)

**Proposed cure.** Transposition to three altitudes with three owners. (1) Pane containment moves INTO demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue as <PaneErrorBoundary :key="liveKey"> — liveKey already lives there (PaneSlot.vue:113-125); keying the boundary makes `caught` structurally incapable of outliving its subject and drops blast radius from the application to one slot. (2) Shell containment moves ABOVE App, at the mount site in the new main.ts (L2-2). (3) Reporting moves to main.ts. App.vue then holds ZERO boundary markup.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L2-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** There is no boot module anywhere in demo/ — the only `createApp` in the repository is an inline <script type="module"> inside index.html. Consequently error REPORTING has no home: the live app has no app.config.errorHandler and no window.onerror, and the boundary's `return false` makes it a terminal sink even when a handler does exist.

**Mechanism.** Three responsibilities collapsed into one file, and one of them has no home at all: containment (shell), presentation (design system), reporting (boot). The nine files in demo/color-picker/composables/boot/ are all called from App.vue's setup() — i.e. from inside the component tree, after the app object is gone — so app.config.errorHandler is unreachable from every module that exists. Round 1 prescribed a cure site (boot/useErrorReporting.ts) that cannot be called.

**Evidence.**

```
`find demo -name main.ts -o -name main.js` → no output. `grep -rn createApp demo/ --include=*.ts --include=*.vue --include=*.html` → only demo/color-picker/index.html:206 and :210. index.html:205-213 is the whole boot (createApp/use(router)/mount). Live: {"errorHandler":"undefined","warnHandler":"undefined","window_onerror":"object"} (i.e. null). Probe R2-C with a real app.config.errorHandler installed on a real createApp: {"probe":"R2-C","boundary_announced":true,"app_errorHandler_calls":0}.
```

**Reproduction.** find demo -name "main.ts" -o -name "main.js"  (empty) ; grep -rn "createApp" demo/ --include="*.ts" --include="*.vue" --include="*.html" ; node docs/.../probes-L-r2/live-net.mjs ; npx vitest run --config docs/.../probes-L-r2/vitest.config.ts (R2-C)

**Proposed cure.** Create demo/color-picker/main.ts (Vite's canonical entry). index.html reduces to <script type="module" src="./main.ts"></script> (the classic fouc-guard script at :159-203 is unaffected). main.ts owns what only it can own: app.config.errorHandler + window 'unhandledrejection' + window 'error' — the async half no onErrorCaptured can ever see (the matrix's one console error, `safari-desktop-light /#/: WebGL: context lost.`, is exactly that class). PaneErrorBoundary then emits `caught: [err, info]` and stops owning the decision; it never returns false.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure beneath `demo/color-session/` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The catalog of "which color spaces exist" has FOUR independent homes with 18 / 13 / 11 / 9 members. This component owns the superset and drives all four; every downstream consumer covers its shortfall with a masking fallback, an `as any`, or a `v-if`. Five of the 18 offered spaces have no `colorSpaceInfo` row; seven have no markdown doc.

**Mechanism.** Unique semantic ownership violated four ways. A label table (`PICKER_SPACE_NAMES`) sits inside a math module wedged between PICKER_CHANNELS and buildColor, so it could not be the key set per-space CONTENT is written against; every content surface therefore grew its own enumeration. Nothing in the type system relates them — one is a frozen Record, one an object literal, one a hand-written string union, one an array — so no gate can see a gap. The masking fallbacks then convert the gap into confident misinformation instead of a visible failure.

**Evidence.**

```
Homes: `demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:72` PICKER_SPACE_NAMES (17) → `color-model.ts:75` DISPLAY_COLOR_SPACE_NAMES (18, read at ColorSpaceSelector.vue:150); `demo/color-session/colorSpaceInfo.ts:18` (13); `demo/scenes/about/AboutPane.vue:79` type MarkdownSpace (11); `demo/color-session/color-space-meta.ts:26` INTERPOLATION_SPACES (9). Masks: `ColorNutritionLabel.vue:210-215` `: colorSpaceInfo.rgb`; `ConsoleRail.vue:174` `(colorSpaceInfo as any)[space]`; `AboutPane.vue:51` `v-if="activeMarkdownModule"`. Measured cross-table: srgb-linear / display-p3 / a98-rgb / prophoto-rgb / rec2020 present in PICKER_SPACE_NAMES, absent from BOTH other tables. Live page text after selecting Display P3: "About the color spaces, Display P3 … Definition: A color space based on the additive mixture of red, green, and blue light. White Point: Varies (typically D65). Gamut: Limited (device-specific). Created: 1931. Conversion Graph RGB→XYZ RGB→Kelvin RGB→HSL RGB→Hex". Screenshots: probe-display-p3-about.png (this directory) and scratchpad/after-display-p3.png (independent 2nd-seat capture).
```

**Reproduction.** `node scratchpad/repro2.mjs` — chromium 1440×900 → http://localhost:9000/#/ → click `[aria-label="Select color space"]` → click the "Display P3" option. Also reproduced independently by the first pass via scratchpad/chL-css-probe.mjs at 1600×1000. Both hosts' titles read "Display P3"; the entire nutrition card beneath reads CIE RGB 1931; the "Detailed Guide" section renders nothing (`contains 'Oh snap': false`).

**Proposed cure.** Architectural transposition, not gap-filling. (1) The LIBRARY gains the space registry it already half-owns: export from `src/subpaths/color.ts` a mapped type `SPACES: { readonly [S in SpaceId]: SpaceDescriptor<S> }` carrying `id · label · cssSerializable · channels`. A mapped type over `SpaceId` IS exhaustiveness-checked, so adding a space fails the library build until its descriptor exists; this retires PICKER_SPACE_NAMES, PICKER_CHANNELS and both CSS_*_SPACES sets. (2) The DEMO keeps exactly one product layer, `color-session/space-catalog.ts`: `DisplayColorSpace = SpaceId | "hex"` and one `Record<DisplayColorSpace, SpaceDoc>` carrying the prose and the doc loader — a Record over the same union the selector enumerates, so the 5-space and 7-space holes become COMPILE ERRORS. `colorSpaceInfo.ts`, `color-space-meta.ts`, `AboutPane.vue:79-98` and all three masks delete.

### `design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system ` · D-1 · design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)

**Defect.** Safari phone (390px): the pane title GROWS 1.62x on scroll and overflows the header band, colliding with the collapse chevron and crowding the gradient rail. The file at PaneHeader.vue:137-139 explicitly claims this band is a deliberate no-op ('degenerating to exactly 1 on phones ... the shrink self-neutralizes').

**Mechanism.** CSS-arithmetic-as-design-law. WebKit degrades the <angle> returned by atan2() to a bare <number>, and tan() then correctly reads a bare number as radians: tan(atan2(1.618rem,1.618rem)) evaluates as tan(45 radians) = 1.6197751 instead of tan(45deg) = 1. Isolates prove it is argument-specific, not a blanket bug: tan(45deg)*1000px = 1000px and tan(atan2(1px,1px))*1000px = 1000px are both CORRECT in WebKit; only the rem/clamp arm fails. The @supports gate at :177 cannot catch it — CSS.supports for atan2 returns true in WebKit.

**Evidence.**

```
PaneHeader.vue:140-142. Measured `probe-shrink-ratio.mjs`: webkit phone-390 ratioVar="1619.765625px" (=1.619766) vs chromium "1000px" (=1.000000); trueRatio (heading 25.888 / display-1 25.888) = 1. Terminal transform matrix(1.619775,...); titleInkH 27.16 -> 43.99px inside headerH 68.97px (pt-4 pb-2 = 16/8 -> 44.97px content box). Frames: shots/webkit-phone390-light-STUCK.png, shots/webkit-phone390-dark-STUCK.png.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-shrink-ratio.mjs (dev server live on :9000). Or: open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient in Safari at 390px width, scroll the pane 120px; the title enlarges.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the trig. `--pane-title-shrink-ratio: calc(var(--type-heading) / var(--type-display-1))`. Measured identical in BOTH engines at BOTH bands (618.015625px/1000 = 0.618016 at 1440; 1000px/1000 = 1.000000 at 390). <length>/<length> -> <number> is CSS Values 4 and both engines already honour it. tan(atan2(a,b)) was never an identity that needed inventing; it is contrivance (owner edict 3) with a shipped visual consequence. Preferred gestalt: cure D-4 first (two-state discrete contraction), which removes the transform entirely and dissolves the ratio question rather than patching it.

### `design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system ` · D-3 · design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)

**Defect.** The constitutive veil NEVER occludes. At its strongest state (opacity 1, the 'swell complete' the source calls O-11 gate 3), content scrolling beneath is still legible through the header — the 'Easing' section heading renders on top of the 'Gradient' title, ink on ink, in both engines and both schemes.

**Mechanism.** Material-cannot-occlude — arithmetic, not an engine quirk. Computed ::before fill is `color(srgb 0.994 0.96 0.926 / 0.65)`. opacity 1 x alpha 0.65 = 0.65 MAXIMUM coverage, so 35% of the underlying luminance transmits at every state, by construction. There is no scroll offset at which this component occludes anything; the swell only makes the window 35% naked instead of 66% naked. The gate-3 claim in the source comment is false as written.

**Evidence.**

```
PaneHeader.vue:159-162 ('the veil is near-full before any ink collision (O-11 gate 3, the F2 double-exposure cure)') and :172-176 ('RE-VERIFIED at W4-7 ... no naked window under the earliest colliders'). Measured A/B pixel difference of the 510x103 header band, content visible vs visibility:hidden, at terminalVeilOpacity=1: webkit {maxChannelDelta:235, meanChannelDelta:18.993, pctOver8:14.73, pctOver24:14.12}; chromium {maxChannelDelta:239, meanChannelDelta:21.245, pctOver8:24.63, pctOver24:16.99}. Frames: shots/webkit-leak-A-content-under-veil.png vs -leak-B-content-hidden.png; also chromium-desktop1440-light-STUCK.png, webkit-desktop1440-dark-STUCK.png, webkit-rtl-STUCK.png.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-occlusion-prm-fc.mjs — the LEAK lines. Or open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, scroll the pane past 120px, and read 'Easing' through the header.

**Proposed cure.** Make the veil a MATERIAL decision, not an opacity ramp. Rest keeps the ratified 0.52-of-0.65 breathing floor (that part is well judged). Stuck must actually occlude, which an alpha-0.65 fill cannot do at any opacity — so the stuck state needs an OPAQUE plate token, not the resting fill at opacity 1. That is a producer request through the standing glass-ui BH/BI relay (the P3 rest-floor/feather knobs are already booked; add a stuck fill). Because the stuck state then becomes static material rather than animation, this repairs D-14 and D-7 by construction, leaving nothing for the blunt PRM guard to fail to reach.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (pass 4)` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Reordering while a search filter is active silently relocates every palette the filter excluded. `onEnd` builds its id list from the FILTERED projection, and `reorderPalettes` rebuilds the store from `orderedIds` first and appends everything else at the tail — so the matches are hoisted to the head of the library and the non-matches are banished to the end.

**Mechanism.** projection-as-total-order — a partial view used to express a complete ordering

**Evidence.**

```
PalettesPane.vue:190 (`pm.filteredSaved.value.map(p => p.id)`), usePaletteStore.ts:153-167 (the two-loop rebuild with the append-the-rest tail). Live: `filtered DOM ('l') : Alpha Charlie Delta (Bravo is filtered OUT)` → `full store order : Charlie Alpha Delta Bravo` — Bravo moved from index 1 to index 3 without being touched. Offline harness gives the identical result.
```

**Reproduction.** `node .../repro-C2-live.mjs` section (b), and `npx vite-node .../repro-C1-sortable.ts` section C-2. Pass 3 declined to re-run this; measured live for the first time this pass.

**Proposed cure.** A projection cannot express a total order. Either map filtered indices back onto the full order before writing (reorderPalettes should take a complete order, or a (fromId, beforeId) pair), or — the KISS reading, and what every list app does — disable the sortable while a query is active.

PaletteCardMenu.vue:108 `<DropdownMenuSubTrigger class="gap-2 cursor-pointer" @click.prevent>`. reka guard: node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Menu/MenuSubTrigger.js `onClick: async (event) => { if (props.disabled || event.defaultPrevented) return; … }`. Only sub-trigger in the demo: `grep -rn DropdownMenuSubTrigger demo --include=*.vue` → PaletteCardMenu.vue:108/111/188 only.
