### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (PalettesPane, pass` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The FIRST drag-reorder after every page load silently scrambles the entire persisted palette library. `useSortable(sortableEl, pm.filteredSaved.value, …)` passes the computed's LIVE CACHED array (with an empty query `useFilteredList` returns `items.value` by identity, and `savedPalettes` is a `.filter()` computed). VueUse's default `onUpdate` is NOT displaced by the supplied `onEnd`, so `moveArrayElement` splices that same array in place (synchronous removal, `nextTick` re-insert); SortableJS dispatches `update` BEFORE `end`; the component's `onEnd` then re-reads `pm.filteredSaved.value` — now n−1 with the dragged item missing — and splices it by the ORIGINAL DOM indices before persisting via `reorderPalettes`.

**Mechanism.** aliased-derived-value mutation — a read-only computed's cached array handed to a library that owns and mutates its list, with two writers (library default onUpdate + component onEnd) racing across one Sortable event sequence

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:183 + :187-196; useFilteredList.ts:10; usePaletteStore.ts:51-55; node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js:14-16,23-26,82-90; node_modules/sortablejs/modular/sortable.esm.js:2002-2008 (update) then :2023-2027 (end). LIVE headless Chromium (PPC-probe1.mjs / PPC-probe2.mjs): `P1 store BEFORE : Alpha Beta Gamma Delta` / `P1 store AFTER  : Gamma Delta Beta Alpha` / `P1 EXPECTED (drag idx0 -> idx2): Beta Gamma Alpha Delta` / `P1 pageErrors: 0`. Second instance, 6 palettes, drag 0→1: `I after warm-up drag: Gamma Beta Delta Zed1 Zed2 Alpha` — both exactly as the mechanism predicts. CONTROL proving aliasing is the cause: force one store write first so the computed recomputes a new array, and the identical gesture is correct — `P2 store AFTER : Beta Gamma Alpha Delta Zeta  == EXPECTED`. Same-session sequence: `A t1 (1st drag 0->2): Gamma Delta Beta Alpha` WRONG, `A t2` and `A t3` correct.
```

**Reproduction.** Seed localStorage["color-palettes"] with 4 local palettes, load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, do NOT type in the search box, drag card 0's `.drag-handle` onto card 2 with real mouse down/move/up. Store order becomes `Gamma Delta Beta Alpha` instead of `Beta Gamma Alpha Delta`. Repeat the same drag: correct from the 2nd onward.

**Proposed cure.** Stop handing Sortable a derived list at all — it can never satisfy the library's "I own and mutate this list" contract, as a value OR as a ref. Call `useSortable(sortableEl, [], { handle, animation, ghostClass, onUpdate(evt){ … } })` and own the move explicitly in `onUpdate` (the hook the library reserves for the reorder), translating the DOM move into a move over `pm.savedPalettes.value` and passing the FULL id list to `reorderPalettes`. `onEnd` is a lifecycle notification, not a mutation site; doing the work there while leaving `onUpdate` at its default is what created two writers to one array.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/palettes/br` · C-23 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** MiniColorPicker (the subject's only child) latches its drag flags `canvasDragging`/`hueDragging` to true on pointerdown and clears them ONLY on pointerup. There is no `pointercancel` or `lostpointercapture` handler. After a cancelled touch gesture the drag never ends, and subsequent plain hover moves (buttons=0) keep driving the colour — which propagates through `update:hex` into SearchFilterBar's `pickerHex` AND `colorText`, so the colour that the next Search press actually searches changes because the pointer moved.

**Mechanism.** Pointer-session state cleared by one of its terminators instead of by the session; hand-rolled duplicate of an in-tree component that already solves it.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/search/MiniColorPicker.vue:126-137 (and :143-149 for the hue strip). Measured, probes/probe-C-r4-6.mjs → evidence-r4/probeC-r4-6.json: "stuckDrag": { beforeTouch "#7e93a4", midTouch "#9badbb", afterCancel "#9badbb", afterHoverOnly "#000509", dragStuckAfterCancel true } with CONTROL "control": { base "#a7b7c4", after "#a7b7c4", changed false }. `grep -nE "pointercancel|lostpointercapture|releasePointerCapture" MiniColorPicker.vue` → no matches, while `grep -rn "pointercancel\|lostpointercapture" demo/` returns 5 other sites including demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue:18-19 — the same SV-canvas widget, with both handlers.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probes/probe-C-r4-6.mjs against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000 — no fixture. Sequence: open /#/browse → click ⋮ Filters → click the swatch → CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent touchStart(12,12) → touchMove(30,30) → touchCancel[] → then eleven page.mouse.move across the canvas with no button held. Colour moves #9badbb → #000509. Control: identical eleven hover moves after a clean pointerup → unchanged.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the hand-rolled pointer machine rather than patching it: either consume demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue (already correct, already in-tree) or express the drag with @vueuse/core (already a dependency — glass-ui's own Input uses useVModel) so the flag is owned by the pointer session. If the hand-rolled form is kept, @pointerup, @pointercancel and @lostpointercapture must all clear it, with `e.buttons !== 0` in updateCanvas as the belt.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/palettes/br` · C-24 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `onPickerHexUpdate` writes BOTH `pickerHex` and `colorText` unconditionally on every `update:hex`, and MiniColorPicker emits that from a `watch` on a `computed` — i.e. once per reactive tick of a drag, not once at commit. The user's typed query is silently destroyed by touching the picker. There is no history and the picker has no cancel.

**Mechanism.** One ref serving two disagreeing roles (user query vs. swatch readout); a live writeback loop with no authored-text guard.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:175-178 (`colorText.value = hex`) bound at :70; MiniColorPicker.vue:105 `watch(currentHex, (hex) => emit("update:hex", hex))`. Measured, evidence-r4/probeC-r4-2.json: "clobber": { typed "rebeccapurple", beforeDrag "rebeccapurple", afterDrag "#081f33", clobbered true }. Rate measured at evidence-r4/probeC-r4-3.json "churn": 41 emissions for 41 pointermoves.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probes/probe-C-r4-2.mjs — no fixture. Open /#/browse → ⋮ → fill the colour field with `rebeccapurple` → click the swatch → one SV-canvas drag. Field reads `#081f33`.

**Proposed cure.** Split the two roles. `pickerHex` is the picker's value (swatch + picker bind to it); `colorText` is the user's query, written by the user and by `applyColorSearchFromPicker` (:180-187) only — that is the explicit commit where overwriting is the user's own instruction. Delete the single line `colorText.value = hex;` from `onPickerHexUpdate`. This also deletes 41 of the 41 spurious writes behind C-30.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/palettes/br` · P4-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** With one palette card's dropdown open, the neighbouring cards' identical `⋯` menu triggers fall inside the open menu's item rows and are not the hit target at their own coordinates. Card N+1's trigger centre lands on `Publish`; card N+2's lands on `Delete`. Clicking them activates those items on card N — destroying or publishing a palette the user was not pointing at.

**Mechanism.** Geometric congruence between a repeated-row list and the menu it spawns, compounded by a modal layer. The card list pitch (112 px) is a near-multiple of the menu item pitch (44 px) with the menu top 22.4 px below the trigger centre, so offsets 112 and 224 land 19.5 px and 9.5 px from item centres; the last item is the destructive one. reka's `modal: true` default puts `pointer-events: none` on `<body>`, so the covered triggers cannot absorb their own clicks (`triggerComputedPE "none"`, `triggerIsTopMost false`) and the topmost hit target is the menu item. Neither number that produces the collision appears in the source file — it exists only when the component is rendered beside copies of itself, which is the only way it is ever rendered.

**Evidence.**

```
probe evidence/pass-4/pcm-p4-c.mjs, /#/palettes, 1440x900, 6 seeded palettes. `::C1_collisionMap` → cardPitch 112, itemPitch 44, menuRect {x 1010, y 516, w 192, h 240.1}; items Publish[564.1,608.1] Rename[608.1,652.1] Export[661.1,705.1] Delete[705.1,749.1]; trigger centres card0 (1184,493.6) landsOnItem null, card1 (1184,605.6) landsOnItem "Publish" elementFromPoint "div{menuitem}", card2 (1184,717.6) landsOnItem "Delete" elementFromPoint "div{menuitem}". `::C3_afterClickOnThatTrigger` after clicking (1184,717.6) → store ["Probe Palette 1".."Probe Palette 5"], cards 5, dialogs 0 — "Probe Palette 0" destroyed. `::C4_control_afterClick` same coordinates with no menu open → store unchanged, menus 1, openOwner "Probe Palette 3". probe pcm-p4-d.mjs `::D2_determinism` → 3 runs, storeBefore/After 8→7, 7→6, 6→5, removed ["Probe Palette 0"],["Probe Palette 1"],["Probe Palette 2"], dialogs 0, undoAffordance {hasUndoText false, hasRestore false}. probe pcm-p4-f.mjs `::F1_clickPoint {cx 1184, cy 605.6, itemAtPoint "Publish"}` and `::F2_afterStrayClick` → card 0 text "Probe Palette 0 2 Failed to create session", h 100→128, while the pointer was over card 1. probe pcm-p4-e.mjs `::E1_summary {cards 8, openingsWithACoveredTrigger 8, openingsThatCoverDelete 4, distinctCoveredItems ["Publish","Delete","Export"]}`; mobile `::E2_summary {cards 8, openingsWithACoveredTrigger 2, openingsThatCoverDelete 2, cardPitch 130}`. Visibility: probe pcm-p4-d.mjs `::D1_coveredTriggerVisibility` on the identical 36x36 rect {x 1166,y 700} → closed inRectContrast 7.85, openUnderMenu 1.72, pixelsChangedGt8 366/1296, maxLumDelta 157.7. Source levers: PaletteCardMenu.vue:2 (no `:modal`), :7 (`align="end"`, no side/align offset, no collision-padding), :133-140 (`Delete` last, unconfirmed).
```

**Reproduction.** 1. `pnpm dev` (server live at http://localhost:9000). 2. `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/evidence/pass-4/pcm-p4-c.mjs`. Manually: seed localStorage `color-palettes` with >=3 local palettes, open /#/palettes at 1440x900, click the first card's `⋯`, then click the THIRD card's `⋯` at its own centre. The first palette is deleted with no confirmation.

**Proposed cure.** Do not fix by geometry — any bottom-anchored menu in a repeated-row list covers the rows beneath it; changing the offset only relocates which item lands on the trigger. Two architectural changes, which together also discharge P4-2, P4-4, P4-5, C2-14 and C2-15: (a) destructive actions in a per-row menu are CONFIRMED — route `delete`/`adminDelete` through the glass-ui `AlertDialog` naming the palette (the admin path already is; the owner path is the outlier), so a stray activation costs a dismissal rather than a palette; and treat `publish` (a real remote write, PaletteCard.vue:295) the same way. (b) `:modal="false"` on PaletteCardMenu.vue:2, so neighbouring triggers stay hit-testable and reka's `onPointerDownOutside` turns the cross-row gesture into "close this menu, open that one" instead of "activate an item".

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/palettes/Pa` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Drag-to-reorder inside a search-filtered view silently reorders the entire persisted library, not just the visible subset.

**Mechanism.** A projection (the filtered list) is passed to an API whose contract is a total order; the store's append-the-rest branch then relocates every untouched palette.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:187-196 (`const ids = pm.filteredSaved.value.map(p => p.id)` → `pm.reorderPalettes(ids)`) + demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:153-167 (`reorderPalettes` emits orderedIds first, then APPENDS every palette not in the list). Live headless-Chromium repro output: `C. store order BEFORE drag: Alpha Beta Gamma Delta Zed-one Zed-two` / `visible under q='zed': ["Zed-one3","Zed-two3"]` / `D. store order AFTER drag: Zed-two Zed-one Alpha Beta Gamma Delta` / `E. rendered order with q cleared: ["Zed-two3","Zed-one3","Alpha3","Beta3","Gamma3","Delta3"]`. Node harness transcribing both functions: `BEFORE: alpha beta gamma delta zed-one zed-two` → `AFTER (clear q): zed-two zed-one alpha beta gamma delta`.
```

**Reproduction.** Seed localStorage['color-palettes'] with 6 local palettes; open http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; type `zed` in the pane SearchBar; mouse-drag the second visible card's `.drag-handle` above the first; clear the search box. The 4 non-matching palettes have moved from positions 1-4 to 3-6 and the new order is persisted.

**Proposed cure.** A drag is a gesture over a total order; a filtered list is a projection — stop conflating them. KISS answer: withdraw the drag affordance while a filter is active (`:draggable="!pm.searchQuery.value"` on PaletteCard plus `option('disabled', …)` on the sortable). Richer answer: translate the projection move into the base order — locate the dragged id and its target neighbour in `pm.savedPalettes.value`, splice there, and pass the FULL id list.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (CurrentPaletteEditor.v` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Data loss: `confirmUpdatePalette` commits an unvalidated, never-revalidated target. Proven twice — renaming after the duplicate banner appears overwrites the palette matched by the OLD name, and emptying the buffer then pressing Update wipes an existing palette's colours to [].

**Mechanism.** M2 — deferred mutation whose target is captured at detection time and committed at click time, with the intervening state never re-checked (TOCTOU on a UI intent). No confirmation, no undo, no announcement.

**Evidence.**

```
CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:267-276 — only guard is `if (id == null) return`; `duplicateTarget` (:241) is set once at collision detection and never invalidated on name change or buffer change; contrast the emptiness guard at :248 in saveCurrentPalette. usePaletteStore.ts:106 assigns whatever it is handed. Probe (a): pre-seeded {id:"pre-existing-id",name:"Dup Test",colors:["#111111"]} → after renaming the field and pressing Update: "afterUpdate":[{"id":"pre-existing-id","name":"Dup Test","colors":["oklch(50% 0.1 200deg)","oklch(90% 0.05 100deg)"]}] (#111111 destroyed). Probe (b): "before":[{"name":"Victim","colors":["#111111","#222222","#333333"]}] → "after":[{"name":"Victim","colors":[]}], with the well simultaneously rendering "Start a new palette | \"Victim\" already exists. | Update | Cancel".
```

**Reproduction.** node .../cpe-challenge-c-probe2.mjs (`afterUpdate`) and node .../cpe-challenge-c-probe4.mjs (`before`/`afterRemoveAll`/`after`).

**Proposed cure.** Delete the `duplicateTarget` ref. Derive the collision: `const duplicate = computed(() => savedColorStrings.length ? savedPalettes.find(p => p.name.toLowerCase() === effectiveName.value.toLowerCase()) : undefined)` and gate the confirm on `duplicate.value` at commit time. The banner then vanishes the instant the name or buffer stops justifying it, and Update is structurally incapable of addressing a palette the visible label does not name; the three manual `= null` resets (:163, :263, :274) disappear with it.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (PaletteSlugBar.vue)` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `@submit.prevent="onSlugSwitch"` binds to glass-ui SearchBar, which declares `inheritAttrs: false` and spreads non-class $attrs onto its inner `<input>`, not the `<form>` root. **Evidence.**

```
PaletteSlugBar.vue:5-15; node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/search.js:309 `inheritAttrs: !1` and :327-341 (root gets only class + data-surface; `o.value` = $attrs-minus-class is spread onto the `b("input", w({ref_key:"inputRef"...}, o.value, ...))`). Live measurement: URL before `http://localhost:9000/#/extract` → after clicking the type=submit button `http://localhost:9000/?#/extract` (Playwright: "Execution context was destroyed, most likely because of a navigation"); sessionStorage.PROBE_SWITCH === null. Navigation-safe rerun: formVei null, inputVei null, eventsAfterSubmit [].
```

**Reproduction.** Mount the unmodified SFC into the live dev page via Vite /@fs, click Login, type a slug, click the submit Button — the page navigates (a `?` is appended to the URL) and the switchSlug emit never fires.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (SearchFilterBar.vue, a` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Tag-filter checkboxes bound to `:checked` / `@update:checked`, which glass-ui 7.0.0's Checkbox does not expose (contract is `modelValue` / `update:modelValue`). `:checked` degrades to a dead DOM attribute, `@update:checked` listens for an event never emitted, and the component runs uncontrolled — so it visibly toggles and flips aria-checked to "true" while `update:selectedTags` never fires and nothing filters. The prop-driven initial state is also ignored (a selected tag renders unchecked).

**Mechanism.** prop/emit-name drift against a major design-system upgrade (glass-ui 7.0.0, W44 whole-major adoption) left unbound because vue-tsc runs with strictTemplates defaulted OFF, so unknown props/handlers fall through as attrs

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55. Contract: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/checkbox/Checkbox.vue.d.ts (CheckboxProps has modelValue/defaultValue/disabled/value/id/class — no `checked`); compiled component node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.js:451 `emits: ["update:modelValue"]`. Measured (vitest+@vue/test-utils mount of the real SFC): rendered HTML `<button data-slot="checkbox" checked="false" role="checkbox" aria-checked="false" data-state="unchecked">`; `emitted after click: ["click"]`, `update:selectedTags = undefined`; `before click data-state: unchecked aria-checked: false` -> `after click data-state: checked aria-checked: true` with `update:selectedTags emitted: undefined`; with props selectedTags=['a','b'], `checkbox aria-checked: [ 'false', 'false' ]`. Family: `grep -rn "<Checkbox" demo/` returns exactly 2 sites — SearchFilterBar.vue:51 and TagEditPopover.vue:27 — and `grep -rn "update:checked|:checked=" demo/` shows both miswired (SearchFilterBar.vue:52-53, TagEditPopover.vue:28-29).
```

**Reproduction.** npx vitest run --config <scratch>/probe.config.ts with a mount of demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue (Popover/PopoverTrigger/PopoverContent stubbed open, availableTags=[{name:'warm'}]): click `[data-slot="checkbox"]` -> data-state flips unchecked->checked and aria-checked false->true, while w.emitted()['update:selectedTags'] is undefined. Latent in prod only because `curl -s https://api.color.babb.dev/colors/tags` returns `[]` (HTTP 200), hiding the section via v-if at line 47; e2e/smoke/admin/flows/tag-create.spec.ts creates tags on every run.

**Proposed cure.** Bind the real contract: `:model-value="selectedTags.includes(tag.name)" @update:model-value="() => toggleTag(tag.name)"` (toggleTag already derives the next array from the prop, so the CheckedState payload is discardable); same repair at TagEditPopover.vue:28-29 where the payload IS used — `(checked) => onToggle(tag.name, checked === true)`. The gestalt cure is architectural, not per-site: set `"vueCompilerOptions": { "strictTemplates": true }` in tsconfig.base.json so the whole prop/emit-drift class becomes a compile error instead of silent runtime breakage.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (SearchFilterBar.vue, a` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The "Find by Color" text field is decorative. Everything outside `/^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i` — 3-digit hex, 8-digit hex, hsl()/oklch(), named colours, whitespace, outright garbage — is silently discarded and replaced by `pickerHex.value` (default `#4488cc`), after which the component sets colorSearchActive=true, increments the filter badge and emits, reporting success for a colour the user never asked for. The placeholder advertises the capability it drops (`placeholder="#hex, hsl(...)"`).

**Mechanism.** masking fallback — a validity guard that substitutes a plausible wrong value for the error it should raise (owner edict 2: no masking fallbacks), gratuitously narrowing a stack that already parses full CSS L4

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:213-225 (the ternary at line 218), placeholder line 92, pickerHex default line 170. Measured emissions, all bit-identical: `hsl(120 100% 50%)` -> [0.61358428709272,-0.04147814390571797,-0.11751090263911201]; `#f00` -> same; `not-a-color` -> same; `"   "` -> same; and `oklab(#4488cc) = [0.61358428709272,-0.04147814390571797,-0.11751090263911201]` — exact match. Control `#ff0000` -> [0.6279553639214311,0.2248630684262744,0.125846277330585] (correct). The correct answers the guard threw away, measured through the SAME function: `oklab(hsl(120 100% 50%)) = [0.8664396175234368,-0.23388758093655815,0.1794984451609376]`, `oklab(#f00) = [0.6279553639214311,0.2248630684262744,0.125846277330585]`. The parser is fully capable: SearchFilterBar.vue:206 -> demo/color-session/color-utils.ts:11 -> demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:109-113 (parseCssColor), which throws a typed PickerColorError on real failure (picker-color.ts:112) — the exact error signal the component discards.
```

**Reproduction.** Mount SearchFilterBar (Popover stubbed open), `input[type=text].setValue('hsl(120 100% 50%)')` then `.trigger('keydown.enter')` -> emitted colorSearch payload is the OKLab of #4488cc, not of green. Repeat with '#f00', 'not-a-color', '   ' — identical payload each time; '#ff0000' is the only shape that works.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the regex and the fallback. Parse the trimmed text directly (rename hexToOklab -> cssToOklab, since it was never hex-only); on empty input or PickerColorError set a local `parseError` and DO NOT emit; render parseError into the polite aria-live region C-6 already requires. Net KISS deletion: one regex and one fallback out, one honest error branch in.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/palettes/brows` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The swatch is not an interactive element: glass-ui 7.0.0 `WatercolorDot` declares `inheritAttrs:false` and re-applies only `attrs.class`/`attrs.style`, so `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click.stop` — plus everything reka's `PopoverTrigger as-child` grafts on — are silently discarded onto a hardcoded `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">`. The touch popover therefore never opens, `onSwatchClick`/`onPopoverUpdateTouch` are unreachable code, and the swatches are invisible to assistive tech.

**Mechanism.** Silent prop/listener drop across a component boundary — `inheritAttrs:false` with a partial attrs re-application, consumed as if it were a polymorphic `as`/`tag` component. No type or template gate is aimed at unknown props on a producer component.

**Evidence.**

```
Producer source `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js`: `inheritAttrs:!1`, props `{color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed}` (no `tag`), render `o("span",{"aria-hidden":"true", …, style:u([f.value,{…,pointerEvents:"none",…}])})`. Consumers: SwatchHoverMenu.vue:14-20 and :29-36. iPhone-13 emulation (`matchMedia("(hover: hover)")` → false), expanded card, tap swatch centre → `{"rekaPopover":0,"floatingPanel":false,"addBtn":false}`. Desktop toggle-close proof: with the panel open, clicking the swatch left it open (`desktop.panelAfterClickWhileOpen: true`) — `useHoverPopover.ts:51-54 onSwatchClick` never ran.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe5.mjs — read `touch.popoverOpen`, `touch.triggerDom`, `desktop.panelAfterClickWhileOpen`. Requires an isolated vite with VITE_API_URL set (the :9000 server latches `misconfigured` and never fetches).

**Proposed cure.** Semantics belong to the consumer, not the decoration: `SwatchHoverMenu` renders its own `<button type="button" :aria-label>` and mounts `<WatercolorDot>` inside it as pure decoration — its `aria-hidden` and `pointer-events:none` then become correct by construction. One element, one file, no new producer prop. A polymorphic `tag` belongs in glass-ui (edict 4) only if genuinely wanted; KISS says do not buy back with a producer prop what a wrapping `<button>` gives free.

**Defect.** The card's primary action (expand/collapse — the only route to the swatches, the slug and every per-colour affordance) is mouse-only: a `<div role="article">` with `@click`, `cursor-pointer`, no `tabindex`, no `@keydown`, no `aria-expanded`. WCAG 2.1.1 Level A.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/palettes/browse` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The "Find by Color" text field is decorative. `applyColorSearch` masks every input that is not an exact 6-digit hex — 3-digit hex, 8-digit hex, hsl(), oklch(), named colours, whitespace, the empty string, outright garbage — replacing it with `pickerHex.value` (default #4488cc), then setting `colorSearchActive = true` and emitting. The badge increments and the wall filters, so the user is shown a SUCCESSFUL search for a colour they never asked for. The placeholder advertises the capability it discards (`placeholder="#hex, hsl(...)"`).

**Mechanism.** A masking fallback substituted for an error path: a narrowing regex in front of a parser that is already total, with the rejection routed to a silent default instead of to the user. The component has no error surface at all, which is why the fallback exists and why it cannot be fixed by deleting the regex alone.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:213-225, the ternary `const hex = text.startsWith("#") && /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i.test(text) ? text : pickerHex.value;` (line 218) — a masking fallback, a direct violation of owner edict 2. LIVE (probes/probe-C2.mjs, evidence/probeC2.json): typed `totally-not-a-color`, clicked Search -> {"badgeText":"1", "fieldStillReads":"totally-not-a-color", "swatchLabel":"Open color picker, current color #4488cc", "errorTextPresent":false, "clearAllPresent":true}. The guard is also unnecessary: hexToOklab (line 205) calls parseColorIn -> demo/color-session/color-utils.ts:11 -> parsePickerColor -> parseCssColor (demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:109-113), which parses all of the rejected inputs correctly and throws a typed PickerColorError on genuine failure (picker-color.ts:112) — the exact signal a 'no such colour' affordance needs, discarded.
```

**Reproduction.** cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probes/probe-C2.mjs ; read the `garbageSearch` key. By hand: open http://localhost:9000/#/browse, click the Filters button, type `hsl(120 100% 50%)` into the colour field, press Enter — the wall filters against #4488cc and the badge reads 1.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the regex and the fallback; parse the text and surface the failure. `const text = colorText.value.trim(); if (!text) { parseError.value = "Enter a colour."; return; } try { const {L,a,b} = cssToOklab(text); parseError.value = null; colorSearchActive.value = true; emit("colorSearch", L, a, b); } catch (e) { parseError.value = e instanceof PickerColorError ? "Not a CSS colour." : "Search failed."; }` — with parseError rendered into the aria-live region C-8 independently requires. Net: one regex and one fallback out, one honest branch in. Rename hexToOklab -> cssToOklab (see C-13); it was never hex-only.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation interrogation (pass 4) of demo/` · C4-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Under prefers-reduced-motion the expand/collapse state machine never completes: inline height/opacity/transition are frozen permanently and the swatch subtree is NEVER removed from the DOM on collapse.

**Mechanism.** A JS-driven height morph gates Vue's transition done() on `transitionend` with propertyName==="height"; the app's own PRM policy rewrites transition-property to a five-property allow-list that excludes height, so the event can never fire, done() is never called, and onAfterEnter/onAfterLeave never run.

**Evidence.**

```
probe-C4d-pass4-results.json (PRM): computed transitionProperty = "opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow"; captured transition events touching the panel = [["run","opacity","overflow-hidden v-enter-"],["end","opacity","overflow-hidden v-enter-"]] — no height event of any kind; panelInline 2s later = "height: 127px; opacity: 1; transition: height 350ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), opacity 350ms;". probe-C4c-pass4-results.json: C_prm.afterCollapse {panelPresent:true, inlineStyle:"height: 0px; …", scrollH:182, swatchCount:24} vs C_no-prm.afterCollapse {panelPresent:false}. probe-C4e-pass4-results.json: expand+collapse 6 cards → no-prm 608→608 totalDomNodes; prm 607→1628 (+1021, +168%), swatchPanels 6, zeroHeightPanels 6, swatchNodes 4→148. Source: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHeightTransition.ts:30-39 and :59-71; policy: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/utilities/a11y-overrides.css @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) *:not([data-allow-motion]) { transition-property: opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow !important } imported at demo/styles/foundation.css:56.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCard/probe-C4c-pass4.mjs (and probe-C4e-pass4.mjs) against http://localhost:9000 — seeds {version:1,palettes:[…]} into localStorage['color-palettes'], loads /#/palettes in a chromium context with reducedMotion:'reduce', clicks a card to expand, clicks again to collapse, waits 2.5s and reads the panel node. Manual: enable Reduce Motion in the OS, open /#/palettes, expand then collapse a palette card, inspect the card — the swatch panel div is still present with inline height:0px.

**Proposed cure.** Delete useHeightTransition.ts and its wiring; render the swatch panel with the demo's existing CSS transition family `<Transition name="vj-morph">` plus --vj-morph-collapse/--vj-morph-expanded (demo/styles/animations.css:103-135) — the very family the same file already uses twelve lines above for the rename row (PaletteCard.vue:112-120, .rename-morph at :358-363). A CSS-declared family is neutralised correctly by the PRM guard by design; a JS one is silently disarmed by it. Also retires the repo's own 'a fourth family name is a defect' law violation (animations.css:60-80).

### `CHALLENGE-C · implementation audit of `demo/palettes/BrowseP` · P-2 · CHALLENGE-C · implementation audit of `demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue` (pass 3, independent re-run against the REAL production commons)

**Defect.** The browse search composes two mutually incompatible predicates and hands over between them at 2 characters, so typing the second character of a word empties the commons and renders the "the commons is empty, go publish one" invitation.

**Mechanism.** Two engines answering one question, composed in series. A length threshold SWAPS which engine answers, and the two engines disagree about what a match is (substring vs whole-word/stem, name+slug vs name-only, untrimmed vs trimmed). The composition is an intersection of disagreeing predicates, and the intersection is usually empty.

**Evidence.**

```
Client predicate: demo/palettes/useFilteredList.ts:8-12 (untrimmed, any length) + demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:43-45 (`p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || p.slug.includes(q)`), rendered at BrowsePane.vue:340 (its only consumer in the tree). Server predicate: useBrowsePalettes.ts:52-61 (`q.trim()`, sent only when `length >= 2`) → api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:95-96 (`f.$text = {$search: q}`) → api/src/platform/db/db.ts:57-60 (`createIndex({name:"text"})` — WORD/stem matching on `name` only). Measured live (probe-C3/probe-c3-live-proxy.mjs, real production commons, 10 public palettes incl. `Ocean Depths`): typed `o` → request `/palettes?limit=50&sort=newest` (no q) → 3 cards; `oc` → `…&q=oc` → 0 cards + "No published palettes here yet."; `oce` → 0; `ocea` → 0; `ocean` → `…&q=ocean` → 1 card; cleared → 10 cards. Server side confirmed independently: `curl "https://api.color.babb.dev/palettes?limit=50&sort=newest&q=oc"` → 0 rows; `…&q=ocean` → 1 row ['Ocean Depths']. Trim divergence measured: `' o'` → server sends NO q (trims to 1 char) → 10 rows returned → client filters `name.includes(" o")` → 0 cards + true-empty invitation.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe-C3/probe-c3-live-proxy.mjs — the `perKeystroke` array is printed unconditionally. Manually: type `oc` into "Search the commons…" against any reachable backend. Frame: probe-C3/c3-cliff-at-oc.png.

**Proposed cure.** One predicate, one place. EITHER the server owns search — delete `filteredBrowse` outright, render `remotePalettes` directly, and replace `$text` with a prefix-capable matcher (anchored name+slug regex or an Atlas autocomplete index), because `$text` structurally cannot answer a type-ahead — OR the client owns it and `q` never goes on the wire. What cannot stand is a length threshold that swaps engines. Same fix as C-6/P-4: the colour seam wants to move server-side by the same move.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (component: demo/palettes/browser/slug/` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The login form cannot submit. `@submit.prevent="onSlugSwitch"` is bound to the inner `<input type="search">`, not the `<form>`, because glass-ui 7.0.0's SearchBar is `inheritAttrs: false` and spreads $attrs onto its input. The `<form>` has no submit listener, so nothing calls preventDefault and a real browser performs an unprevented native form submission (GET to the current URL) that reloads the SPA and discards the typed slug.

**Mechanism.** producer-contract misuse — SearchBar is a field, not a form host, but accepts tag="form" without objecting, so a consumer's @submit silently relocates onto an element that can never fire that event; `onSubmit` is a legal fall-through attr so typechecking cannot catch it

**Evidence.**

```
Producer source, node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/search.js SearchBar: `inheritAttrs: !1` … `b("input", w({ ref_key:"inputRef", ref:s, type:"search" }, o.value, {...}))` where `o` = $attrs minus class. Probe output (probes/submit.test.ts, probes/submit2.test.ts): `[dom] form attrs = data-v-e6a0327e,class,data-surface` / `[dom] input attrs = type,placeholder,class,value` / `[A] submit on <form> -> switchSlug emitted = null` / `[B] submit on <input> -> switchSlug emitted = [["brave-amber-quiet-fox",false]]` / `[btn0] type="submit" aria-label="Sign in with slug"` `[slot] buttons render inside <form>? = 2` / `Error: Not implemented: HTMLFormElement.prototype.requestSubmit` / `[click] switchSlug emitted = null` / `[click] slugEditMode still true = true`. Source: PaletteSlugBar.vue:5-15.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vitest run --testTimeout=60000 --config probes/vitest.config.ts probes/submit.test.ts — dispatch a real cancelable `submit` Event on the rendered <form>: switchSlug is NOT emitted. Dispatch the same event on the <input>: it IS emitted. Then probes/submit2.test.ts clicks the genuine type="submit" button and switchSlug stays unemitted with edit mode still open.

**Proposed cure.** Two altitudes. Producer (glass-ui BH/BI relay per the standing edict): SearchBar must either refuse tag="form" or route non-input listeners to its root. Consumer: a credential entry is not a search field at all — the Account Dialog should own a real `<form @submit.prevent>` around a real `<input autocomplete=…>`, exactly the idiom SlugEditLayer.vue:76-100 already ships correctly.

**Mechanism.** Three stacked: (1) the consumer's `tag="button"` prop is a no-op in glass-ui 7.0.0, which renders a `<span>` — a glass-6 API dropped in the glass-7 adoption with no compile-time or runtime signal (same class as the dead .cartoon-cast and --card-press-t); (2) `inheritAttrs:false` swallows the consumer's aria-label and the producer stamps aria-hidden; (3) inline pointer-events:none kills the swatch's own @click, so onSwatchClick and the touch-toggle path are dead code. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (PaletteCard, six-file folder + its gri` · D3-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** MT-F036(a) root mechanism located: the hard-edged shadow slab is a PAINT-CONTAINMENT CLIP in PaletteCardGrid, not a shadow token in PaletteCard. Every card loses its left facet; the last card also loses its bottom facet.

**Mechanism.** `contain: content` = `layout paint style`; paint containment clips descendants to the padding box. The grid has zero padding and the card is exactly grid-width, so the -7px left facet begins 7px outside the clip and the last card's +7px bottom facet ends 7px outside it. A component drew a decoration its own container is contractually forbidden from painting, and no gate noticed.

**Evidence.**

```

```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCard/probe-D5b.mjs, then compare evidence/p3-corner-clip-ON.png with p3-corner-clip-OFF.png

**Proposed cure.** Do NOT cure by deleting the containment (that inverts the priority: performance vs decoration). Land the canon-frozen tuple `{size:sm, material:content, tier:quiet, surface:opaque, shadow:false, grain:false, specular:off}` (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1; §7 'matte specimen slips … not cartoon casters'; PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05 terminal verb REMOVE). With shadow:false the clip has nothing to clip and the artefact is structurally impossible — no producer change needed for this half.

Run docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D3-pcm.mjs.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (PaletteCardMenu.vue)` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The Export submenu cannot be opened by touch: `@click.prevent` on DropdownMenuSubTrigger defeats reka-ui's only touch open path, so all five export formats are unreachable on every touch device.

**Mechanism.** Vue's `.prevent` modifier compiles to a no-op handler wrapped in withModifiers(['prevent']) that calls event.preventDefault() before reka's handler runs. Reka opens submenus from three paths — onPointermove (hover), onKeydown, onClick. A touch pointer produces no pointermove, so onClick is its only path, and it early-returns on defaultPrevented. Desktop hover opens the submenu first, entirely masking the defect from the desktop matrix.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteCardMenu.vue:108 `<DropdownMenuSubTrigger class="gap-2 cursor-pointer" @click.prevent>`; node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Menu/MenuSubTrigger.js:131-140 `onClick: async (event) => { if (props.disabled || event.defaultPrevented) return; ... menuContext.onOpenChange(true) }`. probe-D4-results.json touchTap (iPhone 14, hasTouch:true, real tap()): before/afterTap1/afterTap2 all `subContentPresent: false, ariaExpanded: "false"`, afterTap1 `dataState: "closed"`. Same-context control: `nonCancelableClick: { subContentPresent: true, ariaExpanded: "true" }`. probe-D5-results.json instrumented tail: both pointer modes end `click` with `defaultPrevented: true`; desktop has a preceding pointermove and opens, touch has none and stays closed. Witness: evidence/touch-tap-export-subtrigger.png.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D4-pcm.mjs (or probe-D5-pcm.mjs) against the live dev server at :9000. Open the card menu with tap(), then tap() the 'Export' row twice — aria-expanded stays "false".

**Proposed cure.** Delete the `@click.prevent` modifier at :108. It carries no handler, no comment, and buys nothing — the card's click is already stopped by the `@click.stop` wrapper at PaletteCard.vue:82. This is shipping breakage that should not wait for the D-1 transposition.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (PaletteCardMenu.vue)` · D-4 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The `misconfigured` availability arm is unhandled: `apiOffline` tests only `=== "unavailable"` of a four-state enum, so the menu renders Publish enabled and undecorated while the app's own status lamp reads 'DEV MISCONFIGURED — RUN `NPM RUN DEV`'.

**Mechanism.** A four-state enum was consumed by a boolean predicate; three of the four arms fall through to the fully-optimistic render, including the one arm the availability module explicitly designed to fail loud.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteCardMenu.vue:217 `const apiOffline = computed(() => availability.value === "unavailable");` vs demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:40-45 `export type ApiAvailability = "unknown" | "available" | "unavailable" | "misconfigured";` and availability.ts:29-35 ('enter a DISTINCT, designed `misconfigured` state that fails LOUD (never the generic degraded affordance)'). evidence/desktop-light-menu-open.png shows the DockStatusLamp rendering `● DEV MISCONFIGURED — RUN 'NPM RUN DEV'` in --destructive at top-right while probe-D-results.json records the adjacent Publish item as `disabled: false` with no annotation. Two consumers of one latch, one honest, one not.
```

**Reproduction.** Run the dev server without VITE_API_URL on a loopback origin (the default `npm run dev:web-only` footgun described in availability.ts:22-35), open /#/palettes and the card menu. The lamp says misconfigured; the menu offers Publish enabled. Screenshot: evidence/desktop-light-menu-open.png.

**Proposed cure.** Replace the boolean with a four-arm match on the enum; `misconfigured` gets its own loud annotation, distinct from `offline` and from silence. Availability is a property of the action (disabled + named reason), not of the entity.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (PalettesPane.vue), pass 3` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The first drag-to-reorder of every session permutes the entire library. Two competing reorder authorities run on one gesture: vueuse's surviving defaultOptions.onUpdate (which splices a detached array snapshot AND physically re-parents a DOM node Vue's v-for owns) plus the component's own onEnd (which writes the store).

**Mechanism.** dual reorder path — a captured non-reactive computed snapshot plus a surviving library default that mutates DOM Vue owns

**Evidence.**

```
probe4.mjs, 3 fresh WebKit contexts: `TEST1 run1/2/3: before=P1,P2,P3,P4,P5 after=P3,P4,P2,P5,P1 intended=P2,P3,P1,P4,P5 *** WRONG ***`; `TEST2 drag#2 -> P4,P2,P3,P5,P1 (correct)`. Mechanism pasted from node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js:11-26 — `const defaultOptions = { onUpdate: (e) => moveArrayElement(list, ...) }` then `new Sortable(target, {...defaultOptions, ...resetOptions})`; PalettesPane.vue:183-197 passes onEnd, never onUpdate.
```

**Reproduction.** Seed 5 palettes in localStorage['color-palettes']; load /#/palettes; drag row 1's .drag-handle onto row 3; read localStorage. 3/3 deterministic. Independently replicated byte-for-byte against the pass-2 seat.

**Proposed cure.** Delete SortableJS from this component. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 already specifies reorder as a model verb (Space grabs, Up/Down move ordinal, Space drops, Escape cancels, every move announces `position of total`). A named <button> emitting move(id, delta) against the STORE's order — never a filtered projection, never a captured array — kills D-1, D-1b, D-9 and D-25 together and removes a dependency.

**Defect.** Corrupt or wrong-schema palette storage is rendered as an empty library. usePaletteStore's serializer catches JSON.parse failure and returns defaultStore, so an unreadable library is presented as a library the user never filled — and the empty invitation encourages them to save over it.

**Mechanism.** masking fallback (owner edict 2) collapsing an error arm onto the empty arm; the §7 recovery composition does not exist in the component

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (PalettesPane.vue), pass 3` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The pastel-rainbow identity — one of exactly two sanctioned coordinates — is perceptually achromatic in dark. The contrast certifier's only lever is L, but the ramp's identity is hue; on a dark plate the feasible walk direction is lighter, so all three stops land at L≈0.958 where cusp chroma is ~0.02 for every hue.

**Mechanism.** contrast-first certification applied to a hue-carrying identity — the guard cannot fail to destroy what it guards

**Evidence.**

```
Live computed root tokens: light `--palettes-ramp-title-0/1/2` C = 0.188343 / 0.188343 / 0.124795 (C̄ 0.1673) at L 47.093%; dark C = 0.033662 / 0.021053 / 0.023120 (C̄ 0.0260) at L 95.832% — a 6.44× collapse, all three dark stops sharing L to 11 decimals. Shipped Safari PNG pixels agree: dark glyph cores OKLCH C 0.0257 / 0.0206 / 0.0205. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2: "Both coordinates render in light and dark."
```

**Reproduction.** Load /#/palettes with prefers-color-scheme: dark; read getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--palettes-ramp-title-0..2'). Or crop 'Palettes' from shots/safari-desktop-dark/palettes.png and convert glyph-core pixels to OKLCH.

**Proposed cure.** Certify on an axis the identity does not live on: hold hue and chroma, satisfy the floor by compositing the letterforms against a local plate the ramp owns. Failing that, choose the walk direction by chroma preservation with L free only inside a chroma floor — dark-scheme identity ink is normally more chromatic, not less.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (pass 2)` · P2-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** On /#/mix the entire PaletteCard — this menu's trigger included — is nested inside a <button aria-pressed>. Invalid HTML content model plus an ARIA presentational-children hazard that permits the trigger to be pruned from the accessibility tree.

**Mechanism.** button's content model is phrasing content with NO interactive-content descendant; role=button is a role whose descendants are presentational, so a UA may remove the whole subtree from the a11y tree. Mix wrapped the card in the selection button instead of putting the button inside the card, and this component's trigger is the interactive content that makes it illegal rather than merely untidy. The same call site passes zero listeners, so all 17 emits are inert there.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:238-268 wraps <PaletteCard> in <button :aria-pressed :aria-label="`… palette ${palette.name}`" @click="togglePalette(palette)">. Measured live: probe-D6-pass2-results.json "mix": {"nestedInteractiveInButton":2,"nestedSample":[{"tag":"BUTTON","label":"Palette menu","outerLabel":"Select palette Muted Terracotta and Deep Sea Foam Study"},{..."Select palette Temp"}],"paletteCardsInsideButton":2}. Screenshot: evidence/pass2-mix-source.png.
```

**Reproduction.** Dev server up; `node docs/.../probe-D6-pass2.mjs` (its mixNesting arm navigates to /#/mix, selects the Palettes source mode, and counts `button button` matches). Static confirmation: MixSourceSelector.vue:238-268.

**Proposed cure.** PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5 law 12 already specifies the shape: the Card/article root is a noninteractive container whose one native named <button type="button" aria-pressed> child spans the specimen/identity region. Invert the nesting — the selection seat goes inside the card, not around it. Under P2-1's transposition the menu leaves the card entirely and the illegality dissolves with it.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (pass 3)` · P3-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** AT identity annihilation: opening a card menu removes the whole palette pane from the accessibility tree, while the menu's own computed name is a generic string identical on every card and the palette-name label inside it is programmatically inert.

**Mechanism.** An anonymous per-entity transient overlay borrows its accessible name from a trigger whose label is entity-agnostic, and reka's modal hideOthers strips the entity it belongs to out of the AT tree at the moment the overlay opens. The visible identity is a bare text node with no id and no aria-labelledby reference.

**Evidence.**

```
probe-D15-pass3.mjs: BEFORE totalAriaHiddenTrue=33, card ancestor chain hidden nodes=[]; AFTER open: totalAriaHiddenTrue=50, chain gains `DIV.pane-wrapper pane-wrapper--right aria-hidden=true data-aria-hidden=true`. probe-D14-pass3-results.json (CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree): {"role":"menu","name":"Palette menu","nameFrom":["relatedElement:aria-labelledby"]}. probe-D10-pass3-results.json triggerNames: three triggers, all ariaLabel "Palette menu"; paletteNameLabelReferenced: {id:null, text:"Muted Terracotta and Deep Sea Foam Study", referencedBy:0}. PaletteCardMenu.vue:9-11; PaletteCard.vue:100.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D15-pass3.mjs and probe-D14-pass3.mjs with the dev server up on :9000

**Proposed cure.** Architectural transposition, not an aria-label patch: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 already sends rename/lifecycle/export actions and durable operation state to the selected inspector. An inspector is a named page region whose heading IS the palette identity — it does not need to borrow a name, does not hide the field to exist, and announces the destructive action next to the entity it destroys. Adding an entity-scoped aria-label to the overlay would spell the identity a third time and still leave the field hidden.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-01 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** One Retry click permanently blanks the pane body. Transition mode="out-in" on the three-state container makes DOM presence a function of a 200ms animation clock, while the state machine settles synchronously; the pending enter never mounts and the pane is left as a void under the search field with no error, no empty plate, no skeleton and no recovery.

**Mechanism.** Animation clock owns DOM presence — branch identity is animated with mode="out-in" across an async boundary that can settle faster than the leave duration.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:40 (`<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">`); demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:188-195 (assertApiAttemptAllowed throws synchronously, unconditional for `misconfigured`). Live Playwright/WebKit 1440x900, sampled every 25ms from the click: t=0 n=1 h=224.5 "The commons is unreachable.Failed to load palettes"; t=28 n=1 vj-morph-leave-from|vj-morph-leave-active; t=227 n=1 vj-morph-leave-active|vj-morph-leave-to; t=251 n=0 h=12.0 ""; t=1202 n=0 h=12.0 "". Second clean-page run, 6s tail: {wrapChildren:0, wrapH:12, paneText:"BrowseDiscover palettes from the community."}; after typing into the search field: {wrapChildren:0, same paneText}. Screenshots: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/evidence/D-browse-before-retry.png vs D-browse-after-retry-6s.png.
```

**Reproduction.** 1) `http://localhost:9000/#/browse` at 1440x900 (dev server without VITE_API_URL, so the misconfigured latch is armed — the state all 60 audit captures show). 2) Wait ~3.5s for the error plate. 3) Click Retry once. 4) The state container's element children go 1→0 at ~251ms and stay 0 indefinitely; wrapper height 224.5px→12px. Typing in the search box does not restore it.

**Proposed cure.** Stop animating branch identity. Keep one persistent state region whose CONTENT cross-fades (default simultaneous mode), or drop the Transition on the state container entirely and let the individual plates own their entrance. A v-if guard inside mode="out-in" only narrows the window; it does not close the class.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The keyboard focus indicator of the primary disclosure control renders at 1.024–1.202:1 contrast; its 2px ring is entirely clipped by `overflow-hidden` on the wrapper. Two engines, both schemes.

**Mechanism.** A `div` was made the button and then clipped: `ring` is a box-shadow with outward spread, and the row's border box equals the clipping wrapper's content box, so the whole indicator falls in the clipped region — leaving a background tint as the sole signal.

**Evidence.**

```
AdminUsersPanel.vue:82 (`focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring`) vs :68 (`overflow-hidden` on the wrapper). probe-D3b/D3c/D3d: WebKit light 1.034:1 (maxΔ 27), WebKit dark 1.166:1 (maxΔ 62), Chromium light 1.024:1 (maxΔ 34), Chromium dark 1.202:1 (maxΔ 72); `:focus-visible` true and boxShadow `rgb(28,25,23) 0 0 0 2px` present in all four; changed-pixel bbox 11,12→470,67 maps to exactly the row border box 225,374→684,429 — the ring contributed ZERO pixels. Control in the same probe: sibling native `button[aria-label="Delete user mbabb"]` maxΔ 177 (Chromium light) / 290 (Chromium dark). Frames frames-D3/focus-webkit-light-before.png vs -after.png are visually indistinguishable.
```

**Reproduction.** node probe-D3b.mjs then probe-D3c.mjs — real Tab presses to the row (`role=button][aria-expanded]`), 400ms settle, pixel diff of the row clip; contrast computed from the mean RGB of a text-free band inside the row.

**Proposed cure.** VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 already states the anatomy: one native `<button type="button">` spanning the specimen/identity region, sibling to the action cluster. A native button inherits the producer focus register, needs no ring hack, and has no clipping ancestor. Deleting `overflow-hidden` alone is a patch that leaves the container-as-button (D-3 is the visible half of the same defect as the row's accessible-name swallowing).

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

Live WebKit 1440x1200, seeded 5 palettes, real mouse drag, 2 identical runs — drag row 0 -> row 1: DOM+localStorage become ['Charlie','Bravo','Zulu One','Zulu Two','Alpha']; after reload ['Alpha','Bravo','Charlie','Zulu One','Zulu Two']. **Evidence.**

```
Measured live (5 seeded palettes, 1440 and 390, light and dark): card root tabindex=null, tabIndex=-1, onkeydown=false, aria-pressed=null, aria-expanded=null, aria-selected=null, cursor='pointer', class='group rounded-card cartoon-surface border-card-edge bg-well cursor-pointer'. Tab order inside the pane: ['Search your palettes...','Delete all saved palettes','Palette menu' x5] — the card never appears. Wired at PalettesPane.vue:91 `@click="pm.toggleExpand(palette.id)"` onto PaletteCard.vue:22-26 (`role="article"` + `@click="$emit('click')"`). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 verbatim: 'A palette card is a bounded entity article, not a clickable role=article … The card body owns no expand, inline rename, action menu, transient result or hover-only swatch-action path.'
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with a seeded store; Tab through the pane — focus goes search -> delete-all -> palette menus, never to a card; press Enter/Space anywhere and nothing expands. `document.querySelector('[role=article]').tabIndex` returns -1.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the omnibus. Card root becomes a non-interactive <article> carrying the exact §3.1 tuple (Card size='sm' material='content' tier='quiet' surface='opaque' :shadow='false' :grain='false' specular='off'); the specimen+identity region becomes one native <button type='button' :aria-pressed> that selects into the inspector lane; rename, menu, export, publish and their durable state move to that inspector; the reorder handle stays a separate named sibling control.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The /palettes desktop composition is an exact 50/50 split — neither sanctioned ratio, 14 percentage points below the Library field floor — and the companion lane is the Picker, not the mandated selected-inspector.

**Mechanism.** A default two-up layout was used where an earned composition is required, and the second lane was filled with an unrelated instrument instead of the Library's own inspector. The missing inspector is the direct cause of D-4 (all entity actions collapse into the card body) and D-7 (operation state has nowhere persistent to live).

**Evidence.**

```
Measured live, WebKit 1440x900: `.pane-container--dual` gridTemplateColumns = '512px 512px'; lane 0 (Picker) x=199 w=512, lane 1 (PalettesPane) x=729 w=512 — exactly 50.000%/50.000%. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 1 permits only golden (61.8033989/38.1966011) or preview-dominant (66.6666667/33.3333333); §3.1 Library row requires field 64%…66.6666667% and a 'complementary selected action/history inspector at 33.3333333%…36%'.
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 1440x900 and evaluate getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.pane-container--dual')).gridTemplateColumns -> '512px 512px'.

**Proposed cure.** Adopt the §3.1 Library composition literally: owner-state field at 64–66.7%, selected action/history inspector at 33.3–36%, inspector ABSENT (not empty) when nothing is selected. The Picker does not belong in the Library route's stage.

**Mechanism.** The empty state is rendered inside a fixed half-viewport lane with col-span-full + justify-center + min-h-[120px], so it inherits the protagonist's geometry instead of shrinking to its own content.

**Evidence.**

```

VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 2: 'Empty secondary content occupies at most a narrow invitation tray (≤15% of the stage) or disappears. It never receives half the viewport.' §7: 'A true empty invitation content-hugs its text/action.' PaletteCardGrid.vue:28-30 exposes an #emptyAction slot; PalettesPane.vue:75-81 never fills it.

Also visible in the tracked capture docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The pastel-rainbow identity — one of exactly two sanctioned coordinates in the product — is chromatically dead in dark mode; the three 'rainbow' stops are perceptually one near-white colour.

**Mechanism.** demo/color-session/palettes-ramp.ts:104-120 certifies each stop to a WCAG floor by walking LIGHTNESS along the hue's gamut cusp. Against a dark plate the reachable direction is up, so all three stops land at L 95.8%, where OKLCH chroma is arithmetically tiny for every hue. The certification succeeds by destroying the thing it certifies — the module's own header admits the open bracket.

**Evidence.**

```
Live computed tokens, WebKit 1440. Light --palettes-ramp-title-0/1/2 = oklch(47.093% 0.188343 329.834) / oklch(47.093% 0.188343 9.834) / oklch(47.093% 0.124795 49.834); dark = oklch(95.832% 0.033662 329.834) / oklch(95.832% 0.021053 9.834) / oklch(95.832% 0.023120 49.834). Mean chroma 0.1671 light vs 0.0260 dark = 6.4x collapse; OKLab ΔE between outer stops 0.207 light vs 0.0221 dark = 9.4x less separation (ΔE 0.022 at L 0.958 is at or below JND for text glyphs). Independently confirmed by per-column glyph-ink sampling of the tracked 2880x1800 Safari PNGs: light chroma mean 0.1502 (hue 336.7 -> 54.8 deg), dark chroma mean 0.0239. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2: 'Both coordinates render in light and dark.'
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with colorScheme dark and read getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--palettes-ramp-title-0/1/2'); or open docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-dark/palettes.png beside safari-desktop-light/palettes.png.

**Proposed cure.** Certify hue-preserving CHROMA, not lightness alone: hold the analogous fan's chroma at the dark-plate cusp and take the contrast from the plate (darken the resting tier locally behind the word) rather than from the ink. If the plate cannot move, take the large-text 3:1 floor at a mid lightness in dark (L ~0.72–0.78) where C ~0.10 is still reachable, so the word reads as pastel rainbow — the whole point of the coordinate.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** A search that matches nothing renders the empty-library invitation, so the pane asserts '5 saved' in its header and 'No saved palettes yet.' in its body at the same time, and offers the wrong remedy.

**Mechanism.** One boolean is asked to carry three distinct states (empty library, no matches, populated). The role=status region also announces the wrong sentence to AT on every keystroke that empties the result set.

**Evidence.**

```
PalettesPane.vue:77-80 keys `:empty` to `pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0` while the copy speaks about the unfiltered collection. Measured live (5 seeded palettes, query 'qqqzzz', both schemes, 1440 and 390): header badge '5', sr-only '(5 saved)', body [role=status] '· empty plate · No saved palettes yet. Add colors above, then save the set.', cards rendered 0, delete-all still present true. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.1 requires the in-route filter to 'announce changed result count/state through the owning status region' — when results return (query 'Zulu' -> 2 cards, measured) the status region unmounts and nothing is announced.
```

**Reproduction.** Seed 5 palettes into localStorage `color-palettes`, load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, type 'qqqzzz' into the search field, and read the header badge and the [role=status] text in the same frame.

**Proposed cure.** Three named states: empty-library (0 saved), no-matches (saved>0 and filtered=0 — copy names the query and offers 'Clear search'), populated. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-6 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Export failure is console.warn-only — precisely what the palette contract forbids verbatim — so a failed export shows the user nothing.

**Mechanism.** Failure was modelled as a log line rather than as operation state on an entity. The demo's toast layer was removed (vue-sonner) and the calls were replaced with console.warn, leaving no user-facing failure channel anywhere in the pane.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/usePaletteExport.ts:21-23 `catch (e) { console.warn('Export failed:', e); }`, wired at PalettesPane.vue:96 `@export="(p, fmt) => onExport(p, fmt)"` and consumed at PalettesPane.vue:211. PALETTE-CONTRACT.md Appendix W51 opening: 'A serializer either yields the bytes below or a visible terminal/retryable operation state — never a partial download or console.warn-only result.' Appendix W51 §8 further requires a durable ExportOperation with states captured|ready|retryable-failure|terminal-failure|handoff-initiated and failure codes storage_quota|serialization_resource|handoff_unavailable|snapshot_corrupt|serializer_contract — PalettesPane renders none, and libraryPort exposes no field to render them from.
```

**Reproduction.** Trigger any export throw (e.g. quota, or a serializer contract failure in demo/palettes/export/png.ts) via the palette card menu on http://localhost:9000/#/palettes: the DOM is unchanged and only the console records it. Static: grep -n 'console.warn' demo/palettes/usePaletteExport.ts.

**Proposed cure.** Model export as an operation on an entity: put the ExportOperation record in the store keyed by (snapshotDigest, format), surface Prepare FORMAT -> Download FILENAME in the selected inspector's action region, and render retryable-failure / terminal-failure as visible persistent state with a real Retry. Delete the try/catch -> console.warn.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · P3-B1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The entire Tags filter section is inert: it calls a retired shadcn/radix-era Checkbox API against glass-ui 7, so ticking a tag paints checked and changes nothing.

**Mechanism.** Pre-glass-7 component API called against a glass-ui 7 contract. Vue fallthrough fails silently: the undeclared prop lands as a raw DOM attribute and the undeclared emit never fires; with `modelValue` absent the producer runs uncontrolled, so the box paints checked while the product holds no such state.

**Evidence.**

```
node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/checkbox/Checkbox.vue.d.ts declares `modelValue?: CheckedState|null` and emits ONLY `update:modelValue`. demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55 passes `:checked` and `@update:checked`. Neither exists. `toggleTag` (:197) is never called and the `update:selectedTags` emit declared at :156 has no live caller.
```

**Reproduction.** Static: read Checkbox.vue.d.ts against SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55. Live: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probe-P3-3-truth.mjs (the section is absent in this environment, so the static proof is the load-bearing one).

**Proposed cure.** Transpose onto glass-ui `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` with `v-model` on one owned selectedTags model; the local toggleTag array-splice helper disappears with it. No shim, no dual path.

**Defect.** The active-filter count badge is clipped to an illegible olive crescent — 49.3% of its area painted away, digit entirely absent — and the count never reaches the accessible name either.

**Mechanism.** A hand-positioned overhanging badge inside a producer root that declares paint containment; `contain: paint` clips to the padding box and the capsule radius bevels the remainder. The non-square icon-only geometry is what puts the overhang inside the bevel.

Hit test 3 cardinal points, 7/7 matrices: centre true, top false, right false. Pixel census at DPR 4: surviving gold bbox 46x45 device px = 11.5 x 11.25 CSS px of a nominal 16.2 x 16.2 chip = 49.3% lost. AT tree of the trigger is exactly `- button "Filters" [expanded]: - img` — `aria-label` overrides the inner textContent "1".

**Reproduction.** node .../probe-P3-4-pixels.mjs; see shots-p3/P3-px-light-badge.png and P3-px-dark-badge.png. Manually: /#/browse, open ⋮, select the Featured tier, press Escape and look at the trigger.

**Proposed cure.** Use the producer `Badge` atom as a sibling of the trigger, outside the contain:paint root, and put the count in the name (`aria-label="Filters, 2 active"`). Stop overriding `h-8 w-8` so `iconOnly` can keep its square. Never hand-position an overhang inside a producer root.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · P3-B4 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The field labelled 'Search by CSS color' with placeholder '#hex, hsl(...)' accepts exactly one syntax and silently searches a different colour for everything else, with no error state anywhere — and even a valid hex leaves the swatch wrong.

**Mechanism.** A regex gate placed in front of the product's own competence, failing CLOSED to a silent substitution instead of OPEN to the parser. With no error state and no representation of the applied colour, the substitution is undetectable from the UI.

**Evidence.**

```
SearchFilterBar.vue:218 `const hex = text.startsWith("#") && /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i.test(text) ? text : pickerHex.value;`. Six inputs driven live (evidence-p3/P3-3-truth.json -> substitution): `hsl(200 50% 50%)`, `rebeccapurple`, `oklch(0.7 0.15 30)`, `#abc`, `not-a-color` and `#FF0000` all left the swatch label at 'current color #4488cc', badge '1', zero `[role=alert]`, `aria-invalid: null`. `parseColorIn` — the library's own parser, which handles all six — is imported at :145 and used at :206.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe-P3-3-truth.mjs. Manually: /#/browse, open ⋮, type `hsl(200 50% 50%)` in Find-by-Color, click Search — the badge increments and the wall filters, on #4488cc.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the regex gate at :218; pass the trimmed text to `parseColorIn` in a try/catch and render the two real states — parsed: the swatch and a removable applied-filter chip both take that colour; unparsed: a named error on the field with `aria-invalid`. This also makes the currently-unreachable `searching` register meaningful.

**Reproduction.** `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D18-pass4.mjs` with the dev server on :9000 — seeded 11-palette store, open card 1's menu, click Delete; read F_irreversible. Isolated browser context; no user data touched.

**Proposed cure.** Not "add a confirm dialog to the menu". Per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:102 the lifecycle actions move to the selected inspector, where a destructive commit has room for a named consequence, a Cancel, and durable post-state — the exact anatomy PalettesPane.vue:101-119 already mounts for the bulk twin. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · P4-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The irreversible row's screen position is a function of the card's scroll position. On the first card the panel opens downward and `Delete` is 233.5px BELOW the trigger (the farthest row from the pointer); on the last card it flips upward and `Delete` is 51.5px ABOVE it (the NEAREST row, 4.5x closer). A 285px swing — 2.85 card heights — for the same command on the same screen, in identical ink to `Rename` (D-2) with no separator above it (D-14).

**Mechanism.** a per-row floating panel inherits the producer's collision flip, so the commit geometry of a repeated species is determined by viewport position rather than by the composition; the destructive verb has no fixed relation to the affordance that summons it

**Evidence.**

```
probe-D17-pass4-results.json B_destructiveRowPosition: card 1 trigger cy 487.6, data-side "bottom", panel y 510…750.1, rows Publish 580.1 / Rename 624.1 / Export 677.1 / Delete 721.1, deleteOffsetFromTrigger +233.5. card 11 trigger cy 754.6, data-side "top", panel y 492…732.1, rows Publish 562.1 / Rename 606.1 / Export 659.1 / Delete 703.1, deleteOffsetFromTrigger -51.5. swingPx 285. Card height 100px (A_pressLeak.rest.h). Photographs: evidence/pass4-G-flip-top.png, evidence/pass4-G-flip-bottom.png.
```

**Reproduction.** `node docs/…/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D17-pass4.mjs`; read B_destructiveRowPosition. Visually: seed 11 palettes, open the last card's menu at 1440x820.

**Proposed cure.** The transposition in D-1: the destructive commit lives in the selected inspector, a fixed region of the page, so its position is invariant across every row of the field. Any patch that keeps a flipping per-card panel keeps a scroll-dependent destructive target.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · P4-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** In an RTL document the portalled panel is a hard-coded `dir="ltr"` island: the SAME palette name renders in two opposite directions 40px apart, and the two truncations keep OPPOSITE HALVES of it (the card keeps the head, the menu header keeps the tail). The row glyph gutter lands on the physical left while the card's own grip handle is on the physical right; the submenu opens away from the reading direction.

**Mechanism.** the content is portalled to <body> so it inherits no direction; reka's `dir` prop defaults to "ltr", this component passes none, and the app mounts no ConfigProvider — so every portalled surface is a pinned-LTR island inside an RTL document

**Evidence.**

```
probe-D19-pass4-results.json dir ancestor chain: content node `dropdown-menu-content dropdown-menu__content …` dirAttr:"ltr" computedDir:"ltr"; its parent DIV, BODY.relative and HTML all computedDir:"rtl". Header (palette identity): direction "ltr", scrollW 317 / clientW 178 -> clippedPx 139 (44%). Card's own name span: direction "rtl", x 320.1…648. glyphGutter: rowX 245, svgX 253 -> "physical LEFT of the row". probe-D18-pass4-results.json C_rtl: subRtl parent x 238…430, child x 423…665 (opens physical right). `grep -rn "ConfigProvider" demo` -> no matches. Photograph: evidence/pass4-C-rtl-arabic.png. Repo's own claim falsified: demo/color-picker/index.html:2 "U.W-A11Y · U-F58 (BR-10) — RTL mechanical readiness".
```

**Reproduction.** `node docs/…/PaletteCardMenu/probe-D19-pass4.mjs` — seeds one Arabic-named palette, sets documentElement.dir="rtl" after boot, opens the menu, dumps the dir chain and both truncations; writes evidence/pass4-C-rtl-arabic.png.

**Proposed cure.** Structural: the actions live in an in-document inspector region, which inherits `dir` for free. Immediate one-node repair for the whole app: mount a reka `ConfigProvider` with the document direction at the app root — it repairs every portalled surface at once. NOTE this corrects pass 1's D-8: `ml-auto` never renders in RTL because its box is force-LTR, so fixing the margin alone would change nothing.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1b · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** REPLICATED (pass 3). Dragging one card while a search filter is active silently rewrites the global order of the whole library: every matched palette is promoted to the head and every unmatched palette demoted, invisibly, persisted immediately, with no undo and no announcement.

**Mechanism.** a view projection is used as the authority for a store-wide ordinal rewrite

**Evidence.**

```
PalettesPane.vue:183-197 hands `useSortable` the filtered list and calls the global writer `pm.reorderPalettes(ids)`; usePaletteStore.ts:153-167 rebuilds the store as [given ids in order, ...everything else appended]. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:132 requires `position of total` announcement.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/challengeD-reorder-probe.mjs (Chromium, live :9000). Pasted output: BEFORE : Alpha,Bravo,Charlie,Delta,Echo,Foxtrot,Golf,Hotel / FILTERED: ["Foxtrot","Hotel"] (typed `ot`) / AFTER : Hotel,Foxtrot,Alpha,Bravo,Charlie,Delta,Echo,Golf / VISIBLE AFTER CLEAR: same. One local swap between items 6 and 8 produced a global re-shuffle of all eight.

**Proposed cure.** The reorder command must express a relative insertion (`move(id, before: id)`) that the store resolves against the full list, never a full-order array derived from a projection. Drag should additionally be disabled while a filter is active, since the ordinal the user manipulates and the ordinal the store writes are different quantities.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** REPLICATED (pass 3), measured per-stop. The ruled pastel-rainbow identity — one of exactly two sanctioned coordinates, ruled by the owner — is chromatically dead in dark mode. Chroma drops 82% and the three stops become visually indistinguishable near-white.

**Mechanism.** palettes-ramp.ts:117 certifies each stop with `certifyAccentInk(guarded, surfaceL, floor)`, an objective function that optimises WCAG contrast only; in dark the feasible band is near-white where chroma is arithmetically unavailable, so the walk destroys the exact quantity the ruling is about — inter-stop chromatic distance is not in the objective at all

**Evidence.**

```
Computed :root tokens, WebKit 1440. Light: oklch L 0.4709 C 0.1883 H 329.8 / C 0.1883 H 9.8 / C 0.1248 H 49.8 -> rgb(144,32,140), (170,0,67), (144,65,0). Dark: L 0.9583 C 0.0337 / 0.0211 / 0.0231 -> rgb(255,234,252), (255,236,238), (255,237,228) — identical in red, max delta 24/255 in one channel. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:23 and :188 both require the identity in BOTH schemes. Visible: shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png vs shots/safari-desktop-dark/palettes.png.
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes in a dark-scheme context and read `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--palettes-ramp-title-0'|'-1'|'-2')`.

**Proposed cure.** Add a chroma floor and a minimum inter-stop deltaE as hard constraints and solve lightness/contrast within them. In dark that means dropping off the near-white ceiling to roughly L 0.80-0.85, where the 3:1 large-text floor is still met with C >= 0.10. Identity is inter-stop distance; it must be an explicit term in the certification, not a hoped-for side effect.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-6/D-7 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** REPLICATED (pass 3). The three most consequential operations have no durable truth. Export failure is swallowed into console.warn; publish has no pending state, its result is a 2500ms auto-dismissing chip, and it is silently dropped on two reachable paths.

**Mechanism.** operation state was routed through an imperative child ref instead of through the port that owns the entity, so it has nowhere durable to live and no lifecycle

**Evidence.**

```
usePaletteExport.ts:21-23 `catch (e) { console.warn("Export failed:", e); }`, wired at PalettesPane.vue:96 for five formats. PalettesPane.vue:203-208 returns early when `palette.id == null` and no-ops when `cardRefs[id]` is absent (card filtered out mid-flight); the destination ActionFeedback.vue auto-dismisses at 2500ms. usePalettePorts.ts:129-146 shows libraryPort has no loading/error ref while browsePort beside it has `browsing` and `browseError`. PALETTE-CONTRACT.md:317-327 is the W51 verbatim authority requiring a visible retryable-failure/terminal-failure state; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:101; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:52 (PR-08).
```

**Reproduction.** Trigger any export from a card's `...` menu with a failing serializer (or read the catch block); nothing appears. For publish: publish a palette and immediately type a non-matching search query — the card unmounts and the result is discarded with no user-visible trace.

**Proposed cure.** libraryPort grows the pending/error shape browsePort already has; the card renders a durable status row driven by it; the transient chip becomes decoration over that truth. The `cardRefs` imperative channel (:84, :177, :205) dissolves entirely, which also removes its unpruned-map leak.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-02 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Revert is `opacity: 0` at rest with `pointer-events: auto`, revealed ONLY by `group-hover`, which Tailwind compiles inside `@media (hover: hover)` — so on every touch device the rule does not exist and the destructive button is permanently invisible yet tappable.

**Mechanism.** Hover-gated reveal of a destructive control; the reveal rule is media-gated out of existence on coarse pointers.

**Evidence.**

```
VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:75-84 `class="... opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-100"`. Verbatim from node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/components.css: `@media (hover:hover){.group-hover\:opacity-100:is(:where(.group):hover *){opacity:1}}` — the only rule in the cascade that raises this element's opacity. Measured at rest (probe2.json secondOpen.revertButtons): {w:90, h:36, opacity:"0", pointerEvents:"auto"}.
```

**Reproduction.** grep the shipped CSS for `group-hover\:opacity-100` — it is inside @media (hover:hover); no other rule sets non-zero opacity. (Caveat stated in report: Playwright's mobile arms emulate viewport, not the hover media feature, so the touch consequence is CONFIRMED-BY-CSS, not from a driven touch device.)

**Proposed cure.** Promote Revert out of hover into the row as a persistent, named `text-small` control — the 44px invisible band is layout the design already pays for. Identical on touch and pointer. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-07 names this species (`Hover-only/unlabeled controls` → ADD-AFFORDANCE/REMOVE).

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** A failed moderation command is completely invisible: approve/reject/delete swallow every error to console.warn. The panel designed error≠empty for LOADS (W5-5/F-2) and designed nothing at all for MUTATIONS — the only thing a moderator actually does here.

```
demo/palettes/useColorNameQueue.ts:76-78, :87-89, :99-101 — `catch (e: any) { console.warn("Failed to approve:", e?.message); }` and identical for reject/delete.
