```

**Reproduction.** Sign in as admin on /#/admin/names with >=1 pending item; make the API return 500 for POST /colors/:id/approve; click Approve. The row does not move, no error appears, nothing is announced; only a console.warn fires.

**Proposed cure.** Make the row the state owner: give AdminListItem a `state` slot fed by a per-item operation record (idle | inflight | failed) so an in-flight row dims and disables its own actions and a failed row keeps its place carrying the machine message and a real per-row Retry. The EmptyState variant="error" register already exists — this is the same species one altitude lower, not a new mechanism.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design: visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D4-01 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The commit has no designed outcome; under an active filter it renders four contradictory truths in one frame, announces the opposite of what happened to assistive tech, and destroys keyboard focus.

**Mechanism.** A mutation whose outcome was never designed. The component treats commit as a fire-and-forget emit, so the product's only feedback comes from unrelated regions that are each individually correct and jointly contradictory; and the control gates its own existence on the state its action destroys, so it unmounts itself while focused.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Inverted dependency: the domain/server-state composable `useAdminUsers` imports the SFC, holds a template-ref to its instance, and mutates the component's private state through 5 `defineExpose`d members. Latent module cycle; 5 optional-chain masking fallbacks.

**Mechanism.** Split ownership: `expandedUserSlug`/`userPalettes`/`loadingUserPalettes` (AdminUsersPanel.vue:236-238) are stored in the view but every mutation originates in the state layer, so the state layer must reach across the layer boundary through an instance handle.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:14 `import type { AdminUsersPanel } from "./browser/admin";` · :27 `const adminUsersPanelRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof AdminUsersPanel> | null>(null);` · :95 `adminUsersPanelRef.value?.updatePaletteTier(...)` · :117 `?.removeUserPalette(...)` · :132/:146 `?.clearUserPalettes(...)` · demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:123 `admin.adminUsersPanelRef.value?.onPruneDone(pruned);` · demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:27,:134 · AdminUsersPanel.vue:389 `defineExpose({ removeUserPalette, updatePaletteTier, clearUserPalettes, onPruneDone, userPalettes })`. Measured: `grep -rn --include='*.ts' 'from "[^"]*\.vue"' demo/ | wc -l` = 25, of which 24 are barrel re-exports — useAdminUsers.ts:14 is the sole state module importing a component. `grep -rn --include='*.vue' defineExpose demo/` = 14 sites; this is the largest (5) and the only one whose consumer is a composable. tsconfig.base.json:8 `verbatimModuleSyntax: true` is why the cycle erases.
```

**Reproduction.** AdminPane.vue:26 mounts the panel under `v-if="subView === 'admin-users'"`. Call `useAdminUsers.onDeleteUser(slug)` (:140-150) and switch the admin sub-view during the `await deleteUser(token, slug)`; `adminUsersPanelRef.value` is then null and the `?.` at :146 silently swallows `clearUserPalettes(slug)`. The panel remounts with the deleted user's `userPalettes` never cleared. Same swallow at all 5 call sites.

**Proposed cure.** Lift the three refs into a `useAdminUserPalettes()` composable colocated with `useAdminUsers`; the panel receives them as props and emits `toggleUserExpand`. Then delete AdminUsersPanel.vue:352-389 (4 state fns + defineExpose), useAdminUsers.ts:14/:27 and the 4 `?.` call sites, usePalettePorts.ts:123/:197, AdminPane.vue:27/:134. Net: −5 exposed members, −1 port member, −1 inverted import, −1 latent cycle, −5 masking fallbacks.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** PaletteCard feeds arbitrary user/API color strings into `certifyAccentInk`, a demo-side wrapper that converts the library's typed Result error into a thrown exception during render. Any palette color carrying alpha < 1 destroys the whole hosting pane via the error boundary; zero cards render and the poison is persisted in localStorage.

**Mechanism.** Ownership inversion at the library boundary: the library owns 'certification may fail, here is a typed error'; demo/color-session/ink.ts unilaterally re-declares it as 'cannot fail' and PaletteCard consumes that re-declaration on untrusted data. A total function was made partial at the wrong layer.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteCard.vue:226 `firstColor = props.palette.colors[0]?.css ?? …`; PaletteCard.vue:229-230 `const { safeCss } = useSafeAccentFn("well"); const safeFirstColor = computed(() => safeCss(firstColor.value))`; demo/color-session/ink.ts:78 `if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`Ink certification failed: ${result.error.code}`)`; src/color/operations.ts:213-214 `if (accent.alpha !== 1 || surface.alpha !== 1) return err({ code: "color_invalid_input" })`. node against the served dist: `lab(50% 20 10 / 82.7%) => safeAccent ERR color_invalid_input`, `oklch(0.7 0.1 200 / 0.5) => ERR color_invalid_input`, `#e11d48 => OK`. Live: pane shows `This panel hit an unexpected error. / color_non_finite`, articles: 0. The app's own persisted state held `color-picker = {"inputColor":"lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)"}`, i.e. it mints alpha'd colors itself.
```

**Reproduction.** With the dev server live at http://localhost:9000: (1) in the page, `localStorage.setItem('color-palettes', JSON.stringify({version:1,palettes:[{id:'p',slug:'p',name:'Probe',isLocal:true,colors:[{css:'lab(50% 20 10 / 82.7%)',position:0},{css:'#0ea5e9',position:1}]}]}))`; (2) full reload of `/#/palettes`, settle 2s. Observed `{url:'http://localhost:9000/#/palettes', boundary:true, bodyHead:'…This panel hit an unexpected error.\n\ncolor_non_finite…', articles:0}`. Repeats with `lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)`. Control with `['#e11d48','#0ea5e9']` → no boundary. (Exact throw site among ink.ts:47/59/78 is a hypothesis; the Result-to-throw class is confirmed.)

**Proposed cure.** Make `certifyAccentInk` TOTAL on dynamic input — return the input css (or the muted-ink token) for every non-certifiable value, exactly as it already does for unparseable input at ink.ts:136, and add the alpha pre-condition the library states at operations.ts:214. Keep throws only for producer literals (ink.ts:53), which are build-time invariants. Then no ink consumer can crash a pane and PaletteCard needs no guard at all.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The state layer imports the view and drives it through a template ref. `useAdminUsers` (a server-state composable) imports the SFC's type, holds its INSTANCE, and mutates the component's private state via defineExpose'd methods; the instance handle is published on the app-wide ADMIN_PORT_KEY surface. **Mechanism.** Split semantic ownership across a layer boundary: storage of "the expanded admin user's palettes" lives in the view (AdminUsersPanel.vue:236-238), mutation lives in the composable — so the lower layer must reach up through an instance handle. Yields a type-level cycle (erased only by `import type` + verbatimModuleSyntax), five masking `?.` swallows, and mutators that see one list but not the other.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:14 `import type { AdminUsersPanel } from "./browser/admin";` · :27 `ref<InstanceType<typeof AdminUsersPanel>|null>` · :95/:117/:132/:146 `adminUsersPanelRef.value?.<method>()` · demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:123 `admin.adminUsersPanelRef.value?.onPruneDone(pruned)` · :197 publishes the handle on adminPort · demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:27 `ref="adminUsersPanelRef"` + :134 `const adminUsersPanelRef = pm.adminUsersPanelRef` (the pane BORROWS the composable's ref) · AdminUsersPanel.vue:389 defineExpose of 5 members incl. mutable `userPalettes`. Uniqueness measured: of 25 .ts->.vue edges in demo/, 24 are barrels; this is the only state module importing a component.
```

**Reproduction.** Divergence (exact steps; NOT executed — needs an admin token and the step is destructive, this seat was read-only): admin-authenticate -> #/browse, note palette P -> #/admin/users, expand P's owner -> delete P from the row -> #/browse: P is still listed. Swallow variant (r1, mechanically certain): trigger onDeleteUser then switch admin sub-view during the await (AdminPane.vue:26 v-if unmounts the panel) -> `adminUsersPanelRef.value` is null -> clearUserPalettes silently skipped.

Net: -5 exposed members, -1 port member, -1 inverted edge, -1 latent cycle, -5 masking fallbacks, and the remotePalettes divergence becomes unrepresentable because one module sees both lists.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-16 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** useHoverPopover reads `e.currentTarget` inside a nextTick callback — i.e. after event dispatch has completed, when the DOM spec guarantees it is null. Every swatch hover throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')` and the popover's position is never applied. The `as Element` cast is the masking assertion that hid it from vue-tsc.

**Mechanism.** Hand-rolled floating positioning inside a demo composable, duplicating @mkbabb/glass-ui/popover which the same component already imports and uses on its other branch. A dual path (edict 2) reimplementing a design-system primitive (edict 4); the `as Element` cast (edict 2 — masking fallback) let the null flow through typecheck.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHoverPopover.ts:30 — `nextTick(() => positionPanel(e.currentTarget as Element));`. Live capture with an unhandledrejection listener: {"captured":["REJ:TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')"],"inline":"top: 0px; left: 0px; transform: translateX(-50%);"} — the inline top/left are still the reactive initial 0px, proving positionPanel never completed. Spec: DOM Standard §2.2 — "The currentTarget attribute … When an event is dispatched, this is set to the object whose listener is being invoked, and reset to null afterwards."
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, seed one palette, expand the card, dispatch/perform pointerenter on a swatch wrapper with `window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', …)` installed. The rejection fires on every hover, on every desktop browser (canHover = matchMedia('(hover: hover)')).

**Proposed cure.** Capture the element at dispatch time (`const el = e.currentTarget as Element` BEFORE nextTick) is the patch; the transposition is to delete the branch — let the design-system Popover anchor to its own trigger so no coordinate is ever computed in demo/ at all.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-19 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The "Prune empty" confirmation dialog names a count computed from a ≤50-row client page while the endpoint it authorises deletes EVERY empty user in the corpus. An irreversible, unrecoverable delete is guarded by a false statement about its own scope.

**Mechanism.** Discarded wire contract at a module boundary: PaginatedResponse.total (demo/palettes/types.ts:127) is published by the transport and thrown away by the composable, so the component is handed a page under a name (`totalUsers`) that asserts it is a corpus, and computes a destructive action's blast radius from it. The panel is not wrong to render emptyCount; it is wrong to POSSESS it.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:59 `const res = await listUsers(token, 50); adminUsers.value = res.data;` (res.total discarded) → demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:33 `:total-users="pm.adminUsers.value.length"` → demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 `const emptyCount = computed(() => users.filter(...).length)` → :289-291 `title: \`Prune ${emptyCount.value} empty users?\`` / "This will permanently delete N users … This cannot be undone." → demo/palettes/api/admin-users.ts:69-71 `POST /admin/users/prune-empty` with NO body → api/src/modules/admin/service/users.ts:232 `const slugs = await users.findEmptyUserSlugs();` (whole collection, no limit/offset) + :243-246 `sessions.deleteByUserSlugs(slugs); users.deleteMany(slugs)`. Then AdminUsersPanel.vue:303-308 prints the SERVER's count back: `Pruned ${count} users`.
```

**Reproduction.** CONFIRMED by code path — every link quoted above, all files read this pass. End-to-end browser run requires a roster >50 users with ≥1 empty user beyond row 50; this read-only seat cannot seed the API, so I do not claim to have run it. Deterministic recipe: seed 51+ users with the empty ones sorting past row 50; open #/admin/users with an admin token; click Prune empty; compare the dialog's number to `pruned` in the POST /admin/users/prune-empty response. Nothing in the chain is conditional. Compounding: useAdminUsers.ts:191-193 repairs only page 1 after the global delete and issues no refetch.

**Proposed cure.** The roster composable returns a page-aware value object, never a bare array: `type Roster = {state:"unauthenticated"} | {state:"loading"} | {state:"error";message} | {state:"loaded";rows:User[];total:number;offset:number;limit:number}`. Blast-radius numbers then become unrepresentable from client state. Preferred form: prune takes an explicit slug list, so the confirmation names exactly what it will send — which also makes the operation idempotent and gives the audit log per-slug membership instead of a bare count.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · N-10 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The palette wire contract has no single home. It is declared independently in api/src/modules/palette/format.ts (FormattedPalette — the authority, constructed by formatPalette) and hand-transcribed in demo/palettes/types.ts (Palette — what BrowsePane and every pm.* member is typed against). 20 of 22 fields diverge. ```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe-L4/typediff.mjs

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-17 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Drag-to-reorder under an active search filter silently rewrites the stored order of palettes the user cannot see. The pane hands a filtered projection to `reorderPalettes`, a TOTAL reordering primitive that completes any partial ordering by appending the remainder to the tail.

**Mechanism.** Ownership of list ORDER is split: the store owns the array but exposes only a total-permutation API, while the view owns the gesture and can only see a projection. No type expresses the totality precondition, so a filtered view silently violates it.

**Evidence.**

```

Live probe output, HEAD 9268f054: {"seedOrder":["A(alpha)","B(beta)","C(gamma)","D(delta)","E(epsilon)"],"filter":"e","visibleNames":["beta","delta","epsilon"],"afterDragWithinFilter":["D","B","E","A","C"],"intended":["A","D","B","C","E"]}
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/live3.mjs — headless Chromium against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000; page.addInitScript seeds localStorage["color-palettes"] with five local palettes A..E; navigate /#/palettes; fill input[placeholder="Search your palettes..."] with "e"; retrieve the app's own Sortable instance off .palette-card-grid via Object.keys(grid).find(k=>k.startsWith("Sortable")) and invoke options.onUpdate then options.onEnd with {oldIndex:0,newIndex:1}; read localStorage back. Persisted D,B,E,A,C.

**Proposed cure.** Retire `reorderPalettes(orderedIds: string[])` entirely — it is the wrong primitive because it makes every caller responsible for a totality the type system never states. Replace with a RELATIVE move the store can always satisfy against its own source array: `movePalette(id: string, before: string | null)`. The view supplies two identities from the gesture; the store performs one splice on `store.value.palettes`. A projection can correctly express "put A before C" even when B is filtered out, which a permutation structurally cannot. This transposition also subsumes L-1's cure.

Owner-edict #2 violation: `=== "unavailable"` is a masking fallback that maps two unhandled states onto "fine". `PaletteCardMenu.vue:217` `const apiOffline = computed(() => availability.value === "unavailable")` vs `demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:40-44` `export type ApiAvailability = "unknown" | "available" | "unavailable" | "misconfigured"` and `availability.ts:187-193` `assertApiAttemptAllowed()` which throws `DevMisconfigError` on `misconfigured` AND `ApiUnavailableError` on `unavailable`. Live measurement (probe-L3-misconfig-latch.mjs, one page load): LATCH-STATE surfaces = ["dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`", "The commons is unreachable."]; console = "[value.js] value.js dev is MISCONFIGURED: http://localhost:9000 has no VITE_API_URL … " plus "Failed to load remote palettes: DevMisconfigError"; and on the same session MENU = [{"text":"Publish","ariaDisabled":null,"dataDisabled":false}, …], `in-menu annotations rendered: []`. ```

**Reproduction.** `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/probe-L3-misconfig-latch.mjs` against the live dev server with VITE_API_URL unset. Or manually: `npm run dev:web-only` on a loopback origin, load /#/browse (trips the latch to `misconfigured`), then open any saved palette's card menu on /#/palettes — Publish is enabled with no `offline` annotation; clicking it throws DevMisconfigError synchronously.

**Proposed cure.** Move the predicate to its own layer as a TOTAL function: `demo/platform/transport/degraded.ts` exporting `describeAvailability(a: ApiAvailability): Degraded | null` as an exhaustive `switch` returning `{role, short, long, doomed}`. Adding a fifth latch member then becomes a compile error at ONE site instead of a silent `false` at three. `status-lamp.ts` becomes `isDev ? describeAvailability(a) : null` (the dev gate is the dock's policy, not the concept's — which is what made the pure resolver structurally unreachable from feature leaves). ApiOfflineChip consumes `long`; the menu consumes `short`+`doomed`. Generalised as Amendment 3 of the lattice: every domain predicate must be total over its union — the same rule dissolves the `isPublic` and `!palette.isLocal` defects.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure under demo/palettes/browser/` · LP2-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The Tags filter section is completely inert: SearchFilterBar binds `:checked` and `@update:checked` on glass-ui's Checkbox, but glass-ui 7.0.0 declares neither. Both bindings fall through to $attrs, so `toggleTag` is never invoked and `update:selectedTags` is never emitted; the control is additionally uncontrolled (modelValue undefined) so it can latch visually while selectedTags stays empty forever.

**Mechanism.** Markup written against a retired design-system API. Vue permits arbitrary fallthrough attributes on a component, so vue-tsc cannot reject an ABSENT prop (it is not wrong, it is missing) — the toolchain is structurally unable to see it. Same mistake disables tag filtering in the browse bar and tag editing in the popover.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55 binds `:checked="selectedTags.includes(tag.name)"` + `@update:checked="toggleTag(tag.name)"`. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/checkbox/Checkbox.vue.d.ts:4-11 declares `CheckboxProps { modelValue?: CheckedState | null; defaultValue?; disabled?; value?; id?; class? }` — no `checked` — and :21 declares the emit map `{ "update:modelValue": (value: CheckedState) => any }` — no `update:checked`. Blast radius measured: `grep -rn 'update:checked\|:checked=' demo --include=*.vue` returns exactly 4 sites in 2 files, both in this cluster (TagEditPopover.vue:28-29, SearchFilterBar.vue:52-53).
```

**Reproduction.** CONFIRMED by type declaration, not by click — the Playwright MCP profile was held by a concurrent seat ("Browser is already in use for .../mcp-chrome-83447af"). Pass 1 (challenge-L-library-pass1-c654824e.md, its L-1) reports measuring it live; the declarative evidence is independently sufficient since the named prop and emit do not exist in the installed package.

**Proposed cure.** Immediate: `:model-value` + `@update:model-value`. Structural (preferred): the component should own no tag-selection state at all — hoist all four filters into one `useBrowseQuery` store (see LP2-5 lattice) so the bar becomes a stateless view over `v-model:query` and a desynchronised control becomes unwriteable.

### `D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-sys` · D-2 · D

**Defect.** The login form cannot submit. `@submit.prevent` is bound to glass-ui 7's `SearchBar`, which is `inheritAttrs: false` and spreads all non-`class` attrs onto its inner `<input type="search">` rather than onto the `tag="form"` root. An `<input>` never fires `submit`, so the `<form>` carries no submit listener and nothing calls `preventDefault()` — the browser performs an unprevented native GET submission that reloads the SPA and discards the typed credential. Prior run identified the cause but could only argue the consequence 'from the HTML spec rather than a probe' (jsdom died at `requestSubmit`); this run reproduced the navigation in a real browser.

**Mechanism.** producer-contract misuse — SearchBar is a field, not a form host, but accepts `tag="form"` without objecting, so the consumer's `@submit` silently relocates to the inner input. Typecheck cannot see it: `onSubmit` is a legal fall-through attr. Landed in the glass-7 adoption commit f2c8f565.

**Evidence.**

```
CAUSE, compiled producer read directly: `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/search.js` — `inheritAttrs: !1`; `o = computed(() => { let {class: e, ...t} = useAttrs(); return t })` is spread into `b("input", w({ref_key:"inputRef", ref:s, type:"search"}, o.value, {...}))` while the root `j(e.tag)` receives only `class` and `data-surface`. CONSEQUENCE, WebKit, two arms (probes/psb-submit2.mjs): arm A listener-on-FORM -> `{handlerRuns:1, formStillPresent:true}`, navigations `[]`. arm B listener-on-INPUT -> `{handlerRuns:"gone (page navigated)", formStillPresent:false, url:"http://localhost:9000/?#/palettes?..."}`, 3 recorded main-frame navigations. The interposed `?` is the native GET-submission signature. Binding site: demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue:5-15.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteSlugBar/probes/psb-submit2.mjs (dev server live at :9000). Two arms print handlerRuns + recorded navigations.

**Proposed cure.** Architectural, not a patch: the component is deleted (D-1), so at the value.js altitude the cure is that the Account Dialog owns a real `<form @submit.prevent>` around a real `<input autocomplete=…>`, exactly as the live sibling demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:76-79 already does. Separately, a glass-ui BH/BI relay item: `SearchBar` must either refuse `tag="form"` or route non-input listeners to its root — every future consumer hits this silently.

### `D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-sys` · D-1 · D

**Defect.** The first drag-to-reorder of every session permutes the entire library and the scramble persists to localStorage. Drags 2..n are correct, hiding the defect from any two-drag manual test.

**Mechanism.** `useSortable(sortableEl, pm.filteredSaved.value, …)` passes a plain array, not the ref. `useFilteredList` returns `items.value` unchanged for an empty query, so that array IS the object the `savedPalettes` computed caches. vueuse's `defaultOptions.onUpdate` is spread BEFORE caller options and the caller supplies only `onEnd`, so the default survives; `moveArrayElement` takes the no-copy branch (`isRef` false) and `array.splice(from,1)` runs synchronously with the re-insert deferred to nextTick. SortableJS dispatches update->sort->end, so `onEnd` then maps N-1 ids; `reorderPalettes` places those and appends the two orphans at the tail. Traced by hand to `[P3,P4,P2,P5,P1]` — the exact measured value.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:183-197; useFilteredList.ts:9; node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js:14-15,32-35,78-88; node_modules/sortablejs/modular/sortable.esm.js:2002-2028; usePaletteStore.ts:153-167. Measured (scratchpad/drag2.mjs, 3/3 fresh WebKit contexts): `store before: P1,P2,P3,P4,P5` / `store after : P3,P4,P2,P5,P1` / `(intended: P2,P3,P1,P4,P5)`. Same session: `drag#1 *** WRONG ***`, `drag#2 OK`, `drag#3 OK`.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/drag2.mjs — seed 5 palettes into localStorage key `color-palettes`, load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, drag row 1's `.drag-handle` onto row 3's centre, read the store. Deterministic 3/3 in fresh contexts.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the useSortable/SortableJS dependency. Reorder is a model operation on an ordinal and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 already specifies it as one (Space grabs, Up/Down move, Home/End, Space drops, Escape cancels, announce `position of total`). Emit `move(id, delta)` against the store's own order — never a filtered projection, never a captured array. Kills D-1, D-1b and D-9 together and removes a library.

### `D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-sys` · D-1b · D

**Defect.** Reordering while a search filter is active silently rewrites the positions of palettes the user cannot see.

**Mechanism.** `onEnd` builds the id list from the filtered projection; `reorderPalettes` treats that partial list as the head of the new order and appends the unmatched remainder, so any filtered reorder hoists every match to the top of the library and demotes every non-match.

**Evidence.**

```
PalettesPane.vue:190-195 maps only `pm.filteredSaved.value` ids; usePaletteStore.ts:163-165 appends everything not in the id list. Measured: `store before: P1,P2,P3,zebra one,zebra two` -> query 'zebra' -> swap the 2 visible rows -> `store after : zebra two,zebra one,P1,P2,P3`.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/drag2.mjs (TEST4) — seed 3 palettes plus 2 named 'zebra …', type 'zebra' in the search field, drag the first visible row onto the second, read the store.

**Proposed cure.** Same as D-1: the reorder verb must address the store's order, and a filtered view must either disable reorder or map the moved ordinal back through the projection before writing.

### `D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-sys` · D-2 · D

**Defect.** The pastel-rainbow identity — one of exactly two sanctioned colour-bearing text sites in the product — is chromatically dead in dark mode; it renders as white with an imperceptible tint.

**Mechanism.** `certifyAccentInk`'s cusp walk does not stop AT the floor; it runs to the end of its reach, landing at OKLCH L 0.958 where the sRGB gamut cusp permits almost no chroma at any hue. The entire chroma budget is spent buying contrast nobody asked for. Not a gamut limit: oklch(0.72 0.150 329.8) -> rgb(216,127,209) measures 3.19:1 in gamut, and oklch(0.75 0.140 9.8) -> rgb(248,134,154) measures 3.57:1 — C ~0.14-0.15 at the declared floor, ~6x the shipped dark chroma.

**Evidence.**

```
VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §2 verbatim: 'Both coordinates render in light and dark.' Measured live root tokens: LIGHT `--palettes-ramp-title-{0,1,2}` C = 0.188343 / 0.188343 / 0.124795 (mean 0.16716); DARK C = 0.033662 / 0.021053 / 0.023120 (mean 0.02594) — dark is 15.5% of light, a 6.44x collapse. Ramp arc dE(OKLab) first->last: 0.2071 light vs 0.0374 dark (5.5x less). Pixel-sampled from the tracked Safari captures: light mean C 0.1649, dark mean C 0.0227, versus neutral `My` ink C 0.0061/0.0063. Contrast measured against the sampled dark plate rgb(94,72,65): shipped ink 7.47:1 against a declared RAMP_LARGE_TEXT_CONTRAST_FLOOR of 3 — a 2.49x overshoot.
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with colorScheme dark and read `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--palettes-ramp-title-0..2')`. Or open docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-dark/palettes.png and compare with the light capture; scratchpad/ramp-chroma.py reproduces the pixel numbers.

**Proposed cure.** Make the walk stop at the floor by bisection instead of running to reach, and hold chroma at the cusp for the L actually chosen. The dark arm then lands in the pastel band the resolver's own doc promises, at the same chroma register as light.

### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, depende` · L-1 · L

**Defect.** The state layer imports the view and drives it through a template ref. `useAdminUsers.ts:14` imports the SFC type; `:27` holds its instance; `:95/117/132/146` + `usePalettePorts.ts:123` mutate component-private state through a 5-member `defineExpose` (`AdminUsersPanel.vue:389`). The handle is published on the app-wide ADMIN port (`usePalettePorts.ts:197`) and the mount site BORROWS it (`AdminPane.vue:134`). Type cycle: useAdminUsers -> browser/admin/index.ts -> AdminUsersPanel.vue -> usePalettePorts -> useAdminUsers. Consequence: `onAdminDeleteUserPalette` (`useAdminUsers.ts:112-125`) updates the panel copy and the server but NEVER `deps.remotePalettes` — while its sibling `onAdminDeletePalette` (`:101-110`) does — so Browse renders a deleted palette until reload.

**Mechanism.** Inverted ownership: one concept ('the palettes of the expanded admin user') has its STORAGE in the view (AdminUsersPanel.vue:236-238) and its MUTATORS in the composable, bridged by a broadcast instance handle. The lower layer depends on the higher one.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:14,27,95,117,132,146; demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:123,197; demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:27,134; demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:389. Divergence re-read this pass at useAdminUsers.ts:112-125 (no `deps.remotePalettes` write) vs :101-110 (filter present).
```

**Reproduction.** Structural claim CONFIRMED by file:line. Behavioural reproduction (NOT executed — needs an admin token and the step is destructive; this seat is read-only): authenticate as admin -> #/browse, note palette P -> #/admin/users, expand P's owner -> delete P from the row -> #/browse: P is still listed.

**Proposed cure.** Lift the three refs into `useAdminUserPalettes()` beside `useAdminUsers` — it is the same server-state slice the composable already writes. The panel receives expandedUserSlug/userPalettes/loadingUserPalettes as props and emits toggleUserExpand. Then delete, in order: AdminUsersPanel.vue:389, :352-387, useAdminUsers.ts:14+:27 and its four `?.` sites, usePalettePorts.ts:123+:197, AdminPane.vue:27+:134. The remotePalettes divergence becomes unrepresentable because one module then sees both lists.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/composables/useSliderTouchGates.ts:57-68 — `if (!gate.isTouchDevice) return; if (!gate.isActive.value) { e.stopPropagation(); gate.handleTouchStart(el, e.clientY); }` — e.pointerType is never read. gate.isTouchDevice comes from node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useTouchGate-B4mzQcHJ.js:20 `l = typeof window < "u" && "ontouchstart" in window`. MEASURED (scratchpad/probe8.mjs, two contexts, identical 1440x900 viewport and identical mouse gesture at 15% of the R track): plainDesktop {ontouchstart:false, maxTouchPoints:0} before ["200","80","40","100%"] afterClick1 ["36","80","40","100%"] firstClickWorked:true — touchCapableDesktop {ontouchstart:true, maxTouchPoints:1} before ["200","80","40","100%"] afterClick1 ["200","80","40","100%"] afterClick2 ["36","80","40","100%"] firstClickWorked:false secondClickWorked:true.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/probe8.mjs against http://localhost:9000 — launch two Chromium contexts at 1440x900, one with hasTouch:false and one with hasTouch:true, navigate to /#/?space=rgb&color=rgb(200%2080%2040), mouse.down()+mouse.up() at 15% of the first .slider-track, read the .channel-meter texts. Without touch the R meter goes 200->36 on click 1; with touch it stays 200 until click 2.

**Proposed cure.** The gate's predicate is per-EVENT, not per-DEVICE. Delete the construction-time isTouchDevice sniff from the consumer entirely and gate on `e.pointerType === "touch"` inside the handler — the exact field Pointer Events provides for this question. That also deletes the second, independent copy of the sniff this component carries (useSliderTouchGates.ts:27-28, consumed as spectrumGateIsTouchDevice at ComponentSliders.vue:203): one predicate, one place. The real transposition is upstream — glass-ui's useTouchGate should take the event, not the device, making this a producer RELAY rather than a demo-side condition.

PERMANENT WEDGE (probe3.mjs): pre ["60.0%","0.1","30.0deg","100.0%"] / duringErrs ["Missing oklch.h"] / afterOrdinaryEdit to oklch(80% 0.2 200) STILL ["60.0%","0.1","30.0deg","100.0%"] with afterErrs [] / afterSpaceChange to rgb STILL ["60.0%","0.1","30.0deg","100.0%"]. COLD PATH (probe7.mjs): rgb(255 0 0) control = 4 strips/1 console/1 spectrum; rgb(255 0 0 / none) = 0/0/0, main innerText "This panel hit an unexpected error. color_missing_alpha Try again"; rgb(none 0 0) and oklch(50% 0.1 none) = 0/0/0, `[Vue warn]: Unhandled error during execution of setup function at <App>` + `pageerror: color_missing_channel at valueOrThrow (picker-color.ts:154:8) at convertPickerColor (:162:9) at useColorPipeline (useColorPipeline.ts:57:18) at setup (App.vue:77:20)`, main innerText EMPTY.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/probe3.mjs — load /#/?space=oklch&color=oklch(60%25%200.15%2030), then set location.hash to #/?space=oklch&color=oklch(50%25%200.1%20none): pageerror 'Missing oklch.h' fires and every subsequent hash-driven colour edit and space change is ignored while the meters stay frozen. node scratchpad/probe7.mjs — cold-load /#/?space=rgb&color=rgb(none%200%200) and observe 0 .channel-strip, 0 .sliders-console, 0 .spectrum-picker and an empty main.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPic` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The hero readout renders `contenteditable="true"` on a span whose children Vue owns and patches (`.fig-int`/`.fig-frac`). Any user edit replaces those nodes; every later patch writes into detached nodes and silently no-ops, so the cell is permanently orphaned from the vdom and displays a value that is not the color.

**Mechanism.** Vue-controlled subtree made user-writable: contenteditable lets the browser mutate DOM that the virtual DOM believes it owns, so vnode-held element references go stale and patching becomes a no-op.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/ColorComponentDisplay.vue:21-39. Live Playwright probe against http://localhost:9000/#/ returned: {"afterTyping":["45","20.1","10"],"afterTypingInnerHTML":"<b>45</b>","afterSliderDrag_cells":["45","20.1","10"],"afterSliderDrag_innerHTML":"<b>45</b>","afterSliderDrag_meter":["43.8%","20.1","10.0","100.0%"],"url":"http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(43.8%25+20.05+10)"} — URL, page title and channel meter all say 43.8; the hero readout says 45. The `<b>` wrapper proves the browser destroyed Vue's two child spans (and that the field accepts arbitrary rich text/paste).
```

**Reproduction.** 1) Open http://localhost:9000/#/ . 2) Click the `l` readout cell, press Cmd+A, type `45`, wait 1200ms. 3) Focus the L channel slider thumb (`.channel-slider [role="slider"]` first) and press ArrowLeft 12 times. 4) Read `document.querySelectorAll('.readout-fig')[0].innerText` (= "45") against `location.href` and `.channel-meter` (= 43.8%).

**Proposed cure.** Architectural transposition, already half-ordered by W48 §Work-1: delete the contenteditable path entirely; render the tuple as a read-only numeric headline and put editing in real `<input type="number">` controls. A Vue-controlled subtree may never be contenteditable — there is no patch that makes it safe. Also strengthen W48's completion gate: its `agree in one settled routed frame` check is single-frame and would pass with this defect fully present; it must edit a cell, then change the color by an independent path, then assert agreement.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPic` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** All five channels share ONE 500ms debounce timer instance, so a numeric edit to channel A silently cancels a pending edit to channel B. User edits are lost with no error and no visual signal.

**Mechanism.** Debounce over a multiplexed argument: the primitive assumes successive calls express the same pending intent, but the `component` argument makes each call a distinct intent, so coalescing them is data loss rather than throttling.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts:209 (`const updateColorComponentDebounced = debounce(updateColorComponent, 500)`) over the single-timer closure at demo/shared/utils.ts:22-44; both ColorPicker.vue:51 and ColorPicker.vue:233 route every channel through that one instance. Unit repro via `npx tsx`: an `l` write at t=0 and an `a` write at t=100ms produced `applied writes: [[80,"a"]]` — the `l` write never executed. Live repro from `lab(80% 20 30)`: typed `30` into `l`, then 120ms later `10` into `b`; final `url":"http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(80%25+20+10)"` — b took 10, l is still 80, the `30` is gone.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(80%25+20+30) . Click the `l` readout cell, Cmd+A, type `30`. Within 500ms click the `b` cell, Cmd+A, type `10`. Wait 1.5s and read location.href — it reads lab(80% 20 10); the l edit is discarded.

**Proposed cure.** Key the debounce per channel (`Map<string, debounced>`) — or, KISS and preferred with C-1's cure, drop the debounce entirely: real `<input>` editors commit on change/blur and need no coalescing. Note W48 §Work-3 makes 'W21 numeric fields the sole editors' without noticing this, so landing those fields on the same shared instance would reship the defect in new markup.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPic` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The window keydown listener is registered in `onMounted` while the component lives inside `<KeepAlive>`, so `onUnmounted` never fires on deactivation. The listener stays live on every other route and calls `e.preventDefault()`, hijacking Cmd+K app-wide.

**Mechanism.** KeepAlive lifecycle mismatch: mount/unmount hooks used where activate/deactivate hooks are required, so a global side effect outlives the component's visible lifetime.

**Evidence.**

```
ColorPicker.vue:376-385 (onMounted/onUnmounted) under demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120-127 (`<KeepAlive :max="6">`), mounted at demo/color-picker/App.vue:101-110. Live probe after SPA-internal navigation to #/gradient: {"afterSwitch":{"hash":"#/gradient","pickerInDom":false,"gradientPresent":true},"events":[{"k":"Meta","meta":true,"dp":false},{"k":"k","meta":true,"dp":true}],"pickerExpanded":"absent"} — the picker is NOT in the document yet its handler still ran and still returned defaultPrevented=true. The correct idiom is used in the same directory: demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:246 uses onActivated() and explains why at :232-245.
```

**Reproduction.** 1) Load http://localhost:9000/#/ and wait for the picker to mount. 2) `location.hash = '#/gradient'` (SPA route change, no reload); wait 2.5s; confirm `document.querySelector('.title-row button')` is null. 3) Install a window keydown logger, press Meta+k. 4) The logged event has defaultPrevented === true. Measured parser behaviour via `npx tsx` against src/css/index.ts: "oklch()" THREW TypeError Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace'); "light-dark(#fff, #000)" NOT-OK; "color-mix(in oklab, red, blue)" NOT-OK; "currentcolor" NOT-OK; "#12345" NOT-OK. The same hole exists on the second exposed entry point: useColorPipeline.ts:182-188 (`applyExternalColor`) parses unguarded and usePaletteWiring.ts:122-123 calls it directly — while onPaletteAddColor/onPaletteApply/applyColorString (useColorPipeline.ts:212-257) DO try/catch, showing the guarding is inconsistent.

End-to-end: a stored palette color of `color-mix(in oklab, red, blue)`, `light-dark(#fff,#000)`, `currentcolor` or `oklch()` returned by api.color.babb.dev, then clicking that swatch's edit affordance, hits ColorPicker.vue:286 unguarded. **Reproduction.** Serve the demo (http://localhost:9000/), open #/?space=lab&color=lab(50%25%2020%2030) at 1440x900, wait for settle, focus the second [contenteditable="true"][role="textbox"] cell, collapse the selection to the end of its contents, document.execCommand('insertText', false, '5'), wait 900ms, then read the cell text, every [role=slider] aria-valuetext, location.hash and document.title. If an inspector is genuinely absent, §3.1 is explicit that it "leaves no filler" — the stage takes the full width rather than being halved by a peer document. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-01 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The plate is invariant under the colour-space selection — the flagship instrument of a colour-space laboratory paints the same hard-coded sRGB HSV field in Lab, OKLCh and HSL. Its only reactive input is the HSV hue; s and v are axes of a space the user did not select and, in Lab/OKLCh/XYZ, cannot select.

**Mechanism.** A CSS linear-gradient can only express sRGB HSV, so the field's parameterisation is frozen at authoring time and cannot be a function of the selected space. Every downstream row (D-11 gamut, D-18 dead black area, D-05 no edge, D-14 background-size animation) descends from this one choice.

**Evidence.**

```
probe/SPCD-probe3.json .spaceInvariance — computed background-image is BYTE-IDENTICAL across all three spaces: `linear-gradient(to top, rgb(0,0,0), rgba(0,0,0,0)), linear-gradient(to right, rgb(255,255,255), rgb(255,0,59))`; dot left/top identical at 62.7886%/0%; aria-label identical; only the readout changes (92.0%,88.8,20.0 → 95.8%,0.3,9.8deg). Source: useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:36-39. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:5 ("chromatic laboratory… one dominant instrument"), :42 (Picker protagonist = "optical color stage"), :182 ("The optical stage dominates").
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/picker-spectrumcanvas/probe/SPCD-probe3.mjs against a live http://localhost:9000 — section 1 switches the space selector and diffs getComputedStyle(.spectrum-picker).backgroundImage. Manually: open /#/, note the plate, switch Lab→OKLCh in the space selector, observe zero change.

**Proposed cure.** Make the file's own name true. Replace the gradient div with a stage that paints a projection of the SELECTED space (two of its axes at the third's current value, gamut-mapped) — one canvas or paint worklet, one projection function per space, owned by one composable. The dot's (s,v) model becomes (axis1, axis2) of the selected space, which simultaneously supplies D-04's two named numeric axes, gives D-11's overlay a real gamut boundary to draw, gives D-05 a surface that can own an edge, and stops D-18's black wedge. This single transposition closes D-01, D-04, D-05, D-09, D-10, D-11, D-14, D-18 and makes D-06/D-07 trivial.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-02 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Under RTL the marker renders 267 px outside the instrument. `.spectrum-dot { position: absolute }` loses a silent specificity tie to the glass-ui producer's `.watercolor-swatch{position:relative}`, so the marker is an in-flow flex item whose left/top are offsets from its static position — x=0 in LTR (correct by coincidence), x=width−28 in RTL.

**Evidence.**

```
probe/SPCD-probe4.json .rtl → dotCenterFractionFromPlateLeft = 1.5682, i.e. 0.5682 × 469.06 px = 266.5 px beyond the plate's right edge. probe/SPCD-probe5.mjs output → getComputedStyle('.spectrum-dot').position === "relative", getComputedStyle(plate).display === "flex". Arithmetic check: (469.06−28)/469.06 + 0.6279 = 1.568, matching to four decimals. Source: SpectrumCanvas.vue:260 vs glass-ui.css `.watercolor-swatch[data-v-292b9032]{…position:relative}` — both specificity (0,2,0), producer wins on source order.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/SPCD-probe4.mjs (section 3), or on the live /#/ route run document.documentElement.setAttribute("dir","rtl") and observe the marker fly out of the plate onto the About pane.

The marker's positioning belongs to the stage: place it with the stage's own absolutely-positioned seat element (which also gives D-09 its "named enclosing geometric seat" and D-10 a place to clip), and move it with translate/transform (D-07) rather than left/top. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-03 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** `pointercancel` commits the aborted gesture instead of reverting it. handleSpectrumCancel, handleSpectrumUp and onLostPointerCapture all call the same stopDragging(), which FLUSHES pendingCoords. No pre-gesture colour is stored anywhere, so a revert is structurally impossible.

**Mechanism.** Three semantically distinct terminations (completed / aborted by platform / capture stolen) collapsed into one handler, with no latched pre-gesture state to restore to.

**Evidence.**

```
probe/SPCD-probe4.json .cancel — before: saturation 63%/lightness 100% (readout 92.0%,88.8,20.0); pointerdown at (25%,75%): 25%/25% (21.7%,8.0,0.6); drag to (85%,15%) then dispatch pointercancel: **85%/85% (48.1%,68.9,26.2)**. Source: SpectrumCanvas.vue:182-185 (cancel) and :187-200 (stopDragging flushes pendingCoords at :191-194). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 "Tuning is continuous and interruptible."
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/SPCD-probe4.mjs (section 1). On iOS the live path is a system edge-swipe or scroll takeover mid-drag, which silently rewrites the user's colour.

**Proposed cure.** Latch the colour at pointerdown into a ref. pointerup commits; pointercancel and lostpointercapture restore the latch and drop pendingCoords without flushing. Three lines and one ref, and it makes the §5 select→tune→commit grammar true rather than asserted.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The ornament is achromatic and has no figure-ground separation from its own plate: rendered ΔL(bead, plate) = 0.0168 OKLab vs the 0.15 INK_FLOOR the code claims to enforce; rendered bead chroma is 16% (light) / 1.7% (dark) of the picked chroma.

**Mechanism.** Open-loop photometric correction: the floor is computed against a MODELLED plate lightness and applied to the renderer's INPUT palette, never compared to the renderer's OUTPUT. Compounded by the derivation choice — `node -e "import('@mkbabb/glass-ui/color')"` gives deriveBlobPalette('lab(92% 88.8 20)',{stopCount:4,harmony:'analogous',chromaCeiling:0.2725}) -> L{0.8683,0.9283,0.9800,0.9800} C{0.0879,0.0388,0.0097,0.0099}, meanL 0.9392 meanC 0.0366, hex #ffbde0 #ffdde5 #fff6f6 #fff6f4 — two of four stops are white. floorStops then computes push=-0.2377 (flip branch: headroom 0.041 < need 0.062) yielding L{0.630,0.690,0.742,0.742} — yet the rendered bead measures L 0.848, i.e. the lit/Fresnel/SSS shader relights the body straight back to plate lightness and discards the correction entirely.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:73-78,93,97-111,117-130. Measured OKLab over composited pixels — live Chromium 1440 light: bead L 0.8347 C 0.0446, plate L 0.8515 C 0.0695, |ΔL| 0.0168, contrast 1.00:1. docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/picker.png: bead L 0.8494 C 0.0461, plate L 0.8649 C 0.0465, |ΔL| 0.0156. shots/safari-desktop-dark/picker.png: bead C 0.0047 (achromatic white pearl). Seed lab(92% 88.8 20) = OKLCH(0.9583, C 0.2724, H 9.8). Owner mark: audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-6-blob-vibrancy.png.
```

**Reproduction.** 1) node --input-type=module -e "const m=await import('@mkbabb/glass-ui/color'); const s=m.cssToOklch('lab(92% 88.8 20)'); console.log(JSON.stringify(m.deriveBlobPalette('lab(92% 88.8 20)',{stopCount:4,harmony:'analogous',chromaCeiling:Math.max(0.16,s.C)})))" 2) open http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(92%25+88.8+20+/+82.7%25), screenshot the .hero-blob-anchor clip, convert to OKLab, compare the inner-0.75 body disc against a plate ring at 1.9-2.6 body radii clipped inside the card.

**Proposed cure.** Delete INK_FLOOR, floorStops and the chromaCeiling knob outright. Compute ONE number — bodyLightness = plateL ± 0.15, sign by headroom — and hand it to the producer's shipped seam (glass-ui/dist/composables/color/index.d.ts:118-126: "the body stop (t=0) anchors at exactly this L ... without moving the seed hue/chroma"). Proven: adding bodyLightness:0.70 lifts meanC 0.0366 -> 0.1405 with the body stop at C 0.242 = 89% of the seed. Then CLOSE THE LOOP: gate on the producer's exposed `settledFrame` sampled body pixels, never on the input stops. The palette-shaping policy leaves the consumer entirely.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** A parked blob still costs the picker route ~64% of its frame rate, permanently — violating VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 "Paused, parked and offscreen mean no animation work"; and it doubles the route's TBT.

**Mechanism.** The producer's `paused` seam freezes the visible delta (frame SHA-1 identical from t=8111ms through t=18577ms) but does not suspend the per-frame work; and the consumer never gates the mount on intersection or on the producer's `settled` quiescence read, so an ornament nobody is looking at holds full frame budget.

**Evidence.**

```
Own self-rescheduling rAF chain, 20s, no screenshot perturbation, only difference = route-level abort of .../demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue. CPU 1x: idle fps t>=10s 40.1 (mounted) vs 112.8 (blocked); TBT 468ms vs 0ms; long tasks [158,170][1921,518] vs [159,166]. CPU 4x: fps 33.6 vs 112.3; TBT 981 vs 373; 3-rep TBT median 661 vs 318 ms. The t>=10s window is entirely post-park (park completes 7.0-8.1s, proven by frozen frame hashes).
```

**Reproduction.** scratchpad/HBD-probe3.mjs: TAG=x CPU=1 node HBD-probe3.mjs vs TAG=y CPU=1 BLOCK=1 node HBD-probe3.mjs (BLOCK aborts only URLs matching /HeroBlob/i). Compare fpsBySec for t>=10 and tbt.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The demo discards the library's Result contract at the boundary and blanks the whole application. picker-color.ts:104-107 `valueOrThrow` converts every Result failure into a thrown PickerColorError; useColorPipeline.ts:74 calls it in root setup() unguarded; ErrorBoundary is mounted INSIDE App.vue's own template (App.vue:50, closing :140) so onErrorCaptured can never catch an ancestor's setup throw. CSS Color 4 `none` channels are legal and the library preserves them.

**Mechanism.** Error-contract ownership inversion: the library owns 'this may fail, here is why' (Result<T,E>); the demo bridge owns 'convert that to an exception'; the demo shell owns no recovery. The contract dies between hop one and hop two, and the only recovery mechanism is mounted one level too low to fire.

**Evidence.**

```
PAGE-ERROR STACK: PickerColorError: color_missing_channel / at valueOrThrow (demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:154:8) / at convertPickerColor (picker-color.ts:162:9) / at useColorPipeline (useColorPipeline.ts:57:18) / at setup (App.vue:77:20) / at callWithErrorHandling … mountComponent … patch — then: `app innerText len: 0`, `body text sample: ` (empty), `sliders-console: 0  spectrum: 0`. Screenshot is a flat #b1748f FOUC-guard field, nothing else. Library side proven by node probe against dist: parseCssColor('oklch(none 0.2 30)') → {"ok":true,"value":{"space":"oklch","channels":["none",0.2,30],"alpha":1}}; convertColor(that,'oklch') → ok:true, none survives; convertColor(that,'rgb') → {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"color_missing_channel"}}. clampPickerColor passes "none" through explicitly (picker-color.ts:197). package.json:4 declares the library "failure-explicit".
```

**Reproduction.** With the dev server live: `node scratchpad/probe3.mjs "http://localhost:9000/#/?space=oklch&color=oklch(none%200.2%2030)"` (Playwright chromium, goto + waitForTimeout 2500, pageerror listener). Note the HASH route form is required — the app uses hash routing, so a non-hash query is ignored. Guarded paths for contrast: typing the same string in the color input is safe (useColorParsing.ts:39-44, 63-84 try/catch) and useColorUrl.applyUrlToModel is guarded (:44); ONLY boot/hydrate is bare — i.e. this is a shared-deep-link failure.

**Proposed cure.** Architectural, not a patch. Delete `valueOrThrow` outright — do not relocate it. picker-color.ts's public surface returns the library's `Result` unchanged (the type already ships). useColorPipeline accepts a Result at hydrate and, on !ok, seeds the documented default color and surfaces `diagnostics` through the existing status-lamp channel. Independently, hoist ErrorBoundary ABOVE App.vue — wrap <App/> at the createApp mount site in the boot entry — which is the only position from which a root-setup throw is catchable. Born-RED gate: navigate the URL above and assert #app innerText length > 0 with zero page errors.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** App-scoped state (ActionBarContext + the colour-edit state machine) lives inside a KeepAlive'd route-leaf component and is reached by instance ref; the mobile mount path never captures that ref, so the picker's entire dock action bar is absent at mobile widths.

**Mechanism.** Ownership inversion — state whose lifetime must be the app's is assembled in a component whose lifetime is a pane-routing accident, then reached imperatively through a template ref captured on only one of two mount paths.

**Evidence.**

```
ColorPicker.vue:315-328 builds actionBarContext; :331-344 defineExpose. App.vue:38 `:action-bar="colorPickerRef?.actionBarContext ?? null"`, :41-42 commit/cancel, :342 usePaneRouter, :351 usePaletteWiring. colorPickerRef is populated only by onDesktopLeftMount (App.vue:323-328), wired to the desktop PaneSlots at :105 and :131; the mobile PaneSlot at App.vue:83-91 passes no :on-mount, and PaneSlot.vue:124 renders `:ref="onMount ? ... : undefined"`. MEASURED live at http://localhost:9000/#/ : at 1440x900 nav exposes Back, Reset color, Copy color, Random color, Palettes, Extract palette, Open color input; at 390x844 (data-layout=mobile) it exposes NONE and the #action-bar DockLayer is absent from the DOM (actionBarLayerPresent:false), with the toggle surviving as a 32x32 button inside a 0-width .action-bar-toggle-slot at tabindex=-1. Corroborated by the shipped shots: safari-desktop-light/picker.png shows the 'Tools' group; safari-mobile-light/picker.png does not.
```

**Reproduction.** With the dev server on :9000, open http://localhost:9000/#/ at 1440x900 and evaluate `[...document.querySelectorAll('nav button')].map(b=>b.getAttribute('aria-label'))` -> includes 'Reset color','Copy color','Random color','Palettes','Extract palette','Open color input'. Resize to 390x844, reload http://localhost:9000/#/, evaluate the same -> none of those six; `!!document.querySelector('nav [id="action-bar"]')` -> false.

**Proposed cure.** Move ActionBarContext and the commit/cancel edit machine into a color-session composable (useColorEditSession / useActionBarContext) provided by App beside COLOR_MODEL_KEY; the Dock injects it. defineExpose and colorPickerRef disappear entirely, and with them usePaletteWiring's picker parameter and its retry loop.

### `design (CHALLENGE-D) — visual truth, state coverage, motion,` · D-1 · design (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** The "ONE container-scaled rhythm law" (:318-333) is a two-state step function whose clamp ceilings are structurally unreachable dead code. The comment claims it retired a hard `<lg` band switch for a rhythm that is "a smooth function of width, never two hand-tuned states". It is not: the `cqi` container (.pane-wrapper, shell.css:83) is itself capped at `--pane-max: 32rem` (foundation.css:441), so the ceilings 2.625rem/42px (needs 600px container) and 0.5rem/8px (needs 533px) can never be reached, and the shipped rhythm has exactly TWO values switching at the pane-layout breakpoint. The discontinuity survived at reduced amplitude (1.83x -> 1.12x); only its disguise changed. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.7 ("No desktop-tight/mobile-airy fork and no breakpoint pile") and PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.8 ("Real rendered relation wins over token intent").

**Mechanism.** a fluid unit measured against a container that is itself clamped to a constant — the fluidity is nominal, the clamp arms are unexecutable, and the real breakpoint moved from a media query into the layout

**Evidence.**

```
demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:328-333. Measured .pane-wrapper inline-size and resolved rhythm (scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs -> CSD-out.json): 1440 -> container 512.00, min-block-size 35.84px, row-gap 7.68px | 3440 -> container 512.00, 35.84px, 7.68px (BYTE-IDENTICAL to 1440) | 390 -> container 358.00, 7cqi=25.06 -> FLOOR 32.00px, 1.5cqi=5.37 -> FLOOR 6.00px | 320 -> container 288.00, 7cqi=20.16 -> FLOOR 32.00px, gap FLOOR 6.00px. Container cap: `--pane-max: 32rem` at demo/styles/foundation.css:441; grid clamp recorded at demo/DESIGN.md:358. Same clamp copy-duplicated at demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:216.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs against http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(92%25+88.8+20+/+82.7%25) at viewports 1440/3440/390/320; read paneWrapperWidth, rowGap, stripMinBlock

**Proposed cure.** Delete both cqi clamps. The row is not a function of the pane container (a clamped constant) but of the control it houses: `min-block-size: calc(var(--slider-track-block) + 2 * var(--console-row-air))` with the track metric fed by the producer and the air a glass-ui spacing rung. If two densities are genuinely wanted they are a named `density` rung declared once on the producer Slider/Card, not a clamp pretending to be continuous. One home for the rhythm, consumed by ConfigSliderPane instead of cloned.

### `design (CHALLENGE-D) — visual truth, state coverage, motion,` · D-2 · design (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** The channel drag thumb is a 12px-wide operable target in every render matrix, failing WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (24x24 minimum) on the inline axis. The `@media (pointer: coarse) .channel-slider::before` hit-area extension addresses the wrong element and the wrong axis: it sits on the SliderRoot and grows only the block axis (`inset-inline: 0; block-size: max(100%, 2.75rem)`), so it enlarges the track-TAP zone (a press there is a value jump) and never the thumb-DRAG zone (a press there is a grab). PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.7 ("Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities") is the exact law broken — all three were conflated into one pseudo-element on the wrong box.

**Mechanism.** a consumer pseudo-element attempting to resize a node the consumer does not own — the affordance is extended on the ancestor while the target the interaction actually requires (the thumb) is untouched

**Evidence.**

```
demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:345-357. Measured [role="slider"] rects (scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs): desktop-1440 12x24 (::before content:none) | desktop-3440 12x24 | narrow-320 12x24 | mobile-390 fine-pointer 12x24 (::before content:none — no extension at all) | mobile-390 COARSE 12x44 (::before content:"", height 44px — height moved, WIDTH STAYED 12) | forced-colors-1440 12x24. Independently corroborated by the shipped matrix: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json lists all four thumbs under smallTapTargets in ALL FOUR Safari matrices, e.g. {"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"L channel"} (safari-desktop-light /#/) and {"w":12,"h":44,"tag":"span","label":"ALPHA channel"} (safari-mobile-dark /#/). Desktop row block = 35.84px around a 24px control (+49% dead block) despite the comment at :335-344 claiming the rung is preserved "not [by] row inflation".
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs; compare thumb rects across the `mobile-390` and `mobile-390-coarse` contexts. Or read REPORT.json results[].probe.a11y.smallTapTargets for route /#/ in any of the four Safari matrices.

**Proposed cure.** Thumb geometry is a producer concern. glass-ui `Slider` must expose a density/thumb rung whose coarse arm is >=24px inline (44 preferred) AT THE ROOT; the consumer then deletes `::before` outright rather than compensating around it. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8; lead the BH/BI relay packet with this row since it is the one with a shipped accessibility consequence.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/scenes/abou` · K-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `output: "htmlAndMathml"` (Katex.vue:41) puts KaTeX's raw-LaTeX `<annotation>` into the accessible name on WebKit, so all 64 formulas are announced twice — once as math, once as raw TeX source. Chromium hides the annotation via its UA MathML stylesheet; WebKit does not.

**Mechanism.** A vendor option chosen for accessibility whose accessibility behaviour was never measured on the declared target engine. The component trusts a third-party stylesheet to hide a node that the third-party stylesheet does not hide, and the hidden-but-exposed (`clip`/1x1px) pattern is exactly the pattern that keeps a node in the a11y tree.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/scenes/about/katex/Katex.vue:41 `output: "htmlAndMathml"`. probes/KTX-probe7.mjs against the live dev server, both engines:
webkit → {"annotationDisplay": "block", "annotationVisible": false, "mathDisplay": "block"}; ariaSnapshot: "- math: \"f ( t ) = { t 3 t > ϵ κ t + 16 116 otherwise f(t) = \\begin{cases} \\sqrt[3]{t} & t > \\epsilon \\\\ \\frac{\\kappa\\, t + 16}{116} & \\text{otherwise} \\end{cases}\""; aria contains raw TeX: true
chromium → {"annotationDisplay": "none"}; ariaSnapshot: "- math: \"f ( t ) = { t 3 t > ϵ κ t + 16 116 otherwise\""; aria contains raw TeX: false
Corpus scope: `grep -o "<Katex" assets/docs/*.md | wc -l` → 64 across 11 documents. The component's own comment at Katex.vue:34-40 asserts the MathML layer is there "for the accessibility tree" and names the WebKit/S-22 risk.
```

**Reproduction.** node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/Katex/probes/KTX-probe7.mjs   (dev server live on http://localhost:9000; navigates /#/, scrolls the first display formula into view, takes locator.ariaSnapshot() in webkit then chromium)

**Proposed cure.** One rule beside the existing global stylesheet import (Katex.vue:20) or in demo/styles/: `.katex-mathml annotation { display: none; }`. VALIDATED LIVE in real WebKit via probes/KTX-cure.mjs + page.addStyleTag — BEFORE: `- math: "... otherwise f(t) = \begin{cases} \sqrt[3]{t} ..."`; AFTER: `- math: "f ( t ) = { t 3 t > ϵ κ t + 16 116 otherwise"`; `still contains raw TeX: false`.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/scenes/about/ma` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Unguarded `await module()` in an async onMounted turns a content-area fetch failure into an app-wide crash, and makes the component's own designed error branch unreachable dead code.

**Mechanism.** unguarded-async-rejection escalating through a coarse-grained error boundary; designed fallback branch has no reachable input state

**Evidence.**

```
Markdown.vue:58-62 (`currentDoc.value = await module()` — no try/catch/finally), :69-71 (`onMounted(async () => { await loadDocs(); })`), :19-31 (the unreachable `v-else` Alert). Boundary scope: App.vue:50 wraps the whole `<main>` two-pane grid; ErrorBoundary.vue:59 `onErrorCaptured` returns false. Measured: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/Markdown/probe-C3.mjs abort` → {"aboutCardPresent": false, "mdBody": false, "wrapper": false, "skeletons": 0, "trap": {"rejections": [], "errors": []}, tailHTML ends `…lucide-rotate-ccw…> Try again</button></div></main>`}. Frame: frames/C3-abort.png shows the entire app replaced by a bare "Try again" button.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/Markdown/probe-C3.mjs abort — Playwright/WebKit routes /assets/docs/*.md to route.abort("failed"), loads http://localhost:9000/#/, waits 15s, dumps the tree.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The certified-accent heading ink system collapses to a single perceptual ink in dark mode: every rung of the h2/h3/prose ladder falls at or below the OKLab JND, an 8.3x weakening from light. The component's headline design idea does not exist in the dark scheme.

**Mechanism.** certifyAccentInk enforces a WCAG contrast FLOOR against the plate but carries no SEPARATION obligation from the body ink or the adjacent rung. Against a dark plate the floor walk has nowhere to go but toward white, so lightness rises to 0.958 and chroma is gamut-mapped to 0.021. The h3 rung then mixes 61.8% of an already-near-white accent toward an already-near-white foreground, producing zero step.

**Evidence.**

```
docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/Markdown/evidence/M2-rhythm-inks-light.json and M3-rhythm-inks-dark.json. Measured deltaE_ok — h2 vs prose: LIGHT 0.3153 / DARK 0.0378 (8.3x); h3 vs prose: 0.1938 / 0.0230 (8.4x); mark vs prose: 0.3153 / 0.0378; h2 vs h3: 0.1215 / 0.0149 (8.2x). Accent chroma: light C=0.1887 -> dark C=0.0208 (9.1x collapse); dark accent = oklch(95.83% 0.021 9.83). Consuming sites: Markdown.vue:163,172,187,252,312; producer useMarkdownColors.ts:55-79. Visual: evidence/E2-populated-desktop-dark.png shows h2, h3 and prose all as plain white.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/Markdown/evidence/probe4.mjs light ; node .../probe4.mjs dark ; compare the deltaEok blocks. Dev server must be live at http://localhost:9000.

**Proposed cure.** Make the ink contract two-sided in the producer: certifyAccentInk gains a minSeparation obligation alongside its floor. When the floor walk would cross the separation minimum, the rung changes CARRIER (weight, size, or a rule) rather than silently converging on the body ink. Acceptance bench already exists: h2-vs-prose deltaE_ok >= 0.10 and h2-vs-h3 >= 0.05 in BOTH schemes, measured by probe4.mjs.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The designed error state is structurally unreachable, and the real doc-load failure mode tears down the entire route — picker included — instead of degrading in place.

**Mechanism.** An async lifecycle hook with no failure ownership. The success path is the only path the state machine models; the failure path exits the function before the state transition, so the third rendered branch is dead template and the rejection becomes the parent's problem.

**Evidence.**

```
Markdown.vue:58-62 — `currentDoc.value = await module(); isLoading.value = false;` with no try/catch, so a rejection leaves isLoading true forever and the v-else Alert branch (Markdown.vue:19-31, "Oh snap...") can never render. Rejection escapes onMounted (:69-71) into ErrorBoundary (demo/color-picker/App.vue:50-140, onErrorCaptured at ErrorBoundary.vue:59) which wraps the whole workspace. Measured with /assets/docs/*.md aborted: {"aboutCardPresent": false, "skeletonsPresent": 0, "markdownWrapperPresent": false, "alertPresent": false, "ohSnapPresent": false} — evidence/M7-failure-state.json. Screenshot evidence/E6-doc-load-failure-whole-route-collapse.png: both panes gone, bare "Try again" button on the ambient field. Also AboutPane.vue:50-51 already guards v-if="activeMarkdownModule", so the Alert's copy describes a condition the parent prevents — doubly dead. Violates PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:52 (PR-08) and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/Markdown/evidence/probe6.mjs failure — routes /assets/docs/*.md to abort('failed'), waits 9s, then reads the DOM and screenshots.

**Proposed cure.** The loader owns its failure. Three explicit states (loading | ready | failed) driven by try/catch/finally; the failed state renders IN PLACE as a named, retryable role="status" region scoped to the document region — not a stock Alert, and never an app-level unmount. Delete the unreachable Alert branch entirely (its copy is obsolete against the parent guard).

**Reproduction.** node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/blobprobe6.mjs then blobprobe7.mjs. Manually: load /#/blob, wait ~8s without touching anything, then drag Warp from 0.35 to 1.0 — nothing changes.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `resetDefaults()` is a shape-blind `Object.assign` that destroys the live picker→blob palette coupling — and it stays destroyed until the picker colour next changes.

**Mechanism.** Type erasure at the component boundary. Props are `config: Record<string, unknown>` / `defaults: Record<string, unknown>` (:41-52), so the only reset expressible is 'overwrite every top-level key'. The reads are shape-aware (dot-path, :57-64); the write is shape-blind. Reset semantics were re-minted demo-side while `@mkbabb/glass-ui/configurator` — already imported at :21 — ships `useConfiguratorState<T>.resetCurrent()` against a preset baseline plus per-row `canReset`/`@reset` on ConfiguratorRow.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:92-94 `Object.assign(config, structuredClone(defaults))`. BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.color.paletteStops = ['#b5947f','#d4b27d','#dad6b1'] (measured: `node --input-type=module -e "import {BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS} from './node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/blob-config.js'; console.log(BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.color.paletteStops)"`). The only writer is a non-deep watch at demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:389-401. BlobPane.vue:8-9 documents paletteStops as the live feed, deliberately not a slider.
```

**Reproduction.** Node, real producer defaults + real Vue reactivity, both code paths verbatim:
1. after boot          paletteStops = ["#derived1",...,"#derived4"]  derives: 1
2. after Reset click   paletteStops = ["#b5947f","#d4b27d","#dad6b1"]  derives: 1
3. 50ms later          paletteStops = ["#b5947f","#d4b27d","#dad6b1"]  derives: 1
4. after picker moves  paletteStops = ["#derived1",...,"#derived4"]  derives: 2
Collateral atoms also silently reverted: quality, morphT, satellites.absorbedDuration, surface.rimColor. Full script pasted in report §L-1.

**Proposed cure.** Delete `resetDefaults`. Adopt `useConfiguratorState<T>` with the two preset tables as `presets` so reset is restore-to-baseline over declared keys only, and add `can-reset` per ConfiguratorRow. A reset that can only touch declared slider keys cannot reach `paletteStops`.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L4-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The ESLint lattice enforcing the demo's module boundaries is dead and reports green. `no-restricted-imports` resolves to `undefined` for every file under `demo/`, including the subject component. Two of the three demo-side blocks (G-DEMO-1, G-DEMO-3a) have file globs pointing at `demo/@/components/**`, `demo/@/lib/**`, `demo/@/composables/**` — a tree W43/RF-15 deleted (vite.config.ts:68 records the cause). The one block whose glob still matches (`demo/color-picker/**`, G-DEMO-3b) bans the specifier `@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue`, and the `@components` alias was deleted by the same wave, so it matches zero imports. `npm run lint --max-warnings=0` exits 0, so the demo's module lattice reads as structurally enforced while enforcing nothing. Only the library-side ban (inv-K-1, glob `src/**/*.ts`) survives.

**Mechanism.** Enforcement drifted from the tree it guards. A restructure renamed the directories; the lint globs were not moved with them, and nothing detects a glob that matches zero files. The failure is silent and inverted: absent enforcement would be honest, but a rule that resolves to `undefined` under a passing `--max-warnings=0` gate manufactures a false green across every tranche document that cites G-DEMO-1/3a/3b as discharged.

**Evidence.**

```
`npx eslint --print-config demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue | jq '.rules["no-restricted-imports"]'` → `undefined`. Same for demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue and demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue. `npx eslint --print-config demo/color-picker/App.vue` → `[2,{"patterns":[{"group":["@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue"],…}]}]` while `grep -rn 'from "@components' demo/ --include="*.vue" --include="*.ts" | wc -l` → `0`. `ls -d demo/@ demo/@/components demo/@/composables demo/@/lib` → 4× "No such file or directory". `npx eslint --print-config src/index.ts` → inv-K-1 still live. Globs at eslint.config.js:232-238 and :275-278; ban prose at :249-251, :290-292, :294-296, :299-301. vite.config.ts:68 ("W43 (RF-15) killed the demo `@…` path aliases").
```

**Reproduction.** cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && npx eslint --print-config demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue | node -e "let s='';process.stdin.on('data',d=>s+=d).on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.parse(s).rules['no-restricted-imports']))"  # prints: undefined

**Proposed cure.** Three moves, the third being the durable one. (1) Re-point the three demo-side globs at the current tree (demo/{picker,scenes,shared,palettes,workbenches,shell,color-session}/**) and re-express the bans against current module names. (2) Add the two bans this audit's findings call for: bare `@mkbabb/glass-ui` (force the published subpath) and `**/demo/ui/*` (so the alias layer cannot regrow after deletion). (3) ARCHITECTURAL: make a zero-match `files` glob a build failure — a ten-line preflight asserting every configured glob resolves to ≥1 file. This is the one-home principle applied to enforcement itself: a rule and the tree it guards must not be able to drift apart in silence. Without it, every cure this audit programme lands is one rename away from becoming prose.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L4-C1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** CARRIED + INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED from r3 (its L-1). `Reset` silently destroys the live picker→blob palette coupling: `Object.assign(config, structuredClone(defaults))` is a whole-subtree overwrite, so pressing Reset on /#/blob replaces `config.color` entire — including `color.paletteStops`, the picker-derived ramp that BlobPane's own header comment declares is not a slider.

**Mechanism.** Re-minted reset semantics that are shape-blind: `resetDefaults` never consults `sections`, the only description of what is a knob, so it cannot express "restore the knobs, preserve the derived state". A second home for a concept glass-ui already owns.

**Evidence.**

```
ConfigSliderPane.vue:92-94; BlobPane.vue:8-9 states the invariant the pane then breaks; useAtmosphere.ts:381 mints the reactive config, :393 writes the derived stops; the recovery watch at :386-392 is keyed on `atmosphereColor`, so the blob stays wrong until the picker colour next changes. glass-ui ships the correct semantics: useConfiguratorState.d.ts:9-14,42 — `resetCurrent()` over a declared preset baseline with an injectable `clone` hook for exactly the derived/unclonable case. r3's node reproduction (paletteStops 4 user stops → glass-ui's canned 3-stop tan ramp) replays correctly against the installed glass-ui@7.0.0.
```

**Reproduction.** node --input-type=module -e "import {BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS} from '@mkbabb/glass-ui/blob-config'; const live=structuredClone(BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS); live.color.paletteStops=['#112233','#445566','#778899','#aabbcc']; Object.assign(live,structuredClone(BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS)); console.log(live.color.paletteStops)"

**Proposed cure.** Delete `resetDefaults`. Drive reset from `useConfiguratorState<BlobConfig>({presets})`, whose baseline is a declared preset rather than a raw defaults object; the derived `paletteStops` then sits outside the preset table by construction. Iterating `sections` and writing only slider paths is strictly worse — it keeps the second home for reset alive.

Measured contradiction on one route: nutrition label renders "Red0 to 255" while assets/docs/rgb.md one scroll below says "`R`: Red component (0 to 1)"; hsv label "0deg to 360deg" vs hsv.md "`H`: Hue (0 to 1)"; oklch label "C 0 to 0.5" vs oklch.md "C: Chroma (0 to ~0.4)" (ARCHITECTURE.md:97: raw 0-0.5, % reference 0.4 — neither copy models the distinction).
