### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Four of BlobPane's five Geometry sliders (and surface.fissionAmp, and color.paletteStops) never reach the renderer: HeroBlob.vue hard-writes literals after spreading the injected config, and it passes that object as the `config` PROP, which the producer's `config ?? injectedConfig` seam prefers outright. The pane's own header (BlobPane.vue:19-21) claims a compile-time guard against 'silently no-op'ing a slider' — the guard is type-level and cannot see an override authored in a different component.

**Mechanism.** A preset/override layer authored as literals inside a leaf view component instead of as data in the config module. glass-ui publishes both the concept (`ConfiguratorPreset<T>`) and a concrete blob hero preset (`BLOB_HERO`, glass-ui/dist/presets-5myqNv59.js, exported from ./blob-config) — `grep -rn 'BLOB_HERO' demo src test e2e` returns NOTHING, and the demo maintains a divergent second hero register inline (producer: orbitRadius 0.3 / satRadius 0.1 / ecc 0.04 / satCount 4 / smoothK 0.06; demo: bodyRadius 0.325 / orbitRadius 0.4 / satRadius 0.09 / ecc 0.03). Two hero registers alive = dual path.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:152-178 (`geometry: { ...appBlobConfig.geometry, bodyRadius: 0.325, orbitRadius: 0.4, satelliteRadius: 0.09, eccentricity: 0.03 }`) and HeroBlob.vue:13-19 (`<Blob :config="heroConfig">`); only one <Blob> exists in the demo (`grep -rn '<Blob\b' demo` → HeroBlob.vue:13). MEASURED via scratchpad/probe/props.mjs against the live dev server, reading props.config off the Blob instance through __vueParentComponent: `pane rows: Body Radius0.450 | Orbit Radius0.480 | Sat Radius0.200 | Eccentricity0.500 | Satellites4 | Warp1` vs `delivered to <Blob>: {"geometry":{"canvasSize":200,"bodyRadius":0.325,"satelliteCount":4,"satelliteRadius":0.09,"orbitRadius":0.4,"eccentricity":0.03},"surfaceFission":0.6,"membraneWarp":1}`. satelliteCount and warpAmp passing through prove the write mechanism itself works. Corroborated by docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/blob.png (pane prints 0.220, bead renders 0.325). SECOND repro: with the blob parked (BLOB_IDLE_MS 2000 + SLEEPY_POSE_MS 3300, HeroBlob.vue:211-225) four screenshots after Body-Radius-max, Satellites-max and Reset are byte-identical — sha256 1b24742e25fb3f534b028a983b241e18259d60c3939443421ee753667e0cc89e for all of hero-A/B/C/D.png — because noteBlobActivity() (HeroBlob.vue:216) is wired only to cssColorOpaque and savedColorStrings.length and has no idea a tuning pane exists.
```

**Reproduction.** Dev server at localhost:9000. `node scratchpad/probe/props.mjs` — loads /#/blob, drives Body Radius / Orbit Radius / Sat Radius / Eccentricity / Satellites / Warp to their maxima with the End key, then prints the pane readouts beside the config object actually delivered to the <Blob> component instance. Four rows diverge; two agree.

**Proposed cure.** Architectural transposition: the tuning pane must own its own stage and its own preset table. Replace ConfigSliderPane with glass-ui's shipped `<Configurator>`: `:presets="[{key:'default',config:BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS},{key:'hero',config:BLOB_HERO}]"` + `#stage` slot rendering its own <Blob> + `<ConfiguratorLayer>` per section. HeroBlob then SELECTS the 'hero' preset instead of hand-patching four keys. The readout becomes true by construction because the pane renders the blob it tunes.

**Defect.** `npm run gh-pages` at HEAD emits a 0.69 kB application bundle containing only Vite's modulepreload polyfill, alongside 59 KaTeX font files totalling 1.1 MB and no KaTeX stylesheet at all — 1.1 MB of orphan fonts in a non-functional artefact.

**Mechanism.** module-graph collapse at render time while the CSS asset graph still emits url() targets — cause UNIDENTIFIED. I formed and FALSIFIED the obvious hypothesis (package.json:19 "sideEffects": false applied to a demo graph with no demo/package.json, entry = demo/color-picker/index.html:205-213 inline module script whose whole body is pure side effect): forcing rolldownOptions.treeshake={moduleSideEffects:true} did NOT resurrect the bundle (ghp2 still 0.69 kB).

**Evidence.**

```
`npx vite build --mode gh-pages --outDir <scratch>/ghp --emptyOutDir` → "✓ built in 4.40s"; `ls <scratch>/ghp/assets | wc -l` → 63, of which 59 are KaTeX_*; non-font files are favicon-BpOvZXpk.svg, glass-fonts-DH5GtBvs.css, index-Dezn_h7o.js (0.69 kB), quantize-worker-*.js. `cat assets/index-Dezn_h7o.js` → modulepreload polyfill only, zero app code, zero katex JS, zero katex CSS. Identical result with deferGlassFonts() removed (ghp3: 62 files, 59 KaTeX, index still 0.69 kB). The checked-in dist/gh-pages (2026-07-27 18:46) has the identical 698-byte index-Dezn_h7o.js. shots/LIVE-color.babb.dev.png shows the deployed site rendering correctly → this is a regression at HEAD.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vite build --mode gh-pages --outDir /tmp/ghp --emptyOutDir ; ls /tmp/ghp/assets | wc -l ; cat /tmp/ghp/assets/index-*.js   (reproduced 3x from cold)

**Proposed cure.** Attribution stated plainly: this is the known W44 §F gh-pages empty-mount carry, independently reproduced, and NOT caused by Katex.vue. What is attributable is that anchoring the 1.1 MB KaTeX font corpus to a leaf scene component's side-effect CSS import is what makes it survive a build that drops everything else. The build-time transposition (L-5) removes the runtime engine and lets the ~90 kB of actually-used woff2 be emitted from demo/styles/ where the typography law lives. **Defect.** The demo typechecks `@mkbabb/value.js/css` against the PUBLISHED npm 4.0.0 tarball while running it against the LOCAL working-tree build. `tsconfig.demo.json#paths` is a hand-copied mirror of `package.json#exports` and has drifted in both directions: 3 phantom entries (`.` → dist/index.d.ts, `/parsing`, `/units` — all three target files that do not exist) and 2 MISSING real subpaths (`/css`, `/value`). ```
demo/scenes/about/markdown/composables/useMarkdownColors.ts:3-4 imports /color and /css. `npx tsc -p <probe extending tsconfig.demo.json> --traceResolution` output: `'@mkbabb/value.js/color' ... matched pattern ... successfully resolved to '/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/dist/subpaths/color.d.ts'` vs `'@mkbabb/value.js/css' ... Loading module from 'node_modules' folder ... successfully resolved to '/Users/.../node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts' with Package ID '@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts@4.0.0'`. `wc -l`: local css.d.ts=382, installed=350; `diff -q` DIFFER (color.d.ts IDENTICAL). **Proposed cure.** Generate tsconfig.demo.json#paths from package.json#exports with the SAME generator vite.config.ts already uses for valueJsSelfAlias — one map, one generator, two consumers. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `resetDefaults()` is a shallow `Object.assign(config, structuredClone(defaults))` over a nested config graph, so Reset overwrites whole atom subtrees including derived state that is not a slider — destroying the live picker→blob palette coupling.

**Mechanism.** Reset semantics re-minted demo-side; the re-mint is shape-blind because the only description of what is a knob (the `sections` table) is never consulted. glass-ui owns the concept: `useConfiguratorState.resetCurrent()` restores a declared preset baseline with an injectable `clone` hook (useConfiguratorState.d.ts:9-14,42).

**Evidence.**

```
demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:92-94; invariant stated and broken at demo/scenes/blob/BlobPane.vue:8-9; writer at demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:386-393. Pasted: `node --input-type=module -e "import { BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS } from '@mkbabb/glass-ui/blob-config'; const live = structuredClone(BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS); live.color.paletteStops = ['#112233','#445566','#778899','#aabbcc']; Object.assign(live, structuredClone(BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS)); console.log(live.color.paletteStops)"` → `after resetDefaults(), paletteStops = ["#b5947f","#d4b27d","#dad6b1"]` (4 stops → 3, user colour gone).
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/blob at ≥1024px, change the picker colour so the blob repaints, then press Reset in the pane footer. The blob reverts to the canned tan ramp and stays wrong until the picker colour next changes. The node one-liner above reproduces it headlessly against the installed glass-ui@7.0.0.

**Proposed cure.** Delete `resetDefaults`. Adopt `useConfiguratorState<BlobConfig>({ presets: BLOB_PRESETS })` and wire `@reset="resetCurrent"`; derived state (paletteStops) then lives outside the preset table by construction. Do NOT patch by iterating `sections` — that keeps a second home for reset alive.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `variant="spectrum"` is the wrong design-system variant for 31 abstract numeric sliders. One prop produces three independently measured defects: no value fill, a token-role-violating track re-ink, and 31 sub-24px tap targets.

**Mechanism.** A design-system variant whose contract is 'the consumer paints a gradient; there is no filled/unfilled split; the thumb is a narrow position marker' was applied to a population that has no spectrum. The author then treated the resulting invisibility as a fact to work around (ConfigSliderPane.vue:190-202 documents the whole detour) rather than as evidence of the wrong primitive, and fed the text-ink token `--ink-muted` into the control-surface variable `--slider-track-bg`.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:146. glass-ui contract in dist/glass-ui.css: `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-range{background:0 0}` and `.slider-thumb{width:calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*.75)}`. Measured WebKit 1440 on /#/blob: `{rowCount:31, trackBackground:"oklch(0.446872 0.003862 34.629978)", trackBackgroundImage:"none", rangeBackground:"rgba(0,0,0,0)", rangeWidth:"163.46875px"}`. Audit: REPORT.md:41 — /#/blob = 39 smallTapTargets, worst of all 60 captures (next worst 8); REPORT.json lists 31 entries of `{"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"Body Radius"|"Satellites"|…}`; threshold is WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 at capture.mjs:98 (`m.w < 24 || m.h < 24`). Still RED on touch: measured 12×44 at 390 coarse. Visual: shots/safari-desktop-light/blob.png shows 31 charcoal slabs beside the picker's four real spectra.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/blob at 1440. `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.config-console .slider-range')).backgroundColor` → `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` with `width` 163px; `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.config-console .slider-track')).backgroundImage` → `none`. Thumb `getBoundingClientRect()` → 12×24.

**Proposed cure.** `variant="standard"`, and delete `--slider-track-bg` (:202) and the `:deep(.configurator-row .font-mono)` re-ink (:204-206) with it. Three defects, one root, one prop.

### `design` · D-1 · design

**Defect.** In forced-colors mode the slider track's extent is 1.00:1 against the well (invisible) and the focus indicator disappears entirely, because both are expressed in the single channel forced-colors overrides.

**Mechanism.** Single-channel control semantics: the track's entire visual definition routes through `background` (a custom property), which forced-colors overrides to Canvas; no border and no painted range remain as a second channel. Focus ships as box-shadow with outline-style:none, and forced-colors strips shadows. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:84 ("Focus remains visibly distinct ... forced colors") and WCAG 1.4.11. `grep -rn forced-colors demo/scenes/` returns zero hits.

**Evidence.**

```
Chromium forcedColors:"active", /#/atmosphere 1440x900 (scratchpad/chD-csp-probe2.mjs -> forcedFocus): trackBg rgb(255,255,255) === wellBg rgb(255,255,255), trackEqualsWell:true, trackBorderWidth 0px, rangeBg rgba(0,0,0,0); outlineStyle:"none", boxShadow:"none". Frame: scratchpad/chD-csp-forced-focus.png shows three orphan pill outlines with no track. Cause: ConfigSliderPane.vue:202 `--slider-track-bg: var(--ink-muted, var(--muted-foreground))`. The tracked matrix shots/forced-colors-desktop/blob.png could not catch this — WebKit ignores Playwright's forcedColors, so that frame is byte-comparable to the ordinary light frame.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/chD-csp-probe2.mjs (Chromium arm); or Chrome DevTools -> Rendering -> Emulate CSS forced-colors: active -> http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere

**Proposed cure.** Fold into the F1 cure: retire variant="spectrum" so the producer's `.slider-range` paints the value, delete ConfigSliderPane.vue:202 and :204-206, and let glass-ui's Slider own a forced-colors arm — `border: 1px solid` on `.slider-track`, `.slider-range { background: Highlight; forced-color-adjust: none }`, and `outline` (not box-shadow) for :focus-visible. Producer change, not demo (edict 4).

### `design` · D-3 · design

**Defect.** No slider in the pane indicates its value: the producer's fill element is correctly sized and paints nothing, while the inert track is painted from a body-text ink token so it reads as 100% filled.

**Mechanism.** ConfigSliderPane.vue:146 sets variant="spectrum" — the producer's chromatic-rail recipe whose `.slider-range` is transparent by design because a gradient supplies the value read. :198-199 admits it ("the spectrum .slider-range is transparent by recipe so no filled/unfilled split reads either") and ships anyway. :202 then re-inks the information-free track with `--ink-muted`, amplifying the empty channel. Figure and ground invert: the background reads as the filled value, the thumb as a hole punched in it. Diagnosed twice historically and cured neither time (N/audit/lanes2/U-CONTROLS.md:54; N/waves/N.W13.md:28).

**Evidence.**

```
/#/atmosphere 1440x900, Colour Energy 0.760 of 0..1 (scratchpad/chD-csp-probe.mjs): .slider-track w962 h24 backgroundColor oklch(0.4469 0.0039 34.63) backgroundImage none; .slider-range width 731 (=76.0%, exactly the value) backgroundColor rgba(0,0,0,0) backgroundImage none opacity 1; [role=slider] w12 h24 backgroundColor rgba(0,0,0,0). Contrast via 1x1 canvas sRGB round-trip: track vs well 5.82:1 light / 8.30:1 dark — identical to the live readout ink (same token). Visible in shots/safari-desktop-light/blob.png (Body Radius 0.220 and Satellites 3 are identical bars) and shots/safari-mobile-dark/atmosphere.png (near-white slab brighter than the display title).
```

### `design (CHALLENGE-D) — visual truth, state coverage, motion,` · D-1 · design (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** RTL mirrors scientific notation — subscripts and superscripts swap sides, destroying the meaning of every formula. `L*` renders as `*L`, `Y_n` as `_nY`, `a*/500` as `*a/500`, and the \begin{cases} brace points the wrong way.

**Mechanism.** root element supplies none of its own design properties — direction inherited from the document with no LTR isolation

**Evidence.**

```
demo/scenes/about/katex/Katex.vue:2 emits a bare <div> with no `dir` and no `unicode-bidi`; katex.render is called with no direction option (Katex.vue:31-42). KaTeX's own CSS never sets direction: `grep -o "direction:[a-z]*" node_modules/katex/dist/katex.min.css | sort | uniq -c` -> `1 direction:column / 1 direction:row` (both flex-direction). Measured under dir=rtl: `direction: rtl`, `textAlign: right`, and the layout is genuinely recomputed — widest block scrollWidth 778 -> 752px (evidence/p2-rtl.json). Frame: frames/D-rtl-1440.png.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/Katex/evidence/probe2.mjs (arm p2-rtl); or on http://localhost:9000/#/ run document.documentElement.setAttribute("dir","rtl") and scroll the About pane to the Lab formulas.

**Proposed cure.** The component root owns its own direction: `dir="ltr"` + `unicode-bidi: isolate` on the root it already renders, in the component that knows it is emitting math — not a consumer override. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 ("numeric/scientific sign never mirrors") and §6.1 (LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose) already legislate this for every weaker member of the class.

### `design (visual truth · state coverage · motion · design-syst` · D-01 · design (visual truth · state coverage · motion · design-system boundary · proportion/seat law)

**Defect.** A single content chunk failing to load destroys the entire application scene, and the component's designed error state is structurally unreachable dead code

**Mechanism.** Unhandled async-lifecycle rejection. Vue wraps lifecycle hooks in callWithAsyncErrorHandling, so the rejected promise propagates to the app-root ErrorBoundary (App.vue:50; ErrorBoundary.vue:59-69 returns false and swallows the whole subtree). The component's own error branch is guarded on a condition the code cannot produce.

**Evidence.**

```
Markdown.vue:58-71 (loadDocs has no try/catch/finally; onMounted awaits it). chD-err2.mjs output: abortedUrls: ["http://localhost:9000/@fs/.../assets/docs/lab.md?import"] · alertRole: "This panel hit an unexpected error.Importing a module script failed. Try again" · pickerPresent: false · aboutPresent: false. The v-else Alert branch (Markdown.vue:19-31, 13 lines) can never render: currentDoc is only null while isLoading is true, and a dynamic import() never resolves to null.
```

**Reproduction.** node chD-err2.mjs — Playwright WebKit, page.route(/assets\/docs\/.*\.md/, r => r.abort('failed')), navigate http://localhost:9000/#/, wait 9s. Exactly one URL is aborted; picker and About both unmount.

**Proposed cure.** try/catch/finally in the loader; delete the unreachable v-else and replace it with an in-place named failure state that never escapes to the app boundary. Wave W-MD-3 (pass-1 table), amended by N-3.

### `design (visual truth · state coverage · motion · design-syst` · D-02 · design (visual truth · state coverage · motion · design-system boundary · proportion/seat law)

Rendered borderRadius '4px' despite rounded-full. loadingHostHeight 181px vs loaded .markdown-body height 6244px. Frame: frames/pass-2/m3-skeleton.png.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/shell/dock/` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The local `useLayerTransition` shim produces no visual transition at all — the entire crossfade apparatus (leavingLayer ref, 260ms timer, is-leaving class) is inert machinery over an instantaneous cut.

**Mechanism.** Hand-reimplementation of a producer primitive that kept the bookkeeping (which id is leaving) and dropped the thing doing the work (the animated scalar). glass's DockCrossfade drives a per-face `--dock-t` opacity scalar from useDockSpring; the shim drives nothing, and the producer CSS it piggybacks on has no opacity transition to trigger.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:53-95. Live probe, http://localhost:9000/#/: getComputedStyle of the two `.dock-layer-grid` children returns transition == "visibility" (active) and "visibility 0s linear 0.3s" (inactive) — no `opacity` entry in either. Nine-frame sample across the swap (+2/+17/+61/+131/+201/+250/+281/+401/+621 ms): leaving-layer opacity == "0" and entering-layer opacity == "1" at EVERY frame, zero intermediate values; `.glass-dock[data-morphing]` == false at every frame. Producer source: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/layers.css declares only `:where(.glass-dock,.dock-layer-group) .dock-layer { transition: visibility 0s linear var(--duration-normal); }`.
```

Then click the `Open color input` toggle while polling `getComputedStyle(g.children[i]).opacity` — it reads only "0" or "1", never between.

**Proposed cure.** Architectural transposition, not a patch: delete lines 53-95 and the template's hand-bound class/inert, and mount the producer's public primitive — `<DockCrossfade :active="showInput ? 'input' : 'actions'" reserve="inline"><DockLayer id="actions">…</DockLayer><DockLayer id="input">…</DockLayer></DockCrossfade>`. This one move also discharges D-3, D-4, D-6, D-7, D-9 and D-14.

demo/shell/dock/ActionBarToggle.vue:92 (`:tabindex="visible ? 0 : -1"`) + :93 (`@click="emit('toggle')"`) vs demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:48, :113, :153, :86-87. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/shell/dock/Col` · R2-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The send button can never submit typed text: `onInputBlur` wipes the contenteditable back to the canonical colour, and because the UA moves focus on mousedown but fires click on mouseup, `onSubmitColor` always reads the already-wiped DOM and re-submits the stale colour.

**Mechanism.** DOM-as-source-of-truth: a mutable DOM node is both the draft store and the read-back channel, with two handlers writing and reading it in UA-imposed order.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:191 (`inputColorRef.value.innerText = formattedCurrentColor.value`) and :215 (`parseAndSetColor(inputColorRef.value.innerText)`). Live measurement: {"committed":"rgb(255 0 0)","typed":"rebeccapurple","afterBlur":"rgb(255 0 0)","afterSend":"rgb(255 0 0)"} in 292 ms total. Short-circuit that hides it: demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:69.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/ → dock → 'Toggle action bar' → 'Open color input'. Focus the field, type a new valid colour, click the arrow (send) button within 2 s. Nothing happens; ~2 s later the colour changes anyway.

**Proposed cure.** Retire the contenteditable as the source of truth. Hold the draft in a local `shallowRef<string>` written by @input, render from it, and let blur only decide whether to DISCARD the draft — never rewrite a node a pending click is about to read. `onSubmitColor` then reads the ref and the blur/click ordering is irrelevant. This is edict 7's synchronous-local-cache idiom, and it dissolves round 1's C-16 (six imperative innerText writers over three sources of truth) in the same stroke.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/shell/dock/Col` · R2-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The 2000 ms debounced parse is never cancelled by this component — not on blur, Enter, send, mode switch, or unmount (there is no onUnmounted at all) — so an abandoned edit silently overwrites a later, deliberate colour commit, and can mutate the global model after the component is destroyed.

**Mechanism.** A hidden timer owns pending state with no lifetime binding; combined with round 1's C-8 (the debounce is an app-wide singleton), the only `.cancel()` in the application belongs to ColorPicker's lifetime — so this component's pending parse is cancelled by the wrong unmount and by nothing else.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:92 (`debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000)`); demo/shared/utils.ts:36-41 (`.cancel()` exists); `grep -rn onUnmounted demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue` → no matches; the sibling consumer DOES cancel at demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:383. Measured with real timers: `C1 committed #abcdef` → `C2 after committing #00ff00 color=rgb(0 255 0)` → `C3 2.3s later, nothing touched color=rgb(255 0 0)`. Unmount path: demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:153 `v-if="hasAnyActionBar"` and :156 `v-if="actionBar"`.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vite-node --config vite.config.ts <scratchpad>/parseprobe2.ts — scenario C. In the app: type a colour into the dock input, blur without committing, immediately pick a different colour by slider/swatch; ~2 s later the colour reverts to the abandoned text.

**Proposed cure.** Give the pending commit the component's lifetime and make it visible reactive state rather than a hidden timer: fold the debounce into the draft `shallowRef` of R2-1, cancel on every path that resolves the edit, and add `onBeforeUnmount`. Do not merely add a cancel call — the singleton ownership (C-8) is the same defect seen from the other side.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/dock/Colo` · R3-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The custom-name round-trip is broken: `formattedCurrentColor` is a name-or-CSS union, and the component writes it into the contenteditable at five sites and reads it back into `parseAndSetColor` at three. Approved custom names are never registered with the parser, so the app's own canonical display text fails the app's own parser.

**Mechanism.** type-confused single value — one computed serves both 'label a human reads' and 'value a machine round-trips', so the DOM node that is the source of truth for submission is seeded with a value from the wrong domain

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/useColorNameResolution.ts:31-46 returns `findCustomName(...)` (an arbitrary user-proposed name) before ever reaching `serializePickerColor`. demo/color-session/useCustomColorNames.ts:61-66 resolves against a demo-side Map built from GET /colors/approved; `grep -rn registerColorNames src/ demo/ api/src` yields ONE hit, a comment at useCustomColorNames.ts:46. The parser's only name table is the frozen 148-entry NAMED_COLORS (src/css/grammar.ts:31,265; src/css/named-colors.ts:1). Writers: ColorInput.vue:191, :240, :265, :272, :278. Readers: :199, :208, :215. Measured: `model colour: rgb(20 60 200) / formattedCurrentColor: "babb-blue" / parseCssColor(displayed).ok: false / after re-submitting the displayed text -> parseError = true / model colour now: rgb(20 60 200)`.
```

**Reproduction.** VITE_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9/api npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-colorinput/probe.vitest.config.ts — test B in roundtrip.probe.ts. Drives the real useCustomColorNames + useColorNameResolution + useColorParsing; only globalThis.fetch is stubbed, and the stub name `babb-blue` is legal under the server's own zod schema (api/src/modules/color/schema.ts:8-19).

**Proposed cure.** Split the union at the pipeline, not with a guard at the call site. Expose `canonicalCssColor` (always serializePickerColor) alongside `displayLabel`; render the label, seed and submit the canonical. The custom name then becomes what it always should have been — presentation, exactly like the crown tooltip beside it. This also collapses R2-1 and C-16: with one canonical string source there is no reason for six imperative innerText writers or for blur to rewrite a node a pending click is about to read.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/dock/Colo` · R3-MT-F001 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** MT-F001 is SWALLOWED by this path and mislabelled as a user typo. A shipped-library TypeError is rendered byte-identically to a plain typo, reaches no telemetry, and leaves the field in a final state indistinguishable from working.

**Mechanism.** an undiscriminated catch converting a defect in a dependency into an accusation of user error, with a latch that then erases even that signal

**Evidence.**

```
Library leg re-measured against src/css/index: `"oklch()" "rgb()" "hsl()" "lab()" "lch()" "color()" "oklab()" "hsl(  )" -> THROW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`. Site: src/css/grammar.ts:178 guards `slash[1]?.trim()` with optional chaining while :180 asserts `slash[0]!.replace(...)` — the two adjacent indices of the same array handled with opposite rigour, one line apart. Path: ColorInput.vue:194 -> :199 -> useColorParsing.ts:60 -> :64 -> picker-color.ts:110 -> parseCssColor. Live (frames/probe-1.json B-f001-light): afterEnter badgeText 'not a valid color', inputBorder rgb(219,36,36), and pageErrors: []. Swallow site: useColorParsing.ts:84-87, a bare `catch` with no binding and no discrimination, so PickerColorError (which carries result.diagnostics per picker-color.ts:96-112) and a library TypeError render identically.
```

**Reproduction.** Test A in roundtrip.probe.ts for the library leg; frames/probe-1.json + frames/B-f001-error.png + frames/B-f001-after2s.png for the live leg. The tail nobody had recorded: after2s = {badge:false, text:'oklch()', border:'lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827)'} — the invalid text remains, the error styling is gone, and previousInvalid is now latched to 'oklch()' so useColorParsing.ts:61 short-circuits and pressing Enter again produces nothing at all.

**Proposed cure.** Narrow the catch: `catch (e) { if (!(e instanceof PickerColorError)) throw e; ... }`. A genuine syntax rejection stays a quiet inline error; anything else reaches window.onerror, where MT-F001 would have surfaced on day one. ParseEchoReadout (ColorInput.vue:109) — already rendering astEcho and gamutVerdict from the same pipeline — is the natural home for the diagnostics the catch discards. The library-side `!` at src/css/grammar.ts:180 is a separate repair; route to the library seat, together with R2-7's adjacent false-accept of `oklch(0.5 0.1 250 / )`.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/dock/Colo` · R2-1-UPHELD · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** CARRIED AND STRENGTHENED — the send button is structurally incapable of submitting typed text, in every browser engine. I attempted to refute this as a Chromium-only focus artefact and the refutation FAILED.

**Mechanism.** DOM node as source of truth, mutated by an event that the UA guarantees fires before the event that reads it

**Evidence.**

```
ColorInput.vue:183-193 onInputBlur overwrites the field with formattedCurrentColor; :213-217 onSubmitColor reads that same node back. Cross-engine test of the exact three-part shape: chromium 148.0.7778.96 / webkit 26.4 / firefox 150.0.2 all produced `typed activeEl=ce` -> `mousedown activeEl=ce` -> `BLUR read="typed-value" -> overwrite` -> `CLICK read="CANONICAL"`. WebKit and Firefox indeed do not focus the button on mousedown, but they blur the contenteditable anyway — the distinction the refutation relied on does not exist for this shape.
```

**Reproduction.** scratchpad/blurorder.html + blurorder.mjs (session scratchpad; a 12-line static page, no app dependency). `node scratchpad/blurorder.mjs`. Round 2's live app measurement stands as the in-situ leg.

**Proposed cure.** Same cure as R3-1 and C-16, one stroke: hold the draft in a local shallowRef written by @input, render from it, and let blur decide only whether to DISCARD the draft — never to rewrite a DOM node a pending click is about to read. onSubmitColor then reads the ref and the blur/click ordering becomes irrelevant. This is the synchronous-local-cache idiom edict 7 already mandates for the defineModel round-trip; the hazard class is identical.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/dock/Colo` · R2-2-UPHELD · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** CARRIED — the pending 2000 ms parse is never cancelled, and the component has no teardown of any kind. An abandoned edit overwrites a later, deliberate commit, and can fire from a destroyed component.

`grep -n "onUnmounted\|onBeforeUnmount\|clearTimeout\|cancel()" demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue` returns NO OUTPUT WHATSOEVER — no lifecycle hook, no timer clear, no debounce cancel, despite the file owning a setTimeout at :256, an rAF at :262 and a 2000 ms debounce via :199. debounce exposes .cancel() (demo/shared/utils.ts:36-41) and the sibling consumer uses it (demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:383), so the omission is demonstrated, not stylistic. The unmount leg is real: Dock.vue:153 `<DockLayer v-if="hasAnyActionBar">` and :156 `<ActionBarLayer v-if="actionBar" ...>`.
```

**Reproduction.** Round 2's vite-node reproduction stands (C1 committed #abcdef -> C2 committed #00ff00 -> C3 2.3s later the abandoned 'red' won). Round 3 independently confirms both structural preconditions by grep.

Mechanism anchor: demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:239-251 (cache validity key `document.documentElement.classList.contains("dark")` read at :242).
```

**Reproduction.** Boot http://localhost:9000/#/ in light, expand the dock, open the @mbabb menu, click `Dark mode`, press Escape, read `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--accent-live')`. Compare with the same read after a reload in dark. Repeat the flip twice more to see the one-behind alternation. Script: scratchpad/psec-probe-d.mjs.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Focus indicator is the user's raw alpha-bearing colour with the UA outline suppressed; measured contrast 1.00:1 for reachable colours; no forced-colors fallback; error state overwrites focus state.

**Mechanism.** Accessibility-critical state expressed through a user-data-driven decorative channel with no floor, no fallback register, and no separation from a competing state — instead of a design-system focus register.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:16 (`focus-visible:outline-none`) and :162-166 (`if (inputIsFocused.value) return { borderColor: cssColor.value }`). Live after a real click: `focused: true, outline: "none 1px rgb(0,95,204)", inlineStyle: "border-color: lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827);"`. Measured contrast vs the field's own measured background rgb(251,250,248): `#fbfaf8` → 1.00, `rgb(255 255 255)` → 1.04, `oklch(0.7 0.1 200 / 0)` → alpha 0 / invisible. Forced-colors roster membership measured via el.matches() against foundation.css:702-720: colorInput → false, sendBtn → true; colorInput attrs = [data-v-…, contenteditable, role, aria-label, class] (no tabindex). Error+focus measured inline style: `border-color: var(--destructive)`. Contrast-safe primitive available and unused for this purpose: demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:273-292, injected at ColorInput.vue:157 and spent on the arrow stroke at :74/:81.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/ at >=1440px viewport → hover the dock → click `Tools` (aria-label="Toggle action bar") → click `Open color input` → drag the alpha channel slider to 0 (or set the colour to white in light mode) → click the field. Focus is undetectable. In WHCM the element matches no outline-restoration selector.

**Proposed cure.** Delete `focus-visible:outline-none` and the focus branch of `inputStyle` entirely. Focus comes from the house register — demo/styles/focus-ring.css / the `.focus-ring` class that four sibling dock controls measurably carry (measured siblingButtonsUsingFocusRing: 4, colorInput.usesFocusRing: false). Architecturally this dissolves by adopting glass-ui `Input`, which owns its own focus register. If the live colour must appear on this control it appears as a swatch, never as the focus boundary.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-01 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The mobile dock action bar is a row of dead buttons: on /#/gradient, /#/generate and /#/mix the Tools trigger opens an action layer whose buttons are named, sized, focusable and clickable, and every handler is a silent no-op on mobile.

**Mechanism.** Desktop-only capability wiring masked by optional chaining. demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:206-208 (gradient), :193-196 (generate), :217-220 (mix) call `paneRefs.<view>.value?.<cmd>?.()`. demo/color-picker/App.vue:320-327 writes gradientPaneRef/generatePaneRef/mixPaneRef ONLY inside onDesktopLeftMount/onDesktopRightMount — the file's own comment at :314-316 says "Populated by the onMount callbacks on the desktop PaneSlots". The mobile PaneSlot (App.vue:81-89) passes no :on-mount. Violates owner edict 2 (no masking fallbacks) at the highest-cost site.

**Evidence.**

```
D-dock-probe6.mjs, clipboard pre-seeded with SENTINEL-NOT-TOUCHED then "Copy CSS" clicked in the dock action bar on /#/gradient:
MOBILE 390x844:   clipboard="SENTINEL-NOT-TOUCHED"                                          pageErrors=[]
DESKTOP 1440x900: clipboard="linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(75% 0.15 145deg) 0.00%, oklch(7…" pageErrors=[]
Bar renders in full at 390 (D-dock-probe5.mjs): slot opacity:1, trigger tabIndex:0 32x32; Back 44x44, Reset 32x32, Copy CSS 32x32, Seed from palette 32x32.
```

**Reproduction.** node D-dock-probe6.mjs against the live dev server: newContext 390x844 → goto /#/gradient → seed clipboard → click "Toggle action bar" → click the button named exactly "Copy CSS" → read clipboard. Repeat at 1440x900.

**Proposed cure.** Invert the direction of the dependency: the dock must not hold references to pane instances. The pane provide()s a command object keyed by view; the dock injects it. A view that provides no commands renders no Tools trigger; a provided command is live in whichever slot mounted it, by construction. Delete paneRefs, onDesktopLeftMount, onDesktopRightMount and every `?.` on a handler — an action that can be absent must be ABSENT, never present-and-inert.

**Defect.** The field cannot be edited, only replaced: clicking anywhere in the value selects the entire value, so the next keystroke destroys it. No undo.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · R3-02 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** No cancel path exists, and a 2000 ms commit debounce means valid input typed and blurred inside two seconds is silently discarded with zero signal.

**Mechanism.** Two sources of truth (contenteditable text vs. model) reconciled only by a long debounce and an unconditional blur repaint, with no cancel gesture and no uncommitted-state affordance.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:92 `debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000)`; ColorInput.vue:202-211 handles only `Enter`; :183-193 blur repaints from the model. Measured, frames/r3probe2.json: `"cancel":{"typed":"rebeccapurple","afterEsc":{"text":"rebeccapurple","focused":true},"afterBlur":"lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)","escapeCancels":false,"blurCommitted":false}`.
```

**Reproduction.** Open the field -> select all -> type `rebeccapurple` (valid CSS) -> press Escape (nothing happens) -> click elsewhere within 2 s. The value reverts to the previous colour with no error, no toast, no 'unsaved' mark.

**Proposed cure.** Escape restores the model value and exits; blur either commits or warns but never silently discards; drop the debounce to a live-preview cadence (~150 ms) once the field is no longer the sole commit path. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:75 already mandates commit/cancel/error semantics for editors — adopt the W21 numeric-field contract instead of inventing a third one.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The component hand-applies GlassDock's PRIVATE shell-pane classes (`.dock-layer` + `is-active`/`is-leaving`) to arbitrary consumer components. In Glass 7 the public face class is `.dock-face`; `.dock-layer` is emitted only by GlassDock's own two internal plates. Because every `.dock-layer` rule is scoped `:where(.glass-dock, .dock-layer-group) .dock-layer`, the counterfeit faces match the dock's private plate rules — including two that are actively hostile during a dock morph.

**Mechanism.** consumer styles itself from producer internals — a silent breakage contract, since no public API ever promised these class names

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:91. Scan of the producer bundle: `python3 -c "...re.finditer(r'dock-layer(?![-a-z])', open('dist/dock.js').read())..."` returns exactly two emission sites, both internal: `class: L(["dock-layer dock-layer--full", {...}])` and `class: L(["dock-layer dock-layer--summary", {...}])`. The public face component emits `class: L(["dock-face", { "is-active": ..., "is-le..." }])`. Hostile rules in layers.css: `.glass-dock[data-morphing] .dock-layer.is-leaving { opacity: calc(1 - var(--dock-morph-t)); }` and `.glass-dock[data-morphing] .dock-layer.is-active > * { opacity: var(--child-reveal); scale: calc(0.82 + 0.18 * var(--child-reveal)); }`.
```

**Reproduction.** grep the emission sites as above; then on the live page confirm the consumer nodes carry the class: the two `.dock-layer-grid` children report className `"flex items-center justify-around flex-1 dock-layer is-active"` and `"grid grid-cols-1 gap-y-2 p-0 m-0 dock-layer min-w-0"`. (The compound swap-during-dock-morph symptom is a HYPOTHESIS — the rules and the class match are both confirmed, but I did not capture a simultaneous frame.)

**Proposed cure.** Same transposition as D-1 — `<DockLayer>` faces inside `<DockCrossfade>` carry the producer's own `.dock-face` packaging, so the consumer stops naming producer internals at all.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The chip has no material presence: its own surface measures 1.112:1 (light) and 1.059:1 (dark) against the ambient field immediately beside it. It is an outline drawn on the sky, and its dark-mode treatment is inert by construction.

**Mechanism.** ApiOfflineChip lives inside a palette Card (an opaque specimen well, VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 tier 4) where a 55% `--background` film sits on a known neutral and reads as a real chip. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Below 1024px the lamp is a `role="alert"` with an EMPTY accessible name and zero rendered content — the user is shown a 6.4px dot and told nothing by any channel. The component's own comment claims the opposite.

**Mechanism.** The compaction strategy deletes the only named channel instead of hiding it. Accessible-name computation excludes non-rendered nodes; with no aria-label and an aria-hidden dot, the live region's name resolves to the empty string. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 requires that failed/pending states are 'never color-only' and that 'role, accessible name, state/value ... are explicit' — under 1024px this state is both colour-only AND nameless.

**Evidence.**

```
Live at 390x844: role="alert", aria-label=null, textContent="dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`", innerText="" (empty), labelDisplay="none", lampRect 26x18 CSS px. Source: DockStatusLamp.vue:67-69 `.lamp-label { display: none }`; the dot at :18 is aria-hidden="true". The comment at DockStatusLamp.vue:64-66 asserts "The role + label stay in the accessibility tree (visually-hidden, not v-if'd)" — display:none removes a subtree from the a11y tree, so the claim is false. Frame: frames/band-390.png.
```

**Reproduction.** Live dev server, resize to 390x844, evaluate: document.querySelector('.dock-status-lamp').innerText === '' while .textContent is the full sentence. Reproduced 2026-07-27.

**Proposed cure.** `display:none` must become a visually-hidden idiom (`position:absolute; clip-path: inset(50%)`) so the label survives in the accessibility tree at every viewport — and, under the D-6 cure, the compaction decision moves to the dock's own container/overflow logic where a truncation can be announced rather than deleted.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The failure state does not exist. A rejected login says nothing, anywhere — no error copy, no status region, no live announcement, no visual delta at all.

**Mechanism.** State-without-surface: the error state was authored in script and never given a rendered region, then its data path was re-routed to a component that is not mounted. Compounded by the layer self-dismissing at `:56` in the same synchronous tick the request is fired, so even a correct region would be unmounted before the outcome arrives.

**Evidence.**

```
Live repro output (probe2 §A4): `{"alerts":["dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`"],"errorCopyVisible":[],"slugLayerStillActive":false,"inputValue":"","loginButtonStillThere":true}`. Source: `demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:13` declares `slugError`, `:49,:59,:60,:61,:62` write it, template `:75-119` references it ZERO times. `:54` calls `pm.onSlugSwitch(...)` un-awaited; `demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:51-89` catches its own failures internally so `:57`'s catch is unreachable. `useSlugMigration.ts:84-87` routes 409/404/429/other into `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`; `grep -rn "PaletteSlugBar" demo` returns barrel exports only (`browser/index.ts:44`, `browser/slug/index.ts:3`) and NO template usage, so `slugBarRef` is permanently null. The only rendered error region in the repo is `demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue:124-125`, in that unmounted component.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/ at 1440x900 → click `Login` → type `brave-swift-red-fox` → click `Switch to slug` → wait 2.5s. The dock returns to its pre-login appearance, still signed out, with no statement of what happened.

**Proposed cure.** Architectural, not a patch: retire the dock layer and move sign-in into the Account Dialog that VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 already assigns to W23, where an error region, a pending region and a real field all have room. Delete `useSlugMigration`'s `slugBarRef` limb and the unmounted `PaletteSlugBar` with it so exactly one error owner exists. Minimum honest in-place repair: await the port, keep the layer mounted until it resolves, render one `role="status"` region under the field.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The dock auto-collapses out from under the user mid-edit after 5 seconds of idle, expelling focus and discarding the typed slug.

**Mechanism.** A text-entry surface hosted inside an idle-collapsing container that never registers itself as a keep-open driver. The authors wrote a cleanup watcher for the collapse (`Dock.vue:76`) instead of a hold — i.e. the collapse was known and the data loss was not.

**Evidence.**

```
`demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:86` — `shouldKeepOpen = actionBarLayerActive || anyEditActive || isAnyOpen`; `slugEditMode` is NOT a driver. `Dock.vue:132` `:collapse-delay="5000"`. Measured (slug-probe6): `t=4000ms {slugFaceActive:true, faceOpacity:"1", groupW:285}` → `t=6000ms {slugFaceActive:false, faceOpacity:"0", groupW:56, sealVisible:true}` with `value:"brave-swift-red-fox"` still in the detached DOM. Inactive faces measure `{inert:true, ariaHidden:"true"}`, so focus is expelled. `Dock.vue:76` then clears `slugEditMode`; re-opening runs `SlugEditLayer.vue:16-17` whose first statement is `slugInput.value = ""`.
```

**Reproduction.** 1440x900 → `Login` → type `brave-swift-red-fox` → move the pointer away from the dock → wait. Between 4s and 6s the dock collapses to the 56px wax seal; the input is gone and the value is discarded on re-open. Desktop only (`always-expanded="!isDesktop"` exempts mobile; measured 8s idle at 390/320 leaves it intact).

**Proposed cure.** The producer already exposes the right primitive — GlassDock's ref-counted `keepOpen()/release()` pair, which `Dock.vue:87` already drives. Add `slugEditMode` to the `shouldKeepOpen` disjunction at `Dock.vue:86`. One word. (Moot under the gestalt cure — a Dialog does not evaporate on a wall-clock timer.)

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The field is optically absent in every state including focus, and its only label — the placeholder — is truncated mid-word in every viewport.

**Mechanism.** A hand-rolled `<input>` carrying `bg-transparent border-none outline-none w-40` (`SlugEditLayer.vue:85`) deletes boundary, fill and focus ring with nothing put back, and fixes a width that was never held up against the string it must hold. The donor twin uses `enter slug...` (13 chars, fits) inside a composed `SearchBar` (`PaletteSlugBar.vue:5-12`).

**Evidence.**

```
Rendered frames show `enter slug or to` (1440 light AND dark) and `enter slug or toker` (390, 320) against the authored `enter slug or token...` (`SlugEditLayer.vue:84`). Arithmetic: Fira Code advance 0.6em; measured font-size 16.4px desktop → 9.84px/char × 22 chars = 216.5px required vs `w-40` = 160px measured; ⌊160/9.84⌋ = 16 chars predicts `enter slug or to` exactly; mobile 14px → ⌊160/8.40⌋ = 19 chars predicts `enter slug or toker` exactly. Field styling measured: `border-width:0px`, `background-color:rgba(0,0,0,0)`, `outline-style:none`, `box-shadow:none`, `::before/::after content:none`, `min-height:auto`, padding 0 → height 22.9px desktop / 19.6px mobile is pure line-box. Focus proof: `shots/input-unfocused.png` ≡ `shots/input-focused.png` after an 800ms settle with `:focus-visible === true`; webkit pre/post computed-style snapshot returns `{"same":true,"activeIsInput":true}`. Accessible name: `{ariaLabel:null, id:"", hasLabelEl:false, labelledBy:null}` — matches REPORT.json's `{"w":160,"h":23,"tag":"input","label":""}`. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 ("Focus remains visibly distinct… in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency") and WCAG 2.4.7.
```

**Reproduction.** Open the layer at 1440x900 → read the dock: the label reads `enter slug or to`. Blur, screenshot, focus the input, wait 800ms, screenshot again — the two crops are identical.

**Proposed cure.** Consume the design system's field primitive: `<Input>` from `demo/ui/input` (a one-line re-export of `@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms`), or the `SearchBar` + `:icon` composition the twin already uses. Promote the placeholder to a real label; the placeholder then carries an example, not the name.

demo/shell/dock/menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:43,47-50. **Defect.** In RTL the SegmentedTabs pill indicator is drawn over the UNSELECTED tab, so the pane switcher reports the opposite of the pane actually rendered. Upstream: `grep -c "rtl\|direction" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/tabs.js` → 0.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The selection ink is inverted in BOTH schemes: the UNSELECTED label is drawn at higher contrast than the SELECTED one, so the ink carries ~1.2:1 of state signal in the wrong direction and selection survives only as the glass indicator fill (a color-only state, contra VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83).

**Mechanism.** A producer control whose entire state signal is the (--foreground vs --muted-foreground) pair was seated inside a container that redefines --muted-foreground to contrast-color(--card) — a MAXIMUM-contrast pick (pure black/white) — while leaving --foreground untouched. The dock legibility rule, meant to RAISE muted ink to a floor over live aurora, overshoots past --foreground and inverts every muted/normal pair in the dock. It becomes a state-semantics failure only here, because this is the one dock site where that pair IS the state model.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured computed color on the live control. Light: selected rgb(28,25,23) L=0.01004; unselected rgb(0,0,0) L=0 → ink-vs-ink contrast 1.20:1, unselected DARKER. Dark: selected rgb(233,230,226) L=0.7943; unselected rgb(255,255,255) L=1.0 → 1.24:1, unselected BRIGHTER. Mechanism pinned at the tab node: {supportsContrastColor:true, unselectedTabIsInsideGlassDock:true, mutedAtTab:'contrast-color(light-dark(hsl(30 85% 96%), hsl(26 22% 17%)))' → rgb(0,0,0), fgAtTab:'light-dark(hsl(24 10% 10%), …)' → rgb(28,25,23)}. Source: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/adaptive-legibility.css — `@supports (color: contrast-color(white)) { :where(.glass-dock) { --muted-foreground: contrast-color(var(--card)); } }`. Producer state model: dist/components/tabs/styles/segmented.css — `.segmented-tab { color: var(--muted-foreground) }` / `[aria-pressed="true"] { color: var(--foreground) }`. Crops: scratchpad/psc-light-ltr.png, psc-dark-ltr.png.
```

**Reproduction.** node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/cc.mjs (mechanism) and psc-probe3.mjs (light-ltr/dark-ltr ink blocks). Visually: scratchpad/psc-light-ltr.png — 'About' reads heavier than the selected 'Picker'.

**Proposed cure.** Relay to glass-ui BJ: the dock adaptive-legibility rule must clamp --muted-foreground TOWARD the foreground floor, never past it (color-mix in oklab toward var(--foreground)), preserving `muted < normal` as a producer invariant rather than using contrast-color(). Add a producer assertion that L(--muted-foreground) never crosses L(--foreground) in any container scope. Nothing is fixable in the consumer; note this is NOT a legibility failure (both labels clear 12:1 on their fields) — it is a hierarchy failure.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** PaneSlot imposes <KeepAlive> on all ten routed panes, but not one pane in the entire demo implements the deactivation half of the contract. Global window/document listeners, render loops and WebGL contexts survive deactivation for the whole session.

**Mechanism.** caching-contract imposed by the container, deactivation contract implemented by nobody; the ref-capture seam IS honest about deactivation (runtime-core.cjs.js:6588-6598 fires setRef(null) BEFORE the KeepAlive deactivate branch), which is exactly what made the component-level debt invisible

**Evidence.**

```
PaneSlot.vue:120 <KeepAlive :max>. Census: `grep -rn "onActivated|onDeactivated" demo/` returns exactly two hits, both in demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue (:27 import, :246 onActivated) — ONE activation hook, ZERO deactivation hooks. HeroBlob.vue:246-250 even calls blobRef.value?.resume() on activation without ever pausing. MEASURED listener survival (window.addEventListener/removeEventListener instrumented via addInitScript before app boot, full 14-route cycle): `boot on /#/ add=3 rem=0 LIVE=3` then add=3 rem=0 LIVE=3 on #/gradient, #/generate, #/extract, #/browse, #/atmosphere, #/mix, #/palettes, #/blob, all five #/admin/*, and back to #/. rem=0 throughout; `picker in DOM on /#/gradient: false`. ColorPicker.vue:376-383 registers window keydown in onMounted and removes it in onUnmounted — onUnmounted never fires once. handleKeydown (ColorPicker.vue:249-267) calls e.preventDefault() on cmd+k and on Escape/Enter while isEditing. Full listener census in the report: ColorPicker.vue:247,377; ImageEyedropper.vue:239; usePointerDebug.ts:227-232 (6 document listeners); useSliderTouchGates.ts:124. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6: "Paused, parked and offscreen mean no animation work." REPORT.md:17 records `safari-desktop-light /#/: WebGL: context lost.`
```

**Reproduction.** node /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/keepalive-listener-probe.mjs against http://localhost:9000 — prints add/rem/LIVE per route. NOTE: the listener SURVIVAL is CONFIRMED; the specific Cmd+K swallow is a HYPOTHESIS in this seat (my synthetic and real page.keyboard Cmd+K on /#/gradient returned defaultPrevented:false — the useMagicKeys arm did not latch under automation). The WebGL-context-exhaustion link to REPORT.md:17 is also a HYPOTHESIS.

**Proposed cure.** Global listeners have no business inside a cached subtree. Move Cmd+K and Escape/Enter to a shell-owned command bus (the shell is never deactivated); for the render loops, add real onActivated/onDeactivated pairs. If PaneSlot keeps imposing KeepAlive it must own the contract — the KISS answer is that it should not impose it at all and each pane opts in.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The failure-explicit Result contract is destroyed at the demo boundary, so a LIBRARY CRASH and a USER TYPO are the same event. src/css/grammar.ts:181 throws TypeError on eight inputs; demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:109-113 is a throwing facade that only handles `result.ok === false` and lets the raw TypeError escape past its own typed PickerColorError; demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:80-85 catches everything with a bare `catch {}` and renders the hardcoded literal 'not a valid color'. Re-derived and confirmed this pass; first filed by the prior pass.

**Mechanism.** Contract transposition, three hops, each lossy: Result → exception (picker-color.ts valueOrThrow/PickerColorError) → bare catch {} (useColorParsing) → a constant string literal (ColorInput.vue:88). The discriminant is erased at every hop. Two further silencers compound it: `initialParse` (useColorParsing.ts:83) suppresses a composable's first failure, and `previousInvalid` (useColorParsing.ts:62) makes any REPEAT of the same string a total no-op — the state a frustrated user reaches within two seconds.

**Evidence.**

```
Contract: src/css/types.ts:25-27 (`ParseResult<T> = {ok:true,...} | {ok:false, diagnostics:[ParseIssue,...]}`), package.json:4 ('failure-explicit'). Throw site: src/css/grammar.ts:181 `splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g," "), "space")` where splitTopLevel("","/") returns [] (grammar.ts:79,85). Measured against the exact dist the dev server serves (dist/subpaths/css.js, Jul 24 14:04, newer than src/css/grammar.ts Jul 17 14:48): all of oklch() rgb() hsl() lab() lch() color() oklab() 'hsl(  )' THROW `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`, while 'oklch(' and 'notacolor' correctly return ok:false. Live at http://localhost:9000/#/ after typing oklch()+Enter: {"inputText":"oklch()","errorBadge":null,"borderColor":"lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827)"} and browser_console_messages(level=error) → Errors: 0. Diagnostics loss is total: ParseIssue carries {code,start,end,expected,actual} (src/css/types.ts:10-24) and the only three demo readers of `.diagnostics` are internal-invariant sites with no human present (useGradientCSS.ts:128, useImageSampler.ts:60, useMarkdownColors.ts:33); the one surface where a human types CSS reads it never.
```

**Reproduction.** `npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-colorinput/probe.vitest.config.ts` → 5/5 green. The harness drives the REAL useColorParsing composable and the REAL picker-color facade against the PUBLISHED dist/subpaths/{color,css}.js and proves: (1) all eight throw while 'oklch(' returns ok:false — the crash is narrower than the failure path and therefore invisible beside it; (2) parsePickerColor re-throws a raw TypeError, not PickerColorError; (3) with the initialParse gate burned, all eight leave the model object-identical (toBe) and set the same boolean a typo sets; (4) the first parse of a composable's life leaves parseError===false; (5) a repeat of the same crasher early-returns on previousInvalid — no badge, no console, no model change. Live: the gesture chain above.

**Proposed cure.** Delete valueOrThrow and PickerColorError from picker-color.ts and every bare catch on the parse path. parseCssColor already returns the right shape — let it reach the component: `parsePickerColor(s): ParseResult<CssColor>`; `useColorParsing.commit(source)` returns it; ColorInput renders `diagnostics[0].expected` and marks [start,end] in the field. No try, no catch, no previousInvalid cache. An unexpected TypeError then has nowhere to hide — it becomes a page error the existing visual-audit harness already reports, so 'pageErrors — 0' becomes a real green instead of a manufactured one.

**Defect.** parseCssColor is typed and documented as total and failure-explicit (ParseResult<CssColor>; package.json:4 says "failure-explicit") but is partial: it throws TypeError on eight degenerate functional bodies. demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:104-113 then inverts the library's entire Result surface back into exceptions (valueOrThrow / PickerColorError), and demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:84 catches with a BARE `catch {}` that cannot distinguish a user typo from a library crash and discards the library's structured ParseIssue[] diagnostics entirely. ColorInput.vue SWALLOWS MT-F001 — it neither guards nor crashes.

**Mechanism.** error-model inversion at a library boundary whose declared totality is untrue (Mechanism A)

**Evidence.**

```
src/css/grammar.ts:181 `splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g," "),"space")` — the `!` is false. Against shipped dist: `node -e "const {parseCssColor}=await import('./dist/subpaths/css.js')..."` → oklch() rgb() hsl() lab() lch() color() oklab() 'hsl(  )' all THREW `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`; oklch(0.7 0.1 200) => ok:true. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The library's sole failure protocol is destroyed at the demo boundary, and the live MT-F001 TypeError is swallowed indistinguishably from a user typo. picker-color.ts re-throws the Result as an exception; useColorParsing catches it bare; ColorInput renders one flat badge.

**Mechanism.** A — the failure-explicit contract is inverted at the demo boundary: Result → throw → bare un-narrowed catch → one flat English string. Once re-thrown, the catch cannot discriminate a declared parse failure from a library bug.

**Evidence.**

```
src/css/grammar.ts:181 (`splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g," "), "space")` — the `!` is false for an empty body); demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:104-113 (valueOrThrow / parsePickerColor throw); demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:88-95 (`} catch { previousInvalid = input; if (!initialParse) flashParseError(); }`); demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:87-89. `grep -n "instanceof PickerColorError" demo` → no matches. Authority: docs/tranches/V/ARCHITECTURE.md:245 — "ParseResult<T> = … is the only parse-failure protocol … never a partial Color or substitute." Live probe output: AFTER ENTER {"text":"oklch()","errorBadgeText":"not a valid color","errorClass":true,"newConsoleErrors":[],"newPageErrors":[]} vs CONTROL zzzzz {"errorBadgeText":"not a valid color","errorClass":true,"newConsoleErrors":[]} — bit-identical. In-graph library probe: "oklch()" -> THROWS TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace'); "zzzzz" -> ok:false + diagnostics.
```

**Reproduction.** Dev server at http://localhost:9000. Fresh Chromium context, 1440x900. Navigate to /#/, wait 2.5s. Click button[aria-label="Toggle action bar"], then button[aria-label="Open color input"]. Click span.color-input, Meta+A, type `oklch(` then `)`, press Enter. Observe: red badge "not a valid color", zero console errors, zero page errors. Repeat with `zzzzz` — identical. Script: /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/CHL-colorinput-probe.mjs. Screenshot: .../scratchpad/CHL-oklch.png. Node-only: `node --input-type=module -e "import {parseCssColor} from './dist/subpaths/css.js'; parseCssColor('oklch()')"` → TypeError.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the exception channel entirely. `parsePickerColor` returns ParseResult<CssColor> unconverted; useColorParsing consumes it structurally with NO try/catch, so a genuine exception propagates to demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue where it is visible; `parseError` becomes ShallowRef<readonly ParseIssue[] | null> and ColorInput renders diagnostics[0].code/.expected — the library already carries UTF-16 spans, expected, actual and stable codes (src/css/types.ts:10-23) and the demo throws all of them away. valueOrThrow survives only for total operations. Separately, at the library: src/css/grammar.ts:181 `slash[0] ?? ""` so the empty-body path falls out as components.length !== 3 → failure(source). Net deletion, no new abstraction.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-30 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** A failed login is completely silent: the slug-edit layer closes as if it succeeded, and there are three independent, redundant reasons no error can reach the user. (1) `SlugEditLayer.vue:54` calls `pm.onSlugSwitch(...)` with no `await` inside a `try`, while `useSlugMigration.ts:51` declares it `async` — the `catch` at :57 is unreachable, and :55-56 close the layer synchronously before the network call resolves. (2) It would not matter: the callee catches everything itself (`useSlugMigration.ts:74-88`) and dispatches onto `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`, a permanently-null ref. (3) `slugError` is written at six sites in SlugEditLayer and rendered at zero — the template contains no reference to it. And the substring branches at :59-62 are a verbatim resurrection of the exact bug `useSlugMigration.ts:77-82` records as killed at S.W2 W2-6 (`ApiProblem` does `super(title)`, so `e.message` is the server title and can never contain '409'/'404'/'429').

**Mechanism.** error channel swallowed three ways: un-awaited async across a component boundary; callee catches into a null instance ref; error state with no template binding — plus a condemned string-sniff re-authored after its cure was recorded

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:54 (un-awaited) · :57 (catch) · :59-62 (substring sniff) · :13,18,43,49,59-62 (slugError writes) · `sed -n '74,119p' SlugEditLayer.vue | grep slugError` → no output (never rendered). demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:51 (`async function onSlugSwitch`) · :77-82 (the S.W2 W2-6 ruling comment) · :84-87 (correct typed path, dispatched into null). demo/platform/transport/api-problem.ts:22-33 (`super(title)`). LIVE REPRODUCTION (LDOCK-probe6.mjs, WebKit 1440x900, http://localhost:9000): after filling 'aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd' and clicking button[aria-label="Switch to slug"] — `[after submit] inputValue:"" layerInert:true layerAriaHidden:"true" errorish:[]`, dock still shows 'Login', console tail contains only the two boot lines, no error from the login attempt.
```

**Reproduction.** node LDOCK-probe6.mjs (scratchpad) against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000 — open the dock Login button, fill the slug input, submit; observe layer closes inert+aria-hidden, input cleared, zero error text anywhere in the DOM (`errorish: []`), clean console. The dev server's API is deliberately misconfigured (its own status lamp reads 'dev misconfigured'), so the attempt is guaranteed to fail.

**Proposed cure.** `onSlugSwitch` returns its outcome (`Promise<Result<void, ApiProblem>>`) instead of dispatching it onto a component instance; the layer awaits and renders the failure. One contract change removes all three swallows at once — awaiting makes it observable, returning kills the instance-ref channel, rendering kills the dead state. Rides L-6/L-24's move of the session port to `demo/platform/auth/`, so the login surface becomes a function with a typed result rather than a feature-owned side effect.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The dock view-select trigger renders an EMPTY label on 7 of the demo's 14 views: the Select's model value and its option set are owned by different modules with different ranges, so the selected value routinely matches no SelectItem.

**Mechanism.** split enumeration / no single owner of the navigation taxonomy — the option set and the model value are computed from two different modules

**Evidence.**

```
Screenshots, same matrix (safari-desktop-light, 1440 CSS px, isDesktop true): docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png shows the trigger reading "Browse"; atmosphere.png and admin-users.png show icon+chevron with NO text. Mechanism from source: DockViewSelect.vue:73 renders `<SelectValue v-if="isDesktop" />` with no placeholder; node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Select/SelectValue.js:33-42 computes `selectedLabel` by looking modelValue up in `rootContext.optionsSet` and falling back to "", and `slotText` returns `props.placeholder` (default "", lines 10-14) when the lookup misses. Ranges: `:model-value="currentView"` (Dock.vue:169) has range 14 (viewSchema.ts:30-44); `viewEntries` (Dock.vue:173) has range 7 at a time (useDockAdminMode.ts:26-27,34-40). All three shots also show the "Login" control, i.e. unauthenticated — capture.mjs has no login step (grep for admin|login|auth returns only the five route literals at lines 32-36).
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere (or /#/blob or any /#/admin/*) unauthenticated at viewport width >= 1024px. The dock view-select trigger shows its icon and chevron with no visible label. Compare /#/browse, which reads "Browse". Already captured in the harness shots listed above.

**Proposed cure.** Do NOT add a placeholder — that hides it. Make it structurally impossible: derive the option set as `viewsInGroup(activeGroup) ∪ {currentView}` so the model value is an option by construction. Requires the single nav schema of L-2.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The component is homed one directory above its only consumer. `demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:15` is the sole upward SFC edge out of the `dock/` module — every other `../` edge from `dock/*.vue` carries a key or a type, never a component. W43b's stated rule ("feature homes") was applied correctly 15 times and mis-applied once: the file was routed to the shell layer because it is called "Pane...", not to `dock/` where its only consumer lives. A module boundary a component's name can override is not a boundary. Compounded by CARRY-LEDGER.md:22 keeping the file alive "for exactly this gate" — structure held in place by an audit counter has no owner.

**Evidence.**

```

Component's own admission: `demo/shell/PaneSegmentedControl.vue:39-40` "This control lives inside the dock's mobile aperture (312px at 390w)". Origin: `git show --name-status --find-renames --format="" 6dc12aad | grep -i segmented` -> `R100  demo/@/components/custom/panes/PaneSegmentedControl.vue  demo/shell/PaneSegmentedControl.vue` (commit `6dc12aad feat(v-w43b)!: panes/ 16->0 — distribute/promote/relocate to feature homes`), a zero-content rename. `ls demo/shell/` -> only PaneSegmentedControl.vue, PaneSlot.vue, dock/, usePaneRouter.ts, useViewManager.ts, viewSchema.ts; the other four all have multiple cross-feature consumers.
```

**Reproduction.** cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && grep -rn 'from "\.\./[^/]' demo/shell/dock/*.vue demo/shell/dock/*/*.vue && git show --name-status --find-renames --format="" 6dc12aad | grep -i segmented

**Proposed cure.** DELETE the file (this is what W47's `1->0` means; it is not a move). Add `paneTabs: Ref<readonly {label:string; value:"0"|"1"}[] | null>` to `ViewManager`, derived from `currentConfig`; `Dock.vue` then renders `<SegmentedTabs :options="viewManager.paneTabs.value" ...>` inline in ~7 declarative lines with zero derivation (adding no logic to the 359-line Dock.vue, per edict 1). Eleven pane authors are asked to remember a rule nobody wrote down.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The mobile PaneSlot instance omits `:on-mount`, so `colorPickerRef` is provably always null at mobile viewports. Six affordances become silent no-ops (dock action bar, commit-edit, cancel-edit, two palette-pane edit emits, emitApply/emitSetCurrentColor fallbacks) and the palette->edit path stalls 2000 ms then console.warns and abandons.

**Mechanism.** A whole-application capability (edit commit) is wired per-slot-instance by hand in the template. Three slots, two wirings, nothing in the type system to catch the third — `onMount?` is an OPTIONAL prop. Every downstream call site then masks the omission with `?.`, so the failure is silent rather than loud.

**Evidence.**

```
colorPickerRef.value has exactly ONE writer: demo/color-picker/App.vue:325, inside onDesktopLeftMount (App.vue:323-328). `grep -n "on-mount" demo/color-picker/App.vue` returns ONLY :105 (desktop-left) and :131 (desktop-right). The mobile slot at App.vue:83-91 passes component/component-key/component-props/transition-name/max/appear/on-appeared and NO :on-mount. Breakpoint gate: App.vue:310-312 `(min-width: 1024px) and (min-aspect-ratio: 1.1)`. Dead consumers: App.vue:38 `:action-bar="colorPickerRef?.actionBarContext ?? null"`, App.vue:41 `@commit-edit="colorPickerRef?.commitEdit(); ..."`, App.vue:42 cancel-edit, demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:156-157, demo/color-picker/composables/usePaletteWiring.ts:66-72 and :122-126. Stall: usePaletteWiring.ts:33-58 `PICKER_WAIT_ATTEMPTS = 40` x `setTimeout(poll, 50)` = 2000 ms, then console.warn('[usePaletteWiring] gave up waiting for the color picker to mount (startEdit).'); reached from emitStartEdit at :106-119. Affected surface captured at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/palettes.png.
```

**Reproduction.** Static enumeration is complete and airtight: the sole writer of colorPickerRef.value (App.vue:325) is inside onDesktopLeftMount, which is bound only at App.vue:105 (desktop-left slot). Therefore under `!isDesktop` (App.vue:77 v-if branch) colorPickerRef is null for the session lifetime. Runtime signature to observe: load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 390x844, click a saved palette colour's edit affordance, watch the console — the [usePaletteWiring] give-up warning fires ~2 s later and the edit never starts.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the onMount ref-capture channel entirely. Panes that expose commands REGISTER them into a `PANE_COMMANDS_KEY` registry provided once by App.vue, filling their slice in onActivated and clearing it in onDeactivated. The shell reads `commands.picker?.commitEdit`. One home, provided once, structurally identical at every breakpoint — and whenColorPickerReady's 2 s poll, the PaneActionRefs Ref<any> triple, and eight `?.()` maskings die in the same commit.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** ActionButton hand-rolls glass-ui's dock keep-open protocol by reaching into `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock`'s DI context from a leaf, without the producer's single-token latch or its onScopeDispose release. The unbalanced acquire/release pair corrupts a shared ref-count owned by GlassDock and steals Dock.vue's own hold, collapsing the dock while its action bar is open.

**Mechanism.** Duplicated ownership of a library-owned ref-counted protocol, implemented without the invariant (one outstanding token per owner) that makes the shared counter safe; plus a cross-boundary DI reach from a leaf component into the design system's dock context.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/ActionButton.vue:55 (`import { useOptionalDockContext } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock"`), :81-88 (`dock?.keepOpen()` / `dock?.release()`). Producer already ships the prop: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/popover/Popover.vue.d.ts:16 `/** Hold an ancestor GlassDock open while this surface is visible. */ keepDockOpen?: boolean;` and dockContext.d.ts:14 'Hover-driven dock popovers compose <Popover trigger="hover" keep-dock-open>'. Producer impl with latch+teardown: dist/popover-BQGYXZyO.js:41-47 (`let b=r(),x=!1; function S(){x&&=(b?.release(),!1)} watch([c,()=>n.keepDockOpen],([e,t])=>{e&&t&&b&&!x?(b.keepOpen(),x=!0):(!e||!t)&&S()},{immediate:!0}), onScopeDispose(S)`). Counter that clamps: dist/dock.js:332 `function I(){g.value++,T()}` / :336 `function L(){g.value=Math.max(0,g.value-1),…}`. LIVE MEASUREMENT (Playwright, http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, 1440x900, Tools open, DockContext instrumented with stack capture): after hover -> log=[release <- ActionButton.vue:71, keepOpen <- ActionButton.vue:69], held=true; after click -> +[release,keepOpen] both ActionButton.vue, held=true; after pointer leave -> +[release], held=FALSE while toolsPressed="true"; after 8s -> +[release], dock class = COLLAPSED with toolsPressed="true". Final tally keepOpen x2 / release x4, all four attributed to ActionButton.vue. (Served-SFC lines 69/71 are script-setup offsets for source lines 84/86.)
```

**Reproduction.** 1) dev server at localhost:9000, viewport 1440x900. 2) navigate #/gradient, wait for settle, hover the dock to expand. 3) click aria-label="Toggle action bar". 4) in the page, walk document.querySelector('.glass-dock').__vueParentComponent.provides[Symbol(glass-ui:dock-context)] and wrap keepOpen/release with counters + new Error().stack. 5) mouse.move onto button.action-button-wrapper[aria-label="Copy CSS"], wait 1.2s -> keepOpen fires. 6) mouse down+up in place, wait 1.8s. 7) mouse.move to (700,820), wait 1.5s -> held becomes false though the action bar is still open. 8) wait 8s -> .glass-dock gains class `collapsed` while aria-pressed="true" on the Tools toggle.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the useOptionalDockContext import and both hold handlers; declare the hold on the component already being wrapped: `<Popover trigger="hover" keep-dock-open :open-delay="300" :close-delay="0">`. The latch and onScopeDispose come from the owner of the counter. Unique semantic ownership restored: the dock hold is glass-ui's.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The action ActionButton fires is a three-hop optional-chained dispatch through `Ref<any>` owned by the shell router, and it is structurally dead on the mobile layout: the mobile <PaneSlot> binds no :on-mount, so all three pane refs stay null. All nine generic dock actions are silent no-ops on phones while the button still plays its 400ms success animation.

**Mechanism.** Inverted ownership direction — a pane's own verbs are declared in the shell router, keyed by string, and dispatched onto the pane through a layout-specific template-ref capture. The capability becomes a function of which PaneSlot rendered the component, and every hop is an untyped `?.` that silently no-ops.

**Evidence.**

```
Chain: ActionButton.vue:98 `emit("action")` -> GenericActionBar.vue:28 `@action="act.handler()"` -> demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:196-222 e.g. :208 `handler: () => paneRefs.gradient.value?.reset?.()` -> demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientPane.vue:12 `reset: () => visualizerRef.value?.resetGradient?.()`. Untyped: usePaneRouter.ts:106-110 `generate: Ref<any>; gradient: Ref<any>; mix: Ref<any>`; App.vue:317-319 `ref<any>(null)`; eslint.config.js:70,184 `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: off`. Layout asymmetry: demo/color-picker/App.vue:83-91 (mobile PaneSlot — NO :on-mount) vs :105 `:on-mount="onDesktopLeftMount"` and :131 `:on-mount="onDesktopRightMount"`; App.vue:315 comment 'Populated by the onMount callbacks on the desktop PaneSlots'. LIVE MEASUREMENT at 390x844 on #/gradient reading the App instance setupState: {"innerWidth":390,"innerHeight":844,"mq":false,"isDesktopSetup":false,"gradientPaneRef":"null","dockActionButtons":3}. Confirmation animation fires regardless: ActionButton.vue:92-99 sets isClicked for 400ms unconditionally.
```

**Reproduction.** 1) viewport 390x844. 2) navigate http://localhost:9000/#/gradient and reload; wait 5s. 3) evaluate: walk .glass-dock __vueParentComponent up to the App instance, read setupState.gradientPaneRef (unwrapping refs) -> null; matchMedia('(min-width: 1024px) and (min-aspect-ratio: 1.1)').matches -> false; document.querySelectorAll('button.action-button-wrapper').length -> 3. 4) open Tools and click Reset/Copy CSS/Seed — handler evaluates `null?.reset?.()`, nothing happens, no console error, icon still animates.

**Proposed cure.** Invert the dependency: add `demo/shell/dock/dockActions.ts` exporting a typed `DockAction { key, icon, title, description, rotateOnClick?, iconClass?, disabled?, active?, run: () => void }` plus `DOCK_ACTIONS_KEY` and `provideDockActions()`. Each pane calls provideDockActions([...]) in its own setup, closing over its own local functions — fully typed, no refs, no `any`, no `?.`, layout-independent. Delete PaneActionRefs, the three Ref<any>, the 27 lines of handler literals in usePaneRouter, both onDesktop*Mount callbacks in App.vue, and the pure-forwarding defineExpose shims in GeneratePane/GradientPane. The mobile/desktop asymmetry is then inexpressible.
