### `design` · D-1 · design

**Defect.** The certified accent ink on the Login/Profile dock trigger measures 3.43:1 rendered contrast in the light scheme (WCAG 1.4.3 floor 4.5:1 for 16.4px/700 normal text). Dark scheme fails on the neighbour: @mbabb measures 4.18:1.

**Mechanism.** Missing composite layer in the ink referent. demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:151-153 resolves the `chrome` rung from `.glass-dock`'s backgroundColor over the ambient — ONE alpha layer. The glyph composites over TWO: the dock band plus the Button's `glass-wash` capsule. The same two-layer divergence is documented and cured for `veil` at useContrastSafeColor.ts:154-206 and never migrated to the dock trigger. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1 ('a token name is not evidence') and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.8.

**Evidence.**

```
Pixel measurement on docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png over the glyph band x768-834, y30-50 CSS: ink=(170,0,67) L=0.0895, ground=(200,167,172) L=0.4290 -> 3.43:1. The ink equals the live computed `color: oklch(0.470927 0.188343 9.834023)` exactly, so the sample is the glyph core. Dark shot: @mbabb ink=(212,205,202) on (112,88,80) -> 4.18:1. Button's own background measured `oklab(0.721325 0.00492 0.010865 / 0.6)`.
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(92%25+88.8+20+/+82.7%25) at 1440x900 light. Sample the 'Login' glyph pixels and the pill background behind them; contrast = 3.43:1. Equivalently: getComputedStyle on the button returns color oklch(0.470927 0.188343 9.834023) and backgroundColor oklab(0.721325 .00492 .010865 / 0.6) over a dock band measured (246,169,194).

**Proposed cure.** Delete the wash from under the accent ink rather than teaching the certifier about it: glass-ui 7's `emphasis="quiet"` paints `background: transparent; box-shadow: none`, so the glyph composites on the one surface the `chrome` rung already models — the referent becomes true by construction and the control regains a real hover. If the wash must stay, add a `chrome-trigger` InkSurface probed off the MOUNTED button, the exact idiom `veil` already uses. System rule: an ink's referent is the mounted element's own painted stack, never a modelled tier.

### `design` · D-2 · design

**Defect.** The GitHub menu row renders as a broken two-line item — glyph on line 1, the word 'GitHub' on line 2, flush left instead of in the shared text column — in both schemes, desktop and mobile. It also nests a focusable <a href> inside [role=menuitem][tabindex=-1].

**Mechanism.** glass-ui's DropdownMenuItem does not forward `as-child`, so the anchor stays a child of the item. As a shrink-to-fit block (53.6px) inside a 200.6px flex row it cannot hold a 14px glyph plus ' GitHub ' on one line, and wraps. Secondarily the anchor is focusable inside a roving-focus menu, so Tab can leave the menu's own order.

**Evidence.**

```

Computed: row display:flex gap:8px width 200.6; anchor display:block width 53.6 height 36.9. Row geometry (offsets within row): Share color icon 8/15 text 30/12.4 h44.0 | GitHub icon 8/6 text 8/21.9 h48.9 | Dark mode icon 8/10 text 32/12.4 h44.0. Mobile (iPhone 14): GitHub 55.4 vs 44.0 siblings. Visible in evidence-mbabb-menu-light.png and -dark.png.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/ at 1440x900, click the @mbabb trigger. The GitHub row shows the octocat on one line and 'GitHub' beneath it, misaligned by 22-24px from the sibling text column, row 48.9px vs 44px.

**Proposed cure.** A link row IS a link: use the producer's supported `as="a"` on the item so exactly one element carries role=menuitem, the href and the row layout. Retire the hand-rolled 700-byte octocat <path> (duplicated byte-for-byte at ProfileSection.vue:161 and MobileMenuDropdown.vue:95) in favour of one system-owned icon so the menu's icon family stops mixing solid and 2px-stroke marks.

**Defect.** The magnifier loupe renders blank on every first show and stays permanently blank on the touch path. `showLoupeAt` flips `loupeVisible` and calls `drawLoupe` in the same synchronous tick, but the canvas is behind `v-if="loupe.loupeVisible.value"`, so `loupeCanvasRef.value` is still null and the draw is silently skipped. ```
demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60 (showLoupeAt) and :27-30 (drawLoupe early return); ImageEyedropper.vue:78-86 (v-if + canvas). MEASURED (probe2 §A): A_pinned {loupeVisible:true, loupeNonZeroPx:9604, di110:2} → Escape → A_tapNoHover {loupeVisible:true, loupeNonZeroPx:0, di110:2} → A_afterOneMove {loupeNonZeroPx:0, di110:2}. Independent replication (probe4): {"pointermoves":40,"getImageDataCalls":40,"loupeDraws":39} — the missing draw is the first. Visual: .playwright-mcp/eyedropper-live.png shows an empty green-ringed circle.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/extract → upload any image → click the preview to open the eyedropper → tap once WITHOUT moving the pointer first (i.e. any touch tap). The loupe appears and is empty; it never fills. Scripted: .playwright-mcp/probe2.js section A.

**Proposed cure.** Keep the loupe canvas permanently mounted and gate visibility on opacity/visibility instead of v-if. This kills the race by construction, lets the already-declared `.loupe { transition: opacity }` (ImageEyedropper.vue:270 — currently dead CSS) actually run, and removes a DOM create/destroy from the hover path. **Defect.** `justUnpinned` is a component-scope latch whose only exit is inside `onTap`; a drag never reaches `onTap`, so after pin → press-drag → release the flag stays true and the NEXT legitimate tap is silently swallowed.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · C1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Drop-to-upload is inoperative in the empty state: the root never cancels `dragenter`, so Chromium does not deliver `drop` when the release lands on a drag update that changed the drag target element. Silent — no error line, no live region, no state change.

**Mechanism.** drag-target-crossing: only `dragover` is cancelled, so any drag update that changes the target element is not accepted and the following release is never dispatched as `drop`; the zone's own children guarantee the crossings

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:23-25 (@dragover.prevent + @drop.prevent, no dragenter handler); children at :46-48 are independently hit-testable. MEASURED (evidence/idz-probe6.mjs, real CDP Input.dispatchDragEvent): G1_shipped_travelThenRelease -> {"dropEventsDelivered":0,"previewNaturalW":null,"errorLine":null}, trace `dragEnter@P1 -> dragenter@ROOT / dragOver@P1 -> dragover@ROOT / dragOver@P2 -> dragenter@span.prompt + dragleave@ROOT / dragOver@P3 -> dragenter@svg.icon + dragleave@span.prompt / drop@P2 -> dragenter@span.prompt + dragleave@svg.icon` (no drop). G2_cured_travelThenRelease (identical gesture + one injected line `zone.addEventListener("dragenter", e => e.preventDefault())`) -> {"dropEventsDelivered":1,"previewNaturalW":64} with `drop@P2 -> drop@span.prompt`. G3_shipped_stillPointer and G4_shipped_replaceOverPreview both -> 1 drop / naturalWidth 64. Canon: MDN 'HTML Drag and Drop API - Define a drop zone' requires preventDefault() in BOTH the dragenter and dragover handlers.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imagedropzone/evidence/idz-probe6.mjs — compare G1_shipped_travelThenRelease.dropEventsDelivered (0, no preview) with G2_cured_travelThenRelease (1, naturalWidth 64). By hand: http://localhost:9000/#/extract with no image loaded, drag a PNG from Finder onto the zone, move the pointer across the icon/caption, release. No image loads.

**Proposed cure.** Transposition, not patch: the zone is trying to be a drop target AND a container of independently hit-testable children. Make it one thing — `pointer-events: none` on every child of the drop surface, so the root is the only drag target and no crossing ever occurs; that single declaration cures C1 and C2 together and adds no handler, no module, no wrapper. Add `@dragenter.prevent` regardless, because the spec requires it to make the target valid on first entry.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `data-mix-target` — the documented anchor the mix convergence lands on — is silently dropped and never reaches the DOM; the animation falls back to a guessed landing point. Compounded: the anchor's host element is also absent for the first ~281 ms of every re-mix.

**Mechanism.** F-A: a declared thing the runtime silently declines to honour. `inheritAttrs:false` + no `$attrs` forwarding voids the attribute contract, and `vue-tsc` models unknown component attributes as legal fall-through so nothing diagnoses it. F-B: the anchor also lives inside the `<Transition mode="out-in">` (:60) that serialises leave-then-enter, so it is absent at the `flush:"post"` tick where `collectStage` measures.

**Evidence.**

```
MixResultDisplay.vue:69 stamps `data-mix-target` on `<WatercolorDot>`. glass-ui@7.0.0 `dist/watercolor-dot.js` compiles to `inheritAttrs: !1` with only `c = i(() => n.class)` and `f = i(() => n.style)` bound — no `mergeProps($attrs)`. Live (evidence/challengeC-probe3.mjs): `dataMixTargetCount: 0` while `platePresent: true, ghostDot: true`; ghost-dot attribute list = [data-v-292b9032, data-v-0f138735, aria-hidden, class, data-testid, data-variant, style]. Consumer at mixStage.ts:121-124 then always takes `{ x: root.clientWidth/2, y: root.scrollHeight*0.7, r: 28 }`. Re-mix rAF trace (evidence/challengeC-probe10.mjs): t=22ms wellPresent:false innerCls 'vj-morph-leave-from vj-morph-leave-active' → t=281ms wellPresent:true; MIX_ARRIVE_MS=700 (mixStage.ts:22).
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-resultdisplay/evidence/challengeC-probe3.mjs (anchor count 0) and .../challengeC-probe10.mjs (281 ms arrival) against the dev server at http://localhost:9000.

**Proposed cure.** Hoist the announced destination OUT of the `<Transition>` so one persistent box serves both phases, and stamp `data-mix-target` on that element — one this component owns, not on the glass-ui primitive. This subsumes the attribute fix and the 281 ms absence in one move. Separately relay a `v-bind="$attrs"` / `as`/`asChild` seam request to glass-ui (BH inbox), but do not wait on it.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (component: demo/workbenches/gr` · C-01 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** All three `back` family tiles destroy the entire Gradient workbench on a single click. The strip paints, labels, and renders bespoke overshoot headroom for curves whose codomain leaves [0,1]; a demo seam demotes the library's Result into an uncaught throw inside a render-path computed, so the error boundary eats the pane.

**Mechanism.** Domain contract violated across a module boundary, with a Result->throw demotion at the seam; the throw is raised inside a computed on the render path.

**Evidence.**

```
Live at HEAD f36f780c, one clean WebKit context per press (probe-C3-back-family-crash.mjs):
{"id":"ease-out-circ","clicked":true,"stripAlive":true,"pressed":["ease-out-circ"],"readout":"cubic-bezier(0.075, 0.82, 0.165, 1)","boundary":null}
{"id":"ease-in-back","clicked":true,"stripAlive":false,"pressed":[],"readout":null,"boundary":"unexpected error."}
{"id":"ease-out-back","clicked":true,"stripAlive":false,"pressed":[],"boundary":"unexpected error."}
{"id":"ease-in-out-back","clicked":true,"stripAlive":false,"pressed":[],"boundary":"unexpected error."}
Chain: src/color/operations.ts:65 (returns err color_progress_out_of_range) -> demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientInterpolation.ts:37 and composables/useGradientCSS.ts:207 (throw) -> easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:53-59 (called inside a computed) -> easingCatalogue.ts:176-190 (mints back tiles, no domain check). EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:172-179 documents the overshoot and sets overflow:visible for exactly these curves.
```

**Reproduction.** Start dev server on :9000. Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, wait for the Easing card, click [data-specimen='ease-in-back'] (or ease-out-back / ease-in-out-back). The whole pane is replaced by the error boundary. Control: [data-specimen='ease-out-circ'] presses clean. Script: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-easingspecimenstrip/probe-C3-back-family-crash.mjs

**Proposed cure.** Total the progress domain ONCE at the ramp seam rather than patching call sites: clamp eased t to [0,1] where it becomes a mix progress (useGradientCSS.easingFnOf's return, or a rampProgress(fn,t) beside it) so useSpecimenRows, serializeIntervalRamp and serializeCoalescedGradient all inherit totality; then DELETE both throw sites, which become unreachable. A CSS gradient interval physically cannot produce a color outside its endpoints, so an overshooting timing function MEANS hold-at-endpoint. Deleting the back family instead is strictly worse: the producer picker still offers those curves and it contradicts the strip's own overshoot design.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfig` · R4-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The `HSL` row this component offers (one of nine, rendered identically to the eight that work) makes the pane's only verb throw `color_non_finite` for a pure-white operand, and the throw collapses the entire application to the app-root error boundary. The component's own missing-chip signal is rendered as the same blank it uses for 'honest absence', so the UI actively conceals the fault.

**Mechanism.** Division by a denominator that is exactly zero at the L=1 domain boundary, guarded on the wrong operand (numerator `delta` instead of the denominator), combined with a demo boundary (picker-color.ts:105-117 `valueOrThrow`) that converts the library's Result discipline back into exceptions on a path with no handler.

**Evidence.**

```
src/color/anchors.ts:167-174 (`delta === 0 ? 0 : delta / (1 - Math.abs(2 * lightness - 1))`); src/color/operations.ts:47-52 routes all cross-space conversion through XYZ; measured `white -> srgb-lin: [1.0000000000000004, 0.9999999999999998, 1]` so delta≈6e-16≠0 while the denominator is 0. Cube sweep: `samples=4096  failures=1  rgb(255 255 255) -> color_non_finite`. Per-space startMix for [#ffffff,#000000]: 8 spaces return a color, `hsl  chip=NULL(hidden) startMix=!!! THREW: color_non_finite`. `grep -rn "catch|try {|error|Error" demo/workbenches/mix/*.vue demo/workbenches/mix/composables/*.ts` → zero matches. useMixingState.ts:87 `parseColorIn(selection.css, colorSpace.value)` uncaught. Live: `{ boundaryVisible: true, bodyText: "… This panel hit an unexpected error. color_non_finite Try again", panes: 0 }` with errors `none` in both steps.
```

**Reproduction.** EXECUTED, live, on http://localhost:9000 — (1) navigate to /#/gradient; (2) type `linear-gradient(90deg, #ffffff 0%, #ff0000 100%)` into the field labelled 'Gradient CSS'; (3) choose 'HSL' from the 'Interpolation space' combobox (the same INTERPOLATION_SPACES array MixConfigBar.vue:18,107 renders). Result: both panes replaced by the ErrorBoundary, `panes: 0`, no console error and no page error emitted. Module-level: `parseColorIn("#ffffff", "hsl")` throws PickerColorError("color_non_finite") from picker-color.ts:106. In MixConfigBar's own pane the identical click fires the moment C-2 is cured, or today in palettes mode with two saved palettes containing white (MixSourceSelector.vue:246 is a real native button).

**Proposed cure.** Two independent repairs, both subtractive. (1) anchors.ts:173 — guard the denominator: `const denom = 1 - Math.abs(2*lightness - 1); denom === 0 ? 0 : delta / denom`; one expression kills the whole L∈{0,1} class. (2) Stop converting Results into throws on a user-reachable path: the library is Result-typed by design and sample.ts already handles failure honestly at :64/:81 — startMix (useMixingState.ts:79-101) is the only one of the two that lies. Keep the Result and render an honest failure instead of letting it climb to App.vue:50.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (r3: blind third replication + ` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The magnifier loupe renders nothing on every touch device, permanently: `showLoupeAt` paints before Vue mounts the `v-if` canvas, and `onHover`'s `if (pinned.value) return` guarantees no redraw ever follows a tap.

**Mechanism.** Event handler mutates reactive state then acts on the DOM synchronously, before the render flush — the effect is a side effect of the event rather than a derivation of the state.

**Evidence.**

```
WebKit mobile DPR 3, single tap: {"readout":"lab(54.290541404672% 80.804928170435 69.890964768624)","loupeVisible":true,"loupeOpaquePx":0,"backing":110,"dpr":3,"buttons":3}. Chromium mobile DPR 2: loupeOpaquePx 0 at tap, still 0 at +800ms, still 0 after tap#3. Same code path with a preceding hover (desktop): loupeOpaquePx 9683. Code: useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60 (paint in the same tick as the visibility flip), guard at useLoupeCanvas.ts:30, v-if at ImageEyedropper.vue:78-86, hover gate at ImageEyedropper.vue:165. ```

**Reproduction.** Open /#/extract on any touch device (or Playwright hasTouch context), upload an image, tap the preview to open the eyedropper, tap the image once. The loupe circle is empty and never fills. `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe3.mjs` section 1 (WebKit) reproduces it.

**Proposed cure.** Stop conditionally mounting the loupe canvas. Keep it permanently in the DOM and drive only its visibility (opacity/hidden) from `loupeVisible`, so `drawLoupe` always holds a live 2D context and the paint stops being ordered against Vue's scheduler at all. Equivalently (r2's formulation): make the paint a post-flush `watch([loupeVisible, loupeRelX, loupeRelY], …, { flush: 'post' })` inside `useLoupeCanvas`, which also deletes `drawLoupe`'s exported-but-unused surface. A `nextTick` inside `showLoupeAt` is the wrong patch — it makes a synchronous pointer handler async and re-opens the race under rapid taps.

Touch (CDP-dispatched multi-event drag): tap#1 red quadrant -> {"readout":"lab(54.290541404672% 8","buttons":3,"pinned":true}; after drag -> {"readout":"lab(54.290541404672% 8","buttons":1,"pinned":false}; tap#2 on the YELLOW quadrant -> {"readout":"lab(54.290541404672% 8","buttons":1,"pinned":false} (NO change at all); tap#3 same spot -> {"readout":"lab(97.607007864501% -","buttons":3,"pinned":true}. Code: ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 (capture interceptor sets the flag), :151-155 (only clearer), useInertiaGesture.ts:277-281 (`if (!didMove)` gate).

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (round 2) of demo/workbenches/g` · C2-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Three of the twenty-seven shipped specimen tiles (the whole `back` family) destroy the Gradient pane on a single click, in the default two-stop state — and the crash emits ZERO page errors and ZERO console errors, so every automated console gate (including this formation's own visual audit) is structurally blind to it.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (premise: the compo` · C-29 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Every teardown in the extract subtree is registered on `onBeforeUnmount`, but every pane in this app is rendered inside `<KeepAlive>` (demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120, routed by demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:85). A view change DEACTIVATES the subtree — the DOM leaves the document but the component is not unmounted — so `onBeforeUnmount` never fires and NO teardown in this component ever runs on a view switch. Three independent resources leak as a result: the camera MediaStream, the quantize Worker, and the eyedropper's window keydown listener. This OVERTURNS the pass-2 negative result which recorded these same three hooks as 'Clean' on the basis of source presence.

**Mechanism.** lifecycle-hook mismatch with the host contract — teardown registered for an unmount the component never receives

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120 `<KeepAlive :max="max">` · demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:85 `if (name === "extract") return ExtractPane;` · ExtractWorkbench.vue:281 `onBeforeUnmount(stopCamera)` · useImageQuantize.ts:148-151 · useExtractSession.ts:194-196 · ImageEyedropper.vue:242-245. MEASURED (probe-r3/WBX-probe7.mjs): `after open : {"fileInputs":1,"videos":1,"videoHasSrcObject":[true],"streams":1,"states":[["live"]]}` → `at #/mix : {"fileInputs":0,"videos":0,"streams":1,"states":[["live"]]}` → `at #/gradient: {..."states":[["live"]]}` → `6s later : {..."states":[["live"]]}`. MEASURED (WBX-probe8.mjs): `boot {made:0,terminated:0,kd:3,files:1}` → `eyedrop open {made:1,terminated:0,kd:4,files:1}` → `at #/mix {made:1,terminated:0,kd:4,files:0}` → `at #/gradient {made:1,terminated:0,kd:4,files:0}`. The repo already documents this hazard for a sibling: demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:232-233 'The picker pane is KeepAlive-cached; navigating away parks the blob'.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/extract → click 'Open camera' → grant permission (let it fully resolve; videoHasSrcObject === true) → click any other view (Mix, Gradient). Camera hardware stays live indefinitely; only a full page reload releases it. Three steps, no timing dependency. Re-run: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-workbench/probe-r3/WBX-probe7.mjs`

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · C1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Proposed cure.** Make ordering a property of the operation, not of the array: one model action `setStopPosition(id, pos)` that maps then sorts, so sortedness is total by construction, paired with C2's identity-keyed intervals so the re-sort cannot scramble easing. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · C2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Easing intervals are keyed by array INDEX and synced by a length watcher that appends/truncates at the TAIL, while addStop inserts in sorted position — so inserting a stop silently moves the user's authored curve onto a different pair of stops and reverts the authored segment to linear.

**Mechanism.** An adjacency relation (which pair of stops a curve belongs to) is modelled as a positional array, and the sync watcher observes only `stops.length`, so it cannot know where the stop landed and always guesses 'at the end'.

Code: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:89-100.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000 → Gradient → click the rail at 50% → open interval row 2 → click the `steps` specimen → click the rail at 25% → read `.readout-rail code` and `.interval-head` text.

**Proposed cure.** Hang the interval on the stop that OPENS it — `GradientStop { id, cssColor, position, easing }` (last stop's easing ignored) — so the curve travels with its own stop through any insert/remove/sort. Sites: src/color/operations.ts:65 (returns err, correct); demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientInterpolation.ts:37 (throws); demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:207 (throws); demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:53-59 (the throw inside a computed); easingCatalogue.ts:176-190 (mints the back tiles unguarded). The strip's own CSS comment at EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:172-179 explicitly renders headroom for these overshoot curves.
```

**Reproduction.** Fresh http://localhost:9000/#/gradient (default two-stop gradient, Easing row 1 open). Click [data-specimen="ease-in-out-expo"] -> OK, readout cubic-bezier(1, 0, 0, 1). Click [data-specimen="ease-out-circ"] -> OK, readout cubic-bezier(0.075, 0.82, 0.165, 1). Click [data-specimen="ease-in-back"] -> pane replaced by the error boundary. ease-in-out-back reproduces independently.

**Proposed cure.** Make the gradient's progress type TOTAL, once, at the ramp sampler — not in the catalogue and not as a try/catch. Introduce the [0,1] clamp at the single point where an eased t becomes a mix progress (useGradientCSS.easingFnOf's return, or a rampProgress(fn,t) helper beside it) so useSpecimenRows, serializeIntervalRamp and serializeCoalescedGradient all inherit it; this is the correct CSS-gradient semantic (an interval cannot produce a color beyond its endpoints, so overshoot MEANS hold-at-endpoint), a domain law rather than a masking fallback, and the repo already speaks the idiom (test/value-domain-clamp.test.ts). Then delete both throw sites (useGradientInterpolation.ts:37, useGradientCSS.ts:207) — with a total domain they are unreachable, and an unreachable throw on a render path is a liability. Deleting the back family instead is strictly worse: it removes curves the producer's own picker still offers and contradicts the strip's overshoot-headroom design.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The stage emits authored easing values raw across a domain-narrowing boundary: its canvas advertises y ∈ [-0.6, 1.6] while the consuming sampling law requires progress ∈ [0,1]. Two keystrokes of the component's primary interaction destroy the entire workspace with an uncaught throw.

**Mechanism.** Unguarded emission across a domain-narrowing boundary — the authoring codomain [-0.6,1.6] meets a consumer domain [0,1] and nothing reconciles them; `onAuthored` is the single funnel where they meet and it is a pass-through.

**Evidence.**

```
Live Chromium probe (scratchpad/EAS-probe4.mjs) against http://localhost:9000/#/gradient:
```
handles=2
valuetext0=x 1.000, y 1.000
press 1: x 1.000, y 1.100 | literal=cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1.1)
*** PANE DIED after 2 ArrowUp presses ***
BODY: ... This panel hit an unexpected error. Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range Try again
```
Throw chain: src/color/operations.ts:65 and :90 (`if (progress < 0 || progress > 1) return err({ code: "color_progress_out_of_range" })`) → demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:199 (`const easedT = easing(t)`, no guard) → :204-206 (`throw new Error(...)`). Second unguarded sink at demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:53-59. Emission funnel: EasingAuthoringStage.vue:57-60.
Blast radius measured over the 30 bezierPresets at the demo's own 33-sample grid: `ESCAPES [0,1] -> CRASHES: 3 — ease-in-back (0.0969), ease-out-back (0.0868), ease-in-out-back (0.0927); SAFE: 27`. All 3 are live clickable tiles (tileCount 27 measured).
Tile-path reproduction (EAS-probe3.mjs): BEFORE {"rowCount":1,"tileCount":27,"mainLen":91083} → AFTER {"rowCount":0,"tileCount":0,"mainLen":2832}. Screenshot scratchpad/EAS-after-tile.png shows BOTH panes destroyed.
Boundary razor: cubic-bezier(0,0,1,1.12) max escape 0.00000 → safe; cubic-bezier(0,0,1,1.2) max escape 0.01953 at t=0.9688 → CRASH.
```

**Reproduction.** 1. http://localhost:9000/#/gradient  2. row 0's easing head is open by default  3. click the rail button "Author a custom curve"  4. focus `#easing-authoring-0 circle[role='slider']` index 0  5. press Shift+ArrowUp twice → whole workspace replaced by "Try again". Equivalent single-click repro: click `[data-specimen='ease-out-back']` in the open row.

**Proposed cure.** Do NOT clamp in `onAuthored` — that lies about what the user authored and must be repeated at every future consumer. Make the SAMPLING LAW total over the easing codomain, where the transposition belongs: `sampleCoalescedStops` (useGradientCSS.ts:190-212) is the one place the demo turns an easing output into a mix progress, and CSS's own linear-gradient semantics already answer the question (an overshooting timing function paints the endpoint colour past the range). ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/workbenches/g` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Pressing any `back`-family specimen tile — or dragging a picker control point outside y∈[0,1] — throws and destroys the whole Gradient pane. 3 of 27 catalogue tiles are a live crash in the default app state.

**Mechanism.** missing-domain-boundary: an easing callable's output (a motion value, unbounded) is fed straight into a color-mix progress parameter (a ratio strictly on [0,1]) at three separate sites, with no clamp at the sampling law that owns the domain.

**Evidence.**

```
Probe output: `ease-out-back  rails=[] CRASH=["This panel hit an unexpected error.Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range Try again"]` — same for ease-in-back and ease-in-out-back; linear/ease/steps/step-start/step-end/ease-in-out-expo all CRASH=no. Guard: src/color/operations.ts:88 `if (progress < 0 || progress > 1) return err({ code: "color_progress_out_of_range" });`. Unclamped call sites: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:199-208 (sampleCoalescedStops), demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:52-59 (fn(0.5)), demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer.vue:78-85 (colorAtPosition). Measured ranges on the real sampling grid (vite-node against src/subpaths/easing): ease-in-back min=-0.0969 out-of-range 18/33 fn(0.5)=-0.0636; ease-out-back max=1.0868 out-of-range 19/33 fn(0.5)=1.0676; ease-in-out-back min=-0.0923 max=1.0927 out-of-range 21/33. Drag repro: `AFTER DRAG: {"literal":null,"crash":["...color_progress_out_of_range..."]}`. Catalogue built by blind enumeration: easingCatalogue.ts:178 `for (const name of Object.keys(bezierPresets))` with no compatibility filter; GradientEasingEditor.vue:73-76 emits with no validation.
```

**Reproduction.** 1. open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient (easing row `1 → 2` is open on arrival). 2. click the `back` family's `out` tile (`[data-specimen='ease-out-back']`). 3. the entire pane is replaced by the ErrorBoundary reading "This panel hit an unexpected error. Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range". Scripted: node scratchpad/wbge-probe4.mjs ease-out-back ease-in-back ease-in-out-back. Recoverable via "Try again" (probe 7: crash 1 → 0, heads back to 1) but all pane state is lost.

**Proposed cure.** Progress into a color mix is a ratio on [0,1] and the sampling law is the ONE place that owns it. Add a private `rampProgress = (t) => Math.min(1, Math.max(0, t))` in useGradientCSS and route sampleCoalescedStops' easedT, useSpecimenRows' fn(0.5) and colorAtPosition's easedT through it — matching CSS's own behaviour (an overshoot timing function on a <color> interpolation clamps to the endpoint colour). The overshoot stays visible where it belongs: in the glyph, which samples the raw callable and needs no clamp, and in the authoring canvas. Do NOT delete the back family — the curves are legitimate and the picker authors them freely; the defect is the missing domain boundary, not the curves.

Independent tile repro: click [data-specimen='ease-out-back'] → before {mainLen:717, rows:1, tiles:27} after {mainLen:102, rows:0, tiles:0}, errs:[] (swallowed by Vue's boundary — no window.error, no console error). Preset census: `presets 30 | SAFE 27 | ESCAPES [0,1] -> CRASHES 3` — ease-in-back 0.09686@t=0.3438, ease-out-back 0.08679@t=0.6250, ease-in-out-back 0.09268@t=0.7813, all three live tiles. OR: click [data-specimen='ease-out-back'] in the open row. Both 100% deterministic.

Add a back-family regression loop to test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts, which already imports SPECIMEN_TILES.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect interrogation of demo/wo` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The component's single stated purpose — Law 3, "zero letterbox (O-17): the drawn plot IS the element box" — is dead code. Both arms (the syncVbRatio querySelector and the scoped CSS rule) key on `svg[role="img"]`, an ARIA role glass-ui removed at 6.0.0. --vb-ratio is frozen at its birth constant and the producer's inline aspect-ratio/block-size/margin survive untouched.

**Mechanism.** A consumer seat reaching into a third-party component's private DOM through an ARIA role used as a query/style hook — a coupling every instrument in the pipeline (vue-tsc, eslint, vitest) is structurally blind to. The producer's change was itself correct (a canvas of role=slider handles is a group, not an img); the consumer had no way to hear it.

**Evidence.**

```
EasingAuthoringStage.vue:48-50 (querySelector "svg[role='img']") and :104 (`.easing-authoring :deep(svg[role="img"])`). Producer: `grep -o 'role[:"][^,}]\{0,30\}' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/easing.js | sort | uniq -c` → `1 role: "group" / 1 role: "slider" / 2 role: "status"` — zero role:"img". BISECTION (new): npm pack @mkbabb/glass-ui@5.0.0 → `1 role: "img"`; @6.0.0 → `role: "group"`. value.js jumped 5→7 in one commit: `git log --oneline -S'"@mkbabb/glass-ui": "^7' -- package.json` → f2c8f565, whose body migrates a dozen symbol-level drifts and never mentions the canvas role. LIVE MEASUREMENT at #/gradient row 0 disclosed: {svgRoleImgFound:false, svgRole:"group", vbRatio:"1.2", svgInlineStyle:"aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; block-size: clamp(200px, 38cqi, 320px); margin-inline: auto;", computed:{aspectRatio:"1 / 1", blockSize:"200px", inlineSize:"272px"}, rect:{w:272,h:200}, viewBox:{x:0,y:-0.1,w:1,h:1.2}, elAspect:1.36, vbAspect:0.8333, letterboxPx:{L:52.67,R:52.67,T:0,B:0}}. Second probe at a wider pane: element 410x200 → 121.67 px per side = 59.35% of inline extent dead. O-17 tolerance is ±1 px. After 20 ArrowRight presses the viewBox moved to `0 -0.1 1 1.2000000000000002` while --vb-ratio still read "1.2".
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; expand easing row 1→2; press the sliders icon in the readout rail; console: `const s=document.querySelector('#easing-authoring-0 svg'); s.getAttribute('role')` → "group"; `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.easing-authoring')).getPropertyValue('--vb-ratio')` → "1.2"; `const r=s.getBoundingClientRect(),vb=s.viewBox.baseVal; (r.width - r.height*vb.width/vb.height)/2` → 52.67.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (demo/workbenches/extra` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The magnifier loupe renders blank on every first show, and on the touch path never renders at all — the canvas is painted one tick before the v-if element that owns it exists.

**Mechanism.** Event handler mutates reactive state and then acts on the DOM in the same synchronous tick, before Vue's render flush creates the element — compounded by a state gate (pinned) that makes the miss permanent instead of self-healing.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60 (showLoupeAt sets loupeVisible.value=true then calls drawLoupe synchronously) + :30 (early-return on !loupeCanvas) + ImageEyedropper.vue:78-86 (canvas is inside v-if="loupe.loupeVisible.value") + ImageEyedropper.vue:165 (onHover opens with `if (pinned.value) return`). MEASURED live at http://localhost:9000 (dpr 2): hover1 @ image(8,8) -> loupe opaquePx 0/12100, centerRGBA [0,0,0,0]; hover2 @ SAME coords -> opaquePx 9604/12100, centerRGBA [0,255,0,255]. Touch path, two independent runs/fixtures: A_firstTapGreen.loupe = {opaquePx:0, total:12100, centerRGBA:[0,0,0,0]}; touchTapLoupe (512x512 grid fixture) = {opaquePx:0, total:12100}.
```

**Reproduction.** On a touch device (or with synthesised touch PointerEvents): open /#/extract, drop an image, click the preview to open the eyedropper, TAP once anywhere on the image. The loupe circle appears and is fully transparent (no magnification), and stays that way until you unpin. On desktop, hover once -> blank; hover a second time -> it fills.

**Proposed cure.** Make the paint a function of state, not a side effect of an event: delete the exported-but-unused drawLoupe call from showLoupeAt and drive the canvas from a single `watch([loupeVisible, loupeRelX, loupeRelY], ..., { flush: 'post' })` inside useLoupeCanvas. That removes the ordering hazard structurally rather than sprinkling nextTick, and collapses the composable's public surface.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (demo/workbenches/extra` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `justUnpinned` is a cross-tick latch with exactly one exit, so a pan-while-pinned leaves it set and the NEXT clean tap is silently swallowed — no sample, no pin, no feedback.

**Mechanism.** A hand-rolled boolean flag carried across two separate gestures through a capture-phase side channel, whose clear-path is reachable only on one of the three ways a gesture can end.

**Evidence.**

```
ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 (capture-phase pointerdown sets justUnpinned=true whenever pinned) + :151-155 (onTap is the ONLY clearer) + useInertiaGesture.ts:277-281 (onTap fires only when !hasMoved). MEASURED, one scripted touch sequence, 16x16 fixture: A tap(8,8) -> readout `oklch(86.643961752344% 0.294827224543 142.495345041444deg)` (=#00ff00, pins); B press+drag 80px+release -> readout unchanged, pinned now false, flag stuck; C clean tap -> readout UNCHANGED (swallowed); D byte-identical tap at identical coords -> readout `oklch(59.987080562215% 0 none)` (=#808080). C and D are the same input with different outcomes.
```

**Reproduction.** Open the eyedropper, tap to sample+pin, then press-drag to pan the image, release. Now tap once to sample a new pixel — nothing happens. Tap again — it works. Every first tap after a pan is dropped.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the flag and the capture-phase interceptor. Move `pinned` into useInertiaGesture, which already owns hasMoved/isPanning, and let it decide at pointerup between unpin / sample / pan-end from facts it already has. One state machine in one place instead of two halves talking through a boolean.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/workbenches/gr` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** An ordinary edit in the CSS box (`oklch()` — the state you get by selecting the channel values and pressing Delete) destroys the entire Gradient pane and silently reseeds the model to defaults.

**Mechanism.** `applyCSS` is documented model-or-reject but is not total: `parseGradientCSS`→`isColorToken`→`parseCssColor` throws on an empty colour function (src/css/grammar.ts:181 non-null assertion). The throw crosses an emitted-handler boundary, so Vue's callWithErrorHandling routes it to onErrorCaptured; the boundary unmounts the subtree. Because `useGradientModel()` is instantiated INSIDE the component (line 32), the model's lifetime is the view's lifetime — any throw is a data-loss event.

**Evidence.**

```
GradientVisualizer.vue:102-108 (`onParseCSS`, no try); demo/color-picker/App.vue:50 + ErrorBoundary.vue:59-69. Live run, pasted: {"step0":{"handles":2,"easingReadout":"cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"},"afterMain":"This panel hit an unexpected error.\n\nCannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')\n\nTry again","handlesAfter":0,"verdict":null,"editorStillThere":false}. Headless: `npx vite-node probes/visualizer-probe.ts` → `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue) → THREW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')` (same for rgb()/color()). Screenshot: evidence/gradient-pane-destroyed-by-oklch-empty.png shows the auto-recovered pane holding the DEFAULT gradient, not the user's.
```

**Reproduction.** goto http://localhost:9000/, wait 1.2s, set location.hash='#/gradient' in-page, wait for [role=textbox][aria-label='Gradient CSS'], select all its text, insertText 'linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)', dispatch input, wait 2000ms → main.innerText is the error card, 0 stop handles, no verdict.

**Proposed cure.** Two independent moves: (a) make the grammar total — return a failure for an empty component list in src/css/grammar.ts rather than asserting slash[0] (a try/catch in the pane would be a masking fallback, edict 2); (b) transpose the ownership — hoist `useGradientModel()` to a route-scoped provide ABOVE the ErrorBoundary so the model outlives its view and 'Try again' remounts a view over surviving state.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/workbenches/gr` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Adding or removing a stop anywhere but the end silently re-hosts every authored easing curve one slot to the left and drops the last one.

**Mechanism.** Intervals are a parallel array keyed by index and reconciled by length; an insert at index k shifts the meaning of every interval ≥ k without touching the array, and appends a fresh linear at the end. Remove truncates the tail, not the removed adjacency.

**Evidence.**

```
GradientVisualizer.vue:90-92 (`onAddStop`) and :143 (`@remove`) wire into useGradientModel.ts:89-100, a watcher keyed on `stops.value.length` alone. My run: `before: 0,50,100 → cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1) | steps(4, jump-end)` / `after: 0,25,50,100 → cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1) | steps(4, jump-end) | cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)` — 'interval that was 50→100 (steps) now covers: 25→50'.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vite-node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/visualizer-probe.ts → section P2. In the UI: author steps(4) on the second easing row, click the rail at 25% to add a stop, watch the steps curve jump to the first quarter and the second half revert to linear.

**Proposed cure.** Stop modelling an adjacency relation as a parallel array. Carry the outgoing curve on the stop that begins the interval (one array, no synchronisation possible), or key intervals by the id pair `${a.id}:${b.id}` so an insert must SPLIT an interval explicitly.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/workbenches/mi` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The Mix verb is unreachable and this component's entire T-17 preview apparatus is dead in the shipped app. The only add-color affordance passes `tag="button"` to a glass-ui 7.0.0 WatercolorDot that has no `tag` prop and hard-codes `pointerEvents:"none"`, so it renders as a non-interactive, non-focusable, `aria-hidden` <span> with the consumer's aria-label and click listener dropped. `canMix` can therefore never become true in the default colors mode, `operandColors` is `[]` forever, `sampleInterpolationRamp` returns null for every row, and every preview chip is permanently absent.

Shipped runtime `dist/watercolor-dot.js` (~offset 3507): `style: u([f.value, { backgroundColor: …, borderRadius: m(b), pointerEvents: "none", … }])`. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The instrument lies: the preview <img> and the extracted palette + '% of the image' readout can describe two different images. `onFile` writes `lastFile` synchronously but writes `previewDataUrl` after an un-sequenced `await readAsDataUrl(file)` (FileReader completion is size-ordered, not call-ordered), then calls `runQuantize()` which re-reads `lastFile.value` at await-resume time. No request token reconciles the two paths.

```
demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:164-168. Live repro output: {"fileSizes":{"A":11537022,"B":107},"previewIsA_bigRed":true,"previewDataUrlLength":15382718,"dominantReadout":["oklch(45.201371817442% 0.313214388634 264.05202261637deg)"],"verdict":"DESYNC: preview=A(red), palette=B(blue)"} — hue 264.05deg is image B (blue) while the rendered img carries A's 15.4MB data URL (red).

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/gen` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The per-swatch copy verb is entirely dead: `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click` are all silently discarded by glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot, which renders a hardcoded aria-hidden span with pointer-events:none. The swatches are not buttons, have no accessible name, are not focusable, and cannot be clicked; copyColor() is unreachable.

**Mechanism.** Producer/consumer contract break absorbed by Vue's legal-fallthrough semantics: a component with inheritAttrs:false that hand-forwards a whitelist of attrs silently swallows every unlisted attr AND every listener, and the type system treats unknown attributes on a component as valid fallthrough. The consumer's documented idiom (tag="button") was never a prop.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:199-208 (the four bindings) · node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts:23-52 declares {color,variant?,animate?,cycleDuration?,range?,seed?} and no emits · `grep -o "tag" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js | wc -l` → 0 · watercolor-dot.js setup body: `inheritAttrs:!1` with `n=h(), c=i(()=>n.class), f=i(()=>n.style)` (class/style only) and root `<span aria-hidden="true" style=[attrs, {backgroundColor, borderRadius, pointerEvents:"none", …}]>` · LIVE DOM at http://localhost:9000/#/generate: {"tag":"SPAN","ariaHidden":"true","ariaLabel":null,"tabIndex":-1,"tagAttr":null,"pointerEvents":"none","cursor":"pointer","w":40,"h":40} and tabbablesInPlate = [INPUT "Palette name", BUTTON "Regenerate", BUTTON "Save palette", BUTTON "Copy all colors"] — the 5 swatches contribute 0
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/generate → click any colour swatch inside [data-generate-plate] → nothing is copied, no focus moves, no state changes. Structurally: the DOM dump above (SPAN / aria-hidden=true / pointer-events:none / tabIndex -1 / aria-label null).

**Proposed cure.** The dot is a FACE, not a SEAT. Transpose rather than patch: a real <button> seat wraps the dot (dot stays the decorative aria-hidden child it was built to be; the button carries name, focus affordance, ≥24px target, listener). Better for a 9-consumer species: glass-ui grows the seat — a WatercolorDotButton, or an explicit as/tag + attr-forwarding contract on WatercolorDot. Relay R-1 to the glass BH inbox; the consumer half is BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8. Do NOT delete the three dead bindings — that retires the verb, not the defect.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/gra` · C1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Drag (and shift+arrow) inverts stop order — the model has no ordering invariant, so the app emits CSS that its own parser rejects and the rail/tile paint a CSS-clamped lie

**Mechanism.** No invariant owner for the ordered-stop model: updateStop is a primitive map() that never re-sorts, while the parser enforces monotonicity on input only. Sortedness is an invariant on insert and a coincidence on drag.

**Evidence.**

```
Live, my own run: afterDrag labels ["Gradient stop at 77%","…50%","…63%","…100%"] (DOM order == model order); rail computed background-image head = linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 76.6%, oklch(0.657192 0.177842 256.369) 74.18%, oklch(0.664384 0.175685 247.739) 71.76%, …) — positions DESCEND. Round-trip: `npx vite-node evidence/parse-probe.ts` → parseGradientCSS -> reject: stop positions must be non-decreasing. Source: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:127-131 vs the sorting addStop at :118; guard on the way IN at gradientParse.ts:284-290.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/ → set location.hash='#/gradient' in-page → click the rail at 50% → drag the leftmost handle right to ~75%. Read the handle aria-labels in DOM order and getComputedStyle(bar).backgroundImage.

**Proposed cure.** Replace updateStop with one model action that owns ordering totally — setStopPosition(id, position) that maps then .sort((a,b)=>a.position-b.position) — landed together with C2's identity-keyed intervals so the re-sort cannot scramble easing. Sort, do not clamp: clamping to (prev,next) would make a stop un-reorderable.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/gra` · C11 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Grab-offset teleport: pressing anywhere but a handle's exact pixel centre and moving the pointer 1 px relocates the stop by the whole grab offset

**Mechanism.** onHandlePointerDown records no grab offset, so the first pointermove snaps the stop centre to the raw pointer. The 4px dead-zone the function already computes (handleGesture.moved) is wired only to the re-tap-to-deselect decision, never to the position emit.

**Evidence.**

```
Live, pasted: RESULT_grab_offset = { grabbed_px_right_of_centre: 8, pointer_travelled_px: 1, handle_travelled_px: 10.12, label_before: "Gradient stop at 0%", label_after: "Gradient stop at 2%" } on a 462px rail. Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:136-146 — emit("update:position", id, getPosition(e)) is absolute and ungated; the hit pseudo that invites the off-centre grab is .rail-handle::before at :374-391 (24px fine / var(--touch-target)=44px coarse).
```

**Reproduction.** Fresh /#/gradient, 2-stop seed. page.mouse.move(handleCentreX + 8, barCentreY); mouse.down(); mouse.move(handleCentreX + 9, barCentreY). Read the handle's aria-label and bounding-box centre before/after.

**Proposed cure.** Capture grabDx = e.clientX - handleCentreX at pointerdown (together with a cached bar rect, which also kills C3's per-move forced layout), gate the first emit on the dead-zone the file already computes (`if (!handleGesture.moved) return;`), and emit positionAt(e.clientX - grabDx). ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/gra` · C2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Adding a stop silently re-attaches every authored easing curve to a different pair of stops; removing one does the mirror

**Mechanism.** Intervals are an index-keyed parallel array; the watcher observes only stops.length so it cannot know where the stop landed and always guesses 'at the end'. An adjacency relation modelled as a positional array.

**Evidence.**

```
Live (pass 1, retained): before insert heads ["1 → 2linear","2 → 3steps"]; after clicking the rail at 25% heads ["1 → 2linear","2 → 3steps","3 → 4linear"] — steps(4, jump-end) moved from 50%→100% onto 25%→50%. Source: useGradientModel.ts:89-100 (length watcher pushes/truncates at the TAIL) vs addStop at :118 (inserts in SORTED position).
```

**Reproduction.** /#/gradient with stops [0,50,100]; open easing interval row 2, pick the steps specimen; click the rail at 25%; read the interval readouts and row heads.

**Proposed cure.** Hang the interval on the stop that OPENS it — GradientStop { id, cssColor, position, easing }, last stop's easing ignored — so the curve travels with its own stop through any insert/remove/sort. That deletes the intervals array, its sync watcher, and the three 'Gradient interval N is missing' throws (useGradientCSS.ts:189/240, GradientVisualizer.vue:77) outright.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects of demo/workbenches/gra` · C1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** User-typed CSS is fed to a partial parser with no throw path in the component's contract: the debounced `parse` emit reaches `parseCssColor`, which throws TypeError on every empty-argument colour function, and the throw escapes into Vue's emit error propagation and takes down the whole App-level ErrorBoundary — destroying both panes and all authored gradient state, with no verdict, no destructive border, and no recovery by navigation.

**Mechanism.** Partial (throwing) oracle consumed through a two-valued failure model. `parseGradientCSS` is documented model-or-reject, but `parseCssColor` has a third outcome — throw — that neither gradientParse nor the editor represents, so the failure escapes the component's verdict channel entirely and is absorbed by an app-wide error boundary. **Evidence.**

```

Blast radius via evidence/crash-forensics.mjs: {"mainChildren":1,"gradientDom":0} — the boundary is App.vue:50 wrapping the whole <main> grid (App.vue:47-140), so the palettes pane dies too. Work destroyed, evidence/state-loss.mjs: {"authored":{"stops":4},"crashed":{"stops":0},"afterRetry":{"stops":2}}. Sticky across routes, R1b: navigated to #/mix and back to #/gradient -> {"editorPresent":0,"errorBoundaryVisible":1}. Module-level corpus (npx tsx evidence/parse-probe.ts) throws for oklch() rgb() hsl() lab() lch() color() oklab() hsl(  ) AND hwb() rgba() — two beyond MT-F001's registered eight.
```

**Reproduction.** Dev server at http://localhost:9000. `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-codeeditor/evidence/live-probe.mjs` (R1, R1b, R1c). By hand: open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, click the 'Gradient CSS' editor, Cmd+A, type `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)`, wait 0.5s. The entire workspace is replaced by 'This panel hit an unexpected error.' R1c reproduces the true mid-typing sequence: type `linear-gradient(90deg, red, rgb(` -> graceful verdict 'unparseable color "rgb("'; add the closing `)` -> dead.

**Proposed cure.** Two moves, root first. (1) Land the already-ruled total parser — registry/adjudicated/parser-band.md (cand-O): `parseCssColor` must be total, `string -> Result`, killing the family rather than this instance. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The sampled color is not the color displayed under the cursor — stage, loupe and sampler use three different resampling rules over the same bitmap, and the displayed color additionally changes with devicePixelRatio while the sample does not.

**Mechanism.** useImageSampler.ts:111-119 sampleAt takes one nearest source texel via Math.floor((rx-panX)/zoom); the visible canvas (ImageEyedropper.vue:69-75) has no image-rendering declaration so the compositor smooths; useLoupeCanvas.ts:40 sets imageSmoothingEnabled=false. No single sampling model.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured composited pixels from probe/shot-desktop-light-pinned.png: (300,560)=[127,0,128], (350,500)=[159,0,96], (301,561)=[183,0,72]. Readout at that location: lab(29.568301979097% 68.287364602547 -112.029709525105) = #0000FF. Measured stage zoom 0.4233. probe/shot-forced-colors.png shows crisp red/blue texels in the loupe and flat purple in the surrounding stage in ONE frame. DPR dependence: same region reads flat purple in shot-desktop-light-pinned.png (DPR 1) and resolved red/blue moire in shot-zoom200.png (DPR 2).
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/probe/probe.mjs (displayedVsSampled.zoom 0.4233, displayedCentrePixel [95,0,160]) then probe2.mjs (hoverReadout = pure-blue lab). Or by eye: probe/shot-forced-colors.png.

**Proposed cure.** One resampling law owned in one place. zoom>=1: stage paints image-rendering:pixelated so a texel is a visible square and the loupe is that same law magnified. zoom<1: the sample is the area-average over the 1/zoom x 1/zoom source box the pointer's display pixel actually covers. Stage, loupe, reticle and readout then read one SamplerModel instead of three.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Every second tap is a dead tap that also discards the pin, leaving the PREVIOUS color displayed as if it were the current sample. On touch this is the only sampling interaction.

**Mechanism.** ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 adds a capture-phase pointerdown listener that unpins and raises `justUnpinned`; onTap (:151-155) consumes the flag with an early return. Touch has no hover, so half of all taps are no-ops while the readout keeps showing a color from a different part of the image.

**Evidence.**

```
probe2.mjs tapCycle: tap purple -> lab(29.5683...) pinned(3 buttons); tap grey -> readout UNCHANGED lab(29.5683...), unpinned(1 button); tap grey again -> lab(53.585013452169% 0 0) pinned; tap purple -> readout UNCHANGED lab(53.5850...), unpinned.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/probe2.mjs — see tapCycle table.

**Proposed cure.** Delete justUnpinned and the second, never-removed event-binding mechanism (the composable already binds the element at useInertiaGesture.ts:327-350). A tap always samples and always pins; re-sampling the same texel is idempotent; unpin belongs to Escape/close, which already own it (:226-235).

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The magnifier loupe never draws a single pixel on touch — the user taps to sample and gets an empty ring with the raw image running straight through it.

**Mechanism.** useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60 showLoupeAt sets loupeVisible=true then synchronously calls drawLoupe; the canvas is behind v-if (ImageEyedropper.vue:78-86) so loupeCanvasRef.value is still null and drawLoupe returns at :30. Every subsequent touch repeats it because the capture pointerdown handler calls hideLoupe(), unmounting the canvas again.

**Evidence.**

```
probe.mjs, WebKit 390x844 @3x hasTouch, after page.touchscreen.tap(): mobile.loupe.paintedPx = 0 of totalPx 12100. Visible in probe/shot-mobile-dark-tapped.png. Desktop after hover: paintedPx 9684 (the disc IS painted) — hover is the only thing masking it.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/probe.mjs -> mobile.loupe.paintedPx: 0.

**Proposed cure.** The loupe canvas is a fixed 110px node — keep it mounted and drive visibility with opacity, which is what the CSS already animates (:270). The v-if buys nothing and costs the first frame, which on touch is the only frame.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** In RTL the specimen canvas is rendered 692px outside its own clipping stage and disappears entirely, while the sampler keeps returning values for an image nobody can see.

**Mechanism.** The canvas is an inline-level element positioned by static flow; its layout box is the full attribute width (1200px), so in an RTL block it right-aligns from the stage's right edge (1239-1200=39) and the transform is applied on top of an accidental origin. In LTR canvasX == stageX by coincidence, and viewportToImage (useImageSampler.ts:103-109) silently depends on that coincidence. Separately the readout inherits direction:rtl with unicode-bidi:normal (measured) for a string full of parentheses and minus signs.

**Evidence.**

```
probe4.mjs — LTR: canvasX 201, stageX 201, w 508 (aligned). RTL: stageX 731 but canvasX 39, w 508 — zero overlap, and the stage is overflow-hidden. Transform identical in both, matrix(0.423333,0,0,0.423333,0,139.04). rtlRead still returns lab(29.568301979097% ...).
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/probe4.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** State the specimen's origin instead of inheriting it from flow: absolutely position the canvas at the stage's physical top-left — exactly the frame viewportToImage already assumes. Add dir=ltr / unicode-bidi:isolate on the readout per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1.

MixSourceSelector.vue:148, :150, :164-176, :211-221. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The `isProcessing` loading state never renders. During the entire compute window the UI shows the unchanged empty-state ghost and the caption "· undeveloped plate — feed it an image ·", instructing the user to do what they have already done.

**Mechanism.** `mode="out-in"` holds the entering branch until the leaving branch's transition resolves; by then isProcessing has flipped back to false, so the branch that wins is always the developed card. The out-in mode chosen to protect the skeleton is what makes it unreachable. The `role="status"` / aria-label="Loading palette" announcement is likewise never made.

**Evidence.**

```
probe-D-final.json, MutationObserver + per-rAF occupant sampler, Chrome CPU throttled 20x, 2400x2400 source: OCCUPANT TRACE = [[0,"ghost"],[2894,"card"]] — two occupants in 2.9 seconds; SKELETON never appears. Corroborated unthrottled in both engines (probe-D-focus-transition.json: ghost through t≈210ms, then card; no SKEL sample in 60 samples over 2.1s). Source: ExtractWorkbench.vue:102-107 (`<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` + `v-if="session.isProcessing.value"`). The claim it breaks is ExtractWorkbench.vue:92-99: "isProcessing swaps ghost → KNOWN-IMMINENT skeleton IN PLACE (same bones — a material change, not a layout jump)".
```

**Reproduction.** node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-workbench/probe-D-final.mjs — read the OCCUPANT TRACE line.

**Proposed cure.** Collapse ShadowPalette and PaletteCardSkeleton into ONE plate component with state: "empty" | "working" | "developed", and drop mode="out-in" so the working register can cross-fade in. The 'same bones' promise then holds structurally instead of by hand-copy across two files (which already differ: ShadowPalette strip uses gap-px + flex-1, PaletteCardSkeleton uses no gap + width:100/count%).

Frames + probe scripts at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-easingeditor/frames-r3/.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient at 1440x900 dsf2 (light, then dark). Screenshot. Crop the head's name span rect (see frames-r3/probe-contrast-targets.json) and any 40x27 patch of plate 20px to its right. Compute WCAG relative luminance: ink = 0.5th percentile (light) / 99.5th (dark), ground = luminance mode. Yields 3.86-3.90 light, 3.73-3.75 dark. Reproduced twice with different geometry.

**Proposed cure.** Do not add a third well. The defect is that one row carries three text runs across two material tiers with one ink. Put the row's identity on one tier and let the tier own certification: either the whole row head sits on the same opaque rung the rail already uses (one surface per row — which also dissolves D3-04 and D3-06), or the identity run takes an ink minted against the live pane through useSafeAccentFn('resting'), the machinery this component's own useSpecimenRows.ts:40 already uses for the decorative glyph but not for the text.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-02 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Focusing a COLLAPSED interval row changes zero pixels — measured live in the shipped app at N=4, not in a fixture. The row's overflow-hidden (:114) clips a box-shadow-only focus ring (:228-231, outline:none) whose head is flush with the clip rect on all four sides. Even the OPEN row keeps only one ring edge of four: a 4px band, 244 px². With N stops there are N-1 rows and at most one is open, so N-2 rows are permanently in the zero-indicator state.

**Mechanism.** a box-shadow-only focus indicator (outline explicitly suppressed) on an element whose border box coincides with an ancestor's overflow clip rect on every side — the ring is minted and then 100% clipped

**Evidence.**

```
Live at 1512x900 @dsf2, N=4: collapsedFocus = {isFocused:true, matchesFocusVisible:true, outline:'none 3px rgb(28,25,23)', boxShadow:'color(srgb 0.665 0 0.2615 / 0.3) 0 0 0 2px, ... 0 0 8px 0', rowOverflow:'hidden', insets:{t:1,b:1,l:1,r:1}, rowH:41.2, headH:39.2}. PIL/numpy diff of frames-r3/D3-02-focus-collapsed-BEFORE.png vs D3-02-focus-collapsed-AFTER-zero-delta.png: 'px with maxdelta>2: 0 / >4: 0 / >8: 0; bbox(>8): None'. Same diff on the open row: 'px with maxdelta>8: 244; bbox(>8): x 25->944, y 104->107' — a 4px band along the bottom edge only. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:84; WCAG 2.4.7/2.4.11. Component comment :220-221 asserts it uses the house ring 'never a bespoke outline'.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. Click .gradient-rail at 25%, 50%, 75% (5 stops, 4 rows, row 0 open). Blur, screenshot a clip around the head of row index 2 (collapsed). Focus that head via .focus(), wait 400ms, screenshot the same clip. Diff the two PNGs: zero pixels differ above a 2/255 threshold. Repeat on row 0 (open): 244 px differ, in a 4px band on the bottom edge only. Script: frames-r3/probe-n2.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** The clip has no job — nothing in the row overflows (.head-glyph's declared overshoot stays inside the 39px head band) and border-radius alone rounds the panel corners. Delete overflow-hidden; better, delete the per-row card box entirely (see D3-05/D3-06), at which point no clip rect exists. If a clip must survive, express focus as outline, which no ancestor overflow clips and which forced-colors preserves and recolors. Seating glass-ui's Collapsible (r1 D-05) gets both for free.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-02 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The confirmation animation for the component's only two commit actions fires exactly once per session and never resets. `@animationend="swatchPulse = false"` is bound to `<WatercolorDot>`, but glass-ui 7.0.0 declares `inheritAttrs: false` and forwards only `class` and `style` from `useAttrs`, so the listener is never attached to any element. `swatchPulse` latches true forever: every Add-to-palette and Apply after the first is completely silent, and the `.swatch-pulse` rule permanently overrides the `w-7 h-7` utility.

**Mechanism.** event listener silently dropped by a producer component's `inheritAttrs:false`; the success state is encoded as a transient CSS class whose removal depends on that dropped event

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:18-23 (`@animationend`), :285-289 (`.swatch-pulse{width:1.75rem;height:1.75rem;animation:swatch-pop 0.65s … forwards}`). node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js:82 `inheritAttrs: !1` with `setup(e){ let t=e, n=h(), c=i(()=>n.class), f=i(()=>n.style) …` — only class and style consumed. Measured transcript: `A| ADD#1 => "swatchClass":"shrink-0 transition-transform swatch-pulse watercolor-swatch"` / `A| 1.65s after ADD#1 => …swatch-pulse…` / `A| ADD#2 => …swatch-pulse…` (animation is 0.65s, so 1.65s later it is long over and the class is still on).
```

**Reproduction.** Open the eyedropper (steps as D3-01), hover twice and click to pin, then click the 'Add to palette' button. Wait 1.5s and read `document.querySelector('[class*="z-popover"] [data-testid="watercolor-swatch"]').className` — still contains `swatch-pulse`. Click Add again: no animation, no feedback of any kind. Driver section A of probe-CHD-p2.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Stop encoding a commit result as a one-shot animation whose reset depends on an event the design system does not forward. Derive the swatch's state from the data — a durable 'in palette' mark computed from the palette store — so the confirmation is a rendered fact that survives, replays and needs no teardown. If a pulse is still wanted it belongs on a plain element the consumer owns, not on a producer face with `inheritAttrs:false`.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-01 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** BLOCKER (NEW) — The dominance readout points at nothing. The design deleted its dominant marker on the stated grounds that the card's first swatch IS the dominant specimen; it is not. `extractedPalette` (useExtractSession.ts:85-89) preserves quantizer return order while `dominant` (useExtractSession.ts:121-142) is an independent max-population scan with a deliberate chroma tiebreak (:120). When populations tie, the tiebreak walks the dominant off index 0 and the card is never told. No ring, no ordinal, no reordering — the label names one of five identical circles with no way to find it. Pass 1 accepted the comment as fact (pass1 D-16 line 468: 'the dominance readout names swatch #1 in text'); that clause should be struck.

**Mechanism.** Invariant asserted in a comment, bound by no structure — two independent orderings (quantizer return order for the card, max-population+chroma-tiebreak for the label) are documented as identical and never reconciled.

**Evidence.**

```
probe/probe5-log.txt, 1440x900 light, 200x200 PNG of four equal 50px bands #c81e5a/#1e5ac8/#5ac81e/#e8e0d0. `=== dominant serialized === oklch(73.892055422424% 0.217857767251 137.844885067367deg)` (L=73.89 -> the GREEN). `"swatchSeats": [{"bg":"oklch(0.544872 0.202432 7.683829)","x":238}` (crimson, index 0), `{"bg":"oklch(0.738921 0.217858 137.844879)","x":302}` (green, index 1 = the dominant), blue, cream]. Source: demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:113-117 and :137-141; demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:85-89 vs :120-142. Screenshot: probe/P2-fold-1440x900.png, and probe/P7-crop-rails.png where at k=5 swatch 0 is blue and the dominant is still green.
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/extract. Upload a PNG of four equal-height solid bands (equal populations force the chroma tiebreak). Compare `document.querySelector('code.fira-code').title` with the first swatch's computed backgroundColor. They differ deterministically on the first attempt. Script: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-workbench/probe/wbex-probe5.mjs

**Proposed cure.** Sort `extractedPalette` by population descending in useExtractSession.ts:85-89. Index 0 then IS the dominant by construction, the comment becomes true, and the card's population-proportional strip gains a second meaning for free — left-to-right becomes a ranking, which is what a viewer already assumes a proportional strip means. One sort closes three defects (this, the unbound label, and the strip's currently-arbitrary order). The alternative — restore a marker on the dominant seat — is acceptable; asserting the binding in prose and rendering nothing is the only option worse than either.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-02 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** BLOCKER (severity upgrade of pass1 D-1) — The preview crop is not a fidelity nuisance: it makes the preview and the palette disagree about what is in the picture. `object-contain` is declared (ImageDropZone.vue:41) inside an `overflow-hidden` container clamped to `max-h-[min(320px,40dvh)]` (ExtractWorkbench.vue:20), but the img's `h-full` resolves against the content box, computing to 458px inside a 320px box — 69px destroyed top and bottom. **Mechanism.** `h-full` on a child of a max-height-clamped flex column: percentage height resolves against the indefinite content box, the img exceeds the clamp, and `overflow-hidden` center-crops it — defeating the declared `object-contain`. Same family as D3-01: a fidelity law stated in prose (ImageDropZone.vue:3-5, 'the specimen never lies') with no binding structure.

```
probe/probe6-log.txt: `"imgRect":{"y":131.7,"h":458,"bottom":589.7}`, `"containerRect":{"y":200.7,"h":320,"bottom":520.7}`, `"containerOverflow":"hidden"`, `"imgObjectFit":"contain"`, `"imgHeightDecl":"458px"`, `"croppedTopPx":69`, `"croppedBottomPx":69`, `"croppedFraction":0.301`. Visual proof: probe/P7-crop-rails.png — the source carries an 8px solid black rail at its top edge and another at its bottom; NEITHER appears anywhere in the preview, yet the card renders a black strip cell and a black swatch at k=5. Source: demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:8,41 and demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:20,175.

Script: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-workbench/probe/wbex-probe6.mjs

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · F-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** One keystroke in the panel headed `CSS` silently destroys every authored easing curve

**Mechanism.** Two serializers for one model. `serializeGradient` (useGradientCSS.ts:147-162) emits only type/direction/raw stops; every keystroke in that panel triggers a full re-parse that re-seeds all intervals to the linear preset. The destructive act happens in the one surface that cannot display what it destroys.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientVisualizer.vue:102-108 (`onParseCSS` → `applyCSS`), :259 (panel binds `simpleCSS`), GradientCodeEditor.vue:55-62 (500 ms debounce on every input). Measured: authored easing "cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)" → after typing ONE trailing space → "cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"; tile @3.13% rgb(107,199,112) → rgb(106,200,116); easingSurvived: false.
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → click the `ease-in-out` easing specimen → click into the CSS panel → press End → type a single space → wait 1.4 s → read the interval literal and the tile background. Script: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/ (pass-3 dataloss run, transcript pasted in report §6 F-1).

**Proposed cure.** The code well is a representation of the model, not a second model. Serialize every field the model holds — `linear-gradient(<angle> in <space> <hue> hue, …)` — and parse the same production, so the panel round-trips itself and Copy writes the bytes under the caret. If a compact authored form survives it becomes a named, visible representation toggle, and replacing the model becomes an explicit `Replace` command that states it discards per-interval easing.

**Proposed cure.** Architectural transposition, not a patch: replace the Card column with glass-ui `InstrumentChassis` variant="golden", boundaries={[]}, reserve="none" per OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5's binding row. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The in-place editable palette name is silently discarded on save: GenerateControls emits `save: [colors, name]` but GeneratePane's handler accepts only `colors` and hard-codes the name "Generated Palette". Every palette this pane writes is named identically.

**Mechanism.** F2 contract dropped at the seam — TypeScript permits a handler with fewer parameters, so the two-arg emit contract is breached silently at compile time. An affordance that consumes user attention and returns nothing.

**Evidence.**

```
GenerateControls.vue:48-50 `const emit = defineEmits<{ save: [colors: string[], name: string] }>();`, :103 `emit("save", [...palette.value], paletteName.value);`, :144-149 the bound `<input v-model="paletteName">`. GeneratePane.vue:14 `function onSave(colors: string[])` — second arg never accepted — and :19 `pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", paletteColors);`. The source comment at GenerateControls.vue:44-47 states the wire as the pane owner's "one-liner" — never written. Live proof: input value at save time `ZZZ-PROBE-NAME`; localStorage `color-palettes` -> {"name":"Generated Palette","slug":"generated-palette-263727f3",...}. Aggravated by usePaletteStore.ts:66-81 which dedups on name+colors.
```

**Reproduction.** node probe: webkit 1440x900, goto #/generate, fill [data-generate-plate] input[aria-label='Palette name'] with "ZZZ-PROBE-NAME", click [data-generate-plate] button[aria-label='Save palette'], read localStorage['color-palettes']. Persisted name is "Generated Palette".

**Proposed cure.** Immediate: `function onSave(colors: string[], name: string)` -> `pm.createPalette(name, paletteColors)`. Gestalt: under D-1's transposition the naming job should not live on the specimen plate at all — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5 rules that rename/lifecycle actions live in the selected inspector, so Generate's commit region should hand off to the Library inspector rather than fork a second naming path.

Net effect: 5-12 operable ornaments with no name, no role and no focus, plus a color tool whose colors appear nowhere in its accessible text (REPORT.md:124 route text 310 chars contains the seed hex and no color value).

**Evidence.**

Tab order inside the plate: ["Palette name","BUTTON","Save palette","Copy all colors"] — zero swatches. PaletteColorStrip.vue:2-4 is also aria-hidden role=presentation, so BOTH renderings are hidden. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.2 ("V abrogates a selection outline and interactive host on WatercolorDot ... ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The image preview does not contain the image. `h-full` (height:100%) against a parent with indefinite height (height:auto + max-height) resolves to `auto`, so the <img> takes its intrinsic height and `object-fit:contain` becomes a dead declaration; `overflow-hidden` then silently center-crops. At large overflow ratios the preview paints nothing at all — a blank plate.

**Mechanism.** indefinite-box geometry — the well declares no block-size, so the content dictates the box and the max-height clip arbitrates

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:41 (`w-full h-full object-contain`) inside :8-9 (`flex flex-col items-center justify-center overflow-hidden`), caller max-h at demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:20. Measured (evidence/seatD-probe4.mjs): desktop 1440x900 light + 1200x900 (4:3) -> zone 462x320, img 458x343.5, visibleFraction 0.932, 599/625 image-colour pixels; desktop light + 400x1200 -> img 458x1374, visibleFraction 0.233, **0/625 image-colour pixels**; mobile 390x844 dark + 400x1200 -> img 320x960, visibleFraction 0.333, **0/600 pixels**; mobile light same input -> 149/600 (24.8%). elementFromPoint at zone centre returns IMG, img.complete=true, naturalWidth=400, opacity 1, visibility visible. Crop threshold = zoneWidth/maxHeight: 1.44 at 1440x900, 1.01 at 390px, 2.57 at 200% zoom (seatD-probe3: maxHeight==minHeight==180px at 720x450). Screenshots: evidence/D1-blank-preview-desktop-light-tall.png, D1-blank-preview-mobile-dark-tall.png, D1-crop-desktop-light-4x3.png
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imagedropzone/evidence/seatD-probe4.mjs (dev server on :9000). Or manually: open http://localhost:9000/#/extract at 1440x900, upload any portrait image -> the drop zone renders blank while the result column still says 'undeveloped plate — feed it an image'.

**Proposed cure.** Transpose: the specimen well declares its own geometry and the image fits INTO it (today the image dictates and the well truncates). Give the zone a definite block-size (aspect-[3/2] well or a fixed rung), make the <img> `absolute inset-0 w-full h-full object-contain`, DELETE `h-full`. object-contain then does what its name promises, every aspect letterboxes, nothing overflows the clip so the blank cannot occur, and `max-h-[min(320px,40dvh)]` dies with it (also curing D-16).
