### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · P2-4 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** BLOCKER (confirmed) with CORRECTED MECHANISM. Two `<DockSeparator />` render 0px tall while consuming 26px of the control row and announcing `role="separator"` to AT. Pass 1 found the symptom and the canon violation correctly but attributed it to a missing `align-self: stretch`; the real cause is an undefined custom property, and pass 1's proposed producer cure (beta4) would therefore not work.

**Mechanism.** `DockSeparator` is a dock-scoped primitive whose height is EXPLICITLY declared from `--dock-separator-height`, a token the Dock chassis supplies. Rendered inside a workbench plate the property has no substitution value, `height` resolves to `unset` → `auto`, and an empty div is 0px. `align-self` never enters it — an explicit `height: auto` beats stretch. Triple defect: canon says count must be 0 (measured 2); the primitive is not portable and draws nothing; and `role="separator"` with no `aria-hidden` announces a boundary that has zero pixels, so sighted and non-sighted users receive different structures.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:57 and :81. Live probe on the separator element: computed height `0px`; `getPropertyValue('--dock-separator-height')` → EMPTY; margin `0px 6px`; role `separator`; sepCount 2. Producer rule (glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/controls/): `.dock-separator { width: 1px; height: var(--dock-separator-height); margin: 0 0.375rem; background: var(--surface-tint-15); }`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.2 + PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05 rule the divider count ZERO for every non-Admin composition; Extract is a P122 InstrumentChassis member per §3.1.
```

**Reproduction.** Load /#/extract; query `.dock-separator` inside the extract control row; read computed `height` (0px) and `getPropertyValue('--dock-separator-height')` (empty). Visually confirm in any of the four Safari captures: the gap between the camera icon and `kC` is empty whitespace.

**Proposed cure.** DELETE both — PR-05 already rules the disposition REMOVE, and spacing plus material already carries the boundary (PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.4). Quantified payoff: returns 26px to the row; at a 300px plate the kC track measures 68.46px, so deletion is a +38% track (68.46 → ~94.5). AMEND blocked-wave beta4: strike 'align-self: stretch'; the only producer options are a token fallback `var(--dock-separator-height, <intrinsic>)` or documenting the primitive Dock-band-only — the latter preferred, which makes beta4 fully moot once the consumer deletion lands and reduces the Glass 8 obligation to beta1/beta2/beta3 alone.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 (r1, re-reproduced) · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** A mid-typing keystroke destroys the entire Gradient workbench and the user's authored text. The component designs a two-state failure model (verdict null | string) over a PARTIAL oracle, and the throw is raised inside a detached setTimeout so it bypasses the verdict path entirely and reaches the pane error boundary.

**Mechanism.** partial oracle behind a total contract; exception raised in a detached timer bypasses the designed failure state

**Evidence.**

```
Unguarded seam: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse.ts:92-94 `function isColorToken(token: string): boolean { return parseCssColor(token).ok; }`. Path GradientCodeEditor.vue:55-62 (debounce 500ms, demo/shared/utils.ts:29-34) → GradientVisualizer.vue:102-108 → useGradientModel.ts:158-160 → gradientParse.ts:191 → :92. Live at 1440x900: {"hasEd":false,"bodyText":"…This panel hit an unexpected error.\n\nCannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')\n\nTry again"}. Live at 390x844: {"vw":390,"rectBefore":{"w":324,"h":94},"hasEdAfter":false,"bodyAfter":"→\nGradient\nPalettes\n\nThis panel hit an unexpected error.\n\nCannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')\n\nTry again"}. Contract falsified: GradientCodeEditor.vue:38-40.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → focus the Gradient CSS editor → type `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)` → wait 500ms. Whole panel unmounts; text is unrecoverable. Reproduced at 1440x900 and 390x844. Also reached mid-sequence with `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch()  , blue)` (element detached; getComputedStyle(ed).borderColor returned "").

**Proposed cure.** Not a try/catch at the call site (that manufactures a mystery verdict). One explicit machine on the editor — empty | pending | applied | rejected(reason) | oracle-failed(diagnostic) — with gradientParse as the ONLY place the library oracle is touched, behind a total-by-construction adapter (the ruled parser-band candidate already is). The oracle-failed arm is a designed state with its own copy and never destroys the buffer.

**Defect.** The preview stage crops instead of containing; `object-contain` is inert, so portrait images lose ~85% of themselves and the extracted palette displays colors absent from the visible frame.

**Mechanism.** Cross-component contract carried by a stringly-typed fallthrough DOM attribute on a producer component, consumed by querySelector on an anonymous grandparent subtree — no type, prop, emit, or test on the path; plus a masking fallback (owner edict 2) that fabricates coordinates instead of failing loudly.

Measured: fallback={x:255,y:478.1,r:28} (mixStage.ts:124), real well layoutCenter={x:68,y:528,r:28}, distance=194 px; root.clientWidth=510, root.scrollHeight=683. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** A decorative Canvas2D renderer owns the phase machine's ONLY forward edge. When `getContext("2d")` returns null the mix strands forever: the result plate stays ghosted at opacity 0.55 showing only the word "Result", with no error, timeout, or recovery.

**Mechanism.** Essential state transition owned by an inessential subsystem; four abort paths guarded by firing onSettled, the fifth (null 2D context) left unguarded.

**Evidence.**

```
useMixingState.ts:5-15 declares the ONE-CLOCK LAW; MixAnimationCanvas.vue:15 repeats it. useMixingAnimation.ts:145 writes `if (ctx) ctx.setTransform(...)` then proceeds to collectStage + loop.start() regardless; frame 1 hits lines 92-95 `if (!canvas || !ctx || !stage) { loop.stop(); return; }` — stop WITHOUT onSettled. Reproduced live: patching HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext to return null for the mix canvas then calling startMix gives after 1800 ms { ghostStuck: true, plateOpacity: "0.55", hasResultText: false, plateText: "Result" }.
```

**Reproduction.** In the page: `const o=HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext; HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext=function(...a){return this===mixCanvas?null:o.apply(this,a)}`; then startMix; wait 1.8 s; `.mix-plate--ghost` still present at opacity 0.55 with no result content.

**Proposed cure.** Invert ownership: useMixingState advances mixing→done itself (the math is synchronous, nothing to wait on); the narration becomes epiphenomenal, observing `phase` and never gating it. Delete `onSettled` as a state edge — this also removes the four escape hatches and the PRM special case.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design of demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVi` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** On touch, tapping inside a SELECTED stop handle's own advertised hit region DELETES the stop. The remove chip (top-11, 44px below the rail) carries the same always-on hit inflation (--touch-target 2.75rem = 44px) as the handle, and the selected handle's scale(1.25) also scales its ::before expander to 55px, so the two invisible regions overlap with the destructive one on top (chip z-20 vs handle z-10). **Mechanism.** two invisible expanded hit targets stacked on one axis, with the destructive one painted on top

**Evidence.**

```
iPhone 14 / WebKit, evidence/p4.mjs T11: `T11 before {"n":3,"pos":["0","50","100"]}` → select mid stop → `T11 after tap at handle-centre + 20px {"n":2,"pos":["0","100"]}`. Hit map from p3.mjs T7: `handle-hit offsets -26 → 13 | chip-hit offsets 14 → 40` (offsets from handle centre); `expander 44px x 44px`. Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:288 (top-11, z-20), :262 (scale 1.25), :374-391 (::before expander), :385-391 (coarse 44px).

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p4.mjs — block T11 (iPhone 14 context against http://localhost:9000/#/gradient)

### `CHALLENGE-D — design of demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVi` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** No ordering invariant: a drag can carry a stop across its neighbour, leaving stops[] non-monotonic. sampleCoalescedStops then emits DESCENDING percentages into a CSS linear-gradient, which the browser clamps into a hard band, and the per-interval easing curves silently re-pair because intervals are keyed by array index rather than by the stop pair.

**Mechanism.** an ordinal identity that exists in the UI vocabulary ('stop 2', '1 → 2') but has no representation the model defends

**Evidence.**

```
evidence/p4.mjs T10: `T10 stops after cross {"n":4,"pos":["0","29","8","100"],"centers":[235,362.6,270.6,675]}`; painted rail percentages `[…,26.36, 29, 27.1, 25.2, 23.3, 21.4, 19.5, 17.6, 15.7, 13.8,…]` with `descendingPairs=[[12,29,27.1],…,[21,11.9,10]]`. Screenshot evidence/D02-cross-drag-hard-band.png shows the resulting seam. Source: useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (updateStop never sorts; addStop at :118 does), useGradientCSS.ts:195-200 (pos = s0.position + t*(s1-s0), negative range), GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88 (colorAtPosition assumes sorted). Interval labels stay index-keyed: p2.log T3 `["1 → 2","2 → 3"]`.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p4.mjs — block T10

**Proposed cure.** The model owns the ordinal: re-sort on every position commit and re-key intervals to the stop PAIR, or clamp a dragged stop into (prev, next). Only then is VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2's explicit reorder grammar (Space grabs, 'position of total' announcement, Escape cancels) implementable at all.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design of demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVi` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The instrument has two different position axes for one domain quantity. The ramp is painted across the full border-box; handles, the add-ghost and the pointer inverse ride an inset [HANDLE_HALF, W-HANDLE_HALF] track. They agree only at 50%. The file's own doc-comment asserts they 'share one axis by construction'.

**Mechanism.** two coordinate systems for one domain quantity, neither derived from the other

**Evidence.**

```
evidence/p1.mjs: `BAR x=224.00 w=462.00`, handle 'Gradient stop at 0%' `centerX=235.00` (ramp paints 0% at x=224), handle 'Gradient stop at 100%' `centerX=675.00` (ramp paints 100% at x=686) → 11px = 2.38% of the ramp. evidence/p5.mjs (iPhone 14): bar w=324, centres 44/346 → 11px = 3.40%. evidence/p3.mjs T6: ten clicks at rail fractions .12 .20 .28 .36 .44 .52 .60 .72 .80 .88 produce `pos ["0","10","19","27","35","44","52","60","73","81","90","100"]` — click at 12.0% mints 10%, click at 88.0% mints 90%. **Proposed cure.** One axis, expressed once. Either paint the ramp on the inset track (background-position: 11px 0; background-size: calc(100% - 22px) 100% — the pill caps then hold flat terminal colour, which is what a 0%/100% stop actually means), or put the handles on the full-width axis and inset the rail's silhouette instead. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries / ownersh` · R2-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The eased-ramp concept ('the colour of an eased ramp at parameter t') has no home in any package, so the demo implements it three times, and all three copies hand value.js's `mixColors` a progress value its own contract forbids. Reachable in one click from the landing state of /#/gradient, and the throw destroys the entire application, not just the pane.

**Evidence.**

```
src/easing.ts:62-64 ships `ease-in-back` [0.6,-0.28,0.735,0.045], `ease-out-back` [0.175,0.885,0.32,1.275], `ease-in-out-back` [0.68,-0.55,0.265,1.55]. Three demo copies of the law: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:175-216 (sampleCoalescedStops, discrete 32 sub-stops), demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88 (colorAtPosition, continuous), demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:52-59 (midpoint fn(0.5)). Throw sites useGradientCSS.ts:207 and useGradientInterpolation.ts:37, both inside Vue computeds (useGradientCSS.ts:325-327). Measured (vite-node): ease-in-back eased outputs 0.0000 -0.0427 -0.0754 -0.0944 -0.0935 -0.0636 0.0091 0.1437 0.3584 0.6531 1.0000, min -0.0944; serializeCoalescedGradient THROWS, serializeRailRamp THROWS, colorAtPosition THROWS. ease-out-back max 1.0858 -> both serializers THROW. ease-in-out-back min -0.0927 max 1.0921 -> all three THROW. LIVE webkit after one click on [data-specimen="ease-in-back"]: {"bodyText":141 (was 611),"tile":null,"cssBlockText":"This panel hit an unexpected error.\n\nGradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range\n\nTry again"}. Tiles enumerated live include "ease-in-back","ease-out-back","ease-in-out-back". easingCatalogue.ts:13 states the catalogue IS value.js bezierPresets; easingCatalogue.ts:174 FAMILY_ORDER includes "back".
```

**Reproduction.** 1) `node_modules/.bin/vite-node <scratchpad>/repro-back.mts` — headless, all three presets throw. 2) LIVE: `node <scratchpad>/live-back.mjs` — webkit, goto http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, wait 2500ms, click `[data-specimen="ease-in-back"]`; body text collapses 611->141 and the whole app becomes a 'Try again' pill (screenshot <scratchpad>/after-back-click.png). 3) By hand: open /#/gradient, scroll the Easing specimen strip right to the `back` family, click its `in` tile.

**Proposed cure.** Transposition, not a patch at the throw site. New `src/gradient/ramp.ts` published as `@mkbabb/value.js/gradient`: `sampleRamp(stops, spans, opts): Result<RampSample[], RampError>` and `rampColorAt(stops, spans, position, opts): Result<AnyColor, RampError>`, framework-free. `sampleRamp` owns and NAMES the one decision the demo has nowhere to put — what an eased t outside [0,1] means for a colour mix: `overshoot: "clamp"` (default, matching how browsers rasterise an overshooting native gradient) or `"extend"` (unclamped mix in the working space). All three demo copies then delete and become calls; the divergence in R2-7 becomes structurally impossible; and one fix serves every future consumer.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The stop-ordering invariant ("positions are non-decreasing") has three owners with three contradictory policies: gradientParse REJECTS violations, addStop SORTS, and updateStop — the mutator this component drives on every pointermove and arrow key — does NOTHING. The result is a live model whose own serializer emits CSS that its own parser rejects, and a rail ramp with decreasing sub-stop positions that CSS clamps into a flat band.

**Mechanism.** unique-semantic-ownership violated — a model invariant enforced by whichever mutator remembers it rather than by the type that carries it

**Evidence.**

```
Owners: gradientParse.ts:284-290 (reject) vs useGradientModel.ts:118 (sort) vs useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (no policy); driven by GradientStopEditor.vue:94,145,179 -> GradientVisualizer.vue:94-96. LIVE (localhost:9000/#/gradient, fresh mount, add stop at 50% then drag first handle to 80%): handles = ["Gradient stop at 80%","Gradient stop at 50%","Gradient stop at 100%"]; CSS readout = `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 80%, oklch(70% 0.165 205deg) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)`; computed --rail-ramp = `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(75% …) 80.00%, oklch(74.68% …) 78.13%, oklch(74.37% …) 76.25%, …` (DECREASING). Screenshot: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence-rail-after-reorder.png shows the rail as one flat green slab to ~78% with a hard band to blue. LIVE round trip: feeding that CSS back into [aria-label="Gradient CSS"] yields verdict "stop positions must be non-decreasing (hard-stop reordering isn't modeled)". HEADLESS: `npx vite-node` on the demo modules -> serialized `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 70%, oklch(0.7 0.16 200) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)` -> re-parse REJECT with the same reason. Untested by the gates: e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:161-172 drags only the MIDDLE handle to 75%, strictly between its neighbours.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient -> click the rail at ~50% (adds a stop) -> drag the leftmost handle to ~80% -> read the CSS box: positions descend (80%, 50%, 100%). Retype that same string into the CSS box -> the destructive verdict appears. Headless equivalent: vite-node script calling updateStop-shaped mutation then serializeGradient -> parseGradientCSS.

**Proposed cure.** Brand the list. A model/stops.ts owns the ordering algebra and is the ONLY producer of an `OrderedStops` (readonly branded array): insertStop / moveStop (re-sorts, stable — the CSS-native behaviour a user expects from dragging past a neighbour) / removeStop. serializeGradient, sampleCoalescedStops and parseGradientCSS all take OrderedStops, so the parser's reject-branch becomes unreachable-by-construction instead of a runtime tripwire aimed at the app itself.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The published `@mkbabb/value.js/css` surface is NOT total: parseCssColor throws a TypeError on eight empty-argument colour functions instead of returning {ok:false}. The demo's entire "library-oracle" architecture (gradientParse.ts header lines 16-17: "validated by the LIBRARY's own parsers — the validity oracles; the demo never hand-validates a color") is therefore structurally unsound, and the throw escapes the model-or-reject contract as an uncaught TypeError.

**Mechanism.** a published API whose type says ParseResult<CssColor> and whose runtime says "or I throw" — partiality hidden behind a non-null assertion; every consumer written against the type is structurally wrong

**Evidence.**

```
Root cause src/css/grammar.ts:181 `const components = splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g," "), "space");` — the non-null assertion over splitTopLevel("","/") which returns []. Consumer gradientParse.ts:92-94 `return parseCssColor(token).ok`. node on working-tree dist/subpaths/css.js: oklch()/rgb()/hsl()/lab()/lch()/oklab()/hwb()/color() all -> `THROW: TypeError Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`; rgb(1 2 3)/red/oklch(0.7 0.1 30) -> ok. node on the INSTALLED node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 -> same THROW (the bug is in the published package). In-browser dynamic import of the exact aliased module the demo runs -> {"oklch()":"THROW: …","rgb()":"THROW: …","oklch(0.7 0.1 30)":"ok"}. Through the demo parser (npx vite-node): `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)` -> UNCAUGHT TypeError; `linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(), blue)` -> UNCAUGHT; `linear-gradient(90deg, color(), blue)` -> UNCAUGHT; `linear-gradient(90deg, red, blue)` -> ok.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vite-node with `import { parseGradientCSS } from 'demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse'; parseGradientCSS('linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)')` -> uncaught TypeError. Or type that string into the gradient CSS box on a mounted pane.

**Proposed cure.** Totality is the library's contract, not the consumer's try/catch. Replace the non-null assertions in parseFunctionalColor with an explicit empty-body reject (failure(source,"css_syntax",["components"])), and add a property test over {rgb,rgba,hsl,hsla,hwb,lab,lch,oklab,oklch,color} × {""," ","/",",,"} so the surface can never regress to partiality. Do NOT wrap isColorToken in try/catch — that moves the library's contract into its consumer.

The producer may rename any prop and every consumer keeps compiling and keeps rendering something — worse than breaking, because it is invisible. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 (pass-1, CONFIRMED LIVE by pass 2) · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The palette name the user types is silently discarded on save: the child emits `save: [colors, name]` but the pane's handler declares arity 1 and passes the literal "Generated Palette" to the persistence port. Data loss on user input.

**Mechanism.** Ownership split with an untyped joint: the NAME is owned by the leaf component, the PERSISTENCE PORT (LIBRARY_PORT_KEY) is injected by the parent, and the two are joined by a Vue emit. TypeScript cannot catch it — a handler is always assignable to an emit with more parameters. Second symptom of the same split: `string[] → PaletteColor[]` is synthesised twice (GenerateControls.vue:55-57 and GeneratePane.vue:15-18) because neither file owns 'the generated palette as a domain object'.

**Evidence.**

```
GenerateControls.vue:48-50 `defineEmits<{ save: [colors: string[], name: string] }>()`, :52 `paletteName = ref("Generated Palette")`, :102-104 `emit("save", [...palette.value], paletteName.value)`. GeneratePane.vue:14 `function onSave(colors: string[])` — name parameter never bound — and :19 `pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", paletteColors)`. LIVE REPRODUCTION (pass 2, which pass 1 had to abandon under shared-browser contention): {"url":"http://localhost:9000/#/generate","inputAfterSet":"ZZ-PROBE-NAME","nameMatches":[["color-palettes",["Generated Palette","Sunset","Empty Plate","Overflowing"]]]} — the v-model round-trip is verified and the persisted store contains zero occurrences of ZZ-PROBE-NAME. Comment at :44-47 asserts 'this emit is already truthful' — it is not.
```

**Reproduction.** Playwright at /#/generate with the self-healing hash idiom: set input[aria-label="Palette name"] to ZZ-PROBE-NAME via the native value setter + input event (verified round-trip), click button[aria-label="Save palette"], read localStorage['color-palettes'] → names are ["Generated Palette","Sunset","Empty Plate","Overflowing"].

**Proposed cure.** ESCALATION RECOMMENDED — this is the highest-value action available before Glass 8. GeneratePane.vue is NOT in the hold's pinned receiver set (the four pinned files are ComponentSliders.vue, ConfigSliderPane.vue, ExtractControls.vue, GenerateControls.vue), so binding the second emit argument at GeneratePane.vue:14-19 cures the data loss WITHOUT touching any pinned file. The full cure is the session hoist: `useGenerateSession()` owning preset/harmony/count/seed/name/palette/regenerate/save, provided at the pane under a typed InjectionKey — one writer, one adapter, and the name-drop becomes unrepresentable.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The published library declares its own demo's design system as a runtime dependency, forming a declared package cycle and forcing 5.8 MB of unused install weight on every consumer.

**Mechanism.** wrong-direction dependency declared at the package manifest level: demo-only tooling placed in `dependencies` instead of `devDependencies`, creating value.js → glass-ui → value.js.

**Evidence.**

```
package.json:82-85 `"dependencies": {"@mkbabb/glass-ui":"^7.0.0","@mkbabb/keyframes.js":"^6.0.0"}` — the ONLY two entries. Measured: `grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui|@mkbabb/keyframes" src/ | wc -l` → 0; `grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui" dist/subpaths/*.js dist/value.js | wc -l` → 0; `grep -rn "@mkbabb/keyframes" demo/ | wc -l` → 0 (referenced by NOTHING in the repo). `du -sh node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui node_modules/@mkbabb/keyframes.js` → 5.2M + 608K, against dist/subpaths at 132K. glass-ui/package.json peerDependencies includes `"@mkbabb/value.js":"^4.0.0"`.
```

**Reproduction.** `npm i @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0` in an empty non-Vue project: the install pulls a Vue design system plus a keyframes engine and glass-ui's own peer set (vue, reka-ui, embla-carousel, tailwindcss, @mkbabb/pencil-boil). `import { CubicBezier } from "@mkbabb/value.js/easing"` uses none of them.

**Proposed cure.** Move both entries to `devDependencies`. `dependencies` becomes `{}` — the honest shape for a zero-runtime-dependency value library. Nothing breaks: `"files": ["dist", "!dist/gh-pages", …]` (package.json:49-53) never ships the demo.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The gradient domain model — including a headless CSS parser with zero Vue in it — is typed by a Vue component's v-model payload imported from the design system.

**Mechanism.** inverted semantic ownership: the concept 'an authored easing curve = mode + re-parseable CSS literal + resolved callable + raw params' is a value.js concept, but value.js publishes no such record, so its own demo borrows one from a package that depends on it.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:49 `export type GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue;` (imported from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/easing` at line 12). glass-ui's own declaration calls it "The picker's v-model payload" (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/composables/useEasingPicker.d.ts). It propagates into UI-free code: gradientParse.ts:41 `interface ParsedGradientModel { …; intervals: GradientInterval[] }` (that module has zero Vue imports); useGradientCSS.ts:53-62,120-133,232-254; and the subject's own public contract GradientEasingEditor.vue:48-50 `"update-interval": [index: number, value: EasingPickerValue]`.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE (latent). Failure scenario: glass-ui 8 renames `term`→`jump` or makes `points` optional for steps mode — a semver-legal design-system component change. That silently breaks value.js's headless gradient CSS parser, its serializers and its persisted model shape, none of which involve a picker.

**Proposed cure.** value.js `/easing` mints the record: `export interface AuthoredEasing { readonly mode: "bezier"|"steps"; readonly css: string; readonly fn: EasingFunction; readonly points: readonly [number,number,number,number]; readonly steps: number; readonly term: JumpPosition }`. Then `GradientInterval = AuthoredEasing` (no glass-ui import in the model at all) and glass-ui narrows to `export type EasingPickerValue = AuthoredEasing` — consuming the library's vocabulary, the direction its peerDeps already declare. The glass-ui type imports at useGradientModel.ts:12, easingCatalogue.ts:31-35 and GradientEasingEditor.vue:30 all collapse to `@mkbabb/value.js/easing`.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The stop-ordering invariant is homeless: three write paths into stops[] with three contradictory policies. addStop sorts (useGradientModel.ts:118); parseGradientCSS rejects violations (gradientParse.ts:284-290); updateStop — the path this component drives from drag (:94,:145) and keyboard (:179) — enforces nothing (useGradientModel.ts:127-131). The model's serializer therefore emits CSS its own parser calls unmodelable, and intervals[i], defined as the span between stops[i] and stops[i+1], ends up attached to an inverted span.

**Mechanism.** Unique semantic ownership violated — position semantics live in the leaf component (pixels/keys → number), array identity lives in the model, the ordering law lives in the parser. One concept, three homes; the invariant died in the seam. Root structural cause is L-3: hand-rolling a multi-thumb slider instead of consuming one.

**Evidence.**

```
Live at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, fresh mount, keyboard only — 10x shift+ArrowRight on stops[0] then 10x shift+ArrowLeft on stops[1] yields labels ["Gradient stop at 100%","Gradient stop at 0%"] and CSS readout `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 100%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 0%)` with errs: []. Feeding that exact string to the app's own parser in-page: `import('/@fs/…/gradientParse.ts').parseGradientCSS(...)` → "REJECT: stop positions must be non-decreasing (hard-stop reordering isn't modeled)"; the ordered control case returns OK. Computed --rail-ramp came out with DECREASING positions (100.00%, 96.88%, …, 3.13%, 0.00%), which CSS Images 3 §3.4.3 colour-stop fixup silently repairs. Coverage: `grep -rn "non-decreasing|monotonic" e2e test` finds the invariant only in the parser and its unit test; e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:144 drags but never asserts order.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → focus the 0% stop handle → shift+ArrowRight x10 → focus the other handle → shift+ArrowLeft x10 → read the CSS box. Positions descend. Retype that string into the CSS box and the destructive parse verdict appears.

**Proposed cure.** Do NOT add .sort() to updateStop — that makes a fourth policy holder. Transpose the instrument: bind stop positions to a multi-thumb glass-ui Slider (variant="stops"), where the invariant is already solved, shipped and installed one import line away — node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Slider/SliderRoot.js:124 calls getNextSortedValues on every commit, utils.js:8 sorts. Ordering becomes structurally unrepresentable rather than guarded.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** parseGradientCSS is documented total ("model-or-reject … never a partial", gradientParse.ts:5-6) and is not: it delegates validity to a non-total library oracle. gradientParse.ts:16-17 explicitly names parseCssColor/parseCssScalar "the validity oracles; the demo never hand-validates a color". parseCssColor throws instead of returning {ok:false} for 8 empty-argument colour functions, so isColorToken (gradientParse.ts:92-94) is a crash site and the throw escapes the whole model-or-reject contract. The /css subpath publishes a ParseResult-typed API — a type-level promise of totality — and breaks it.

**Mechanism.** A published boundary whose type says ParseResult<CssColor> and whose runtime says "or I throw". The consumer built its own totality guarantee on a guarantee never given, and no structural check exists that would catch the gap.

**Evidence.**

```
In-page, against the real module: `parseGradientCSS('linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), red)')` → THROW: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace'); same for rgb() and color-mix(). Library site confirmed by `grep -n "replace(/,/g" src/css/grammar.ts` → line 181: `const components = splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g, " "), "space");` — a `!` non-null assertion over splitTopLevel("", "/") which returns [].
```

**Reproduction.** Type `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), red)` into the gradient CSS editor at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. Chain: GradientCodeEditor.onInput → debouncedParse (GradientCodeEditor.vue:55) → emit("parse") → GradientVisualizer.onParseCSS (:102) → applyCSS → parseGradientCSS. The parseVerdict UI that e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:222 certifies ("garbage input fails LOUD") never runs — these 8 inputs fail silently and wrongly.

**Proposed cure.** Totality is the library's contract and belongs in the library: parseFunctionalColor must return failure(source) on an empty body, plus a property test over {fn} × {"", " ", "/", ",,"} so the surface cannot regress to partiality. Explicitly do NOT wrap isColorToken in a try/catch — that is a masking fallback (edict 2) and moves the library's contract into its consumer.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The published ParseResult contract is a type-lie: parseCssColor/parseCssValue declare totality (src/css/types.ts:25-27 has no throw channel) but throw TypeError on every closed-empty color function. src/css/grammar.ts:181 `splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g," "), "space")` — the `!` is false because splitTopLevel drops empty parts and returns [] for an empty body. Live blast radius: the whole two-pane <main> unmounts, with zero telemetry, and recovery destroys the user's authored gradient.

**Mechanism.** Non-null assertion (`!`) on an index into a possibly-empty split result, inside a function whose published return type promises totality — a partial implementation behind a total type. Vue's emit routes the setTimeout throw through callWithAsyncErrorHandling to the nearest errorCaptured, so the debounce isolates nothing and the app-root boundary catches a leaf fault.

**Evidence.**

```
src/css/grammar.ts:181 (the sole `slash[0]!` in the file — `grep -n "slash\[0\]\!" src/css/grammar.ts` → 1 hit). Against the shipped artifact: `node --input-type=module -e "import { parseCssColor } from './dist/subpaths/css.js'"` → "oklch()" "rgb()" "hsl()" "lab()" "lch()" "color()" "oklab()" "hsl(  )" ALL => THREW TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace'); "oklch(" => ok:false; "oklch(0.7 0.1 145)" => ok:true. Live Playwright on http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → {"bodyText":"→\nGradient\nPalettes\n\nThis panel hit an unexpected error.\n\nCannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')\n\nTry again","hasEditor":false,"hasStops":0}. After clicking Try again → {"recovered":true,"editorTextAfterRecovery":"linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)"} (the seed, not the user's text). Consumer site: gradientParse.ts:91-94. Falsified invariant: GradientCodeEditor.vue:38-40. Boundary: App.vue:50; silence: ErrorBoundary.vue:68 `return false`.
```

**Reproduction.** 1) `node --input-type=module -e "import { parseCssColor } from './dist/subpaths/css.js'; console.log(parseCssColor('oklch()'))"` → throws. 2) Navigate http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; focus [role="textbox"][aria-label="Gradient CSS"]; set textContent to 'linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)'; dispatch InputEvent('input',{bubbles:true}); wait >500ms → the pane grid is replaced by the error boundary; click 'Try again' → the seed gradient returns and the authored text is gone.

**Proposed cure.** Library-side, architectural not patch: (a) guard the head at grammar.ts:181 and return failure(source,"css_syntax",["color components"]); (b) STRUCTURAL so it cannot recur — give splitTopLevel a total signature `readonly [string, ...string[]] | readonly []` (or a splitTopLevelNonEmpty returning the head separately) so tsc rejects the unguarded index instead of trusting an author's `!`; then sweep the remaining `!`-on-index in src/css/grammar.ts, since MT-F001 is one instance of a family; (c) move the ErrorBoundary from App.vue:50 to per-pane inside usePaneRouter (demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:74-87) so a workbench fault cannot evict an unrelated pane; (d) table test over {rgb,rgba,hsl,hsla,hwb,lab,lch,oklab,oklch,color} x {"()","(  )","( / )"} asserting .ok===false — `grep -rn "oklch()\|rgb()" test/*.test.ts` returns nothing today. REFUSE the demo-side try/catch: it is a masking fallback over a broken contract (edict 2) and would report oklch() as 'unparseable color'.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-13 · CHALLENGE-L

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:21 (@click, own branch) · :22 (@keydown.enter.space.prevent, mirrors ONLY the own branch) · :19 (:tabindex) · demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:25 `@click="session.previewDataUrl.value && (eyedropperActive = true)"` — undeclared, not in defineEmits (:74-76). MEASURED (pass2-probe/probe3-intake-and-keyboard.json): afterPng {tabindex:"-1", aria:"Image preview area, tap to sample colors"} · focusProbe {activeIsZone:true} · afterEnter {eyedropperCanvas:false} · afterClick {eyedropperCanvas:true}.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure / module boundaries / owners` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The loupe canvas has two owners: `useLoupeCanvas` holds its ref by template-string (`useTemplateRef("loupeCanvasRef")`) while `ImageEyedropper.vue` owns the element's existence with `v-if`. `showLoupeAt` flips the flag and calls `drawLoupe` synchronously, so the ref is still null and the draw silently early-returns. On touch there is no follow-up pointermove and `hideLoupe` unmounts the element again, so the magnifier NEVER paints.

**Mechanism.** ownership split — element lifetime owned by the template, element reference owned by a composable, joined only by a string name and by Vue's flush ordering

**Evidence.**

```
useLoupeCanvas.ts:21 (useTemplateRef by string), :30 (silent early return), :56-59 (flip + synchronous draw); ImageEyedropper.vue:78,85 (v-if owns the element). jsdom+Vue reproduction output: 'sample #1 … drawLoupe() sees loupeCanvasRef = null -> EARLY RETURN, no paint' / 'after nextTick: <canvas>' / 'sample #2 … -> paints'. Visual: probe/shot-mobile-dark-tapped.png shows the loupe ring fully transparent — the fixture's purple/grey edge continues through the circle at 1:1 scale, not the 10x blow-up a painted loupe would show.
```

**Reproduction.** node --input-type=module -e '<appendix A2 in the report>' — prints the null-ref early return on sample #1. Independently visible in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/probe/shot-mobile-dark-tapped.png.

**Proposed cure.** Do not split existence from reference. The DPR-correct, paint-on-demand 2D surface is a design-system primitive: glass-ui `./canvas` publishes `useCanvas2D`/`useCanvasLifecycle` (loop-shaped) and needs a paint-on-demand sibling; the loupe becomes a `Loupe.vue` that owns its canvas outright through it. Relay the glass-ui half to the BH inbox per the standing relay invariant.

### `D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-sys` · D-1 · D

**Defect.** Typing an empty-argument colour function (`oklch()`, `rgb()`, `hsl(  )`) — exactly what a human produces mid-keystroke — DESTROYS the entire Gradient workbench, falsifying the component's own written contract at GradientCodeEditor.vue:38-40 ("A failed parse keeps the user's text verbatim alongside the verdict — WIP is never destroyed").

The escape route is a bare `emit("parse", text)` inside a 500ms setTimeout (GradientCodeEditor.vue:63-65), so the throw surfaces asynchronously, detached from any interaction; the parent's onParseCSS (GradientVisualizer.vue:107-111) has no try, and it propagates to the route ErrorBoundary which unmounts the whole workbench.

Adopt the adjudicated parser band (registry/adjudicated/parser-band.md, cand-O) so parseCssColor returns a failure value instead of throwing — the component's contract then holds by construction. ### `D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-sys` · D-2 · D

**Defect.** The specimen well is not painted: `glass-wash` on the code plate computes to zero fill, zero backdrop-filter, and only a bevel + drop shadow — so the hljs crayon palette, which its own theme header certifies only against the opaque `--well-bg` ground, renders on the live chromatic atmosphere and every token fails 4.5:1 in all four matrices.

**Mechanism.** A material-tier contract enforced by convention instead of structure. The hljs theme deliberately ships `background: transparent` and delegates the ground to the consumer; the consumer applies a class (`glass-wash`) that paints a bevel and a drop shadow but no fill and no blur. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:14-19 defines the Specimen-well tier for "code artifact" as an OPAQUE/quiet neutral stage and states "Glass earns its blur by revealing live content; otherwise it is a neutral well" — this surface has backdrop-filter:none, so it earns nothing. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:82: "a token name is not evidence". Because the delivered ground is the seed-driven atmosphere, the ratio is a function of the user's colour and can never be certified once.

**Evidence.**

```
Computed live at GradientCodeEditor.vue:93 (evidence/cd-probe5.mjs): backgroundColor `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`, backgroundImage `none`, backdropFilter `none`, boxShadow includes an outer `… 0px 2px 8px …`. Spec quote demo/styles/hljs.css:22-33: "the rung-2 well (`--well-bg` = card 92% + fg 8%) … Post-fix on the well: comment 5.33/5.04, string 4.99, number 4.91, keyword 4.91, entity/title 5.41 (light) — all ≥4.5"; `--code-comment: hsl(30 22% 34%); /* warm muted gray (well-guarded) */`; `.dark { /* … lifted for the dark chocolate WELL field. */ }`; hljs.css:56-58 `.hljs { background: transparent; }`. Ground ranges: light rgb(240,189,202)…rgb(240,209,206) L .592–.686; dark rgb(119,78,85)…rgb(119,92,88) L .100–.123. Prior claim contradicted: docs/tranches/T/audit/SYNTHESIS.md:121 says "post-fix: the two sites (GradientStopEditor.vue:171, GradientCodeEditor.vue:93) paint their rung". Sibling cure present at GradientEasingEditor.vue:170-176 (`bg-well`, comment records the same "~2.7:1"). Rendered plate ΔL vs the surrounding pane: −0.050 light, −0.012 dark (the dark well is optically absent).
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → scroll to the CSS field → getComputedStyle(editor).backgroundColor === 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)'. Contrast: evidence/cd-probe4-codeeditor.mjs then the Pillow sampler over crop-m-*-D-empty.png (pasted numbers above).

**Proposed cure.** Make the well a TIER, not a class two components remember to apply: one well material owns every code/value artifact on the route (the `bg-well` rung the sibling already proves), applied at the tier level so `.hljs` always lands on the ground it was guarded for. Do NOT re-tune the crayons — the ground error has opposite sign per scheme. ### `design — visual truth · state coverage · motion · design-sys` · D-1 · design

**Defect.** Colors mode — the route's default mode — has no reachable add affordance. Both operand-entry paths are `WatercolorDot`s carrying `tag="button"`, an API glass-ui 7.0.0 removed. The producer is `inheritAttrs:false`, reads only `class`/`style` from `useAttrs()`, renders a hard-coded `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">`, and has no slot — so `@click`, `aria-label`, `:disabled`, `:title` and the `<Plus>` glyph are all silently discarded.

**Mechanism.** producer-contract drift — a major-version adoption (glass-ui 7.0.0, W44) migrated the package but not the call sites; `inheritAttrs:false` swallows the dropped props with no Vue warning. `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:91` abrogated the `tag="button"` interactive host by name and listed Mix among the sites to migrate.

**Evidence.**

```
`node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js` render fn (`inheritAttrs: !1`; `let n=h(), c=i(()=>n.class), f=i(()=>n.style)`; `o("span",{"aria-hidden":"true", … style:u([f.value,{…,pointerEvents:"none",…}])})`). Call sites `demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:164–176` and `:211–221`. Live WebKit probe: `ghost = {tagName:"SPAN", attrs:[data-v-292b9032, data-v-a3e86846, aria-hidden="true", class=…, data-testid, data-variant, style], pointerEvents:"none", tabIndex:-1, isFocusable:false, svgClasses:["watercolor-filter-host"]}` — complete attribute list, no aria-label/disabled/title/onclick, and the `<Plus>` svg is absent. `ADD-SLOT FORCE-CLICK: chips before = 0 after = 0`. `FOCUSABLES IN SOURCE SELECTOR SUBTREE: ["BUTTON|name=Colors","BUTTON|name=Palettes"]`.
```

**Reproduction.** `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-sourceselector/evidence/challenge-D-r3/WBMSS-probe.mjs` against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000; or open /#/mix and attempt to add a colour — nothing is clickable or focusable.

**Proposed cure.** Do not restore `tag`. Transpose onto the seat/face split the canon already specifies: one `SwatchSeat` composition IN GLASS-UI — a named `<button>` seat owning accessible name, `disabled`, focus and press, containing the `WatercolorDot` as an `aria-hidden` face plus the glyph as a sibling. Same seat serves Gradient stops and Generate specimens (VC:91). Discharges D-21, D-25, D-26, D-27, D-28 and the naming half of D-15 as a consequence.

### `design — visual truth · state coverage · motion · design-sys` · DB-1 · design

**Defect.** BLOCKER — the mix result settles 317 px below the scroll fold and the pane never scrolls to it. In Palettes mode the operand rack renders five PaletteCards, the column overflows, and MixPane.vue:111-119 appends the result plate to the end of it with no scroll management. The user presses the page's one verb and the viewport does not change. This voids the component's own stated thesis at MixPane.vue:107-110 — 'No spinner row: the animation IS the progress' — because the convergence choreography converges on an off-screen target, and pass A already measured `liveRegions: []`, so there is no announcement either.

**Mechanism.** No region model. `Card` + one flex column has no notion of an inspector or an action region, so 'the place the result appears' is wherever the column happens to end. Same causal family as pass A's D-1 (the housing was declined), but producing a user-stranding outcome rather than a proportion outcome.

**Evidence.**

```
Live, WebKit 1440x900, `hash: "#/mix"` asserted in the same evaluation, reproduced twice 2.2 s after clicking Mix: cardRect {x:729,y:103,w:512,h:774} → visible bottom 877; plateRect (.mix-plate) {x:754,y:1023,w:462,h:171} → plate bottom 1194; cardScrollTop 0; cardScrollH/clientH 1106/772; plateBottomBeyondFold = 317 px. At pass A's card height (684.8, bottom 832.8) the same plate sits 361 px below the fold, so it is not an artefact of the taller measurement. Frame: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-pane/frames/DB-01-palettes-result-below-fold.png — the post-settle viewport containing no result. Source: demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue:62,107-119; demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue:9-19.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/mix → Palettes tab → select 'Sunset Ridge' and 'Deep Ocean' → click Mix → wait 2 s. `document.querySelector('.mix-plate').getBoundingClientRect().y` === 1023; the card's visible bottom is 877; `card.scrollTop` === 0.

**Proposed cure.** Do NOT add scrollIntoView — it fights prefers-reduced-motion and focus order and still leaves the region unowned. Under pass A's D-1 transposition the result IS the chassis `#inspector`: a geometrically reserved, always-visible region, with the operand rack scrolling independently inside `#stage`. DB-1 dissolves there. The consequence is that step 1 of the cure order must now be justified as a correctness fix, not only a proportion fix.

### `design — visual truth · state coverage · motion · design-sys` · DB-0 · design

**Defect.** BLOCKER (confirms and EXTENDS pass A D-5 / wb-mix-sourceselector D-1) — Colors mode has zero reachable add-operand affordance, and BOTH of its add paths are dead, not one. Pass A recorded the add-slot ghost; the second path — the 36 'From palettes' swatches at MixSourceSelector.vue:211-221 — is dead by the identical mechanism. The design consumes `WatercolorDot tag="button"`, an interactive host glass-ui 7 deliberately abrogated (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:91, P051: 'V abrogates a selection outline and interactive host on WatercolorDot… Selection, activation, drag and keyboard focus belong to a named enclosing geometric button/seat'). The component was never migrated to the enclosing-seat pattern.

**Mechanism.** Design-system boundary breach: the composition consumed a producer capability the design system had explicitly withdrawn. The failure is invisible-by-omission rather than broken-by-error, so it renders, looks plausible, and screenshots as an 'empty state' — which is exactly how all four Safari captures of /#/mix were recorded.

**Evidence.**

```
Live with the 'From palettes' disclosure expanded: 36 WatercolorDots rendered, every one a `<span aria-hidden="true">` with inline `pointer-events: none` and a NULL aria-label (the consumer's `:aria-label` is dropped by the producer). The card's complete focusable inventory is UNCHANGED at 6: 2 segmented-tab, 1 disclosure-trigger, 2 selects, 1 `disabled` Mix. `document.elementFromPoint` at the add-ghost centre returns a DIV, not the ghost (`hitIsGhost: false`). Playwright refuses the click: 'element is visible, enabled and stable … <div class="swatch-row flex items-center gap-2.5 flex-wrap"> intercepts pointer events' ×13 → TimeoutError 5000ms. `canMix` (useMixingState.ts:51) needs ≥2 colours; `selectedColors` starts [] (:42) with no reachable mutator. glass-ui version confirmed 7.0.0.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/mix → Colors tab → click the dashed ghost in 'Selected' by mouse or reach it by Tab: unreachable. Expand 'From palettes' and click any of the 36 swatches: nothing happens. Mix stays disabled forever.

**Proposed cure.** Do not re-add tag="button". Transpose to the pattern the canon already names: an operand SEAT — a native `<button type="button">` enclosing an inert WatercolorDot face — owning activation, focus, the selection ring, the accessible name and the DB-2/D-10 reorder grab. One seat serves the add-slot, the selected chips and the from-palettes swatches; the dot becomes pure specimen, which is what §4.2 says it is. Gradient's stops need the identical cut (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:206), so the seat belongs in glass-ui, not demo/ui/.

### `DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D, round 3) — demo/workbenches/mix/MixConf` · R3-1 · DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D, round 3)

**Defect.** `h-9` on all three SelectTriggers destroys the producer's vertical padding rather than selecting a smaller register; the crush is 41% at desktop and 84% under coarse pointer, and it drops the tap target below the producer's own 44px floor.

**Mechanism.** consumer asserts producer-owned geometry — a hard-coded box dimension layered over a producer register that already resolves height, padding and touch floor from `--ui-scale`

**Evidence.**

```
MixConfigBar.vue:100,123,147 append `class="h-9"`. Live rendered class attribute shows the collision in one string: `... rounded-pill px-3 py-2 text-dropdown ... h-9` (producer padding + consumer height). WebKit probe at 390x844 isMobile+hasTouch (resolved `--ui-scale: 1.5`, `--control-floor: 2.75rem`): {"h":36,"height":"36px","minBlockSize":"auto","contentBoxH":34,"fontSize":"21px","lineHeight":"31.5px","padBlock":"8px/8px"}. Border-box arithmetic 36-2-16=18px content box holding a 31.5px line box -> 13.5px overflow -> producer padding surviving = 1.25px of 8px. Desktop 1440: lineHeight 24.6px -> 6.6px overflow -> 4.7px of 8px. PNG edge scan of the shipped capture `visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/mix.png` (1170x1992, DPR 3) at device x=300: capsule top specular rgb(251,230,233) at y=1355, pane resumes rgb(239,185,201) at y=1460 -> (1459-1355)/3 = 34.7 CSS px measured tap height vs `--touch-target: 2.75rem` = 44px. Same probe: Mix button h=60 (min-block-size honoured), so the bar's two control species differ by 24px where the producer intended 6px (54 vs 60). Chevron stays `h-4 w-4` = 16px at both 1440 and 390-coarse while sibling type goes 16.4px -> 21px (glyph/label 0.98 -> 0.76).

**Reproduction.** webkit.launch() -> newContext({viewport:{width:390,height:844}, isMobile:true, hasTouch:true, deviceScaleFactor:3}) -> goto http://[::1]:9000/#/mix -> getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[data-slot=select-trigger]')) returns {height:'36px', lineHeight:'31.5px', paddingBlockStart:'8px'} with clientHeight 34. Cross-check: decode docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/mix.png and scan device column x=300 rows 1300-1520.

**Proposed cure.** Delete `h-9` from all three triggers and `h-10 gap-2` from the Button — seven class strings total. If a shorter register is genuinely wanted, `SelectTrigger` already exposes `size?: "sm" | "default"` (glass-ui/dist/components/select/SelectTrigger.vue.d.ts), which carries its own padding. ### `DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D, round 3) — demo/workbenches/mix/MixConf` · R3-2 · DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D, round 3)

**Defect.** The dark scheme inverts protagonist and support — it strengthens the secondary dropdown's boundary and weakens the primary verb's — and the caption that names every control fails WCAG 1.4.3 in BOTH schemes, worse in dark.

**Mechanism.** emphasis and boundary expressed only as alpha over an ambient wash, never as a material tier — so contrast is a byproduct of the live seed rather than a designed value, and no scheme-specific treatment exists

**Evidence.**

```
Real Safari pixels, decoded from visual/shots/safari-desktop-{light,dark}/mix.png (2880x1800, DPR 2). Boundary contrast vs local ground — Select capsule: light rgb(246,219,220) vs rgb(240,186,202) = 1.278:1; dark rgb(76,52,52) vs rgb(119,75,85) = 1.581:1. Mix capsule shipped-disabled: light rgb(237,198,205) = 1.095:1; dark rgb(108,75,79) = 1.060:1. Mix capsule ENABLED, derived by the exact opacity:0.5 algebra plate_enabled = 2*plate_disabled - ground: light 1.197:1, dark 1.123:1 (the light figure reproduces r1's independently canvas-composited 1.20:1 to three digits, validating the method). Support/protagonist ratio: 1.07x light, 1.41x dark. Peak-ink search inside the caption glyph rect: `COLOR SPACE` light ink rgb(101,84,66) @CSS(757.5,429.5) vs ground rgb(240,187,202) = 4.367:1; dark ink rgb(195,185,172) vs ground rgb(119,76,85) = 3.681:1 — at 14.384px weight 400 (normal text, 4.5:1 floor). Same rect for the value: 13.504:1 light / 8.998:1 dark, a 3.1x separation between the choice and the word naming it. Mechanism measured: trigger computed backgroundColor = rgba(0,0,0,0), backdropFilter = none; its entire boundary is `1px solid color(srgb 0.11 0.098 0.09 / 0.14)` plus four 1px inset bevels.
```

**Reproduction.** node png-scan.mjs / node png-ink.mjs (session scratchpad; a from-scratch node:zlib PNG inflate + unfilter) over docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-{light,dark}/mix.png. Sample points: pane (1150,700), aboveBar (900,446), triggerPlate (900,467), mixPlate (880,517) in CSS px. Ink rects: label {x:754,y:424,w:120,h:21}, value {x:766,y:455,w:60,h:24}. Outputs pasted verbatim in the report. NOTE: the claim that a different seed could erase the control entirely is a HYPOTHESIS — no capture exercises a second seed; the alpha-only construction that permits it is measured fact.

**Proposed cure.** Emphasis must survive as a material delta, not an alpha delta: reach the producer's `emphasis="primary"` branch (glass-ui components/button/styles.css `.button[data-emphasis="primary"]`, the only rule supplying the tinted plate + font-weight 650), which is currently unreachable because `variant="primary-audacious"` is a dead attribute (r1/r2 D-1). ### `DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D) — demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue` · D-1 · DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** `variant="primary-audacious"` is a dead attribute on glass-ui 7.0.0's Button — the page's ONE commit verb ships as the default quiet secondary wash with 1.20:1 plate contrast against its own pane

**Mechanism.** Retired producer prop handed to the glass-ui 7.0.0 major; Vue fallthrough attributes turn a wrong prop into a decorative DOM attribute rather than an error, so neither vue-tsc nor the runtime announces it.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:163. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts: `export interface ButtonProps extends PrimitiveProps { emphasis?: ButtonEmphasis; tone?: Tone; size?: ButtonSize; iconOnly?; loading?; type?; disabled?; class?; }` — no `variant`. `$ grep -rl "primary-audacious" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → no output (0 files). Live DOM (Playwright/WebKit, localhost:9000/#/mix): `data-slot=button | data-emphasis=secondary | data-tone=neutral | data-size=md | class=button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash glass-capsule glass-capsule-hover h-10 gap-2 font-medium font-display | variant=primary-audacious`. Measured composited contrast: enabled plate vs pane 1.20:1, disabled 1.10:1 (WCAG 1.4.11 floor 3:1). Family counts: `grep -rn 'variant=' demo/ | wc -l` → 106; `grep -rn 'emphasis=' demo/ | wc -l` → 2. Second site: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:158.
```

**Reproduction.** Navigate http://localhost:9000/#/mix (server is IPv6-only: curl http://[::1]:9000/ → 200; 127.0.0.1 → 000). Evaluate: `[...document.querySelectorAll('[data-slot="button"]')].find(b=>b.textContent.trim()==='Mix').outerHTML` → shows data-emphasis=secondary alongside the stray variant attribute.

**Proposed cure.** Delete `variant` here and at GenerateControls.vue:158; pass `emphasis="primary"` plus a named `tone`. Then close the family architecturally: fail the build on any `variant=` reaching a glass-ui root, because Vue fallthrough guarantees the remaining ~104 sites will never announce themselves. Drop the `h-10 gap-2 font-medium font-display` costume; a taller commit rung is `size="lg"` at the root.

### `DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D) — demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue` · D-2 · DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** BLOCKER — `Hue method` is inert in the shipped default state, and the "four-arc quartet" is never four in ANY reachable state. ESCALATES round 1 D-4, which proved only the acylindrical case by construction.

**Mechanism.** the bar models the dependency that does not matter (mode→leftover strategy, gated at :144) and refuses the one that does (space→hue relevance); an over-enumerated, partly synonymous vocabulary is presented as flat and orthogonal at equal geometry, material and weight to the control that actually decides the mix.

**Evidence.**

```
src/color/anchors.ts:360-366 `HUE_INDEX = { hsl:0, hsv:0, hwb:0, lch:2, oklch:2 }`; src/color/operations.ts:101-111 reads `options.hue` only inside `if (i === hueIndex)`. Default space is oklab (useMixingState.ts:44). Runnable proof, red→green, 8 samples, all 9 offered spaces: oklab/lab/rgb/xyz → distinct ramps 1/4 (all four methods byte-identical); oklch/lch/hsl/hsv/hwb → distinct ramps 2/4 (increasing≡shorter, decreasing≡longer). Comment at MixConfigBar.vue:127-128 claims "the four-arc quartet".
```

**Reproduction.** node -e "import('./dist/subpaths/color.js').then(({rgb,convertColor,mixColors})=>{ /* unwrap Results; for each space build 8-sample ramps under all 4 hue methods; count distinct */ })" — output pasted in the report. Zero UI steps needed.

**Proposed cure.** Gate the row on `HUE_INDEX[colorSpace] !== undefined` (one boolean from the library, no new vocabulary) so a space without a hue channel has no hue row at all — the same honest-absence restraint already used for the operand ramps. Then reduce the surviving vocabulary to the two real arcs; `increasing`/`decreasing` are library-level synonyms of `shorter`/`longer` for a two-operand mix and should not be separate UI rows. Preview chips then always show two genuinely different ramps, which is the only reason to show chips.

### `design (CHALLENGE-D) — demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay` · D-25 · design (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** The result is delivered off-screen. On iPhone 14, 0.00 px of the 215.81 px result plate is inside the scroll viewport at the moment the convergence completes. On desktop the bottom 28.5 px is clipped, which by the plate's own box model is the action row — Copy/Save/Reset are sliced in half. Nothing scrolls, focuses, or announces on settle.

**Mechanism.** Missing reveal contract. MixPane.vue:62 houses the pane in an inner `overflow-y-auto` Card; the plate is appended as the last child of that column. useMixingState.ts:104-106 `settleMix()` flips a phase and returns — no reveal, no focus move, no announcement. ### `library structure — module boundaries, ownership, dependency` · N-1 · library structure

**Defect.** Three of the 27 specimen tiles this component renders (the whole `back` family) destroy the entire Gradient pane on click. The demo converts value.js's Result error back into a thrown Error inside a Vue `computed`, which has no error channel, so it escapes to the app ErrorBoundary. The structural cause is a missing seam owner: no package owns 'an eased t may leave [0,1]; a colour ramp clamps'.

**Mechanism.** Result→throw conversion at a render boundary + a domain seam (overshooting eased progress vs mixColors' [0,1] contract) that has no owner in any of the three packages; the catalogue that offers curves and the sampler that consumes them are two homes for one invariant.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:199-208 (`const easedT = easing(t); … if (!mixed.ok) throw new Error("Gradient color mix failed: " + mixed.error.code)`) against src/color/operations.ts:65 (`if (progress < 0 || progress > 1) return err({ code: "color_progress_out_of_range" })`). Duplicated verbatim at demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientInterpolation.ts:37. Measured ranges over dist/subpaths/easing.js: ease-in-back [-0.0969, 1.0000] · ease-out-back [0.0000, 1.0869] · ease-in-out-back [-0.0927, 1.0927]. Live capture — BEFORE {"rows":1,"tiles":27,"stage":1} / AFTER {"rows":0,"tiles":0,"stage":0,"bodyText":"… This panel hit an unexpected error. Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range  Try again"}.
```

**Reproduction.** Headless Chromium → http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → wait for settle → click the `ease-out-back` specimen tile in the open easing row (`[data-specimen='ease-out-back']`). The pane is replaced by the ErrorBoundary. Script: scratchpad/L-crash.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Give the seam a single owner: new `demo/workbenches/gradient/model/rampDomain.ts` exporting `clampProgress(t: number): number`, and route EVERY eased-t → colour call through it (sampleCoalescedStops, interpolateStopColors). Clamping is not a fallback — it is what CSS itself does when interpolating a gradient, so overshoot curves then render exactly as `linear-gradient` renders them, while overshoot survives where it is meaningful (glyph portraits, picker canvas). Simultaneously delete the duplicated Result→throw conversion and thread an explicit `{ok:false, reason}` verdict the way `applyCSS` already does (useGradientModel.ts:158-168). Codify the repo invariant: `src/` returns Result; `demo/` may throw only from an event handler, never from a computed, a watch callback, or module top-level.

### `library structure — module boundaries, ownership, dependency` · N-2 · library structure

**Defect.** The 'zero letterbox' law in EasingAuthoringStage is not fragile — it is already dead. Both its JS probe and its `:deep()` CSS target `svg[role="img"]`, and glass-ui 7.0.0 ships zero `role:"img"` (its picker canvas is `role="group"`). `--vb-ratio` is frozen at its seed forever, all four style declarations are inert, and the T-48 liquid-morph `transition: aspect-ratio` animation has been silently DELETED from the product while remaining in the source (edict 6).

**Mechanism.** Consumer styles the producer by internal DOM selector (ARIA role, class name, and `data-testid` — a test contract used as a styling contract) instead of through published props; the coupling died silently across a glass-ui major with no gate catching it. Compounded by the demo scraping from the DOM a value (`viewBox`) the producer already publishes as a ComputedRef on `useEasingPicker`.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue,` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** MT-F023 confirmed independently and ADOPTED (structure, not gate); the root's stated mechanism is understated and I supply the stronger one. The three scroll-timeline animations run at full amplitude under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. The root says the global guard cannot reach them because a scroll animation has animation-duration:auto — but the guard DOES compute onto the element (0.00001s); both engines simply ignore a time-valued duration on a progress-based timeline. Duration-based neutralisation is therefore CATEGORICALLY incapable of reaching any scroll-/view-driven animation, so no widening of the guard can ever fix this class.

**Mechanism.** M-A — same family as C-1: engine behaviour asserted from spec reading rather than measured. Specifically, the file argues at :148-151 that a position-mapped scrub 'needs no PRM gate'; the design system it consumes contradicts that argument in code at four separate sites.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:177-194 (the three ungated declarations) and :148-151 (the argument for omitting the PRM gate). demo/styles/animations.css:184-192 (the guard) and :178 (the false 'app-wide' headline the root already flagged). probe-09-prm-mechanism.mjs: webkit rm=no-preference title {"duration":"auto","timeline":"--pane-scroll"} / rm=reduce title {"duration":"0.00001s","timeline":"--pane-scroll"}; chromium rm=reduce {"duration":"1e-05s","timeline":"--pane-scroll"} — the guard lands the property and the animation still scrubs. probe-01-structure.mjs: under reduce, webkit still 1 -> 0.310808 and veil 0.52 -> 1; chromium still 1 -> 0.618029 — identical to no-preference to the last digit. Producer precedent, glass-ui 7.0.0: dist/styles/scroll-driven.css wraps .scroll-progress AND [data-scroll-reveal] > * in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { @supports (animation-timeline: scroll()) { ... } }; dist/styles/scroll-choreography.css does the same for .scroll-cascade > * and .scroll-pin-stage .scroll-pin-phase-*.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-09-prm-mechanism.mjs  (guard reaches the property, animation ignores it) ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-01-structure.mjs  (full-amplitude scrub under reduce, both engines) ; the root's own node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/probes/prm-scroll-timeline.mjs reproduces the same observable

**Proposed cure.** Adopt the root's disposition verbatim and do NOT weaken it into another override stacked on the blunt guard: move the three declarations at PaneHeader.vue:177-194 inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), PRM outside and @supports inside. This is the producer's own idiom, used at four sites in glass-ui 7.0.0, so it is edict-4 conformance rather than an invention. It costs nothing at rest because the from-state already equals the base state (verified: inactive-timeline hosts paint transform:none / veil 0.52). Also correct animations.css:178's headline, which claims app-wide neutralisation it cannot deliver for progress-based timelines.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue,` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The 'collapse' reclaims ZERO scrollport and leaves a 92px pointer-opaque dead band. Because the choreography is transform/opacity only (the F3 layout fork was retired without replacing what it did), the sticky header's reserved height never changes: it still eats 136.6px of a 900px viewport while showing 28.6px of title and a fully transparent description that keeps its 18.7px box. Every point in the band hit-tests to the header, so 92px x full pane width of click surface is swallowed.

**Mechanism.** M-B — a transform-only collapse asked to do a layout job. transform and opacity are definitionally layout-neutral, so a 'shrink' expressed purely in them cannot return the space a shrink exists to return.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:145-157 (the compositor-only rationale) and :183-193. probe-01-structure.mjs, webkit #/ scrolled 300: headerH 136.59 -> 136.59, titleRectH 91.91 -> 28.57, descOp 1 -> 0, descRectH 18.69 -> 18.69 (chromium identically 136.64 -> 136.64). probe-05-deadband.mjs: {"headerH":136.6,"viewportH":900,"titleBottom":148.6,"descWrap":{"top":213.9,"h":18.7},"deadBandPx":92,"deadBandPctOfViewport":10.2} — 65.3px of pure void plus 18.7px of invisible description. elementFromPoint sampled down the header's centre column returns, at y=151/163/175/187/199 DIV.pane-header, at y=211/223 P.pane-header-desc, at y=235 DIV.pane-header — inHeader:true at all eight points. Chromium dead band 63.8px / 7.1% of viewport.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-05-deadband.mjs  (needs http://localhost:9000; also emits shot-webkit-desktop-about-scrolled300.png)

**Proposed cure.** Give the choreography exactly ONE honest layout channel rather than resurrecting the retired three-channel per-frame fork: animate .pane-header-desc-wrap's grid-template-rows 1fr -> 0fr so the description's BOX collapses (this simultaneously discharges C-9's hit-target and a11y-tree residue), and let the title's scale ride a matching margin-block-end reduction on the header. One box, one property, still compositor-cheap. Note the gate interaction: O-11 gate 4's live half asserts <=5 Layout events over a 0->300px scrub, so it must be reformed to BOUND layout per scrub rather than forbid it, or it will veto the cure.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue,` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** O-11 gate 3's 'no double-exposure' certification is measured on the wrong quantity. The gate asserts the veil animation's opacity reaches 1 and calls that the cure; opacity 1 of a 65%-alpha fill is not opacity. At the swell-complete state 35% (light) / 28% (dark) of the scrolled content transmits through, behind only a 7px blur, so pane content remains fully legible inside the band and is overprinted by the shrunken title.

**Mechanism.** M-B — a consequence of the same transform-only collapse: because C-3 leaves a 92px band of scrollport occupied by nothing, there is a large region for under-scrolled content to sit inside, and the material chosen for that region is translucent by construction (--glass-bg-resting, the rung-1 resting fill).

**Evidence.**

```
e2e/smoke/oracles/o11-header-gates.spec.ts:154 (`expect(at64.opacity, ...).toBe(1)`) and :18-19 (the gate's stated purpose). probe-06-veil-alpha.mjs, #/ scrolled 300: light {"animOpacity":"1","bg":"color(srgb 0.994 0.96 0.926 / 0.65)","backdrop":"blur(7px) saturate(1.4)"}; dark {"animOpacity":"1","bg":"color(srgb 0.2074 0.165013 0.1326 / 0.72)","backdrop":"blur(7px) saturate(1.3) brightness(1.14)"}. Visual confirmation: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/shot-webkit-desktop-about-scrolled300.png — inside the 136.6px band the h2 'Basic Information' and the rows 'Dependency: Device-independent' and 'White Point: Variable (typically D50 or D65)' are plainly legible, with the 0.311x title 'About the color spaces, Lab' printed directly across them.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-06-veil-alpha.mjs  (needs http://localhost:9000) ; then read shot-webkit-desktop-about-scrolled300.png

**Proposed cure.** Two separable moves. Gate: O-11 gate 3 must read the COMPOSITED result — sample pixels of a known glyph inside the band versus the same glyph outside it — not getComputedStyle(el,'::before').opacity, which cannot see material alpha. Design: do not raise the veil's alpha under the stuck state, which would be a per-instance override of a producer token and violates edict 5; instead let C-3's real box collapse remove the band, so there is no 136.6px window for content to be double-exposed in.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue,` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** A leaf component emits an UNSCOPED global rule imposing `contain: layout style paint` on nine sibling pane roots it does not own, justified by a rationale that is not how the feature works ('isolates the named scroll-timeline' — timeline-name lookup resolves to the nearest declaring ancestor; the scoping property is timeline-scope). The containment is measurably non-load-bearing for the animation, and its real effect is to make every pane a containing block for position:fixed descendants plus a paint clip — a latent mispositioning trap on nine surfaces.

**Mechanism.** M-C — a leaf component legislating for surfaces it does not own. The unscoped block reaches nine sibling roots, and the justification given for it describes a behaviour the property does not have, so no later reader can discover the cost by reading the file.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:54-57 (the rule) and :50-53 (the false rationale). Nine consumers carry the class: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:2, demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:2, demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:2, demo/scenes/about/AboutPane.vue:4, demo/workbenches/mix/MixPane.vue:62, demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientPane.vue:20, demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:31, demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractPane.vue:5, demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:106. probe-07-misc.mjs — a position:fixed;top:0;left:0 probe appended inside a live pane lands at the host's content-box origin, not the viewport: #/admin/users {"fixedTop":234,"fixedLeft":200,"hostTop":233,"hostLeft":199,"contain":"content"}; #/ {"fixedTop":104,"fixedLeft":730,"hostTop":103,"hostLeft":729,"contain":"content"}. CONTROL EXPERIMENT, probe-08-taptarget-and-contain.mjs — with `.pane-scroll-fade{contain:none !important}` injected, the animation values are byte-identical (webkit REST {"contain":"none","titleTf":"matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)","veil":"0.52"} -> STUCK [{"titleTf":"matrix(0.310808, ...)","veil":"1"}]; chromium STUCK matrix(0.618029,...), veil 1) while the fixed probe returns to {"fixedTop":0,"fixedLeft":0}. Producer precedent: glass-ui 7.0.0 dist/styles/scroll-choreography.css uses the narrower `.scroll-pin-stage { position: sticky; inset-block-start: 0; contain: layout paint; }` on a stage the producer owns.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-07-misc.mjs  (the fixed-position trap) ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-08-taptarget-and-contain.mjs  (the contain:none control experiment)

**Proposed cure.** Delete `contain` from PaneHeader.vue:55 — measured non-load-bearing, and the overflow-y:auto / overflow-x-hidden already present on all nine consumers supplies the paint clip they actually rely on. If timeline scoping is genuinely wanted, timeline-scope is the property that provides it. Then relocate the surviving single-declaration `scroll-timeline: --pane-scroll block` rule to glass-ui beside dist/styles/scroll-driven.css under edict 4 — a producer-shaped scroll grammar does not belong in an unscoped <style> block inside a leaf consumer.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue,` · C-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The pane's primary title — the largest text on every pane, the acknowledged single site all nine panes inherit — is a hardcoded <h3> with no level prop, and the application has ZERO <h1> anywhere. On the About pane the h3 is followed by its own <h2> section headings, so the pane title sits at a LOWER level than its children: the document outline is inverted. Secondarily, consumers slot non-title content (a <button>, a live-count <Badge>) into the heading, polluting its accessible name.

**Mechanism.** M-C — the same overreach as C-5: a leaf component fixing a document-structure decision for nine consumers that only the consumer can know, and offering a single unnamed slot that forces adornments to become heading children.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:21 `<h3 class="pane-header-title font-display"><slot /></h3>`, with :12-14 confirming it is 'the ONE site; all 9 panes inherit'. docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md:119-178 — the h1 column reads 0 in all 60 captures (4 matrices x 15 routes). probe-01-structure.mjs, #/ document order (* = PaneHeader's): H3 H3* H2 H2 H2 H2 H2 H2 H3 H3 H2 H3 H3 H3 H2 H3 H3 H2 H3 H3 H2 — H3* 'About the color spaces, Lab' precedes its own H2 children, and h1Count:0 on every route probed. probe-07-misc.mjs: #/ title 'About the color spaces, Lab' childEls ["BUTTON.bg-transparent"]; #/admin/users title 'Users 0' childEls ["DIV.badge-atom"]. The suite already compensates: e2e/smoke/admin/admin-walk.spec.ts:73-77 carries a .first() workaround for heading ambiguity on these routes.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-01-structure.mjs  (heading order + h1Count, all routes/engines) ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-07-misc.mjs  (heading children)

**Proposed cure.** Two small changes inside the component, adding no wrapper and no shared directory (edict 3): (a) a `level` prop rendered as a dynamic tag (`<component :is="`h${level}`">`), defaulting to 1 for a pane's primary title, so each consumer places itself in the outline; (b) a dedicated named slot (#adornment) rendered as a SIBLING of the heading rather than a child, so the accessible name is the title alone and stops mutating when a badge count refreshes. (b) also discharges C-7 structurally by removing the interactive content from the scaled box.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue,` · C-7 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The shrink applies transform:scale() to the whole <h3>, so it scales any interactive content a consumer slots into the title. AboutPane's color-space <button> drops from 88.6x47.9 to 27.6x14.9 on WebKit when the pane is scrolled — under the 24x24 minimum on BOTH axes. This is a DYNAMIC tap-target regression the at-rest visual audit structurally cannot see, so the audit's smallTapTargets count is understated on every scrollable route.

**Mechanism.** M-B — the transform-only collapse again: because the collapse is expressed as a scale on the heading BOX rather than on its text, every descendant including live controls is scaled with it. Compounded by C-1: at the designed 0.618 (Chromium) the control still passes with 5.6px of margin; only C-1's erroneous 0.311 pushes it under the bar.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:183-188 (scale applied to .pane-header-title) + :21 (the unnamed slot that admits interactive children). probe-08-taptarget-and-contain.mjs, #/ at 1440x900, rest -> scroll 300: webkit REST {"name":"Lab","w":88.6,"h":47.9,"wcag258_24px":true} -> STUCK {"name":"Lab","w":27.6,"h":14.9,"wcag258_24px":false}; chromium REST {"w":88.6,"h":48,"wcag258_24px":true} -> STUCK {"w":54.8,"h":29.6,"wcag258_24px":true}. docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md:33 records `/#/: 8` small tap targets — measured at scrollTop 0, where this control is a compliant 88.6x47.9; scroll the pane on Safari and it becomes 9. WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), level AA.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-08-taptarget-and-contain.mjs  (needs http://localhost:9000)

**Proposed cure.** Take the scale off the interactive box. Either drive the collapse on a text-only inner span so slotted controls keep their rest geometry, or express the collapse as font-size driven by a @property-registered scalar rather than a box transform — both keep the compositor arm and neither can reach a descendant control's hit box. C-6's sibling #adornment slot removes the AboutPane and AdminPane cases structurally; fixing C-1 restores the margin but only to 5.6px, which the next type-rung change can spend, so the geometric cure is the durable one.

The gates assert the shape of the CSS (which properties appear, inside which at-rules) rather than the rendered result, so they are invariant to every value-level and engine-level defect in this component.
