ENGINE HOLE: o11-header-gates.spec.ts lives in e2e/smoke/oracles/, which is the `smoke` project with browserName:"chromium" (playwright.config.ts:143-160); the WebKit project smoke-safari has testDir:"./e2e/smoke/safari" (playwright.config.ts:252-256), a different subtree — despite that project's own comment (:240-247) declaring its purpose is catching iOS-Safari-class divergence. NO UNIT TESTS: grep -rln 'pane-header|PaneHeader' test/ returns nothing.
```

**Reproduction.** grep -n 'reducedMotion|emulateMedia|scrubTo' e2e/smoke/oracles/o11-header-gates.spec.ts  (gate 5 never scrubs) ; grep -rn 'pane-title-shrink|shrink-ratio|pane-desc-shrink|pane-header-veil' e2e/ test/  (zero hits) ; sed -n '142,160p;252,256p' playwright.config.ts  (oracles are chromium; smoke-safari is a different testDir) ; grep -rln 'pane-header|PaneHeader' test/  (no unit tests)

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (demo/color-picker/` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Total diagnostic blackout. `return false` at :68 makes Vue's handleError return before app.config.errorHandler and before logError; the component logs nothing itself and emits nothing on catch. The hook signature additionally discards Vue's `instance` and `info` arguments, and the app installs no global net at all, so the error reaches no channel anywhere.

demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:59 (`onErrorCaptured((err) => {` — instance and info dropped), :68 (`return false`). Unit probe C-B, my run: `console.error mentioning the throw: false`, `console.warn mentioning the throw: false`, `app.config.errorHandler invocations: 0`, `component emissions on catch: {}`. Live: with INDUCED-AUDIT-THROW caught, the full session console+pageerror capture contains zero mention of it. `grep -rn "errorHandler|unhandledrejection|window.onerror" demo/` returns only ErrorBoundary.vue:67's own comment; demo/color-picker/index.html:210 calls createApp(App) with no config.errorHandler. Contradicts the honesty contract App.vue:144-149 preserves elsewhere.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/color-sessi` · C-6 · CHALLENGE-C

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/color-session/c` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The F7 "golden plate" law is false as written: `inline-size: 2.618rem` is root-anchored while `block-size: 1em` is inheritance-anchored, so the two axes resolve in two different font contexts. The measured ratio is 2.554, not phi-squared = 2.61803, and the chip is 19% taller than the description line it claims to join.

**Mechanism.** rem-vs-em anchor split: the comment's own arithmetic ("φ² × 1em") is only true when the inherited font size equals the root font size. It does not here (16.4px vs 16px) and would not under any user font-size override. Separately, the chip is a SIBLING of `.text-micro` (MixConfigBar.vue:110-113), not a descendant, so its `1em` resolves against the option's NAME lane (16.4px), never the description lane (11px/13.75px) — "joins the description line" was never true of the cascade.

**Evidence.**

```
PreviewRamp.vue:9-11 ("the chip joins the description line — height 1em, width one golden plate (φ² ≈ 2.618rem)") and :43-44 (`inline-size: 2.618rem; block-size: 1em;`). probe-C-paint2.mjs fontContext, measured at the chip's exact DOM slot with the menu open: {"wrapperFontSize":"16.4px","microFontSize":"11px","microLineHeight":"13.75px","microH":13.75,"nameFontSize":"16.4px","rootFontSize":"16px","chipWouldBe":{"wPx":41.888,"hPx":16.4}}. 41.888/16.4 = 2.554.
```

**Reproduction.** node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PreviewRamp/probe-C-paint2.mjs, section `fontContext`.

**Proposed cure.** Write the law in one unit against one anchor — `block-size: 1em; inline-size: 2.618em;` — so the plate is phi-squared by construction at every scale, and give the chip the font size of the lane it claims (`font-size: var(--text-micro)`, or move the chip inside the description lane). Do it once, in the single rooted chip plate.

The opacity:0 description keeps its 18.7px box, still wins the hit test, and is still in the accessibility tree (aria-hidden is null).

**Mechanism.** M-B — a transform-only collapse asked to do a layout job; the F3 retirement (PaneHeader.vue:145-157) removed the layout channel without replacing what it did.

**Evidence.**

```
probe-C2-03-live.mjs: chromium 1440x900 /#/ REST hdrH=136.64 -> STUCK hdrH=136.64 (webkit 136.59 -> 136.59); descOp 1 -> 0 with descH 18.7 -> 18.7 unchanged. probe-C2-07-consequences.mjs(c): {headerH:136.6, viewportH:900, titleBottom:176.8, headerBottom:240.6, deadBandPx:63.8, deadBandPctViewport:7.1, descOpacity:"0", descRectH:18.7, descAriaHidden:null, hitColumn:["179:DIV.pane-header","191:DIV.pane-header","203:DIV.pane-header","215:P.pane-header-desc","227:P.pane-header-desc","239:DIV.pane-header"]} — the invisible <p> is the hit-test winner at y=215 and y=227.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-C2-07-consequences.mjs (section (c)) ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-C2-03-live.mjs

**Proposed cure.** Collapse the description's BOX, not only its ink: animate `.pane-header-desc-wrap { grid-template-rows: 1fr }` to `0fr` (the wrap div already exists at PaneHeader.vue:22, which is why the -wrap element is there at all), with the title's scale riding a matching margin-block-end reduction. One channel, one box — it removes the reserved space, the hit target and the a11y-tree entry together and REPLACES the opacity keyframe rather than adding to it. O-11 gate 4's live half (<=5 Layout events) must then be reformed to BOUND layout per scrub rather than forbid it.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shared/ui/PaneH` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** A leaf component writes `contain: layout style paint` in an UNSCOPED <style> block onto .pane-scroll-fade — a class on the root of nine sibling pane surfaces it does not own — on a rationale that is not how the feature works. The declaration is measurably non-load-bearing for its stated purpose, and it silently traps every position:fixed descendant of every pane.

**Mechanism.** M-C — a leaf component legislating for surfaces it does not own, via a global unscoped block, on an unverified rationale.

**Evidence.**

```
PaneHeader.vue:54-57 (rule) and :50-53 (the false rationale: 'contain isolates the named scroll-timeline'). probe-C2-08-contain.mjs control experiment, both engines: SHIPPED contain="content" rest{veil 0.52, matrix(1)} stuck{veil 1, matrix(0.618029 chromium / 0.310808 webkit)}; contain:none contain="none" — BYTE-IDENTICAL animation values. Same probe, the trap: fixedLandsAt {top:104,left:730} shipped vs {top:0,left:0} with contain removed, hostOriginAt {103,729}. timeline-scope — the property that actually scopes timeline names — is supported in both engines (probe-C2-01: `timeline-scope: --pane-scroll` -> true on webkit and chromium). Producer precedent: glass-ui dist/styles/scroll-choreography.css uses `.scroll-pin-stage { contain: layout paint }` — narrower, on a stage it owns.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-C2-08-contain.mjs

**Proposed cure.** Delete `contain` from PaneHeader.vue:55 (measured non-load-bearing); the `overflow-y-auto overflow-x-hidden` already on all nine consumers provides the paint clip they actually rely on. If timeline scoping is genuinely wanted, use `timeline-scope`. The remaining single-declaration `scroll-timeline` rule is a producer-shaped concern and belongs in glass-ui beside scroll-driven.css under edict 4, not in an unscoped <style> block inside a leaf consumer.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shared/ui/PaneH` · C-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The pane's primary title is a hardcoded <h3> with no level prop; the app has ZERO <h1>; on About the pane's <h3> is immediately followed by its own <h2> section headings, inverting the outline; and consumers slot interactive (<button>) and live-updating (<Badge> count) content INTO the heading, so an interactive control is nested in an <h3> and the heading's accessible name mutates on every data refresh.

**Mechanism.** M-C — a leaf component legislating for surfaces it does not own: one hardcoded heading level and one undifferentiated slot imposed on all nine panes.

**Evidence.**

```
PaneHeader.vue:21 `<h3 class="pane-header-title font-display"><slot /></h3>`. probe-C2-03-live.mjs: h1Count=0 in all 24 route-cells; /#/ outline = `H3 H3* H2 H2 H2 H2 H2 H2 H3 H3 H2 H3 H3 H3 H2 H3 H3 H2 H3 H3 H2` (* = PaneHeader title). Slotted children: /#/ -> ["BUTTON.bg-transparent"] (AboutPane.vue:15-27), /#/admin/users -> ["DIV.badge-atom"] (AdminPane.vue:5). Corroborated by docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md: h1 = 0 in all 60 captures. e2e/smoke/admin/admin-walk.spec.ts:73-77 already carries a .first() workaround for heading ambiguity — the suite is compensating for the component's shape. WCAG 1.3.1 (heading-order, page-has-heading-one).

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-C2-03-live.mjs

**Proposed cure.** Give PaneHeader a `level` prop resolving to a dynamic tag (`<component :is="`h${level}`">`), defaulting to 1 for a pane's primary title; and a dedicated named slot for adornments rendered as a SIBLING of the heading, not a child, so the accessible name is the title alone. Two small changes inside the component; neither adds a wrapper component nor a shared directory (edict 3). The sibling slot also structurally removes C-7's AboutPane and AdminPane cases.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shared/ui/PaneH` · C-7 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** pane-title-shrink applies transform: scale() to the <h3>, so every interactive control a consumer slots into the title scales with it. On Safari at 1440x900 the About colour-space <button> drops to 27.6 x 14.9 px — under WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) on both axes. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shared/ui/PaneH` · C-8 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The certifying oracle is vacuous in four independent ways: (i) O-11 gate 5 never scrubs under PRM, so it returns the SAME verdict for the defect and for its cure; (ii) O-11 gate 3's green is an artifact of the smoke project's hard-coded 1280x720 viewport — the identical assertion FAILS at 1440x900 and 1512x982 on both engines; (iii) nothing anywhere asserts the shrink ratio, the title scale or the header height, so `--pane-title-shrink-ratio: 0.05` keeps every gate green; (iv) the header oracle runs on Chromium only, so the entire C-1 divergence class is structurally unreachable by the suite.

**Mechanism.** Vacuous gate — assertions positioned where they cannot discriminate: gate 5 measures the one state both branches share; gate 3 measures a property of the config, not of the component; gate 4 measures names, not values; and the one engine that fails is the one engine the oracle never runs on.

**Evidence.**

```
e2e/smoke/oracles/o11-header-gates.spec.ts:278-348 (gate 5: readVeils at :40-55 has no scroll; scrubTo at :59-73 exists and is never called by gate 5; the assert at :306-308 compares rest to rest). Gate 3's assert at :154 `expect(at64.opacity, ...).toBe(1)`; replicated verbatim by probe-C2-07-consequences.mjs(a): chromium 1280x720 max=211 at64=1 PASS; chromium 1440x900 max=61 at64=0.9775 FAIL; chromium 1512x982 max=5 at64=0.5575 FAIL; webkit 1280x720 at64=1 PASS; webkit 1440x900 at64=0.97 FAIL; webkit 1512x982 at64=0.5425 FAIL. playwright.config.ts:159 pins viewport {width:1280,height:720}. `grep -rn "pane-title-shrink|shrink-ratio|pane-desc-shrink|pane-header-veil" e2e/ test/` -> zero hits; O-11 gate 4 checks only property NAMES (new Set(["transform","opacity"]), :176,184), never values. playwright.config.ts:142-160 smoke = browserName "chromium"; :252-256 smoke-safari testDir "./e2e/smoke/safari" (a different subtree). `grep -rln "pane-header|PaneHeader" test/` -> no files.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-C2-07-consequences.mjs (section (a)) ; grep -rn "pane-title-shrink\|shrink-ratio\|pane-desc-shrink\|pane-header-veil" e2e/ test/ ; grep -rln "pane-header\|PaneHeader" test/

**Proposed cure.** Gate 5 must call scrubTo under `reduce` and assert stuck == rest — the property its own title claims. Gate 3 must assert against the pane's own travel (min(64, maxScroll)) or run a viewport matrix, not one hard-coded size. Add one gate asserting `--pane-title-shrink-ratio` resolves to `--type-heading / --type-display-1` within 1e-4 AND that the stuck title's rendered box is never larger than its rest box — a single assertion that catches C-1 at every width on both engines. And give the header oracle a WebKit arm (widen smoke-safari's testDir to include oracles/, or add a smoke-safari-oracles project); without it even the new ratio gate would have missed C-1 entirely.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (assume the design is flawed)` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The 'one golden plate' is not golden at any measured viewport (2.5731…3.0166 vs phi^2 = 2.6180, a 17.1% spread; 2.2886…2.9911 over the earlier seat's wider sweep, 30.7%), and its `1em` height is inherited from the popover's scroll container rather than from any type role in its lane — on /generate the plate stands 1.481x the font-size of the copy it is declared to 'join'.

**Mechanism.** Two axes on two different unit scales cannot hold a constant ratio, and the em axis is anchored to a scroll container rather than a declared type rung — so one declaration produces two different optical objects in the two hosts and drifts with every clamp arm and every browser zoom level. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.8: 'Real rendered relation wins over token intent.' Owner edict 5 (root-level styling) is violated twice with the token unused in the same stylesheet tree.

**Evidence.**

```
probes-D2/out/lane-type.json: /generate@1440 chip 41.923x16.292 ratio 2.5731, chip font-size 16.4px, copy `.text-micro` 11px, chipH/copyFont 1.481, font-size inherited from `max-h-[inherit] overflow-y-auto px-(--overlay-pad-inline)`; /atmosphere@1440 42.117x15.890 ratio 2.6505 (chipH/copyFont 0.969); /generate@390 ratio 3.0126; /atmosphere@390 ratio 3.0166. Earlier seat's five-viewport sweep (probes-D/ratio-sweep.log): 2.2886…2.9911, zero exact hits.
Source: PreviewStrip.vue:59-60 (`inline-size: 2.618rem` root-relative x `block-size: 1em` locally inherited). Token already exists and is ignored twice: demo/styles/foundation.css:462 `--phi-4: 2.618rem` vs the literal at PreviewStrip.vue:59 and PreviewRamp.vue:43 (`grep -rn "2\.618" demo/` → 8 hits). `--radius-sm` measured 4px fixed against a 13.9–16.4px plate.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PreviewStrip/probes-D2/lane-type.mjs

**Proposed cure.** One unit system, one token, one anchor: `block-size: 1lh` (or 1em of a DECLARED lane role) with `inline-size: calc(var(--phi-2) * 1em)` from the same em, hoisted to the shared glass-ui root of D-7 so phi^2 is true by construction at every clamp arm and zoom level, and the radius scales with the plate.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (assume the design is flawed)` · D-7 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The primitive was never rooted: 'n colour bands in a clipped plate' is minted three times — twice under the SAME class name in two `scoped` blocks that cannot reach each other, and a third time as PaletteColorStrip imported into the same file — with three different elision laws, two unit systems, a colliding glass-ui name and an unused design token.

**Mechanism.** Owner edicts 3 (KISS/no contrivance), 4 (glass-ui is the design system; reuse existing component-type names) and 5 (root-level styling, never per-instance) all violated by the same root cause: the shared law lives in prose and in duplicated scoped CSS rather than in one design-system primitive, so it silently diverges.

**Evidence.**

```
(1) `.preview-chip` declared at PreviewStrip.vue:56-65 and PreviewRamp.vue:40-49, both `scoped`, already drifted `inline-flex` vs `inline-block` — which is precisely the difference that makes the ring paint in one and not the other (D-1). color-chips/index.ts:2-4 claims the opposite: 'ONE focused common module for the multi-feature chip grammar, never a per-pane copy'. (2) GenerateControls.vue:16 imports PaletteColorStrip and :20 imports PreviewStrip; PaletteColorStrip.vue:47-48,62-64 carries the 8% legibility floor PreviewStrip most needs while PreviewStrip lets segments fall to 5.99 px with no floor. (3) `node -e` on @mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 package.json: exports `./chip` → {"types":"./dist/chip.d.ts","import":"./dist/chip.js"}, shipping dist/components/chip/{Chip.vue.d.ts,chipVariants.d.ts,types.d.ts}; demo/ mints `.preview-chip` with an unrelated meaning. (4) demo/styles/foundation.css:462 `--phi-4: 2.618rem` unused while both chips hardcode the literal.
```

**Reproduction.** grep -rn "preview-chip" demo/ ; grep -rn "2\\.618" demo/ ; node -e "const p=require('./node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json'); console.log(p.version, JSON.stringify(p.exports['./chip']))"

**Proposed cure.** One primitive rooted in glass-ui — a specimen strip (a Chip variant or its sibling) owning the opaque well, the per-stop gutters, the forced-colors arm, the logical-direction elision cue and the phi^2 plate in one unit system. PreviewStrip, PreviewRamp and PaletteColorStrip collapse into three thin domain adapters over one law. That single move closes D-1, D-2, D-4, D-5, D-8 and D-13 at once — the tell that it is the right altitude.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (assume the design is flawed)` · D-8 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The truncation cue is a ~4.5 px alpha ramp inside a 6 px sliver, indistinguishable from a genuinely pale stop; it is a physical `90deg` mask inside a direction-aware flex layout; and it is the first thing erased by forced colors.

**Mechanism.** A colour-only, physical-direction, alpha-based signal used to carry a discrete semantic state (elision). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: states are never colour-only. §6.1: chrome and layout follow the document's logical inline direction.

**Evidence.**

```
PreviewStrip.vue:73-74 `mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, black 20%, transparent 95%)`. probes-D2/out/ring-occlusion.json: at the cap each segment is 5.988–6.016 px, so the fade runs ~1.2 px→5.7 px inside a 6 px sliver. On Pastel every stop already measures ≤1.474:1 against the row (probes-D2/out/contrast.log) so the cue is invisible by construction. Forced colors: `mask: "none"` (probes-D2/forced.mjs) — a 7-stop and a 12-stop palette become the same blank rectangle. RTL: reproduced by the earlier seat (frames-D/D7-rtl-mask-inverted.png) — with dir="rtl" honoured, segments run x 1197→1161 while the mask still fades rightward, i.e. inward; today reka-ui's hard dir="ltr" on SelectContent conceals it, so this surfaces the moment the obvious upstream RTL fix lands.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PreviewStrip/probes-D2/ring-occlusion.mjs (segW + lastMask per count); node probes-D2/forced.mjs (mask: none); prior seat: node probes-D/rtl-forced-rhythm.mjs (scenario rtl-forced)

**Proposed cure.** Delete the mask in favour of D-3's structural cue — a hairline tick per elided stop or an explicit numeral — which has no direction, no alpha, and survives forced colors.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue, area co` · D-9 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** One 10px gap token serves four semantic ranks; the rendered ink rhythm is 14 : 23 : 16 and it INVERTS the canon's title-gap / section-gap relation.

**Mechanism.** A single flex `gap` across three different font metrics (Fira 14.38/21.58, Fraunces 25.89/35.60, Fira 16.4/22.96) — half-leading differs per pair, so a uniform box gap cannot produce a uniform ink gap. Result: the eyebrow is optically bonded to the ornament (14px) and detached from the statement it labels (23px).

**Evidence.**

```
gap-2.5 at EmptyState.vue:16 and :28 is the only vertical relation. Box gaps measured exactly 10px between all four children (D2-probe5.mjs offsets from plate top: trio 32-76, eyebrow 86-107.58, headline 117.58-153.17, hint 163.17-186.14). Per-row ink scan of probes/probeD-inkscan.png (DPR 1, 462x218, threshold dLuma>18): bands (32,75)(90,100)(124,149)(166,181) -> rendered gaps 14px / 23px / 16px. Canon PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:68 requires distinct title vs section gaps; :73 requires the rendered relation to govern.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/D2-probe5.mjs (inkGeo block) then the PIL row-scan of probes/probeD-inkscan.png.

**Proposed cure.** Trim the line boxes so token == ink (`text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic` on the three text rows), then split into two tokens: --empty-title-gap (eyebrow->statement, tight) and --empty-section-gap (mark->eyebrow, statement->action, phi larger).

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue, area co` · D-10 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** `max-w-[26ch]` on the Fraunces display line is 46% looser than authored, because `ch` samples the display serif's lining figure rather than its average glyph.

**Mechanism.** `ch` is font-relative and is being used as a character-count proxy in a proportional display face where `0` is 46% wider than the mean advance.

**Evidence.**

```
EmptyState.vue:20 and :58. Computed at 1440: font-size 25.888px, max-width 469.474px -> Fraunces ch = 18.06px = 0.698em. Rendered average advance: "No saved palettes yet." = 22 chars in 272.84px = 12.40px/char. 469.474/12.40 = ~38 characters permitted against an authored 26. The two Fira Code rows are exact (36ch->363.32px at 10.09px/ch; 44ch->444.06px) because they are monospace. Side effect: the hint's honest 36ch measure (363px) is NARROWER than the headline's nominal 26ch (469px).
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/D2-empty-probe.mjs — kids[].maxWidth and kids[].w for the headline row on #/admin/users at 1440.

**Proposed cure.** Author display measures in `em` of their own face or as a token (--measure-display: 22em); retain `ch` only on the monospace rows.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-4 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The P019 paired-clamp law is not implemented. The identity and the headline scale on two different bases — a `vw` clamp vs a `cqi` expression times a runtime JS factor — so a fixed ratio is structurally impossible. Measured ratio drifts 0.729 → 0.975 and is 0.975 at the desktop reference viewport, a +24.0% error against the required 1/√φ.

**Mechanism.** F2 — two scaling bases: identity on vw, headline on cqi times a JS factor

**Evidence.**

```
Identity: ColorSpaceSelector.vue:209 `font-size: var(--type-display-2)` = clamp(2.058rem, 1.5rem + 2.2vw, 3.33rem) — viewport-driven. Headline: demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/ColorComponentDisplay.vue:136-139 `font-size: calc(min(var(--type-display-4), max(11.65cqi, 2.618rem)) * var(--readout-fit, 1))` — container-driven times a JS factor. Measured (probe-D.mjs; 1/√φ = 0.786151): 1440x900 → 53.280/54.646 = 0.9750 (+24.0%); 720x450 → 39.840/54.646 = 0.7290 (-7.3%); 390x844 → 32.928/41.888 = 0.7861 (exact); 320x700 → 0.7861 (exact). The law holds at the floor arm only, because 2.058rem/2.618rem happens to equal 1/√φ. Confirmed stable across five colour spaces at 1440: Lab, OKLCh, ProPhoto RGB, Hex, Kelvin all report ratio=0.9750 err=24.0%. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:62 "BI P019 supplies a paired clamp whose complete rendered ratio is 1/√φ; independently clamped display-2/display-3 tokens and a local approximation are forbidden"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:46 (PR-02) "`Lab` competes typographically with numeric specimen → TIGHTEN". Visual confirmation: ../../visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png — "Lab" and "92.0%, 88.8, 20.0" read as the same optical weight, and the Fraunces italic is heavier in colour than the Fira numerals so optically the label wins.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ColorSpaceSelector/probe-D.mjs — compare `triggers[].fontSize` against `headlineCandidates[0].fs` per arm. PR-02's TIGHTEN was never delivered; only the T-51 one-rung step-down (:200-208) landed, and it moved the wrong arm.

**Proposed cure.** One clamp, one base. Either both arms consume `cqi` from the same container, or the producer ships the P019 paired token and both arms consume it. Two independent clamps cannot be patched into agreement — the ratio must resolve from a single source through floor, fluid arm and ceiling, exactly as §3.2 specifies.

VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1 verbatim: 'Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence.' §2: 'One surface has one tier.' LIGHT: statement rgb(28,25,23) on rgb(242,93,163) = 5.72:1 PASS; detail rgb(86,84,83) @16.4px = 2.46:1 FAIL(4.5); glyph rgb(219,36,36) = 1.60:1 FAIL(3.0). DARK: statement rgb(233,230,226) = 2.46:1 FAIL; detail rgb(221,218,216) = 2.20:1 FAIL; glyph rgb(235,71,71) = 1.24:1 FAIL. Backdrop is rgb(242,93,163) in BOTH schemes — the ambient field does not darken (evidence/EB12-cured-dark-1440.png). Source: ErrorBoundary.vue:12-14 and :79-86 offer the token name as the evidence; useAtmosphereBoot.ts:85 certifies --ink-muted 'floor-clamped against the live resting plate'; EmptyState.vue:50-53 records the static token it replaced at 3.84:1.

**Defect.** The plate is a fork of `EmptyState`'s `error` variant rather than a use of it. The next contrast or type cure applied to the shared atom will silently miss the one surface that appears when everything has gone wrong. Owner edict 3 (KISS, no contrivance); PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §3 ('Multiple instances sharing one cause share one family row plus an exhaustive site list').

```
gap 10px→12px (EmptyState.vue:16 `gap-2.5` vs ErrorBoundary.vue:18 `gap-3`); block padding 32px→40px (`py-8` vs `py-10`); glyph 24px→28px (:19 `w-6 h-6` vs :23 `w-7 h-7`); statement measure 26ch→28ch (:20 vs :24); detail measure 44ch→46ch (:23 vs :27); `.plate-ink` rule identical (EmptyState.vue:102-104 == ErrorBoundary.vue:84-86). EmptyState.vue:98-100 declares itself 'the ONE shared empty atom (8 consumers incl. the admin walls), so every consumer inherits the cure'; its props at :72-91 already expose variant/message/detail/#action.
```

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-7 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Focus is programmatically thrown to an unnamed 1408x804 container instead of the recovery button; the resulting focus ring encloses 87% of the viewport, and in the shipped state it does not paint at all because it is occluded by the same canvas as D-1. The container also fires an assertive alert AND moves focus into itself, racing the two announcements, and exposes no accessible name and zero headings.

**Mechanism.** F2 — announcement and focus are aimed at the container rather than the verb. `role="alert"` already implies aria-live=assertive + aria-atomic=true, so the explicit aria-live at :20 is redundant; the real defect is doing both announce and move. Under D-3 this fires again on every failed retry. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: 'Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency.'

**Evidence.**

```
evidence/EB-measurements.json → EB1.state.activeElement = {tag:'div', cls:'vj-error-boundary …', outline:'auto 3px rgb(28,25,23)', boxShadow:'none'}; boundaryRect {w:1408, h:804}. Ring visible as a full-band rectangle in evidence/EB8-cure-test-position-relative.png, EB12, EB10 — and absent in the shipped EB1. evidence/EB-probe3.json → mobile.a11y: {role:'alert', ariaLive:'assertive', ariaLabel:null, ariaLabelledby:null, tabindex:'-1', headingsInside:0, isActive:true, tabbables:['button:Try again']}. Caught document headingCount 0 (EB1) vs healthy 1 (EB6). REPORT.md h1 column is 0 across all 60 captures. Source: ErrorBoundary.vue:19-21, :62-64.
```

**Proposed cure.** Announce through the `role="alert"` region and move focus to the named recovery button, which carries its own accessible name and the producer-owned `focus-ring` recipe. Drop `aria-live`, drop `tabindex="-1"`, drop the container `focus()`. Give the failure statement a heading level so it has an entry point.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-D

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-7 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** MT-F023 confirmed — the three scroll-timeline animations are structurally unreachable by the global PRM guard. ADOPTED, but the proposed cure is measurably worse for the cohort it protects, and the real structural fix is D-16.

**Mechanism.** duplicate-choreography — a scroll-driven animation has animation-duration:auto, so animations.css:184-190 (which overrides only animation-duration / animation-iteration-count / transition-duration) cannot reach it

**Evidence.**

```
Reproduced both engines under reducedMotion:reduce — shipped: webkit title matrix(0.310808,..), veil 1, desc 0; chromium matrix(0.618029,..), veil 1, desc 0. Naive cure (all three declarations inside @media prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) pins the PRM user at the veil's WEAKEST state: webkit/chromium naiveCure veil=0.52. Leak under exactly that condition is worse on every metric, both engines: webkit mean 18.993->23.911, pctOver8 14.73->15.59, pctOver24 14.12->14.34; chromium mean 21.245->26.439, pctOver24 16.99->17.89. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 says reduced motion resolves to the FINAL state, not rest. PaneHeader.vue:149-151's defence ('a scroll SCRUB ... needs no PRM gate', 'under PRM the rest state is byte-identical') is falsified — the rest state is never reached.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-occlusion-prm-fc.mjs; naive-cure baseline via the same A/B differencing with reducedMotion:'reduce' and `animation: none !important; animation-timeline: auto !important` injected on the three selectors, veil asserted at 0.52 before differencing

**Proposed cure.** Keep the root's disposition (STRUCTURE not gate, L-8) and strengthen it. Wrapping the three declarations in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) is still a scroll-timeline fork, merely a gated one, and it trades a legibility floor for stillness. D-16 dissolves MT-F023 entirely: both sibling implementations drive condense from a discrete state attribute through TRANSITIONS, which the global guard DOES reach (transition-duration: 0.01ms !important), and the producer belt-and-braces with its own `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { transition: none }` in card-scroll.css. Nothing is gated, overridden or patched — the defect ceases to exist. If the jury stages the work, the interim gate must be the no-preference wrapper PLUS a static `--pane-veil-rest: 1` under reduce, never the wrapper alone.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The "one golden plate (φ² ≈ 2.618rem)" proportion is φ² at NO viewport the app ships. `inline-size: 2.618rem` is root-relative and viewport-invariant; `block-size: 1em` is font-relative and rides the fluid text-dropdown rung, so the plate's aspect ratio is a function of viewport width.

**Mechanism.** unit-family mismatch — a ratio asserted across two different length bases (rem vs em) so it holds only where root font-size equals inherited font-size, which never happens at this site

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/color-chips/PreviewRamp.vue:43-44 (`inline-size: 2.618rem; /* one golden plate — φ² × 1em (F7) */` + `block-size: 1em`). Measured live on /#/mix with the Color-space menu open: desktop-1440 lane 16.4px → 41.875×16.391px, aspect 2.5548 (−2.41% vs φ²=2.6180339887); mobile-390 lane 14px → 41.875×14.000px, aspect 2.9911 (+14.25%); mobile-320 identical (+14.25%); zoom-200 lane 14.6px → 41.88×14.59px, aspect 2.869 (+9.6%). Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73 §5.8 "Real rendered relation wins over token intent … token presence alone cannot close a row."
```

**Reproduction.** node /tmp/pr_live7.mjs  (navigates http://localhost:9000/#/mix at 1440/390/320, opens the Color-space Select, injects a span carrying PreviewRamp's exact declarations into each option's description lane, reads getBoundingClientRect) → the three-row table above. node /tmp/pr_states.mjs supplies the zoom-200 row.

**Proposed cure.** One sized axis, one unit family: `block-size: 1em; aspect-ratio: 2.618;` (or `inline-size: calc(1em * 2.618)`). The ratio then holds by construction at every clamp arm and cannot drift when the type rung is retuned.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-6 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The inset hairline ring fails its own stated job by ≈2.4×. `inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 12%, transparent)` composites to 1.281:1 (light, over a white chip stop) and 1.231:1 (dark, over a black chip stop) — against a 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor. Against the light menu surface the ring reads 1.114:1 while the white chip it is meant to rescue reads 1.150:1: the exact failure the docstring claims to have solved is the failure that ships.

**Mechanism.** contrast by token-faith — an alpha chosen for aesthetic quietness and asserted to perform a boundary job, never measured against either neighbour it must separate

**Evidence.**

```
PreviewRamp.vue:46-48 and :10-12 claim the ring makes "light chips survive light glass, dark chips dark glass, and designed color out-ranks accidental bleed-through (F8)". Live tokens: --foreground = light-dark(hsl(24 10% 10%), hsl(30 14% 90%)) → rgb(28,25,23) / rgb(233,230,226); ringShadow light `oklab(0.216128 0.00350075 0.00518669 / 0.12)`, dark `oklab(0.925196 0.00238398 0.00574207 / 0.12)`; menuBg light `oklab(0.955857 0.0095643 0.0296614 / 0.7488)`. Computed (WCAG 2.x relative luminance): LIGHT ring over white chip = ring px [228,227,227], contrast 1.281:1; DARK ring over black chip = ring px [28,28,27], contrast 1.231:1; LIGHT white chip vs menu surface 1.150:1; LIGHT ring vs menu surface 1.114:1.
```

**Reproduction.** node /tmp/pr_live6.mjs for the live token/computed values, then `node -e` with the WCAG relative-luminance formula compositing 12% --foreground over the extreme chip stop and over the menu surface → the four ratios above.

**Proposed cure.** A single-tone 12% ring cannot bound an arbitrary colour against arbitrary translucent glass; the problem is scheme-symmetric so the answer must be. Draw a two-tone hairline — an inner --background-derived stroke and an outer --foreground-derived stroke, each at the alpha that clears 3:1 against its own neighbour — which is the construction glass-ui already ships on .watercolor-swatch (`inset 0 0 6px …background 35%…, inset 0 -2px 4px …foreground 6%…, 0 2px 6px …foreground 10%…`). One ring, both schemes, no per-scheme override.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design interrogation of `demo/shared/ui/EmptyS` · D-9 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** One flat `gap-2.5` serves four semantic ranks, so the rendered ink rhythm is ragged and there is no title-gap / section-gap distinction at all.

**Mechanism.** a single spacing token applied across elements with different line-heights yields three different rendered intervals — flat authored rhythm, ragged rendered rhythm

**Evidence.**

```
EmptyState.vue:16,28 apply `gap-2.5` (measured row-gap 10px) between every sibling. Measured line boxes: eyebrow 14.384/21.576, headline 25.888/35.596, hint 16.40/22.96 → half-leadings 3.596 / 4.854 / 3.280. Rendered ink gaps: mark→eyebrow 13.60px, eyebrow→headline 18.45px, headline→hint 18.13px. The decoration is bound 26% more tightly to the label than the label is to the statement, and the two most distinct joints get indistinguishable intervals. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:68 §5.3 "Header→headline uses title gap; headline→next semantic section uses section gap"; :73 §5.8 "Real rendered relation wins over token intent."
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; measure the four children's getBoundingClientRect y/height and computed font-size/line-height.

**Proposed cure.** Two named gaps from the glass-ui ladder: title gap (label→statement) and section gap (statement→action), with half-leading compensated so the RENDERED ink intervals — not the box gaps — carry the rank.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design interrogation of `demo/shared/ui/EmptyS` · D-10 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Nothing about the plate is container-scaled, and the type pair's ratio drifts 19.5% across the viewport range because one arm is fluid and the other is frozen.

**Mechanism.** mixed scaling law — fixed Tailwind rungs for space and ornament, a fluid token for one type arm and a fixed token for the other

**Evidence.**

```
Measured 1440px vs 320px on the same host: padding-block 32px → 32px (0%), row-gap 10px → 10px (0%), trio width 116px → 116px (0%), eyebrow font-size 14.384px → 12.032px (−16.4%, `text-mono-caption` is fluid), headline font-size 25.888px → 25.888px (0%, `text-heading` is fixed). Headline:eyebrow ratio 1.800 → 2.152 = +19.5% drift. At 320px the 116px mark occupies 45.7% of the 254px plate. Laws: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:33 §3.7 "Spacing is container-scaled from glass-ui tokens"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:15 requires a paired clamp holding the ratio "through floor, fluid arm and ceiling rather than only at endpoints". Frame: probes/state-320-admintags.png.
```

**Reproduction.** Playwright viewport 320x900 → http://localhost:9000/#/admin/tags; compare computed padding/gap/font-size against 1440x900.

**Proposed cure.** Container-scale padding and gap from the glass-ui ladder, and put the caption/headline on one paired clamp so the ratio is invariant across floor, fluid arm and ceiling.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design interrogation of `demo/shared/ui/EmptyS` · D-11 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The 26ch/36ch/44ch measures are font-relative across three families, so the authored ladder does not render — and the headline's measure is inert on every plate the component currently occupies.

**Mechanism.** `ch` is font-relative; mixing it across three families and sizes makes the authored numbers non-comparable and the display line's constraint accidentally inert

**Evidence.**

```
Measured resolved `max-inline-size`: headline (Fraunces 25.888px, `max-w-[26ch]`) = 469.474px; error detail (Fira 16.4px, `max-w-[44ch]`) = 444.062px; hint (Fira 16.4px, `max-w-[36ch]`) = 363.323px. Plate width is 462px on /#/palettes, /#/browse and all five admin plates — so the headline's 469.474px clamp NEVER engages, while the two support clamps do. Above a 469.5px container it silently switches on. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:218 mandates "Each Admin route uses the full main width", which would cross that threshold. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73 §5.8 "token presence alone cannot close a row."
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; `getComputedStyle(headlineP).maxInlineSize` = "469.474px" while the plate rect width = 462px.

**Proposed cure.** Express all three measures in one shared measure token (or one font's ch), so the authored ladder is the rendered ladder and the crossover threshold is chosen rather than accidental.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `<body>` is simultaneously the Vue mount container and the teleport/portal host — two roles collapsed onto one element, so the app root and every portal escape hatch are siblings with no intervening app container.

**Mechanism.** role collapse on one DOM node — mount container conflated with portal host

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-picker/index.html:214 → `<body class="relative" id="app" data-paper-field></body>`. Live probe at http://localhost:9000/#/ returned `{"appIsBody": true, "appTagName": "BODY", "appLayoutParent": "BODY#app", "bodyChildCount": 5, "bodyChildren": ["DIV","DIV.app-layout","SPAN","DIV","DIV"]}` — `.app-layout` is one of five body children; the other four are teleported overlay hosts. `app.mount()` clears `container.innerHTML`, so the mount also owns body's initial children.
```

**Reproduction.** Playwright evaluate on the live dev server: `document.querySelector('#app') === document.body` → true.

**Proposed cure.** Keep `data-paper-field` on `<body>` (it correctly must dominate the body-portaled dialogs — index.html:203-213 documents this) and give Vue its own container: `<body data-paper-field><div id="app" class="relative"></div></body>`, with `#app { position: relative; min-height: 100dvh }` in demo/styles/shell.css (the sheet that already owns `.app-layout` at :19). Only expressible once L-1's main.ts exists, because today the mount call lives inside the HTML that declares the body.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-3 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `vite.config.ts` imports an application feature composable four levels deep; `ground.ts` carries two disjoint lifetimes (browser runtime contract + node build-time HTML transform) in one module, so a build-only function ships to the browser and the build depends on app internals.

**Mechanism.** two execution lifetimes in one module → inverted build→app-internals dependency

**Evidence.**

```
vite.config.ts:15 → `import { injectGroundTokens } from "./demo/color-picker/composables/boot/ground";`. ground.ts (146 lines) splits as: runtime = GROUND_STORE_KEY/GROUND_RECORD_VERSION/GROUND_STOP_COUNT/FIRST_VISIT_GROUND/normalizeGroundStops/buildGroundRecord (consumer boot/useAtmosphere.ts); build-only = injectGroundTokens :131-146 (sole consumer vite.config.ts:150-155). Live resource probe on /#/ lists `composables/boot/ground.ts` in the browser's eager module set — a node-only string-replace function in the runtime graph. `ls plugins/` → vite-defer-glass-fonts.ts, vite-source-export.ts (the correct home already exists; no new directory needed).
```

**Reproduction.** vite.config.ts:15 pulls a demo/ app module into the node build graph; the live `performance.getEntriesByType('resource')` probe shows the reverse edge shipping ground.ts (with injectGroundTokens) to the browser.

**Proposed cure.** Split by lifetime, not feature: demo/shell/boot/ground.contract.ts (constants + buildGroundRecord + normalizeGroundStops, browser only) and plugins/vite-ground-tokens.ts (a `Plugin` exporting `groundRecordInject()`, node only, importing the contract). vite.config.ts then imports from plugins/ like its two siblings and the edge reverses to build → contract, which is legal.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-3 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The boundary is a terminal, unreportable sink: `return false` suppresses Vue's own logError, the app installs no error handler of any kind, and the async failure class is structurally uncatchable.

**Mechanism.** three responsibilities (containment / presentation / reporting) collapsed into one file, two of which then have no home at all

**Evidence.**

```
ErrorBoundary.vue:68 `return false`. node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js:238-239 — `if (errorCapturedHooks[i](...) === false) { return; }` — early return skips logError at :256 (the 'Unhandled error during execution of…' warn + rethrow-in-dev). `grep -rn "errorHandler|onErrorCaptured|unhandledrejection|window.onerror" demo/ src/` returns 4 matches, ALL inside ErrorBoundary.vue. demo/color-picker/index.html:205-213 is the whole boot: createApp/use(router)/mount — no app.config.errorHandler. Probe P4: on catch `w.emitted()` deep-equals {} — no event, no callback, no reporter. Probe P5: a raw promise/setTimeout escape never reaches the hook. The visual audit's one console error (audit/visual/REPORT.md §consoleErrors: 'safari-desktop-light /#/: WebGL: context lost.') is exactly this uncatchable class.
```

**Reproduction.** `npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/probes/vitest.config.ts` — P4 asserts no console.error/console.warn carries the thrown message and w.emitted() === {}; P5 asserts an async throw leaves the boundary unfired and the pane rendering 'fine'.

**Proposed cure.** Split reporting out to the boot directory whose actual job it is: demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useErrorReporting.ts installs app.config.errorHandler + window.onerror + unhandledrejection — ONE place that knows how a failure is recorded, and it covers the async half a boundary structurally cannot. The boundary emits `caught: [err: unknown, info: string]` and stops owning the decision.

The consequence is a RED oracle at HEAD.

**Evidence.**

```
THREE PRODUCERS: (1) sample.ts:39-41 `serializeStop` = colorToCss(stop,"oklch") + `.replace(/ \/ 1\)$/, ")")`; (2) generate-color.ts:235-243 `generatedCss` = mapColorToGamut → serializeCssColor, measured live as "oklch(88.673398030922% 0.060467090141 33.371415752918deg)"; (3) aurora-harmony-stops.ts:26-28,38 = local `fmt` (`v.toFixed(4).replace(/\.?0+$/,"")`) + template literal, library serializer BYPASSED. Numerically identical, textually never equal. Origin: `git log -S "serializeCssColor(mapped.value)"` → a68ecdc1 "feat(demo)!: v4 consumer migration".
```

**Reproduction.** VJS_E2E_PORT=9000 npx playwright test --project=smoke e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts --reporter=list (output pasted above). Live three-leg comparison: node scratchpad/PSL-probe2.mjs → o20WouldPass:false, plus the strip's painted segments vs stamp.

**Proposed cure.** One branded `PaintableStop = string & {__brand}` minted by ONE adapter (`demo/color-session/stops.ts`, toPaintableStop(color): PaintableStop | null). Every producer routes through it; generate-color's three throws and aurora-harmony-stops' `fmt` delete. The chip types on `readonly PaintableStop[]` so a raw string[] cannot reach it, and the oracle compares PARSED colors (parseCssColor both sides, ≤1e-9 per channel) — form-independent, which also retires o14's hand-written parseOklchTriples regex (a fourth re-derivation of the serializer grammar). NOTE: the o20 RED itself is already filed at registry/DEFECT-LEDGER.md:4480, 20007, 20990 by the wb-generate-controls seat; NEW here is the three-producer census and the library-structure mechanism.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L2-8 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** All ten panes are bare `defineAsyncComponent` calls with no errorComponent, no onError and no retry policy, so the chunk-404 class (a stale index.html after a gh-pages redeploy) lands in this generic boundary. Measured: Retry does re-invoke the loader but cannot recover, and the only affordance that would work — a page reload — is not offered.

**Mechanism.** A generic boundary cannot distinguish 'this render is broken' from 'this build is stale', because the discriminating information lives in the async loader it does not own. So it offers one affordance for two classes and it is wrong for one of them — and it shows the user machine truth for the wrong machine ('Failed to fetch dynamically imported module'). NOTE, recorded honestly: I predicted defineAsyncComponent memoisation would make Retry a no-op; measured, attempts went 1→2, so the loader IS re-invoked. The prediction was wrong; the defect is not.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:69-78 — ten one-argument defineAsyncComponent calls (AboutPane, PalettesPane, BrowsePane, ExtractPane, GeneratePane, GradientPane, MixPane, AdminPane, AuroraPane, BlobPane); `grep -rn defineAsyncComponent demo/` shows no options-object form anywhere. gh-pages build config: vite.config.ts `base: "./"` with hashed chunk names. Probe R2-B: {"probe":"R2-B","caught_on_load_failure":true,"detail_shown":true,"loader_attempts_after_retry":2,"still_announced_after_retry":true,"pane_present_after_retry":false,"text_after_retry":"This panel hit an unexpected error.Failed to fetch dynamically imported module Try again"}.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ErrorBoundary/probes-L-r2/vitest.config.ts  (probe R2-B, prints the JSON above)

**Proposed cure.** The load-failure class goes home to the loader: defineAsyncComponent({ loader, onError: (err, retry, fail, attempts) => attempts <= 2 ? retry() : fail(), errorComponent: PaneLoadFailed }) where PaneLoadFailed offers RELOAD. Ten call sites collapse to one factory in usePaneRouter.ts, which already owns the registry table. The boundary is then left with the one class it can genuinely own — a synchronous render throw.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure beneath `demo/color-session/` · L-16 · CHALLENGE-L

The subject component branches its entire display policy on the copy, and the drift is structurally invisible to `npm run typecheck`.

**Mechanism.** The library owns the union as a TYPE and hides it as a VALUE, exporting no classifier. A `new Set<T>([...])` literal is checked for element assignability, never for coverage, so the consumer's hand-copy can silently fall behind the type it is annotated with. This is the root shared by L-1 (four catalogs) and L-2 (five precision rules): every consumer materialises its own copy of a fact the library declines to publish.

Drift proof: `npx tsc --noEmit --ignoreConfig --strict --target ES2022 --moduleResolution bundler --module ESNext scratchpad/exh/probe.ts` → `tsc exit code: 0` with a 14th member added to the type and the Set literal left short.

Fold it into the library-side space registry as `SPACES[s].cssSerializable` (see L-1 cure step 1). `grammar.ts:290` reads the registry; the demo has nothing to copy; and because the registry is a mapped type over `SpaceId`, the exhaustiveness the Set literal provably lacks is enforced at the library build.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure beneath `demo/color-session/` · L-3 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Out-of-gamut, non-parseable CSS ships to screen as the component's user-facing statement of "your color, in this space". The gamut decision has no home; `specimenFor` never makes one.

**Mechanism.** `serializePickerColor` (`picker-color.ts:206-211`) forwards any `CssColor` to `serializeCssColor` regardless of domain, and the component performs no projection, so the mathematically-correct-but-physically-impossible conversion is presented as valid CSS. Projection is a per-callsite choice with no owner, and this callsite never made one.

**Evidence.**

```
Live DOM rows at the default `lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)`: `rgb(385.302835934518 …)` (r > 255); `hsl(346.045357898758deg -1295.152156124318% 103.662622110611% / 82.7%)` (s = −1295 %); `hwb(… 56.226092874351% -51.09915134687%)` (b < 0); `color(srgb-linear 2.580409706575 …)`. `picker-color.ts:195` already exports `clampPickerColor` and `:119` `mapPickerOklabToSrgb` wraps the library's `mapColorToGamut`; neither is on this path — `ColorSpaceSelector.vue:158-161` goes `convertPickerColor` → `serializePickerColor` with no projection step.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/, click the color-space title, read any CSS-native row. Captured verbatim in the 18-row dump from `node scratchpad/repro.mjs`.

**Proposed cure.** The `formatColor` cure of L-2 takes gamut as part of its contract — project through `mapColorToGamut` before serializing, or emit the space's own valid range. One home for "how a color is shown", covering precision AND domain, since they are the same decision.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure under demo/shared/ui/EmptySt` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The published `@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0` declares `@mkbabb/glass-ui@^7.0.0` and `@mkbabb/keyframes.js@^6.0.0` as RUNTIME dependencies, while glass-ui declares `@mkbabb/value.js@^4.0.0` as a peerDependency — a package-level cycle, and the exact cycle eslint rule inv-K-1 exists to forbid, declared in the one file inv-K-1 does not police. The published graph imports neither; every downstream consumer of a parse/convert library installs 5.8 MB of Vue design system.

**Mechanism.** the demo lives inside the library's own package manifest, so demo-only dependencies are indistinguishable from library dependencies; the invariant is enforced on the import graph (eslint) but not on the manifest, and the manifest is what npm resolves.

**Evidence.**

```

```

**Reproduction.** `npm pack` then inspect: files:["dist"] ships nothing importing either package, yet `npm i @mkbabb/value.js` in a fresh tree installs glass-ui + keyframes.js (5.8 MB) and creates a resolution cycle back to value.js via glass-ui's peer. Verified statically by the four measurements above rather than by a live install.

**Proposed cure.** Immediate: move both entries to `devDependencies` — nothing in the published graph resolves them, `files:["dist"]` ships nothing that needs them, and the generated self-alias set (vite.config.ts:38-51) is untouched. Structural (preferred): make `demo/` a private workspace package with its own manifest, so the demo's dependency set cannot leak into the library's published one by construction — the same class of guarantee the repo already chose for the exports-derived alias set.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-6 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The "switch color space" operation has no home. The canonical pipeline command `updateToColorSpace` has exactly one caller — a watcher inside ColorPicker.vue. This component instead emits a state-write that each of its two hosts reinvents differently; the actual conversion is a side effect of the picker's watcher, so the About-side selector converts the color only because the Picker happens to be mounted.

**Mechanism.** a command modelled as a state-change-plus-watcher, with the effect owned by one of two peer hosts instead of by the domain — no unique home for the operation

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts:170-173 defines updateToColorSpace. `grep -rn "updateToColorSpace" demo/` returns exactly 4 lines: the definition (:170), the return key (:324), the destructure (ColorPicker.vue:214) and the sole call site (ColorPicker.vue:352, inside `watch(() => model.value.selectedColorSpace, …)` at :348-354). Two divergent host writes: ColorPicker.vue:43 `updateModel({ selectedColorSpace: colorSpace })` vs AboutPane.vue:24 `model = { ...model, selectedColorSpace: colorSpace }`. Shared single pipeline: App.vue:257 `provide(COLOR_MODEL_KEY, pipeline)`. Panes are KeepAlive'd: demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120. Target architecture that breaks the coupling: ARCHITECTURE.md:41 "About is a quiet trailing destination, not Picker's permanent right-hand companion" with /about a first-class route.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE for the picker-free break — labelled HYPOTHESIS: I did not stand up a picker-free /about route, so the failure is predicted from the call graph. All call-graph facts above are verified greps.

**Proposed cure.** The component calls the pipeline operation directly — colorModel.updateToColorSpace(space) — and stops emitting a state-write for hosts to reinvent. Both host handlers die; ColorPicker's watcher at :348-354 dies. One command, one home, zero host-specific write mechanics.

**Mechanism.** an unbounded ambient renderer with no user-facing lifecycle seam; the overture DAG exposes beats to START motion and nothing to stop it

Measured sustained rAF rate over t=8.5s->14.6s (probe-overture.mjs, instrumented requestAnimationFrame, two concurrent loops so ~2x frame rate): desktop-1440-light 261.0/s (raf 2024@8565ms -> 3590@14576ms); desktop-1440-dark 284.0/s (2304@8112ms -> 4008@14117ms); mobile-390 259.5/s (2193@8624ms -> 3750@14631ms). No control exists: `grep -rniE "animation-play-state|pauseAnim|\"pause\"|'pause'|isPaused" demo/` → no output. App.vue:285-289 mounts the atmosphere renderer and App.vue:9-17 owns its canvas, so the control has no other home. (The reduced-motion arm IS satisfied — rafPer1500ms=0 under reducedMotion:reduce, STATES.json — but an OS preference is not the persistent, announced, remembered control §6 demands.)

### `DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D) — demo/color-picker/App.vue, the app sh` · D-9 · DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** App.vue's boot contract is split across a file it does not own and duplicated in two languages. It mounts onto `<body>` as a three-root fragment, depends on three host attributes declared in index.html (one of which is provably dead), makes the canon's required static boot-error region structurally impossible to preserve, and re-runs the prepaint script's URL/storage/default precedence a second time in TypeScript — which §6.2 forbids in those words.

**Mechanism.** split root ownership — the component's own root contract (positioning ancestor, material attribute, boot precedence) lives in the entry HTML, so it is untyped, untestable, invisible to the component, and duplicated

**Evidence.**

```
Measured (probe-app-D.mjs, all three matrices): mountHostIsBody=true, appLayoutParent="body", bodyAttrs=`class="relative" id="app" data-paper-field="" data-v-app=""`, groundState=null. The mount is demo/color-picker/index.html:205-213 (MT-F012's P0 inline module) ending `app.mount("#app")`, and `#app` IS `<body>` (index.html:226). App.vue is a 3-root fragment: div.app-layout (:2), comment nodes (:144-149), MigratePalettesDialog (:152). (1) `class="relative"` is DEAD: the atmosphere canvas (App.vue:9-17, `absolute inset-0`) is a descendant of `.app-layout` (App.vue:2) which is already `position: relative` (shell.css:25), so the nearest positioned ancestor is never `<body>` — a legacy positioning ancestor, owner edict 2. (2) `data-paper-field` is glass-ui's field contract governing App.vue's own descendants incl. portalled dialogs (index.html:222-226) yet is declared where App.vue cannot see it. (3) Mount replaces the host's children, so `<body>` can hold no `<noscript>` and no pre-rendered fallback — while VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:168 requires "A static semantic boot-error region already present in HTML becomes visible through that data state"; measured groundState=null confirms the whole §6.2 latch (data-ground-state / -schema / -store) is unimplemented. (4) index.html:180-200 runs URL/storage/default precedence in vanilla JS writing --saved-bg-0..N; App.vue:231 `resolveHydratedBootModel()` runs URL->storage->default AGAIN in TypeScript (boot/hydrate.ts:53-78) — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:172: "The hydrated model consumes the frozen boot object ...; it does not repeat scheme/URL/storage precedence, reconstruct an initial palette in TypeScript, or repaint a second 'equivalent' ground."
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/probe-app-D.mjs  → every row: mountHostIsBody true, appLayoutParent "body", bodyAttrs 'class="relative" id="app" data-paper-field=""', groundState null. Then read index.html:205-213 (mount), :222-226 (data-paper-field rationale), :180-200 (prepaint precedence) against boot/hydrate.ts:53-78 (the second precedence engine).

**Proposed cure.** Take MT-F012's cure and finish it. Move the 8 lines to main.ts referenced via `src=`, with `<div id="app">` as the host. Then: `.app-layout` becomes the app's own root and already declares position:relative, so `class="relative"` is DELETED not moved; `data-paper-field` moves onto `.app-layout` — the element App.vue owns and documents; `<body>` regains the right to carry §6.2's static boot-error region and a `<noscript>`; and main.ts becomes the single reader of the frozen `window.__VALUE_GROUND_BOOT__`, handing it to `createApp(App, { boot })` so App.vue CONSUMES the boot object as §6.2 requires and `resolveHydratedBootModel`'s duplicate precedence engine is deleted outright rather than kept in sync. Necessary but insufficient: it does not fix the 3-root fragment, D-2, D-3 or D-4.

### `design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system ` · D-4 · design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)

**Defect.** The header never contracts. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.5 requires 'title, padding, and band all take the compact token step'; measured, only the title's OPTICS step and the band, padding and description wrapper are byte-identical rest vs stuck on 30/30 captures. The vacated space becomes dead reserved acreage — 58-79% of the stuck content box is empty.

**Mechanism.** Optical-not-layout contraction. The shrink is a compositor `transform` on a box that keeps its size, so nothing reflows. The component chose compositor purity (correctly killing the F3 layout-animating fork at :152-155) over §3.5, and never recorded the trade — contraction IS layout.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured on 2 engines x 3 matrices x 5 routes: band height 88.66/88.69 desktop and 68.97/68.98 phone, IDENTICAL rest->stuck (delta 0.00px); padding-top 16px and padding-bottom 8px unchanged; descWrapH 18.69px retained at opacity 0. At full stuck desktop: content box 64.66px, visible title ink 13.67px (webkit) -> 50.99px = 79% empty; chromium 27.18px -> 37.51px = 58% empty. Visible in shots/chromium-forcedcolors-light-STUCK.png as a white void between title and first content row. This is the PROPORTION-AUDIT §2/§4 PR-01 mechanism ('Both vertical reservations must die') on 9 unregistered sites; also §5.3 and §5.8.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-paneheader-design.mjs — compare rest.headerH/headerPadTop/descWrapH to stuck.* on every row.

**Proposed cure.** Transpose from a continuous scrub to a TWO-STATE DISCRETE STEP — which is what §3.5 literally asks for ('the compact token STEP'). One `data-stuck` boundary detected once per crossing (a zero-height IntersectionObserver sentinel today; @container scroll-state(stuck: top) when both engines ship it), driving a single tokenized transition over padding-block, font-size, and the desc wrapper's grid-template-rows: 1fr -> 0fr. Layout runs once per crossing, not per frame, so the dead F3 fork does not return. This dissolves D-4 (band and desc actually collapse), D-8 (one clock, one token, zero magic ranges) and D-5 (no transform survives, so there is no origin to mirror).

### `design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system ` · D-7 · design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)

**Defect.** MT-F023 (PRM scrub unreachable by the global guard) is ADOPTED and independently reproduced — but its proposed cure is REJECTED as written, because I measured that it leaves the prefers-reduced-motion user pinned at the veil's WEAKEST state (0.52) and makes the content leak strictly worse on both engines.

**Mechanism.** Material-cannot-occlude, PRM arm. The blunt guard at demo/styles/animations.css:184-190 overrides only animation-duration / animation-iteration-count / transition-duration; a scroll-driven animation has animation-duration:auto, so it is structurally unreachable — MT-F023 is right about that. But the naive structural cure conflates a MATERIAL ramp (the veil's opacity, which translates and scales nothing) with MOTION (the title scale and desc translateY), and so trades a legibility floor for stillness for exactly the cohort the guard exists to protect.

**Evidence.**

```
Reproduced: `PRM webkit shipped={"title":"matrix(0.310808,...)","veil":"1","desc":"0"}` and `PRM chromium shipped={"title":"matrix(0.618029,...)","veil":"1","desc":"0"}` under reducedMotion:"reduce" — the scrub runs in full. Naive cure simulated (all three declarations gated to no-preference): `naiveCure={"title":"none","veil":"0.52","desc":"1"}` on both engines. Leak measured under exactly that condition vs the shipped terminal state: webkit meanChannelDelta 18.993 -> 23.911, pctOver24 14.12 -> 14.34; chromium 21.245 -> 26.439, pctOver24 16.99 -> 17.89. Strictly worse on every metric, both engines. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 says 'Reduced motion resolves directly to the FINAL geometry and stable chromatic state' — final, not rest.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-occlusion-prm-fc.mjs (PRM lines) and node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-naive-cure-leak.mjs (NAIVE-CURE-LEAK lines).

**Proposed cure.** AMENDED cure, in the root's own idiom (structure, not another override stacked on the blunt guard): (1) gate ONLY the two transform channels — pane-title-shrink and pane-desc-shrink's translateY — inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), matching the existing idiom at animations.css:43; (2) do NOT gate the veil's opacity ramp — under PRM the veil resolves to its STUCK value, which is the 'final ... stable chromatic state' §6 names, not its rest value; (3) preferred: once D-3's cure lands, the stuck veil is static opaque material rather than an animation, so there is nothing for the guard to reach and PRM is satisfied by construction. Also fix the false headline comment at animations.css:178 ('Neutralises CSS keyframe animations and transitions app-wide').

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (AdminUsersPanel.vue, area pale` · C-23 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** NEW. A request that never answers leaves the prune control terminally spinning: `pruning` is set true at :295 and cleared only by onPruneDone, which only runs after the awaited port call settles — and there is no AbortController, AbortSignal or timeout anywhere in demo/. The identical shape strands loadingUserPalettes and the disclosure skeletons.

**Mechanism.** work started with no bounded termination (mechanism C) — an unbounded promise is the sole clearing path for a UI flag

**Evidence.**

```
AdminUsersPanel.vue:295,304,359-364; usePalettePorts.ts:121-124; demo/platform/transport/client.ts:67-92 (fetch(input, init) with no signal, inside a retry loop). `grep -rn "AbortController\|AbortSignal" demo/ | wc -l` → 0. probe/aup-probe4.mjs H1: `t+1000ms {"disabled":true,"spinner":true}` / `t+5000ms …true` / `t+10000ms …true`.
```

**Reproduction.** node probe/aup-probe4.mjs chromium H1 — route POST /admin/users/prune-empty to never fulfil; the button spins, disabled, indefinitely; only a reload recovers.

**Proposed cure.** Put the deadline in the transport once: give fetchWithRateLimitRetry an AbortSignal.timeout(ms) composed with any caller signal, so all ~30 API wrappers inherit a bounded wait and ApiProblem/ApiUnavailableError become reachable on a hang. The panel then derives `pruning` from the port's in-flight state instead of hand-toggling it at two call sites — the same move C-1's keyed-resource cure already needs. A per-component setTimeout watchdog would be the contrivance.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (AdminUsersPanel.vue, area pale` · C-25 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** NEW. The app ships a working Idempotency-Key replay store (server middleware mounted globally, covering /admin/*; both transport helpers forward the header) and uses it on palette saves — while EVERY admin destructive verb (prune-empty, deleteUser, deleteUserPalettes, deletePaletteAdmin, featurePalette) sends un-keyed mutations. C-15's double-fire therefore reaches the server as two genuinely distinct prunes, not one replayed request.

**Mechanism.** one concern (mutation replay safety) with two contradictory implementations in one directory — the server-side half of mechanism C, already built and simply not called

**Evidence.**

```
api/src/app.ts:69-73 (`app.use("*", idempotency)`); api/src/platform/http/idempotency.ts:93-99 (opt-in per header); demo/platform/transport/client.ts:112-114 and :145-147 (header forwarded). `grep -rn "idempotencyKey" demo/palettes/api/` → only palettes.ts:80,145,161 (crypto.randomUUID()); `grep -rln idempotencyKey demo/palettes/api/admin-*.ts | wc -l` → 0. demo/palettes/api/admin-users.ts:69-71 is the un-keyed prune.
```

**Reproduction.** The greps above are exact. The consequence is measured by node probe/aup-probe4.mjs chromium H2 (two distinct POSTs from one gesture). Rider, source-derived and labelled: the replay key scopes on `c.var.sessionToken ?? c.var.userSlug ?? "anon"` (idempotency.ts:108), which a Bearer-authenticated admin may collapse to "anon" — I did not run the server.

**Proposed cure.** Two lines per admin mutation — { method: "POST", idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID() } — using the header, helper and middleware that already ship; add the admin identity to the server's scope key. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The edit target is identified by array index, and the same composable re-indexes that array on removal — so committing an edit after removing an earlier swatch writes past the end and APPENDS a phantom duplicate colour; the edit overlay also silently vanishes, stranding the user in edit mode with no commit/cancel affordance on desktop.

**Mechanism.** ordinal identity carried across a mutation that redefines the ordinals; both halves of the invariant live in one file and neither enforces it

**Evidence.**

```
useSwatchActions.ts:76-83 emits `colorIndex: index`; :90-94 `filter((_, i) => i !== index)` shifts every later index. Consumer usePaletteActions.ts:99-107: `oldCss = savedColorStrings[colorIndex]` (undefined) → passes the `oldCss === newCss` bail → `updated[colorIndex] = newCss` grows the array. LIVE (cpe-probe7.mjs): `0 savedColors: ["lab(50% 20 -30)","lab(70% -40 10)","lab(30% 5 60)"]` → `1 after startEdit(2) — overlays: 1` → `3 after remove(0) — swatches: 2 savedColors: ["lab(70% -40 10)","lab(30% 5 60)"] overlays: 0` → `4 after Enter-commit — swatches: 3 savedColors: ["lab(70% -40 10)","lab(30% 5 60)","lab(30% 5 60)"]`, `4 count label: 3 colors`.
```

**Reproduction.** 1440x900 /#/palettes with 3 seeded colours: hover swatch index 2 → Edit; hover swatch index 0 → Remove; press Enter (ColorPicker.vue:377 global keydown → :258 commitEdit). savedColors gains a duplicate third entry, persisted.

**Proposed cure.** Identify the edit target by identity, not ordinal — mint a per-entry id where the buffer is minted (useColorPipeline.savedColors) and key edits on it; resolve any index at the moment of mutation only. Minimum hardening if the ordinal stays: `commitColorEdit` bails when `colorIndex >= savedColorStrings.length`, and the emit that re-indexes the array clears the pending edit target.

```
useSwatchActions.ts:42-59. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (bugs, races, cleanup, reactivi` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

```

Component sites PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:35-36; host BrowsePane.vue:50 (`v-for="i in SKELETON_COUNT"`, :207 SKELETON_COUNT=4) and :130 (2 more on load-more). Interacting host defect: BrowsePane.vue:47 puts `aria-label="Loading palettes"` on a bare `<div>` (role=generic), for which ARIA 1.2 prohibits aria-label — the name is dropped. The file's own header (:29-31) claims the status role exists precisely so the wait is announced.
```

**Reproduction.** node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/PCS-probe6.mjs — PRE-SWAP block prints statusTextContent and ariaHiddenChildren.

**Proposed cure.** One live region per wait, owned by the host list, carrying real text; the ghost plates become pure decoration. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation audit (pass 2) of demo/palettes` · C2-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The Export items write attacker-controlled markup to the user's disk, and fail silently at the empty-collection boundary. `exportAsSVG` interpolates `c.css` and `palette.name` raw into SVG attributes and text.

**Mechanism.** string-concatenation markup generation with no escaping, plus a catch-all console.warn that turns every failure into silence while an unused ActionFeedback channel sits on the same card

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/export.ts:63-80 (`fill="${c.css}"`, `>${palette.name}<`); silent swallow at demo/palettes/usePaletteExport.ts:22-24 `catch (e) { console.warn("Export failed:", e); }`. API accepts anything: api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:28 `css: z.string().min(1).max(200)` — no colour grammar. LIVE probe pcm-p2-i.mjs downloaded `ampersand-tag-quote.svg` containing `<rect … fill="#00ddaa" onload="alert(1)" />` and an unescaped `&`/`<tag>` in the text node. Empty palette: `::EMPTY_png {"downloads":[],"newWarnings":["Export failed: Error: Failed to create PNG blob at …/export.ts:83:13"]}`; `::EMPTY_svg` downloaded a `width="0"` file.
```

**Reproduction.** Seed a local palette named `Ampersand & <tag> "quote"` with a colour `#00ddaa" onload="alert(1)`; open its card menu → Export → SVG Swatch. The downloaded SVG contains the injected `onload` handler. Then Export → PNG Swatch: nothing downloads, only `console.warn`. Separately, seed a palette with `colors: []` and Export → PNG Swatch: nothing downloads. Reachable from another user's data because the public API stores any ≤200-char string as a colour.

**Proposed cure.** Build the SVG with `document.createElementNS` + `setAttribute` instead of template concatenation — unbreakable by construction and no more code. Guard `colors.length === 0` before offering the raster/vector items. Route every `catch` in `usePaletteExport` into the card's existing `showFeedback(msg, "error")` (already exposed at PaletteCard.vue:244) so a failed export is a state, not silence.

**Defect.** `isPublic = palette.visibility !== "private"` collapses a 3-state enum: an `unlisted` palette renders byte-identically to a public one and is offered an action that destroys the middle state with no path back.

```

**Reproduction.** Serve the dev server over its LAN host (non-loopback ⇒ detectDevMisconfig false ⇒ requests are really issued), seed localStorage["palette-user-slug"]="probeuser", and page.route() the browse feed to return owned remote palettes with visibility public/unlisted/private/undefined. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (AdminFlaggedPanel.` · F-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Delete does not clear the flag queue. The admin delete soft-deletes the palette and never cascades its flags, and the flagged aggregation's $lookup has no deletedAt filter, so the row survives server-side AND rejoins fully populated. The panel meanwhile splices the row out locally and decrements total, so the moderator is told the opposite of the truth. Server-side `total` (countDistinctPalettes over flags) is unchanged by a delete, so the client counter also drifts permanently.

**Mechanism.** M-B: optimistic local mutation without server truth, compounded by a missing backend cascade

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:93-103; api/src/modules/admin/service/palettes.ts:53-79 (no flags touched; module docstring L6 claims 'delete palette + cascade votes/flags'); api/src/modules/palette/repository/flag.ts:88-95 ($lookup on slug, no deletedAt filter); api/src/modules/palette/repository/flag.ts:117-129 (countDistinctPalettes)
```

**Reproduction.** EXECUTED (repro/flagged-composable.test.ts, C6): `C6 after delete → items = 0 | total = 0` then `C6 after refresh → items = 1 | total = 1`. The 'looks alive' half is EXECUTED in repro/probe-flagged.mjs: the soft-deleted p2 joins with `palette={"name":"SoftDeleted","colors":[{"css":"#000"}],…}`.

**Proposed cure.** Client: await the mutation then reload from the server (never splice-and-decrement). Backend (relay to the API owner): call flags.deleteByPaletteSlug(slug) inside deletePalette's existing withTransaction — the repository method already exists — and filter deletedAt in the flagged $lookup so the queue means what it says.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (AdminFlaggedPanel.` · F-6 · CHALLENGE-C

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (PalettesPane, pass` · C-8 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** One malformed colour string in the store tears down the entire pane on card expand, and it is a CLASS not an instance — `oklch()`, `color()`, `lab()` and `rgb()` (any empty-argument functional form) each collapse the subtree into ErrorBoundary, contributing ZERO additional console or page-error signal.

**Evidence.**

```
PPC-probe7.mjs, one fresh browser context per row: `CONTROL_valid before=1 after=1 grid=true boundary=false pageErr=0 consoleErr=1` / `oklch_empty before=1 after=0 grid=false boundary=true pageErr=0 consoleErr=1` / `color_empty … boundary=true` / `lab_empty … boundary=true` / `rgb_empty … boundary=true` / `zero_colors … boundary=false`. consoleErr=1 on the CONTROL too (pre-existing dev-API error), so the crash adds no signal. Ingress: demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts onSaveRemote → usePaletteStore.ts:121-151 addPublishedPalette spreads an unvalidated server row; the serializer at usePaletteStore.ts:23-31 validates only `typeof parsed.version === "number"`.
```

**Reproduction.** Set localStorage["color-palettes"] to a store whose single palette has colors [{css:"lab()"}], load /#/palettes, click the card. `.palette-card-grid` becomes null and the body reads "This panel hit an unexpected error."

**Proposed cure.** Validate once at the serializer `read()` — the one honest choke point for every store ingress — so `PaletteStore` is a real type rather than a cast (shape + per-colour `CSS.supports("color", css)`), and route `addPublishedPalette` through the same validator. Then wrap the CARD, not the pane, in the ErrorBoundary the repo already owns so one bad palette costs one row.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (pass 3) on demo/pa` · C3-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The K-INV5 'small-caps register' — named three times in this file's own comments and implemented as two inline `style="font-variant: small-caps"` attributes — is INERT. The sibling `text-mono-caption` utility applies `text-transform: uppercase`, which consumes the lowercase letters before small capitals can be synthesised from them, so the declaration cannot have any effect.

**Mechanism.** two mutually exclusive answers to the same design question (`text-transform: uppercase` vs `font-variant-caps: small-caps`) applied to the same element; CSS Text 3 runs the transform before CSS Fonts 4 synthesises small caps, so the later declaration is applied-and-inert

**Evidence.**

```
Measured on the SHIPPED span (evidence/pass-3/pcm-p3-b.mjs, real owned-remote menu via LAN host + stubbed feed): `::B1_realAnnotation widths {asShipped_smallCapsPlusUppercase: 55.266, smallCapsRemoved_uppercaseKept: 55.266, uppercaseRemoved_smallCapsKept: 39.094, bothRemoved: 55.266}`, `smallCapsIsInert: true`. Synthetic control: `withUppercaseUtility ON 64.469 / OFF 64.469 (delta 0)`, `withoutUppercaseUtility ON 59.266 / OFF 83.391 (delta 24.125)`. Utility source: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/utilities.css `@utility text-mono-caption { ... text-transform: uppercase; }`. Component: PaletteCardMenu.vue:35-39 and :56-59; comments at :24-26 and :42-47. Corroborated by the AX name `"Make private PUBLIC"` (::B3_axMenuItems).
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/evidence/pass-3/pcm-p3-b.mjs with PROBE_HOST set to the LAN host. Or in any page that loads the demo stylesheet: append `<span class="fira-code text-mono-caption" style="font-variant: small-caps">offline</span>` and the same span without the inline style, and compare getBoundingClientRect().width — identical.

**Proposed cure.** Define the register once in glass-ui as a named utility (`@utility text-annotation`) that uses `font-variant-caps: small-caps` and NOT `text-transform: uppercase`, and consume it as a single class at both call sites. That deletes both inline `style=` attributes (curing C2-12), gives C2-9's `aria-hidden` one place to live, and makes the register a real named thing. If the owner in fact wants uppercase, delete both inline declarations and every comment that names a small-caps register — because uppercase is what ships.
