```

**Reproduction.** `npx vitest run --config <probe cfg>` on a mount of ActionFeedback via a host replicating PaletteCard's wiring: showFeedback('Saved!','success'); advanceTimersByTime(2400); showFeedback('Delete failed','error'); advanceTimersByTime(100) → visible === false. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/palettes/b` · C-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `useHoverPopover.onHover` reads `e.currentTarget` inside a `nextTick` callback, after the event handler has returned and the DOM has reset it to null. **Proposed cure.** Capture `const el = e.currentTarget as Element` inside the synchronous handler body and close over the local — the cast then reflects reality. Moot if C-2 is cured by adopting the reka-ui `Popover`, which positions itself and makes `positionPanel` deletable.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/palettes/b` · C-7 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `defineExpose({ showFeedback })` forces both consumers to maintain a component-instance map, and both register it with `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[key] = el)"`. demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:244 `defineExpose({ showFeedback })` · BrowsePane.vue:94 and PalettesPane.vue:84 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)"` · BrowsePane.vue:209 / PalettesPane.vue:177 `reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})` · growth drivers: BrowsePane.vue:140 `pm.loadMoreRemotePalettes()` paging, plus filter/sort re-keys

**Reproduction.** NONE — code-level certainty rather than an executed measurement (the shared dev browser in this formation had a concurrent writer, so a live key count would not have been attributable). The omission is unambiguous: Vue invokes function refs with `null` on unmount and the guard drops that call.

**Proposed cure.** Architectural transposition, not a delete-key fix: make feedback DATA. ```
demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:89 (v-model), :216-224 (try/finally, no catch), :217 (`colorText.value.trim()`). My compile: `SearchFilterBar.vue(89,46): error TS2322: Type 'string | number' is not assignable to type 'string'.` Declaration: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/input/Input.vue.d.ts — `"update:modelValue": (value: string | number) => any`.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/palettes/br` · P4-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `<DropdownMenu>` (:2) never passes `:modal="false"`, so reka's `modal: true` default makes the entire document inert while a per-row card menu is open. One omitted prop produces five measured symptoms — including the mechanism of P4-1 — and the scroll lock it applies does not lock the actual scroll container.

**Mechanism.** A library default chosen for singleton menus applied unexamined to the only menu rendered once per list row. The modal barrier's stated job (make outside content inert, lock scroll) is simultaneously over-applied (it disables every sibling control on the page, which is what stops the covered triggers absorbing their own clicks) and under-delivered (it writes `overflow: hidden` to `<body>` while the real scroller is an inner div that still scrolls 200 px).

**Evidence.**

```
reka default: node_modules/reka-ui/dist/DropdownMenu/DropdownMenuRoot.js:26-30 `modal: { type: Boolean, required: false, default: true }`. Prop exists and is forwarded: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenu.vue.d.ts `modal?: boolean` in `DropdownMenuBaseProps`, doc-comment "Whether opening the menu makes outside content inert", runtime default `modal: boolean`. `$ grep -rn ":modal" demo --include="*.vue"` → no output. Consumers: `$ grep -rn "DropdownMenu" demo --include="*.vue" -l` → PaletteCardMenu.vue, UserSortMenu.vue, MobileMenuDropdown.vue, ProfileSection.vue (the other three are dock/filter singletons). Symptoms — probe pcm-p4-a.mjs `::A1_afterOpenCard0 {bodyPointerEvents "none", bodyOverflow "hidden"}`; probe pcm-p4-b.mjs `::B0_hitTestUnderLock {topMost "div", triggerIsTopMost false, triggerComputedPE "none", bodyPE "none"}`; `::B4_scrollUnderLock {window {before 0, after 0, moved false}, inner {before 0, after 200, moved true, cls "glass-resting card rounded-card text-card-foreground scrollb…"}, bodyOverflowInline "hidden"}`; `::B2_crossCardSequence` click1 lastClickTarget path ["div{menuitem}","div{menu}","div"] menuCount 0, click2 menuCount 1 owner "Probe Palette 1", click3 menuCount 0 target ["html"], `::B3_clicksToMoveMenu {opened true, clicksNeeded 3}`.
```

**Reproduction.** `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCardMenu/evidence/pass-4/pcm-p4-b.mjs` — see `::B0_hitTestUnderLock`, `::B4_scrollUnderLock`, `::B2_crossCardSequence`. Manually: open any card's menu, then click a different card's `⋯` — it takes three clicks to move the menu, and the first one activates an item on the card you are leaving.

**Proposed cure.** `:modal="false"` on PaletteCardMenu.vue:2. If a modal barrier is genuinely wanted for the dock singletons, make it a glass-ui `DropdownMenu` default that per-row consumers override — the shipped truth is that no consumer has made the choice deliberately, because none of the four names the prop. This one edit also gives the APG `Tab` behaviour for free (P4-5), removes the ineffective body scroll lock (C2-15), and converts P4-1's cross-row gesture into the ordinary dismiss-then-open.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/palettes/br` · P4-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Two menu items render the identical visible label `Publish` and the identical `Globe` icon while emitting different actions into different host emits: `:33` emits `'publish'` (mint a new remote palette from a local one) and `:52-55` emits `'makePublic'` (flip an existing remote's visibility). Same word, same glyph, different API call.

**Mechanism.** One English verb reused for two different state transitions across two `v-if` branches four lines apart, with no discriminating icon and no discriminating accessible name — the same untyped `action: [action: string]` channel (`:225`) that C2-1 showed the `if (!fn) return` dispatcher (PaletteCard.vue:316) will silently swallow.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteCardMenu.vue:27-40 (`v-if="paletteKind === 'saved'"`, `<Globe/>`, text `Publish`, `@click="$emit('action','publish')"`) vs :48-60 (`v-if="paletteKind === 'remote' && isOwned"`, `<component :is="isPublic ? EyeOff : Globe"/>`, text `{{ isPublic ? "Make private" : "Publish" }}`, `@click="$emit('action', isPublic ? 'makePrivate' : 'makePublic')"`). Host divergence: PaletteCard.vue:295 `publish: () => emit("publish", props.palette)` vs PaletteCard.vue:302 `makePublic: () => emit("setVisibility", props.palette, "public")`. Name is the only AT discriminator because the menu inherits the trigger's name (pass-3 C3-2: `"Palette menu"` x6, `ariaLabelledby: "reka-dropdown-menu-trigger-…"`). Test-locator exposure: the repo's idiom is `getByRole("menuitem", { name: … })` — e2e/smoke/flows/palette-delete.spec.ts:48 uses the anchored `/^Delete$/` precisely because this menu's names are ambiguous; neither Publish branch is covered by any spec.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — source-level, verified by reading both branches at HEAD e39da983 and both host handlers. Reachable at runtime whenever a remote+owned palette has `visibility === "private"`; the /#/browse route needs a configured API, so I did not drive it live.

**Proposed cure.** Name the operations for what they do. The saved item becomes `Publish to the commons…`; the remote flip becomes `Make public` / `Make private`, which is what `isPublic ? EyeOff : Globe` already implies. The label then carries the transition and the K-INV5 annotation (:56-59) carries the current state — the same `state display + transition` shape C2-5 and C3-5 independently converge on. Replace `action: [action: string]` with a string-literal union so the two verbs cannot be confused at the emit either.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/palettes/Pa` · D-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `cardRefs` retains unmounted PaletteCard instances forever and grows without bound.

**Mechanism.** A short-circuit guard written for truthiness swallows the framework's own release signal; each retained value is a component public-instance proxy holding $el, setupState, the effect scope and the useLiquidPress/useHoverPopover closures.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:84 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.id] = el)"` — the `el &&` guard discards Vue's unmount call. Vue calls function refs with null on unmount: node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js:1763 `const value = isUnmount ? null : refValue;` then `if (shared.isFunction(ref)) callWithErrorHandling(ref, owner, 12, [value, refs])`. Measured (filter to nothing): `A. after mount, 6 seeded: {n:6, cards:6}` → `B. search 'zzzznomatch': {n:6, cards:0}`. Measured (unboundedness, 5 churn rounds of deleteAll+create-2-with-fresh-UUIDs, only 2 cards ever rendered): n = 2 → 4 → 6 → 8 → 10 → 12.
```

**Reproduction.** Seed 2 palettes, open /#/palettes, then repeatedly call the port's `onDeleteAllSaved()` and `createPalette(...)` (fresh crypto.randomUUID ids). Read `Object.keys(cardRefs).length` off the PalettesPane instance between rounds: it rises 2,4,6,8,10,12 while `.palette-card-grid > [role=article]` stays at 2. Released only by page reload.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the map — it is contrivance. The pane needs at most one card's feedback at a time: move the feedback state into `usePaletteActions` as `feedbackFor: Ref<{id,message,variant}|null>` and have PaletteCard render ActionFeedback from a prop. Data down, no instance reaching. That one move also deletes D-5, the `defineExpose({showFeedback})` and two `any` casts. If a map must survive, the guard must be `(el) => { if (el) cardRefs[id] = el; else delete cardRefs[id]; }`.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/palettes/Pa` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** A publish whose result lands after its card unmounts is silently lost — and the result is written into a retained dead instance, because the leak makes the `if (card)` guard always pass.

**Mechanism.** Unguarded post-await imperative reach into a child instance, compounded by D-4: the leak keeps `cardRefs[id]` truthy so the code takes the 'delivered' branch and writes to a corpse; the card that remounts is a fresh instance with feedbackVisible=false.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:199-209 — nothing revalidates mount state after `await pm.onPublish(palette)`. Measured with a control (port onPublish replaced by a 1200ms one modelling a real round trip, everything else shipped code): `CONTROL (card mounted, +1.6s): ["Published!"]` — chip renders; `RACE in-flight state: {"retained":true,"isUnmounted":true}`; `RACE chips after remount (+0.5s): []` — nothing, ever.

**Reproduction.** Seed 2 palettes; open /#/palettes; invoke the pane's onPublish on the first palette; while the request is in flight set `pm.searchQuery.value = 'zzzznomatch'` (unmounting the card); wait for resolution; clear the search. No feedback chip ever appears, for success or failure.

Reachability: api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:111-118 — an owner listing their OWN userSlug receives every visibility, unlisted included (non-owners are forced to `public`); api/src/platform/migrations/check.ts:53-60 asserts every doc carries one of the three. Truth table: visibility="unlisted" ⟹ isPublic=true ⟹ label "Make private", annotation "public", emit makePrivate — all three wrong.
```

**Reproduction.** NOT EXECUTED — recipe (the current dev server is dev:web-only, so the latch short-circuits every request before it leaves the page; see C-2): 1) `npm run dev` (full local stack via scripts/dev.sh up), sign in. 2) create a palette, then PATCH /palettes/:slug with {"visibility":"unlisted"} (api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts accepts the enum). 3) open /#/browse filtered to your own userSlug and open that card's ⋯ menu. 4) observe the item reads "Make private" with annotation `public`. An isolated @vue/test-utils mount was attempted (scratchpad pcm-mount.test.ts + pcm.vitest.config.ts, run via npx vitest run --config …): the suite runs but reka's DropdownMenuPortal/Presence renders nothing under this repo's jsdom even with ResizeObserver/DOMRect/matchMedia polyfills — document.body.textContent is empty for every case. That negative is itself recorded (see C-4).

**Proposed cure.** Minimum: `const isPublic = computed(() => palette.visibility === "public");` — the canonical predicate, matching format.ts:86 and isActivePublic. Gestalt cure: stop modelling a ternary as a toggle. Annotate the ACTUAL value (public / unlisted / private) in the K-INV5 register and offer the transition that is missing, so the control is a state display plus transitions rather than a two-way flip that pretends the middle state does not exist — the API already treats all 9 (visibility, tier) tuples as legal resting states; the UI is the only layer that flattened it.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/palettes/brow` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The hex round-trip through the parent destroys hue AND saturation, and the thumb deserts the pointer. watch(currentHex) -> emit update:hex -> parent pickerHex -> :hex prop -> watch re-parse forms a closed loop through an 8-bit-per-channel hex, which is not injective for HSV. The `if (d === 0) return; // keep existing hue` guard catches only exact greys; near-black quantization garbage passes it and rewrites hue, and `sat.value = max === 0 ? 0 : d / max` has no guard at all.

**Mechanism.** non-injective lossy round-trip used as the render source of truth; no pointer-space raw coordinate cache (the stableHue/rawS-rawV family of cure)

**Evidence.**

```
MiniColorPicker.vue:107,110-125 (esp. :118 sat, :119 the half-guard) + SearchFilterBar.vue:175-178. Live, pointer held at x=60% and dragged straight down: `P6 after pointerdown at x=60% y=15%: thumbStyle "left: 59.9078%" hex #5798d9 hueVar "--hue: 210;"` then `P6 after drag to BOTTOM (still x=60%): thumbStyle "left: 50%" hex #010202 hueVar "--hue: 180;"` — thumb renders at 50% while the pointer is at 60%, and hue flips 210->180 with no hue interaction. Algebraic (verbatim transcription of :85-125): `worst |Δsat| over 4000 random states: 0.7916 = thumb x-jump of 79.16% of canvas width`; `val=0.005 hex=#000101 -> sat becomes 1.0000 (was 0.7500)`; `updateCanvas(val=0) -> emit #000000 -> after prop round-trip {hue:210,sat:0,val:0} SATURATION CLOBBERED: YES`. House cure named in comment at SpectrumCanvas.vue:58-63 ('Raw spectrum coords to avoid HSV roundtrip jitter').
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/browse -> ⋮ Filters -> swatch -> press at 60% width / 15% height of the SV field and drag straight down to the bottom edge; observe the thumb's computed `left` (50%) versus the pointer (60%) and `--hue` flipping 210 -> 180. Scripts: scratchpad/mcp-live.mjs (block P6) and scratchpad/mcp-math.mjs (blocks C-1, C-7, C-8).

**Proposed cure.** Adopt SpectrumCanvas's rawS/rawV discipline: hold pointer-space coordinates as the render source of truth and clear them only when the color changes from a non-canvas source. Falls out for free by consuming SpectrumCanvas rather than re-implementing it.

**Mechanism.** target sized by a bare Tailwind height utility with no minimum-target floor; clipping container inherited from a decorative rounded-full treatment while the thumb is centre-translated

**Evidence.**

```
MiniColorPicker.vue:26 (`h-3` = 12px, `overflow-hidden`), :10 (`overflow-hidden`), :18 and :33 (translate). Measured on both matrices: `P10 {"cls":"relative w-full h-3 mt-2 rounded-f","w":174,"h":12}` and `R4 mobile geometry: {"hueStrip":[174,12],"hueThumb":[16,16],"searchBtn":[53,24]}`. Clipping: `T1 CLIPPED left px: 7  clipped top px: 7 (overflow: hidden)` on a 16px thumb, `T2 thumb overhang past right edge: 6 px => visible half-width: 6 of 12`. Screenshot: evidence/mini-picker-edges.png. Counter-example in house: SpectrumCanvas.vue:234 sets `overflow: visible` explicitly. Coverage note: the visual matrix never sees this component (two popovers deep) — REPORT.md's `/#/browse` row of 4 small tap targets counts four other elements, and shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png shows the trigger closed on an error-state pane.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/browse -> ⋮ Filters -> swatch; measure getBoundingClientRect() on the hue rail (174x12 desktop and mobile). Drag the SV thumb past the top-left corner and the hue thumb past the right end, then compare thumb rect to container rect. Script: scratchpad/mcp-live5.mjs (T1/T2) and mcp-live3.mjs (R4).

**Proposed cure.** Replace the rail with the glass-ui Slider (which ships a >=24px hit area with a visually thinner track) and set overflow: visible on the SV plate as SpectrumCanvas does — i.e. the same transposition that cures C-1/C-2/C-3. Separately: extend the visual-audit STATES matrix to open the ⋮ Filters popover and the swatch, so this component enters the tap-target budget at all.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/palettes/brow` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The `hex?: string` prop contract is a lie and the divergence is never reported outward. The :111 guard silently discards anything that is not a >=7-char '#'-prefixed string, and parseInt's leniency accepts and mangles partial garbage; 8-digit alpha hex is truncated and the alpha destroyed on the echo; 3/4-digit hex and named/oklch colors are silently no-ops. Meanwhile the mount-time update:hex emission is measured NOT to reach the parent inside the reka popover, so the component can display one color while the parent believes another and never says so.

**Mechanism.** hand-rolled narrow parser + hand-rolled serializer standing in for the repo's own color pipeline, combined with an outward binding whose mount-time half is context-dependent on the Vue scheduler / reka Presence mount ordering

**Evidence.**

```
MiniColorPicker.vue:65-68 (prop type), :110-125 (guard + parse), :107 (outward watch). Algebraic, verbatim transcription: `in="#12345g" -> emit #123405` (parseInt("5g",16)===5), `in="#zzzzzz" -> state {hue:null,…} -> emit #000000`, `in=#3b82f680 (50% alpha) -> emit #3b82f6 (alpha gone)`, `in=#f00 -> state UNCHANGED -> emit #528fcc (parent asked for #f00)`, `in=rebeccapurple / oklch(0.7 0.15 210) -> state UNCHANGED`. Missing mount emission: `Q1 t=1200ms after outer open: {"colorText":"","swatchLabel":"Open color picker, current color #4488cc"}`, `Q2 mini open: {"hexLabel":"#4488cc","colorText":""}`, `S1.2 after flipping Tier=Featured (forced parent re-render), field shows: ""` — yet hexLabel #4488cc proves sat moved 0.6->0.6667 (currentHex(210,0.6,0.8)==="#528fcc"), so currentHex did change. The identical logic DOES emit at mount outside the popover on the app's own Vue: `R1 vue version: 3.5.35 / R1 after MOUNT — emissions: [["emit","#4488cc","#4488cc"]]`. The parent already imports the real parser at SearchFilterBar.vue:145 (parseColorIn) and advertises `placeholder="#hex, hsl(...)"` at :92.
```

**Reproduction.** Contract half is PROVEN algebraically against a verbatim transcription of :85-125 (scratchpad/mcp-math.mjs, blocks C-2..C-5) but is currently LATENT through SearchFilterBar, which only ever feeds the component its own 6-digit output (SearchFilterBar.vue:170,176,181). Missing-mount-emit half is PROVEN live: http://localhost:9000/#/browse -> ⋮ Filters -> read the 'Search by CSS color' field (empty) while the swatch reads #4488cc, then flip Tier=Featured to force a parent re-render — still empty (scratchpad/mcp-live2.mjs Q1/Q2, mcp-live4.mjs S1). Isolated control: scratchpad/mcp-live3.mjs block R1.

**Proposed cure.** Stop hand-rolling both directions. Parse with the repo's own parseColorIn (already imported by the parent at SearchFilterBar.vue:145, fronting parsePickerColor/convertPickerColor), hold the value as a PickerColor, and serialize to hex only at the readout. That deletes the 20-line inline HSV->hex switch (:85-105) and the 15-line inline hex->HSV block (:110-125), both duplicating src/units/color, and makes the prop accept what its type and the sibling field's placeholder already promise.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/palettes/brow` · C-7 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Duplicate create appends unconditionally, producing a duplicate pill with a duplicate v-for key inside one category group; and create re-sorts the whole list while load preserves server order, so creating one tag silently reorders every other tag.

**Mechanism.** Unreconciled transport boundary — append-by-position instead of reconcile-by-identity, plus two different orderings for one list.

**Evidence.**

```
useAdminTags.ts:75-77 (`tags.value = [...tags.value, tag].sort(...)`) vs :54 (load preserves server order); AdminTagsPanel.vue:93 (`:key="tag.name"`). Measured: seed [moody/mood, warm/temperature, cool/temperature], create moody/mood → {"tagNames":["moody","moody","cool","warm"],"mainText":"Tags … 4 tags\nMOOD\nmoody\nmoody\nTEMPERATURE\ncool\nwarm"} — note warm/cool also swapped.
```

**Reproduction.** scratchpad/tags-probe.mjs pass 2 (duplicate section) / tags-probe2.mjs section C: seed the three tags, then create a tag whose name already exists and have the stub echo it back.

**Proposed cure.** Reconcile by identity — `const next = new Map(tags.value.map(t => [t.name, t])); next.set(tag.name, tag);` — and apply the single ordering inside the groupedTags computed where it belongs, so load and create cannot disagree.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defectiveness of demo/palettes/` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Any input that is not exactly four lowercase hyphenated words is silently reclassified as an ADMIN TOKEN and emitted with isAdmin=true. The parent then executes `deps.clearUserSlug(); deps.adminLogin(value)` — i.e. a single typo in your own slug logs you out of your identity and stores junk as an admin credential, with no error and no confirmation.

**Mechanism.** binary negation used as a classifier — 'not shape A' is treated as 'therefore credential B', with no third (invalid) outcome and no confirmation before a destructive session mutation

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteSlugBar.vue:205 `const isAdmin = !looksLikeSlug(normalized);` → :213 `emit("switchSlug", isAdmin ? normalizeTokenInput(raw) : normalized, isAdmin)`. demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:51-57 `if (isAdmin) { deps.clearUserSlug(); deps.adminLogin(value); setActiveTab("saved"); return; }`. Measured (PROBE D, 6/6): 'azure-drifting-teal'→[…,true]; 'azure drifting teal fox'→[…,true]; 'azure-drifting-teal-fox-extra'→[…,true]; 'azure_drifting_teal_fox'→[…,true]; 'azure-drifting-teal-fox2'→[…,true]; 'azure--drifting-teal-fox'→[…,true].
```

**Reproduction.** PROBE D in probes/c3-slugbar.probe.test.ts (parameterised over the six near-miss strings).

**Proposed cure.** Three-way outcome: slug | adminToken | invalid. adminToken reachable only via the explicit `ADMIN_TOKEN=` sentinel normalizeTokenInput already parses, or a separate affordance; everything else is invalid and renders an error WITHOUT touching session state.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defectiveness of demo/palettes/` · C-26 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** NEW (pass 3). A rejection from the async parent handler escapes the component entirely and lands on the global error channel as an unhandledRejection plus a Vue warn — it is not merely undisplayed. `emit()` returns void, the component's try/catch has already completed synchronously, and Vue routes the listener's rejected promise to app.config.errorHandler (absent) → console noise on every failed login.

**Mechanism.** fire-and-forget emit across an async boundary — the event contract is synchronous while its only implementation is asynchronous, so failures cannot be caught locally and are promoted to global

**Evidence.**

```
PROBE B, parent listener `async () => { throw new Error("404 Slug not found") }`: `[B] rendered error text: null` · `[B] unhandled rejections captured: [ 'Error: 404 Slug not found' ]` · stderr `[Vue warn]: Unhandled error during execution of component event handler at <PaletteSlugBar …>`. Live listener is `async function onSlugSwitch` at demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:51.
```

**Reproduction.** PROBE B in probes/c3-slugbar.probe.test.ts.

**Proposed cure.** Make the contract honest about being async: either the parent owns pending/error state and the component becomes presentational (pending/error as props), or the event carries a completion handle `switchSlug: [slug, isAdmin, done: (err?) => void]`. Do NOT bolt a `.catch()` onto the emit site — that hides the failure one level lower.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defectiveness of demo/palettes/` · C-27 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** NEW (pass 3). Bounding proof for C-5: the predicate `looksLikeSlug` is a TOTAL SOUND ACCEPTOR of the real slug space — all 268,435,456 slugs the API can mint pass it, and no word list entry contains a hyphen or non-[a-z] char. Therefore the defect is exactly and only the unconditional negation at line 205, not the regex. Corollary defect: api/src/modules/session/slugWords.ts is now an undocumented load-bearing contract of the client parser — adding one hyphenated word would start silently logging users out.

**Mechanism.** cross-module shape coupling with no declared contract — a client-side regex silently encodes the server's generator grammar

**Evidence.**

```
api/src/modules/session/slugWords.ts:84-90 `return `${adj}-${verb}-${color}-${animal}``. Enumeration over the four parsed lists: `ADJECTIVES 128 / VERBS 128 / COLOR_TERMS 128 / ANIMALS 128`, `NON-[a-z]+ WORDS: none`, `slug space 268435456  looksLikeSlug failures 0`.
```

**Reproduction.** node script parsing the four const arrays out of slugWords.ts and cross-producting them against /^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-[a-z]+-[a-z]+$/ (transcript pasted in the report).

**Proposed cure.** Keep the predicate; replace the else-branch with an explicit `invalid` outcome (see C-5). Add a comment in slugWords.ts naming the client-side shape contract, or better, have the API expose the shape so the client stops guessing.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects · demo/palettes/browser` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `const isAdmin = !looksLikeSlug(normalized)` makes the ADMIN branch the catch-all: any input that is not exactly four lowercase hyphenated words is submitted as an admin token, and the parent's admin branch first destroys the user's persisted identity. `useAdminAuth.login()` performs no validation at all.

**Mechanism.** One text field asked to carry two disjoint credential types, disambiguated by a NEGATED shape test that reads 'unrecognisable' as 'privileged'. Latent in this component behind C-2; byte-identical and LIVE in SlugEditLayer.vue:25-27,39-66.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteSlugBar.vue:184-186, :205, :213. useSlugMigration.ts:51-57 `if (isAdmin) { deps.clearUserSlug(); deps.adminLogin(value); setActiveTab("saved"); return; }`. demo/platform/auth/useAdminAuth.ts:34-37 `function login(token){ adminToken.value = token; safeSetItem(localStorage, STORAGE_KEY, token); }` with `isAuthenticated = computed(() => !!adminToken.value)` — no server round-trip. Server slug shape api/src/modules/session/slugWords.ts:84-90 = `${adj}-${verb}-${color}-${animal}`, all words `[a-z]+` (node scan: the only non-[a-z]+ literals in the file are `node:crypto`, `./repository/user.js`, `findBySlug`, and an error string). LIVE repro through the byte-identical twin: `D · typo'd 3-word slug -> palette-admin-token: "brisk-leaping-azure" {"hasAdminPill":true,"snippet":"→ Palettes Tools admin @mbabb …"}`.
```

**Reproduction.** `node scratchpad/probe.mjs` step D — WebKit, http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, clear `palette-admin-token`, reload, click dock Login, type `brisk-leaping-azure` (a dropped-word typo of a real 4-word slug), press Enter, then read `localStorage.getItem("palette-admin-token")`.

**Proposed cure.** Make the admin route explicit and non-inferred (a distinct affordance, or the `ADMIN_TOKEN=` prefix as the ONLY admin trigger — see C-23), and reject anything that is neither with authored copy ("That doesn't look like a slug — four words, e.g. cool-blue-fox-jump"). NEVER clear the existing session before the new credential is accepted by the server.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects · demo/palettes/browser` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The slug input is never focused after opening edit mode: `nextTick` resolves ~0 ms after the flag flip while `<Transition mode="out-in">` holds the incoming branch for the full 200 ms leave, so `searchBarRef.value` is null and `?.` eats the focus call. There is no retry.

**Mechanism.** A time-based guess (setTimeout 50 ms) stacked on a lifecycle fact (Transition out-in completion). Two clocks, no handshake. Compounded by the Vue 3.4 string-ref idiom (`ref<InstanceType<typeof SearchBar>|null>(null)`) instead of `useTemplateRef` — edict 7; SlugEditLayer.vue:14 already uses useTemplateRef.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteSlugBar.vue:172-182 (`setTimeout(… , 50)` → `slugEditMode.value = true` → `nextTick(() => searchBarRef.value?.inputRef?.focus())`), :4 (`<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">`). demo/styles/animations.css:111-116 `.vj-morph-leave-active { transition: … var(--duration-fast) … }`; node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/scheme-motion.css:1 `--duration-fast: 0.2s`. Pass-1 live rAF timeline: `insertedAtMs: 276`, `document.activeElement` never becomes the input at any of 7 samples.
```

**Reproduction.** Structural + token-corroborated; pass-1 captured the live rAF timeline against a `/@fs/` mount of the unmodified SFC (preserved at challenge-C-implementation.run-1.md §C-3).

**Proposed cure.** Delete the timer and the guess entirely; focus from the transition's own `@after-enter` hook via `useTemplateRef("searchBarRef")`. Pair with C-20(c) so focus is both PLACED on open and RESTORED to the trigger on cancel.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects · demo/palettes/browser` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `slugSwitching` is set true and false inside one synchronous turn (`onSlugSwitch` is `async` with zero `await`), so Vue never flushes a render between them: the Loader2 spinner, the `aria-label="Signing in…"` in-flight name, and the `:disabled` double-submit guard are all unreachable states.

**Mechanism.** A loading flag wrapped around a FIRE-AND-FORGET emit — the real network work happens in the parent (`useSlugMigration.onSlugSwitch`, which IS async) and the child holds no handle on it. The declared `async` is vestigial.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteSlugBar.vue:198-225 — `slugSwitching.value = true` (201), `emit("switchSlug", …)` (213), `slugEditMode.value = false` (215), `finally { slugSwitching.value = false }` (223), with no `await` anywhere in the try. Dead consumers at :23 (`:disabled="!slugInput.trim() || slugSwitching"`), :24 (`:aria-label="slugSwitching ? 'Signing in…' : …"`), :26 (`<Loader2 v-if="slugSwitching">`). Pass-1 live measurement across 5 inputs: `slugSwitchingAfterSyncCall: false`, `spinnerRenderedAnyFrame: false` for every one.
```

**Reproduction.** Structural (statement order, no await in scope); pass-1 measured it 5× live via the dev instance handle (run-1.md §C-4).

**Proposed cure.** Make the port's `onSlugSwitch` return `Promise<void>` and `await` it here. One change repairs the spinner, the disabled guard, the error path (C-16) and the optimistic close (C-21). glass-ui `Button` also ships a first-class `loading` prop that this file hand-rolls.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects · demo/palettes/browser` · C-21 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The form closes optimistically: the credential is cleared and the field unmounted in the SAME synchronous turn as the emit, before the parent's async login resolves. Even with C-1 and C-2 cured, the error can never reach the field it describes, and every retry requires a full re-type.

**Mechanism.** Success-path-only sequencing: the view treats a fire-and-forget emit as a completed transaction. Distinct from C-4 (flag lifetime) and from C-14 (clearing) — this is what ORPHANS the error from its field rather than merely leaving it stale.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteSlugBar.vue:213-215 in order — `emit("switchSlug", …)`; `slugInput.value = ""`; `slugEditMode.value = false`. Parent resolves later: useSlugMigration.ts:74-88 (`await deps.userLogin(value)` … `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`). The error `<p>` at :124 renders OUTSIDE the `<Transition>`, which is exactly why it can paint in a mode where the input no longer exists. Observable end state measured live in C-1: `C · error text visible: []` with the field already closed.
```

**Reproduction.** Structural — derived from statement order at 213-215 against the async parent at useSlugMigration.ts:74-88. Live end-state captured by `node scratchpad/probe.mjs` step C.

**Proposed cure.** The same `await` as C-4. Close the field on SUCCESS only; preserve the typed value on failure so the retry is one keystroke, not a re-type. Move the error `<p>` inside the edit branch so it cannot outlive its field.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects · demo/palettes/browser` · C-20 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The account menu lies about its role, has no menu semantics, and never restores focus: `aria-haspopup="dialog"` contradicts the `role="group"` glass-ui actually renders (with no aria-label); the four commands are bare `<button>`s with no role=menu/menuitem and no arrow-key navigation; and every cancel path unmounts the focused element with no focus restoration.

**Mechanism.** A menu hand-rolled out of a generic disclosure primitive: the ARIA was authored by hand to describe a surface the primitive renders differently, and the keyboard contract a real menu primitive supplies for free was simply not implemented.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteSlugBar.vue:84 `aria-haspopup="dialog"`; :88 `<PopoverContent class="w-auto p-1 flex flex-col gap-0.5 z-popover" align="end" :side-offset="4">` — no aria-label. Vendor source node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/popover-BQGYXZyO.js: `"data-material":"overlay", "data-reveal":"menu", role: "group", "aria-label": t.ariaLabel`. Menu items are plain `<button>`s at :89-118. Focus: `@keydown.escape.stop="slugEditMode = false"` (:14) and the X button `@click="slugEditMode = false"` (:36) both remove the focused node via the v-if flip with no restore target. The dock's own equivalent uses DropdownMenu/DropdownMenuItem for the SAME four commands (ProfileSection.vue:53-90).
```

**Reproduction.** NONE for the focus-restoration leg — the component is unmounted (C-1), so it is structural: the focused node is removed by the v-if with no receiving element. The role contradiction is read directly off the vendor source plus lines 84/88.

**Proposed cure.** Replace the hand-rolled Popover-as-menu with glass-ui `<DropdownMenu>` + `<DropdownMenuItem>` (edict 4 — reuse the existing component-type name; the dock already does). Drop the hand-written `aria-haspopup` — the primitive sets its own — and get roving focus, typeahead, Escape and reka's `onCloseAutoFocus` restoration for free.

**Defect.** The async error is never announced and never associated with the field: the error <p> has no role=alert / aria-live, and the input carries no aria-describedby and no aria-invalid.

**Mechanism.** An async result rendered as static prose — the status-message contract was never wired.

Fails WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages) and 3.3.1 (Error Identification).
```

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects · demo/palettes/browser` · C-8 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The identity pill and the only copy explaining what a slug IS are unreachable by keyboard AND by touch: a non-focusable <span> behind `<Popover trigger="hover">`, which routes to reka-ui's HoverCard whose pointer handlers are excludeTouch-wrapped and whose trigger adds no tabindex.

**Mechanism.** A disclosure built on a non-interactive element: `cursor-help` promises an affordance the markup does not provide, and the chosen trigger mode is the one input modality the majority of the audited matrix (mobile Safari) cannot perform.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteSlugBar.vue:45-60. Measured against the live stylesheet: `"pill": { "w": 270.31, "h": 28.94 }, "spanTabIndex": -1`. glass-ui routing, dist/popover-BQGYXZyO.js: `let _ = … window.matchMedia("(pointer: coarse)").matches, v = i(() => n.trigger === "hover" && !_); E({ usesHoverRoot: v })`. reka-ui HoverCardTrigger.js: `props: { as: { default: "a" } } … onPointerenter: excludeTouch(rootContext.onOpen)($event), onPointerleave: excludeTouch(handleLeave)($event), onFocus: rootContext.onOpen(), onBlur: rootContext.onClose()` — no tabindex anywhere. So onFocus exists but the span can never receive focus, and touch is explicitly excluded.
```

**Reproduction.** `node scratchpad/probe2.mjs` — inject the exact markup from lines 47-52 into the live page inside `.app-layout`, read getBoundingClientRect and `.tabIndex`. Mechanism read directly from the two vendor sources above.

**Proposed cure.** The pill is a disclosure — make it one. A real <button> (or the span with tabindex="0" + role="button") behind glass-ui Tooltip/Popover with a trigger mode that accepts focus. Reuse the existing component-type name (edict 4) rather than hand-rolling.

node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts: `export interface ButtonProps extends PrimitiveProps { emphasis?: ButtonEmphasis; tone?: Tone; size?: ButtonSize; iconOnly?: boolean; loading?: boolean; type?: …; disabled?: …; class?: … }` — no `variant`. Live fallthrough on a mounted sibling (`node scratchpad/probe.mjs` step A): `A · [variant] fallthrough: { "count": 2, "sample": ["BUTTON variant=outline class=button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash …", "BUTTON variant=ghost class=button …"], "emphasisAttrs": 0 }`. **Reproduction.** `node scratchpad/probe.mjs` step A against http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit`; `npx eslint demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue`.

**Proposed cure.** `emphasis="quiet"` (ghost's successor rung) and `loading` instead of the hand-rolled spinner. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/palettes/brows` · C-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `ActionFeedback` is silent to assistive tech, truncates a second message that arrives inside the dismiss window, and never clears its timer on unmount.

**Mechanism.** State change keyed on a boolean visibility edge rather than on message identity; plus a missing scope disposal.

**Evidence.**

```
Live: `chipAfterFirstSave = {text:"Saved!", role:null, ariaLive:null}` — no live region on the sole surface reporting four async outcomes (BrowsePane.vue:230,239,249,264). Timing: Save at t=0, Save again at t=2250 ms while the chip was still up → `secondChipLifetimeMs: 613` (promised 2500). Control run with the second Save at t=2523 ms (outside the window) → `secondChipLifetimeMs: 2752`. Cause: ActionFeedback.vue:39-47 watches `props.visible`; PaletteCard.vue:240 writes `feedbackVisible.value = true`, a no-op write when already true, so the watcher never fires and the in-flight timer is neither cleared nor re-armed. Third defect: `let timer` (:37) has no unmount cleanup.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe7.mjs — read `secondSaveAtMs` and `secondChipLifetimeMs`; flip the intermediate wait to 1750 ms for the outside-window control.

**Proposed cure.** Watch the message identity (`() => [props.visible, props.message]`) and key the transition on it so a new message is a new node; add `role="status" aria-live="polite"`; register `onScopeDispose(() => clearTimeout(timer))`. Better: hoist dismissal to the caller and let the chip be pure presentation — that also deletes the `update:visible` round-trip and half of C-8.

The repo already documents this crash class at e2e/smoke/admin/a11y-authed-admin.spec.ts:100-135; the boundary (demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue) catches it, which is exactly the problem — roster, Prune, Refresh and every delete disappear together.

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-impl-c10.mjs (case nullSlug). Frames: frames-impl/C10-{chromium,webkit}-nullSlug.png.

**Proposed cure.** The crash belongs to the component, not the boundary. Validate at the transport/composable seam: a row whose slug is not a string is a row the panel does not render (or renders as a flagged, non-actionable row), so a single bad record degrades one row instead of the console. **Evidence.**

```
`grep -c 'plugin-vue\|plugins' vitest.config.ts` → 0 (no plugins key at all, so .vue is untransformable under `npm test`); `grep -rn 'from ".*\.vue"' test/ demo/test/ | wc -l` → 0 across `find test demo/test -name '*.ts' | wc -l` → 25 files; `grep -rln '@vue/test-utils' test/ demo/test/ e2e/` → no output (devDependency ^2.4.10 with zero importers, alongside jsdom ^26.1.0); `grep -rln 'AdminUsers\|prune' test/ demo/test/` → no output.
```

**Reproduction.** Named mutation that keeps every gate GREEN: replace AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 `const emptyCount = computed(() => users.filter((u) => !(u.paletteCount ?? 0)).length);` with `const emptyCount = computed(() => users.length);` — the panel then offers "Prune 5 empty users?" for a five-user roster and prunes globally, while e2e/smoke/admin/flows/user-status.spec.ts (asserts only that DELETE /admin/users/<slug> fires), both a11y-authed-admin.spec.ts battery tests (assert nameless==[] and undersized==[], both already true — see negative proof), the BR-9 keyboard test and the U-F58 boundary test all pass. Note also `expect(report.controlsChecked).toBeGreaterThan(0)` — the spec's own guard against an empty-scope false green — is satisfied by the toolbar's Prune/Refresh/Sort buttons with ZERO user rows present.

**Proposed cure.** Give vitest a vue plugin (`plugins: [vue()]` in vitest.config.ts) so the already-installed @vue/test-utils + jsdom can mount SFCs, then gate the behaviours no browser cheaply reaches: (i) a prune whose transport throws must not render success-family copy; (ii) a second action-result survives its own full dismissal window; (iii) a late palette response for a stale key does not render; (iv) a failed disclosure renders the error plate, not the empty one; (v) no count is rendered while loadError is set. Both Buttons in this file pass it; it falls through to the DOM as an inert attribute while `emphasis` takes its default `"secondary"` and `tone` its default `"neutral"`, which makes the component apply `glass-wash glass-capsule glass-capsule-hover`. The author asked for a transparent ghost button and shipped a filled glass capsule — measured at 52% and 60% background opacity. This is why the component's two quiet commands read as primary chrome.

**Mechanism.** Same glass-ui 7 whole-major API drift as C-1, in the styling axis instead of the behaviour axis. Harder to spot by eye because `variant` IS a real prop on 12 other glass-ui components (Badge, Card, ToggleGroup, SelectTrigger, ...), so the reader has no local signal that it is wrong here — it needs a compiler.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:5 and :111-112. Contract: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/types.d.ts — ButtonProps = {emphasis?, tone?, size?, iconOnly?, loading?, type?, disabled?, class?} extends PrimitiveProps; no `variant`. Compiled: dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js `props: { emphasis: { default: "secondary" }, tone: { default: "neutral" }, ... }` and `g = computed(() => p.tone === "neutral" && (p.emphasis === "primary" || p.emphasis === "secondary")), x = computed(() => cn("button tap-squish focus-ring", g.value && "glass-wash glass-capsule", ...))`. LIVE (evidence/probeC1.json A_trigger): {attr_variant:"ghost", data_emphasis:"secondary", classList:"button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash glass-capsule glass-capsule-hover relative h-8 w-8", backgroundColor:"oklab(0.915626 0.00551148 0.0130686 / 0.52)"}. Clear button (evidence/probeC2.json clearAll): {variantAttr:"ghost", dataEmphasis:"secondary", bg:"oklab(0.721321 0.00495294 0.0108792 / 0.6)"}. Family: a multiline scan of every demo/**/*.vue `<Button ...>` tag containing variant= returns 51 sites {outline:28, ghost:19, destructive:1, default:1, 'primary-audacious':2} — the shadcn-vue vocabulary verbatim. In this directory: SearchFilterBar.vue:5, :111, UserSortMenu.vue:6, MiniColorPicker.vue:47.
```

**Reproduction.** cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probes/probe-C1-buttonvariant.mjs ; read `A_trigger`. Also visible without tooling in evidence/C-r2-overflow-mobile-390x664.png as the filled pill on the search bar. Family count: the node walker in the report's section 4.

**Proposed cure.** `emphasis="quiet"` at line 5 and `emphasis="quiet" size="sm"` at line 111. Repo-wide the mapping is ghost->quiet, outline->secondary, default->primary, destructive->tone="destructive". The gestalt cure is again C-7: strictTemplates makes all 51 sites compile errors. BH/BI relay item — glass-ui 7.0.0 shipped no variant->emphasis migration note, and 51 consumer sites in this repo alone still speak the old vocabulary and fail silently.

Any mutation is vacuous.

**Mechanism.** A gate set that cannot see the failure mode the codebase actually has. vue-tsc's default strictTemplates:false makes component prop/emit contracts unenforced precisely when a design system takes a major version; the visual matrix samples only default route state, so overlay-resident UI is unaudited; and there is no unit or e2e coverage to fall back on.

Baseline: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` -> no output (clean); `npx eslint demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue` -> no output, exit 0. With one config line added (probes/tsconfig.strictTemplates-probe.json adds "vueCompilerOptions":{"strictTemplates":true}): 271 error TS lines demo-wide, 8 on this file — (5,25) TS2353 'variant' does not exist; (52,38) 'checked' does not exist; (53,38) 'onUpdate:checked' does not exist; (89,46) TS2322 Type 'string | number' is not assignable to type 'string'; (93,37) 'aria-label'; (95,38) 'onKeydown'; (112,29) 'variant'; (115,30) 'onClick'. Full text at evidence/C-r2-strictTemplates-SearchFilterBar.txt. Gate-blindness proof: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` (clean) then `npx vue-tsc -p docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probes/tsconfig.strictTemplates-probe.json --noEmit` (8 errors on this file, 271 demo-wide).

It has one honest prerequisite, measured: 3 of this file's 8 errors are glass-ui DECLARATION GAPS, not demo defects — aria-label and onKeydown on Input, onClick on Button all reach the DOM at runtime (Input sets inheritAttrs:false and spreads forwardedAttrs onto its <input> root; the a11y tree reports textbox "Search by CSS color"; the Clear button's click demonstrably fires). ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/palettes/browse` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The loading state is dead code. `applyColorSearch` is declared `async` but contains no `await`, so it runs to completion synchronously and `searching` goes true->false inside one call, before Vue's scheduler gets a turn. ```
demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:213-225 (async, no await), :102 (<Loader2 v-if="searching" class="animate-spin"/>), :98 (:disabled="searching"), :214 (if (searching.value) return), :142 (Loader2 import). Corroborated by evidence/probeC2.json inputGeometry {"btnDisabledAttr": null}.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/palettes/browse` · C-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** "Clear all filters" unmounts itself while focused. It lives under `v-if="activeFilterCount > 0"`; activating it zeroes the filters, `activeFilterCount` falls to 0, and the focused button is removed from the DOM mid-activation. Focus falls to <body>, which trips reka's dismissable-layer focus-outside handling, so the ENTIRE filter popover closes as a side effect of clearing filters.

**Mechanism.** Conditional rendering of a control keyed on state that the control itself resets: the element destroys its own focus anchor, and in a focus-scoped overlay that destruction reads as focus-outside and cascades into a dismissal. Compounds with C-3: because the Clear row is off-screen at every tested viewport, the only reachable activation path is the keyboard, so a keyboard user must Tab to a control they cannot see (WCAG 2.4.7, 2.4.11), activate it blind, and then have focus dumped to <body> (2.4.3).

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:110-120 (v-if wrapper), :227-232 (onClearAll), BrowsePane.vue:329-332 (onClearFilters). LIVE (probes/probe-C2.mjs, evidence/probeC2.json), focus set then activated — exactly what keyboard activation does: clearAll {"active":"Clear all filters"} -> clearAllAfter {"activeTag":"BODY", "activeText":"->BrowseToolsBrowsePalettes Login  @mbabb", "clearStillPresent": null, "badgeText":""}. `clearStillPresent: null` means no popper content wrapper remained in the DOM — the panel dismissed itself.
```

**Reproduction.** cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/probes/probe-C2.mjs ; read clearAll / clearAllAfter.

**Proposed cure.** Keep the row mounted and disable it: `:disabled="activeFilterCount === 0"`. KISS, it preserves the focus anchor, and it stops the popover resizing under the pointer — which also removes one of the two states C-3 has to fit. If the row must stay conditional, move focus to the popover content root before the state change.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/palettes/browse` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `loadAuditLog` has no request sequencing — no in-flight token, no sequence id, no AbortController — so a slow stale response overwrites a newer one, and `loading` is cleared by whichever request settles first. Refresh is never disabled while loading; nextPage/prevPage gate on hasNext/hasPrev but not on loading.

**Mechanism.** Last-writer-wins over a shared mutable cell; `loading` modelled as a boolean where a concurrent-request count is required.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:48-71 (no guard), :68-70 `finally { loading.value = false }`, :73-85 (nextPage/prevPage ungated on loading); AdminAuditPanel.vue:30 (Refresh Button, no `:disabled`), :115 (debounced load), :119 (mount load). Mount: `[C-7] after fresh(page3) lands: entries=[{"id":"off-40"}] loading=false` then `[C-7] after stale(page2) lands: entries=[{"id":"off-20"}] page=3` — the pager reads page 3 while the rows are page 2's, and `loading` went false with a request still pending.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vitest run --config …/pi/vitest.probe.config.ts (case C-7) — mock getAuditLog with manually-held resolvers, fire page 2 then page 3, resolve page 3 first then page 2. By hand: hold the Next button, or type in the target filter while a refresh is in flight.

**Proposed cure.** A monotonic request id captured at call time; apply the response only if it is still the newest (`if (seq !== latest) return`), and clear `loading` on the same condition. Disable Refresh and the pager while a request is outstanding. Lives in the composable, not the SFC.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/palettes/browse` · D-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The 300ms filter-debounce `setTimeout` is never cleared on unmount. There is no `onUnmounted`/`onScopeDispose` in the file, and the callback closes over the module-singleton admin port — so it fires after destruction, resets `page` to 1 and issues an orphan fetch into state the user is no longer looking at.

**Mechanism.** A timer whose lifetime exceeds its owner's, writing into state whose lifetime exceeds them both — the classic missing-cleanup leak, amplified because the target is a shared singleton rather than component-local state.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue:110-117 (`let filterTimeout`, `setTimeout(…, 300)`, no cleanup hook anywhere in the 120-line file). The port is a singleton: demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:72 + :245; the panel is a plain `v-if` with no KeepAlive at that level: demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:61. Mount with fake timers: `[C-3] after unmount + 400ms -> loadAuditLog calls=2 page=1` (mounted with page=4).
```

**Reproduction.** npx vitest run --config …/pi/vitest.probe.config.ts (case C-3). By hand: type one character in the "Action…" filter, then click the Users tab within 300ms.

**Proposed cure.** Move the debounce into the composable that owns the state — expose `setFilters(action, target)` from `useAdminAudit` and let its own `effectScope` own the timer. Minimum viable: `onUnmounted(() => clearTimeout(filterTimeout))`.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation interrogation (pass 4) of demo/` · C4-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The card grid declares role="list" while every child declares role="article": the list owns zero listitems, so AT announces an empty list.

**Mechanism.** ARIA 1.2 gives `list` the required owned element `listitem`; article is not an allowed owned element, so the list has no items and item navigation finds nothing. PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-8 comments assert the opposite.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 role="list"; PaletteCard.vue:22 role="article". probe-C4-pass4-results.json: A1_listSemantics {gridRole:"list", gridChildRoles:["article","article","article","article"], cardCount:4, listitemCount:0}; A1_roleCounts {list:1, listitem:0, article:4, listitemsInsideGrid:0}.

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteCard/probe-C4-pass4.mjs — leg A1 (DOM query + Playwright role engine) on /#/palettes with four seeded palettes.

**Proposed cure.** The card owns its role: role="listitem" on the card root (with the palette name as accessible name), dropping role="article" which is not a landmark and buys nothing. If the card is ever hosted outside a list, the role becomes a prop — never two contradictory comments.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation interrogation (pass 4) of demo/` · C4-14 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** ActionFeedback is a split-brain state machine: the parent owns the visibility state, the child owns the dismissal timer, and they synchronise through an event — which is why a second verdict inherits the first's deadline.

**Mechanism.** The child's watcher only fires on a visible transition, so calling showFeedback while the chip is already shown changes the message without rearming the timer; no fix inside either file can see the missing information.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteCard.vue:233-244 (feedbackVisible/feedbackMessage/feedbackVariant + showFeedback + defineExpose) vs ActionFeedback.vue:37-47 (let timer; watch(() => props.visible)). Pass 3 P8 measured the consequence: a second message lived 1005 ms of a promised 2500 ms.
```

**Reproduction.** Pass 3's P8 (preserved at challenge-C-implementation.pass-3-2026-07-28.md): call showFeedback twice 1500 ms apart on a mounted card and poll the chip every 250 ms.

**Proposed cure.** One owner: a useActionFeedback() composable holding {message, variant, visible} AND the timer, exposing show(message, variant) that resets the deadline by construction and disposes on scope teardown. ActionFeedback becomes a pure presenter (props in, no watch, no timer, no emit) and PaletteCard's showFeedback/defineExpose becomes a one-line re-export.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation interrogation of demo/palettes/` · N-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** NEW + CORRECTION of pass-1 C-16 — a FAILED abuse report closes the dialog as if it succeeded. `onFlagSubmit` awaits `pm.flagged.report(...)` and then sets `flagDialogOpen = false` unconditionally; `report` catches internally and returns `undefined`, so it never rejects. Same shape: a failed revert is a silent no-op.

**Mechanism.** Typed failure collapsed to `undefined` at the composable boundary, then discarded at the call site; the pane owns a feedback rail (cardRefs[...].showFeedback) it declines to use for these verbs.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:296-300 (unconditional close) against demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:120-131 (`catch (e) { console.warn(...); return undefined; }`). Revert twin: BrowsePane.vue:277-284 `if (!updated) return;` against demo/palettes/useVersionHistory.ts:88-92 (catch -> undefined). Pass-1 C-16 claims "no try -> rejection leaves the dialog open and raises an unhandled rejection" — not reproducible: the awaited call cannot reject.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — hypothesis-free but statically total: the only return paths of `report`/`revert` are a value or `undefined`, and neither call site branches on it. Source-deterministic, not separately driven in-browser.

**Proposed cure.** `report` and `revert` return a typed verdict (`{ ok } | ApiProblem`); the pane renders it on the same feedback rail save/delete/visibility already use. Never close a dialog on an unexamined result.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation interrogation of demo/palettes/` · N-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** UPGRADE of pass-1 C-5 — `cardRefs` unbounded growth measured in the RUNNING component (pass 1 measured a synthetic re-implementation). The `el &&` guard swallows Vue's unmount `null` call, so no key is ever deleted.

**Mechanism.** Lifecycle state never released: an inline function ref plus a truthiness guard that discards the unmount signal.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:94 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)"` + :209 `reactive<Record<...>>({})`. Live read of the real setupState via `#app.__vue_app__._instance`: `after initial load | visible cards = 6 | cardRefs entries = [6,6]` -> `after 4 reloads | visible cards = 6 | cardRefs entries = [30,30]` -> `after 8 reloads | visible cards = 6 | cardRefs entries = [54,54]`. Retained values are expose proxies (ownKeys ["showFeedback"]) whose `$el.isConnected === false` from reload 4 onward. `[30,30]` is two numbers because /#/browse mounts the pane in BOTH responsive slots — the leak is doubled. Pane is KeepAlive'd, so nothing clears it.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../BrowsePane/probe-C2/probe-c2-cardrefs-live-growth.mjs

**Proposed cure.** Delete the registry. Card feedback is card-local state and belongs in PaletteCard, driven by a prop/event, not by an imperative reach through a parent-held instance handle. (If the registry must survive: `if (el) map[slug] = el; else delete map[slug]`, and shallowReactive, not deep reactive, for template refs.)

### `CHALLENGE-C — the implementation of demo/palettes/browser/sl` · C-30 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** NEW — the `ADMIN_TOKEN=` disambiguator is stripped and then ignored: classification is purely shape-based, so an admin token in four-word form is routed to USER login and POSTed in cleartext to the unauthenticated `/sessions/login` endpoint as a `slug`, and admin login is unreachable for that whole token class.

**Mechanism.** A masking fallback (edict-2 violation) used as a security boundary — normalizeTokenInput cleans the input so a shape heuristic can classify it, then the explicit user-supplied label is discarded, so a legitimate credential is silently reclassified as a public identifier.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteSlugBar.vue:204-205 `const normalized = normalizeTokenInput(raw).toLowerCase(); const isAdmin = !looksLikeSlug(normalized);`. Measured emission table (probe P4-3): `ADMIN_TOKEN=correct-horse-battery-staple -> ["correct-horse-battery-staple", false]`; `ADMIN_TOKEN="correct-horse-battery-staple" -> ["correct-horse-battery-staple", false]`; contrast `ADMIN_TOKEN=change-me-to-a-secure-random-string -> [..., true]`. Wire shape: demo/platform/auth/sessions.ts:18-25 `POST /sessions/login body: JSON.stringify({ slug })`. Token format: api/.env.example:2 `ADMIN_TOKEN=change-me-to-a-secure-random-string`. Byte-identical logic live at demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:25-54.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteSlugBar/probes/c4-vitest.config.ts — read the `RAW="ADMIN_TOKEN=correct-horse-battery-staple" -> [...]` line in P4-3.

**Proposed cure.** Move the decision into one exported predicate in demo/platform/auth/: an `ADMIN_TOKEN=`-prefixed input is an admin token BY DECLARATION; a bare input is a slug only if it matches the generator's alphabet; anything else is an explicit rejection with a message. Never a silent reclassification. Collapses C-5, C-23, C-24, C-30 and half of C-19 in one move.

Vendor render (dist/search.js) emits only ref/type/attrs/value/placeholder/class/onInput. Admin branch un-lowercased: PaletteSlugBar.vue:213 `emit("switchSlug", isAdmin ? normalizeTokenInput(raw) : normalized, isAdmin)`.

**Proposed cure.** Replace with the design system's form primitive carrying name, autocomplete="off", autocapitalize="off", autocorrect="off", spellcheck="false", a real label/aria-label and aria-describedby pointing at an announced error region; and lowercase-normalize both branches or neither.

### `CHALLENGE-C — the implementation of demo/palettes/browser/sl` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `slugSwitching` is set true and false within one synchronous turn, so the spinner, the in-flight accessible name and the double-submit guard are all unrenderable.

**Mechanism.** An emit is not an await. The component models an async operation it does not actually own — the parent's handler is the async one, and its promise is discarded.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteSlugBar.vue:201-224 — `slugSwitching.value = true` … the emit at 213 is synchronous … `finally { slugSwitching.value = false }` runs before any render. The `:disabled="!slugInput.trim() || slugSwitching"` guard (line 23) and the `:aria-label="slugSwitching ? 'Signing in…' : ..."` (line 24) can never be observed; the `Loader2` at line 26 never paints.
```

**Reproduction.** Read PaletteSlugBar.vue:198-225; pass 3 measured `spinner nodes while parent pending: 0`.

**Proposed cure.** Either the component owns the async call and awaits it, or it renders no in-flight state at all and the owning composable exposes a `pending` ref. Half-owning it is the defect.

### `CHALLENGE-C — the implementation of demo/palettes/browser/sl` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Focus never reaches the slug input: `nextTick` inside a 50 ms `setTimeout` resolves in the same microtask as the mode flip, while the `mode="out-in"` leave holds insertion for a measured 200 ms.

**Mechanism.** A microtask scheduled against a CSS transition — nextTick tracks the render queue, not the transition's completion, so the ref is still null when focus() is attempted.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteSlugBar.vue:176-181 `setTimeout(() => { slugEditMode.value = true; nextTick(() => searchBarRef.value?.inputRef?.focus()) }, 50)`. Measured leave (probes/c4-live.mjs): `.vj-morph-leave-active` → `transitionProperty: "opacity, transform, max-height"`, `transitionDuration: "0.2s, 0.2s, 0.2s"`; token `--duration-fast: 0.2s`.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/.../probes/c4-live.mjs — read the `morph` block.

**Proposed cure.** Focus on the Transition's `@after-enter` hook (or `@enter`), which is the event that actually means "the input exists". The arbitrary 50 ms delay then disappears, taking C-11 with it.

**Defect.** Slug search is explicitly offered by the code and is dead in the product: it works at exactly one character and nowhere else.

useBrowsePalettes.ts:44 offers `|| p.slug.includes(q)`; the server's text index covers `name` only (api/src/platform/db/db.ts:57-60), so any query of 2+ chars is answered before the slug predicate is reached. Upgrades pass-1 C-6, which established that BrowsePane.vue:339-349 is a line-for-line second copy of `colorMatcherFor` (api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:159-181) including the magic 0.15 radius, running over <=50 loaded rows with zero network requests.

**Reproduction.** curl -s "https://api.color.babb.dev/palettes?limit=50&sort=newest" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(sum(1 for p in d['data'] if not p.get('oklabColors')),'/',len(d['data']))" → `5 / 10`. In-app: set any colour search on /#/browse; those five rows can never appear.

**Proposed cure.** Thread `colorL/colorA/colorB/colorRadius` into `currentFilterOpts()` and DELETE `displayedBrowse` + `colorSearchParams` outright. The server already pages honestly across a colour filter (crud-list.ts:211-270 fetch-ahead loop); the client copy cannot, and it fights the cursor, the sort and the tag/tier set instead of composing with them.

**Defect.** The failure state is broken three independent ways: (a) it overlaps the following content by 8px at every viewport; (b) `whitespace-nowrap` on an absolutely positioned box means a real server message is 758px wide inside a 286px host and is silently clipped, discarding the actionable half; (c) it is a color-only failure with no role, no aria-live, no aria-invalid on the field and no aria-describedby association — so it disappears entirely in forced-colors and is never announced.

**Evidence.**

Real-cascade measurement, probes/geom.mjs, invariant across three arms: `### desktop-1440 errOverlapsFollowing: 8 errOverflowsBarBox: 16` / `### mobile-390 errOverlapsFollowing: 8 errOverflowsBarBox: 16` / `### narrow-320 errOverlapsFollowing: 8 errOverflowsBarBox: 16` (root min-h-9 + measured marginBottom "8px" vs bottom:-1rem and a 19.59px line box). probes/geom2.mjs against the real host: `### narrow-320 { hostTag: "DIV.pane-header.px-4.sm:px-6", hostWidth: 286, shortErrW: 267.08, shortErrOverflowsHost: -2.92, longErrW: 758.16, longErrOverflowsHost: 488.16, longErrOverflowsViewport: 471.16 }`; document.scrollWidth stayed 320, so an ancestor clips. probes/mount.test.ts: `[error] tree has role=alert|status = false` / `aria-live = false` / `aria-invalid = false` / `aria-describedby = false`. Quoted law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit."; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.3.
```

**Reproduction.** node probes/geom.mjs (8px overlap, all three arms) and node probes/geom2.mjs (488px host overflow for a realistic API title, 2.92px of slack for the SHORTEST authored string); npx vitest run --config probes/vitest.config.ts probes/mount.test.ts for the missing a11y attributes.

**Defect.** The 'Your slug' explanation is hover-only on a bare `<span>` that carries no tabindex, no role, no accessible name and no aria-expanded — unreachable by keyboard, and on coarse pointers glass-ui falls the Popover back to a CLICK root, turning the span into an operable control with no name or focus. The component also overrides the producer's 150ms hover-intent closeDelay to 0, so moving the pointer toward the panel dismisses it.

**Mechanism.** PR-07 hover-only affordance plus a per-instance override of a producer-tuned default (edict-5 failure mode); as-child forwards data-state and handlers but never synthesizes focusability on a non-interactive element

Pointer adaptation in the same file: `matchMedia("(pointer: coarse)").matches` gates `trigger === "hover"`, falling back to the click PopoverRoot on touch. Quoted law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-07 "Hover-only/unlabeled controls and invisible drag state → ADD-AFFORDANCE / REMOVE" and §5.5 "Decorative controls and operable ornaments without names are forbidden."
```

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (component: demo/palettes/browser/slug/` · D-9 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** An admin secret token is typed into a hardcoded `type="search"` field with no autocomplete, autocapitalize, autocorrect, spellcheck or inputmode. iOS Safari capitalises the first character by default, and the admin path at :213 forwards the token with its original casing, so a correct token typed on iPhone fails silently. The placeholder says 'enter slug...' while the parser accepts ADMIN_TOKEN=<secret>.

**Mechanism.** credential hygiene — a search field pressed into service as a credential input; type=search specifically feeds UA search/datalist history, and the absent mobile input attributes let the platform mutate a secret before it is read

**Evidence.**

```
Probe: `[dom] input attrs = type,placeholder,class,value` — exactly four attributes. type is producer-hardcoded: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/search.js — `b("input", w({ ref_key:"inputRef", ref:s, type:"search" }, ...))`. Source: normalizeTokenInput at :188-196 explicitly parses `/^ADMIN_TOKEN\s*=\s*(.+)$/i`; :204 lowercases only the slug path (`normalizeTokenInput(raw).toLowerCase()`); :213 emits `isAdmin ? normalizeTokenInput(raw) : normalized` — the admin arm keeps original casing. Placeholder :12 = "enter slug..."; the live sibling SlugEditLayer.vue:84 = "enter slug or token...".
```

**Reproduction.** npx vitest run --config probes/vitest.config.ts probes/submit.test.ts — the rendered input exposes only type,placeholder,class,value. On iOS Safari, autocapitalize defaults to sentences, so a token entered as `abc…` is submitted as `Abc…` through :213 and rejected, with no announced error (D-3c).

**Proposed cure.** Credential entry belongs in the Account Dialog with a real `<input>` the consumer controls: explicit autocomplete, autocapitalize="none", autocorrect="off", spellcheck="false", and copy that names what the field accepts. If the producer field is reused, glass-ui must expose `type`/input-attribute pass-through (BH/BI relay item).

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (PaletteCard, six-file folder, area pal` · D-10 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The six-file decomposition is not along seams — it is a god module distributed across six files; two children own no state and one has no root element at all.

**Mechanism.** A line-count cap was met by relocating markup rather than by moving responsibility, so the coupling surface (16 members for Swatches; the parent's own flex context for Meta) was preserved intact across a file boundary. The Meta extraction actively CAUSED D-1: the shrink-0 decision that starves the title now lives in a file that cannot see the title.

**Evidence.**

```
Line counts: PaletteCard.vue 364, PaletteCardMenu 228, PaletteCardSwatches 96, PaletteRenameInput 66, PaletteCardMeta 64, ActionFeedback 58 (876 total). PaletteCard retains 11 props, 17 emits, a 19-entry string-keyed action table (:293-313), four composables, and two pieces of UI state. PaletteCardSwatches owns NO state and takes 8 props / re-emits 8 events, all forwarded straight back into useHoverPopover. PaletteCardMeta has no root element — five sibling root nodes (:8,16,26,36,43) laid out by the parent's flex row; measured parent row reports metaChildren:8 with the meta chips as direct children. Source comments record the history: "T.W5 PP-8 cap cure", "the H.W3 sub-component precedent". VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 names the result: "seven-mode omnibus" — and the prop list is literally seven modes (expanded, isOwned, editableName, isAdmin, showSlug, draggable, layout).
```

**Reproduction.** Read the six files; count props+emits on PaletteCardSwatches (8+8, zero state) and root nodes on PaletteCardMeta (5, no wrapper). At runtime, the parent's identity row reports metaChildren:8 — the child's chips are the parent's flex items.

**Proposed cure.** Subtraction, not re-cutting. The canon anatomy — Card(frozen tuple) > button[aria-pressed] over specimen+identity, plus one named reorder handle — with expand/rename/menu/transient-result/swatch-actions moving to the selected inspector DELETES PaletteCardSwatches, PaletteRenameInput, ActionFeedback and most of PaletteCardMenu from the card, and dissolves D-1, D-7, D-9 and D-17 as a side effect. Per feedback_kiss_no_contrivance the fix is not a seventh file or a shared/ dir.

**Defect.** One trailing slot carries two orthogonal facts, and availability destroys the visibility readout: when the backend goes down the annotation flips from `public`/`private` to `offline`, so the user loses the ability to read what state the palette is frozen in.

PaletteCardMenu.vue:56-59 `{{ apiOffline ? "offline" : isPublic ? "public" : "private" }}` — one span, mutually exclusive ternary. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (PaletteCardMenu.vue)` · D-11 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Four type-jurisdiction violations of the CLOSED VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 matrix; the sharpest renders all five export format names in italic because `text-caption` is the producer's italic caption voice and only its font-style survives.

**Mechanism.** `.dropdown-menu__item{font-size:var(--dropdown-text)}` overrides the SubContent's caption size but nothing overrides font-style, so a class chosen for size delivers only obliqueness. glass-ui already ships the correct utilities for this exact context — `.text-dropdown` and `.text-dropdown-secondary` — and they are unused.

**Evidence.**

```
VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:75 ('control or label, including dropdown options → text-small, Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold'), matrix declared closed at §4. Measured: (a) :7 `text-small` on Content → items render Fira Code 16.4px (mono is a root decision at demo/styles/foundation.css:374 `--dropdown-menu-font: var(--font-mono)`); (b) :112 `text-caption` on SubContent → glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/semantic.css `@utility text-caption { ... font-style: italic; ... }`; probe-D2-results.json `subContent.fontStyle: "italic"`, `subItem.fontStyle: "italic"`, and subItem fontSize 16.4px identical to the parent — the size intent is overridden, only the italics inherit; (c) :9 `font-bold` → measured font-weight 600; (d) :155 `text-mono-caption uppercase tracking-wider` for the 'Admin' SECTION HEADING → mono, which §4 reserves for 'value, code, or provenance'. Witness: evidence/mobile-light-submenu-open.png shows JSON / CSS Custom Properties / Tailwind Config / SVG Swatch / PNG Swatch all in italic mono while the parent menu is upright.
```

**Reproduction.** Open the card menu on /#/palettes, hover 'Export', and read getComputedStyle on the sub-content and its items; or node probe-D2-pcm.mjs section menuVsSub.

**Proposed cure.** Consume `.text-dropdown` / `.text-dropdown-secondary` where a rung is genuinely needed and otherwise let the producer own the item type. Relay the mono-for-control-copy question (foundation.css:374 vs VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:75) as a root-level ruling, not a per-component override.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (PaletteCardMenu.vue)` · D-12 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Hover and keyboard focus are literally the same declaration — one background tint with no non-colour channel — so in a menu containing an irreversible Delete there is no visual answer to 'where will Enter land'.

**Mechanism.** reka's single `data-highlighted` attribute serves both pointer-hover and roving keyboard focus, and the producer expresses it with one background tint; the consumer adds no second channel. Compounded by D-2 (destructive ink already dead) and D-14 (Delete grouped with a disclosure).

**Evidence.**

```
probe-D2-results.json `states`: rest `{ bg: "rgba(0,0,0,0)", outline: "none 3px", boxShadow: "none", textDecoration: "none" }`; focused `{ bg: "oklab(0.915626 0.00551148 0.0130686/0.52)", outline: "none 3px", boxShadow: "none", textDecoration: "none" }` — background-color is the only delta. The keyboard walk (probe-D2-results.json `keyboard`) shows the identical bg on every row with outline 3px but outline-style none. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: 'Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency.'
```

**Reproduction.** Open the menu, ArrowDown through it, and diff getComputedStyle before/after — only backgroundColor changes. node probe-D2-pcm.mjs section `states`.

**Proposed cure.** Producer relay: focus needs an independent non-colour register (outline / inset ring) distinct from the hover tint, surviving forced-colors and reduced-transparency, per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (PaletteSlugBar.vue, area palettes)` · D-19 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The identity pill has no containment law; the root recipe `.slug-pill` omits white-space / max-inline-size / min-inline-size / overflow / text-overflow, so every consumer re-decides geometry per instance and the subject decides nothing. As authored it wraps into a two-line stadium at the mandated narrow arms; the sibling `whitespace-nowrap` patch converts that into a pane overflow instead.

**Mechanism.** root recipe incomplete → per-instance geometry override (owner edict 5 inverted: extracted for paint, not for geometry)

**Evidence.**

```
demo/styles/foundation.css:585-587 (`.slug-pill { @apply text-mono-small font-bold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full border; }`). Patch census: ProfileSection.vue:73,96 + MobileMenuDropdown.vue:48,67 add `whitespace-nowrap`; AdminUsersPanel.vue:98,167 add `flex items-baseline min-w-0 max-w-full` / `inline-block align-middle mx-0.5`; PaletteSlugBar.vue:48,65 add nothing. Corpus: api/src/modules/session/slugWords.ts:99-104 → `adj-verb-color-animal`, longest 40 chars (iridescent-threading-champagne-jellyfish), hyphens are CSS break opportunities. MEASURED (probes/psb-wrap.mjs, WebKit, live pane): `390 long-40ch as-authored normal 2 lineBoxes 296.01 x 45.28`; `390 long-40ch PATCHED nowrap 1 362.63 overflowPx 22.62`; `320 median-32ch as-authored normal 2 lineBoxes 226 x 45.19`; `320 long-40ch PATCHED nowrap 1 362.63 overflowPx 92.63`; single-line heights 25.59-28.94 across arms; font "Fira Code" 16.4px, border 1px.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteSlugBar/probes/psb-wrap.mjs (dev server on :9000). Also `grep -rn "slug-pill" demo/` for the patch census.

**Proposed cure.** Put the law in the root: `.slug-pill { white-space: nowrap; min-inline-size: 0; max-inline-size: 100%; overflow: clip; text-overflow: ellipsis; }` and delete all six per-instance patches. The full string stays recoverable through the already-existing named `Copy slug` action — identity becomes data in the clipboard and label in the layout, and the two stop fighting. Note that nowrap ALONE is not the cure: applied to PaletteSlugBar it would create the 92.63px overflow.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (PaletteSlugBar.vue, area palettes)` · D-20 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The only explanation of what a slug is announces as NOTHING on desktop and as `role="dialog"` on touch, and is unreachable by keyboard — because a hover-`Popover` was used where the design system's `Tooltip` primitive already ships and is already consumed by five demo components.
