### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-6/P4-3 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `demo/ui/` is 19 pure re-export shims over glass-ui — a second naming authority for every design-system component — and PalettesPane.vue speaks both dialects inside one import block: Card/Button/Badge through the shim (:129-131), Dialog/SearchBar direct from the published subpaths (:141-149), while `demo/ui/dialog/index.ts` exists and exports all six Dialog symbols.

**Mechanism.** An alias layer that adds nothing but a second name (standing edict 2: no aliases/dual paths; edict 4: glass-ui is the design system). The root-barrel re-export additionally defeats the granularity glass-ui publishes.

**Evidence.**

```
All 19 `demo/ui/*/index.ts` are bare `export { … } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui…"` (full cat in report). Repo split: 5 files consume `demo/ui/dialog`, 2 consume `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog` — PalettesPane is one of the 2. 46 demo files reach through the shims. glass-ui publishes 74 subpaths including ./card ./button ./badge (dist/card.js 217 B, button.js 71 B, badge.js 92 B) vs the root barrel glass-ui.js at 25,239 B of re-exports over 66 chunks. In this pane's live graph the root barrel module is 234,285 B of its 293,136 B glass-ui footprint; 11 modules reach it (7 shims + PaletteCard.vue, PaletteCardSwatches.vue, useSwatchActions.ts, usePaletteActions.ts). demo/ui/input/index.ts already uses the narrow `@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms`.
```

**Reproduction.** `for f in demo/ui/*/index.ts; do cat $f; done`; per-component consumer counts via grep (pasted); `node scratchpad/devgraph4.mjs` for the root-barrel importer set.

**Proposed cure.** Delete `demo/ui/` outright and codemod the 46 consumers to `@mkbabb/glass-ui/<subpath>`. IMPORTANT SCOPING (P4-3): the production cost of the root barrel is only 969 B (esbuild, minified: 26,540 B via root barrel vs 25,571 B via ./card+./button+./badge — glass-ui declares sideEffects ["*.css"] and shakes correctly). Sell this cure on one-name-per-concept and dev-graph latency, NOT on bundle size.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1(re-verified) · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Two writers own palette order on every drop. The pane supplies `onEnd`, which does not override vueuse's default `onUpdate`, so vueuse's `moveArrayElement` also runs — performing raw removeChild/insertBefore DOM surgery on a Vue-managed subtree — while the pane's onEnd writes the store. The `list` argument is a dereferenced computed (`pm.filteredSaved.value`), i.e. a setup-time snapshot where a ref/getter is required.

**Mechanism.** Ordering has no single home: sortable holds one truth, the store another, and the store patches the difference. The same hazard class as the documented Teleport insertBefore NotFoundError at vite.config.ts:83-90 — Vue-managed DOM mutated outside Vue.

**Evidence.**

```
PalettesPane.vue:183-197. node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js:11-16 — `const defaultOptions = { onUpdate: (e) => { moveArrayElement(list, e.oldIndex, e.newIndex, e); } }` then `new Sortable(target, { ...defaultOptions, ...resetOptions })`; `moveArrayElement` at :77-91 opens with `removeNode(e.item); insertNodeAt(e.from, e.item, from)` and its splice is a no-op for a non-ref list (`isRef(list)` false). useFilteredList.ts:8 returns a ComputedRef; usePaletteStore.ts:51-55 makes savedPalettes a computed that mints a new array each recompute. usePaletteStore.ts:161-165 completes a partial id list by appending, so a filtered reorder hoists the visible subset (pass-3 L-17, mechanism re-confirmed by reading).
```

**Reproduction.** Code path confirmed by reading vueuse + store, pasted. The live drag was NOT re-run this pass — the shared Playwright browser was held by another seat (`Error: Browser is already in use for … mcp-chrome-83447af`). Pass 3's live reproduction (seeded A,B,C → persisted C,B,A; filtered A..E → persisted D,B,E,A,C) stands as the executed evidence.

**Proposed cure.** Order is store state. Move the sortable binding into PaletteCardGrid.vue, which owns the element it operates on, and pass a getter not a snapshot: `useSortable(rootEl, () => library.savedPalettes.value, { handle, animation, ghostClass, onUpdate })` — supply onUpdate so the default is genuinely replaced and no unowned DOM mutation runs; disable dragging while searchQuery is non-empty. The pane then never mentions sortable, and PalettesPane.vue:180-181's `(… as any)?.$el` reach into the child's DOM disappears with it.

useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:38-41 `background: linear-gradient(to top, #000, transparent), linear-gradient(to right, #fff, hsl(${hue}deg, 100%, 50%))` vs MiniColorPicker.vue:159-163 `background: linear-gradient(to top, #000, transparent), linear-gradient(to right, #fff, hsl(calc(var(--hue) * 1deg), 100%, 50%))` — same two layers, same order, same stops. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-3 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The hue-stability domain law is re-invented locally with a strictly weaker threshold. The colour session's law is `s·v > 0.01` (near-achromatic); the component substitutes `d === 0` (exact achromatic only).

**Mechanism.** Copied-and-weakened domain law. A documented invariant of the colour model was re-derived from scratch by a component that cannot see the model.

**Evidence.**

```
Canonical law, stated twice: demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts:92 `if (s * v > 0.01) stableHue.value = channelNumber(hsv, "h")` and demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:43 `if (saturation * value > 0.01) stableHue.value = ...`, documented at useColorPipeline.ts:73-76 ('oklch→HSV loses hue at low chroma (atan2(0,0)=0)'). Local substitute: MiniColorPicker.vue:119 `if (d === 0) return; // keep existing hue`. Exhaustive measurement over all 16,777,216 sRGB hexes (scratchpad/huelaw.mjs): `divergence band: 4578 / 16777216 (0.027%)` — e.g. #000001 (s=1, v=0.0039, s·v=0.00392) where the component slams hue to 240 from a 1/255 channel difference while the canonical law holds it steady. Corroborating: the library itself returns hue "none" for #000000 (CSS Color 4 powerless channel) — the exact case the canonical law is built around and which `d === 0` handles only by accident, at a single point.
```

**Reproduction.** node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/huelaw.mjs → 4,578/16,777,216 hexes in the divergence band. The band is small but is exactly the region users hit dragging into the black corner of the plate.

**Proposed cure.** Do not hold hue locally at all. Read HSVCurrentColor (useColorPipeline.ts:106-109), which already applies stableHue. Separately — and this is the real root cause — the law is written TWICE inside the session itself before this component wrote it a third time differently; export the 0.01 constant with a docstring exactly as spectrumLuma.ts:21 does for its 0.5 threshold.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-4 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The shared plate-luma helper is bypassed — the precise failure its own docstring forbids. spectrumLuma.ts exists solely to keep every instrument agreeing about the same (s,v) region; the component drops the concept and hardcodes a white thumb border.

**Mechanism.** A third instrument disagreeing about the same (s,v) region, in direct defiance of a helper written to prevent exactly that.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/picker/controls/spectrumLuma.ts:3 'ONE function, ONE threshold — instrument coherence', :9 'Share the function, never copy the constant (overlay-amendment.md §4.1)', :21 SPECTRUM_LUMA_FLIP = 0.5, :33 spectrumFieldIsLight. Canonical consumer flips the thumb border black/white at useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:55-60. MiniColorPicker.vue:18 hardcodes `border-2 border-white` unconditionally — neither shares the function nor copies the constant. Measured: 30.70% of the SV field reads LIGHT by the canonical model (node -e over a 1000×1000 lattice of spectrumLuma > 0.5). Live default state (E5 probe): thumbLeft 66.6667%, thumbTop 20% ⇒ s=0.667, v=0.8 ⇒ luma = 0.8×(1−0.667/2) = 0.5333 > 0.5 ⇒ inside that region on first open, with measured thumbBorderColor rgb(255,255,255).
```

**Reproduction.** node -e "const luma=(s,v)=>v*(1-s*0.5); console.log(luma(0.667,0.8))" → 0.5333 > SPECTRUM_LUMA_FLIP (0.5). Live: /#/browse → Filters → colour swatch, then read getComputedStyle on the thumb → rgb(255,255,255).

**Proposed cure.** Consume spectrumFieldIsLight, which follows automatically once the plate is shared (L-2). IMPORTANT HONESTY QUALIFIER recorded in the report: the STRUCTURAL defect is CONFIRMED, but the contrast failure it would normally imply is a HYPOTHESIS, not observed — I captured the live plate and looked at it, and the white ring stays legible at the default position because shadow-cartoon-sm supplies an offset dark shadow the canonical instrument does not rely on. I do not claim an observed contrast failure.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-7 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The component's public contract is a hex `string`, which caps the entire colour-search feature at 6-digit hex and produces a masking fallback in the parent that silently discards input the UI explicitly invites.

**Mechanism.** A stringly-typed boundary between two components that both sit above a typed colour model, plus a masking fallback (edict 2: no masking fallbacks). Invalid states are representable because the contract is `string`.

**Evidence.**

```
MiniColorPicker.vue:65-74 types props/emits as bare `string`. Decode gate at :111 `if (!incomingHex || !incomingHex.startsWith("#") || incomingHex.length < 7) return;` silently rejects #48c, named colours, and every functional CSS colour — all of which the library accepts (scratchpad/cure.mjs section B). The cap propagates: SearchFilterBar.vue:92 advertises `placeholder="#hex, hsl(...)"` but :218 reads `const hex = text.startsWith("#") && /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i.test(text) ? text : pickerHex.value;` — a user who types the hsl(...) the placeholder invites gets the picker's current colour searched instead, with no error. The parent already imports the library-backed parseColorIn (SearchFilterBar.vue:137) that would parse it correctly.
```

**Reproduction.** Read SearchFilterBar.vue:92 against :218 — the regex is unambiguous. Typing `hsl(210 60% 50%)` into the colour field searches pickerHex instead. Code-path confirmed by reading; I did NOT drive this one live, so the live user-facing symptom is a hypothesis while the code path is confirmed.

**Proposed cure.** Type the boundary as AnyColor / PickerColorIn<"hsv"> (both already exported from demo/color-session/picker-color.ts), making invalid states unrepresentable. SearchFilterBar then feeds parseColorIn(text, "oklab") directly and the advertised hsl(...) finally works. Delete the :218 fallback rather than fixing it.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-6 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** 'How many versions a palette has' has two homes that provably diverge: the palette document's `versionCount` (card badge) and `listVersions().total` (drawer header and v-numbering).

**Mechanism.** Unique semantic ownership violated across the API/demo seam: one concept, two independently-written numbers, plus a version-identity model that is global-by-content while the read path is scoped-by-palette.

Card badge reads palette.versionCount at demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardMenu.vue:101; drawer reads page.total at VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:11, :37 (`v{{ total - i }}`) and :89 (load-more gate). Deeper: version identity IS the content hash globally (`_id: hash`, versions.ts:60) while listVersions filters `{paletteSlug}` (repository/paletteVersion.ts:22). Live corroboration: `curl https://api.color.babb.dev/palettes?limit=50` shows hey-v2-cd3e1e3b-remix-fecce815 and hey-v2-cd3e1e3b-remix-2a95820d sharing the SAME currentHash 6691aae4.
```

**Reproduction.** Code-path proof pasted above (unconditional $inc vs early-return on existing hash). Live end-to-end reproduction NOT run: no public palette has versionCount > 1 (measured — all 10, hasMore:false), so no revert can be performed against the live commons.

**Proposed cure.** Derive versionCount from the palette_versions count rather than $inc-ing the document, so both surfaces read one number; and make version identity per-palette (composite {paletteSlug, hash}) rather than a global content hash, so a shared-content row cannot be invisible to one of its owners.

**Defect.** `demo/ui/` is a 19-directory alias layer that owns nothing — 18 of 19 barrels are single-line re-exports of the glass-ui ROOT barrel, when glass-ui 7.0.0 publishes a fine-grained subpath for every one of them. **Mechanism.** legacy alias layer / dual path — a redirect-only module tier standing between consumers and the design system's real public surface

**Evidence.**

```
AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:139-140 imports Button/Badge via `../../../ui/button`, `../../../ui/badge`. demo/ui/button/index.ts is exactly `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`; demo/ui/badge/index.ts likewise. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json#exports declares `./button`, `./badge`, `./card`, `./skeleton`, `./dialog`, `./tabs`, `./select` … (70+ entries). Dual path measured across demo/: 41 shim sites (button/badge/card) vs 37 bare-root sites vs 82 direct-subpath sites; `Dialog` reached both ways (shim + `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog` ×2); AdminPane.vue:87 mixes both in one script block. Dist fan-out: `grep -oE 'from *"\./[^"]+"' glass-ui.js | sort -u | wc -l` → 43 chunks / 168,303 B, vs button.js = 71 B / 1 chunk, badge.js = 92 B / 1 chunk. Live dev server resource timing: `@mkbabb_glass-ui.js` = 234,309 B, the largest glass-ui module loaded.
```

**Reproduction.** `for f in demo/ui/*/index.ts; do cat $f; done` — 18 one-line root re-exports. Then `node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json').exports))"` shows the subpath for each. Bundle claim is bounded honestly: glass-ui declares `sideEffects: ["*.css"]` and `grep -c '\.css"' dist/glass-ui.js` → 0, so Rollup CAN tree-shake the root barrel in production — the 234 KB is a measured dev-server cost, not a proven production regression.

**Proposed cure.** Delete `demo/ui/` entirely and rewrite the 41 import sites to name the glass-ui subpath they actually want (`@mkbabb/glass-ui/button`, `/badge`, …). ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure under demo/palettes/BrowsePa` · L5-3 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The `cardRefs` registry never prunes, retaining a live ComponentPublicInstance for every slug ever rendered. Extends pass-1 L-12, which asserted the leak but did not prove the mechanism — and the obvious reading ("Vue nulls the ref on unmount, so the entry clears") is wrong in a way easy to miss on review.

**Mechanism.** Inverted data flow plus a discarded lifecycle signal. Verdict state ("Saved!", "Deleted", a fork error) is data that flows down, but is modelled as a sideways imperative method call (PaletteCard.vue:244 `defineExpose({ showFeedback })`), which is why the pane must hand-roll an instance registry at all — and the registry's cleanup path is silently swallowed by its own null guard.

**Evidence.**

```
BrowsePane.vue:209 `const cardRefs = reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})`; :94 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)"`. Vue DOES notify on unmount — node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js:1763 in `setRef`: `const value = isUnmount ? null : refValue;` — and the `el &&` guard short-circuits on exactly that call, so the notification is received and DISCARDED. Growth drivers: useBrowsePalettes.ts:63+ replaces the row set wholesale on every sort/tier/tag change; BROWSE_PAGE_SIZE = 50 at :18 appends 50 per page. Duplicated apparatus at PalettesPane.vue:169,88,178-181.
```

**Reproduction.** Static mechanism, CONFIRMED from Vue's shipped source at runtime-core.cjs.js:1763 read against BrowsePane.vue:94. Deterministic: any unmount of a PaletteCard leaves its cardRefs entry in place.

**Proposed cure.** Delete `cardRefs`, `defineExpose` (PaletteCard.vue:244) and both panes' registries. One `feedback?: { message: string; variant: "success" | "error" } | null` prop on PaletteCard, driven by a single `shallowRef<{slug,message,variant}|null>` on the wall — shallowRef being the correct primitive per edict 7. Self-pruning, declarative, and the "feedback" concept lands inside PaletteCard's own contract instead of two panes' bookkeeping.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure under demo/palettes/BrowsePa` · L5-4 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `request<T>` is a generic type ASSERTION, not a decoder — `res.json()` widened to `Promise<T>` with zero runtime checking — so every function in demo/palettes/api/ (8 modules) claims a shape it never verifies. This is the root cause of pass-1 L-16's masking `Object.values` shim in BrowsePane, and it means pass-4 N-10's types-only cure cannot close the boundary.

**Mechanism.** A wire boundary policed by assertion rather than validation. Ownership (which pass 4 correctly identified) is necessary but not sufficient: naming the same shape on both sides does not make the wire carry it. The shim is therefore structurally required at the leaf, which is why pass 1 could only rank it INFO — at the leaf it looks like defensive noise; at the seam it is a hole with ~40 call sites.

**Evidence.**

```
Chain: demo/platform/transport/client.ts:101,130 `export async function request<T>(path, init?): Promise<T> { … return res.json(); }` → demo/palettes/api/colors.ts:14 `export function getTags(): Promise<Tag[]> { return request("/colors/tags"); }` → demo/palettes/useTagEdit.ts:31,42 `const allTags = ref<Tag[]>([])` / `allTags.value = await getTags()` → BrowsePane.vue:215-220 `Array.isArray(tags) ? tags : Object.values(tags)` with an 8-line apology at :210-214 describing a RUNTIME payload shape no type can forbid. Pass-4 N-10 § Cure explicitly reasons "it is types only, so it costs nothing at runtime" — a `.d.ts` erases, so the shim would survive it. The api tree already ships the authority: zod schemas at api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:89-91 and siblings.
```

**Reproduction.** Static trace, CONFIRMED end to end at the four cited file:line sites. The observable symptom is the repeated Vue "Expected Array, got Object" prop warning that BrowsePane.vue:210-214 was written to suppress.

**Proposed cure.** Ownership from N-10 PLUS validation at the boundary: `request<T>(path, decode: (u: unknown) => T, init?)`. `getTags` becomes `request("/colors/tags", decodeTags)`. Derive the decoders from the same zod schemas that already validate inbound requests in api/, making the contract single-homed in the strong sense (one definition, two directions) rather than the weak one (one type, asserted twice). `availableTags` collapses to `pm.tagEdit.allTags`; the shim and its apology both die; a wire-shape change becomes a loud typed error at the seam instead of a prop warning at a leaf.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure under demo/palettes/browser/` · LP2-3 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** NEW — the published `toRgba8` (@mkbabb/value.js/color) is not channel-symmetric: an achromatic colour projects to a tinted byte triple. Three mathematically identical RGB channels round to [77,76,77] (#4d4c4d), a magenta cast on what must be neutral grey.

**Mechanism.** Two faults compounding: (1) hsv->rgb is not channel-symmetric at s=0, emitting three channels 1-3 ulp apart instead of bit-identical; (2) roundHalfEven's tolerance is scaled by the value's magnitude, so at byte scale it cannot distinguish 'exactly .5' from '0.5 + 2 ulp of upstream conversion error', and it resolves PER CHANNEL what is logically one decision. Net: the library's most depended-on projection is not a pure per-channel map. Structurally this is why the duplicated colour engine (LP2-4) has survived every prior audit — the canonical path is WORSE than the copy on the neutral axis, so nothing ever forced convergence.

**Evidence.**

```
src/color/operations.ts:305-312 `roundHalfEven` gates the half-even branch on `Math.abs(fraction - 0.5) < Number.EPSILON * Math.max(1, Math.abs(value))` — approx 1.70e-14 at 76.5, i.e. ~1 ulp. Measured against dist/subpaths/color.js: for hsv(0,0,0.30000000000000004) the three rgb channels are 76.500000000000042633 / 76.500000000000014211 / 76.500000000000028422, whose |frac-0.5| are 4.2633e-14 / 1.4211e-14 / 2.8422e-14 against tol 1.6986e-14 -> branches false/true/false -> bytes 77/76/77. toRgba8 returns [77,76,77,255]. Rate over UI-emittable ladders: v=k/10 accumulation 2/11; v=k/100 0/101; v=k/255 0/256; v=(k+0.5)/255 67/255, including hsv(0,0,0.5/255) -> [1,0,0] (pure red from a colourless input). 0/200000 over random v — rare-but-exact, which is why sampling tests miss it.
```

**Reproduction.** CONFIRMED against the published surface: `node` importing dist/subpaths/color.js, scripts at scratchpad/gray.mjs plus inline `node -e` probes (all pasted in report §3 LP2-3). UI reachability is a labelled HYPOTHESIS: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:70 sets `:step="0.001"`, and canonical step quantization puts the V-slider .700 detent at `0.001*700 === 0.7000000000000001` (verified in node), which yields bytes [179,178,179] = #b3b2b3 — the value pickerColorToHex (demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:212 via color-model.ts:64) would hand the hex readout and clipboard. I could not confirm reka-ui computes the detent as step*n (no browser).

**Proposed cure.** Make achromaticity structural rather than arithmetic: hsv->rgb at s===0 must emit the value channel three times bit-identically, not compute it three times. Replace roundHalfEven's magnitude-scaled epsilon with one shared rounding decision over the triple (or accept plain half-even on exact .5 and stop treating a float-error window as equality). Add the missing invariant as a property test: for every AnyColor whose RGB channels are equal, toRgba8 returns equal bytes. This must land BEFORE the LP2-4 engine merge.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-20 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `Button variant="…"` is a second dead producer contract. Glass 7 replaced Button's `variant` axis with orthogonal `emphasis` + `tone`; the demo still writes `variant` at 51 sites across 22 files (outline 28, ghost 19, destructive 1, default 1, `primary-audacious` 2 — the last belongs to no vocabulary the producer has ever shipped) against only 4 live `emphasis`/`tone` bindings. The prop falls through to the DOM as a literal invalid attribute and every authored plate collapses to the component default.

**Mechanism.** Structural-typing blindness at the design-system seam (same mechanism as prior L-2, now proven a law rather than one instance): Vue's fallthrough-attr rule makes an unknown prop legal TypeScript, so vue-tsc is green over all 51. The proximate structural cause is demo/ui/'s 19-module pure-alias layer (prior L-4): because every consumer imports `Button` from `../../../ui/button`, the Glass 6→7 upgrade changed NO import specifier anywhere in the demo. The alias layer is a signal absorber — a producer can rename an entire prop axis without any consumer's import changing one character.

**Evidence.**

```
node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts declares exactly `emphasis?: ButtonEmphasis("primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text") · tone?: Tone · size · iconOnly · loading · type · disabled · class` — no `variant`. Runtime: `node -e "s=fs.readFileSync('node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button.js','utf8'); console.log(s.match(/variant:\{[^}]*\}/g))"` → NONE. Census (python parse of every <Button> tag in demo/**/*.vue): Button variant 51 across 22 files; Button emphasis 2; Button tone 2. Live probe (playwright, http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, 1440×900): {"domVariantAttrCount":3,"domVariantAttrTags":["BUTTON[variant=outline]","BUTTON[variant=ghost]","BUTTON[variant=outline]"],"buttonsWithVariantAttr":[{"label":"Login","attrVariant":"outline","dataEmphasis":"secondary","dataTone":"neutral"},{"label":"@mbabb","attrVariant":"ghost","dataEmphasis":"secondary","dataTone":"neutral"},{"label":"(nameless)","attrVariant":"outline","dataEmphasis":"secondary","dataTone":"neutral"}],"dataEmphasisNodes":3}. Sites: demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:134,151,159. Producer documents the migration in Badge.vue.d.ts: "Replaces the former variant=\"destructive|success|warning|info\" (a tone is not a style)."
```

**Reproduction.** 1) dev server at http://localhost:9000; 2) node scratchpad probe: chromium → /#/palettes → `document.querySelectorAll('button[variant]')` returns 3 nodes each carrying a literal `variant` attribute AND `data-emphasis="secondary" data-tone="neutral"`; `outline` and `ghost` render identically. Static: `cat node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts` (no `variant`), `grep -c 'variant=' ` census above.

**Proposed cure.** Delete demo/ui/ entirely (19 zero-logic barrels) so the specifier is `@mkbabb/glass-ui/button` at every call site, and codemod the axis IN THE SAME COMMIT: variant="outline"|"ghost" → emphasis="secondary"|"quiet"; variant="destructive" → tone="destructive"; variant="default" → omit; `primary-audacious` → emphasis="primary" plus a named plate shipped in glass-ui (edict 4), never a string the producer ignores. Then make the seam nominal (prior L-2's cure) — a `satisfies ButtonProps` object or excess-property-checked spread — so site 51 fails the build instead of the eye.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-22 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The palette feature's five injection keys are colocated with a 275-line provider that value-imports 16 composables, so importing a CONTRACT drags its entire IMPLEMENTATION cone. This directly amends prior finding L-7's cure, which instructs this component to inject LIBRARY_PORT_KEY / COLOR_TARGET_PORT_KEY.

**Mechanism.** An injection key is a contract; a provider is an implementation. Colocating them makes every consumer of the contract depend on the whole implementation cone. The repo already contains the correct idiom and this very component already uses it — demo/color-session/keys.ts is keys-and-types only (every import an `import type`), and CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:173 + useSwatchActions.ts:4 each reach it for 27 lines. The palettes feature does the opposite of its sibling.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts is 275 lines; :271-275 declare SESSION_PORT_KEY, LIBRARY_PORT_KEY, BROWSE_PORT_KEY, ADMIN_PORT_KEY, COLOR_TARGET_PORT_KEY in the same module as providePalettePorts, which value-imports 16 composables (usePaletteStore, useBrowsePalettes, useAdminUsers, useAdminAudit, useAdminFlagged, useAdminTags, useVersionHistory, useTagEdit, useSlugMigration, useColorNameQueue, usePaletteActions, useFilteredList + 3 auth). Measured transitive relative-import walk, value (non-type-only) edges only: demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts → 26 modules / 2,971 LoC; demo/color-session/keys.ts → 1 module / 27 LoC. (Full graph incl. type-only edges: 92/9,482 vs 18/2,035 — keys.ts's cone is entirely type-only and erases at build.) Five shell/dock modules already pay the bill for one Symbol: Dock.vue:18, DockViewSelect.vue:8, layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:5, menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:13, menus/ProfileSection.vue:14.
```

**Reproduction.** wc -l demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts → 275; sed -n '1,19p' shows 16 value imports + one `import type { ViewId }`; python transitive walk (value edges only) → 26 modules / 2971 LoC vs 1 / 27 for demo/color-session/keys.ts; grep -rn 'palettes/usePalettePorts' demo/shell → 5 files importing SESSION_PORT_KEY.

**Proposed cure.** Split demo/palettes/ports.ts (the five InjectionKey symbols + the port interfaces, `import type` only, ~60 lines) from demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts (the provider). Consumers import the former; only the app root imports the latter. Mechanical file split, zero behaviour delta, identical in shape to demo/color-session/keys.ts — and it makes prior L-7's cure (inject instead of prop-drill 4 props / 8 emits) free rather than expensive.

### `implementation (CHALLENGE-C) — demo/palettes/browser/admin/A` · C-2 · implementation (CHALLENGE-C)

**Defect.** All five `variant=` props on this panel are inert. glass-ui 7.0.0's Button has no `variant` prop (its axes are `emphasis` + `tone`), so `variant="outline"`/`"ghost"` fall through to the DOM as dead attributes while `data-emphasis`/`data-tone` stay at defaults — Approve and Reject render as the SAME button. The destructive register is instead hand-rolled as a 5-utility per-instance class string, duplicated at :64 and :109.

**Mechanism.** un-migrated pre-Glass-7 API kept alive as a no-op, with per-instance utility classes substituting for the library's own semantic axis

**Evidence.**

```
Rendered from a real mount: `<button data-slot="button" data-emphasis="secondary" data-tone="neutral" data-size="sm" ... variant="outline"> Retry <` (note `size` WAS consumed, `variant` was not). API: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19 (no `variant`); axes.d.ts:16-17 — TONES includes "destructive" with the docstring 'the semantic status register …; NEVER a `variant` member'. Sites: AdminNamesPanel.vue:37,55,61,87,106 and class strings :64,:109. Repo-wide `grep -rn 'variant="\(outline\|ghost\|default\|destructive\|secondary\|link\)"' demo/ | wc -l` → 66. Gate is blind: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → EXIT=0.
```

**Proposed cure.** Delete all 5 `variant=` props and both hand-rolled class strings; express the intent in the library's axes — `emphasis="quiet" tone="destructive" size="sm" icon-only` for reject/delete, `emphasis="secondary"` for approve/retry. `h-7 px-2` dies with them (glass-ui ships `iconOnly` + the size ladder). Repo-wide this is a 66-site migration; make it a wave, and add a lint or codegen guard so an unknown prop on a glass primitive fails the typecheck.

**Defect.** All three moderation mutations swallow their failures into `console.warn` and set no state — the panel maintains a full error idiom for READS and none for WRITES. A failed reject leaves the row in place with no message; the operator cannot distinguish 'rejected' from 'silently failed'.

```

Contrast the read path :44,:61 which sets queueLoadError/approvedLoadError, rendered prominently at AdminNamesPanel.vue:30-41 and :80-91. Aggravated by availability.ts:188-195, which throws BEFORE issuing a request during the latch cooldown, making the failed click indistinguishable from a no-op.

**Reproduction.** NONE (hypothesis for the exact user-visible sequence; the code path is certain). To exhibit: route `POST **/admin/colors/*/reject` to a 500 and click Reject — the row remains, nothing is shown, one console.warn is emitted.

**Proposed cure.** Add `mutationError: Ref<string|null>` to the port, set in each catch and cleared on the next success; the panel renders it once as a `role="alert"` line above the list. Optimistic removal already happens after the await, so only the failure needs a voice.

### `implementation (CHALLENGE-C) — demo/palettes/browser/admin/A` · C-5 · implementation (CHALLENGE-C)

**Defect.** False-empty: with no admin token the loaders early-return without setting loading, error, or any flag, so the panel falls through to the empty plate and asserts '· QUEUE CLEAR · No pending proposals.' when no request was ever issued. The admin route is reachable in that state because the loader watcher is `immediate` while the sign-out guard is not.

**Mechanism.** a designed state (true-empty) used to mask an un-attempted one — a masking fallback, edict 2

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/useColorNameQueue.ts:36-37 and :52-53 (`const token = getAdminToken(); if (!token) return;`). Rendered proof already in the mega-tranche's own capture: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-names.png shows an UNAUTHENTICATED page (dock shows 'Login') at /#/admin/names displaying 'Pending · 0 / Approved · 0' and '· QUEUE CLEAR · / No pending proposals.'. Route reachability: demo/color-picker/composables/usePaletteWiring.ts:148-155 fires the loaders with `{immediate:true}`; the anonymous-eviction watcher at :169-173 is not immediate.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/admin/names with no `palette-admin-token` in localStorage. Panel renders the moderation surface and claims the queue is clear; zero network requests are made. (Confirmed live: my first probe recorded `calls: []` with the panel rendered.)

**Proposed cure.** `if (!token) { queueLoadError.value = 'Not signed in as an administrator.'; return; }`, or better: do not mount the moderation panels without a token and make the eviction watcher `immediate`. 'Empty' must mean the server said zero.

### `implementation (CHALLENGE-C) — demo/palettes/browser/admin/A` · C-6 · implementation (CHALLENGE-C)

**Defect.** Raw transport `e.message` is forwarded verbatim into user-facing copy. On the live route this renders a 484-character developer paragraph — shell commands and env-var instructions — as the body of the moderation panel.

**Mechanism.** no error-to-copy mapping layer — the view renders whatever string the transport threw

**Evidence.**

```
useColorNameQueue.ts:44,:61 (`e?.message ?? 'Backend unreachable'`) → AdminNamesPanel.vue:34,:84 (`:detail="pendingError"`) → EmptyState.vue:23-25 prints it unedited. Live measurement at http://localhost:9000/#/admin/names: `alertLens: [37, 484]`, body = 'The proposal queue is unreachable. value.js dev is MISCONFIGURED: … Run `npm run dev` (the full local stack via scripts/dev.sh up) …'. Screenshot: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminNamesPanel/probe-C-error-state.png.
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/admin/names with an admin token seeded and no VITE_API_URL (the dev-misconfig latch, availability.ts:118-131). The 12-line paragraph fills the Names card. In production the same slot carries ApiProblem detail and raw `TypeError: Failed to fetch`.

**Proposed cure.** Map, do not forward. The transport already throws typed errors (`DevMisconfigError`, `ApiUnavailableError`, `ApiProblem`); the port selects one human sentence per class and keeps the machine text for the console. `detail` should carry an actionable token (status code / correlation id), never prose.

**Proposed cure.** Read the reactive `apiAvailability` cell (availability.ts:47) and make the latch visible: disable Retry with a 'retry in Ns' label during the cooldown, or guarantee the click always produces an observable transition (skeleton → result) plus a polite live-region announcement of the outcome.

**Defect.** The tab strip is an UNNAMED role=group of aria-pressed toggle buttons controlling zero tabpanels — no `aria-controls`, no `role=tabpanel`, no accessible group name — even though glass-ui's SegmentedTabs ships `semantics="tabs"`, per-option `controls`, and `ariaLabel` for exactly this case.

Live at /#/admin/names: `tabs: [{role:null, ariaPressed:"true", ariaControls:null}, {role:null, ariaPressed:"false", ariaControls:null}]`, `groupAriaLabel: null`, `groupLabelledby: null`, `tabpanels: 0`. Mount confirms: `aria-live = 0 | role=tabpanel = 0 | aria-controls = 0`. Library API quotes: `controls` — 'completing the APG tablist↔tabpanel linkage for consumers that own a panel'; `ariaLabel` — 'Accessible name shared by the desktop strip and responsive Select'.
```

**Reproduction.** probe-C-mount.test.ts case D (green) and the live snapshot above; the panel bodies at :24 and :75 are bare `<div class="min-w-0">` with no id or role.

**Proposed cure.** Four lines: `semantics="tabs"`, `aria-label="Color name queue"`, `controls: 'names-pending' | 'names-approved'` on the options, and `id` + `role="tabpanel"` + `tabindex="0"` on the two bodies.

### `implementation (CHALLENGE-C) — demo/palettes/browser/admin/A` · C-9 · implementation (CHALLENGE-C)

**Defect.** The loading state is simultaneously unannounced and triple-announced: `aria-label` sits on a role-less `<div>` (prohibited on ARIA `generic`, so ignored by AT), while the three skeleton children each carry their own `role="status" aria-label="Loading"`. Nothing at all is announced when the load resolves or when a row is approved away.

**Mechanism.** naming an element that cannot be named, plus live-region multiplication in a v-for

**Evidence.**

```
AdminNamesPanel.vue:26 and :76. Measured from a mount: `loading wrapper: tag = DIV | role = NONE | nested role=status count = 3`, and `aria-live = 0` for the whole panel. Spec: WAI-ARIA 1.2 lists `generic` among the roles for which `aria-label` is prohibited; HTML-AAM maps `<div>` → `generic`. The sibling panel does it correctly — AdminTagsPanel.vue:51-56 puts `role="status"` on the equivalent wrapper. Skeleton source: AdminListSkeleton.vue:10-13.
```

**Reproduction.** probe-C-mount.test.ts case B (green): `w.find('[aria-label="Loading pending proposals"]').attributes('role')` is undefined and the element is a DIV; three nested `[role=status]` are present.

**Proposed cure.** One `role="status" aria-live="polite"` wrapper per list region that owns both the loading text and the settled result text ('3 pending proposals'); AdminListSkeleton drops its per-instance `role="status"` (decorative once the container speaks). Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox if the Skeleton primitive itself is touched.

### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, depende` · L-12 · L

**Defect.** The unauthenticated state is costumed as an empty roster. `useAdminUsers.ts:52-54` returns before touching `loadingUsers` OR `usersLoadError`, so the panel takes AdminUsersPanel.vue:63 and renders the TRUE-EMPTY plate ('· roster clear ·' / 'No users found.') plus an authoritative '0 users' count for a roster it never requested. The A-3 guard at :5-10 is defeated by the same hole: it gates on `loading`, which never becomes true on this path.

**Mechanism.** Authorization is a ROUTE precondition modelled as a per-method silent early return. The precondition has no home, so it is re-asserted 22 times, and the one place it matters (the panel's state model) never learns about it — the panel models 3 states (loading/error/empty) where the domain has 4.

**Evidence.**

```

**Reproduction.** CONFIRMED end to end: (1) ensure localStorage has no 'palette-admin-token'; (2) navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users; (3) network log filtered users|/api/ is EMPTY — no request was ever issued; (4) DOM contains 'No users found' and the toolbar reads '0 users'. The app knows it is logged out (the dock says 'Login') while the panel asserts the roster is clear.

**Proposed cure.** One gate at the composition boundary: an `auth: "admin"` flag in demo/shell/viewSchema.ts honoured once in useViewManager, or an <AdminGate> in AdminPane.vue, rendering an authentication plate when !isAdminAuthenticated. ### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, depende` · L-4 · L

**Defect.** 51 dead `variant` props on `<Button>` across 22 demo files (5 in the subject). glass-ui 7.0.0 ButtonProps declares emphasis/tone/size/iconOnly/loading — there is NO `variant`. Every such button renders at the default emphasis and the prop falls through onto the DOM as an inert HTML attribute. The subject speaks BOTH vocabularies 40 lines apart: dead `variant` at :22,33,58,114,123 and correct Glass 7 `emphasis`/`tone` at :174,175. Concretely damaging: the W5-12/F-8 intent documented at :107-111 ('the per-row destructive is quieted to ink-at-rest — red arrives on hover/focus, never as 5 resting beacons down the list') was expressed as variant="ghost" and is therefore SILENTLY REVERTED — the row delete renders at the same emphasis as the 'Palettes' button beside it.

**Mechanism.** The design-system public surface changed at the 6->7 upgrade and this component was only half-migrated. Nothing can catch it: Vue treats an undeclared attribute on a component as a fallthrough attr, so vue-tsc does not flag it, and eslint.config.js has no rule in this space — CI is documented fully green at HEAD (db77dbd8) while all 51 sites ship.

**Evidence.**

```
node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19 (no `variant` member). LIVE DOM measurement, http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users: {"text":"Prune empty","attrs":["data-slot=\"button\"","data-emphasis=\"secondary\"","data-tone=\"neutral\"","data-size=\"sm\"",…,"variant=\"outline\"",…]} and the same for "Refresh" — data-emphasis="secondary" is glass-ui's DEFAULT, and variant="outline" is a fallthrough attribute styling nothing. Fleet count (own python regex over every `<Button …>` tag-open in demo/**/*.vue): 51 sites across 22 files; 5 in AdminUsersPanel.vue at lines 22,33,58,114,123.
```

**Reproduction.** CONFIRMED: navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users and evaluate `[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(b=>/Prune|Refresh/i.test(b.textContent)).map(b=>[...b.attributes].map(a=>a.name+'='+a.value))` — both buttons show data-emphasis="secondary" alongside a stray variant="outline".

**Proposed cure.** Mechanical rewrite: outline->emphasis="secondary", ghost->emphasis="quiet", destructive->tone="destructive", default->emphasis="primary" (row delete becomes emphasis="quiet" tone="destructive", which also retires its two per-instance hover:text-destructive utilities). Structural: wire the installed, unused `vue/no-restricted-static-attribute` ({key:'variant', element:'Button'}) so the drift cannot recur. Relay to glass-ui BH: the rename shipped with no consumer trap — request `variant?: never` or inheritAttrs:false + an explicit allowlist so an unrecognised design-token prop is a VISIBLE no-op.

### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, depende` · L-1 · L

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/useAdminTags.ts:49-51 — `const token = getToken(); if (!token) return;` mutates nothing (loading stays false, loadError stays null, tags stays []), so AdminTagsPanel.vue:52/:69 are both false and :82 renders `eyebrow="· no tags minted ·" message="No tags yet."`. Live: browser_network_requests(filter "admin|tags|colors") on /#/admin/tags returned EMPTY — no request is issued at all. Contradicted by the component's own comment at AdminTagsPanel.vue:67. Family measured: `grep -rn "if (!token) return" demo | wc -l` → 21, across useAdminTags.ts:51,:89 · useColorNameQueue.ts:37,:53,:70,:83,:94 · useAdminAudit.ts:50 · useAdminFlagged.ts:61,:83,:95 · useAdminUsers.ts:56,:73,:84,:107,:118,:133,:146,:159(`return []`),:171,:181(`return 0`).
```

**Reproduction.** Fresh browser profile (no `palette-admin-token` in localStorage) → http://localhost:9000/#/admin/tags → panel renders "0 tags" + "· no tags minted ·" + "No tags yet." with zero network requests. The 60-capture visual-audit matrix IS this render (dock shows "Login"). Full live re-confirmation of the no-token path was impeded by a polluted Playwright profile that restores a stale FAKE-AUDIT-TOKEN, so the finding rests on the captured matrix plus the source, not on inference.

### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, depende` · L-4 · L

**Defect.** `ADMIN_PORT_KEY` is a 34-member god port; the panel injects the whole surface to read one member. The "dissolved" god facade grew.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured: `awk 'NR>=195 && NR<=231' demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts | grep -cE "^\s+[a-zA-Z]+[,:]"` → 34 (adminPort); the same over 157-192 → 32 (browsePort). ### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, depende` · L-5 · L

**Defect.** Injection keys are colocated with the provider, so every leaf statically imports the composition root — and the state layer imports and imperatively drives the view layer, closing a type-level cycle.

**Mechanism.** Wrong direction of dependency. The composable owns a handle to a component instance and mutates the view, instead of the view reading state. (b) demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:14 — `import type { AdminUsersPanel } from "./browser/admin"` — then drives the component from the state layer at :99 (`adminUsersPanelRef.value?.updatePaletteTier(...)`), :121, :136, :150. (ii) Delete adminUsersPanelRef and its four imperative calls: updatePaletteTier / removeUserPalette / clearUserPalettes are mutations of state useAdminUsers already owns (plus a per-user palette map it should own), so the panel re-renders because state changed — which is the only reason the composable exists.

### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, depende` · L-6 · L

**Defect.** Two live import paths to the same design system; `demo/ui/` is 20 pure alias barrels and 24 files use both paths at once.

**Mechanism.** A pass-through re-export barrel is an alias — standing edict 2 verbatim ("no aliases, migration shims, dual paths"). Converting the barrels from local re-implementations to re-exports removed the duplication but left the alias. Second order: the barrels flatten glass-ui's subpath map (Input is really at /forms, Chip at /chip, Skeleton at the root), so a reader cannot see which glass-ui capsules a component depends on — which is why Chip was never found (L-2).

**Evidence.**

```
All 20 files under demo/ui/*/index.ts are pass-through re-exports, e.g. `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`, `export { Input } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/forms";`, `export { Skeleton } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. Measured: `grep -rl "@mkbabb/glass-ui" demo | wc -l` → 82 (direct); barrel importers → 48; files doing BOTH → 24. The subject's own siblings are among them: AdminNamesPanel.vue:124 takes SegmentedTabs from @mkbabb/glass-ui/tabs while :125 takes Button from ../../../ui/button; AdminUsersPanel.vue:197 takes the dialog cluster from @mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog while :188-189 take Button/Badge from barrels. demo/ui/alert/index.ts documents its own history as a converted shim.
```

**Reproduction.** Run the three greps above; open any of the 24 dual-path files (AdminNamesPanel.vue and AdminUsersPanel.vue are the nearest).

**Proposed cure.** Delete demo/ui/ (20 files, ~20 lines total) and rewrite the 48 barrel importers to real glass-ui subpaths. Mechanical, behaviour-neutral, and it makes L-2-class duplication visible at the import line.

### `CHALLENGE-C — assume the implementation is defective; find t` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** In hex mode all four channel meters render EMPTY and every slider's aria-valuetext loses its value, leaving screen-reader users with only the raw 16-digit aria-valuenow — precisely the failure the U-F27/BR-4 announcement gate exists to prevent. Root cause is a duplicated computed: the component re-derives the row list locally WITHOUT the hex guard the pipeline's own copy has.

**Mechanism.** duplicated derivation with divergent guards — two paths to one fact, the live one is the broken one

**Evidence.**

```
MEASURED on a clean load of /#/?space=hex&color=%23ff8800 (probe3.mjs): hexMeters ["","","",""]; per-thumb (probe.mjs): R channel/valuetext "Red"/valuenow "1"/meter ""; G channel/"Green"/"0.5333333333333333"/""; B channel/"Blue"/"0"/""; ALPHA channel/"Alpha"/"1"/"". Screenshot at scratchpad/hex-console.png shows the blank meter column. MECHANISM: ComponentSliders.vue:120-125 builds componentEntries from PICKER_CHANNELS[currentColorSpace] where resolveColorSpace("hex")==="rgb" (color-model.ts:32-34), so 4 rows render; but the meter source short-circuits in hex to a single {hex:...} cell (useSliderGradients.ts:63-68), so meterText's lookup at ComponentSliders.vue:160 misses r/g/b and its alpha fallback is explicitly disabled for hex at :162 — every row returns "" at :167. The pipeline ALREADY publishes the correct guarded version of this computed at useColorPipeline.ts:117-122 (colorComponents), which the component injects around but does not use.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/probe3.mjs — cold-load http://localhost:9000/#/?space=hex&color=%23ff8800, read [...document.querySelectorAll('.channel-meter')].map(m=>m.textContent) => ["","","",""], and read aria-valuetext on the four [role=slider] thumbs => "Red","Green","Blue","Alpha" (no values).

**Proposed cure.** Delete the local componentEntries and consume the pipeline's colorComponents. Hex then renders no channel rows at all — the honest thing, since hex has no channels, it has a string — and the console shows the single hex cell the pipeline already models. The guard divergence is removed by removing the second guard, not by adding a third.

### `CHALLENGE-C — assume the implementation is defective; find t` · D-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The slider-wrapper element map is never pruned. The template's function ref discards Vue's unmount (null) call and no key is ever deleted, so every channel key with no counterpart in the newly selected space keeps pointing at a DETACHED element forever — and both consumers keep iterating them, re-attaching five listeners each on every space change and writing aria-valuetext into dead nodes on every colour edit.

**Mechanism.** DOM mirrored into a hand-managed map with an add-only write path; Vue's unmount signal thrown away

**Evidence.**

```
ComponentSliders.vue:56 — `:ref="(el: any) => { if (el) sliderWrapperEls[component] = el as HTMLElement }"` (the null branch is discarded; nothing ever deletes a key). Consumers iterate the whole map: useSliderTouchGates.ts:53 (Object.entries -> 5 addEventListener each) and useSliderAnnouncements.ts:37 (querySelector + setAttribute). MEASURED PROOF OF RETENTION (probe2.mjs): hold references to the four lab wrappers, change space to rgb in-session — A_before [{L channel, "Lightness 50.0%", connected true},{A channel,"a axis 20.0",true},{B channel,"b axis 10.0",true},{ALPHA,"Alpha 100.0%",true}] -> A_afterSpaceChange [{L channel, valuetext REWRITTEN to "Lightness", connected FALSE},{A channel, REWRITTEN to "a axis", connected FALSE},{B channel,"b axis 10.0",false},{ALPHA,"Alpha 100.0%",false}]. A setAttribute onto a node with isConnected===false is only possible if the map still holds it. b and alpha were NOT rewritten because rgb re-populates those keys and overwrites the entry — the predicted key-collision behaviour, which confirms rather than contradicts the mechanism. BOUND: the union of channel keys across the 17 spaces in picker-color.ts:52-70 plus alpha is 21 (r,g,b,h,s,l,v,w,c,x,y,z,kelvin,i,ct,cp,jz,az,bz,a,alpha), so up to 20 detached reka-Slider subtrees are retained, each with 5 listener closures capturing el, gate and the whole debug object.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/probe2.mjs — on /#/?space=lab&color=lab(50%25%2020%2010) stash [...document.querySelectorAll('.touch-gate-target')] and their thumbs on globalThis, set location.hash to #/?space=rgb&color=rgb(10%2020%2030), wait, then re-read: the L and A entries report isConnected false yet their aria-valuetext has been rewritten by useSliderAnnouncements.apply().

**Proposed cure.** The map is a cache of something Vue already knows. Stop mirroring the DOM: give the v-for row its own small child component that owns its wrapper element and registers/unregisters its own touch gate in onMounted/onUnmounted, so Vue's lifecycle IS the pruning mechanism. (The patch — a delete in the ref's null branch — is strictly inferior; the per-row component also dissolves D-10 and D-11.)

**Defect.** Changing the colour space destroys keyboard focus: the focused slider thumb is unmounted by a container-level :key bump and focus falls to <body>, teleporting a keyboard user to the top of the document.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/picker/cont` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** No pointerId guard: a foreign pointer both steers and terminates the drag. `handleSpectrumMove` predicates only on `isDragging.value`; `handleSpectrumUp`/`handleSpectrumCancel` call `stopDragging()` unconditionally. `capturedPointerId` is tracked but only ever used for releasePointerCapture.

**Mechanism.** Loose parallel pointer state with no ownership invariant — a boolean stands in for pointer identity on a surface that carries `touch-gate-target` and a useTouchGate, i.e. an explicitly multi-touch control.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue:159-166, :177-185 (capturedPointerId declared :78, set :149, read only at :84). Measured (probe/probe5.mjs section P2): {"afterP1":{"left":"10%","top":"10%"},"afterP2Move":{"left":"90%","top":"90%"},"afterP1Continues":{"left":"90%","top":"90%"}}
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/picker-spectrumcanvas/probe/probe5.mjs against http://localhost:9000/ — dispatch pointerdown pid=1 at (10%,10%), then pointermove pid=2 at (90%,90%): the dot follows pointer 2. Then pointerup pid=2: pointer 1's subsequent pointermove to (50%,50%) is ignored. On a phone: rest a thumb on the plate while picking and the picker dies under your finger.

**Proposed cure.** Collapse `isDragging` + `capturedPointerId` + `capturedElement` into ONE `activePointer: { id: number; el: HTMLElement } | null`. Every handler opens `if (activePointer?.id !== event.pointerId) return;`; `isDragging` becomes `activePointer !== null` and ceases to exist as separate state. Three variables to one — the bug becomes unrepresentable rather than guarded.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/picker/cont` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** No button discipline. A right-mouse press picks a colour and takes a pointer capture; if the pointerup is swallowed (context menu dismissed elsewhere) `isDragging` stays true and every buttonless hover over the plate rewrites the colour.

**Mechanism.** The handler treats any pointerdown as a drag start and has no liveness re-check, so recovery depends entirely on a pointerup/pointercancel/lostpointercapture arriving — exactly the event class this repo already knows gets lost (usePointerDebug.forceReleaseAllPointers()'s brute-force recovery walker at usePointerDebug.ts:112+ begins its selector list with `.spectrum-picker`).

**Evidence.**

```
SpectrumCanvas.vue:132-157 (handleSpectrumDown — no button/isPrimary check), :159-166 (no `event.buttons === 0` self-heal). `grep -n "event.button\|isPrimary\|\.buttons" SpectrumCanvas.vue` → no output. Measured (probe/probe6.mjs): real `page.mouse.down({button:"right"})` at 15%/85% changed the label from "saturation 63%, lightness 100%" to "saturation 15%, lightness 85%". Stuck-drag variant: {"afterRightPress":"…20%,80%","afterHover1":"…80%,20%","afterHover2":"…35%,40%"} with buttons:0.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/picker-spectrumcanvas/probe/probe6.mjs — section A uses a real right mouse button and the colour changes; section A' withholds the pointerup and two buttonless hovers each repaint the colour.

**Proposed cure.** `handleSpectrumDown` opens with `if (!event.isPrimary || event.button !== 0) return;`. `handleSpectrumMove` opens with `if (event.buttons === 0) { stopDragging(); return; }` — a standing self-heal so no lost-event class can leave the plate live. The rule, not the patch: the plate accepts exactly one primary left-button pointer and re-checks its own liveness every move.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/picker/cont` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The documented dot-persistence invariant is false. The comment at :58-60 promises the raw coords "persist after mouseup so the dot stays where the user placed it"; measured, they persist for 300 ms and are then wiped by the URL round-trip, and the dot visibly teleports with no user input.

**Mechanism.** Write-origin is being decided by a single-shot boolean rather than by identity. The sentinel is spent by the spectrum's own write, so the URL echo 300ms later reads as external and clears rawS/rawV. Invisible where the roundtrip is lossless (probe P1, default space: 25%/25% held for 1424ms) and glaring where it is lossy.

**Evidence.**

```
SpectrumCanvas.vue:58-75 (boolean sentinel `spectrumIsSource` consumed by one watch) vs demo/color-session/useColorUrl.ts:51-64 (model→URL debounce 300ms) and :72-74 (route.query.color watch → applyUrlToModel → updateModel, with no guard against its own echo). Measured (probe/probe5.mjs section P3, Kelvin space, one pick at s=20%/v=80%, sampled every 100ms with no further input): t=109ms left=20% top=20%; t=209ms left=20% top=20%; t=310ms left=51.1529% top=0%; unchanged thereafter.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/picker-spectrumcanvas/probe/probe5.mjs section P3. Ruled out the other debounced writers: useColorPersistence.ts:94-99 is 200ms and writes localStorage not the model; updateColorComponentDebounced is 500ms and off-path. useColorUrl's 300ms is the only external model writer at that latency.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the boolean. Origin is an identity question, and the pipeline already answers it correctly for stableHue with a reference sentinel (useColorPipeline.ts:57 `lastWrittenModel`, checked at :81). Give the plate the same discipline: store the exact model reference it produced and clear the raw coords iff `model.value !== myLastWrite`. A reference cannot be spent twice, swallowed by a batched flush, or stranded by a throw — which also kills the un-reproduced same-tick batching hazard where a spectrum write and an external write collapse into one watch invocation.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/picker/cont` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The plate writes an HSV pick blindly through `model.value.selectedColorSpace` with no representability check. In the selectable Kelvin space the map is degenerate — the bottom 60% of the plate collapses to a single value — and each pick burns 2–3 ms of synchronous main thread.

**Mechanism.** The component assumes every display space can round-trip a 2-D (s,v) family. Kelvin is a 1-D blackbody locus, and xyzToKelvin's raw-XYZ distance metric never normalises luminance, so dim colours all snap to the 1000 K floor. The plate keeps rendering the dot where the user clicked, so the control lies about what it did.

**Evidence.**

```
SpectrumCanvas.vue:127-129. Kelvin is one-channel (src/color/model.ts:20,66) and selectable (color-model.ts:73-76 spreads PICKER_SPACE_NAMES; ColorSpaceSelector.vue:150 iterates all of it). Measured live (probe/probe6.mjs section C): three picks down the s=50% column at v=50%/30%/10% all read `["1000.0"]` while the dot sits at 50%/50%, 50%/70%, 50%/90%. Sweep (probe/kmap.ts): v=0.6 row and below are 1000 K across all s; 441 sample positions → 135 distinct outputs. Cost (probe/probe4.mjs): pointerdown sync cost default space [0.4,0,0,0.1,0,0] ms vs Kelvin [2,2,3,2.3,1.9,2.1] ms. Isolated (probe/kbench.ts): hsv→kelvin 4.269 ms/op vs hsv→oklch 0.0014 ms/op (~3000×), because xyzToKelvin (src/color/anchors.ts:317-329) is a 39,001-iteration linear search. Rendered proof: probe/kelvin-plate-after-bottom-pick.png — indicator parked in the near-black bottom with a bright-orange fill.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/, switch the space Select to Kelvin, click at s=50% down the v axis three times; the kelvin readout stays 1000.0 while the dot follows the cursor. Scripted: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/picker-spectrumcanvas/probe/probe6.mjs (section C) and probe4.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Two seams. (i) Component-owned: the plate is an HSV s×v instrument — it should write HSV and let the pipeline's display projection handle the selected space; where the selected space cannot round-trip s×v it must present as unavailable, not as a working control that silently discards 60% of its own surface. (ii) Library relay to the src seat: replace xyzToKelvin's 39,001-step scan with a monotone ternary search (~15 evaluations) over a luminance-normalised objective — the un-normalised metric is precisely what drags dim colours to the floor.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/picker/cont` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The dot's border regime is hue-blind. `spectrumLuma(s,v) = v*(1 - s*0.5)` replaces the plate's hue-dependent luminance term with the constant 0.5, so a white border is chosen on bright yellow/green/cyan fields — measured 1.07:1, against WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 for a UI-component boundary.

**Mechanism.** The plate composite is exactly out = v · mix(white, hue, s); mix(white,hue,s)'s luminance ranges from 0.072 (blue) to 0.928 (yellow). One hue-independent constant cannot serve both ends of that range, so the flip predicate is simply wrong across the yellow-through-cyan arc.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/picker/controls/spectrumLuma.ts:20-25 (SPECTRUM_LUMA_FLIP = 0.5, `v * (1 - s * 0.5)`), consumed at useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:53-57. The 2px border is the dot's only boundary against the field (SpectrumCanvas.vue:263). Computed against the exact composite (probe/luma.mjs): h=60 s=1 v=1 → modelLight false → white border on trueLum 0.928 → contrast 1.07 FAIL; h=120 s=1 v=1 → 1.37 FAIL; h=180 s=1 v=1 → 1.25 FAIL; 9/30 sampled (h,s,v) fail. Live (probe/probe7.mjs): yellow top-right pick → dotBorder "rgba(255,255,255,0.9)", dotBg "rgb(250,250,5)"; blue top-right pick → identical white border. Rendered: probe/yellow-corner-dot-border.png (indicator all but invisible) vs probe/blue-corner-dot-border.png (crisp).
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/picker-spectrumcanvas/probe/luma.mjs prints the contrast table; node .../probe/probe7.mjs drives http://localhost:9000/#/?space=hsl&color=hsl(60%20100%25%2050%25), picks the top-right corner and reads the computed border colour.

**Proposed cure.** `spectrumLuma` already receives everything it needs except the hue — pass it and compute the real thing: `v * relLum(mix(white, hslHue(h), s))`, arithmetic the library already ships. Keep the docblock's "one function, one threshold" law; fix the function so the law is worth obeying. Better still, flip on measured contrast rather than a luminance threshold so the predicate answers the question the border is actually asking. Since the dot is a glass-ui WatercolorDot, the cured regime belongs in the producer as a variant/prop (edict 4), not as a deeper consumer override.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/picker/cont` · C-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Zero keyboard operability on a 2-D picker, exposed to assistive technology as a static image, with continuously changing name and no live region.

**Mechanism.** role="img" declares static graphical content, so the element's live name updates (useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:24-28) are announced to nobody, and the control is absent from the keyboard model entirely. The usual mitigation — equivalent function via the sliders — fails here because the sliders expose the SELECTED DISPLAY SPACE's channels (measured on /: L, A, B, ALPHA), not s and v.

**Evidence.**

```
SpectrumCanvas.vue:6-22 (role="img" with five pointer handlers bound to the same element). Measured (probe/probe1.mjs): role "img", tabIndex -1, hasTabindexAttr false, ariaLive null, closestFocusable false, figureHasCaption false, inTabOrder false among 28 focusables. Measured (probe/probe8.mjs): 40 Tab presses cycle the page twice and never reach the plate; after clicking the plate `document.activeElement` is BODY.relative; four arrow presses leave the label at "saturation 21%, lightness 55%" unchanged.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/picker-spectrumcanvas/probe/probe8.mjs sections B and C against http://localhost:9000/.

**Proposed cure.** Adopt the settled 2-D-picker pattern: tabindex="0" plus role="application" (or two coupled role="slider" children), Arrow/Shift+Arrow/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown on both axes, move focus to the plate on pointerdown, and expose the live position through aria-valuetext on the coupled sliders — which ARE announced — instead of a mutating role="img" name.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/picker/cont` · C-7 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Vacuous gates. The only spec that drives the plate asserts nothing about what it produces; a single-token mutation that inverts the vertical axis keeps the entire suite green. No unit test for the plate's maths or its luma regime exists.

**Mechanism.** The spec measures liveness ("did anything change?") and dresses it as correctness (file docblock line 7: "wall-clock evidence that the topology REACTIVITY-B verified is INSTANT"). Every mutation below changes the product and still makes the readout diverge.

**Evidence.**

```
e2e/smoke/reactivity-instant.spec.ts:41-135 asserts only that the readout text diverges from baseline within 2000ms and that the median wall-clock is ≤50ms — never which colour resulted. e2e/smoke/a11y-modality-support.spec.ts:91-119,300-303 certifies forced-color-adjust:none and the presence of a role="img" named /Color spectrum/ — i.e. it locks in the C-6 defect as the expected shape. e2e/smoke/perf/drag-frame-budget.spec.ts:33-70 (the §6.2 p50≤20ms / 0 long-tasks oracle) drives the L-channel SLIDER, not the plate. `grep -rln "spectrumLuma\|useSpectrumPlateStyle\|spectrumFieldIsLight" test/ demo/test/ e2e/` → NONE.
```

**Reproduction.** Named mutations, each one token in SpectrumCanvas.vue:110-130, all GREEN: (a) `const v = clamp(y / rect.height, 0, 1)` at :121 — the picker is vertically inverted; (b) swap s and v at :127 — axes transposed; (c) delete both clamps at :117-118; (d) delete rawS/rawV and the whole watch at :61-75; (e) delete the rAF throttle at :97-108; (f) make spectrumLuma return 0.5 unconditionally.

**Proposed cure.** Three born-RED oracles. (i) Extract the pure `plateCoords(rect, clientX, clientY) → {s,v}` that does not currently exist because the arithmetic is welded between a DOM read and a model write, then table-drive corners, out-of-bounds, zero-width rect and NaN in vitest. (ii) A vitest unit over spectrumLuma/spectrumFieldIsLight asserting ≥3:1 measured contrast across the (h,s,v) grid in probe/luma.mjs — born RED at 9/30 today. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPic` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The Cmd+K handler tests global modifier STATE (`keys.cmd?.value && keys.k?.value`) rather than the event, so any key pressed while Cmd and K are physically held is preventDefault'd and re-toggles the dropdown. There is also no `e.repeat` guard.

**Mechanism.** Chord detection via sampled global key state instead of event inspection — the predicate is true for the whole duration the keys are held, not for the one event that is the chord.

**Evidence.**

```
ColorPicker.vue:263-266. Live probe: hold Meta, hold k (dropdown opens, aria-expanded="true"), then press `a` -> {"A_afterKdown":"true","A_afterOtherKey":"false","A_events":[{"k":"a","meta":true,"rep":false,"dp":true}]}. Cmd+A (Select All) is swallowed AND the color-space dropdown toggles shut on an unrelated keystroke.
```

**Reproduction.** On http://localhost:9000/#/ : page.keyboard.down('Meta'); page.keyboard.down('k'); (dropdown opens) ; page.keyboard.down('a'); page.keyboard.up('a'). The keydown for `a` reports defaultPrevented=true and the trigger's aria-expanded flips true->false.

**Proposed cure.** Test the event: `if (e.key === "k" && (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && !e.repeat)`. The `useMagicKeys()` import (ColorPicker.vue:123,247) then has no remaining consumer and is deleted with it.

**Defect.** The four channel slider thumbs are 12 CSS px wide at every viewport — WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (Target Size Minimum, 24x24) fails four times. The picker contributes half of the entire application's small-tap-target count on all 60 audit captures.

The touch rung at demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:345-357 grows the SliderRoot's vertical hit box (`block-size: max(100%, 2.75rem)`, `inset-inline: 0`) and never touches the thumb, which is why h goes 24->44 on coarse pointers while w stays 12.

Scrolling the card its full 64px (scrollTop=64) leaves condensedClass=false. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPic` · C-8 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The picker cancels its parent's shared, app-wide debounced writes on its own unmount — an ownership inversion that silently drops in-flight color changes belonging to sibling components.

**Mechanism.** A child disposing state it did not create: cleanup responsibility placed on the consumer instead of the owning composable's own scope.

ColorPicker.vue:381-385 calls `parseAndSetColorDebounced.cancel()` and `updateColorComponentDebounced.cancel()`. The pane KeepAlive is `:max="6"` (App.vue:104) over 7 distinct left panes (color-picker, browse, extract, generate, gradient, atmosphere, admin-*), so the picker IS LRU-evictable. The parse debounce window is 2000ms (useColorParsing.ts:92).
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — hypothesis on the observable drop. The ownership violation itself is direct from the cited lines; the concrete drop requires evicting the picker from the 6-slot LRU while a 2000ms parse debounce is pending, which I did not drive.

The producer renders its canvas unconditionally (blob.js: D("canvas",{class:"goo-blob-canvas"}) with no v-if), so canvas 2→1 means the whole subtree never mounted.

**Reproduction.** PARTIAL — the observed failure is the recorded Safari capture (REPORT.json /#/ safari-desktop-light + shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png). I could NOT force it in Chromium: probe-C2 (synthetic webglcontextlost @400ms), probe-C3 (WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext @400/900ms), probe-C4 (getContext patched pre-boot, loss @500/1000/3000ms) all left b2 latching normally (overture:b2@1360..1502) and the blob mounted (canvasCount 2). C4's ctxLog shows the app's first webgl2 context is created at ~126-175ms on a canvas with empty className, so the atmosphere key never matched. The source chain is confirmed by read; the Safari trigger is not yet pinned.

**Proposed cure.** Two independent moves: (a) gate b4 on paint-completion rather than the field's GPU arrival — b3Complete ∧ dockLanded already satisfies the beat DAG's stated order, so the ornament stops depending on an unrelated GPU surface; (b) give the blob the atmosphere's honest terminal by subscribing the producer's SHIPPED `rendererStatus` expose, and on a non-ok status keep the .hero-blob-anchor::before contact shadow as the seated ornament instead of nothing.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-05 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The P019 identity/specimen type pair is at the required 1/√φ only at the phone floor; it drifts to near-parity at 1440, so at desktop the label and the numeric specimen are optically the same size.

**Mechanism.** Two independently clamped sources with different binding arms cannot hold a constant ratio. The register (V-A140) describes this as a fixed two-rung skip; the rendered truth is a ratio that is exactly right at one end of the band and collapses at the other — worse than documented.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured label font-size / headline font-size: 390x844 → 32.928 / 41.888 = 0.7861 (required 1/√φ = 0.78615, correct); 1440x900 → 53.280 / 54.644 = 0.9750. Drift +24.0% across the band. Sources: label = --type-display-2 = clamp(2.058rem, 1.5rem + 2.2vw, 3.33rem) at ColorSpaceSelector.vue:209 (ceiling-bound at 1440); headline = calc(min(var(--type-display-4), max(11.65cqi, 2.618rem)) * var(--readout-fit,1)) at ColorComponentDisplay.vue:137-140 (floor-bound at 390, 11.65cqi-bound at 1440 — --type-display-4 resolves to 86.11px and never binds). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.2: "BI P019 supplies one paired proportional clamp; both sizes resolve from that one clamp … rather than only at endpoints" and "independently clamped display-2/display-3 tokens and a local approximation are forbidden."
```

**Reproduction.** On the settled / route read parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.space-trigger')).fontSize) / parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.readout')).fontSize) at 390x844 (0.7861) and at 1440x900 (0.9750).

**Proposed cure.** One shared P019 paired clamp: derive both arms from a single fluid quantity so label = headline / √φ identically through floor, fluid and ceiling. Delete the local 11.65cqi mint and the independent --type-display-2 claim; the pair becomes one token consumption, not two.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-05 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The instrument has no boundary of its own, and in every colour scheme part of it dissolves into the card. No border, no ring, at-rest box-shadow fully transparent; the plate's own content supplies #fff and #000 at its extremes so its edge can never be self-evident.

At-rest computed boxShadow "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) 0px 0px 0px 0px" (probe/SPCD-probe1.json). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 "One surface has one tier" — the plate is assigned no tier in the material table.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-07 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** 20.6 ms of style recalculation per committed pointer move against a 16.7 ms frame budget, plus 2.76 layouts per move where idle is 0. Two of the three causes are authored in this component: a per-frame write of the INHERITED custom property --spectrum-shadow (whose only consumer is a hover-only decoration), and moving the marker with layout-inducing left/top percentages on an element carrying an SVG feDisplacementMap.

**Mechanism.** An inherited custom property write invalidates the whole subtree's computed style every frame; left/top are layout-inducing where translate/transform are not. The producer went to real trouble to keep this element compositor-only and the consumer reintroduces per-frame layout on it.

**Evidence.**

```
CDP Performance.getMetrics, Chromium 1440×900, 80 synthetic moves (probe/SPCD-probe3.json): plate drag 6732ms wall → LayoutCount 221, RecalcStyleCount 1152, RecalcStyleDuration 1768.9ms, LayoutDuration 67.1ms. Channel-slider drag (identical session update) 5477ms → 151 / 746 / 1200.1ms / 43.8ms. Wall-matched idle 6734ms → LayoutCount **0**, 344, 122.8ms. Net of idle: 1646ms ÷ 80 moves = 20.6 ms/move; plate is 1.49× the slider's per-move cost. Sources: useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:40 (--spectrum-shadow), :60-61 (left/top), consumed only by SpectrumCanvas.vue:236. Producer warning: useWatercolorBlob.d.ts documents that per-frame writes under the SVG filter force filter-graph re-rasterisation and flash Safari, which is why the producer's own liveness rides a compositor transform.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/SPCD-probe3.mjs — section 2 runs an 80-move drag on the plate, an 80-move drag on a channel slider, and a wall-matched idle control, reading Performance.getMetrics deltas around each.

**Proposed cure.** Delete --spectrum-shadow together with D-16's hover shadow (it exists only to feed it). Move the marker with the independent `translate` property composed against the producer's wobble — the same mechanism Tailwind already emits — so the marker never touches layout. Both changes are subtractions.

Owner edicts 5 and 2.

**Defect.** One ornament is described by five different sizes and none of them is its painted mass; its canvas box escapes the card on all four sides and escapes the viewport at 390.

**Mechanism.** The producer's 1.6x canvas overscan was never reconciled with the seat's layout footprint, and the two hand-written reservations (0.76*fp padding, 0.76*fp-0.75rem min-height) were sized from the footprint rather than from the painted body. **Evidence.**

```
Live measurement (scratchpad/HBD-geo.json), 1440: canvas 180.19x180.19 at (564.59,113.72,right 744.78) vs card (199,147.5,right 711) — 33.78px overhang on every side at z-index 20; layout footprint --blob-fp 112.63 (seat.css:43); padding reservation 93.12px (seat.css:88); min-height reservation 73.12px (seat.css:89); rendered painted body diameter 75.09px. Footprint = 112/358 = 31.3% of the card width; padding = 93.12/327.38 = 28.4% of the title row.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-9 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The emerge pose and the engine arm are sequenced backwards, and the repair for that inversion uses a pause seam as a resize API and lands a 537ms long task.

**Mechanism.** The engine arms inside a container that is actively lying about its box, so it presizes from a transformed gBCR (measured historically at dpr2: 126x126 backing for a 180.2px box) and the idle park freezes the low-res frame; the consumer then repairs the consequence instead of removing the cause.

**Evidence.**

```
overture.css:167-178 animates .hero-blob-anchor from scale(0.35) AFTER HeroBlob mounts; HeroBlob.vue:297-316 onEmergeEnd fires pause();resume() to force a backing-store re-measure, conceding "resume() re-measures via idempotent resize() on the was-suspended path". defineExpose offers nudge,setMood,pulse,currentMood,pause,resume,settled,settledFrame,rendererStatus — there is no resize. Cost: at CPU 4x the blob arm shows a 537ms long task at t=3802ms; the reduced-motion arm (where the pose is no-preference-wrapped so onEmergeEnd never fires) shows no late long task at all — [154,799][1222,405][1627,55][1858,482][2353,67], all <=2.4s.
```

**Reproduction.** scratchpad/HBD-probe3.mjs at CPU=4 vs scratchpad/HBD-probe4-prm.mjs at CPU=4; compare longTasks. ATTRIBUTION OF THE 537ms TASK IS A STRONGLY-SUPPORTED INFERENCE (one-arm correlation), not a direct trace — labelled as such in the report.

**Proposed cure.** Invert the order: animate an EMPTY settled seat and arm the engine at the pose's end, not before it. That single inversion deletes onEmergeEnd, the animationName filter, the park guard, the pause/resume pair and its 30-line comment; it moves GL init out of the critical band; and it is verbatim what CARRY-LEDGER W54 already asks for — "D-2 blob truthful lifecycle; arm-after-critical-paint 0px".
