### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-13 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The surface is a constitutional orphan: canon assigns sign-in to the Account Dialog owned by W23, not to a dock layer — and hosting it in the dock is the common cause of six other findings.

**Mechanism.** A fragment of `PaletteSlugBar.vue` was transplanted into the dock without its field primitive, error region, state-bearing accessible names or content-fitted placeholder. D-1 (no room for an error region), D-3 (no room for a real field), D-5 (no overlay focus contract), D-6 (no secret region), D-2/D-8 (no persistence) are not five independent oversights — they are five things a Dialog supplies and a 46px inert-able strip of navigation chrome cannot.

**Evidence.**

```
VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 Account: "Account is one modal side Dialog opened from the Dock, not a route chassis or second main. It owns registration/recovery when signed out… secret retention temporarily replaces its action region… W23 owns the rendered composition and journey while W15 supplies auth/outbox state." Measured cost of the dock hosting: activating the layer marks every sibling `.dock-face` `{inert:true, ariaHidden:"true", opacity:"0"}`, so route selector, Tools and profile all vanish for the duration — against §7 Shell: "Direct route changes keep its full navigation identity." Layer intrinsic width 285px (2nd widest of four) inside an aperture that measures `clientWidth 290` at 390 and `234` at 320.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — this is a canon-conformance judgement, not a runtime failure. Its consequences are the reproductions in D-1..D-8.

**Proposed cure.** Retire the component. The dock keeps one control (`Login` / the slug pill) that opens the Account Dialog; the `slug-edit` DockLayer, `Dock.vue`'s `slugEditRef`/`onStartSlugEdit`/`onCopySlug` three-hop round-trip and the `activeLayer` branch die together. The Dialog composes the field from glass-ui, gives the two authorities two affordances, owns one `role="status"` error region, and awaits the port so pending is real. Delete `useSlugMigration`'s `slugBarRef` limb and the unmounted `PaletteSlugBar` in the same cut.

**Defect.** The §4 type-role matrix is broken three ways inside one popover: (a) prose/help rendered in Fraunces italic 11px; (b) `font-display` on the menu content is cascade-dead; (c) iOS text-autosizing boosts the rows 14→21px while the pill and description are untouched, reordering the rungs so the least important rows are the largest type.

Duplicated at ProfileSection.vue:150. (b) line 43 `class="min-w-menu font-display"` — measured computed style of [role=menu] is Fira Code 16px; --font-display resolves correctly to '"Fraunces", "Fraunces Fallback", serif' and the utility DOES work on the <p> in (a), so it is cascade-dead, not a missing font. Same dead class at ProfileSection.vue:70 and :143. (c) Measured same URL, same 390px viewport, one variable (frames/mmd-probe2.json): isMobile true → menuitem 21px/lh 29.4; isMobile false → 14px/lh 19.6; .slug-pill 14px in BOTH; description 11px in BOTH; @mbabb 14px in BOTH. --type-small = clamp(0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.25vw, 1.25rem) → 14px at 390 in both cases, so 21px is a 1.5x boost applied to the rows only.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-mobilemenudropdown/frames/mmd-probe2.mjs → compare type_isMobile_true vs type_isMobile_false. Visual: frames/D-390-light-loggedin-open.png.

Violates edict 6 (an animation deleted by construction rather than by decision) and edict 5 (per-instance inline override where a root-level class belongs).

No global fallback: `grep -rn "crown-appear" demo/` returns exactly 3 hits — ColorInput.vue:38, ColorInput.vue:369, demo/DESIGN.md:213 (prose). demo/styles/animations.css does not contain it.
```

**Reproduction.** 1) `curl -s "http://localhost:9000/@fs/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=55dadc03&lang.css"` — observe the definition is emitted as `crown-appear-55dadc03`. 2) In any live page at http://localhost:9000, evaluate: `[...document.styleSheets].flatMap(s=>{try{return [...s.cssRules]}catch{return []}}).filter(r=>r.type===CSSRule.KEYFRAMES_RULE).map(r=>r.name).includes('crown-appear')` → false.

**Proposed cure.** crown-appear is a design-language beat, not seat geometry: promote it to demo/styles/animations.css (which already exists and is the declared home for global keyframes) and drive it from a `.crown-badge` CLASS. The inline style attribute dies with it. Adopt the rule repo-wide: if the reference is inline, the keyframe must be global; if the keyframe is scoped, the reference must be a class in the same block. SPACE_SCHEMA, SPACE_IDS, isAnyColor and makeColor are written in src/color/model.ts and never re-exported through src/color/index.ts or src/subpaths/color.ts. Consequence: (a) picker-color.ts:123-144 `buildColor` is a 22-line 17-arm switch that IS makeColor(space, channels, alpha); (b) picker-color.ts:52-70 PICKER_CHANNELS re-declares the channel names and hue positions SPACE_SCHEMA already freezes; (c) 'which spaces are CSS-serializable' now has THREE homes with no derivation between them.

**Mechanism.** public surface narrower than the library's own internal abstraction — forced ownership duplication in the consumer (Mechanism D, new to this axis)

**Evidence.**

```
src/color/model.ts:57 (SPACE_SCHEMA), :76 (SPACE_IDS), :127 (isAnyColor), :136 (makeColor) — none appear in src/color/index.ts's export list nor src/subpaths/color.ts. Proven against the bundle: `node -e "const m=await import('./dist/subpaths/color.js'); console.log(typeof m.makeColor, typeof m.SPACE_SCHEMA, typeof m.isAnyColor, typeof m.SPACE_IDS)"` → `undefined undefined undefined undefined`; the 23 actual exports are a98Rgb convertColor displayP3 hsl hsv hwb ictcp interpolateHue jzazbz kelvin lab lch linearSrgb mapColorToGamut mixColors oklab oklch prophotoRgb rec2020 rgb safeAccentColor toRgba8 xyz. Three homes for the CSS-space set: src/color/model.ts:57-75 (`css:` flags) · src/css/grammar.ts:161-164 (CSS_COLOR_SPACES) · demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:92-95 (CSS_PICKER_SPACES) — all 13 spaces, currently agreeing, none derived.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — this is a structural defect proven by the export-surface measurement above, not a runtime failure. The duplication is exact and read directly from both files.

**Proposed cure.** Export SPACE_SCHEMA, SPACE_IDS, makeColor, isAnyColor through src/color/index.ts + src/subpaths/color.ts, and add the channel-domain table (min/max/unit — already normatively specified in docs/tranches/V/ARCHITECTURE.md §2's space table) beside SPACE_SCHEMA. Then CSS_PICKER_SPACES and CSS_COLOR_SPACES both collapse into SPACE_SCHEMA[space].css, buildColor and PICKER_CHANNELS's structural half are deleted, and 17 factory import bindings go with them. Combined with L-1's cure, picker-color.ts drops 217 → ~70 lines (PICKER_SPACE_NAMES, the "hex" display encoding, pickerColorToHex — the only genuinely demo-owned concepts).

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-18 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** picker-color.ts re-derives PickerColorIn<S> = Extract<AnyColor,{space:S}> for a type the library already publishes as the generic Color<S>, and pays with an `as unknown as` erasure on the single conversion funnel this component reads. A second cast at line 208 exists because /css ships no isCssColor narrowing predicate.

**Mechanism.** E — the demo re-derives a surface that is already public, and pays in erased types. Extract<AnyColor,{space:S}> is not provably equal to Color<S> for a generic S (TS cannot distribute the conditional through the unresolved parameter), so the re-derivation forces a cast through `unknown` at the top of the funnel that types convertPickerColor / withChannel / withNormalizedChannel / withAlpha / mapPickerOklabToSrgb — erasing the space↔channel-tuple discriminant for everything ColorInput reads downstream.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:38 (the re-derivation) and :116 (`return valueOrThrow(convertColor(color, space)) as unknown as PickerColorIn<S>;`). The library exports the generic: `grep -oE "^export declare type [A-Za-z_0-9]+" dist/subpaths/color.d.ts` includes `export declare type Color`. Standalone tsc probe with the demo's exact options: arm A (Extract<> shape, no cast) → `error TS2322: Type 'Readonly<{ space: S; channels: ChannelsBySpace[S]; alpha: Alpha; }>' is not assignable to type 'PickerColorIn<S>'`; arm B (Color<S>) → no diagnostic. `grep -rn "PickerColorIn" demo | wc -l` → 23. `grep -rn "as unknown as" demo/color-session/` → exactly one hit, line 116. demo/color-session/ink.ts:6 already imports `type Color` from the library — two spellings of one concept in one directory. `grep -c "isCssColor" dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` → 0.
```

**Reproduction.** cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js; write a probe .ts containing two functions with the identical body `return valueOrThrow(convertColor(color, space));` — one returning PickerColorIn<S> = Extract<AnyColor,{readonly space:S}>, one returning Color<S> imported from @mkbabb/value.js/color. Run: `npx tsc --ignoreConfig --noEmit --strict --target ES2022 --module ESNext --moduleResolution bundler --verbatimModuleSyntax --lib ES2023,DOM --skipLibCheck <probe>.ts`. Arm A errors TS2322; arm B is clean.

**Proposed cure.** Delete PickerColorIn; use the library's exported Color<S> at all 23 sites. The `as unknown as` dies with it — a net deletion, no new abstraction. File `isCssColor(c): c is CssColor` as a /css addendum (E-3, addenda-not-patch), which retires CSS_PICKER_SPACES and the line-208 cast together. Cure jointly with the prior pass's L-14 (export SPACE_SCHEMA/SPACE_IDS/makeColor/isAnyColor): picker-color.ts then loses buildColor's 17-arm switch, both hand-rolled aliases and both casts in one cut.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-19 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The Vite composition root is a FEATURE directory (demo/color-picker/) while the entire app tree lives one level up at demo/, so 137 of the app's own modules are served through Vite's /@fs/ filesystem-escape route. One source tree, two live URL namespaces — which produced a blocking ENOENT overlay during this audit.

**Mechanism.** F — the composition root is a feature directory. Because it is also the server root, every non-root module is addressable by two different URL forms (/X.vue resolved against demo/color-picker/, and /@fs/<abs>/demo/X.vue), and any tool that picks the wrong one resolves to a path that has never existed.

**Evidence.**

```
vite.config.ts sets `root: "./demo/color-picker/"` for both dev and gh-pages. `ls demo/color-picker/` → App.vue, ErrorBoundary.vue, composables/, index.html, public/, router/ only; shell/, color-session/, picker/, palettes/, workbenches/, scenes/, platform/, shared/, styles/, ui/ are all at demo/. Live resource-timing measurement on /#/: {total: 250, viaAtFs: 227, demoModulesViaAtFs: 137, rootRelativeSample: ["/router/index.ts","/App.vue","/ErrorBoundary.vue","/composables/usePaletteWiring.ts",...]}. Observed vite-error-overlay text: "ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue' at getDescriptor (…/@vitejs/plugin-vue/dist/index.mjs:80:72)" plus 22 sibling `[vite] Failed to reload /@fs/…` console errors including ColorInput's. Authority: docs/tranches/V/ARCHITECTURE.md:9 names the composition root `demo/app/`; :10-11 puts the pre-paint seed at demo/public/; :41 lists `color-picker` as one of eleven ROUTES, not the shell.
```

**Reproduction.** Navigate a browser to http://localhost:9000/#/ and evaluate: `performance.getEntriesByType('resource').map(r=>r.name).filter(n=>n.startsWith('http://localhost:9000/'))` — count entries containing '/@fs/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/' (137 of 250). The ENOENT overlay occurrence was on a long-running dev server (started 10:25AM, probed 13:10) and cleared on hard reload; `git status --porcelain` shows demo/ and src/ clean, so that specific occurrence is a stale-server artefact and is labelled as such — but it is only possible because the two namespaces exist.

**Proposed cure.** Rename demo/color-picker/ → demo/app/ and set Vite `root: "./demo"`. /@fs/ then disappears from the demo graph entirely, the HMR path ambiguity becomes structurally impossible, and ARCHITECTURE.md:9-33's declared physical tree becomes true as written. This is the only finding in the document whose cure moves no logic at all — a directory rename plus a one-line config change.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-5 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Split ownership of the colour-name registry: the READ half is owned by a composable, the WRITE half (an HTTP POST plus session acquisition) is inlined into this dock leaf SFC, which is the only SFC anywhere under demo/shell/ that imports an API call. The write never invalidates the read cache, and it breaks the error-voice policy the read half established.

**Mechanism.** Ownership split of one semantic concept across two homes with opposite architectural altitudes — a composable for read, a leaf SFC for write. Unique semantic ownership violated; the write path has no access to the read path's cache, so the crown indicator reads stale data after a proposal.

**Evidence.**

```
ColorInput.vue:132 imports proposeColorName (POST /colors/propose, demo/color-session/color-names.ts:36-44 over platform/transport/client); ColorInput.vue:230-247 runs session.ensureSession(), the mutation, the optimistic clear and `catch (e: any) { console.warn(...) }` inline. Enumeration: `for f in $(find demo/shell -name '*.vue'); do grep -l "color-names\|/api/\|transport/client" $f; done` → demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue ONLY. The reciprocal read is composable-owned: demo/color-session/useCustomColorNames.ts:19 calls getApprovedColorNames() from the same module and owns customNameRegistry/normalizedCustomNames plus findCustomName/getMetadata/reset. That composable's lines 39-52 establish the house rule for this exact API (dev-only console.debug, never warn/error, so the e2e zero-console-error gate holds); ColorInput.vue:243 uses console.warn.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — static enumeration. The stale-cache consequence is a hypothesis (proposals require moderator approval before entering the approved list, so it may be unobservable in practice); the ownership split and the console.warn policy break are facts at the cited lines.

**Proposed cure.** proposeColorName moves behind useCustomColorNames as `propose(name, css)` — the composable already owns registry state and the error-voice policy and can invalidate its own cache. ColorInput calls propose() and renders `proposing`/`error`. The SFC then imports zero transport modules, which is what `shell → color-session / platform / shared` (ARCHITECTURE.md:47) actually means. Drop the `any`.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-6 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The crown entrance animation is dead by construction: a @keyframes declared inside <style scoped> (hence name-hashed by the SFC compiler) is referenced from an inline style attribute in the template, which the compiler does not rewrite. The animation has never run.

**Mechanism.** Wrong home for the keyframe. A keyframe consumed from outside the scoped block is by definition a global keyframe; placing it inside <style scoped> hashes its name out from under its only consumer. Owner edict 6 (animations are never deleted, only moved or tokenized) is violated in effect — the four-stop gold shimmer was deleted by a scoping accident, and demo/DESIGN.md now records a false fact.

**Evidence.**

```
ColorInput.vue:37-39 template: `style="animation: crown-appear var(--duration-panel) var(--ease-decelerate) forwards;"`. ColorInput.vue:369-376: `@keyframes crown-appear { ... }` inside <style scoped>. @vue/compiler-sfc compileStyle output: crown-appear emitted as `@keyframes crown-appear-55dadc03`, referenced in scoped CSS as: null. Control in the same file: input-mode-flash emitted as `@keyframes input-mode-flash-55dadc03` AND referenced as `animation: input-mode-flash-55dadc03 ...` — correctly rewritten because it is consumed inside the block. Live in the running app with the input layer mounted: {"totalKeyframeNames":54,"crownNames":["crown-appear-55dadc03"],"flashNames":["input-mode-flash-55dadc03"],"crownAnimationsRunning":0} — an element carrying the component's exact declaration returns getAnimations().length === 0. `grep -rn "crown-appear" demo/` → only ColorInput.vue:38, ColorInput.vue:369, and demo/DESIGN.md:213 which documents it as a live --duration-panel consumer.
```

**Reproduction.** Compile-time: `node -e "import {parse,compileStyle} from '@vue/compiler-sfc'" ...` on demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue with id 'data-v-55dadc03', scoped true — grep the output for @keyframes and animation: references. Runtime: open http://localhost:9000/#/, click Toggle action bar then Open color input, then evaluate — enumerate CSSRule.KEYFRAMES_RULE names across document.styleSheets (crown-appear absent, crown-appear-55dadc03 present) and create a div with style.animation='crown-appear 550ms ease forwards' → getAnimations().length === 0. Script: .../scratchpad/CHL-probe2.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Move @keyframes crown-appear to demo/styles/ (the global keyframe home per edict 6 and ARCHITECTURE.md:34) and replace the inline style attribute with a class. The keyframe's real scope is global because its consumer is outside the scoped block; making the home match the scope is the whole fix.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-21 · CHALLENGE-L

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-22 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** MAJOR (new this pass) — the demo contains ZERO link elements. Fifteen routes, no `<a href>`, no `<RouterLink>`; every transition in the product is an imperative `switchView` call, and the primary navigation is a `role=combobox` whose children are `role=option`. vue-router's own navigation primitive is entirely unused.

**Mechanism.** The routing library's link primitive was never adopted; navigation was modelled as 'the selected value of a select' rather than 'a set of destinations'. Nothing is middle-clickable, cmd-clickable, open-in-new-tab-able or crawlable; the product has no link graph. It is also the root of the pass-2 L-13 a11y result (`aria-selected` false on every option, `aria-activedescendant` null on 7 routes): a select with no value to model.

**Evidence.**

```
`grep -rn "RouterLink|router-link" demo --include="*.vue" | wc -l` -> 0. Live: opened listbox reports { expanded: "true", optionCount: 7, options: [Home, Palettes, Browse, Extract, Mix, Generate, Gradient] } against 14 named routes in demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:21-36.
```

**Reproduction.** grep above returns 0. In the running app at any route, no element in the dock nav has an `href`; the trigger is `role=combobox` and its children are `role=option`.

**Proposed cure.** Replace the Select with glass-ui `DropdownMenu` + `RouterLink` items (glass-ui ships ./dropdown-menu; the subpath idiom is already used 15x for /dock and 9x for /dom). This retires the role=option semantics mismatch, the aria-selected gap, the aria-activedescendant gap and the `"__admin_toggle__"` sentinel (pass-1 L-8) in one move — a mode command in a menu is an ordinary DropdownMenuItem, which is not a value and never was.

**Defect.** The "desktop" concept has three homes and two inequivalent predicates; the app's own layout truth and this component measurably disagree, and App.vue's comment asserting they "can never disagree" is false.

**Mechanism.** One named concept, no unique home: three composables (glass-ui useBreakpoint, @vueuse useMediaQuery, Tailwind's breakpoint), two different predicates. The shell's authority is bypassed by the dock's private re-derivation.

App.vue:310-312 glass-ui `useBreakpoint("(min-width: 1024px) and (min-aspect-ratio: 1.1)")` -> stamps `[data-layout]` (App.vue:2); Dock.vue:71 @vueuse `useMediaQuery("(min-width: 1024px)")` (no aspect clause) -> prop-drilled as `isDesktop` (Dock.vue:185); ActionBarToggle.vue:82 and :103 Tailwind `hidden lg:block` (width only). App.vue:305-309 claims "the JS mount condition and the CSS dual grid share one compound query, so they can never disagree." MEASURED: 1440x900 aspect 1.600 -> data-layout=desktop, label/arrow/separator visible; 1200x1100 aspect 1.091 -> data-layout=MOBILE, label/arrow/separator ALL STILL VISIBLE; 1024x960 aspect 1.067 -> data-layout=MOBILE, all still visible. Fourth mechanism in the same demo: demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:71 and demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ConsoleRail.vue:118 use glass-ui `useBreakpoint` with the DOCK's width-only predicate.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/ and resize to 1200x1100. `document.querySelector('.app-layout').dataset.layout` === 'mobile' while the Tools label, ArrowRight and DockSeparator all render (getBoundingClientRect().width > 0).

Provide it as `LAYOUT_KEY` beside the other session keys and inject it in Dock/ActionBarToggle. The `isDesktop` prop dies, Dock.vue:71's useMediaQuery import dies, and the two `lg:` utilities become `v-if="layout === 'desktop'"` — one mechanism, one predicate.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-5 · CHALLENGE-L

**Evidence.**

```
Two independently-declared shapes: demo/color-session/keys.ts:17-27 `interface ActionBarContext` (cssColorOpaque/isEditing/canProposeName/colorModel/reset/copy/random) and demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:49-58 `interface DockActionBar` (label/icon/accentColor?/actions). Paintbrush"`, `:label="genericBar?.label ?? 'Tools'"`, `:accent="genericBar?.accentColor ?? safeAccent"`. ActionBarToggle.vue:44-46 re-declares three of DockActionBar's four fields as anonymous scalars. MEASURED: across 12 routes at 1440x900 (`/`, /palettes, /browse, /extract, /mix, /generate, /gradient, /about, /atmosphere, /blob, /admin/users, /does-not-exist) the rendered label read "Tools" on EVERY one — three props, one observable value, a defaulted chain hiding whether the source ever spoke.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-7 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The boot-vs-runtime phase is re-derived locally with a double-rAF frame count, against the app's own stated named-predicate law, and the resulting private state machine has a reachable stuck state that re-opens the exact clip amputation its 30-line header exists to cure.

**Mechanism.** A concept the app already owns (boot phase) re-derived privately, plus a presence transition hand-rolled in a consumer of a dock that ships its own presence grammar. Wrong home -> private state -> reachable stuck state.

**Evidence.**

```
The app owns a boot authority: OVERTURE_KEY at demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useOverture.ts:81, provided at App.vue:297, exposing b1/b2/b3/b3Complete/b4 and `dockLanded`; its module header states "each beat opens on a NAMED arming predicate, never a timer". <Dock> renders at App.vue:35, inside that provide. ActionBarToggle.vue:50-68 instead uses `requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(...))` — a frame count. Same beat re-rolled at useOverture.ts, useDockArrival.ts and demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue (4 files). STUCK STATE: :59 early-returns once slotLive is true, so `settled` is thereafter re-established ONLY by the grid-template-columns transitionend (:69-72); a presence flicker with no committed width change fires no transition and `is-settled` never returns. MEASURED, four fresh page loads: direct /#/about -> `is-visible is-live is-settled`, overflow visible; gradient -> about -> `is-visible is-live` (NO is-settled), `.action-bar-toggle-inner` computes `overflow: HIDDEN`; picker -> about -> settled/visible; browse -> about -> settled/visible. o15-dock-register.spec.ts:74-78 asserts overflow:visible only on `/` after a fresh load, so the oracle cannot see this path.
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, wait ~4s for settle, then navigate to #/about and wait ~1.2s. `document.querySelector('.action-bar-toggle-slot').className` === 'action-bar-toggle-slot is-visible is-live' (no is-settled) and getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.action-bar-toggle-inner')).overflow === 'hidden'.

**Proposed cure.** Two removals. (a) boot-vs-runtime = `inject(OVERTURE_KEY)`'s b1/dockLanded — one authority, named predicate, PRM-correct by construction. (b) presence belongs to the producer: glass-ui ships DockCrossfade, DockLayer and useLiquidReveal/useBloomUp (@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion). With presence owned upstream, slotLive, settled, onSlotSettled, the three is-* classes and ~34 lines of scoped CSS all disappear — and the stuck state cannot exist in a machine with no state.

MEASURED at innerWidth 430: labelDisplay "none", role "alert", lamp.innerText === "", rect 25.99×17.99. At innerWidth 1440: labelDisplay "block", innerText "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`". Coverage gap: test/status-lamp.test.ts asserts only the pure matrix; e2e/smoke/oracles/o22-status-lamp.spec.ts:56-83 asserts data-variant/role/geometry at desktop only, never the accessible name; the visual audit's a11y probe records only smallTapTargets/imgNoAlt/namelessButtons (REPORT.json results[].probe.a11y), and namelessButtons inspects buttons — an unnamed alert is invisible to it.
```

**Reproduction.** Playwright: browser_navigate http://localhost:9000/#/ ; browser_resize 430×900 ; evaluate → { labelDisplay: "none", role: "alert", lampInnerText: "" }. Then resize 1440×900 → innerText restored. Full outputs pasted in the report.

**Proposed cure.** Adopt glass-ui StatusDot's `label` prop (L-3), or replace display:none with sr-only/clip-rect. Never display:none the only text in a live region. The compact/expanded decision belongs in the shared ApiStatusPill's `compact` prop, tested once, not in each seat's media query.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-5 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Two paths to @mkbabb/glass-ui/dock in adjacent lines of the same file; the barrel that provides the second path exists to serve exactly one import line and re-exports a third-party package.

**Mechanism.** A pass-through barrel with no added value creates a second specifier for an already-public package; the directory then imports its own index from within itself (Dock.vue → ./ → ./Dock.vue). Dual path (edict 2) plus contrivance (edict 3).

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:4 `import { GlassDock, DockLayerGroup, DockLayer } from "./";` sits directly above Dock.vue:5 `import { DockControl, DockSeparator } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock";`. demo/shell/dock/index.ts is 2 export lines: the glass-ui re-export plus `export { default as Dock } from "./Dock.vue"`. Ten other demo sites use the direct specifier: GradientVisualizer.vue:13, MixResultDisplay.vue:3, ExtractWorkbench.vue:187, ExtractControls.vue:98, ImageEyedropper.vue:95, ConfigSliderPane.vue:20, ActionButton.vue:55, DockViewSelect.vue:3, Dock.vue:5, ActionBarToggle.vue:5. Dock.vue:4 is the ONLY consumer of the barrel's re-export. The `Dock` export has one consumer, App.vue:167. DockStatusLamp is NOT in the barrel (Dock.vue:14 imports it relatively) — 2 of the directory's 9 components are published by no stated rule.
```

**Reproduction.** cat demo/shell/dock/index.ts; sed -n '4,5p' demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue; grep -rn '@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock' demo/ (10 direct sites) and grep -rn 'from "\./"' demo/ (1 relevant site).

**Proposed cure.** Delete demo/shell/dock/index.ts. Rewrite Dock.vue:4 to the direct @mkbabb/glass-ui/dock specifier (merging with line 5) and App.vue:167 to `import Dock from "../shell/dock/Dock.vue"`. Net −1 file, −1 indirection, one path to the design system everywhere.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-6 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The api-client provide/inject seam is unsubstitutable — a DI wrapper around module singletons with one provider, no parameters, and no test double — and its only measurable effect is to make the component un-mountable in tests, which is what forced the resolver extraction that L-1 then mislocated.

**Mechanism.** An abstraction with exactly one implementation and no injection point is not a seam; it is indirection. Its cost is real (the component cannot be mounted without an App-root provider), and paying that cost produced the extracted-resolver pattern that was then homed in the wrong directory — L-6 is the proximate cause of L-1.

**Evidence.**

```
useApiClient.ts:36-44 `createApiClient()` takes NO parameters and returns { request, adminRequest, sessionToken: sessionTokenRef, availability: apiAvailability, baseUrl: BASE_URL } — `availability` IS the module ref exported at availability.ts:47. One provider: App.vue:189 provideApiClient(). Three consumers, all reading only `availability`: DockStatusLamp.vue:30, ApiOfflineChip.vue:35, PaletteCardMenu.vue:216. useApiClient.ts:56-60 throws when no provider stands above. Yet the docs claim "never a hard module-singleton import" (useApiClient.ts:2-16, echoed at DockStatusLamp.vue:28-29). test/status-lamp.test.ts never mounts the SFC — it imports the extracted pure function only.
```

**Reproduction.** Read useApiClient.ts:36-44 (zero-parameter factory closing over module state) and grep -rn 'provideApiClient|createApiClient' demo/ → exactly one provider site (App.vue:189) and zero substitutions anywhere in demo/, test/, or e2e/.

**Proposed cure.** Either give the seam a reason to exist — `createApiClient(deps)` with an injectable transport so tests can drive faces through the mounted component — or delete it and import `apiAvailability` directly at the three consumers (three one-line edits). Do not keep a seam that cannot seam.

**Defect.** All three controls render 22x22 because glass-ui's compact dock-control variant ships NO hit-target floor and is explicitly exempted from the dock's own coarse-pointer floor — and the repo's own T-36 cure for exactly this was applied per-instance to a sibling SFC, so it did not propagate here.

Because it is per-instance there is no structural mechanism by which the next compact consumer inherits it. A law enforced by a comment is not enforced.

Live at localhost:9000, state-invariant (measured inert AND active): all three = w22 h22, width_css/height_css '22px', padding '4px', glyph 14x14 (w-3.5 h-3.5). CORRECTION TO MT-F004: measured center distances 47.00 / 75.00 / 28.00 px, all >= 24, so WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 spacing exception IS met — these PASS AA. They fail SC 2.5.5 (AAA 44x44) and the producer's own --dock-touch-target:2.75rem intent. The audit harness's flat 24x24 rule does not implement the spacing exception.

SlugEditLayer.vue:81-87. MobileMenuDropdown.vue:92-99 writes `<DropdownMenuItem ... as-child>`; node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenuItem.vue.d.ts declares `DropdownMenuItemProps = { disabled?, textValue?, inset?, class? }` — no asChild. Live DOM, 390x844, menu open: GitHub row = {tag DIV, role menuitem, h 55.4, containsAnchor true, anchorDisplay block, anchorTabIndex 0}; the three sibling rows = {containsAnchor false, h 44}. Boxes: row 200.6x55.4 at (101, 223.75); live anchor 68.6x43.4 at (109, 229.75) = 26.8% of row area. Touch: tap at (239.6, 251.4) inside the row -> newPages 0, menu closed; tap at anchor centre -> newPages 1, https://github.com/mkbabb/value.js. Keyboard: ArrowDown roving walk = Login -> Share color -> GitHub -> Dark mode (focus never reaches the anchor); Enter on the focused GitHub row -> {urlChanged false, newPages 0, menuStillOpen false}. Byte-identical at ProfileSection.vue:158-165 (part of the 28-line identical run).

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-mobilemenudropdown/probe/probe-aschild.mjs (DOM shape + focus walk), probe-enter.mjs (Enter on the focused row), probe-tap.mjs (dead-zone vs anchor tap). Manual: open http://localhost:9000/#/ at 390x844, tap the ⋮ Menu, tap the GitHub row anywhere right of the word 'GitHub' — nothing opens.

**Defect.** MobileMenuDropdown and ProfileSection are a 78.7% byte-identical fork of one concept, and the responsive split is CSS-only so BOTH components mount, inject and run their live-ink probes at every viewport.

**Evidence.**

```
difflib.SequenceMatcher over whitespace-normalised lines: ProfileSection 170 non-blank, MobileMenuDropdown 108 non-blank, 85 identical = 78.7% of MobileMenuDropdown; longest identical run 28 lines (ProfileSection[142] == Mobile[80]) = the entire @mbabb block (avatar + Share color + GitHub + separator + Dark mode); next runs 15 lines (slug pill), 9 lines (avatar/bio), 7 lines (import tail). Live DOM census: at 390x844 [aria-label="Menu"] inDom 1 / visible 1 and `nav .hidden.lg\:flex` hosts inDom 2 / visible 0; at 1440x900 the Menu trigger is inDom 1 / visible 0 and the desktop hosts are 2 / 2. nav button counts: 12 inDom / 10 visible at 390; 20 / 17 at 1440. Dock.vue:67-69 keeps three usePopupMutex keys alive for two menus of which one is always invisible.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-mobilemenudropdown/probe/probe-branches.mjs (prints the inDom/visible matrix at both viewports). Fork ratio: python3 difflib over the two SFCs' non-blank stripped lines.

**Proposed cure.** One model, two views. demo/shell/dock/identity/useDockIdentityMenu.ts returns MenuRow[] = { id, icon, label, kind: "command"|"link", onSelect?, href? }, reading platform/session + platform/identity — ONE home for what the menu contains. demo/shell/dock/identity/DockIdentityMenu.vue takes { rows, variant: "bar" | "overflow" }: "bar" renders labelled Buttons + DockSeparators (today's desktop), "overflow" renders one DockTrigger + one DropdownMenu (today's mobile). **Defect.** The accent colour is certified twice: Dock.vue passes the already-resting-certified SAFE_ACCENT_KEY ink down a prop named `cssColorOpaque`, and the component re-certifies it against the floating rung — systematically over-muting the user's picked colour.

**Mechanism.** Ownership of 'which colour travels this prop' is unstated across three parties: the prop NAME claims raw, the WIRING supplies certified, the COMPONENT re-applies the guard. certifyAccentInk is a monotone walk away from the surface, so composing two walks can only over-correct — the direction is structural, not a function of the rung model I measured against.

**Evidence.**

```
useAtmosphereBoot.ts:91 provides SAFE_ACCENT_KEY = safeAccentCss (certifyAccentInk against the RESTING plate, useContrastSafeColor.ts). Dock.vue:35 injects it; Dock.vue:209 (and :220 for the twin) passes `:css-color-opaque="safeAccent"`. MobileMenuDropdown.vue:23-24 then does `useSafeAccentFn("floating")` + `safeCss(cssColorOpaque)`. The raw pick was one identifier away — Dock.vue:34 injects CSS_COLOR_KEY into the same scope and does not use it here. Measured drift by dynamic-importing demo/color-session/ink.ts in the live document (static rung model, ambient 0.62, light; L_resting 0.85, L_floating 0.924), contract single walk vs shipped double walk: oklch(0.75 0.15 30) L 47.52%->42.08% (-5.43pp); oklch(0.62 0.2 140) L 44.47%->39.17%, C 0.1432->0.1261 (-12%); oklch(0.55 0.18 250) L 45.80%->40.34%, C -12%; oklch(0.85 0.1 90) L 45.86%->40.39%; oklch(0.45 0.22 320) L 45.00%->43.14%; rgb(255 0 0) L 48.16%->42.42%, C 0.1976->0.1741; rgb(0 128 255) L 46.19%->40.68%. 7 of 7 picks differ, all darker and lower-chroma. The D6 contract both twins document (ProfileSection.vue:22-27) is 'certify the RAW pick against the surface it composites over'.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-mobilemenudropdown/probe/probe-doublecert.mjs — prints the seven-row contract-vs-shipped table against the live ink module.

**Proposed cure.** Pick one owner, not both. Preferred transposition: the boot writer publishes a per-rung certified ink map (SAFE_ACCENT_RESTING_KEY / _FLOATING_KEY / _CHROME_KEY in demo/color-session/keys.ts), each rung certified exactly once at exactly one site; view components inject the rung they sit on and never hold the guard. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Three disagreeing responsive authorities govern this one control — visibility via a JS-written aspect-aware layout stamp, density via a width-only scoped @media, sibling furniture via a width-only useMediaQuery. At 1024x1366 portrait the control renders at glass-ui's DESKTOP density inside a dock the layout stamp has declared mobile, beside siblings `isDesktop` has put in desktop mode.

**Mechanism.** The control's responsive contract is split across three files and three mechanisms with no single predicate. Nothing in the type system or the build can observe that they disagree. The width-only bug shell.css was written to cure is re-instantiated one level down, inside the component, for density instead of visibility.

**Evidence.**

```
Authority 1: `demo/styles/shell.css:123` `[data-layout="desktop"] .dock-mobile-panes { display: none }` (stamp = min-width:1024px AND min-aspect-ratio:1.1). Authority 2: `demo/shell/PaneSegmentedControl.vue:46-50` `@media (max-width: 639px)` — width only. Authority 3: `demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:71` `useMediaQuery("(min-width: 1024px)")` — width only, fed to `ActionBarToggle :is-desktop` (:185) and `DockViewSelect :is-desktop` (:172). shell.css:118-122 names the exact hazard it cured: "the width-only `lg:hidden` it replaced marooned the second pane there [1024x1366]". LIVE Playwright probe @1024x1366 on http://localhost:9000/#/gradient: `{viewport:[1024,1366], dataLayout:["DIV:mobile"], wrapperDisplay:"block", wrapperVisible:true, controlPresent:true, mq639:false, mq1024:true, mqDesktopGrammar:false, tabPadding:"5px 12px", tabFontSize:"14px", tabBox:{w:82.3,h:31}}`. `5px 12px / 14px` is glass-ui's >=640px desktop rung verbatim (`node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/tabs/styles/segmented.css:1`: `@media (min-width:640px){.segmented-tab{padding:0.3125rem 0.75rem;font-size:0.875rem}}`). Contrast @390x844 /#/palettes: `tabPadding:"4px 6px", tabFontSize:"12.179px", tabBox:{w:57.5,h:26.3}`.
```

**Reproduction.** Playwright: browser_resize 1024x1366, navigate http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, then evaluate `({dataLayout: document.querySelector('[data-layout]').dataset.layout, mq639: matchMedia('(max-width:639px)').matches, mq1024: matchMedia('(min-width:1024px)').matches, tabPadding: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.pane-segmented-control .segmented-tab')).padding})` -> `{dataLayout:"mobile", mq639:false, mq1024:true, tabPadding:"5px 12px"}`. Not a visual break at that width (REPORT.json horizontalOverflow: 0 across all 60 captures) — a structural incoherence that breaks the moment the aperture narrows or labels widen.

**Proposed cure.** One authority. Once the density rung moves upstream (L-3 cure), it is expressed against the component's own container rather than the viewport, leaving the aspect-aware `[data-layout]` stamp as the single app-side authority for BOTH visibility and grammar — which is what shell.css:118-122 already argues for in prose. `Dock.vue:71`'s width-only `isDesktop` should read the same stamp; it currently disagrees with it by measurement at 1024x1366.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-3 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** `:deep(.segmented-tab)` reaches into a glass-ui-PRIVATE class to forge a density variant glass-ui does not expose. `SegmentedTabsProps` has no `size`/`density`/`compact` prop, so the demo synthesized one out of the producer's internals — an edict-4 violation (design-system variant living in demo/) and an edict-5 violation (per-instance override instead of root-level styling) simultaneously.

**Mechanism.** The need is genuine (16px is load-bearing in a 312px aperture); the LOCATION is the defect. A consumer that styles a producer's undeclared internal class has a silent-breakage vector: any glass-ui release renaming `.segmented-tab` or reordering its media rungs breaks this control with no typecheck, no test, no CI signal — the exact failure class this same file already suffered in the BouncyTabs->SegmentedTabs break (`docs/tranches/N/audit/impl/W1A.md:37`).

**Evidence.**

```
`demo/shell/PaneSegmentedControl.vue:46-50`: `.pane-segmented-control :deep(.segmented-tab) { padding: 0.25rem 0.375rem; font-size: var(--type-caption); }`. `.segmented-tab` is emitted by the compiled producer SFC — `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/tabs.js:262` and `:294` (`class: "segmented-tab"`) — and styled by the producer's private stylesheet `dist/components/tabs/styles/segmented.css:1`. It appears nowhere in the published type surface. Full `SegmentedTabsProps` (`dist/components/tabs/SegmentedTabs.vue.d.ts:45-95`) = options, ariaLabel, variant, semantics, activation, orientation, responsive, motion, class — NO density prop. The component's own comment at `:42` admits the reach: "the producer's own .segmented-tab hook". LIVE @390x844: override lands and wins — `padding: "4px 6px"` (0.25rem 0.375rem) beating glass-ui's `0.25rem 0.625rem`; `fontSize: "12.179px"` from `--type-caption` = `clamp(0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem)`; tab width 57.5px vs an unoverridden ~65.5px = 16px of aperture saved in the 312px mobile pill.
```

**Reproduction.** Playwright @390x844 on http://localhost:9000/#/palettes: `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.pane-segmented-control .segmented-tab')).padding` -> `"4px 6px"`; compare `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/tabs/styles/segmented.css:1` which specifies `0.25rem 0.625rem` below 640px.

**Proposed cure.** Move the variant upstream: add `density?: "default" | "compact"` to `SegmentedTabsProps` in glass-ui, emitting `.segmented-tabs--compact` and owning the tightened `.segmented-tab` rung internally. Kills the `:deep` reach at its root and gives a recurring need — a segmented strip inside a narrow chrome aperture — a first-class answer any consumer can use. This is the only piece that cannot land inside value.js; per the standing BH/BI relay edict it goes to the active glass-ui inbox as a component-level ask, justified by the measured 16px aperture saving.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-4 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Four stacked null guards service ONE schema invariant, and one of them is a masking fallback: `?? ''` at the callsite converts absent into empty-string, and the component's `v-if="leftLabel && rightLabel"` tests truthiness — so a relaxed outer guard or a future VIEW_MAP row would make the control silently render NOTHING rather than error. The props also widen a type the schema narrows.

**Mechanism.** `PaneConfig` models ONE fact ("this view has a second pane") as TWO independently nullable fields (`right`, `rightLabel`). Because the type system permits them to disagree, every consumer defensively re-checks and the checks accumulate down the call chain. The four guards are the symptom; the two-field encoding is the defect.

**Evidence.**

```
Invariant: `demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:70-74` — `right: RightPane` (nullable), `leftLabel: string` (NEVER null), `rightLabel: string | null`. Across all 14 VIEW_MAP rows (`viewSchema.ts:98-227`) `right === null` iff `rightLabel === null` — exactly one row, `atmosphere` (`:161-169`); `leftLabel` is a non-empty string in all 14. The four guards: (1) `Dock.vue:197` `v-if="...currentConfig.value.right !== null"`; (2) `Dock.vue:200-201` `:left-label="...leftLabel ?? ''"` / `:right-label="...rightLabel ?? ''"` — DEAD AND HOSTILE; (3) `PaneSegmentedControl.vue:3` `v-if="leftLabel && rightLabel"` — dead given (1), and '' is falsy; (4) `PaneSegmentedControl.vue:31-32` `{ label: leftLabel ?? "", ... }` x2 — unreachable behind (3). Type contradiction: `PaneSegmentedControl.vue:22` declares `leftLabel: string | null` while `PaneConfig.leftLabel` is `string`.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — labelled a latent-defect finding. Guards 2/3/4 are currently unreachable behind guard 1. The dead code and the `string | null` vs `string` type contradiction are present-tense and verified at the cited lines; the silent-blank failure mode requires either relaxing Dock.vue:197 or adding a VIEW_MAP row with `right: "palettes", rightLabel: null`.

**Proposed cure.** Fuse the pair in `viewSchema.ts` so the invariant is unrepresentable-otherwise: `right: { pane: RightPane; label: string } | null` replacing `right` + `rightLabel`, with `RightPane` losing its `| null` member (absence is a property of the SLOT, not of the pane identity). Three of the four guards become TYPE ERRORS rather than review findings, and the `?? ''` masking fallback has nothing left to mask. `useViewManager` then derives one `paneTabs` ref (null when there is no right pane) and `Dock.vue` carries exactly one guard.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-3 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** PaneSlot's documented onMount contract is factually false — it fires on EVERY re-render, not on mount/unmount — and because the component swap is deferred one rAF while the action bar switches synchronously, App.vue files the OUTGOING pane's instance under the INCOMING pane's ref for a full frame.

**Mechanism.** Three independent readings of 'which pane is live': the action bar reads the route synchronously, the slot's ref lands one rAF late, and onDesktopLeftMount resolves WHICH ref to fill from currentConfig at callback time rather than from the instance it was handed. No single owner of pane identity.

**Evidence.**

```
JSDoc claim: PaneSlot.vue:47-51 'Called with the component instance on mount, and with null on unmount.' P1 repro (jsdom + vue 3.5.35, faithful transcription): `after 5 prop ticks refCalls = ["PaneA","PaneA","PaneA","PaneA","PaneA"]`. Mechanism in Vue source: PaneSlot.vue:124 writes a fresh inline arrow every render (`:ref="onMount ? (el: any) => onMount!(el) : undefined"`); runtime-core.cjs.js:5476 re-runs setRef on every patch; setRef's stale-ref branch (runtime-core.cjs.js:1801-1817) handles only string and Ref old-refs, never a function. liveProps updates every colour tick (PaneSlot.vue:101-106). P2 repro (adds App.vue:323-328 verbatim): `t1 (config switched, PRE-rAF) generatePaneRef = ColorPicker; paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.() -> SILENT NO-OP`; `t2 (post-rAF) generatePaneRef = GeneratePane -> regenerated`. Two clocks: usePaneRouter.ts:188-201 switches the action bar off viewManager.currentView synchronously; PaneSlot.vue:86-97 defers the component swap by one requestAnimationFrame.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/paneslot-repro.mjs and node scratchpad/appvue-repro.mjs (jsdom + the repo's own vue 3.5.35, PaneSlot.vue and App.vue:323-328 transcribed verbatim). Outputs pasted in evidence. In the live app: switch the left pane from picker to generate and click the dock's Regenerate button within the same frame — the handler dispatches onto the ColorPicker instance and `undefined?.()` silently succeeds.

**Proposed cure.** Same architectural cure as L-2: panes register their own commands, so an instance can only ever file itself under its own identity and the rAF deferral stops racing the command surface. Independently, the onMount JSDoc must not survive as written — it is load-bearing documentation that is measurably wrong.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-4 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** usePaneRouter.ts is a four-concern god module (component registry + prop factories + three slot computeds + the dock action-bar type and data), and the dock imports its own types back out of it. Its action tables encode nine private method names of three feature panes, reached through Ref<any> and invoked with double-optional calls.

**Mechanism.** Deliberate consolidation of four separable concerns into one file, justified in its own header as de-duplication. The result is that the dock (whose components are the ONLY consumers of DockAction/DockActionBar) must reach two directories into a routing module for its own vocabulary, and the router holds untypeable knowledge of three panes' private APIs.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts (231 lines): registry :69-95; prop factories :126-161; slot computeds :163-184; DockAction/DockActionBar types :38-58 and per-view action tables :186-228. Its own header announces the aggregation ('folds in useGenericActionBar', 'the retired useDockActionBar.ts'). Back-imports: demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:24 `import type { DockActionBar } from "../usePaneRouter"`; demo/shell/dock/layers/GenericActionBar.vue:4 `import type { DockAction } from "../../usePaneRouter"`. Feature internals encoded at :196-223: regenerate, save, copyColors, reset, copyCSS, seedFromPalette, clearSelection, startMix, copyResult — reached via PaneActionRefs `{ generate: Ref<any>; gradient: Ref<any>; mix: Ref<any> }` (:107-111) and called as `paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.()`.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — this is a structural finding, established by reading the file and its two back-importers. Its runtime consequence is reproduced separately under L-3 (the double-optional call silently succeeding against the wrong instance).

**Proposed cure.** Split by concern along lines the areas already suggest: shell/panes/registry.ts (name -> loader, nothing else), shell/panes/props.ts, and shell/dock/actions.ts owning DockAction/DockActionBar AND the per-view tables beside the only components that consume them. Replace the Ref<any> handles with the typed command registry of L-2, at which point `?.()` becomes a compile error instead of a silent success.

**Defect.** The shell statically depends on the palettes FEATURE for a PLATFORM capability. 54 of the dock's 135 statically-reachable files (40%) are palette-feature files, pulled in because five shell components inject SESSION_PORT_KEY from demo/palettes/usePalettePorts — while the correct direct edge to demo/platform/auth/useSession already exists and is already used one directory over. Because the aggregator wires 17 palette composables, every shell consumer of session drags the whole feature into the shell's static graph — and the same subtree now reaches one concept two different ways.

```

**Proposed cure.** Move SESSION_PORT_KEY and its provide to demo/platform/auth/. **Reproduction.** node scratchpad/L-probe6.mjs — load /#/ (gold false), hash to /#/atmosphere (gold true), page.goBack() to /#/ (gold STILL true), hash to /#/palettes (gold STILL true). With admin credentials the damage is functional, not cosmetic: viewEntries (:34-39) then returns only the seven admin views while on /#/palettes, so the dock's own navigation cannot reach the user views except through the `__admin_toggle__` sentinel row.

**Proposed cure.** Derive, do not latch. Add `group: "user" | "admin"` to `PaneConfig` (viewSchema.ts owns the partition) and reduce the composable to `const isAdminMode = computed(() => VIEW_MAP[viewManager.currentView.value].group === "admin")`. The ref, both watchers and both hardcoded ViewId arrays die; `toggleAdminMode` keeps its real job (it navigates) and the flag follows the route by construction — the same transposition `useViewManager.ts:51-58` already applied to `mobilePaneIndex`.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure / module boundaries / owners` · L-20 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The local `useLayerTransition` shim in ActionBarLayer produces no crossfade at all: the producer CSS the template hand-binds declares no opacity transition, so the 260 ms timer window is an instant cut with a transparent inert box held over the live controls.

**Mechanism.** A local fork of a retired producer concept, styled out of the producer's private stylesheet by class-name convention; the fork reimplements the packaging but cannot reach the animation, which the producer moved behind a component.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:62-94 (the shim, SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS = 260, subLayerProps hand-binding `.dock-layer`/`is-active`/`is-leaving`). Producer rules: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/styles/layers.css declares only `transition: visibility 0s linear var(--duration-normal)` on `.dock-layer`; the opacity overlap lives on `.dock-crossfade[data-crossfading] > .dock-face` via `--dock-t` (crossfade.css), reachable only inside `<DockCrossfade>`. Measured live (scratchpad L-probe2.mjs), both faces at rest / +60ms / +460ms across the actions->input swap: `transitionProperty: "visibility", transitionDuration: "0s"` at every phase; opacity steps 1->0 and 0->1 in one frame; the leaving face holds a 442x45 transparent inert box. The public successor exists: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/dock/index.d.ts:5 `export { default as DockCrossfade } from "./DockCrossfade.vue";` — contradicting the shim's own comment at ActionBarLayer.vue:54-61.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/L-probe2.mjs — navigate /#/, click [aria-label='Toggle action bar'], click [aria-label='Open color input'], sample getComputedStyle on both children of `.dock-layer-grid` at 60 ms and 460 ms. transition-property is `visibility` and duration `0s` in all four phases.

**Proposed cure.** Replace ActionBarLayer.vue:62-101 with `<DockCrossfade :active="activeSubLayer" reserve="inline">` wrapping two `<DockLayer id="actions">` / `<DockLayer id="input">` faces. The shim, the 260 ms literal, the timer, `subLayerProps`, `subLayerGridEl`, the `void opts.containerEl` parity argument and the hand-bound producer classes all die (~40 lines), and the producer's spring-driven overlap, peak-size reserve and focus transfer from a dissolving face arrive instead of being approximated.

### `design` · D-3 · design

**Defect.** `variant="outline"` and `variant="ghost"` are not glass-ui 7 API. They ship as literal invalid DOM attributes and do nothing; both controls resolve to the same emphasis, so an account ACTION and an author WORDMARK render as materially identical capsules.

**Mechanism.** Shadcn-era API addressed at a design system two majors on; the props fall through to $attrs. Both buttons therefore take the default emphasis="secondary", so the design-system lever that distinguishes an action from a credit is never pulled. Violates owner edicts 4 and 5 and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.8 ('Supporting fixtures do not compete … through equal size or equal shadow').

**Evidence.**

```
glass-ui 7.0.0 Button props (dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js): emphasis|tone|size|iconOnly|loading|type|disabled|class|asChild|as — no `variant`. Emphasis vocabulary (components/button/styles.css): primary|secondary|quiet|text — no outline, no ghost. Rendered: <button data-emphasis="secondary" data-tone="neutral" data-size="xs" … variant="outline">Login</button> and … variant="ghost">@mbabb</button>. Measured identical backgroundColor oklab(0.721325 0.00492 0.010865 / 0.6), byte-identical 7-part box-shadow, border-radius 9999px on both.
```

**Reproduction.** Inspect either dock trigger on http://localhost:9000/#/ — the `variant` attribute is present on the element and `data-emphasis` is `secondary` on both; computed backgroundColor and boxShadow strings are identical.

**Proposed cure.** Use `emphasis="quiet"` for the wordmark (it already ships `background: transparent; box-shadow: none; color: var(--muted-foreground)` plus the hover this file hand-rolls as `hover:text-foreground hover:underline underline-offset-4`), and the dock's own trigger family for the account seat. One edit also closes D-10's dark 4.18:1 (demo raises --muted-foreground to the ink floor), D-15 and D-17.

### `design` · D-5 · design

**Defect.** The admin identity's gold shimmer is cascade-dead — the glyphs paint opaque gold over the text-clipped gradient — while the infinite `metal-shimmer-sweep` animation keeps running in the dock forever.

**Mechanism.** An inline style attribute beats any author-layer rule, so `color: var(--color-gold)` overrides the utility's `color: transparent` and the clipped gradient is hidden behind opaque glyphs. The animation is unaffected and keeps repainting a gradient nobody can see. Sibling consumers (DockViewSelect.vue:135, PaletteCard.vue:64) set no inline color and work. Violates PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.5 (no decoration without information).

**Evidence.**

```
ProfileSection.vue:96 sets style="border-color: var(--color-gold); color: var(--color-gold)" on a .gold-shimmer span. glass-ui's .gold-shimmer (dist/styles/utilities/base-misc.css) is `background: linear-gradient(…); background-clip: text; color: transparent` + `animation: metal-shimmer-sweep var(--duration-shimmer) linear infinite`. Live probe (transient injection of both spellings, removed in the same evaluate): with inline color -> color = oklch(0.751 0.147 84.199997), animationName = metal-shimmer-sweep; without inline color -> color = rgba(0,0,0,0), animationName = metal-shimmer-sweep.
```

**Reproduction.** In any page that loads the app stylesheet: render <span class="slug-pill gold-shimmer" style="color: var(--color-gold)">admin</span> next to <span class="slug-pill gold-shimmer">admin</span> — the first computes color oklch(0.751 0.147 84.2) (opaque, shimmer invisible), the second rgba(0,0,0,0) (shimmer visible); both report animationName metal-shimmer-sweep.

**Proposed cure.** Drop the inline `color`, keep the gold on a class (`border-gold`, the PaletteCard idiom), and let the producer's one metal register own the ink — this removes the dead decoration, the wasted compositing and one per-instance override in a single edit.

### `design` · D-6 · design

**Defect.** The theme glyph renders 16 x 24 px — non-square and 71% taller than every sibling icon — because the `aspect-square` class written to prevent exactly that is inert.

**Mechanism.** Lucide SVGs carry width="24" height="24" presentation attributes. `w-4` overrides the width to 16px; nothing overrides the height, so the height stays definite at 24px and `aspect-ratio` is discarded. Per-instance glyph sizing (9 sites in this file) instead of the producer's rung — glass-ui already owns it via `.button > svg:not([class*="size-"]) { inline-size: var(--ui-glyph); block-size: var(--ui-glyph) }`. Violates PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.7 and owner edict 5.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured inside the open menu: Share2 `w-3.5 h-3.5` = 14x14; octocat `w-3.5 h-3.5` = 14x14 (fill solid rgb(28,25,23)); Sun/Moon `aspect-square w-4` = 16 wide x 24 tall, computed aspect-ratio '1 / 1', cssWidth 16px, cssHeight 24px, attrW/attrH 24/24. Row offsets confirm the optical break: icon y = 10 vs 15 and 6 for siblings.
```

**Reproduction.** Open the @mbabb menu at http://localhost:9000/#/ and read getBoundingClientRect on the three svgs: 14x14, 14x14, 16x24.

**Proposed cure.** Stop sizing glyphs per instance. Route every dock/menu icon through one `--ui-glyph` rung owned by the producer, and pick one icon family (all 2px-stroke outline) so a solid octocat never sits beside hairline marks.

Live menu content: class = 'dropdown-menu-content dropdown-menu__content glass-reveal glass-floating min-w-menu font-display', computed fontFamily = "Fira Code", --dropdown-menu-font = '"Fira Code", "Fira Code Fallback", "Fira Mono", monospace'. glass-ui components/_shared/menu.css: `font-family: var(--dropdown-menu-font, inherit)`. **Defect.** Each trigger paints a desaturated neutral slab inside its own chromatic capsule, and states its boundary three times: capsule ring, inner wash edge, and a DockSeparator on each side.

**Mechanism.** A page-primitive Button (neutral `glass-wash`) dropped into a chromatic dock band, inset ~10px from its own capsule, adds a second material tier and a second edge inside one control; the separators then add a third statement of the same boundary.

```
Pixel scan of shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png at y=40.5 CSS: band (246,169,194) chromatic; Login border box x757.7-844.2; wash slab x767.5-834.0 measured (200,167,172) near-neutral; separators at x=746.5 and x=854.0 (1px). PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.4/PR-05: spacing plus material already expressing the boundary makes the line duplicative.
```

**Reproduction.** Sample any horizontal row through the dock band in the light capture between x=740 and x=940 CSS: BAND -> separator -> band -> GRAY slab -> band -> separator -> band -> GRAY slab.

### `design` · D-16 · design

**Defect.** The two seats this component owns are 28px tall in a 32px band, and both of its separators are off-centre in their gaps — in opposite directions.

**Mechanism.** `size="xs"` (--control-h-xs) is a valid glass-ui size but the wrong rung for a dock seat, and the component's local `gap-1` nests inside the dock layer's own gap, so the hairlines land off-centre by 3-5px in opposite directions. Violates PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §1 (every element earns its scale and interval from its job) and §5.8.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured seat rects in nav.dock-band at 1440px: Home x496.3 w106.9 h32; Tools x626.2 w104.5 h32; Login x757.7 w86.5 h28; @mbabb x867.2 w76.6 h28. Separator positions from the pixel scan: x=746.5 (15.8px of air from Tools' right edge 730.7, 10.2px to Login's left edge 757.7) and x=854.0 (9.8px from Login's right edge 844.2, 12.2px to @mbabb's left edge 867.2).

### `implementation (CHALLENGE-C) — demo/shell/PaneSegmentedContr` · C-3 · implementation (CHALLENGE-C)

**Defect.** The pane switcher declares TOGGLE semantics but inherits TAB activation, and links to no panel. `semantics` unpassed → pill→toggle → role="group" + aria-pressed; `activation` unpassed → producer default "automatic" → an arrow-key focus move COMMITS the selection; `controls` never populated → aria-controls null; and the panel it governs (.pane-slot-mobile) has no id, no role=tabpanel, no aria-live. A keyboard user arrowing through what is announced as a group of pressed buttons destroys and rebuilds the page's main content on every keypress, with nothing announced.

**Mechanism.** Producer-default adoption by omission — three independent defaults taken without checking that their combination describes this control's actual shape.

**Evidence.**

```
MEASURED at 390x844 on http://localhost:9000/#/palettes via page.evaluate: groupAttrs {role:"group", ariaLabel:null}; tabs[0] {role:null, ariaPressed:"false", ariaSelected:null, ariaControls:null, tabindex:"-1"}; tabs[1] {ariaPressed:"true", tabindex:"0"}. Producer defaults, node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/tabs.js: `activation:{default:"automatic"}`, `semantics:{}` (no default), render `role: W.value ? "tablist" : "group"`. Producer commit-on-focus, node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useTabRovingFocus-YnWh-Ytr.js: `function m(e){ ... o.value[e]?.focus(), a.value==="automatic" && l(n.value,e) }`. Index wrap with r=2: `(e + n*i + r*i) % r`. Panel: demo/color-picker/App.vue:77-91 (.pane-slot-mobile — no id/role/aria-live). Producer affordance available: SegmentedTabs.vue.d.ts SegmentedTabOption.controls — "emitted as the tab's aria-controls, completing the APG tablist↔tabpanel linkage".
```

**Reproduction.** Navigate http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at viewport 390x844, expand the dock, evaluate the attribute set on .pane-segmented-control .segmented-tabs and its .segmented-tab children (pasted above). The keyboard journey itself is DERIVED from the producer source branch, not separately executed — that half is labelled a hypothesis in the report.

**Proposed cure.** Declare the shape once at the call site instead of patching: semantics="tabs", options carrying controls:'pane-slot-mobile', aria-label="Pane"; give .pane-slot-mobile id + role="tabpanel" in App.vue. activation then correctly stays automatic (it is the tablist idiom). Architectural, not a patch: the control stops pretending to be a toggle group and becomes the tablist it actually is.

### `implementation (CHALLENGE-C) — demo/shell/PaneSegmentedContr` · C-1 · implementation (CHALLENGE-C)

**Defect.** The SFC is a pure passthrough wrapper whose entire net contribution over an inline <SegmentedTabs> is 8px of horizontal padding per tab. `variant="pill"` is itself the producer default (no-op). What remains that is genuinely this file's: a 0|1↔"0"|"1" coercion (one unchecked cast), a v-if that can never be false, and a :deep() override that changes vertical padding by 0px. Two sibling SegmentedTabs consumers do the identical job inline, with the identical wrapper div and (one of them) the identical font-display class, with no wrapper SFC.

**Mechanism.** Wrapper-by-accretion — an SFC created to hold a CSS tweak, kept alive after the tweak shrank to a padding delta. Violates Edict 3 (KISS, no wrapper components that do not already exist) and Edict 1 (focused modules with real encapsulation — this one encapsulates nothing and leaks producer internals back out through :deep()).

**Evidence.**

```
Repo-wide census: `grep -rn "PaneSegmentedControl" . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=dist` → demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:15 (import), :192 (comment), :198 (usage), demo/styles/shell.css:119 (comment); all other hits are docs/ prose and e2e comments. USAGE = 1. Siblings: demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:103-105 (same `flex items-center justify-center` div, inline SegmentedTabs, no wrapper) and demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminNamesPanel.vue:14-16 (inline, `class="w-full font-display"`). Producer default proving variant="pill" is a no-op: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/tabs.js `variant:{default:"pill"}`.
```

**Reproduction.** The grep census above plus reading the three call sites. NONE required — established by enumeration.

**Proposed cure.** W47 as written, executed losslessly: first relay the compact density rung to glass-ui as a producer prop (C-4), then inline <SegmentedTabs> at Dock.vue:198 building options from currentConfig directly, then delete the SFC. Carry the C-2/C-3/C-7 prop declarations to the inline site or the 1→0 is cosmetic.

### `implementation (CHALLENGE-C) — demo/shell/PaneSegmentedContr` · C-9 · implementation (CHALLENGE-C)

**Defect.** Vacuous gate: the ONE thing this SFC contributes beyond a passthrough — the compact <style scoped> media query — is the one thing no test observes. Deleting lines 36-52 entirely keeps the whole suite green, so a W47 wave that removes the component would show green while silently changing the dock's mobile metrics.

**Mechanism.** The component's behavioural surface is gated; its only bespoke surface (CSS) is not — the gate was written against the producer's contract, not against the consumer's delta.

**Evidence.**

```
`grep -rn "pane-segmented|segmented-tab|PaneSegmented|mobilePaneIndex|dock-mobile" e2e/ test/` returns only prose comments (page-load-mobile.spec.ts:6; walk.spec.ts:16,91,92,130,134) — no unit test anywhere (test/ = 21 library specs; demo/test/ = export/ + glass/ only). The one real spec, e2e/smoke/mobile/walk.spec.ts:86-149, asserts only aria-pressed / toBeVisible / toHaveCount / toBeHidden — never geometry, padding, font-size, or the 24px tap floor. Green mutations: (1) delete <style scoped> lines 36-52; (2) delete class="font-display" line 10; (3) v-if="leftLabel && rightLabel" → v-if="true"; (4) delete variant="pill" (producer default, byte-identical DOM); (5) Number(v) as 0|1 → v==="1"?1:0. RED mutation (the gate is not fully vacuous): swapping leftLabel/rightLabel in tabOptions fails walk.spec.ts:95.
```

**Reproduction.** Read e2e/smoke/mobile/walk.spec.ts:86-149 and enumerate its assertions against the five mutations listed. Mutation #1 touches no asserted attribute.

**Proposed cure.** Do not add a bespoke CSS assertion — execute C-4 instead: move the compact rung into glass-ui, where the producer's own visual suite gates it, and delete the untestable consumer CSS. The gate problem dissolves with the code that created it.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Alpha is discarded when sampling: `formatHex(data[0], data[1], data[2])` never reads `data[3]`, so a fully transparent pixel is reported — and emitted to the palette via `pick`/`addToPalette` — as opaque black.

**Mechanism.** lossy channel projection — RGBA sampled, RGB formatted, no alpha branch

**Evidence.**

```
useImageSampler.ts:32-35 (formatHex) and :116-118 (getImageData → formatHex, data[3] unread); ImageEyedropper.vue:212-224 (emits sampledColor). MEASURED: sampling the fully-transparent quadrant of the 200×200 probe fixture yields readout `oklch(0% 0 none)` and a solid black WatercolorDot swatch (.playwright-mcp/eyedropper-live.png, top bar); sampledColor = "#000000".
```

**Reproduction.** Upload a PNG with a fully transparent region (fixture: .playwright-mcp/probe.png, bottom-right quadrant) and sample inside it. Readout: oklch(0% 0 none); swatch: black; Add-to-palette inserts #000000.

**Proposed cure.** Read data[3]. Either refuse the sample and return null — reusing the existing out-of-bounds 'no sample here' path at useImageSampler.ts:114-115 — or carry alpha through into the emitted color. Never project a non-existent pixel onto black.

**Defect.** The overlay is inoperable by keyboard and invisible to assistive technology: no role, no aria-modal, no accessible name, no aria-live readout, focus never moves in, no focus trap, no focus restoration; the sampling canvas is aria-hidden with no keyboard alternative; and Add/Apply only render after a pointer-only pin.

MEASURED on the live overlay: role=null, aria-modal=null, aria-label=null, [role=dialog] count 0, [aria-live] count 0, focusables inside overlay = 1, document.activeElement = BODY on open, Tab #1 → INPUT with insideOverlay:false, Tab #2 → INPUT with insideOverlay:false. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · D-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The ResizeObserver calls fitToViewport() unconditionally on every size change, which reassigns zoom and recentres pan — destroying the user's inspection zoom on any window resize, panel reflow, or mobile URL-bar show/hide.

```
useInertiaGesture.ts:353-360 (ResizeObserver → fitToViewport) and :152-167 (fitToViewport assigns zoom.value = fit unconditionally). MEASURED (probe2 §C): ctrl-wheel zoom to 2.6924, then change the overlay height → zoom becomes 1.61. {"beforeZoom":2.6924,"afterZoom":1.61}

Vue types undeclared attributes as $attrs fallthrough, so a major-version prop/slot removal is type-invisible by construction; the behavioural suite that WOULD see it is dark in CI; and a separate dock-stability defect now short-circuits it before the assertion. `grep -rln "mount(" test/` returns nothing — the repo has no component-mount test anywhere, so the whole glass-ui consumer boundary is ungated in the lane CI actually runs. Mutations that keep every running gate green: delete the swatchKeys block and use :key="i"; set MAX_COLORS=1; delete the whole From-palettes Collapsible; drop aria-pressed from the palettes button; invert canRemoveColor.

**Evidence.**

```
`grep -n "playwright" .github/workflows/*.yml` -> no matches; ci.yml runs only npm ci / lint / vue-tsc x2 / build / vitest. Fresh run at HEAD f36f780c: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts --project=smoke` -> "Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded. Error: locator.click ... waiting for getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Select view' }) - attempting click action - waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable at smoke/fixtures/dock.ts:64 at openView" — it never reaches the addSlot assertion at mix.spec.ts:38. (r2 recorded this same spec failing AT line 42; the failure has moved.) Type gate blindness re-measured: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` = 0 diagnostics in 8.591s while tag/@click/aria-label/:disabled/:title are all no-ops.
```

**Reproduction.** npx playwright test e2e/smoke/views/mix.spec.ts --project=smoke --reporter=line  (pasted output above); and time npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit

**Proposed cure.** Sequenced: (1) cure the dock stability defect first or the mix gate cannot speak; (2) wire the five Playwright projects into ci.yml as hard steps — playwright.config.ts already provisions the webServer pair; (3) add the repo's FIRST component-mount Vitest test: mount MixSourceSelector with a stubbed LIBRARY_PORT_KEY, assert getByRole('button', {name: /Add current color/}) exists and that clicking it emits addColor. That single unit test runs in the lane CI already has and would have failed on f2c8f565.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · C-15 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** A palette deleted from the library remains an invisible, un-deselectable operand of the mix — canMix still counts it and mixColors still consumes it.

**Mechanism.** The selector holds a private copy of library rows instead of deriving them. removePalette can only be emitted from a card rendered from savedPalettes, so once a palette leaves the library its selection entry becomes unreachable while remaining live in the reducer.

**Evidence.**

```
MixSourceSelector.vue:230-268 renders selection exclusively from `savedPalettes` while the selection lives in useMixingState.selectedPalettes (useMixingState.ts:43); nothing reconciles them. Independently re-measured this round with a different probe (evidence/r3/probe-r3e-c15-verify.mjs): SELECTED-SOURCES 2 / MIX-DISABLED false; after deleting one selected palette from the store -> CARDS-AFTER-DELETE 2, MIX-SOURCES-AFTER-DELETE 1, MIX-DISABLED-AFTER-DELETE false, and pressing Mix produced a RESULT with ERRS []. canMix requires length>=2 while only ONE selected card is visible — arithmetic proof the deleted palette is still an operand.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-sourceselector/evidence/r3/probe-r3e-c15-verify.mjs

**Proposed cure.** Key selection by slug and DERIVE the operands: `const selectedSlugs = ref(new Set<string>())` plus `const selectedPalettes = computed(() => savedPalettes.value.filter(p => selectedSlugs.value.has(p.slug)))`. Deletion then removes the operand by construction — no watcher, no reconciliation, no possible skew, and a stale Set entry is inert and self-heals. This also retires addPalette's hand-rolled dedupe (useMixingState.ts:66) and fixes C-19 in the same stroke.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · C-14 · CHALLENGE-C

**Mechanism.** Render-time side table holding identity that belongs to the datum. ```

**Evidence.**

```

```

**Reproduction.** EXECUTED — `mixColorSequence([parseColorIn("oklch(100% 0 250)","hsl"), parseColorIn("#ff0000","hsl")], "hsl", "shorter")` then `colorToCss(...)` → `hsl(351.428571428571deg -81.25% 75%)`; feeding that string back through `parseColorIn(_, "hsl")` returns it unchanged.

**Proposed cure.** The R4-1 denominator guard fixes the sign. Independently, makeColor (model.ts:87) should assert the per-space channel domain (hsl.s ∈ [0,1], hwb.w+b, …), catching the corruption where it is created rather than three modules downstream in a saved palette.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfig` · R4-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `Distribute` — one of the three rows this bar's leftover-strategy Select offers — walks a non-monotonic source-index trajectory and emits a palette that doubles back on itself, contradicting its own documented contract.

**Mechanism.** Two remapping rules over one index range: an identity rule for i < len and an interpolation rule for i >= len, which do not agree at the seam. The interpolation formula is correct on its own; the short-circuit that precedes it is what breaks monotonicity.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/mix.ts:7 documents 'linearly interpolate shorter palettes across the longest length'; :79-81 returns the exact source color for every index < len, so only indices past the end reach the :90-103 distribute branch whose formula `fracPos = (index * (len - 1)) / (resultLength - 1)` was written for the whole range. Measured trajectory for len=3, resultLength=7: `0, 1, 2, 1.0000, 1.3333, 1.6667, 2.0000` — a backward jump from 2 to 1 at i=3. Measured output hues: 29°, 142°, 264°, 142°, 183°, 223°, 264° — row 3 byte-identical to row 1, row 6 to row 2.
```

**Reproduction.** EXECUTED — `mixPalettes([{colors:[#ff0000,#00ff00,#0000ff]}, {colors: 7×#808080}], { space: "oklch", hueMethod: "shorter", leftoverStrategy: "distribute" })` returns 7 rows whose 4th equals its 2nd and whose 7th equals its 3rd.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the `index < len` short-circuit for this strategy and let the single fracPos formula own the whole range — it already reduces to the identity when resultLength === len. One branch removed, not one added.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (r3: blind third replication + ` · II-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** NEW (neither r1 nor r2 carries it). A viewport change across a layout breakpoint destroys the entire extract session — the overlay, the sample, the zoom AND the uploaded image itself — because `eyedropperActive` and `useExtractSession` live as local setup state inside an async-loaded pane the shell is free to unmount.

**Evidence.**

```
Chromium, 2400x1800 upload, pinned sample: before resize {"overlayPresent":true,"canvasPresent":true,"viewportRect":[508,378],"transform":"translate(2px, 0px) scale(0.21)","previewStillLoaded":true,"readout":"lab(53.216681509299% …)"}; after 1100x800 unchanged; after 1000x640 {"overlayPresent":false,"canvasPresent":false,"viewportRect":null,"transform":null,"previewStillLoaded":false,"readout":null}; after 600x640 same. `previewStillLoaded` is `img[alt="Uploaded image"]` (ImageDropZone.vue:37-43) i.e. `session.previewDataUrl` — the uploaded image is gone, not merely the overlay. Code: ExtractWorkbench.vue:220,224 (session + eyedropperActive in setup scope), usePaneRouter.ts:72 (async pane).
```

**Reproduction.** /#/extract at 1280x900: upload, open the eyedropper, sample, then resize the window to 1000x640 (or rotate a phone / let mobile Safari's URL bar collapse across a breakpoint). Overlay, sample, zoom and the uploaded image are all gone; the user must re-upload. `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe9.mjs`.

**Proposed cure.** Lift `previewDataUrl` + `eyedropperActive` (and the rest of `useExtractSession`) to the pane-router/store altitude the repo already has — `usePaletteStore` is the in-repo precedent — so a layout switch re-renders the view without destroying the session. This is an altitude fix, not a guard; adding a `keep-alive` or a remount guard would paper over the same misplacement.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (r3: blind third replication + ` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

```
