The second rejection is `img.onerror = reject` at useImageSampler.ts:74 floating out of `loadAndFit()` (ImageEyedropper.vue:238,247). `canvasW: 300 / 300x150` is the browser's DEFAULT canvas geometry, proving useImageSampler.ts:86-92 never ran; imgWidth/imgHeight stay 0 so fitToViewport bails at useInertiaGesture.ts:157; sampleAt returns null at :112.
```

**Reproduction.** /#/extract, choose 'All Files' in the picker and select any non-image (or a truncated PNG), click the preview. The overlay opens onto a dead 300x150 canvas reading 'Tap to sample' forever. `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe.mjs` section C.

**Proposed cure.** `loadImage` returns the repo's own result shape (`{ ok, value } | { ok:false, error }` — see useExtractSession.ts:22-27 and `serializeCssColor`) instead of throwing into the void; the shell owns an `imageError` ref rendered in the destructive register the workbench already has (ExtractWorkbench.vue:79-85) with `role="status"`/`aria-live="polite"`; and `ImageDropZone.onFileSelected` applies the same MIME guard `onDrop` already applies (ImageDropZone.vue:97) — one guard, both entrances.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (r3: blind third replication + ` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The overlay claims modality it does not implement: no dialog role, no accessible name, no aria-modal, no focus move on open, no restore on close, no focus trap, no keyboard sampling path, and no live region on the async result.

**Mechanism.** A modal hand-rolled out of `absolute inset-0 z-popover glass-floating` (ImageEyedropper.vue:8) instead of the design system's dialog primitive — the hand-roll IS the cause of the missing semantics.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured on the live open overlay: {"role":null,"ariaModal":null,"ariaLabel":null,"ariaLive":"none","dialogCount":0,"vpTabIndex":null,"vpRole":null,"focusablesInOverlay":1,"active":"DIV.group"} (desktop — focus stays on the drop zone BEHIND the overlay) / "active":"BODY" (mobile). Tab trail from the open overlay: ["INPUT inOverlay=false","BODY inOverlay=false","SPAN{Number of colors} inOverlay=false","BUTTON[Upload image] inOverlay=false","BUTTON[Open camera] inOverlay=false","SPAN{Chroma weight} inOverlay=false"] — six presses, focus never enters, and it walks controls the overlay physically covers (visible bleeding through the glass in scratchpad/ccED/overlay-dark.png). Canvas is aria-hidden (ImageEyedropper.vue:74); the Add/Apply controls are `v-if="pinned"` and `pinned` is set only from `onTap`, i.e. only from a pointer. Entry point is equally closed: with a preview loaded ImageDropZone sets tabindex=-1 and disables its keydown handler (ImageDropZone.vue:19,22) while the eyedropper opens from the native @click (ExtractWorkbench.vue:25).
```

**Reproduction.** Open the eyedropper and press Tab six times; focus never enters the overlay. Or try to sample with a keyboard: there is no path, and no path to open it either. WCAG 2.1.1 (A), 4.1.2 (A), 2.4.3 (A) fail.

**Proposed cure.** Adopt the glass-ui dialog primitive (edict 4) rather than hand-rolling the overlay: role/aria-modal/labelledby, focus moved to the close control on enter and restored on exit, and a real trap come with it. Bind arrow keys + Enter to the same `sampleAt` the pointer uses so pinning is reachable from a keyboard, give the readout `aria-live="polite"`, and give the three DockControls real accessible names (which needs the `label` prop relayed under r2's N-5 — an `aria-label` at the call site is exactly the per-instance patch edict 5 forbids).

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (r3: blind third replication + ` · C-3-alpha · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Alpha is discarded at the point of formatting: a fully transparent pixel is reported to the user, and emitted to the palette / applied as the current colour, as opaque black.

**Mechanism.** A lossy projection (RGBA -> RGB hex) chosen as the component's internal colour currency, so the alpha channel has no representation anywhere downstream.

**Evidence.**

```
Fixture `alpha.png` (left half opaque #ff0000, right half alpha=0): opaque-red half -> readout `lab(54.290541404672% 80.804928170435 69.890964768624)`; TRANSPARENT half -> readout `lab(0% 0 0)` i.e. #000000. Code: useImageSampler.ts:117 `formatHex(data[0] ?? 0, data[1] ?? 0, data[2] ?? 0)` — `data[3]` is never read.
```

**Reproduction.** Upload a PNG with a transparent region, open the eyedropper, hover/tap the transparent area — it reads as pure black. `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe9.mjs` section ALPHA.

Live DOM (Playwright MCP on /#/gradient): {"tileNodeCount":27,"hasQuart":false,"hasQuint":false}. probe2.mjs: `PRESET MENU OPTIONS: 30 [... "ease-in-quart","ease-out-quart","ease-in-out-quart","ease-in-quint","ease-out-quint","ease-in-out-quint" ...]`. probe3.mjs: `ease-out-quint => {"headName":"1 → 2custom","readout":"cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)","pressedTiles":[]}` and `ease-in-quart => {"headName":"1 → 2custom",...}`. Or live: /#/gradient -> open the row's tune stage -> open the `Easing preset` combobox -> select `ease-out-quint` -> the closed-row head reads `custom` and no tile is pressed, while the readout correctly shows cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1). ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (round 2) of demo/workbenches/g` · C2-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `useSpecimenRows` is one monolithic computed that couples the WCAG ink certification to the whole `modelState` object, so dragging the Gradient DIRECTION slider — which cannot change any curve, endpoint colour or ink — re-derives every row. At 20 stops it is 60.3% of all main-thread JS on the route, 44x the cost of the serialization the drag actually requires.

**Mechanism.** Over-broad dependency: the computed takes `modelState` wholesale but needs only interpolationSpace + hueMethod, and it recomputes cheap per-row identity (48-sample glyph paths, tile ids, labels) in the same body as the expensive ambient-dependent WCAG floor walk.

**Evidence.**

```
CDP Profiler, 100us sampling, inclusive time, 60-move verified drag (direction 90 -> 270), scratchpad/probe13.mjs: 2 stops / 1 interval -> busy 504 ms, useSpecimenRows inclusive 67.3 ms (13.4%), certifyAccentInk 64.2 ms, useGradientCSS 11.3 ms. 20 stops / 19 intervals -> busy 1441 ms, useSpecimenRows inclusive 869.3 ms (60.3%), certifyAccentInk 810.5 ms, useGradientCSS 19.8 ms => 14.5 ms per direction tick (87% of a 16.7 ms frame). scratchpad/probe11.mjs at the live surface lightness (--ink-ambient-l = 0.79): msPerFullSpecimenRowsRecompute = 19.04 for 19 rows. scratchpad/bench.mjs, 2000 iterations each: glyphPath 0.0064 ms, interpolateStopColors 0.0062 ms, certifyAccentInk 1.6849 ms (99.2% of per-row cost). Code: useSpecimenRows.ts:42-73; useGradientModel.ts:102-109 (modelState returns a fresh object literal on any of type/direction/stops/intervals/space/hue); useContrastSafeColor.ts:356 (ambient dep) and :229-232 ('the AMBIENT is what moves per frame').
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/probe13.mjs — paste a 20-stop gradient into the code editor, then pointer-drag [role="slider"][aria-label="Gradient direction"] 60 moves under CDP Profiler; read inclusive samples for `(anon) @ useSpecimenRows.ts:17` (8693 samples = 869.3 ms) vs total busy (1441 ms).

**Proposed cure.** Split the computed along its real seams rather than memoizing the symptom: (1) derive identity per row from (stops[i], stops[i+1], intervals[i]) so an untouched interval never rebuilds its glyph; (2) memoize the certified ink on (c0, c1, space, hue, ambient, dark); (3) stop passing modelState wholesale — take narrow getters `() => modelState.interpolationSpace` / `.hueMethod` so `type` and `direction` cease to be dependencies BY CONSTRUCTION, which is stronger than any cache.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (round 2) of demo/workbenches/g` · C2-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Disclosure state is keyed by array index and never reconciled with the collection, producing two observable failures: a DEAD state (after the interval list shrinks below openInterval, no row is open at all, contradicting the component's own contract) and RESURRECTION (a stale tuneOpen key re-opens the authoring stage on a completely different interval when the list re-grows).

Shrunk to 3 stops -> rows 2, expandedHeads ["false","false"] (NO row open). Re-grown to 8 stops -> expandedHeads [false x6, "true"] and tunePanels [... "easing-authoring-6:block"] — state resurrected onto a different interval whose curve applyCSS had re-seeded to linear (gradientParse.ts:292-297). Code: GradientEasingEditor.vue:61 (openInterval seeded 0), :84-88 (tuneOpen only ever adds keys). **Defect.** MAJOR/NEW — the anchor's host element enters the DOM 239 ms after startMix() on every re-mix, because `mode="out-in"` serialises leave-then-enter while the animation composable measures at flush:"post". Both prior passes' cures for D-1 fail this.

**Mechanism.** F-B: anchoring a measurement target inside the very transition that unmounts it. The docstring's premise ('the plate stands as the announced destination', lines 12-14) is contradicted by a destination that ceases to exist for 239 ms.

**Evidence.**

```
MixResultDisplay.vue:60 `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">`. useMixingAnimation.ts:169-183 watches phase with flush:"post" and comments 'the ghost well ([data-mix-target]) mounts in the same reactive flush that opens the mixing window'. Measured per-rAF from startMix(): `[{t:3, innerFirstChildIsWell:false, innerCls:"flex flex-col gap-3 vj-morph-leave-from vj-morph-leave-active"}, {t:239, innerFirstChildIsWell:true, innerCls:"flex items-center gap-3 vj-morph-enter-from vj-morph-enter-active"}]`. MIX_ARRIVE_MS = 700 (mixStage.ts:22).

**Reproduction.** node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/WBMRD-probe5.mjs — section (e). Requires a prior settled mix (phase 'done') so the re-mix path is exercised.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (premise: the compo` · C-14 (MINOR → MAJOR) · CHALLENGE-C

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (round 2) on demo/w` · R2-N1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** A CANCELLED pointer gesture commits the add. `onBarPointerUp` is bound to both @pointerup and @pointercancel and is the handler that emits `add`. pointercancel means the platform abandoned the gesture (second touch, system gesture, OS interrupt) — committing on it is the inverse of the contract. Same conflation on the handle (@pointercancel -> onHandlePointerUp) runs the re-tap-to-deselect branch on a cancelled press.

**Mechanism.** one handler serving two events with opposite semantics; the tidy-looking reuse ('both end the gesture') erases the only distinction that matters

**Evidence.**

```
GradientStopEditor.vue:207-208 (@pointerup + @pointercancel both -> onBarPointerUp) and :101-110 (the emit('add')); handle at :267-268. Live probe output: `A) handles at rest: 2` / `B) handles after pointerdown → POINTERCANCEL on the bar: 3` / `B) labels: ["Gradient stop at 0%","Gradient stop at 40%","Gradient stop at 100%"]`
```

**Reproduction.** `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/challenge-C-r2-pointercancel.mjs` — touch-enabled context, dispatch pointerdown at 40% of the rail then pointercancel at the same point, no pointerup. Handle count goes 2 -> 3.

**Proposed cure.** Split the handlers. `onBarPointerCancel` clears pendingAdd/draggingId and commits NOTHING; `onBarPointerUp` keeps the commit. Same split on the handle. This is the repo's own pointercancel idiom (ComponentSliders.vue) used correctly — as recovery, never as commit.

Chip width `inline-size: 2.618rem` = 41.9px (PreviewRamp.vue:43). Modelled worst-band deviation (sRGB chord between adjacent stops vs the library's own value at that parameter, Euclidean 0-255): oklch·longer 23.5/255 at band 7; oklch·shorter 1.1/255; hsv·longer 0.5/255. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · D-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The two bezier control handles measure 13.33 x 13.33 px — a 44% shortfall against the WCAG 2.2 AA §2.5.8 24px target-size floor — and the visual audit matrix structurally cannot see them, so the route's reported tap-target count under-counts by 2.

**Mechanism.** A11y geometry as a downstream function of a broken layout law — the handle's affordance size is derived from the canvas's rendered scale rather than declared independently, so D-2's dead selector silently halves it.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured live (EAS-probe5.mjs, stage disclosed, 1280x900):
```
[{"tag":"circle","role":"slider","label":"Bezier control point 1","w":13.33,"h":13.33,"under24":true},
 {"tag":"circle","role":"slider","label":"Bezier control point 2","w":13.33,"h":13.33,"under24":true},
 {"tag":"button","role":"combobox","label":"Easing preset","w":436,"h":40,"under24":false}]
```
Causal arithmetic: handle is r="0.04" in viewBox units → diameter = 0.08 x (plotWidth / vbWidth). Broken: plot 166.67px → 13.33px (matches). Cured: plot 304px → 24.32px (matches the injected-cure measurement exactly).
Under-count: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json reports `smallTapTargets: 6` for safari-desktop-light /#/gradient, none a bezier handle — impossible, because the stage sits inside `v-show="tuneOpen[row.index]"` and measures `PRE-DISCLOSE {"pickers":1,"authoringHosts":1,"wrapperDisplay":"none","intervalRows":1}`, so getBoundingClientRect() returns zeros. shots/safari-desktop-light/gradient.png confirms the stage is not captured. True route contribution = 6 + 2 = 8.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → open row 0 → click "Author a custom curve" → `[...document.querySelectorAll("#easing-authoring-0 circle[role='slider']")].map(e => e.getBoundingClientRect().width)` → [13.33, 13.33].

**Proposed cure.** Fix D-2 and the geometry cures itself (measured: 24.32px, clears the floor with no separate change). Then, defensively and at the producer where it belongs, ask glass-ui for a transparent hit-circle of r >= 24/plotScale behind each visible handle — the standard SVG hit-area idiom — so the handle's affordance stops being a function of the canvas's layout size at all. Also: any future state-aware visual capture pass MUST open the tune disclosure, or this component stays invisible to the matrix.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The producer probe fails silently by construction: `syncVbRatio` collapses "the producer's DOM changed under me" and "the SVG has not laid out yet" into the same bare `return`, with no dev-time warning and no visible degradation the eye reads as broken rather than chosen.

```
demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingAuthoringStage.vue:47-53 —

function syncVbRatio() {
    const vb = rootEl.value?.querySelector<SVGSVGElement>("svg[role='img']")?.viewBox.baseVal;
    if (!vb || vb.width <= 0 || vb.height <= 0) return;
    vbRatio.value = vb.height / vb.width;

No `import.meta.env.DEV` assertion, no console note. Silence corroborated: the live /#/gradient run logged only the unrelated dev-misconfig line, and REPORT.json records `"consoleErrors": [], "consoleWarnings": [], "pageErrors": []` for all four capture matrices while the law was fully inert. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt, `demo/workbenches/` · R3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Blurring inside the debounce window DESTROYS the user's in-progress text and then shows a verdict naming a token that is no longer on screen — a direct breach of the law this file documents at lines 34-40 ("A failed parse keeps the user's text verbatim alongside the verdict — WIP is never destroyed").

**Mechanism.** Stale read on an async round-trip: onBlur (lines 68-73) branches on `hasError`, which is derived from the `parseVerdict` prop — the verdict of the PREVIOUS parse. At blur the pending parse has not run, so the guard consults a value that is about to change. Same family as the repo's recorded defineModel stale-read hazard.

**Proposed cure.** Flush rather than race: on blur, cancel the timer and run the parse synchronously, THEN decide whether to settle to the canonical serialization. Blur and the last verdict become the same instant, and the WIP-preserving law holds by construction instead of by timing luck.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt, round 3 (independe` · R3-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Pressing Enter in the CSS editor silently welds the tokens on either side of the break: the text handed to the parser is read with `textContent`, which does not represent block breaks, so `red` ⏎ `0%` reaches the parser as `red0%` and the user is told a token they never typed is unparseable — on a surface explicitly built for multiple lines.

**Mechanism.** Reading a rich contenteditable's text with the DOM-text accessor instead of the RENDERED-text accessor. `tokenizeTopLevel` (gradientParse.ts:70-89) splits on whitespace, and the whitespace it needed was discarded one layer up.

**Evidence.**

```
GradientCodeEditor.vue:59-62 (`editorRef.value?.textContent`), :93 (`min-h-[5rem] max-h-[12rem] overflow-y-auto whitespace-pre-wrap`). Run `probes/challenge-C-r3-editor-race.mjs` (P2): {"editorText":"linear-gradient(90deg, red0%, blue 100%)","editorHTML":"linear-gradient(90deg, red<div>0%, blue 100%)</div>","verdict":"unparseable color \"red0%\""}. Cure measured in the same probe (P4): textContent "…red0%…" vs innerText "…red\n0%…".
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/.../probes/challenge-C-r3-editor-race.mjs — CONFIRMED, pasted. A real multi-line PASTE is correct (measured: under white-space:pre-wrap the browser inserts literal \n), which is why no spec sees it — `typeIntoEditor` never presses Enter.

**Proposed cure.** `contenteditable="plaintext-only"` on the editor so the browser cannot insert block elements into a code surface at all; failing that, read `innerText` rather than `textContent` (measured to preserve the break exactly). One attribute or one identifier — no shim, no new module.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt, round 3 (independe` · R3-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The stop-ordering invariant breaks on the KEYBOARD path, not just on drag, and the resulting array order desynchronises DOM/tab order from visual order: after a keyboard-only nudge, Tab visits the handles right → left → right.

**Mechanism.** Ordering is treated as a habit of one of three call sites instead of a property of the type; the view renders `v-for` in array order, so an unsorted array is directly a scrambled focus order. WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order + 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence.

**Evidence.**

```
GradientStopEditor.vue:173-179 (`onHandleKeydown` emits the same `update:position` the drag does) → GradientVisualizer.vue:94-96 → useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (`updateStop` writes a raw position, no re-sort; `addStop` at :118 DOES sort and `gradientParse.ts:284-290` REJECTS non-monotonic input — three owners, three policies). Run `probes/challenge-C-r3-focus-order.mjs`: S1 rows=[{0,"Gradient stop at 70%",x:531},{1,"Gradient stop at 50%",x:444},{2,"Gradient stop at 100%",x:665}], domOrder=[0,1,2], visualOrder=[1,0,2]; S2 sequential focus order ["…70%","…50%","…100%"].
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/.../probes/challenge-C-r3-focus-order.mjs — CONFIRMED, pasted; screenshot evidence/challenge-C-r3-crossed-focus-order.png. Gesture: click the rail at 50% to add a stop, focus the first handle, press Shift+ArrowRight x7.

**Proposed cure.** One writer — `setStopPosition(id, pos)` returns the re-sorted model (and re-keys intervals, per C-5) — with `stops` readonly to the view. Ordering becomes unrepresentable-if-violated rather than re-established by whichever call site remembers.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt, subject demo/workb` · C-8 · CHALLENGE-C

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/workbenches/g` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Interval identity is positional: inserting a stop mid-ramp silently re-hosts every downstream authored curve onto a different colour pair, and the accordion's index-keyed disclosure state follows the index rather than the interval.

**Mechanism.** positional-identity: per-item state keyed on an array ordinal over a list whose items are inserted and removed in the middle, so identity shifts silently under every non-tail edit.

**Evidence.**

```
Reproduced (probe 9): BEFORE insert `{"heads":["1 → 2linear","2 → 3ease-in-out-expo"],"stops":["0%","50%","100%"],"open":["easing-interval-1"],"tune":["false","true"]}` — ease-in-out-expo authored for 50%→100%. AFTER inserting a stop at 24%: `{"heads":["1 → 2linear","2 → 3ease-in-out-expo","3 → 4linear"],"stops":["0%","24%","50%","100%"],"open":["easing-interval-1"],"tune":["false","true","false"]}` — the curve is still on row `2 → 3`, which now means 24%→50%; the interval it was authored for is now `3 → 4`, reset to linear. Mechanism: useGradientModel.ts:89-100 the sync watch is append/truncate-only (`while (intervals.value.length < needed) intervals.value.push(linearInterval())`) and only observes `stops.value.length`, while addStop (:116-120) inserts positionally sorted and removeStop (:122-125) filters by id. GradientEasingEditor keys ALL its own state on the same ordinal: openInterval (:61), tuneOpen (:84), copiedIndex (:95), the DOM ids `easing-interval-${row.index}` (:145) / `easing-authoring-${row.index}` (:205), the v-for :key (:113), and the update-interval emit (:49).
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/wbge-probe9.mjs — or manually: 1. open /#/gradient. 2. click the stop bar at 50% (3 stops, 2 intervals). 3. open row `2 → 3` and press the `expo in-out` specimen tile. 4. click the stop bar at 25%. 5. row `2 → 3` still reads ease-in-out-expo but now spans 24%→50%; the 50%→100% interval you authored is now row `3 → 4`, linear.

**Proposed cure.** Give the interval a stable identity derived from the pair it spans, not from its ordinal. Stops already carry uid() (useGradientModel.ts:66-69) — hold intervals in a Map<string, GradientInterval> keyed on the LEFT stop's id. Insertion then splits an interval instead of shifting a list: the new stop's key gets a fresh linearInterval(), every existing key keeps its curve, removal drops exactly one entry. GradientEasingEditor keys its accordion, disclosure, v-for :key, DOM ids and emit on that same id — which also fixes the v-for :key="row.index" that currently makes Vue reuse row DOM across a shift, the reason the disclosure appears to 'stick' to the wrong interval.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/workbenches/g` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Every accordion row mounts in full — specimen strip and a live EasingPicker — although the accordion can display exactly one row at a time; ~75% of the mounted DOM is permanently display:none.

**Mechanism.** eager-mount: a v-show accordion mounts the bodies of rows that have never been disclosed, so mount cost scales with item count rather than with disclosure.

**Evidence.**

```
Row body is v-show (GradientEasingEditor.vue:144); the authoring stage's v-if (:208) guards only `intervals[row.index]`, always truthy. Measured (probes 1 and 2, Chromium 1440×900, /#/gradient): 2 stops / 1 interval → allElements 511, buttons 53, [data-specimen] 27, easing-picker 1, visible rows 1. 5 stops / 4 intervals → allElements 1109, buttons 149, [data-specimen] 108, easing-picker 4, visible rows STILL 1. Delta +598 elements, +96 buttons, +81 hidden tile buttons, +3 fully-wired hidden EasingPicker instances (each with drag handlers and its own curve sampling), plus one useMediaQuery matchMedia subscription per strip (EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:47). Cost on an unrelated interaction, 120 ArrowRight presses on the Direction slider, CDP Performance.getMetrics deltas (probe 8): 1 interval `{scriptMs 13.9, layoutMs 20.7, recalcMs 191.6}` vs 4 intervals `{scriptMs 16.9, layoutMs 26.1, recalcMs 258.0}` → script/tick 0.116ms → 0.141ms (+22%), style recalc +34.7%, layout +26%.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/wbge-probe2.mjs — or manually: open /#/gradient, click the stop bar at 25%, 50% and 75%, then run in the console `({elements: document.querySelectorAll('*').length, pickers: document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="easing-picker"]').length, tiles: document.querySelectorAll('[data-specimen]').length, visibleRows: [...document.querySelectorAll("[id^='easing-interval-']")].filter(e=>getComputedStyle(e).display!=='none').length})` → {elements: 1109, pickers: 4, tiles: 108, visibleRows: 1}.

**Proposed cure.** Keep the alive-once-opened property without the eager fan-out. The v-show choice is documented (:16-18, 'Picker instances stay ALIVE … no remount/echo discipline') and is right for the OPEN row, but does not justify mounting rows never opened. Wrap the existing v-show in `v-if="everOpened.has(row.id)"` — a Set populated by toggleInterval — which gives exactly the stated invariant (no remount, no echo) at one-row cost on arrival. Give the authoring stage the same treatment keyed on tuneOpen: a user who never presses the sliders icon should never pay for an EasingPicker.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect interrogation of demo/wo` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The two bezier control handles — the component's primary direct-manipulation controls — render 13.3 x 13.3 CSS px, 45% below the WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 24px floor; and the megatranche visual audit structurally cannot see them, so the route's tap-target count is under-reported.

**Mechanism.** Handle size is specified in viewBox units, so its rendered target size is a pure function of the canvas layout size — which is exactly what the dead Law 3 controls. Consequence of C-2, not an independent choice.

**Evidence.**

```
Live, stage disclosed: [{tag:"circle",role:"slider",tabindex:"0",label:"Bezier control point 1",w:13.3,h:13.3},{...point 2, w:13.3,h:13.3},{tag:"button",role:"combobox",label:"Easing preset",w:298,h:40}]. Geometry: handle r≈0.04 viewBox units → diameter = 0.08 x plotWidth; broken plot width 166.67 → 13.3px (matches); with Law 3 alive at the 272px canvas → 0.08 x 272 = 21.8px, 64% larger and STILL under 24. Under-count: audit/visual/REPORT.json safari-desktop-light /#/gradient reports smallTapTargets:6, none a bezier handle — the stage sits behind two disclosures (GradientEasingEditor.vue:84 tuneOpen defaults false) and measures display:none at capture, so getBoundingClientRect returns zeros; shots/safari-desktop-light/gradient.png confirms the stage is absent from the capture. True contribution is 6+2 = 8.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; open row 0; click "Author a custom curve"; `[...document.querySelectorAll('#easing-authoring-0 [role="slider"]')].map(e=>e.getBoundingClientRect().width)` → [13.3, 13.3]. HONEST CAVEAT: the producer compensates at the pointer layer — HANDLE_HIT_RADIUS=0.1 / HANDLE_HIT_RADIUS_TOUCH=0.15 viewBox units (glass-ui/dist/components/easing/constants.d.ts) ≈ 16.7/25px radius — so the grab area clears 24px; the visible target and the keyboard focus ring do not.

**Proposed cure.** Fix C-2 (→21.8px), then relay to glass-ui for a transparent hit-circle of r >= 24/plotScale behind each visible handle (the standard SVG hit-area idiom) so handle affordance stops being a function of canvas layout size. A seat-side !important on an SVG `r` is not an acceptable substitute. Separately: any state-aware visual-capture pass must open the tune disclosure, or this component stays invisible to the audit.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect interrogation of demo/wo` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The producer probe fails silently by construction: the ref's birth constant (1.2), the CSS var() fallback (1.2) and the true ratio of the default seeded curve (linear's padded box, 1 + 2*VIEW_PAD = 1.2) are the same number, so a never-synced stage is byte-identical in the DOM to a perfectly-working one. syncVbRatio makes "the producer's DOM changed under me" and "the SVG has not laid out yet" the same bare `return`.

**Mechanism.** A masking fallback (owner edict 2) whose job is to make a broken state look like a working one, combined with a silent early-return on a foreign-DOM probe. This is why a producer major could delete the component's function and leave no trace for eleven days.

**Evidence.**

```
EasingAuthoringStage.vue:45 `const vbRatio = ref(1.2);`, :51 `if (!vb || vb.width <= 0 || vb.height <= 0) return;`, :107 `aspect-ratio: calc(1 / var(--vb-ratio, 1.2)) !important;`. No dev warning, no import.meta.env.DEV assertion, no attribute, no console output. audit/visual/REPORT.json records "consoleErrors": [], "consoleWarnings": [], "pageErrors": [] for /#/gradient in all four Safari matrices. Measured --vb-ratio frozen at "1.2" across mount, watcher and keyboard edit. L45's comment also hardcodes a copy of the producer's VIEW_PAD constant.
```

**Reproduction.** CONFIRMED — this is the mechanism behind C-2 and is evidenced by C-2's measurements: --vb-ratio reads "1.2" whether or not the sync has ever run, with zero console output.

**Proposed cure.** Dissolved entirely by C-2's terminal cure (a producer-owned fit prop has no fallback to mask). If the interim hook is taken instead: drop the var() default, initialise vbRatio to null, and make the miss loud in dev — `if (import.meta.env.DEV && rootEl.value && !el) console.error('[EasingAuthoringStage] producer contract drift: "' + CANVAS_SEL + '" matched nothing')`. A seat that scrapes a foreign DOM must scream when the DOM moves.

**Defect.** A malformed or non-image file produces two unhandled promise rejections and a dead, error-less eyedropper overlay that still advertises "tap to sample"; the <input type=file> path also lacks the MIME guard the drop path has.

**Mechanism.** Async work started from a lifecycle hook as a floating promise, with the failure branch rejecting a non-Error and no consumer-side error state — so the failure is invisible to both the user and the code.

**Evidence.**

```
useImageSampler.ts:72-75 (`img.onerror = reject` — rejects with a raw Event, not an Error) + ImageEyedropper.vue:238,247 (loadAndFit() is a floating promise at both call sites, no catch) + ImageDropZone.vue:87-92 (onFileSelected has NO type check) vs :97 (onDrop DOES check `file?.type.startsWith("image/")`). MEASURED: assigning an application/pdf File to the hidden input yields {previewZoneAppeared:true, previewLabel:"Image preview area, tap to sample colors", overlayOpen:true, canvasBacking:[300,150], readout:"Tap to sample", errorSurfacedToUser:false} and unhandled rejections ["The source image could not be decoded.","error"]. Browser console log .playwright-mcp/console-2026-07-28T13-54-12-549Z.log: `[38906ms] The source image could not be decoded.` / `[38971ms] Event`. canvasBacking [300,150] is the browser DEFAULT — proof loadImage threw before useImageSampler.ts:88-89 ever sized the canvas.
```

**Reproduction.** On /#/extract click the drop zone, choose 'All Files' in the OS picker, select any non-image (a .pdf). The preview zone appears labelled 'Image preview area, tap to sample colors'; click it; the eyedropper opens permanently empty saying 'Tap to sample' with no error anywhere, and two unhandled rejections hit the console.

**Proposed cure.** loadImage rejects with a real Error; the shell owns an `imageError` ref rendered in the same `text-destructive` register the sibling already uses (ExtractWorkbench.vue:80-85); and ImageDropZone applies its existing MIME guard at BOTH entrances rather than only at the drop.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (demo/workbenches/extra` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The eyedropper is 100% inoperable by keyboard and invisible to assistive technology: no dialog role, no focus move/trap/restore, no aria-live on the async readout, and the sampling surface is aria-hidden with no keyboard alternative.

**Mechanism.** A modal surface hand-rolled from positioning utilities instead of adopting the design system's dialog primitive — the hand-roll is the direct cause of every missing semantic.

**Evidence.**

```
MEASURED on the live open overlay: overlay role=null, aria-modal=null, [aria-live] count inside overlay = 0, document.activeElement on open = BODY (focus never enters), focusables inside overlay (unpinned) = 1 (Close only), canvas tabIndex=-1 + aria-hidden="true", viewport div tabIndex=-1 role=null, buttons = [{title:"Close eyedropper", ariaLabel:null, text:""}] at 40x40 CSS px. Source: ImageEyedropper.vue:8 (bare div `absolute inset-0 z-popover ... glass-floating`), :74 (aria-hidden canvas), :35-37 (readout span, no aria-live), :43-58 (Add/Apply are v-if="pinned", and pinned is set only from onTap i.e. only from a pointer). Entry is gated too: ImageDropZone.vue:21 sets tabindex -1 once a preview exists.
```

**Reproduction.** Open /#/extract, upload an image, open the eyedropper, then use only the keyboard. Tab moves into the controls the overlay is visually covering, never into it. **Proposed cure.** Adopt the glass-ui dialog primitive (edict 4) so role/aria-modal/focus-trap/restoration come from the design system; add aria-live="polite" to the readout; and bind arrow keys to the same sampleAt the pointer uses so pinning has a keyboard path.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (demo/workbenches/extra` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** A ResizeObserver is wired directly to the initialiser, so any viewport size change unconditionally discards the user's zoom and pan.

**Mechanism.** Conflation of 'fit' (a one-time initialisation) with 'reflow' (a size-change response), so a continuous observer keeps re-running an initialiser.

**Evidence.**

```
useInertiaGesture.ts:354-360 (`new ResizeObserver(() => fitToViewport())`) + :164-166 (fitToViewport unconditionally assigns `zoom.value = fit` and recentres pan). MEASURED with a 512x512 fixture, changing only a CSS height on a DOM ancestor (no component API called): beforeZoom {zoom:0.691406}, afterWheelZoom {zoom:1.39125}, afterResize {zoom:0.691406}, afterRestore {zoom:0.691406}. A 2.01x inspection zoom is destroyed and does not return when the resize is undone.
```

**Reproduction.** Open the eyedropper on any image, ctrl+wheel to zoom in, then resize the window (or on mobile Safari, scroll so the URL bar collapses). The zoom snaps back to fit and the pan recentres.

**Proposed cure.** Split the two: fitToViewport stays a one-time call from loadAndFit/onTransitionEnd (where ImageEyedropper.vue:203,207 already calls it), and the ResizeObserver runs a distinct `reflow()` that preserves the zoom ratio and the image-space centre point and only re-clamps the pan.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/workbenches/gr` · C-9 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The Direction slider is a dead control whenever Type is Radial, and the authored angle is silently destroyed by the radial round-trip.

```
`npx vite-node probes/direction-probe.ts`: 'radial 0deg vs 270deg identical? true' (linear/conic false). Round-trip: 'simpleCSS shown for radial @137deg: radial-gradient(red 0%, blue 100%)' → 're-parsed direction: 0 (authored 137)'. ```

**Reproduction.** npx vite-node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/direction-probe.ts. Live: set 137°, switch Type→Radial, type a character in the CSS box, switch back to Linear — the angle is 0.

**Proposed cure.** Direction belongs to the linear and conic geometries, not to 'a gradient'. Model a discriminated GradientGeometry so the control's presence is derived from the type and the serializer cannot drop a field the model claims to hold.

**Reproduction.** node+playwright to http://localhost:9000/#/mix, wait 3s, then `[...document.querySelectorAll('label.section-label')].map(l => ({text: l.textContent.trim(), htmlFor: l.htmlFor || null, control: l.control ? l.control.tagName : null}))` → both entries report htmlFor null and control null. Click the visible "Color space" text → document.activeElement stays BODY and no [role=listbox] opens.

**Proposed cure.** One name, one source: `<Label for="mix-space">Color space</Label>` using the glass-ui primitive demo/ui/label already re-exports, plus `id="mix-space"` on the SelectTrigger (accepted as fallthrough), and delete all three duplicated `aria-label`s. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:49-55 (camera control, no :disabled) vs :84 (reset, has it); ExtractWorkbench.vue:70. **Proposed cure.** The same `useCameraStream()` as C-2 — a resource composable is idempotent on start() by construction (it releases or reuses the prior handle). The disabled-prop fan-out in ExtractControls is a symptom; the cure is that the workbench should not be able to acquire twice at all.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C-7 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The component allocates 45.8 MB and transfers 22.9 MB to the worker in order to read 10,500 of 6,000,000 pixels — 99.825% waste — and does the readback on the main thread. `imageFileToPixels` decodes at native resolution, rasterises to a full-size OffscreenCanvas and calls getImageData (main-thread), then `pixels.buffer.slice(0)` copies the whole thing AGAIN before transferring. Meanwhile src/quantize.ts sub-samples with targetPixels=10_000. The preview adds a 15.4 MB retained base64 string for an 11.5 MB file.

**Mechanism.** work done at full fidelity upstream of a sampler that discards 99.8% of it; the worker boundary is defeated by a main-thread readback

**Evidence.**

```
useImageQuantize.ts:18-26 and :93; src/quantize.ts:41,52. Measured (exact imageFileToPixels body replayed on a 3000x2000 JPEG): {"decode_createImageBitmap_ms":8.6,"getImageData_mainthread_ms":13.8,"bufferSlice_copy_ms":1.8,"total_mainthread_ms":24.3,"bytesAllocated_MB":45.8,"bytesTransferredToWorker_MB":22.9,"pixelsInImage":6000000,"pixelsQuantizerActuallyReads":10500,"wastedFraction":0.99825}. Plus previewDataUrlLength 15382718 from the C-1 run.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/extract — in-page, replay imageFileToPixels verbatim on a 3000x2000 JPEG File and time each phase. Scale to a 12 MP phone photo (4032x3024): 48.7 MB ImageData + 48.7 MB slice = ~97 MB transient, on mobile Safari.

**Proposed cure.** `createImageBitmap(file, { resizeWidth, resizeHeight, resizeQuality: 'low' })` sized to sqrt(targetPixels) — the decoder does the downscale off-thread; the canvas becomes 200x150, getImageData becomes 120 KB, and the slice(0) disappears entirely (transfer imageData.data.buffer directly, since the ImageData is discarded on the next line). For the preview, URL.createObjectURL is O(1) and drops 15.4 MB.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C-8 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The dominance readout can name a colour that is not the card's first swatch, contradicting the component's own stated invariant ('the card's first swatch IS the dominant specimen'). src/quantize.ts sorts by population with a STABLE sort (ties keep insertion order); useExtractSession's `dominant` uses a different rule — strict `>` on population PLUS a chroma tiebreak. The two orderings disagree on every population tie.

**Mechanism.** two independent orderings over the same data, only one of which the card renders; a documented invariant enforced nowhere

**Evidence.**

```
Invariant asserted at ExtractWorkbench.vue:113-117. Conflicting orderings: src/quantize.ts:128 vs useExtractSession.ts:121-142. Library derivation (npx tsx on src/quantize.ts, 2x1 image of #ff0000 + #0000ff): index 0 = [0.628, 0.2577, 29.234] pop=1 (RED, first swatch); index 1 = [0.452, 0.3132, 264.052] pop=1 (BLUE). Live readout for that same image: "oklch(45.201371817442% 0.313214388634 264.05202261637deg)" — hue 264deg, the BLUE one.
```

**Reproduction.** npx tsx: quantizePixels(new Uint8ClampedArray([255,0,0,255, 0,0,255,255]), 2, 1, {k:5, chromaWeight:0.5}) returns red at index 0. Then drop that same 2x1 PNG on http://localhost:9000/#/extract: the readout names the blue cluster while colors[0] (and thus the first swatch) is red.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the 22-line `dominant` loop. quantizePixels already guarantees max-population-first, so `dominant = presented.value[0] ?? null` is the whole function, is BY CONSTRUCTION the first swatch, and restores the stated invariant. If a chroma tiebreak is genuinely wanted it belongs in src/quantize.ts's sort, where the card's ordering also sees it — one ordering, one truth.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C2-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `trackInk` costs 1.2975 ms per evaluation and is driven by the SYNCHRONOUS `cssColorOpaque`, not the rAF-coalesced `cssColorOpaqueFrame` that exists for exactly this purpose — roughly 78 ms of main-thread work per second of colour drag while the (KeepAlive-cached) extract pane is alive.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C2-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `useImageQuantize` holds a single pendingResolve/pendingReject pair, so an overlapping quantize orphans the previous promise permanently, and `isProcessing` is cleared by the first worker response while a second job is still queued — the UI declares 'done' and paints a result that is about to be silently replaced.

**Mechanism.** Request/response worker without request identity: a single mutable continuation slot cannot represent more than one outstanding job.

**Evidence.**

```
useImageQuantize.ts:51-52 single-slot pending pair; :89-91 overwritten on every runQuantize; :65 `isProcessing.value = false` in onmessage regardless of outstanding requests; useExtractSession.ts:155 discards the returned promise. Overlap measured — reachable only because the k slider stays live during processing (C2-1's unbound disabled): posts [{t:8115,opts:{k:5,…},bytes:24000000},{t:8531,opts:{k:9,…},bytes:24000000}], 416 ms apart, both in flight.
```

**Reproduction.** evidence/pass-2/xc2-probe3.mjs stage C — upload a 3000×2000 PNG, then press ArrowRight on the 'Number of colors' thumb four times during processing; read window.__wpm.

**Proposed cure.** Give each request a monotonically increasing token carried in the request and echoed in the response; drop stale responses and make isProcessing = (inFlight > 0). That deletes the single slot rather than guarding it. NOTE: the unhandled-rejection leg (a worker {type:'error'} rejecting a floating promise) is a HYPOTHESIS — I could not provoke a worker error; a 1×1 image at k=5 succeeds.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C2-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Mechanism.** Full-resolution decode at the boundary with downsampling deferred to the consumer inside the worker; the library's own guard option is never passed.

**Evidence.**

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/gra` · R3-8 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The per-row derivation performs ~17 ms of unmemoized contrast certification per interval on every modelState tick — including ticks (direction, type) to which its output is provably invariant.

**Mechanism.** Two compounding faults: (a) the composable subscribes to the WHOLE modelState computed (GradientEasingEditor.vue:54-58) although it reads only interpolationSpace and hueMethod, so direction/type invalidate it; (b) certifyAccentInk is unmemoized, so the identical input costs full price every time. The live 367 ms/tick figure is whole-page and NOT attributed wholesale (longTasks: 0 means the cost is spread) — the attributable claim is the node measurement plus the byte-identical-output proof.

**Evidence.**

```
`npx vite-node probes/p9b-ink-cost.ts` -> 'certifyAccentInk x 200 (distinct inputs): total 3402.2 ms -> 17.011 ms/call' ; 'certifyAccentInk x 200 (SAME input): total 3195.5 ms -> 15.978 ms/call (memoized? false)' ; '60 ticks x 5 rows: 6653.1 ms total -> 110.88 ms per tick'. Invariance: `npx vite-node ../wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/cost-probe.ts` -> 'specimenRows same at 90deg and 271deg? true'. Live context (probes/p7-output.log): '20 direction ticks (whole page): {"totalMs":7343.2,"perTickMs":367.2,"longTasks":0}'. Source: useSpecimenRows.ts:40,69 via useSafeAccentFn("resting"); certifyAccentInk at demo/color-session/ink.ts:130 (no cache).
```

**Reproduction.** `npx vite-node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-easingeditor/probes/p9b-ink-cost.ts` and `npx vite-node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/cost-probe.ts`

**Proposed cure.** Narrow rather than cache over: (1) useSpecimenRows takes `() => modelState.interpolationSpace` and `() => modelState.hueMethod` as its own getters so the row derivation stops being a direction/type subscriber; (2) memoize certifyAccentInk on (css, surfaceL, floor) INSIDE useContrastSafeColor — one cache at the instrument serving all six consumers, not a per-consumer wrapper.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/mix` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The `swatchKeys` "stable key" scheme (MixSourceSelector.vue:78-98) embeds the array index in the map key (`${sc.css}::${i}`), and the prune watch (flush 'pre', so it runs BEFORE the render that re-reads the computed) deletes every shifted entry. Removing a chip therefore re-keys every surviving chip at or after that index — Vue unmounts and remounts them. This defeats the FLIP `.vj-enter-move` reflow the shared recipe promises, forces up to N-1 unchanged chips into `position:absolute` simultaneously (collapsing the row), and rebuilds N-1 glass-ui feTurbulence filter graphs in one frame. Strictly worse than :key="i".

**Mechanism.** list identity / reconciliation — a positional key masquerading as an identity key

**Evidence.**

```
MixSourceSelector.vue:79-98 (counter + Map + computed + prune watch); useMixingState.ts:55-61 (immutable add/remove). demo/styles/utils.css:167-179 documents the intent verbatim ("neighbours reflow on the family move class") and sets `.swatch-row > .vj-enter-leave-active { position: absolute }`; demo/styles/animations.css:99 defines `.vj-enter-move`. glass-ui dist/watercolor-dot.js:96,119-127 mounts a per-instance useId()-named <filter> with feTurbulence numOctaves="5" whose own header calls per-frame re-rasterization the Safari §H hazard. MAX_COLORS=12 (MixSourceSelector.vue:38) sets the worst case at 11 rebuilt filters.
```

**Reproduction.** $ node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-mix-sourceselector/swatch-key-churn.repro.mjs (algorithm transcribed verbatim from :79-98, driven through useMixingState.removeColor/addColor) →
render 1  [red,green,blue]      keys = [ 0, 1, 2 ]
render 2  [green,blue]          keys = [ 3, 4 ]   <- green/blue DID NOT CHANGE
render 3  [green,blue,gold]     keys = [ 3, 4, 5 ]
render 4  [green,gold]          keys = [ 3, 6 ]   <- green STILL unchanged
counter   = 7

**Proposed cure.** Key on identity, not position. Mint an id at the single mint point — useMixingState.addColor returns `{ id: ++seq, css, source }` — and use `:key="sc.id"`. The counter, the Map, the prune watch and the swatchKeys computed all delete: 20 lines become 0, and the keys become actually stable.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/mix` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

This directly contradicts PaletteCard's documented contract.

**Mechanism.** a11y — nested interactive content; consumer overriding a component's documented semantic contract

**Evidence.**

```
MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 (native <button> with :aria-pressed/:aria-label wrapping <PaletteCard>). PaletteCard.vue:2-4, verbatim: "W5-a11y: role=\"article\" provides a landmark for each palette; button semantics on the card are omitted because inner interactive controls must be reachable — using article + click is the correct pattern for a card container that also houses nested interactive elements." **Reproduction.** NONE live — savedPalettes is empty on the probed tree so palettes mode renders EmptyState only. Static: the wrapper is unconditional in the template and the inner <Button> is unconditional in PaletteCard. Labelled a hypothesis at the live-DOM level.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/mix` · D-16 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** NEW · MAJOR — an empty palette result makes the gradient strip keep painting the PREVIOUS result's colours. `linear-gradient(to right, )` is invalid, CSSOM rejects the assignment, and the element retains its prior value. The plate does not go blank — it lies.

**Mechanism.** inline style built by string concatenation whose invalid-value failure mode is 'retain the last truth'; compounded by `v-if="result.colors"` treating [] as truthy

**Evidence.**

```
MixResultDisplay.vue:109-116 builds the strip by string concatenation. Engine check, both shipping engines: chromium and webkit alike → `"zero": {"inline":"","computed":"none"}` and `"staleAfterInvalid": "linear-gradient(to right, rgb(255,0,0), rgb(0,0,255))"`. Live in the app: `3-colour palette: {"rowChildren":3,"stripComputed":"linear-gradient(to right, rgb(255,0,0), rgb(0,255,0), rgb(0,0,255))"}` then `EMPTY palette (after 3): {"rowChildren":0,"stripComputed":"linear-gradient(to right, rgb(255,0,0), rgb(0,255,0), rgb(0,0,255))"}`. Reachable: demo/palettes/mix.ts:123 `if (resultLength === 0) return []` under the default `discard` strategy (useMixingState.ts:46), assigned unconditionally at useMixingState.ts:97.

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/wbmix-probe7.mjs — set mixResult to a 3-colour palette, force paints, then set mixResult to {type:'palette',colors:[]}; the swatch dots go to 0 but getComputedStyle(strip).backgroundImage still returns the 3-stop gradient.

**Proposed cure.** Make the empty case unrepresentable: a discriminated union `{type:'palette'; colors: readonly [PaletteColor, ...PaletteColor[]]}` forces startMix to decide what an empty mix MEANS at the one site that knows. While the type is loose, gate the strip on `result.colors.length > 1` rather than on array truthiness so an invalid declaration is never assigned, and route the truly-empty result to the repo's existing EmptyState grammar (MixSourceSelector.vue:239-244) rather than inventing one.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/mix` · D-10' · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** CORRECTED · MAJOR (r1 filed MINOR with the wrong mechanism) — the `<TransitionGroup name="vj-enter">` fires zero transition classes, ever. The cause is not the index key: `<Transition mode="out-in">` remounts the `key="content"` branch on every ghost→live flip, so the group is always an initial render, and TransitionGroup does not animate on initial render without `appear`. Fixing the key alone resurrects nothing.

**Mechanism.** declared animation on a subtree that is always freshly mounted; TransitionGroup's no-initial-transition rule makes the whole `vj-enter` name and the shared `.swatch-row` recipe dead code for this consumer

**Evidence.**

```
MixResultDisplay.vue:60 (`<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">`), :63 `key="well"` / :76 `key="content"`, :92-96 TransitionGroup with no `appear`. MutationObserver over document.body across a real ghost→done flip with forced paints: `total vj-* class mutations: 24` / `on watercolor swatches anywhere: []`. All 24 are vj-morph on plate/content divs plus vj-enter on MixSourceSelector's chip divs (whose group lives across updates, so its transitions do work). The shared recipe at demo/styles/utils.css:174-179 advertises MixResultDisplay as one of three consumers — it is inert for this one.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/wbmix-probe9.mjs — arm a MutationObserver on class attributes, set a 3-colour palette result with animationPhase='mixing', force paints, flip to 'done', force paints; filter the log for elements with data-testid='watercolor-swatch' → empty array.

**Proposed cure.** Decide what the row's arrival IS. If the dots should stagger as the plate inks: add `appear` to the TransitionGroup and key on colour identity (not the index, which also couples a dot's silhouette seed at :104 to its slot rather than to what it is). If the plate's `vj-morph` is meant to be the only motion — one surface, new content, the family law the docstring cites at :17 — then delete `name="vj-enter"` and the `swatch-row` class and correct the utility's comment to two consumers. Deleting an animation that provably never plays is not an edict-#6 violation; the record claiming it plays is.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects of demo/workbenches/gra` · C2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The 500 ms debounce is never cancelled on unmount, so a pending parse fires after the component is destroyed — detonating the C1 crash on whatever route the user has since navigated to.

**Mechanism.** Unreleased timer resource. The debounced callable is created in setup and outlives the component; Vue's `emit` still resolves the retained parent handler after unmount, so the parse runs against a dead model — and, with C1 live, throws into whatever boundary is currently mounted.

**Evidence.**

```
GradientCodeEditor.vue has NO onBeforeUnmount/onUnmounted; the only lifecycle hook in the file is `onMounted` at line 81. `debounce` at demo/shared/utils.ts:24-44 exposes `.cancel()`, which is never called. LIVE (evidence/live-probe.mjs R6): {"tag":"R6: navigated away inside the 500ms debounce window","url":"http://localhost:9000/#/mix","errorBoundaryVisible":1,"errorBoundaryText":"This panel hit an unexpected error.Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace') Try again"}. Screenshot: evidence/R6-unmount-pending-debounce.png — the user is on #/mix and the MIX workbench is what dies.
```

**Reproduction.** `node docs/.../evidence/live-probe.mjs` (R6). By hand: on #/gradient type `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)` into the CSS editor and switch to the Mix view within 500 ms of the last keystroke — the Mix pane is replaced by the error plate.

**Proposed cure.** The debounced call is a resource acquired in setup and must be released there. Minimal: `onBeforeUnmount(() => debouncedParse.cancel())`. Better and idiomatic for this repo: use `useDebounceFn`/`watchDebounced` from `@vueuse/core` (already a dependency), whose effect-scope-bound cleanup makes the leak unrepresentable rather than remembered.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects of demo/workbenches/gra` · C3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Blurring inside the 500 ms debounce window destroys the user's in-progress text and leaves the verdict naming a token that is no longer on screen — a direct breach of the file's own stated law.

**Mechanism.** Stale synchronous read of a prop written by an async parent round-trip — the repo's named `defineModel` hazard family, applied to a props+emit pair. `onBlur` decides whether to overwrite the user's text using the PREVIOUS parse's verdict.

**Evidence.**

```
GradientCodeEditor.vue:68-73 `onBlur()` reads `hasError` (line 32, derived from the `parseVerdict` prop) which the parent will not write until 500 ms later (GradientVisualizer.vue:102-108). The file's docblock at lines 34-40 states: 'A failed parse keeps the user's text verbatim alongside the verdict — WIP is never destroyed.' LIVE, with an isolating control (evidence/live-probe.mjs R2 / R2-control): defect {"editorText":"linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)","editorClass":"border-destructive","verdict":"unparseable color \"notacolor\""} vs control (no blur) {"editorText":"linear-gradient(90deg, notacolor, blue)","verdict":"unparseable color \"notacolor\""}. The only difference between the two runs is the blur.
```

**Reproduction.** `node docs/.../evidence/live-probe.mjs` (R2 and R2-control). By hand: on #/gradient click the CSS editor, Cmd+A, type `linear-gradient(90deg, notacolor, blue)` and immediately click the 'CSS' heading. The editor snaps back to the old canonical gradient, wears the destructive border, and prints a verdict about a token that is nowhere visible.

**Proposed cure.** Blur is an authoring boundary and must RESOLVE the pending parse rather than race it: flush the debounce on blur (parse now, synchronously), then settle the text on the verdict that answers THAT text. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects of demo/workbenches/gra` · C4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `textContent` collapses contenteditable line breaks, so multi-line authoring silently fuses tokens and rejects valid CSS with a message quoting a token the user never wrote.

GradientCodeEditor.vue:60 `const text = editorRef.value?.textContent ?? "";`. ```

**Reproduction.** `node docs/.../evidence/live-probe.mjs` (R3). By hand: click the CSS editor, Cmd+A, type `linear-gradient(90deg, red`, press Enter, type `50%, blue)`. The screen shows two lines; the verdict reads 'unparseable color "red50%"'.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects of demo/workbenches/gra` · C5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The failure surface is announced to nobody: `aria-invalid="true"` with no `aria-errormessage`/`aria-describedby`, the verdict has no `id`, the live region is v-if-mounted together with its content, its politeness contradicts the house register, and the multi-line textbox does not declare `aria-multiline`.

**Proposed cure.** Consume glass-ui's `LabeledField` (@mkbabb/glass-ui/labeled-field, installed 7.0.0). Its slot props are `{controlId, labelledBy, describedBy, errorId, invalid, disabled, required}`, it owns an `error` slot with an `errorLive: "off"|"polite"|"assertive"` prop, and `controlLabelable: false` exists precisely for non-labelable composite roots like a contenteditable div. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design` · D2-06 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Law 2 ("wells, not cards") is a four-property override and therefore does not flatten the producer's glass material at all: the specular pseudo-layer, its hover/active response and a full-width tonal seam all survive on a non-interactive specimen stage — and the override simultaneously suppresses the producer's card-level focus elevation.

**Mechanism.** a material rung is being hand-flattened property-by-property from the consumer instead of being requested as a rung from the design system

**Evidence.**

```
`EasingAuthoringStage.vue:93-99` overrides only background/border/box-shadow/backdrop-filter. `glass-ui/dist/styles/glass/material.css` defines `.glass-card::before` (conic+radial gradient, `mix-blend-mode: plus-lighter`, `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 0.75px`, `opacity: max(--specular-intensity, 0.07)`) plus `.glass-card:hover::before{--specular-intensity:0.1}` and `:active{0.16}`. Measured live: rest `beforeOpacity 0.07` → hover `0.10`, `beforeShadow color(srgb 0.948 0.929333 0.892 / 0.7) 0px 0px 0px 0.75px inset`. Seam isolated: forcing `background:#ff0000 !important` on the card and `visibility:hidden` on the SVG still shows a full-width tonal step at ~56% of card height — frames/D-06-well-seam-over-red-svg-hidden.png; absent under forced-colors where `glass/a11y-fallback.css` sets `.glass-card::before{display:none}`; card-relative not viewport-relative (card y=746.3 and y=564.25 in two runs, same relative offset). Focus: `glass/surfaces.css` `.glass-card:has(:focus-visible){--card-focus-shadow: var(--shadow-md); --card-focus-border: var(--glass-border-floating)}` is in `@layer components`; the seat's `box-shadow:none` is unlayered, so unlayered wins and the focus elevation never paints when a `role="slider"` handle is focused.
```

**Reproduction.** open /#/gradient, disclose the stage, hover the `.glass-card` and read `getComputedStyle(card,'::before').opacity` (0.07→0.10); for the seam run `node .../probes/probe10.mjs` (writes out10/card-red-nosvg.png)

**Proposed cure.** glass-ui ships a real `well` rung (`variant="well"` / `.glass-well`, already booked as producer packet P3 per `demo/styles/foundation.css:322-324`) that is opaque, specular-free and focus-correct by construction. The consumer stops overriding producer internals entirely.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (round 4) — demo/workbenches/mix/MixCon` · R4-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** RECORD CORRECTION — the selected value is hard-sheared at the canon's 320px arm in BOTH engines, with no ellipsis; rounds 2 and 3 certified this as PASS because they measured the trigger <button> (overflow: visible, so scrollWidth==clientWidth is unconditionally true) instead of the value <span> one level down.

**Mechanism.** MixConfigBar.vue:94 pins `grid grid-cols-2` at every width, so a 320px viewport yields 123px cells for a 111px value + 16px chevron + 24px inline padding = 151px needed. The producer's `[&>span]:line-clamp-1` is a VERTICAL clamp (-webkit-box/box-orient:vertical); computed `text-overflow` on that span resolves to `clip`, so a single unbreakable word overflowing HORIZONTALLY is cut with no ellipsis, no title, no aria-description. Layout never sized against its own closed vocabulary (color-space-meta.ts:26-43 contains Increasing/Decreasing/OKLCh; MixConfigBar.vue:85-89 contains 'Discard extras'/'Repeat to pad').

**Evidence.**

```
p10.mjs, both engines, after actually SELECTING 'Decreasing' (prior rounds measured only the default 'Shorter'):
chromium @320  BUTTON w:123 sw:121 cw:121 overflow:visible clipped:false  <-- what r2/r3 measured
               SPAN   w:81  sw:111 cw:81  overflow:hidden  clipped:TRUE   display:-webkit-box  -webkit-line-clamp:1  text-overflow:CLIP
webkit  @320  SPAN   w:81  sw:112 cw:81  clipped:TRUE
both    @390  SPAN   w:111.5 sw:111/112 cw:111/112 clipped:false
Pixel proof: scratchpad/wbmix/trunc-webkit-320.png renders 'Decreas' with the chevron on top of the surviving 's'; trunc-webkit-390.png renders 'Decreasing' cleanly. Contradicts r2 ('Truncation … PASS. scrollWidth == clientWidth at every width') and r3 ('The producer's truncation is intact … 121/121, 156/156, 225/225').
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/wbmix/p10.mjs — for {chromium,webkit} x {320,390}: goto http://localhost:9000/#/mix, wait 3500ms, click [aria-label='Hue method'], click the 'Decreasing' option, walk the trigger's descendant chain reading scrollWidth/clientWidth/overflow/text-overflow. Manual: resize to 320px, open Hue method, choose Decreasing, read the trigger.

**Proposed cure.** Two independent, both wanted. (1) Local: the grid must collapse before its own longest member stops fitting — `grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2`; at 320 the fields stack and the value gets 280px. (2) Producer (glass-ui BH relay): the SelectValue span carries `text-overflow: ellipsis` so ANY under-width consumer degrades legibly instead of silently. Methodological cure for the audit program itself: truncation probes must walk past every `overflow: visible` container to the node that actually carries the property.

Compounded by p3.mjs {disabledBtnFocusable:false, tabIndex:0} — native `disabled` removes the verb from tab order, so a keyboard/AT user never reaches it and is never told why; and by forced-colors, where the UA supplies GrayText and the component's own opacity:0.5 still rides on top (opacity is the one channel the forced-colors palette may not normalise).

**Evidence.**

```
p4.mjs — Playwright element screenshot at DPR 2 -> `magick … rgb:-` -> per-pixel WCAG relative luminance over 75,768 px; background = modal luminance bin, glyph = the 0.2% tail furthest from it:
btn-disabled-light.png {"bg":0.7373,"glyph":0.1932,"contrast":3.24}
btn-disabled-dark.png  {"bg":0.1059,"glyph":0.3813,"contrast":2.77}
Computed (p1.mjs/p3.mjs): opacity 0.5; color UNCHANGED from enabled (rgb(28,25,23) light / rgb(233,230,226) dark); bg oklab(0.915626 0.00551148 0.0130686 / 0.52). Honest scope: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts disabled controls, so this is a constitution failure, not an AA one — but per R4-4 it is the ONLY state the route ever renders.

Once the dead `variant` is replaced by `emphasis`, the enabled<->disabled delta becomes an emphasis step and forced-colors gets a colour it can map. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (round 4) — demo/workbenches/mix/MixCon` · R4-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The open menu was never examined: the selected option is marked by a full-row pill-outline (not the producer indicator gutter the constitution binds the sibling color-space selector to), and the popover inherits the under-width trigger so the explanation lane wraps at 320/390.

**Mechanism.** VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.2 legislates the registered ColorSpaceSelector species: 'the sole glass-ui SelectItem indicator uses its producer-owned gutter … may not add a local pill, halo, pseudo-element, marker'. The route therefore ships TWO different selection markers for the same domain choice (Picker = gutter law, Mix = full-row pill). MixConfigBar.vue:107 passes no class to SelectItem, so the pill is producer-owned (SelectItemProps exposes only value/disabled/textValue/class/hideIndicator) — the defect charged locally is the decision to hand-roll raw Select primitives instead of consuming the registered species, which is what made two markers for one choice expressible. The popover width inheritance propagates the grid-cols-2 decision into a portalled surface the component does not own.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (run 4, independent replication + corre` · D-30 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Run 2's D-18 cure is insufficient — the plate's height snap has a second, independent cause. The `vj-morph` family gates its height leg on `--vj-morph-collapse`/`--vj-morph-expanded`, which are never set on `.mix-plate` or any ancestor, so `max-height` resolves to `none` in all four transition classes and cannot animate even after the scoped `transition: opacity` shorthand is removed.

**Mechanism.** under-consumed motion contract: the component names the family and adopts its curve, then declines the only leg its own use case (a surface whose content genuinely changes height) requires. Two independent blockers stacked, so fixing one leaves the symptom intact.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/styles/animations.css:118-136 gates max-height on the two vars. `grep -rn "vj-morph-collapse\|vj-morph-expanded" demo/` returns ONLY the definitions in animations.css plus demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:361-362 (`--vj-morph-collapse: 0px; --vj-morph-expanded: 3rem;`) — the one consumer that proves the lever works. Measured plate heights, clean WebKit: ghost 118.7 -> color 158.7 (+40.0) -> palette-5 170.7 (+52.0) -> palette-12 218.7 (+100.0), all in one frame. Settled computed `transition: "opacity 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)"` reproduces run 2's D-18 shorthand.
```

**Reproduction.** node evidence/run4-scripts/wbmix-matrix.mjs — compare ghostH/settledH/palH/pal12H; then grep the two custom properties across demo/.

**Proposed cure.** Necessary AND sufficient set: delete the scoped `transition` shorthand (run 2's D-18) AND either set the two vars on the plate or — KISS — drop `mode="out-in"` so the two extremes never need to exist as separate frames and the height is simply content-driven. The acceptance test for that wave must be a MEASURED height transition spanning >1 frame, not the absence of the shorthand.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (subject: demo/workbenches/generate/Gen` · D-19 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The route has no mount state. demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:73 registers GeneratePane with defineAsyncComponent and no loadingComponent, no errorComponent, no timeout, no onError — a slow chunk renders an empty 512x560 glass rectangle and a failed chunk fetch renders nothing forever, with no message and no retry. GeneratePane.vue:10,11 are two non-null-asserted inject(...)! calls that throw on a missing provider with no recovery surface. The pane expresses zero of the five states VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1 requires.

**Mechanism.** F4 — state never designed: only the populated happy path at 1440-light was authored; loading, error, saved, save-failure, overflow/truncation and touch states were not.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:73 `const GeneratePane = defineAsyncComponent(() => import("../workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue"));` — no options object. demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:10,11. Producer vocabulary that goes unused: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/instrument-chassis/types.d.ts `export type InstrumentChassisState = "ready" | "active" | "complete" | "loading";`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1 "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit."; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-08 ADD-AFFORDANCE.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE (hypothesis-free static + producer-API proof; not exercised under a throttled/failed chunk fetch). The absence of loadingComponent/errorComponent on usePaneRouter.ts:73 is directly readable, and Vue's documented behaviour for defineAsyncComponent without those options is to render nothing while pending and to log-and-render-nothing on rejection.

**Proposed cure.** Bind `:state` on the InstrumentChassis from D-3's transposition — "loading" while the generation core is cold, "ready" at rest, "complete" after a commit — and give the async import a real error arm with retry. Under the chassis this is one prop, not a new component; without the chassis it would require inventing a wrapper, which edict 3 forbids.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (subject: demo/workbenches/generate/Gen` · D-20 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The dead card tail is a function of the neighbouring pane, not of the pane's own content. GeneratePane.vue:31 carries h-full, chaining the Generate card's height to whatever the Palettes companion happens to contain, so the composition's vertical rhythm changes when an unrelated pane gains a row.

**Mechanism.** F1 — wrong primitive: h-full is meaningful only because the pane sits in a shell grid it did not ask for; the Card is being used as a page column.

```
demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:31. Measured 1440x900 with an empty library companion: paneCard {y:210, h:560.1}; last control (count-slider label) bottom = 434.2; emptyTailPx = 125.9 = 22.5% of the pane is empty glass. The first CHALLENGE-D pass measured 65px of dead interior on a differently-populated companion — both correct, which is the point: the tail is unstable. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5 law 3 "Renderer, icon or touch footprints may reserve collision space only on the axis where collision exists" (there is no collision here, only coupling); §5 law 1 "A page region, empty column, inner stage or mere padding group does not become a Card by default".
```

**Reproduction.** Load /#/generate at 1440x900 with localStorage cleared and measure the bottom of the count-slider label against the bottom of .pane-scroll-fade: 125.9px of empty card. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-11 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The one motion the component designs is architecturally prevented: TransitionGroup keys embed the array index, so removing one chip invalidates every surviving chip's key — the row plays three leaves and two enters instead of one leave plus a move, and the shared .vj-enter-move neighbour reflow can never fire.

**Mechanism.** SelectedColor ({css, source}) carries no identity, so the site manufactured one from position — which is exactly the quantity a removal changes.

**Evidence.**

```
MixSourceSelector.vue:79-89 keys on `${sc.css}::${i}`. Exact algorithm replay (node -e): initial [0,1,2] -> after removing index 0 [3,4] -> re-add [0,1,2] -> duplicates [0,5]. demo/styles/utils.css:168-178 exists precisely so "neighbours reflow on the family move class" (.vj-enter-move); with index-bearing keys no element survives to be moved. The watch at :90-98 then prunes the map, guaranteeing keys are never reused.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE in the running app (the populated state is unreachable per D-1). Algorithm replayed exactly: node -e '<swatchKeys replay>' — output pasted in the report §D-11.

**Proposed cure.** Mint identity at the source: useMixingState.addColor stamps a stable id on each SelectedColor; the key becomes sc.id and the key map, the counter and the pruning watcher (~20 lines) are deleted outright.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-9 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Copy exists twice in the Mix instrument with divergent feedback and duplicated serialization logic, and neither path renders the producer's `failure` state.

**Evidence.**

```
Plate: MixResultDisplay.vue:31-32,42-47 (`useClipboard({resetMs:1500})`, icon+title swap). Dock: usePaneRouter.ts:222 `{key:'copy', title:'Copy result'}` → MixPane.vue:49-55 (bare `writeClipboard`, `{ok}` discarded, no feedback). Serialization duplicated verbatim: MixResultDisplay.vue:43-46 vs MixPane.vue:51-53. useClipboard.d.ts:3 declares `ClipboardStatus = "idle"|"pending"|"success"|"failure"` plus onCopyError/invalidate; line 32 maps only `success`, so a failed copy is pixel-identical to idle. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-12 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The magnifier is sub-device-resolution and has no reticle: its backing store is 110x110 for a 110 CSS-px box, so nearest-neighbour texels are bilinearly upscaled by the compositor, and nothing marks which of the 11x11 cells was actually sampled.

**Mechanism.** DPR-unaware backing store plus a magnifier with no index mark

**Evidence.**

```
ImageEyedropper.vue:85 hardcodes `width="110" height="110"`; measured loupeBox 110x110 CSS px at devicePixelRatio 2 (desktop) and 3 (mobile) → the buffer supplies 0.5x / 0.33x of the device pixels the box occupies. useLoupeCanvas.ts:40 sets `imageSmoothingEnabled = false` to draw crisp texels, which the compositor then smooths away on every retina display. drawLoupe (lines 27-53) draws the magnified region and never strokes a centre cell; the loupe is also centred exactly on the pointer (loupeStyle, lines 191-196), so it occludes the very pixel being sampled and sits under the finger on touch.
```

**Reproduction.** Hover twice so the loupe paints, then read `document.querySelector('.loupe canvas')` — width/height attributes 110 while getBoundingClientRect() is 110 CSS px at devicePixelRatio 2. No stroked cell appears at the loupe centre in any captured frame.

**Proposed cure.** Size the backing store to `LOUPE_SIZE * devicePixelRatio` and scale the context, stroke the sampled cell's outline so the loupe indexes its own answer, and offset the loupe from the pointer (or render it in the chrome bar beside the swatch) so it stops occluding the target.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-13 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The stage paints with `image-rendering: auto` at up to 10x magnification, so the colour the user sees under the cursor is a bilinear blend while the sample taken is a single integer texel — three surfaces over one bitmap using three resampling laws.

**Mechanism.** three resampling laws over one bitmap

**Evidence.**

```
Measured `getComputedStyle(canvas.eyedropper-canvas).imageRendering === 'auto'` with `transform: matrix(7.9375,0,0,7.9375,0,59.789)` — a 7.94x upscale, and useInertiaGesture allows maxZoom 10 (ImageEyedropper.vue:149). The loupe explicitly disables smoothing (useLoupeCanvas.ts:40); sampleAt takes one nearest texel (useImageSampler.ts:111-119). My N-3 proof shows the sampler arithmetic is exact, so the divergence is entirely display-side: on a 1-px checker the blend is precisely the average of the two texels.
```

**Reproduction.** Load a 1-px red/blue checker, magnify, and compare the composited screen pixel under the cursor against the reported value — the screen shows the blend, the readout reports one texel. Confirmed independently by round 1 (evidence quoted in challenge-D-design.r1.md §D-1: composited rgb(127,0,128) against a reported #0000FF).

**Proposed cure.** One resampling law owned in one place: `image-rendering: pixelated` on the stage above 1x so a texel is a visible square and the loupe becomes a true magnification of the same law. Below 1x, sample the area-average over the source box the pointer's display pixel actually covers — i.e. sample what the pixel shows. Do not patch sampleAt; the arithmetic is correct.

Measured: .family-eyebrow and .tile-label font-size 9px (0.5625rem); the smallest resolving named rung is --text-micro 0.6875rem = 11px. Row measurements, same instant: `1 → 2` / `linear` / `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)` all at 16.4px, Fira Code, rgb(112,89,66), weight 400. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 "This matrix is closed across all eighteen compositions" (one named exception, P019); PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.13. Source admission GradientEasingEditor.vue:134-135: "text-mono-SMALL: curve identifiers are case-sensitive; text-mono-caption would uppercase them".
```

**Reproduction.** Open /#/gradient and read font-size on .family-eyebrow, .tile-label, .interval-head span, .interval-head .truncate and .readout-rail code.

**Proposed cure.** The specimen name takes the identity role from the closed matrix, not the value role; if mono-caption uppercases, add a producer text-transform:none variant on the caption rung rather than substituting a size. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-07 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Specimen selection is effectively colour-only: pressed and unpressed tiles have byte-identical background and box-shadow, zero border, no outline and equal opacity in both schemes. The only non-colour deltas are a 0.50px stroke-width change on a 22px glyph and a weight step on 9px text.

**Mechanism.** Producer boundary crossed at the seat: the Chip's data-state="on" wash contributes no geometric delta here, and the seat delegates the whole selection signal to consumer ink.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured, same page, light: identicalBg=true (both oklab(0.925647 0.009411 0.029177 / 0.83872)); identicalShadow=true (byte-identical 7-layer strings); border 0px both; outline none both; opacity 1 both; filter none both. Dark identical too (oklab(0.467325 0.012705 0.030851 / 0.911296) both). Deltas: glyph stroke oklab(…/0.65)->oklch(0.438102 0.074812 205), width 1.25px->1.75px; label rgb(91,70,51)->oklch(0.438102 0.074812 205), weight 400->600. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 "Selected … states are never color-only"; §4.2 requires "independent nonzero monochrome/forced-colors deltas".
```

**Reproduction.** Open /#/gradient and diff getComputedStyle backgroundColor + boxShadow between .specimen-tile[data-state="on"] and any sibling tile — both strings are equal in light and in dark.

**Proposed cure.** Give selectable Chip a producer-owned geometric selected register (ring, fill or notch) so the pressed state survives monochrome and forced colours; stop using --motion-accent as the selection signal at the seat. (Forced-colours consequence is a HYPOTHESIS: WebKit ignores Playwright forcedColors, so that matrix is not evidence.)
