### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-08 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** RTL breaks twice: the interval identity renders `2 → 1` when the model says `1 → 2` (bidi reorder of a domain coordinate), and every family divider lands on the wrong edge because the rule uses physical border-left/padding-left — no rule at the css|sine boundary, a stray rule at the strip's outer left.

**Mechanism.** Physical-property and bidi assumptions: an LTR writing direction baked into a separator rule and into a coordinate rendered as a bidi-sensitive string.

**Evidence.**

```
(a) useSpecimenRows.ts:63 `label: `${i + 1} → ${i + 2}``; measured logical headLabelText="1 → 2", rendered "2 → 1" in rtl-desktop/gradient.png and my clip DE-rtl-easing.png. Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2: "CSS direction keywords, physical axes, code, hex, slug, ID | preserve the declared physical/domain meaning … inside an LTR-isolated value". (b) EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:143-146 `border-left: 1px solid var(--card-edge); padding-left: 0.875rem`. Measured RTL rects, DOM order: css [962.5→1201.0] border-left 0px; sine [792.3→948.5] border-left 1px pad-left 14px; quad [622.1→778.3] 1px/14px; … steps [-277.1→-122.1] 1px/14px and leftmost with nothing beyond it. css renders to the RIGHT of sine, so sine's left rule separates it from quad, not from its predecessor.
```

**Reproduction.** Open /#/gradient, run `document.documentElement.setAttribute("dir","rtl")`, wait ~1s. Read the head's first span (renders 2 → 1) and getComputedStyle borderLeftWidth/borderRightWidth on each .strip-family (borderLeft 1px, borderRight 0px, on the inline-END side).

**Proposed cure.** border-inline-start / padding-inline-start for the family rule; give the interval ordinal the LTR isolation the constitution already prescribes for code/hex/slug values — or stop rendering an ordinal pair as a bidi-sensitive string at all.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-09 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** A 27-item single-select gallery injects 27 tab stops (28 with its focusable port) into a 52-stop route while hiding 70.6% of itself on desktop and 79.9% on mobile — and the only affordance that made it navigable, the family filter, was deleted and replaced with an aria-hidden decorative eyebrow.

**Mechanism.** Instrument compressed into the wrong housing: a catalogue sized for a 61.8% stage squeezed into a 436px/298px scroll port, with its navigation subtracted and nothing put back.

**Evidence.**

```

EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:96 `<span class="family-eyebrow" aria-hidden="true">`; :136-137 records the deletion: "the kf family filter's information architecture folded INTO the strip (compactness: no second control row)". Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 names roving focus for horizontal rails (Home=first, End=last, activation separate from movement); PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.6 requires ADD-AFFORDANCE when the surviving action is otherwise undiscoverable.
```

**Reproduction.** Open /#/gradient and read `.fading-scroll` clientWidth vs scrollWidth (436 vs 1482); repeat at iPhone 14 (298 vs 1482); count document.querySelectorAll('.specimen-tile') = 27 against the route's 52 visible tabbables.

**Proposed cure.** Roving tabindex over the tiles (one tab stop, arrows move, Home/End jump), and make the family eyebrows the navigation they already look like — jump controls, or a two-row grid showing all eight families. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-16 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The camera capability is implemented twice: useImageQuantize already exports quantizeFromCamera (with the stop() handle) and quantizeFromCanvas, both dead, while the view hand-rolls getUserMedia, video, canvas, toBlob, File and teardown — and the shipping path PNG-encodes and base64-round-trips a canvas to reach a function that accepts a canvas.

**Mechanism.** dual path: a capability written in the composable layer was re-implemented imperatively in the view, leaving the well-formed copy dead and the ad-hoc copy shipping

**Evidence.**

```
grep -rn "quantizeFromCamera" --include=*.ts --include=*.vue demo/ test/ e2e/ → only useImageQuantize.ts:4 (comment), :115 (definition), :159 (export). grep -rn "getUserMedia" demo/ → ExtractWorkbench.vue:242 and useImageQuantize.ts:116. Round trip: ExtractWorkbench.vue:274-277 (canvas.toBlob PNG → File) → useExtractSession.ts:166 (FileReader → data URL) → useImageQuantize.ts:19-25 (createImageBitmap → pixels).
```

**Reproduction.** Run the two greps above; both return the quoted output on branch tranche-u at HEAD c654824e.

**Proposed cure.** Delete startCamera/stopCamera/captureFrame from the view; the session owns a camera sub-state built on quantizeFromCamera, and quantizeFromCanvas consumes the captured frame directly (no PNG encode, no base64, no re-decode).

**Defect.** The failure register is color-only, unannounced, undismissable, prints raw exception text, and rides the wrong channel — camera permission errors are written into quantizeError and rendered in the result column.

**Reproduction.** At /#/gradient set Type=Radial; drag or keyboard the Direction slider 0→360; observe the tile's computed background-image and the CSS panel never change; inspect the `[role=slider]` for aria-disabled/data-disabled.

**Proposed cure.** The control is type-conditional, not type-agnostic: `linear` → "Angle"; `conic` → "Start angle"; `radial` → replaced by the parameters radial actually has (shape, extent). **Defect.** The radius register the owner marked (MT-F030 / OM-4): six boxes in one instrument carry five different radii, and rendered curvature (r ÷ min dimension) runs INVERSELY to box size — the two smallest boxes are full semicircles (0.500) and the largest is 0.082. ```

Tokens measured: --radius-card 1rem, --radius-md 6px, --radius-input 0.25rem(=4px), --radius-pill 9999px. demo/DESIGN.md §Radii says `rounded-pill/rounded-full — chips` (so the disc is 'correct' by the doc) and states --radius-input = 8px, which is DRIFT — live is 4px. Post-fix arithmetic: glass's orphaned `.glass-chip--cell{border-radius:var(--radius-card)}` gives 16/44 = 0.364, still the most-rounded box in the row and now the SAME absolute radius as the 462px plate.
```

**Reproduction.** Load /#/gradient, expand interval 1→2, run probe-D2-radius-material-matrix.mjs; read the radiusRegister block. Compare against docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-4-easing-radius-incoherence.png.

**Proposed cure.** Two halves. OURS: a radius DERIVATION law in the register (the gap DESIGN-CANON-BRIEF.md:73 already names) — corner curvature holds constant or grows with box size, never inverts; nested registers derive from their parent. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-18 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The scoped `transition` shorthand defeats the producer `vj-morph` motion family on the same element by attribute specificity, so the plate's arrival is a 116.0px single-frame snap with no transform and no height morph. Supersedes and corrects the prior run's D-3 diagnosis AND its cure.

**Mechanism.** Scoped-CSS specificity override of a producer motion family. `animations.css:59-62` states the family law verbatim: "The family owns the CURVE + TOKEN pairing; a consuming site may parameterise only GEOMETRY through the `--vj-*` custom properties." This component parameterises the CURVE and the PROPERTY SET via a scoped `transition` shorthand — the two things the law forbids — and wins by attribute specificity. No gate in the tranche can see it.

**Evidence.**

```
chD-probe4.mjs, WebKit 1440x900, live CSSOM + computed style read while the plate carries `vj-morph-enter-active`:
  classes            : mix-plate … bg-well mix-plate--ghost vj-morph-enter-active vj-morph-enter-to
  transitionProperty : opacity
  transitionDuration : 0.2s
  transitionTiming   : cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)   ← --ease-standard
  transform          : none
  maxHeight          : none
The two competing rules read out of the CSSOM:
  .vj-morph-enter-active      { transition: opacity var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-decelerate), transform var(--spring-snappy-duration) var(--spring-snappy), max-height var(--duration-normal) var(--ease-decelerate); }
  .mix-plate[data-v-0f138735] { transition: opacity var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard); }
Specificity (0,2,0) > (0,1,0); the shorthand resets transition-property to `opacity`.
Source: demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue:152-154.
Consequence, chD-probe5.mjs rAF sample every frame for 2500ms across a 12-colour swap, compressed to state changes: [{"t":44,"h":102.7,"op":0.55,"dots":1,"btns":0},{"t":265,"h":218.7,"op":1,"dots":12,"btns":3}] — minHeight 102.7, maxHeight 218.7, no intermediate height. Single-colour arm real flow: desktop 118.7→158.7 (+40.0), mobile 112.3→158.6 (+46.3).
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/chD-probe4.mjs against http://localhost:9000/#/mix; or in DevTools arm a mix and read getComputedStyle($('.mix-plate')).transitionProperty during the enter frame.

**Proposed cure.** Delete `<style scoped>` whole. The ghost dimming belongs on the specimen tier (the `variant="ghost"` dot already expresses it), not on the container. Combined with making the ghost render the result's own shape and count, the container never resizes, `mode="out-in"` becomes unnecessary and there is no height to morph — the family is restored rather than patched.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-19 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The gradient strip depicts an interpolation the user did not choose — it never receives `colorSpace`/`hueMethod` — while the same pane already ships the correct, library-sampled, space-aware ramp primitive forty lines away.

**Mechanism.** Hand-rolled decoration duplicating a shipped, correct primitive; the interpolation axis — the instrument's entire subject — is hard-wired to the engine default instead of the user's selection. Owner edicts 3 (KISS, no contrivance) and 4 (reuse the design system's primitives) both apply.

chD-probe3.mjs, WebKit, identical stops, midpoint pixel sampled from the painted render:
  linear-gradient(to right, …)          → rgb(135,117,169)
  linear-gradient(in oklab to right, …) → rgb(135,117,169)   Δ = 0
  linear-gradient(in srgb  to right, …) → rgb(100,108,168)   Δ = 36
Computed background-image of the live strip carries no `in <space>` clause. MixResultDisplay.vue:109-116 builds it from `result.colors` alone; MixPane.vue:113-118 passes only `result` and `ghost`. The honest primitive already exists in the same pane: MixConfigBar.vue:23,111,133 consumes `sampleInterpolationRamp` + `<PreviewRamp>` from ../../color-session/color-chips (space- and hue-method-aware, with a data-stops oracle).

**Proposed cure.** Delete the strip, or replace it with `<PreviewRamp>` fed the real `colorSpace`/`hueMethod`. Replaced, it stops being decoration and becomes the one thing the swatch row cannot say — the continuum the user chose.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-20 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The gradient strip is outside both colour-surface rosters that its neighbouring swatches are inside, so it loses its colour in high-contrast mode and in print while the dots keep theirs.

**Mechanism.** The app maintains a NAMED colour-surface register precisely so colour content survives system-colour substitution and ink economy; this element was authored as anonymous inline style and fell out of a register it structurally belongs in. This is the general cost of hand-rolling a primitive rather than consuming one (see D-19).

**Evidence.**

```
demo/styles/foundation.css maintains ONE enumerated roster reused by `@media (forced-colors: active)` (≈lines 683-698) and `@media print` (≈lines 832-846): `canvas, .spectrum-picker, .gamut-overlay, .atmosphere-canvas, [data-glass-field-canvas], .gradient-rail, .rail-handle, .readout-rail, .swatch-row > *, .generate-swatch, .shadow-swatch, .goo-blob-canvas, .watercolor-swatch, …, [data-color-surface]`. The strip (MixResultDisplay.vue:109-116) is an anonymous <div> with an inline `background`, no class and no `data-color-surface`, and it is a SIBLING of `.swatch-row`, not a child — matching neither selector. Its twelve neighbouring dots are covered twice over. Live-DOM confirmation: the strip element carries no roster hook.
```

**Reproduction.** grep -n "swatch-row > \*" demo/styles/foundation.css, then inspect the strip in the live plate — no class, no data attribute. The @media print half needs no caveat (textual omission); the forced-colors half is argued from roster construction because WebKit's forcedColors emulation did not visibly substitute system colours on this page.

**Proposed cure.** Moot if the strip is deleted (D-19). If it is kept as `<PreviewRamp>`, the producer component must carry a roster hook (`data-color-surface`) so it joins both registers by construction rather than by a consumer remembering to add a class.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-22 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The result value is raw machine output rendered with `word-break: break-all`, so the plate breaks a number mid-digit and reflows the chassis 2↔3 lines with the payload.

**Mechanism.** An unformatted serialisation paired with the wrong wrap mode. `break-all` breaks inside tokens by definition; for a code-ready colour artifact the token boundary is the only legal break.

**Evidence.**

```
chD-shots/d-light-P5-long.png renders literally:
  oklab(71.666666666667% -0.002284954
  563 0.014917814848)
Measured: 54 chars; desktop w=362, h=45.9 at line-height 22.96 → 2 lines; mobile h=58.8 at 19.6 → 3 lines; `wordBreak: break-all`; `fontVariantNumeric: normal`. Source: MixResultDisplay.vue:85. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4 — "Live numbers use tabular figures and reserve their widest legal representation so value changes never reflow the settled chassis"; PALETTE-CONTRACT.md §3 fixes the canonical spelling at 3/6/3/6 decimals (the plate prints 12). Compare the Picker headline in the same viewport: `92.0%, 88.8, 20.0`.
```

**Reproduction.** Any real 3-operand OKLab mix — `colorToCss` emits the full float; force `{type:'color', css:'oklab(71.666666666667% -0.002284954563 0.014917814848)'}` through MixPane's mixResult binding and screenshot the plate.

**Proposed cure.** Format at the plate: canonical fixed decimals, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (never `break-all`), and reserve the widest legal representation so the plate does not reflow between payloads.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Container-wide `opacity: .55` drops the plate's only text to a pixel-measured 2.61:1 during the entire ghost phase — correcting the prior run's arithmetically-derived 2.21:1 with a measured number.

**Mechanism.** Presence attenuation applied at the container instead of at the specimen tier. Opacity is a compositing operation, not a design token: it de-rates ink, ground, focus rings and specimen colour by the same factor and cannot distinguish "this shape is provisional" from "this word is unreadable". Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1 — "Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence."

**Evidence.**

chD-probe3.mjs, pixel-sampled from the painted render with a minimal in-house PNG decoder (darkest ink pixel vs lightest background pixel inside the label box — an UPPER bound on the true ratio): ghost `rgb(164,127,122)` on `rgb(235,217,210)` = 2.61:1; settled `rgb(112,89,66)` on `rgb(233,225,217)` = 5.08:1. The label computes to Fraunces 700 at 14.384px — below WCAG's large-text floor (18.66px bold) — so 4.5:1 is required. During the ghost phase this label is the only text in the plate (`plate.innerText === "RESULT"`). Source: MixResultDisplay.vue:155-157.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/chD-probe3.mjs; or arm a real mix on /#/mix and screenshot the label box during the ~200ms ghost window.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-03 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The component's stated §8 law 'one ink per specimen' is falsified in the visible frame: four intervals carrying the IDENTICAL curve and the IDENTICAL literal render four different --motion-accent hues. The glyph is the only differentiated mark in the row (r1 D-08), and it is differentiated by the interval's stop colours, not by its curve — so the list's only colour signal asserts that four identical easings differ.

**Mechanism.** an identity ink derived from an expression dominated by variables other than the identity it claims to encode; fn(0.5) is neither injective nor well-defined with respect to the specimen

**Evidence.**

```
Measured at N=4, all four intervals holding the default linear (identical interval.css 'cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)', identical row.name 'linear', identical glyph path): row0 oklch(43.469% 0.0994 159.34), row1 oklch(43.733% 0.0757 189.28), row2 oklch(44.027% 0.0805 220.60), row3 oklch(44.705% 0.1288 250.66); distinctInks: 4. Source: useSpecimenRows.ts:53-59 — ink = interpolateStopColors(s0.cssColor, s1.cssColor, fn(0.5), ...), i.e. two of three inputs are the STOP colours. Witnesses: frames-r3/D3-n4-desktop-1440-four-intervals.png and D3-n4-mobile-390-four-intervals.png. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:70 (§5.5) — a small mark is 'data, status, labeled action, drag affordance, focus/selection register or removed'. Round 2's D2-15 proved the collision direction (five curves -> one ink); this is the injection direction and the one a user sees.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, click .gradient-rail at 25%, 50%, 75%. Read row.style.getPropertyValue('--motion-accent') on each of the four .interval-head parents, or simply look at frames-r3/D3-n4-desktop-1440-four-intervals.png: four rows all reading 'linear', four differently-coloured glyphs.

**Proposed cure.** Either derive the ink from something that actually distinguishes curves — the signed area between the curve and the diagonal separates ease-in from ease-out, which fn(0.5) cannot — or delete the per-row ink and let the shared accent carry the glyph. It must not be a stop colour dressed as a curve identity. This also removes the unbounded fn(0.5) evaluation that round 2's D2-01 BLOCKER runs through.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-04 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Proximity inversion: sibling interval rows sit 8px apart while the parts INSIDE one row sit 10px apart. Elements in one group are further from each other than from elements of another group, so at N>1 the rows read as one continuous striped block. The per-row card border — a boundary this composition's binding table gives a count of zero — is currently the only thing compensating for the inverted spacing scale.

**Mechanism.** one spacing rung used for two opposite semantic distances (between-group and within-group), with a forbidden boundary line added to compensate for the resulting ambiguity

**Evidence.**

```
Measured live at N=4: interRowGaps [8, 8, 8] (GradientEasingEditor.vue:107, 'flex flex-col gap-2'); panelGap 10px (:146, gap-2.5); headPad '8px 12px 8px 12px'; panelChildren ramp 436x20 @y592.13, strip 436x71.42 @y622.13, rail 436x32 @y703.55; intraGaps [10, 10]. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:68 (§5.3) — 'Header->headline uses title gap; headline->next semantic section uses section gap' (two named, different quantities). OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md §5 gives Gradient boundaries [] / dividing line none. Witness: frames-r3/D3-n4-desktop-1440-four-intervals.png. Probe: frames-r3/probe-rhythm.mjs, probe-rhythm.json.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, click .gradient-rail at 25%, 50%, 75%. For each pair of adjacent .interval-head parents compute next.getBoundingClientRect().y - prev.getBoundingClientRect().bottom -> 8.00. Read getComputedStyle on the open row's [id^='easing-interval-'] panel -> rowGap '10px'. Script: frames-r3/probe-rhythm.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Fix the rhythm and the boundary dies with it: inter-row gap must exceed intra-row gap by at least one rung, letting spacing plus material carry grouping — exactly the disposition the binding table already records for Gradient ('grouping job: meniscus, stop seats and code/action interval carry grouping'). ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-05 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** OWNER MARK OM-4 / MT-F030, carried and sharpened: the radius incoherence is intra-element and state-dependent, not merely cross-element. One class, one token (--radius-card 16px), two boxes 8px apart in the same list — the collapsed row renders curvature 0.391 and the open row 0.081, a 4.83x swing that fires on click with no transition. Both readings the owner named ('too rounded in some areas, not rounded enough in others') are present in the SAME declaration.

**Mechanism.** a size-blind absolute radius rung applied to a box whose height varies 4.8x by disclosure state, so rendered curvature is an accident of state rather than a register

Declaration: GradientEasingEditor.vue:114 'rounded-card border border-card-edge overflow-hidden'. Owner mark: ROOT-FINDINGS.md:1421, witness audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-4-easing-radius-incoherence.png. The existing registry rows (DEFECT-LEDGER.md:29659, :31873) are a cross-element census at N=1 (five registers 0/4/6/16/9999px) and contain no state-dependent measurement. Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73 (§5.8) — 'Real rendered relation wins over token intent... measured rects... token presence alone cannot close a row.' Divide. Script: frames-r3/probe-state2.mjs (register block) and probe-rhythm.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** The radius derivation law the canon gap already demands must be stated in terms of CURVATURE, not absolute radius — corner curvature holds constant or grows with box size, never inverts — and a box whose height is state-dependent may not carry a size-blind radius rung. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-06 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** OWNER MARK OM-13 / MT-F037, carried and mechanised: the bg-well rung is applied against a TRANSLUCENT pane, so its declared 'opaque tone-step of the plate' inverts sign between schemes (+0.117 L in light, the well ADVANCES; -0.038 L in dark, it RECEDES) and changes hue family (pink plate -> cream well, ~60 deg apart). That is why the owner's light-mode crop reads as a foreign raised slab rather than a recessed field. Separately, the producer census shows glass-ui 7.0.0 Input has ZERO slots, so the cure is a marked glass-forward ask, not a consume.

**Mechanism.** a material rung defined relative to an opaque token (--card) applied on a translucent host, so the step's sign and hue are set by the ambient atmosphere rather than by the token — the same class of defect as D3-01

**Evidence.**

```
Pixel-sampled from the rendered composite, 1440x900 @dsf2. Light: plate behind the head rgb(240,184,202) L=0.5703; readout well rgb(224,215,206) L=0.6878; delta +0.1174. Dark: plate rgb(119,74,85) L=0.0947; well rgb(76,65,57) L=0.0567; delta -0.0380. Magnitudes differ 3.1x. The row's own background measures rgba(0,0,0,0), i.e. the surrounding 'plate' is glass over atmosphere, not --card. Token recipe: demo/DESIGN.md:98 — '--well-bg: color-mix(in oklab, var(--card) 92%, var(--foreground) 8%)', declared as 'an opaque tone-step of the plate'. Site: GradientEasingEditor.vue:176. Producer census: @mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 exports ./forms -> ./components/input; InputProps has disabled/invalid/readonly/size; compiled dist/Input-9BlLluik.js renders classes ['input','input','input','field-control glass-defined'] and 'slots: false'. Zero demo files consume field-control. Owner mark ROOT-FINDINGS.md:1564, witness owner-marked/OM-13-easing-readout-not-glass-input.png. Same shape recurs at MixResultDisplay.vue:31 and App.vue:362 (DEFECT-LEDGER.md:31542).
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient at 1440x900 dsf2 in light, then dark. Screenshot. Sample a 12x12 patch of the head band background and the central 15% of .readout-rail; convert to WCAG relative luminance. Light: 0.5703 -> 0.6878 (+0.1174). Dark: 0.0947 -> 0.0567 (-0.0380). Producer half: node -e on node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/Input-9BlLluik.js -> /renderSlot/.test(src) === false.

**Proposed cure.** Two halves. OURS: stop applying an opaque --card-derived rung on a translucent pane — the well tier must be defined relative to the surface it is actually drawn on, or the row must supply an opaque host first (which one-surface-per-row, D3-04, gives for free). GLASS (marked ask, relayed on the standing BH/BI inbox with M3): Input must accept a trailing adornment slot, or glass must ship a read-only value/code field with an action rail. Three consumer sites share the shape. A local restyle here would be precisely the masking fallback the standing edict forbids.

```
Live repro, 1440x900 @dsf2. Before: rows 4, expanded [false,false,false,true], openCount 1, visibleLiterals ['cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)'], visibleRamps 1, visibleStrips 1, sectionH 344.5. After deleting the 50% stop: rows 3, expanded [false,false,false], openCount 0, visibleLiterals [], visibleRamps 0, visibleStrips 0, sectionH 139.6, pageErrors [], consoleErrors []. Source: GradientEasingEditor.vue:61 seeds ref(0) and nothing restores it; useGradientModel.ts:88-98 truncates intervals from the END ('intervals.value.length = needed'); GradientEasingEditor.vue:144 v-show='openInterval === row.index'. serializeIntervalRamp (useGradientCSS.ts:236-238) returns null for the out-of-range index rather than throwing, which is why this presents as silence. Law: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:101 (§5) — 'Persistent operation state stays with the entity/workspace.' Witness: frames-r3/D3-08-dead-state-zero-open-rows.png; probe frames-r3/probe-state2.mjs, probe-removal.json.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. Click .gradient-rail at 25%, 50%, 75% (5 stops, 4 rows). Click the LAST row's head (openInterval = 3). Focus the stop handle labelled 'Gradient stop at 50%', press Delete. Result: 3 rows, all collapsed, openCount 0, section height 344.5 -> 139.6px, no error of any kind. Script: frames-r3/probe-state2.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** The accordion's open state must name an INTERVAL, not a slot. Give intervals stable ids the way stops already have them (useGradientModel.ts:117, id: uid()) and key openInterval / tuneOpen / copiedIndex / the update-interval emit on the id. Deleting stop k then removes exactly one interval and leaves every other row's identity, open state and disclosure intact. A glass-ui Collapsible keyed by id (r1 D-05) gets this for free.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-09 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Authored curves migrate to a different interval on insert: the curve follows the array slot, not the interval. Authoring ease-in-out across the whole gradient and then inserting one midpoint leaves ease-in-out governing 0-25% while the remaining 75% silently reverts to linear. No notification, no undo affordance, no mark on the affected row. Round 1 filed this as an explicitly labelled HYPOTHESIS; it reproduces.

**Mechanism.** array position used as entity identity across a structural mutation that renumbers the array, so authored data silently reassigns itself to a different entity

**Evidence.**

```
Live repro, WebKit 1512x900. afterAuthor: heads ['1 -> 2 ease-in-out'], visibleLiterals ['cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)']. afterInsertMid (one click at 25% of .gradient-rail): heads ['1 -> 2 ease-in-out', '2 -> 3 linear'], visibleLiterals ['cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)']. Source: useGradientModel.ts:116-119 addStop inserts position-sorted while :88-98 appends new intervals at the END; GradientEasingEditor.vue keys openInterval (:61), tuneOpen (:84), copiedIndex (:95) and the update-interval emit contract (:49) on array position. The component's own header comment at :52-53 claims 'identity derived from the interval, the truth' — true of useSpecimenRows, false of every stateful ref and of the model beneath it. Probe: scratchpad probe-state.mjs (same recipe as frames-r3/probe-state2.mjs).
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient (2 stops, 1 interval spanning 0-100%). Press the 'in-out' specimen tile in the css family: head reads '1 -> 2 ease-in-out', literal cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1). Click .gradient-rail at 25%. Result: two rows, ['1 -> 2 ease-in-out', '2 -> 3 linear'] — the authored curve now governs 0-25% and 75% of the gradient has reverted to linear.

**Proposed cure.** Same root as D3-08: stable interval ids, and this component keys on the id. It is a model change, but the design assertion is this component's — 'a row is an interval, not a slot' — and it is currently untrue.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-03 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** A pinned sample keeps reporting its old value and old magnification after the transform moves. `drawLoupe` is called only from `showLoupeAt`, which is called only from `onTap`/`onHover`; there is no watcher on panX/panY/zoom. Wheel and trackpad zoom never emit `pointerdown`, so they never trip the unpin handler — the image slides under a stationary reticle while the readout and the loupe content stay frozen. The state the component presents as a commitment (it grows two commit buttons) is the state in which it is least truthful.

**Mechanism.** pinned state is a mode flag rather than a derived value; nothing recomputes the sample when the viewport transform it depends on changes

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:160,170 (only call sites of showLoupeAt); ImageEyedropper/composables/useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60; ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 (unpin is `pointerdown`-only). Measured: `A| TAP GREEN again => {"readout":"lab(87.818534365028% -79.27106","pinned":true,"loupeInk":9683,"transform":"translate(65px, 0px) scale(5.90625)"}` then `A| WHEEL ctrl-zoom while pinned => {"readout":"lab(87.818534365028% -79.27106","pinned":true,"loupeInk":9683,"transform":"translate(53.66px, -10.0088px) scale(6.26063)"}`. Source texel under the unmoved reticle centre: floor((381-65)/5.90625)=53 before, floor((381-53.66)/6.26063)=52 after. Reported value unchanged.
```

**Reproduction.** Open the eyedropper (steps as D3-01), hover then click to pin a pixel. Without releasing the pin, ctrl+scroll (trackpad pinch-zoom) over the stage. The reticle stays put, the readout is unchanged, the loupe canvas is byte-identical, but the transform has changed — so the reticle now sits over a different source texel than the one being reported. Driver section A of probe-CHD-p2.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Replace the `pinned`/`justUnpinned` mode flags with one `sample: {ix, iy} | null` owned by the sampler, and derive the readout, the swatch, the loupe position and the loupe content from it via a `watchEffect` on `(sample, panX, panY, zoom)`. The stale-pin case then cannot be expressed.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-04 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Pinned and unpinned are pixel-identical under forced colors. The only differentiators are `border-color: var(--primary)` and a `box-shadow` ring; forced colors overrides the border colour to the system value and suppresses box-shadow entirely, so the committed state and the live-tracking state become indistinguishable.

**Mechanism.** state encoded only in colour and shadow, both of which the forced-colors palette erases

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:262-276 (`.loupe` / `.loupe-pinned` differ only in border-color and box-shadow). Measured under `forcedColors: 'active'`, both states in one run: `FORCED-COLORS unpinned loupe: {"pinnedClass":false,"borderColor":"rgb(0, 0, 0)","borderWidth":"2px","boxShadow":"none","outline":"none rgb(0, 0, 0)"}` and `FORCED-COLORS pinned loupe: {"pinnedClass":true,"borderColor":"rgb(0, 0, 0)","borderWidth":"2px","boxShadow":"none","outline":"none rgb(0, 0, 0)"}` — identical in every property. Canon: docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 'Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only' and :84 'Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, forced colors and reduced transparency.'
```

**Reproduction.** Launch Chromium with `forcedColors: 'active'`, open the eyedropper (steps as D3-01), hover twice, read the `.loupe` computed style, then click to pin and read it again. The two objects are equal. Driver: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/probe-CHD-p2.mjs section C plus the CHD-p3 forced-colors run described in §3.4 of the report.

**Proposed cure.** Give the pinned state a geometric register the forced-colors palette cannot erase — draw the reticle and its committed variant inside the loupe's own canvas as a contrast-safe double stroke (light-over-dark) rather than as a CSS border-colour swap on a brand hue. That single move also fixes D3-05 and supplies the reticle the canon requires.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-05 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The loupe's own boundary has no contrast law and is measured far below the 3:1 floor for a non-text UI boundary. The unpinned ring is a 50%-alpha near-black; the pinned ring is `var(--primary)`, a brand hue. Both are drawn over arbitrary user photography, so neither can be guaranteed at any ratio — and a brand-hue state marker vanishes entirely when the user samples a pixel of that hue.

**Mechanism.** a single-stroke boundary in a fixed colour drawn over content the design cannot constrain

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:265 (`border: 2px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--shadow-color) 50%, transparent)`) and :274 (`border-color: var(--primary)`). Measured computed value: `"loupeBorder":"2px solid color(srgb 0.11 0.098 0.09 / 0.5)"`. WCAG ratios: pinned olive-green ring vs the red field it sits on in shots/D-02-desktop-pinned.png = 1.52:1; unpinned ring vs a blue field = 1.73:1. Canon: docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:82 — 'Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence.'
```

**Reproduction.** Open the eyedropper (steps as D3-01) over the four-quadrant fixture; hover the blue quadrant — the unpinned ring is effectively invisible. Pin on the red quadrant and compare shots/D-02-desktop-pinned.png: the olive ring computes to 1.52:1 against the field.

**Proposed cure.** Draw every boundary that sits over live content as a two-tone stroke (an inner light stroke and an outer dark stroke, or a dashed alternation) so contrast is guaranteed against any ground by construction. Same treatment for the reticle. Never mark state over user content with a single brand-hue stroke.

**Defect.** `LOUPE_SIZE = 110` is a hard CSS-px constant inside a container-scaled stage, so the magnifier does not scale with the instrument. At 200% browser zoom the stage measures 508x238 and the 110px loupe occupies 46.2% of its height — a flat coloured ball that occludes the region it claims to magnify.

**Defect.** The stage has exactly one layout — a full-width top bar over a full-bleed image — and no response to a short-wide container. At 200% browser zoom the image renders 238x238 inside a 508x238 stage, leaving 53% of the instrument's own well empty.

**Mechanism.** single-layout stage; the chrome bar always consumes the full width regardless of the stage's aspect

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-08 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The unpin flag survives a pan and swallows the next clean tap. `justUnpinned` is set on every `pointerdown` while pinned but consumed only inside `onTap`; a drag never reaches `onTap` (`didMove` is true), so the flag stays set and eats the following genuine sample. The readout still updates from hover, so the user gets partial feedback implying success while the commit affordances never appear.

**Mechanism.** a latch consumed on only one of its two exit paths — the drag path leaves it armed

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/ImageEyedropper.vue:123 (`let justUnpinned = false`), :151-156 (consumed only in onTap), :178-184 (set on every pointerdown while pinned); useInertiaGesture.ts:277-281 (onTap fires only when `!didMove`). Measured: `A| DRAG-pan while pinned => {"pinned":false,"actionBtns":1,…}` then `A| TAP GREEN (.75,.35) after pan => {"pinned":false,"actionBtns":1,…}` (swallowed) then `A| TAP GREEN again => {"pinned":true,"actionBtns":3,…}`.
```

**Reproduction.** Open the eyedropper (steps as D3-01). Hover, click to pin. Then press, drag ~40px to pan, release. Now move to a different quadrant and click once: the readout changes but no pin occurs and the Add/Apply buttons do not appear. Click again in the same place: it pins. Driver section A of probe-CHD-p2.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the flag with the mode. Under the `sample: {ix,iy} | null` model of D3-03, a pointerdown clears `sample` and a tap sets it; there is no cross-gesture latch to leave armed, and no capture-phase DOM listener reaching around the gesture composable to implement it.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-09 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The eyedropper cannot be opened by keyboard, by construction. Its only opener is `ImageDropZone`, which sets `:tabindex="disableClick ? -1 : 0"` and gates its Enter/Space handler on `!disableClick` — and `disableClick` is exactly the condition (a preview exists) under which the eyedropper becomes openable. So the control leaves the tab order and loses its key handler at precisely the moment it acquires the sampling capability, while still announcing 'Image preview area, tap to sample colors'.

**Mechanism.** the same boolean both enables the capability and removes the control's keyboard surface

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ImageDropZone.vue:19 (`:tabindex="disableClick ? -1 : 0"`), :20 (aria-label 'Image preview area, tap to sample colors'), :22 (`@keydown.enter.space.prevent="!disableClick && openFilePicker()"`); demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:22 (`:disable-click="!!session.previewDataUrl.value"`) and :25 (`@click="session.previewDataUrl.value && (eyedropperActive = true)"`). Canon: docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:198 'Eyedropper and sampler have keyboard/numeric alternatives' and :126 (the image-sampler axis row requiring named x/y controls with Home/End plus a reticle).
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/extract, upload an image, then Tab through the page: the preview region is never focused (tabindex -1) and Enter/Space on it do nothing. There is no other opener in the DOM.

**Proposed cure.** Make the sampling entry a real named control rather than a click handler on a role=button div whose tabindex is conditioned away. Then give the overlay the coordinate model the canon already specifies (named x/y numeric fields with Home/End bound to the same `sample` value as the reticle and the readout), which opens the capability keyboard-to-keyboard instead of bolting a shortcut onto a pointer-only instrument.

**Defect.** MAJOR (re-confirmation of pass1 D-8 / pass2 D2-04, with a NEW mobile number) — The headline value renders 30% of itself on desktop and 17% on mobile, because it is an unrounded 58-character float dump. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-C3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** MAJOR (re-confirmation of pass2 D2-08/D2-09 + NEW live proof) — The camera is a modal state implemented additively: no exit, an inert `disabled` contract, and a leaked live MediaStream. The viewfinder contains exactly ONE control (capture); Escape does nothing; stopCamera has only two callers (onFile :236, onBeforeUnmount :281). `:disabled="isProcessing || cameraActive"` (ExtractWorkbench.vue:70) is honoured by 1 of 5 controls — only Reset (ExtractControls.vue:84). Because 'Open camera' stays live, re-pressing it overwrites cameraStream (:242) without stopping the previous stream, orphaning a live MediaStream that only page unload reclaims (OS camera indicator stays lit).

**Mechanism.** A mode modelled as an additive boolean rather than as a stage mode with its own chassis; the disabled contract is asserted at the parent and dropped by four of five consumers.

**Evidence.**

```
probe/probe-log.txt: `"viewfinderButtons":[{"title":"Capture frame","aria":null,"text":""}]` — one control. `=== C3. Escape pressed; video still present: true`. With camera live: `{"t":"Upload image","disabled":false},{"t":"Open camera","disabled":false},{"t":"Reset","disabled":true}` and `"sliders":[{"label":"Number of colors","dataDisabled":false},{"label":"Chroma weight","dataDisabled":false}]`. NEW live proof: `=== C1b. k slider live while camera up === {"ariaValue":"6","shadowSegs":6}` — I drove k 5→6 with the viewfinder open. Leak: `=== C2 === {"streamCount":2,"trackStates":["live","live"]}`. Screenshot: probe/C-camera-active.png.
```

**Reproduction.** Stub navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia with a canvas captureStream, load /#/extract, click 'Open camera'. Press Escape (nothing). Press 'Open camera' again: window.__streams.length === 2, both tracks 'live'. Script: probe/wbex-probe.mjs section C.

**Proposed cure.** The viewfinder becomes a MODE of the stage, not a floating block: entering it swaps the stage content and the action region gains the pair the mode requires — Cancel and Capture — with Escape bound. Guard startCamera with `if (cameraActive) return`. The `disabled` prop must either reach every control in the cluster or be deleted: a contract honoured by 1 of 5 consumers is worse than no contract.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-C4 · CHALLENGE-D

Enter on the focused preview === {"eyedropperOpen":false,"activeEl":"DIV/Image preview area, tap to sample colors"}` — focused programmatically, Enter does nothing. (b) The camera capability exists twice: useImageQuantize.ts:115-146 ships a complete quantizeFromCamera with correct stream lifecycle (stop() at :140-143) and zero consumers, while ExtractWorkbench.vue:239-279 hand-rolls the same thing with a gratuitous canvas.toBlob -> PNG Blob -> File -> createImageBitmap -> OffscreenCanvas round trip. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-C6 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** MAJOR (re-confirmation of pass1 D-26 / pass2 D2-06) — Camera failure renders a raw DOMException into the quantizer's error channel, unannounced and mis-routed. ExtractWorkbench.vue:252 does `quantizeError.value = \`Camera access denied: ${err}\``. Three defects in one line: (1) undesigned copy — `${err}` stringifies the exception, and the word 'denied' is asserted even when the cause is NotFoundError (no camera) or NotReadableError (device busy), so the message lies about two of the three common failures; (2) wrong channel — it writes the quantizer's ref, whose line is captioned in source as being for palette-serialization failures, so the next successful quantize silently erases it (useImageQuantize.ts:86); (3) never announced — role null, aria-live null on a message that appears asynchronously after a permission dialog.

**Mechanism.** Error channel misuse — a device-permission failure routed through a data-serialization error ref, with template-literal exception stringification standing in for written copy.

**Evidence.**

```

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · F-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The panel headed `CSS` omits three of the six model fields (intervals, interpolationSpace, hueMethod)

**Mechanism.** Neither serializer can express the CSS `in <space> <hue> hue` production and the parser has no notion of it, so the instrument whose largest heading is `Interpolation` cannot read, write or round-trip the syntax that expresses interpolation.

```
Change Space OKLCh→HSL: editorIdentical: true (byte-identical text), tileIdentical: false (`oklch(…)` stops → `rgb(…)` stops). `GradientModelState` (useGradientModel.ts:50-60) has six fields; `serializeGradient` (useGradientCSS.ts:147-162) emits three; `serializeCoalescedGradient` (:281-305) bakes space/hue into 33 literal stops; `grep -n "interpolationSpace|hueMethod|shorter" gradientParse.ts` → only a comment.
```

**Reproduction.** Load /#/gradient → open the `Interpolation space` select → choose HSL → diff the CSS panel text and the tile's computed background-image. Transcript in report §6 F-2.

**Proposed cure.** Emit and parse the native interpolation clause; one string carrying all six fields becomes the single on-screen serialization and the clipboard payload.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · F-3 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The Direction axis's operable element is a 0×20 px, opacity:0 box carrying a second, unbranded focus indicator

**Mechanism.** GradientVisualizer.vue:232 renders the bare `<Slider>` with no `variant`, so it inherits the producer's invisible zero-width thumb and the un-suppressed UA outline. WCAG 2.5.8 (24×24) and 2.4.7/2.4.11 both fail; §5's axis composition owes label, unit, reserved value, numeric entry and focus/target behaviour — this callsite satisfies one of five.

```

**Reproduction.** Load /#/gradient → focus `main [role=slider]` → read getBoundingClientRect, computed width/opacity/outline on the thumb and box-shadow on `.slider-track`, plus elementFromPoint at the thumb centre. Script: probes/challenge-D-pass3-reset-focus.mjs.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · F-4 · CHALLENGE-D

```

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · F-5 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Reduced motion is inverted product-wide — the component gains 202 transitioning elements when the user asks for less motion

**Mechanism.** The producer's reduce block is semantically inverted: elements that opted IN to motion (`[data-allow-motion]`) are frozen at 0.01ms, while every element that never asked for motion is GIVEN a 100 ms five-property transition. `:not(…)` (0,1,0) beats the app's own `* {transition-duration:.01ms !important}` guard (0,0,0) at demo/styles/animations.css:184-191. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 requires reduced motion to resolve directly to final geometry.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured on the visualizer subtree (250 elements): no-preference → 48 with non-zero transition-duration (0.12/0.2/0.44 s tokens); reduce → 250, durations seen ONLY 0.1s and 0.15s; tile transition-property becomes "opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow" at 0.1s. CDP CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode names the winner: `:not([data-allow-motion]) { transition-duration:.1s !important; transition-property: opacity,color,background-color,border-color,box-shadow !important }` in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/utilities/a11y-overrides.css:1.
```

**Reproduction.** Launch chromium context with reducedMotion:'reduce', load /#/gradient, count elements in the visualizer subtree whose computed transitionDuration !== '0s' and read the tile's matched rules over CDP. Transcript in report §3.

**Proposed cure.** Producer fix at glass-ui (relay to the BH inbox): the reduce block must zero motion for everything and exempt only opted-in surfaces, not the reverse. Then delete the now-dead app guard rather than layering a third rule. No consumer-side patch (edict 5).

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-6 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The two operable bezier control points are 13.33 x 13.33 CSS px targets (12.31 px once the curve overshoots). WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 floor is 24x24. The dead Law 3 is the direct cause: had it executed, scale would be 304 and the handles 24.32 px — clearing the floor by 0.32 px, which is a coincidence, not a margin.

**Evidence.**

```
Live getBoundingClientRect, identical in all six matrices: `"handles": [{"w":13.33,"h":13.33},{"w":13.33,"h":13.33}]`; at y2=1.1 overshoot `"handleDia": 12.31`. Producer radius 0.04 viewBox units; rendered dia = 0.08 x scale, scale = producer block-size 200px / viewBox height 1.2 = 166.67. Under the seat's intended `inline-size: min(100%, 19rem)` (EasingAuthoringStage.vue:105) scale would be 304 -> 24.32 px. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.7 'Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities.'
```

**Reproduction.** `node docs/.../EASD-probe.mjs desktop-light|desktop-dark|mobile-light|mobile-dark|zoom200|narrow320` — 13.33 px in every one. Note the standing visual matrix reports 6 small tap targets on /#/gradient with the stage CLOSED; this component adds 2 more that the matrix has never measured because it never opens the disclosure.

**Proposed cure.** Producer: give the handle an invisible operable seat sized in CSS px via the existing `--touch-target` token, decoupled from the visual glyph's user-unit radius — glass-ui already does exactly this in `radio-group` (`--radio-seat` / `--radio-seat-offset` in dist/glass-ui.css). Consumer: nothing; this cannot be honestly fixed from a `:deep()`.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-8 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The only motion the component authors is a transition on `aspect-ratio` — a layout-forcing property that reflows the whole accordion column beneath it — it is outside all three named motion families the house declares, and it is dead anyway.

**Evidence.**

```
EasingAuthoringStage.vue:114 `transition: aspect-ratio var(--duration-normal) var(--ease-standard);`. Live computed on the SVG: `"transitionProperty": "all", "transitionDuration": "0s"` — the rule never applies (D-1). The header states the layout animation as a feature at :109-111 ('the canvas EASES to its new ratio instead of lurching the layout below'). demo/styles/animations.css:56-80 declares exactly three named families (vj-enter, vj-morph, vj-move) and states 'a fourth name is a defect'. Under PRM the global guard at animations.css:184-192 does neutralise it (measured `prm: true`, aspect-ratio absent from the transition list) — so the file's PRM claim is true but vacuous.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-4 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The drag-highlight drops off whenever the pointer crosses into a child element: `dragleave` bubbles from children and there is no dragenter counter or relatedTarget guard, so the lit state flickers continuously — worst over a populated zone where the <img> covers 100% of the surface.

**Mechanism.** absent state design — the drag state machine cannot distinguish 'left the zone' from 'entered a child of the zone'

**Evidence.**

```
ImageDropZone.vue:23-24 (`@dragover.prevent="dragging = true"` / `@dragleave.prevent="dragging = false"`); children at :37, :46, :56 carry no pointer-events:none; no dragenter handler. Measured (evidence/seatD-probe1.mjs): `"flicker": [["after dragover on container","DRAG-LIT"],["after dragleave dispatched on CHILD (bubbles)","IDLE"]]`.
```

**Reproduction.** node evidence/seatD-probe1.mjs — the flicker array shows DRAG-LIT then IDLE from a child-dispatched dragleave, which is exactly what the browser fires on a parent->child pointer move.

**Proposed cure.** A dragenter/dragleave depth counter with the lit state driven by depth > 0, or an `e.relatedTarget && el.contains(e.relatedTarget)` guard. Three lines; removes the ambiguity at the source rather than papering it with pointer-events.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · P2-2 · CHALLENGE-D

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-4 (r1, re-confirmed and extended) · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Syntax highlighting is dead exactly while the editor is in use, and after a rejected parse the wrong colours persist indefinitely — typed characters inherit the token colour of the span the caret sat in, so the ink actively lies.

**Mechanism.** a real design trade (caret safety vs live ink) resolved by deleting the feature in the used state

**Evidence.**

```
onInput (GradientCodeEditor.vue:59-62) never calls render(); the model watch (:76-79) early-returns while focused; blur re-render at :72 is gated `if (!hasError.value)`. Measured: inserting characters into the live .hljs-number span leaves {"spanClass":"hljs-number","spanText":"145abc","renderedColor":"oklch(0.49 0.12 78)"} — the NUMBER crayon rendered on letters.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → click inside the literal `145` in the CSS editor → type letters → they render in the ochre number crayon; type something that rejects → blur → the wrong colours never clear.

**Proposed cure.** The overlay idiom: a transparent-ink editable layer over an aria-hidden highlighted mirror. The caret's host is never rewritten, so ink can update every keystroke; it also dissolves D2-3 because the mirror can own pre-style non-breaking layout, and removes the innerHTML rewrite (and with it the undo-stack hazard).

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-12 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The drag-hover state cancels itself whenever the pointer crosses a child, so the drop target strobes while the file is still over it.

**Mechanism.** Absent state design: dragleave bubbles from descendants, and the handler cannot distinguish 'left the zone' from 'entered a child of the zone'; over a populated zone the img covers 100% of the surface.

**Evidence.**

```

Measured (probe2.json, each step awaited across Vue's update tick): rest -> `border-primary/30 bg-primary/5`; dragover on ZONE -> `border-primary bg-primary/10 scale-[1.01]`; dragleave bubbling from CHILD (pointer still inside) -> back to `border-primary/30 bg-primary/5`; dragover from CHILD -> lit again. Computed transition-duration 0.3s on transition-all.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../pass2-probe-D/probe2.mjs — the `drag` array in probe2.json

**Proposed cure.** A dragenter/dragleave depth counter driving the lit state off depth>0, or an `e.currentTarget.contains(e.relatedTarget)` guard. The deeper cure is D-5's: once the stage is not also the button, the drop surface has one uncontested owner.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries / ownersh` · R2-4 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** tsconfig.demo.json `paths` has drifted five rows from package.json#exports — three dead entries (one pointing at a file that does not exist) and two missing, including `@mkbabb/value.js/css`, the subpath this component's graph depends on most. The typecheck gate is structurally incapable of catching it. This corrects r1's negative proof N-1.

**Mechanism.** Two authorities for one fact (the published surface): one generated (Vite), one hand-maintained (TS). The hand-maintained one has no failure mode — a wrong `paths` entry that nothing imports is invisible forever, and a missing entry silently falls through to package self-reference, so /css resolves by a different mechanism than its four siblings with nothing declaring that.

**Evidence.**

```
package.json `exports` = 7 keys, no "." root: ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize. tsconfig.demo.json `paths` declares 8: @mkbabb/value.js, /color, /parsing, /math, /easing, /units, /transform, /quantize. `ls dist/subpaths/` -> color css easing math quantize transform value (.d.ts/.js each); `ls dist/index.d.ts` -> MISSING. So DEAD: "@mkbabb/value.js":["./dist/index.d.ts"] (key not exported AND file absent), "/parsing", "/units" (neither key nor .d.ts exists). MISSING: /css (used at 10 demo sites incl. useGradientCSS.ts:25,28 parseTimingFunction+CssLinearStop+CssTimingFunction; gradientParse.ts:21 parseCssColor+parseCssScalar; color-session/picker-color.ts:27) and /value. Gate blindness measured: `node_modules/.bin/vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit; echo EXIT=$?` -> EXIT=0. tsconfig.demo.json's own comment asserts 'the `exports` map is a CLOSED 8-key set' — stale since the 4.0.0 cut. Contrast vite.config.ts:37-50, which GENERATES its alias set from package.json#exports and is correct by construction.
```

**Reproduction.** `ls dist/subpaths/` and `ls dist/index.d.ts`; read tsconfig.demo.json `paths` against `node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports))"`; then `node_modules/.bin/vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit; echo EXIT=$?` -> EXIT=0 proving nothing catches it.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the value.js `paths` block entirely and let package self-reference resolve all seven subpaths — /css already proves this works under moduleResolution: bundler. If a paths block must remain, GENERATE it from package.json#exports exactly as the Vite alias already is. One authority, zero drift surface; then a lint rule can additionally ban any @mkbabb/value.js specifier absent from the map.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-3 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The rail axis is mapped twice over two different boxes: the forward map (pointer -> position) is TypeScript over the BORDER box (getBoundingClientRect), while the inverse map (position -> pixels) is CSS calc where `100%` resolves against the PADDING box. They disagree by the 1px border at each end, so the two maps are not inverse.

**Mechanism.** one geometric law with two implementations in two languages over two coordinate origins; the CSS one silently changes meaning if a border or padding is ever added to .gradient-rail

**Evidence.**

```
GradientStopEditor.vue:75-81 (forward: origin rect.left=224, span rect.width-20=442) vs :55-57 (inverse: `calc(10px + (100% - 20px) * p/100)` where 100%=460, origin=225). LIVE measured: rail x=224.0 width=462.0 borderLeft=1px; handle "Gradient stop at 0%" style.left="calc(0% + 10px)" measured centre cx=235; handle "…100%" style.left="calc(100% - 10px)" cx=675. Forward map at those exact pixels: pos(235)=0.226, pos(675)=99.774. LIVE confirmation: clicking the bar at x=235 — the exact pixel where the 0% handle is painted, at y=railTop+4 so the bar owns the gesture — minted a stop at 0.2%, rendered `style.left="calc(0.2% + 9.96px)"`, cx=235.88.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient -> in the console, click the rail at exactly `bar.getBoundingClientRect().x + 11` with clientY = rail top + 4 -> the new stop reads 0.2%, not 0%, and its handle lands ~0.9px right of the pointer. Error is antisymmetric: 0 at 50%, ±0.23% at the ends.

**Proposed cure.** A single useRailGeometry(el, halfPx) exposing toPosition(clientX) and toOffsetPx(position) over ONE box, built on clamp+scale from @mkbabb/value.js/math, with the handle positioned in px rather than calc(%) so the two directions are provably inverse. Ghost and handle then ride the same map by construction.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-4 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The self-declared "ONE sampling law" is implemented twice, and the model's interpolation space never reaches the emitted CSS. GradientVisualizer.colorAtPosition re-implements the interval walk / easing / mix that sampleCoalescedStops owns, then injects it into this component as an optional function prop — so the ghost dot and the rail it floats over are painted by two different implementations. Separately, rampGradient emits `linear-gradient(90deg, …)` with no `in <space>` clause, so the browser blends between sub-stops in sRGB while the model's law is oklch; COALESCE_RESOLUTION=32 exists to make that error small, i.e. the coalescing machinery is a polyfill for a CSS Color 4 feature the target browsers already ship.

**Mechanism.** the concept "the colour of this ramp at position p" has no exported home, so it leaks into a component prop; and the model's declared interpolation space is dropped at the serialization boundary, forcing a 32-sample approximation of an exact platform feature

**Evidence.**

```
useGradientCSS.ts:171-174 declares "The ONE sampling law"; useGradientCSS.ts:175-216 implements it; GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88 re-implements it and passes it as `:color-at` (GradientVisualizer.vue:139) into GradientStopEditor.vue:16. useGradientCSS.ts:223 `return \`linear-gradient(90deg, ${parts.join(", ")})\`` — no interpolation-space clause though model.interpolationSpace is in scope. Live computed --rail-ramp confirms: `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(75% …) 80.00%, …)`, no `in oklch`.
```

**Reproduction.** Structural — two call sites, both quoted with file:line. The sRGB-vs-oklch deviation between adjacent sub-stops is bounded by the 32-sample density and was NOT separately measured: that half is labelled a HYPOTHESIS.

**Proposed cure.** model/sample.ts exports both sampleAt(model, position) -> AnyColor (the ghost AND the bar-click mint) and sampleRamp(model); model/serialize.ts emits `linear-gradient(<dir> in <space>, …)` and coalesces ONLY across intervals whose easing is non-linear. Since parseGradientCSS seeds every parsed interval to the `linear` preset (gradientParse.ts:295-298), the common case collapses to an exact two-stop `linear-gradient(in oklch, …)`. The colorAt prop is deleted.

**Mechanism.** Ownership, not typing. useColorGeneration() is instantiated INSIDE GenerateControls (:35-42), so generation state is owned by a component instance and the shell has no way to reach it except by grabbing the instance. The `?.` on the METHOD (as distinct from the instance) exists only to swallow a contract mismatch — a masking fallback in the sense edict 2 forbids: rename `regenerate` anywhere in the chain and the dock button silently no-ops with no type error, no runtime error, no console warning.

**Evidence.**

```
Chain: demo/color-picker/App.vue:317 `const generatePaneRef = ref<any>(null)` → demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:106-110 `interface PaneActionRefs { generate: Ref<any>; gradient: Ref<any>; mix: Ref<any> }` → usePaneRouter.ts:196-198 `handler: () => paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.()` → GeneratePane.vue:23-25 `regenerate: () => controlsRef.value?.regenerate?.()` → GenerateControls.vue:115 `defineExpose({ regenerate, save, copyColors })`. Those three Ref<any> are the ONLY `any` in usePaneRouter.ts (`grep -n 'any' demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts` → lines 108, 109, 110 only).
```

**Reproduction.** Read the five sites above. The same three verbs are ALSO rendered declaratively on the plate (:157-184), so one concept has both a declarative and an imperative path and only the imperative one can break silently.

**Proposed cure.** Invert it. useColorGeneration becomes a pane-scoped session provided by GeneratePane under a typed InjectionKey — the pattern already used in this very tree (CSS_COLOR_KEY, LIBRARY_PORT_KEY, EDIT_TARGET_KEY). The pane declares its action descriptors as typed DATA ({key, icon, title, handler}[]) and hands them to the router, which injects rather than reaches. PaneActionRefs, both defineExpose blocks, controlsRef, App.vue's three ref<any>, and all six ?. masks delete. Pays three times: elegance, correctness (L-1 becomes unrepresentable — save reads the name from the same session the input writes), and performance (session computeds replace per-render template calls, L-9).

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-5 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** Interval identity is positional while stop identity is id-based, and the two are synced across modules by a length-only watcher that appends/truncates at the end — so inserting or removing a stop silently reassigns authored curves to the wrong stop pairs.

**Mechanism.** a shadow array with no modelled identity, kept in size by a length signal that carries no positional information, in a different module from the identity-bearing collection it shadows.

**Evidence.**

```
useGradientModel.ts:33-37 (GradientStop has `id`); intervals have none. useGradientModel.ts:89-100 `watch(() => stops.value.length, len => { …intervals.value.push(linearInterval()); … intervals.value.length = needed })` — told only THAT the length changed, never WHERE. `removeStop` (122-125) removes by id from anywhere. `addStop` (116-120) sorts by position so an inserted stop can land first. The subject cements the ordinal contract: GradientEasingEditor.vue:48-50 `"update-interval": [index: number, …]` → useGradientModel.ts:134-140 `updateInterval(index, value)`.
```

**Reproduction.** Source-derived (all three sites quoted in the report). 1) initial `stops=[A@0%,B@100%]`, `intervals=[linear]` (useGradientModel.ts:79-83). 2) press `ease-out-back` on row `1 → 2` → `updateInterval(0,…)` → `intervals=[back]`. 3) click the rail near 0% → GradientVisualizer.vue:91 `addStop(...)` → sorted, new stop lands FIRST. 4) watcher sees len 2→3 and pushes `linearInterval()` at the END → `intervals=[back, linear]`. 5) `back`, authored for A→B, is now interval 0 = N→A; A→B is linear. Symmetrically `removeStop(firstStopId)` drops the LAST interval, shifting every curve one pair left; the specimen rows relabel (useSpecimenRows.ts:61) and report the wrong assignment as truth. Live confirmation was ABANDONED — the shared dev browser at :9000 is under concurrent control by other seats (the page self-navigated /#/gradient → /#/extract → /#/atmosphere mid-evaluate; other seats' ?probe=4 / ?pro

**Proposed cure.** Architectural transposition: the easing belongs to the LEADING STOP, not a parallel array — `interface GradientStop { id; cssColor; position; easing: AuthoredEasing }` (the last stop's easing is simply unused). The length watcher DELETES; add/remove become identity-correct by construction; `updateInterval(index,…)` becomes `updateStop(id, { easing })` — the same id-addressed door every other mutation already uses; the subject's emit becomes `"update-easing": [stopId: string, value: AuthoredEasing]`; useSpecimenRows derives rows by a pairwise walk over one array instead of zipping two.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L3-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The specimen catalogue re-declares value.js's easing taxonomy as a hardcoded allow-list and FILTERS by it, silently dropping 6 of 30 library `bezierPresets` (all of quart + quint). New library families are now a silent no-op downstream.

```
demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/easingCatalogue.ts:174 `const FAMILY_ORDER = ["css","sine","quad","cubic","expo","circ","back","steps"]` + :191 `FAMILY_ORDER.filter((f) => byFamily.has(f))`. Node run against dist/subpaths/easing.js: `ALL presets: 30` … `DROPPED quart ease-in-quart, ease-out-quart, ease-in-out-quart / DROPPED quint ease-in-quint, ease-out-quint, ease-in-out-quint` → `kept bezier tiles: 24 + 3 steps = 27`. Live page.evaluate on http://localhost:9000/#/gradient: `{ tileCount: 27, glassChipCount: 27, families: ["css","sine","quad","cubic","expo","circ","back","steps"] }`. Blind gate: test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:56 `expect(SPECIMEN_TILES.length).toBeGreaterThan(20)`.
```

**Reproduction.** `node -e 'import("/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/dist/subpaths/easing.js").then(m=>console.log(Object.keys(m.bezierPresets).length))'` → 30; live `document.querySelectorAll("[data-specimen]").length` at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → 27. Downstream (derived from easingCatalogue.ts:219-223): set an interval's easing to `cubic-bezier(0.895, 0.03, 0.685, 0.22)` (= library `ease-in-quart`) and the row head reads `custom` with no tile pressed.

**Proposed cure.** GESTALT: value.js `/easing` publishes the structure it already has implicitly — `export const bezierPresetList: readonly { name: BezierPresetName; family: string; variant: string; points: readonly [number,number,number,number] }[]` — and the demo groups by the library's own `family` field in encounter order, never filtering. KISS/today: change `.filter()` to a sort (known families in FAMILY_ORDER order, unknown appended) so a new library family always appears, merely last. One line.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** value.js's public `/css` surface parses timing functions but cannot serialize them, so the CSS-literal minting law is hand-implemented THREE times across two packages: glass-ui's `useEasingPicker.readout`, this component's `bezierLiteral`/`stepsLiteral`, and a frozen third copy in `linearInterval()`.

**Mechanism.** asymmetric public surface: a grammar module that parses but does not serialize forces every consumer to hand-mint the inverse. N consumers → N copies of one law, each maintained by comment rather than by code.

**Evidence.**

```
src/subpaths/css.ts:53 exports `parseTimingFunction`, :54 exports `serializeCssColor` — the color grammar is symmetric, the timing grammar is not. `grep -rn "export function serialize" src/` → serializeCssValue, serializeCssColor, serializeKeyframeSelector, serializeTimelineOptions; NO serializeTimingFunction anywhere. Copy 1: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/composables/useEasingPicker.d.ts `readout: ComputedRef<string>` ("The complete re-parseable readout literal"). Copy 2: easingCatalogue.ts:48-56, whose comment at :41-45 declares it mirrors glass-ui byte-for-byte. Copy 3: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:56 `css: "cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"` hardcoded. easingCatalogue.ts:44-45 names copy 3 as its own precedent "generalized to the whole catalogue". `bezierLiteral`/`stepsLiteral` are exported but consumed only inside their own file (grep: 4 hits, all in easingCatalogue.ts) — dead public surface on top of duplicated law.
```

**Reproduction.** `grep -n "parseTimingFunction\|serializeCssColor" src/subpaths/css.ts` → :53 :54; `grep -rn "export function serialize" src/` → 4 hits, none for timing. Then `grep -rn "toFixed(3)" demo src --include=*.ts --include=*.vue` shows the demo's mirror at easingCatalogue.ts:49.

**Proposed cure.** value.js `/css` exports `serializeTimingFunction(ast: CssTimingFunction): string` — the exact inverse of `parseTimingFunction`, with `parse ∘ serialize ≡ id` as a round-trip property test over the whole bezierPresets corpus + the steps space. glass-ui's `readout`, `bezierLiteral`, `stepsLiteral` and `linearInterval`'s frozen string all collapse into one call; the "byte-identity with the picker" law stops being a cross-package comment and becomes a fact of the grammar module. Same shape the library already got right for colors.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-4 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** A 27-tile, 133-DOM-node selection strip is mounted for EVERY interval row inside `v-show`, although `openInterval` is a single ref so at most one row can ever be open. One strip is 23% of the entire page's element count; K intervals cost 133·K nodes, 27·K Chip instances and K MediaQueryList listeners for one visible surface.

**Mechanism.** a singleton surface instantiated per collection item: the selection strip is stateless w.r.t. the row and only one row is ever open, so per-row instantiation is pure duplication. The subtree-scoped querySelector workaround exists solely to survive the duplication it should have prevented.

**Evidence.**

```
GradientEasingEditor.vue:61 `const openInterval = ref<number | null>(0)` (single); :112 `v-for="row in specimenRows"`; :144 `v-show="openInterval === row.index"` (mounts); :152 the cheap ramp IS gated `v-if="openInterval === row.index && openIntervalRamp"`; :161 `<EasingSpecimenStrip>` is NOT gated. Live measurement at K=1: `{ stripNodeCount: 133, pageNodeCount: 579, stripShare: 23.0, tileCount: 27, glassChipCount: 27, stripCount: 1 }`. The component documents the consequence and works around it rather than removing it — EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:38-40 "scoped to THIS strip's own subtree (sibling rows mount hidden twins of every data-specimen id)". Port geometry: `{ scrollWidth: 1482, clientWidth: 436 }` = 3.4x overflow, ~8 of 27 tiles reachable at desktop, ~5 of 27 at 390px mobile.
```

**Reproduction.** Live page.evaluate at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient: `document.querySelector('.specimen-strip').querySelectorAll('*').length` = 133 against `document.querySelectorAll('*').length` = 579 (23.0%), with `document.querySelectorAll('[data-specimen]').length` = 27 for a single interval. The K-multiplication follows from GradientEasingEditor.vue:112/144/161 (v-for + v-show, no v-if on the strip).

**Proposed cure.** Hoist ONE <EasingSpecimenStrip> out of the v-for, bound to `openInterval` — the disclosure body can only ever hold one row's content, so move it out of the loop entirely (or Teleport it into the open row). What dies: the `visible` prop (a strip that exists is visible), the "hidden twins" paragraph, the subtree-scoped querySelector, and 133·(K−1) nodes. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The specimen catalogue closes value.js's preset taxonomy with a hardcoded allow-list, silently dropping 6 of 30 `bezierPresets` (the whole `quart` + `quint` families). A named library curve then renders as `custom` with no tile pressed.

**Mechanism.** The library publishes presets as a bare `Record<string, quad>` and does not publish their taxonomy, so the consumer re-derived the taxonomy by regex (`:168`) and then closed it with a hand-written allow-list. A projection of library data masquerading as a mirror; adding a preset family upstream is a silent no-op downstream.

**Evidence.**

```
`demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/easingCatalogue.ts:174` `const FAMILY_ORDER = ["css","sine","quad","cubic","expo","circ","back","steps"]` + `:191` `FAMILY_ORDER.filter((f) => byFamily.has(f))`. Live: strip renders 27 `[data-specimen]` ids, picker offers 30 options. `AFTER selecting ease-out-quart: {"headText":"1 → 2custom","readout":"cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1)","pressedTile":"NONE PRESSED"}`. Gate blind: `test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:56` asserts only `SPECIMEN_TILES.length > 20`.
```

**Reproduction.** Dev server at localhost:9000. `node scratchpad/quart.mjs` → 27 tile ids, no quart/quint. `node scratchpad/quart2.mjs` → open `/#/gradient`, click `button[aria-controls="easing-authoring-0"]`, click "Pick a curve", read 30 options, click option `ease-out-quart` → head reads `custom`, no tile pressed.

**Proposed cure.** Gestalt: value.js `/easing` publishes `bezierPresetList: readonly BezierPreset[]` with `{name, family, variant, points}` — taxonomy as DATA, not a consumer regex. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-12 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** MT-F030 / OM-4 radius incoherence: five distinct radius registers (0 / 4 / 6 / 16 / 9999 px) inside one 462x197 card; three of the five are not role-bearing house tokens, and nothing derives from anything.

**Mechanism.** The house canon lists four radius ROLE tokens but states no DERIVATION law, so nested surfaces pick values off the raw Tailwind scale by eye instead of deriving them from their parent. Compounded by L-5: the tiles' 9999px is glass's `.glass-capsule` winning because `.glass-chip--cell`'s 16px never loads — so the most conspicuous register in OM-4 is glass-owned, and a local fix would be MT-F014.

**Evidence.**

```
Live computed (`scratchpad/radii.mjs`, `/#/gradient`): `rowCard 16px`, `intervalHead 0px`, `fadingScrollPort 0px`, `rampStrip 6px`, `readoutRail 6px`, `railBtn 4px`, `specimenTile 9999px`, `specimenDot 9999px`, `pickerGlassCard 16px`. Sources: `GradientEasingEditor.vue:153` + `:176` use `rounded-md` (6px) — not one of DESIGN.md:192-197's four role tokens; `:242` hand-rolls `border-radius: 9999px` against DESIGN.md:201's explicit prohibition; `:274` uses `--radius-input`, which measures `0.25rem` (4px) while `demo/DESIGN.md:195` documents "8 px" (glass chain: `--radius-input: var(--radius)` → `--radius: 0.25rem` in `dist/styles/components.css`, a Tailwind stock var; demo overrides neither).
```

**Reproduction.** `node scratchpad/radii.mjs` (headless chromium against localhost:9000/#/gradient) prints the token table and every computed radius. Witness image: `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-4-easing-radius-incoherence.png`; dark confirmation `audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-dark/gradient.png`.

**Proposed cure.** Add the missing derivation clause to DESIGN.md §Radii and apply it: (1) a nested surface's radius is its parent's HALVED, floored at `--radius-xs` — 16 → 8 → 4; a surface never picks from the Tailwind scale. (2) The pill register belongs to POINTS (dots, markers, lamps, dock controls — meaning is position); a CELL (glyph + label) takes the derived rect register. Applied: ramp + readout rail 6→8, rail buttons 4, `.specimen-dot` → `var(--radius-pill)`, tile → 8 via glass's cell recipe (banked on M3, NOT patched locally). Separately correct DESIGN.md:195's `--radius-input` value to its actual 4px, or raise the token to the documented 8px in `demo/styles/`.

`GradientEasingEditor.vue:61` `openInterval = ref<number|null>(0)` (single); `:112` `v-for="row in specimenRows"`; `:144` `v-show` (mounts); `:152` the CHEAP ramp is gated with `v-if`; `:161` the expensive strip is not. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-7 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** glass-ui hands the component a named failure channel and the component throws it away. `useClipboard().copy()` returns `Promise<{ok:true} | {ok:false; reason: CopyFailureReason}>` and accepts an `onCopyError` callback — the producer's doc comment says it returns a named failure "rather than a lossy boolean" precisely so consumers can report it. `onCopy` awaits and discards the result and passes no `onCopyError`, so on failure `status` never reaches "success", `copied` stays false, and the button silently does nothing.

**Mechanism.** producer moved from a lossy boolean to a discriminated result; the consumer kept the retired `copyToClipboard` call shape, so the new failure channel is structurally unreachable

**Evidence.**

```
node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts — `export type CopyResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: CopyFailureReason }; copy: (text: string) => Promise<CopyResult>; onCopyError?: (reason: CopyFailureReason) => void;` · demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue:31 `useClipboard({ resetMs: 1500 })`, :32 `const copied = computed(() => status.value === "success")`, :46 `await copy(text);` (return dropped) · git show f2c8f565 commit body claims "No local adapter, no preserved boolean signature" — the symbol was migrated, the fire-and-forget call SHAPE was not
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — hypothesis at the failure branch. The API misuse is confirmed by the signature vs MixResultDisplay.vue:46; the user-visible silence is inferred from `status` never leaving idle/failure, both of which render `copied === false`.

**Proposed cure.** Fold into the L-4 cure: once copy is a `@copy` emit, MixPane owns one clipboard path and surfaces `{ ok: false, reason }` once, in one place, for both entry points (in-plate button and the dock 'Copy result' command).
