useMixingState.ts:44 `const colorSpace = ref<PickerSpace>("oklab")`. src/color/anchors.ts:360-366 `export const HUE_INDEX = { hsl:0, hsv:0, hwb:0, lch:2, oklch:2 } as const;`. src/color/operations.ts:101-112 — `interpolateHue(a,b,progress,options.hue)` is reached only inside `if (i === hueIndex)`; for oklab/lab/rgb/xyz hueIndex is undefined so options.hue is never read. 4 of the 9 INTERPOLATION_SPACES rows (color-space-meta.ts:27-35) are acylindrical, including the default. Truth law quoted at demo/color-session/color-chips/sample.ts:15-19.
```

**Proposed cure.** Derive `hueApplies = colorSpace in HUE_INDEX` from the library (one boolean, no new vocabulary) and let it govern the control's EXISTENCE, not its cosmetics — absent row and absent quartet when the space has no hue channel, matching the honest-absence restraint already implemented at sample.ts:58.

Measured under iPhone 13 emulation: resolved --ui-scale "1.5", --control-floor "2.75rem"; triggers render height 36px, min-block-size auto — contract is max(54px,44px)=54px. Mix button gap measured 8px vs producer calc(0.375rem*1.5)=9px. REPORT.json /#/mix smallTapTargets are picker channel spans (12x24) and slug controls (22x22) — zero MixConfigBar elements.

**Defect.** The convergence anchor `[data-mix-target]` does not exist in the DOM. The component's own docblock claims it plants "the anchor the canvas convergence lands on"; the drops actually converge on a hard-coded geometric guess, visibly nowhere near the plate.

**Mechanism.** glass-ui 7.0.0 WatercolorDot is `inheritAttrs: !1` and forwards only attrs.class and attrs.style (dist/watercolor-dot.js: `let n = h(), c = i(() => n.class), f = i(() => n.style)`). data-mix-target (MixResultDisplay.vue:69), tag="div" (l.67) and :title (l.103) are all discarded. mixStage.ts:121-123 then silently substitutes `{x: root.clientWidth/2, y: root.scrollHeight*0.7, r: 28}` — a masking fallback, owner edict 2.

```

Rendered node: `<span aria-hidden="true" class="shrink-0 w-10 h-10 watercolor-swatch" data-testid="watercolor-swatch" data-variant="ghost">` — no data-mix-target. shots/desktop-light-ghost.png shows the pigment drops strewn across the SOURCE cards at y≈490-660 while the dashed ghost well sits alone at y≈1093.

### `DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D) — visual truth, state coverage, motion,` · D-30 · DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** Selection is not merely colour-only — it is isoluminant. Selected and unselected tile fills are byte-identical in both schemes, and the surviving label-ink delta measures 1.16:1 (light) / 1.11:1 (dark): a pure hue rotation with essentially no luminance. On greyscale, monochrome, print, or a deuteranope's/protanope's cone response the chosen curve is one of twenty-seven identical discs — and this is the component's only job (it calls itself "the compact named-curve SELECTION surface", line 3-4).

**Mechanism.** The seat delegated 100% of the selected register to a producer channel (the doc comment at lines 160-162 asserts the Chip cell recipe "carries … the pressed wash" — it does not, glass-chip.css is orphaned) and kept no structural redundancy of its own. Its own four selection declarations (lines 204-211) are all colour or near-colour: two hue swaps, a 0.5px stroke bump, and a 400→600 weight step on 9px mono. No shape, size, indicator, rule or check delta — so the defect SURVIVES the glass fix. Compounding: `--motion-accent` is the interval's own eased-ramp midpoint (an arbitrary user colour) certified by useSafeAccentFn against a SURFACE, never against the OTHER STATE — the quantity that carries the meaning is the one quantity nothing guards.

**Evidence.**

```
`node chD-contrast.mjs` (DPR-3 element screenshot decoded in canvas; extreme-luminance ink pixel vs modal tile-fill pixel — best case for the ink, so conservative). LIGHT: selected fill rgb(244,222,208) == unselected fill rgb(244,222,208); selected ink rgb(0,92,100), unselected ink rgb(90,69,50); selected↔unselected contrast **1.16:1**. DARK: fills both rgb(105,87,72); inks rgb(79,239,255) vs rgb(213,208,200); **1.11:1**. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only."
```

### `DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D) — visual truth, state coverage, motion,` · D-28 · DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** Twelve pixels of unowned space are pinned above the strip, breaking the card's vertical rhythm to 24px/12px where the author wrote a uniform 10px gap. The FadingScroll port is 72px tall to hold 60px of content and every pixel of the surplus sits above the content.

**Mechanism.** EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:126 sets `.strip-row { display: inline-flex }`. An inline-level box inside a block container generates a line box, so the parent's half-leading lands above the content and the content bottom-pins. `width: max-content` (line 129) already supplies the intrinsic sizing inline-flex was reached for, so the inline-level-ness buys nothing and costs 12px.

**Evidence.**

```
`node chD-p3.mjs`: .specimen-strip t=622.3 b=694.3 h=72 padding:0px; .strip-row t=634.3 b=694.3 h=60 padding:2px; .strip-family t=636.3 b=692.3 h=56. Derived intervals: eased-ramp bottom 612.3 → first ink 636.3 = **24.0px**; last ink 692.3 → readout-rail top 704.3 = **12.0px**. Declared gap is a uniform `gap-2.5` (10px) on the panel (GradientEasingEditor.vue:146). Visible as a pale band under the ramp in shots/chD-row-1440.png. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.7: "Spacing is container-scaled from glass-ui tokens."
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; compare getBoundingClientRect() of `.specimen-strip` (h=72) and `.strip-row` (h=60, bottom flush). Script: chD-p3.mjs

**Proposed cure.** `display: flex`. One word. The 12px is a line-box accident, not authored spacing — no token produced it and no rule intends it.

### `DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D) — visual truth, state coverage, motion,` · D-31 · DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** The 27 support fixtures cast a shadow 3x the blur radius and 2.33x the ink of the card that contains them, while both of that card's sibling instruments cast none — and the "glass" has no blur at all, so each tile is a shadowed opaque disc wearing glass's costume. The host declares the exact opposite law in its own template.

**Mechanism.** `.glass-capsule` is unconditional in Chip's base class list (chipVariants base string), and it conflates three separable things — pill shape, warm tint, floating elevation. The seat chose a capsule-bearing primitive for what its own host declares to be a flat in-plate well, so 27 floating-tier fixtures landed inside a declared-flat plate.

**Evidence.**

```
`node chD-p5.mjs`: specimen tile box-shadow = "…, color(srgb .11 .098 .09 / 0.14) 0px 8px 24px 0px, …" + 4 rim insets; interval row card = "color(srgb .11 .098 .09 / 0.06) 0px 2px 8px 0px"; eased ramp = none; readout rail = none. Blur 24 vs 8 = 3.0x; ink 0.14 vs 0.06 = 2.33x. Measured `backdrop-filter: none` on the tile. Source: glass-ui/dist/styles/glass/glass-capsule.css `.glass-capsule { box-shadow: var(--glass-rim-top), var(--glass-rim-bottom), var(--glass-shadow-floating) }`, `--glass-shadow-floating: 0 8px 24px …14%`. Host contradiction, GradientEasingEditor.vue:108-110: "Z2 in-plate specimen rows: flat on the plate, --card-edge hairline, no shadow (DESIGN.md § Depth)". VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 ("Instrument veil … no drop shadow"; "Glass earns its blur by revealing live content; otherwise it is a neutral well"), §3.8 ("Supporting fixtures do not compete … equal shadow"), PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05 (caster shadows → REMOVE).
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; getComputedStyle('.specimen-tile').boxShadow vs getComputedStyle('.border-card-edge.rounded-card').boxShadow. Script: chD-p5.mjs

**Proposed cure.** Tiles are specimen wells, not floating capsules. The ASK is glass's (pass 2's MT-F026 relay: .glass-capsule must separate shape / tint / elevation so a well-tier chip is expressible) and must be BANKED. The DECISION to seat capsules inside a declared-flat plate is ours and is cured by choosing the well-tier variant once it exists. Cancelling the producer shadow in scoped CSS would be a per-instance override (edict 5) and a masking fallback (edict 2).

**Mechanism.** Fixed-height housing (`h-full` on both wrapper and Card, MixPane.vue:61-62) + top-aligned content (:78 `flex flex-col gap-4`) + a terminal region that does not exist until after a mix.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured at 1440x900 (evidence/challenge-D/D-geometry.mjs): mixCard h 684.73 bottom 832.73; content column bottom 553.16 → dead band 279.57 px = 40.8%. Below the last ink (Mix button bottom 537.16) = 295.57 px = 43.2%. Shrinks only under load: 2 operands 272.4 px (39.8%); 2 operands + result 97.7 px (14.3%); 12 operands + result 32.5 px (4.7%). Canon VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:30 "Empty secondary content occupies at most a narrow invitation tray (≤15% of the stage) or disappears"; :203 "No shadow palette filler appears when an operand is absent"; :47 "absent operands occupy no filler"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md PR-04 "Empty/equal companion Cards and nested housing → REMOVE".
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/mix at 1440x900; `card.getBoundingClientRect().bottom - contentColumn.getBoundingClientRect().bottom` = 279.57.

**Proposed cure.** Under D-1 the chassis content-hugs when #inspector is absent; the rack's empty state becomes a real invitation tray (D-5) rather than a fixed-height well floating inside a fixed-height card.

**Reproduction.** Read MixPane.vue:49-55 against MixResultDisplay.vue:42-47; the dock path returns no signal on a rejected clipboard write while the in-plate path confirms.

### `implementation (CHALLENGE-C) — demo/workbenches/extract/Extr` · C-5 · implementation (CHALLENGE-C)

**Defect.** Any undecodable file produces an unhandled InvalidStateError pageerror with zero user-visible signal — the plate still says no image was supplied, while the preview shows the broken file.

**Mechanism.** throwing async in a fire-and-forget event handler; no Result boundary

**Evidence.**

```
ExtractWorkbench.vue:234-237 (async handler, no catch) → useExtractSession.ts:153-157 (promise discarded) → useImageQuantize.ts:105-108,:18-26 (createImageBitmap unguarded). Measured r2 page errors: ["InvalidStateError: The source image could not be decoded.","InvalidStateError: The source image could not be decoded."]; bodyText retains '· UNDEVELOPED PLATE — FEED IT AN IMAGE ·'.
```

**Reproduction.** Both intake paths: (a) a text/plain File through the hidden input's change event; (b) a correctly-typed image/png File with corrupt bytes through the type-guarded drop path. Both crash identically.

**Proposed cure.** imageFileToPixels returns the repo's own Result<_, Issue> (a new quantize_image_undecodable variant) flowing into the existing quantizeError channel; the preview write moves onto the ok branch of the decode.

### `implementation (CHALLENGE-C) — demo/workbenches/extract/Extr` · C-6 · implementation (CHALLENGE-C)

**Defect.** Once an image loads the eyedropper is unreachable by keyboard, while the element still announces as a button named 'Image preview area, tap to sample colors'; the 'Replace image' label branch is dead code.

### `implementation (CHALLENGE-C) — demo/workbenches/extract/Extr` · C-7 · implementation (CHALLENGE-C)

**Defect.** Nothing caches pixels: every k/kC change re-decodes the whole image and does a full main-thread pixel readback, then copies the buffer again before transferring it.

**Mechanism.** expensive artefact re-derived per reactive tick instead of once per file

**Evidence.**

```
useExtractSession.ts:153-157, useImageQuantize.ts:18-26 and :93. Measured r2 for ONE ArrowRight on the k slider with a 3000x2000 image loaded: {"decodes":[{"ms":11.9,"w":3000,"h":2000}],"getImageData":[{"ms":13.4,"bytes":24000000}]} plus a second 24MB slice(0). src/quantize.ts:51 sub-samples to ~10,000 points regardless (stride 24 for this image).
```

**Reproduction.** Load a 3000x2000 PNG on /#/extract, focus the 'Number of colors' slider, press ArrowRight once, instrument window.createImageBitmap and CanvasRenderingContext2D.prototype.getImageData.

**Proposed cure.** Decode once per file into a session-held {pixels,width,height} — or transfer the buffer to the worker once and re-run k-means on its retained copy; and use createImageBitmap(file, {resizeWidth, resizeHeight}) sized to sqrt(targetPixels) so the readback is ~120KB, not 24MB.

### `implementation (CHALLENGE-C) — demo/workbenches/extract/Extr` · C-8 · implementation (CHALLENGE-C)

**Defect.** The dominance readout can name a colour that is not the card's first swatch, contradicting the component's own stated invariant.

**Mechanism.** two orderings for one claimed identity

**Evidence.**

```
ExtractWorkbench.vue:113-117 asserts 'the card's first swatch IS the dominant specimen'; src/quantize.ts:128 sorts by population (stable, ties keep insertion order) while useExtractSession.ts:121-142 adds a chroma tiebreak. r2 npx tsx derivation: quantizePixels order [0] C=0.2577 H=29.23 (red), [1] C=0.3132 H=264.05 (blue); dominant picks C=0.3132 H=264.05; AGREE? false.
```

**Reproduction.** npx tsx: quantizePixels(px([[255,0,0],[0,0,255]]), 2, 1, {k:5, chromaWeight:0.5}) then apply useExtractSession's dominant loop verbatim — index 0 and the loop's winner differ on any population tie.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the 22-line dominant loop: dominant = presented.value[0] ?? null. quantizePixels already guarantees max-population-first, which restores the invariant by construction. If a chroma tiebreak is genuinely wanted it belongs in src/quantize.ts's sort, where the card's ordering also sees it.

### `library structure — module boundaries, ownership, dependency` · N-3 · library structure

The line that would reproduce N-1 in one action is never executed. The only unit coverage is a NaN-in-glyph proxy that asserts nothing about consumability.

**Mechanism.** A gate red for reason A masks a BLOCKER for reason B; and the invariant that mattered (a tile must be consumable by the sampler that renders the row it selects) was proxied by a glyph-shape check instead of asserted directly.

**Evidence.**

```
e2e/smoke/oracles/o17-easing-composition.spec.ts:52-54 — `const svg = row.locator("#easing-authoring-0 svg[role='img']"); await expect(svg).toBeVisible();` — matches 0 elements (specHit: 0, N-2). The unreached repro is at :118 — `await row.locator("[data-specimen='ease-out-back']").click();`. Run: `VJS_E2E_PORT=9000 npx playwright test --project=smoke e2e/smoke/oracles/o17-easing-composition.spec.ts --reporter=line` → `3 failed`. Unit coverage: test/gradient-v4-consume.test.ts:56-57 asserts only `SPECIMEN_TILES.length > 20` and `every(tile => !tile.glyph.includes("NaN"))`. Zero mentions of the oracle in r1/r2/r3 (`grep -ni "o17|o-17|oracle"` over all three → no matches).
```

**Reproduction.** Run the command above; observe all three tests fail inside `openEasingBench`/`discloseAuthoring`, before any `[data-specimen]` click. Deterministic supporting proof is the in-page `specHit: 0` measurement plus the glass-ui grep, neither of which depends on the harness.

**Proposed cure.** (a) Re-anchor `discloseAuthoring` on the producer's published test hook — `[data-testid="easing-picker"] svg[viewBox]` — so the oracle measures the real canvas. (b) Move the missing invariant DOWN to a unit test where it is three lines: for every tile in SPECIMEN_TILES, `sampleCoalescedStops` over a two-stop model must not throw. That converts N-1 from an e2e-only catch into a vitest one and stops a browser-harness flake from ever hiding it again.

### `library structure — module boundaries, ownership, dependency` · N-4 · library structure

**Defect.** Four sites in the demo convert value.js Result errors back into thrown Errors, two of them reachable from a Vue `computed` and one at module evaluation. Collectively they undo the library's central design decision — that failure is a value the consumer routes, not an exception that unwinds an unknown amount of UI.

**Mechanism.** Result→throw conversion at the wrong altitude. In a Vue computed there is no unwinding target short of the app error boundary, so every one of these is a pane-killer waiting for the right input; the module-level one is a whole-bundle brick waiting for a library data change.

**Evidence.**

```
useGradientCSS.ts:206-208 (mixColors, reachable from computed) · useGradientInterpolation.ts:37 (mixColors, reachable from computed, byte-identical message string) · useGradientCSS.ts:76 and :128 (CubicBezier / parseTimingFunction, via easingFnOf) · easingCatalogue.ts:103 (CubicBezier, thrown at MODULE EVALUATION — easingCatalogue.ts:198 builds eagerly, and the module is a static import of GradientEasingEditor.vue → GradientVisualizer.vue → the async GradientPane chunk).
```

**Reproduction.** N-1 is the realised case for the first two. For the module-level one: NONE — this is a hypothesis, labelled as such (it requires a future malformed `bezierPresets` entry).

**Proposed cure.** One module owns the conversion policy for the gradient feature and its output is a diagnostic VALUE, not an exception: `composables/rampDomain.ts` exporting `clampProgress` plus `sampleCoalescedStops(m): Result<CoalescedSample[], RampIssue>`. The serializers thread the verdict the way `applyCSS` already does, and the component renders a degraded strip with a visible reason instead of vanishing. Build the catalogue lazily behind a memo and skip-with-diagnostic rather than throw. Codify and lint the invariant: `src/` returns Result; `demo/` may throw only from an event handler.

### `library structure — module boundaries, ownership, dependency` · C-2 · library structure

**Defect.** Correction/sharpening of r3's L-6. The `tsconfig.demo.json` `paths` entries do not merely duplicate the exports map — they BYPASS it. Five published subpaths resolve through `paths` and never consult `package.json#exports`, so the T.W1 demo-dogfood keystone is a false proof for them: a subpath could be deleted from `exports`, breaking every real consumer, and `npm run typecheck` would stay green.

**Mechanism.** Two resolution mechanisms for one package, with `paths` taking precedence over the exports map — a hand-rolled twin of the thing vite.config.ts:37-50 correctly GENERATES from package.json#exports so it cannot drift.

**Evidence.**

```
`npx tsc --noEmit --traceResolution -p tsconfig.demo.json` — adjacent imports in demo/color-session/picker-color.ts: `@mkbabb/value.js/color` → "'paths' option is specified … matched pattern … Trying substitution './dist/subpaths/color.d.ts'" (exports map NOT consulted); `@mkbabb/value.js/css` → "Found 'package.json' … Entering conditional exports … Using 'exports' subpath './css'" (exports map IS the gate). Programmatic diff: exports = /color /css /easing /math /quantize /transform /value; tspaths = (bare) /color /easing /math /parsing /quantize /transform /units; MISSING FROM paths: /css /value; NOT IN EXPORTS: bare root, /parsing, /units. `ls dist/index.d.ts` → No such file or directory. None of the three dead specifiers is imported anywhere in demo/.
```

**Reproduction.** Run the traceResolution command above and read the two adjacent resolution blocks; then `ls dist/index.d.ts`.

**Proposed cure.** Delete all eight `@mkbabb/value.js*` entries from tsconfig.demo.json#paths. TypeScript's self-name resolution already routes them through this package's own `exports` (proven for /css), so removal makes the exports map gate typecheck and runtime identically from one source of truth — exactly the invariant the vite alias generator already achieves. This is not tidying; it restores the gate.

### `library structure — module boundaries, ownership, dependency` · C-4 · library structure

**Defect.** Corroboration of r2's L-r2-1, extended: there is zero live import-boundary enforcement anywhere in demo/, now confirmed for the catalogue module as well as the subject. Four of the six demo eslint globs point at `demo/@/`, a tree deleted at W43; the one surviving rule bans a `@components/…` alias W43 also deleted.

**Mechanism.** Structural guards (G-DEMO-1, G-DEMO-3a, G-DEMO-3b) were written against a tree layout that a later restructure deleted; the globs silently stopped matching and nothing reported it, because a rule that matches no files is not an error.

**Evidence.**

```
`npx eslint --print-config demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/GradientEasingEditor.vue` → `no-restricted-imports: undefined`; same for `…/easing/easingCatalogue.ts`; `demo/color-picker/App.vue` → `[2,{patterns:[{group:["@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue"],…}]}]` (an alias that no longer exists). `ls -d demo/@` → No such file or directory. eslint.config.js globs: demo/color-picker/**, demo/@/components/**, demo/@/lib/**, demo/@/composables/**.
```

**Reproduction.** Run the three `--print-config` commands above and the `ls -d demo/@`.

**Proposed cure.** One flat-config object over `demo/**` with a layered ban set expressed in terms of the CURRENT tree: workbenches/** and scenes/** may reach color-session/**, shared/**, platform/**, ui/** and the published packages, but never color-picker/** (boot) and never another sibling feature's interior. Because flat config resolves `no-restricted-imports` by last-match-wins with no merge, this must be one object per file region — the existing comment already knows this and the rules still fragmented.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue,` · C-9 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The faded description remains in the accessibility tree, keeps its 18.7px box, and wins the hit test. pane-desc-shrink drives opacity 1 -> 0, which removes nothing from a11y, layout, hit testing, or text selection: a screen reader still announces the caption while it is invisible, and a pointer still lands on it.

**Mechanism.** M-B — the same transform/opacity-only construction as C-3: opacity is a paint-time property and was asked to do a presence-level job (remove the caption), which it cannot do for layout, hit testing, or the accessibility tree.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:214-223 (the keyframe) and :189-193 (its binding). probe-01-structure.mjs, #/ scrolled 300: descOp 1 -> 0 with descRectH 18.69 -> 18.69 unchanged (chromium 18.7 -> 18.7). probe-05-deadband.mjs elementFromPoint column: y=211 P.pane-header-desc, y=223 P.pane-header-desc, both inHeader:true — the invisible <p> is the hit-test winner over two sample points inside the dead band. probe-01 on #/gradient likewise returns hit 'P.pane-header-desc text-caption' at the dead-zone centre while descOp reads 0.25 -> 0.

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-05-deadband.mjs  (hit-test column) ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-01-structure.mjs  (descOp vs descRectH)

**Proposed cure.** Fold into C-3's cure rather than adding a second mechanism: replace the opacity keyframe on .pane-header-desc-wrap with a grid-template-rows 1fr -> 0fr box collapse. One change removes the box, the hit target, and the a11y-tree entry together, and it is the same declaration C-3 needs to reclaim scrollport — so the two findings share a single line of cure rather than stacking guards.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue,` · C-10 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Three load-bearing rationale comments are measurably false, and the animation shorthand omits the duration keyword the producer writes explicitly. The file is 185 of 224 lines of comment/CSS prose, so the prose is what the next reader audits against instead of the engine — false prose here is worse than none.

**Mechanism.** Spans M-A and M-C: the comments encode the same unverified engine assumptions that produced C-1/C-2, and the same overreach that produced C-5 — each false claim is the justification for a decision that turned out to be wrong.

```
demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:50-53 claims contain 'isolates the named scroll-timeline' — refuted by the contain:none control experiment (C-5, probe-08: identical animation values without it). :136-138 claims the ratio 'degenerat[es] to exactly 1 on phones ... the shrink self-neutralizes' — refuted at 1.619775 on iPhone 14 WebKit (C-1, probe-04). :148-151 claims a scroll scrub 'needs no PRM gate ... under PRM the rest state is byte-identical' — the STUCK state is byte-identical too, i.e. the animation runs at full amplitude under reduce (C-2, probe-01/probe-09), and glass-ui 7.0.0 gates all four of its own scroll-driven animations. Separately :179, :185, :190 write `animation: <name> linear both` with the duration omitted, relying on animation-duration's initial `auto`; glass-ui writes it explicitly (`animation: gl-scroll-grow auto linear`, dist/styles/scroll-driven.css), and `auto` is precisely the value the global guard overwrites with 0.01ms (probe-09), so leaving it implicit conceals the interaction.

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-08-taptarget-and-contain.mjs  (refutes :50-53) ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-04-mobile-inversion.mjs  (refutes :136-138) ; node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-09-prm-mechanism.mjs  (refutes :148-151)

**Proposed cure.** Correct the three claims as part of the C-1/C-2/C-5 cures rather than as a separate pass — each comment is deleted or rewritten by the change it justified. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt, `demo/color-sessio` · C-12 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The F7 'the chip joins the description line — height 1em' law is evaluated in the wrong font context: the chip's em resolves against the option's NAME lane (16.4px display voice), not the description lane (11px), so the chip is 16.26px tall against a 13.75px description line box — 18% oversized. This is also the un-attributed root cause of the broken phi-squared ratio: inline-size is rem (root-anchored) while block-size is em (inherit-anchored), so the plate's two axes are pinned to two different font contexts.

**Mechanism.** em is inherited-font-relative and the chip is a sibling of the micro text rather than a descendant of it, so the cascade hands it the name lane's 16.4px. Combined with a rem width, the plate is phi-squared only by coincidence at exactly 16px root with exactly this inherited size, and decouples entirely under any font scaling (200% zoom, user root-font change, or moving the chip inside the micro lane, where the ratio would become 3.81).

**Evidence.**

```
probe-C2-em-context.mjs: {"chipFontSize":"16.4px","chipH":16.26,"chipW":41.94,"wrapperFontSize":"16.4px","microFontSize":"11px","microH":13.64,"microLineHeight":"13.75px","nameFontSize":"16.4px","rootFontSize":"16px"}. 41.94/16.26 = 2.5793 vs phi^2 = 2.61803. Declarations: PreviewStrip.vue:59-60 (inline-size: 2.618rem / block-size: 1em) and the identical pair at PreviewRamp.vue:43-44. Markup proving the sibling relationship: GenerateControls.vue:243-247 places <PreviewStrip> as a SIBLING of <span class="text-micro">, both inside a wrapper that inherits the option's display voice.
```

**Reproduction.** node /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PreviewStrip/probe-C2-em-context.mjs — output pasted above.

**Proposed cure.** Write the law in one unit against one anchor: block-size: 1em; inline-size: 2.618em; — then the plate is phi-squared by construction at every scale. And set the chip's own font-size to the lane it claims to join (move the chip inside the description lane, or give the rooted chip recipe font-size: var(--text-micro)) so that '1em' means what the comment says. Do it once, in the single rooted chip recipe that C-11's gestalt cure creates.

**Proposed cure.** Two subtractive moves. (1) Make stampStops(stops) a computed alongside truncated/visible — the component already has that exact pattern two lines above; the template call is the only un-memoized read in the file. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/color-session/c` · C-8 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The entire chip is a single CSS declaration, so one unpaintable stop invalidates the whole gradient: the chip becomes a transparent hole while `data-stops` keeps claiming all 17 stops. PreviewStrip cannot fail this way (per-segment background-color costs one segment).

**Mechanism.** CSS gradient parsing is all-or-nothing, and the component has no background-color fallback. The O-14 law reads "the painted gradient must embed exactly those stops"; in this state it embeds none of them, and only the stamp would be checked by anything downstream.

**Evidence.**

```
probe-C-edge.mjs, stop 8 of 17 replaced with an unparseable colour: {"goodBg":"linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.62 0.27 9.8), ...","poisonedBg":"none","poisonedBgColor":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)"}. PreviewRamp.vue:35 sets the whole ramp as one `backgroundImage`; :34 computes `data-stops` independently, so the stamp survives the paint's death.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe-C-edge.mjs, field `render.poisonedBg`. LIVE TRIGGER: NONE FOUND — labelled a robustness finding, not a live bug. I drove the boundary operands through the real sampler in-browser: `transparent` -> valid oklch(... / 0%) stops; `oklch(0.5 0.1 none)` -> the none hue collapses to a number, no `none` reaches the paint; `currentColor` -> null; "" -> null; identical operands -> 17 identical valid stops; kelvin space -> valid. Every reachable path serialises paintable OKLCh.

**Proposed cure.** C-3's hard-stop cure does not fix this (still one declaration). The structural cure is the rooted plate painting per-segment children, which makes the failure local and visible — the same move C-3 and C-6 want.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/color-session/c` · C-9 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `sampleInterpolationRamp`'s exported `k` parameter has no domain guard and breaks the module's own contract at the boundary: k=NaN returns `[]` (neither null nor a ramp, and `[]` is truthy so the host's `v-if` does not catch it), and k=Infinity never terminates.

**Mechanism.** A public exported parameter with no domain guard, in a module whose stated thesis is "honest absence, never a canned swatch". The honesty is enforced for operands (sample.ts:58 and :64) and not for k. `Math.ceil(Infinity/1)+1 = Infinity` makes the inner `for (j < perSegment)` loop non-terminating.

**Evidence.**

```
sample.ts:52-57 documents `string[] | null`; :69 computes `perSegment = Math.max(2, Math.ceil(k / segments) + 1)`. probe-C-edge.mjs: k=0 -> 2 stops, k=1 -> 2, k=-5 -> 2 (the Math.max floor holds); k=NaN -> {"n": 0}; k=Infinity -> non-terminating (observed: hung the page for >170s, the first probe run had to be killed at the 180s tool timeout). Host guard that would miss `[]`: MixConfigBar.vue:111 `v-if="spaceRamps.get(s.value)"`.
```

**Reproduction.** Direct call only. `k` is never passed by any host (MixConfigBar.vue:62 and :71 use the default 16), so neither arm is reachable from the running app today — labelled a hypothesis-grade robustness finding on that basis. To reproduce: node .../probe-C-edge.mjs (kNaN); the kInfinity arm is deliberately stubbed out in the banked probe because re-running it hangs the page.

**Proposed cure.** `if (!Number.isInteger(k) || k < 2) return null;` at the top of the function, beside the existing operand guard. One line, same idiom as the line above it.

**Defect.** Vacuous gate: no unit test exists for EmptyState at all (@vue/test-utils IS installed), the two covering e2e oracles pin only the trio and the eyebrow strings, and no test anywhere presses the Retry button — so the gate is structurally blind to C-1 and C-2 and four named mutations keep the entire suite green.

**Mechanism.** The oracles were written to pin a design ruling (which ghost register speaks at true-empty) rather than the component's contract, so everything the component actually renders per prop — and every interaction it hosts — is untested.

**Evidence.**

```
Covering tests: e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts (trio count/aria-hidden/3 ghosts/3 strokes at :69-77; eyebrow "· empty plate ·" :195, "· the commons ·" :230; getByRole("alert") :255) and o10d-display-voice-census.spec.ts:208-220 ([role="status"] p.font-display). Green-keeping mutations: (a) delete EmptyState.vue:61-63 (the hint <p>) — `grep -rn "Add colors above\|Publish one from My Palettes\|Save two or more palettes\|then save the set" e2e/ test/` → 0 hits; (b) delete EmptyState.vue:23-25 (the error detail <p>, the explicitly designed "machine truth" per BrowsePane.vue:54-58) — `grep -rn "Failed to load palettes" e2e/ test/` → 0 hits; (c) delete the whole <style scoped> .plate-ink block EmptyState.vue:94-105, reverting the certified P4-R2/D6 --ink-muted rung — `grep -rn "plate-ink" e2e/ test/` → 0 hits; (d) any of C-5..C-9. `grep -rln "EmptyState" test/` → no hits.
```

**Reproduction.** Apply mutation (a) or (b) and run the suite: all green. Verified by grep that no assertion string in e2e/ or test/ references any hint text, the error detail text, or the plate-ink class.

**Proposed cure.** A unit test that mounts both variants and asserts rendered lines + roles per prop combination (cheap — @vue/test-utils is already a dependency), plus one e2e leg that presses Retry and asserts the pane still holds an alert AND that focus is somewhere reachable. That leg is born-RED today: it is the C-1 gate.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shared/ui/PaneH` · C-9 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** O-11 gate 3's 'no double-exposure' certification is measured on the animation's opacity sub-property, not on composited alpha. The veil's fill is a color-mix that resolves to alpha 0.65 light / 0.72 dark, so 35% / 28% of the scrolled content transmits through the band behind only a 7px blur — and the double exposure is plainly visible in the committed screenshot.

**Mechanism.** M-B — a gate reading the wrong quantity: opacity:1 of a 65%-alpha fill is not opacity, and perceptual occlusion is the property the gate exists to bound.

**Evidence.**

```
e2e/smoke/oracles/o11-header-gates.spec.ts:154 asserts at64.opacity === 1. --glass-bg-resting is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--card) calc(...), transparent)` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/glass.css:1); resolved live to alpha 0.65 light / 0.72 dark (pass-1 probe-06-veil-alpha.mjs). Visual confirmation read by me: shot-webkit-desktop-about-scrolled300.png shows the underlying <h2> 'Basic Information' and the row 'Dependency: Device-independent' legible INSIDE the 136.6px band, with the 0.311x title 'About the color / spaces, Lab' overprinted directly across them — two type layers, one band.
```

**Reproduction.** Read docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/shot-webkit-desktop-about-scrolled300.png (committed); regenerate with pass-1 probe-06-veil-alpha.mjs

**Proposed cure.** The gate must read the COMPOSITED result — a pixel sample of a known glyph inside the band versus the same glyph outside it — not getComputedStyle(el,'::before').opacity. The design cure is C-4's real box collapse, so there is no 136.6px band for content to sit inside. Raising --glass-bg-resting's alpha only under the stuck state would be a per-instance override and is forbidden by edict 5.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shared/ui/PaneH` · C-11 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The veil scrub is not free, and O-11 gate 4 — named COMPOSITOR-ONLY — measures only the devtools.timeline Layout track. The veil is an opacity animation on an element carrying backdrop-filter, which cannot be a pure compositor property because the filtered backdrop must be recomposed for the new group alpha.

**Mechanism.** M-B — a gate whose name is broader than its measurement; 'compositor-only' certified by the absence of Layout, with style/paint/raster unmeasured.

**Evidence.**

```
e2e/smoke/oracles/o11-header-gates.spec.ts gate 4's live half counts only `Layout` events (<=5). probe-C2-02-scrub-cost.mjs, four conditions interleaved x3 reps, 100 rAF frames each, chromium 1440x900 on /#/, CDP Performance.getMetrics deltas per 100-frame scrub: A(shipped) task=176.4 layout=0.8 style=64.2 script=6.8 ; B(no backdrop-filter) task=165.8 style=58.6 ; C(no veil animation) task=147.1 style=54.1 ; D(neither) task=149.1 style=56.8. Per-frame: A mean=40.06 p95=78 ; D mean=36.25 p95=68.1. Layout really is flat (0.7-0.8ms) — gate 4's structural claim is sound — but ~18% of the scrub's main-thread cost is the veil, and 64.2ms of style recalc per 100 frames lands on an animation the file calls 'compositor-only' (PaneHeader.vue:9-10).
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaneHeader/probe-C2-02-scrub-cost.mjs

**Proposed cure.** Either narrow gate 4's name to what it measures (LAYOUT-FLAT) or widen its measurement to the style/paint/raster tracks with an explicit budget. Recorded at MINOR because the A-D delta is small and the headless baseline is dominated by the GooBlob WebGL rAF on that route — the interleaved delta is the load-bearing number, not the absolutes. Flagged because C-4's cure will be argued against on exactly this ground.

**Defect.** `v-if="stops.length >= 1"` admits count = 1, so a single 42x16 block renders wearing the full palette grammar — plate radius, plate ring, the phi^2 proportion that MEANS 'a sequence'. A strip of one is a swatch.

PreviewStrip.vue:40 (`>= 1`) against GenerateControls.vue:300 (`:min="1"`). The sibling sets its floor one higher for exactly this reason: PreviewRamp.vue:31 `v-if="stops.length >= 2"` ('one stop is not a ramp').

ColorSpaceSelector.vue:125 + :146-148 use the legacy prop + defineEmits pair for `modelValue`, while :144 uses `defineModel` for `open` — two idioms in one file (owner edict 7, idiomatic Vue 3.5; `defineModel<string>()` replaces the pair). `defineModel<boolean>("open", { required: true })` forces every host to own an open ref: demo/scenes/about/AboutPane.vue:73 `const aboutSelectOpen = ref(false)` is declared, bound at :22, and never read — write-only. The only real consumer is demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:265 `selectedColorSpaceOpen.value = !selectedColorSpaceOpen.value` under a `Cmd+K` handler — an unlabelled, undiscoverable keyboard affordance (PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:51, PR-07 "Hover-only/unlabeled controls"). `any` casts: ColorSpaceSelector.vue:11 `(colorSpace: any)`, repeated at ColorPicker.vue:43 and AboutPane.vue:25; the emit is typed `[value: string]` and the `any` masks the reka `AcceptableValue` mismatch rather than resolving it (edict 2, no masking fallbacks). Cohesion: `specimenFor` (:154-166) performs conversion, serialization and two incompatible number formats inside a selector component.
```

**Reproduction.** grep -rn 'selectedColorSpaceOpen\|aboutSelectOpen' demo/ — aboutSelectOpen appears exactly twice (declaration at AboutPane.vue:73, binding at :22) and is never read.

**Proposed cure.** Collapse to one idiom: `const modelValue = defineModel<DisplayColorSpace>()` and `const open = defineModel<boolean>('open')` without `required`, which types the emit correctly and deletes all three `any` casts at once. Move `specimenFor`'s formatting beside `serializePickerColor` so the catalog and the readout share one canonical grammar (which also cures D-3d). Give the Cmd+K affordance a visible name or delete it.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-14 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Physical `padding-left`/`padding-right` on the option row in a document that declares a direction, and no bidi isolation on captions that are CSS strings full of paired brackets. The asymmetric 12/16px gutter is additionally vestigial — it was tuned for the indicator-less row.

**Mechanism.** F1/F3 — physical rather than logical box properties, and an un-isolated domain string in a prose container

**Evidence.**

```
ColorSpaceSelector.vue:65 `class="pl-3 pr-4 py-2"` — physical, measured `paddingLeft: 12px / paddingRight: 16px`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:150 "chrome, navigation and layout | logical inline/block direction follows the document"; the logical form `ps-3 pe-4` is the same character count. The `.specimen-caption` carries no `dir="ltr"`, no `<bdi>`, computed `unicodeBidi: "normal"` and `dir` attribute null; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:154 "CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance | render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose". Captions such as `lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)` contain paired brackets, which UAX #9 rule BD16 mirrors in an RTL paragraph. The 12px leading gutter is also too small to clear the producer indicator's `left-2 + w-3.5` = 22px if D-2 is cured.
```

**Reproduction.** HYPOTHESIS for the rendered mirroring only. With `document.documentElement.dir = "rtl"` the app still computes `direction: ltr` on both the trigger and the caption (probe measured `triggerDir: "ltr"`, `capDir: "ltr"`, `capUnicodeBidi: "normal"`, `capDirAttr: null`), so RTL is presently pinned off and the mirroring cannot be exhibited live. The code-level absence of logical properties and of bidi isolation is FACT, verifiable at ColorSpaceSelector.vue:65 and :87-92.

**Proposed cure.** Use logical `ps-*`/`pe-*` and size the leading gutter from the producer indicator's geometry rather than a tuned constant. Wrap the caption value in `<bdi>` (or `dir="ltr"` + `unicode-bidi: isolate`), which is what VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:154 already requires for every CSS string, hex, slug and ID in the app — this is a house-wide rule, so the cure belongs in whatever shared value-rendering primitive the demo has, not in this file alone.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-15 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** In dark mode the component's one chromatic gesture is achromatic: the certified accent loses 89% of its chroma, so the title that carries the product's colour identity in light mode paints near-white in dark. The component compounds it by hard-coding an 86% alpha with no reference to the tier it lands on, yielding two different rendered contrasts for one "grammar".

**Mechanism.** F3 — the chromatic identity is delegated to a certifier that optimises luminance contrast alone, then a fixed alpha is applied on top without re-certifying against the actual tier

**Evidence.**

```
Measured `--accent-live` (probe-D4.mjs): light `oklch(47.118925176164% 0.188447570516 9.83402284231deg)` chroma 0.188; dark `oklch(95.832172477266% 0.021053120065 9.83402284231deg)` chroma 0.021 — a 89% chroma loss. Rendered trigger ink (probe-D.mjs): light `color(srgb 0.665034 0 0.261497 / 0.86)` — saturated crimson; dark `color(srgb 1 0.924654 0.933001 / 0.86)` — effectively white. Visible in ../../visual/shots/safari-desktop-dark/picker.png. Two rendered contrasts for one ink: PIL sampling of the tracked Safari light capture (peak ink pixel vs modal background over the title bounding box) gives 3.89:1 on the picker plate (bg 236,185,212 / ink 179,26,87) and 4.79:1 on the About plate (bg 247,216,216 / ink 181,30,88) — a 23% spread, because ColorSpaceSelector.vue:191 fixes `color-mix(in srgb, var(--space-title-ink) 86%, transparent)` without reference to the tier. Laws: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:21 sanctions seed tint for the "active accent"; :144 "No path desaturates through gray"; :82 "a token name is not evidence".
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/ColorSpaceSelector/probe-D4.mjs prints `accentLive` per scheme; the two-host contrast spread is reproduced by the PIL block pasted in report §D-15 over the tracked Safari captures.

**Proposed cure.** Mechanism owner is `certifyAccentInk` / demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:302-311, not this file — the certifier must preserve a chroma floor in dark, not only a luminance ratio, or the "active accent" ceases to be one. In this component, delete the 86% alpha and let the certified ink be the rest ink, deriving hover from a second certified rung: an alpha applied after certification silently un-certifies the result and makes the rendered contrast host-dependent.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-9 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** O-14's own doctrine is re-admitted between samples. sample.ts forbids CSS gradient interpolation "because the preview must show what THE APP computes, not what the browser's engine would"; PreviewRamp then paints `linear-gradient(90deg, …)` with no `in <space>`, so 16 of 17 segments of the chip's width are the browser's default (oklab) interpolation — in every row, regardless of which of 9 candidate spaces the row previews. The e2e guard checks only the stop LIST, so the forbidden mechanism is present and unmeasured.

**Mechanism.** doctrine leak — the module's stated prohibition is enforced at the sample points and abandoned everywhere between them, with the oracle blind to the gap

**Evidence.**

```
sample.ts:5-11 states the law. PreviewRamp.vue:25 `linear-gradient(90deg, ${stops.join(", ")})` — no interpolation space declared. e2e/smoke/oracles/o14-preview-truth.spec.ts:360-392 asserts only `painted.length === stamped.length` plus per-component equality of the DECLARED stops. Measured painted pixel vs a direct mixColors recompute at each segment midpoint (RGB Euclidean 0–255, chip rendered at 100× width): hsl/longer worst 15.6 at segment 5 (painted 217,216,23 / library 228,227,24); hsv/longer worst 15.6; oklch/longer worst 5.1 (painted 89,162,10 / library 88,162,5).
```

**Reproduction.** node /tmp/pr_o14b.mjs — builds the 17-stop list with the shipped sampler algorithm against dist/subpaths/color.js, paints it as a linear-gradient in Chromium, screenshots and decodes the strip in-page, samples the midpoint pixel of each segment and compares to mixColors at the same t.

**Proposed cure.** Choose one and say so. Either paint hard segments as PreviewStrip does — the divergence becomes identically zero and the two components collapse toward one grammar — or state honestly in the docstring that the chip is a 17-sample approximation whose inter-sample paint is the UA's, and add a midpoint leg to the oracle with a declared tolerance.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-10 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** An unreachable guard, and the absence law owned in two places. `v-if="stops.length >= 2"` can never evaluate false because the sampler returns either null or an array of length ≥ 2; the host already guards on the same fact. Two guards, one reachable — a masking fallback — and "honest absence" therefore has two owners and no owner.

**Mechanism.** masking fallback — a defensive condition that cannot fire, duplicating a law the caller already enforces, so neither site owns it

**Evidence.**

```
PreviewRamp.vue:31 `v-if="stops.length >= 2"`. sample.ts:69 `const perSegment = Math.max(2, Math.ceil(k / segments) + 1);` and :74 pushes perSegment stops for segment 0, so a non-null return always has ≥2 stops; sample.ts:58 `if (operandsCss.length < 2) return null;`. Host guards: MixConfigBar.vue:111 `v-if="spaceRamps.get(s.value)"` and :133 `v-if="hueRamps.get(m.value)"`. Owner edict 2 (no masking fallbacks).
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — this is a static-reachability finding proved by reading sample.ts:58,69,74 against PreviewRamp.vue:31 and MixConfigBar.vue:111,133. No runtime input makes the inner v-if false while the outer guard is true.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the unreachable v-if and let the sampler's `null` be the single absence authority — which is what D-1's cure requires anyway, since the absence state must be DRAWN by one component rather than silently skipped by two.

**Defect.** The list argument passed to `useSortable` is a detached, unobservable snapshot — a load-bearing-looking argument that does nothing.

**Reproduction.** NONE — hypothesis-free but effect-free by construction: read the two cited sources. No user-visible symptom; the harm is that it reads as intentional to the next maintainer and camouflages D-1.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt, component `demo/pa` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Stringly-typed action contract with a silent swallow. `defineEmits<{ action: [action: string] }>()` plus the parent's `const fn = actions[action]; if (!fn) return;` means any typo on either side is an unnamed masking fallback. The gap is already load-bearing: the parent carries a `copyAll` handler that NO menu item can ever emit — unreachable code the type system cannot see.

**Mechanism.** A cross-component command bus typed as `string`. The compiler cannot check either end, so the exhaustiveness that a discriminated union would enforce is replaced by a runtime `if (!fn) return` that converts every mismatch into a no-op instead of an error — the textbook masking fallback the owner edicts forbid.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteCardMenu.vue:224-227 `defineEmits<{ action: [action: string]; updateOpen: [value: boolean]; }>()`. PaletteCard.vue:315-316 `const fn = actions[action]; if (!fn) return;`. PaletteCard.vue:294 `copyAll: () => void writeClipboard(...)`. `grep -rn "copyAll" demo --include="*.vue" --include="*.ts"` → exactly ONE hit (PaletteCard.vue:294); no emitter exists. Downstream continuation: demo/palettes/usePaletteExport.ts switches on `format: string` with no `default:` case and wraps everything in `catch (e) { console.warn("Export failed:", e); }`, so an unknown format and a real failure are indistinguishable silence — even though the card owns an ActionFeedback channel and `defineExpose({ showFeedback })` that export never uses.
```

**Reproduction.** `grep -rn "copyAll" demo --include="*.vue" --include="*.ts"` returns one line (the handler) and zero emitters — the dead branch is proof the contract is unchecked. To exhibit the swallow: change any `$emit('action', 'exportPNG')` to `'exportPng'` — typecheck passes, tests pass, the menu item silently does nothing.

**Proposed cure.** Declare `export type PaletteCardAction = "save" | "publish" | "delete" | ... | "exportPNG";` once beside the menu; type the emit `action: [action: PaletteCardAction]` and the parent map `Record<PaletteCardAction, () => void>`. That makes the map exhaustive, lets `if (!fn) return` be deleted, and turns `copyAll` into a compile error. Same treatment for the export format string (`"json" | "css" | "tailwind" | "svg" | "png"`), with the swallowed catch routed into the existing ActionFeedback channel.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt, component `demo/pa` · C-8 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Two activation idioms in one menu — 11 items use `@click`, 5 use `@select`. They are not equivalent: `@click` cannot use the primitive's cancelable ITEM_SELECT contract, and it fires from a listener merged AFTER reka's own handleSelect, so the parent's close and reka's onClose race to close the same menu.

**Mechanism.** The DOM event and the primitive's semantic event were treated as interchangeable. They differ in cancelability and in ordering relative to the menu's own close, so the file carries two different activation semantics for what reads as one uniform list — a KISS violation and a latent ordering hazard.

**Evidence.**

```
`@click` at PaletteCardMenu.vue:18, 31, 52, 66, 76, 86, 96, 136, 146, 158, 165; `@select` at :113, :116, :119, :123, :126. node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Menu/MenuItem.js: `emits("select", itemSelectEvent); await nextTick(); if (itemSelectEvent.defaultPrevented) isPointerDownRef.value = false; else rootContext.onClose();` — the cancelable affordance an @click item can never reach. Merge order (renderer fallthrough): onClick = [handleSelect, consumerOnClick], so the emit lands between handleSelect's sync half and its post-nextTick onClose.
```

**Reproduction.** Static, in the reka source quoted above. The race is currently benign only because the parent's competing close-guard is itself dead (see C-6); it becomes observable the moment either close path grows a side effect.

**Proposed cure.** Use `@select` throughout — it is the primitive's contract, it is already what the export half uses, and it is the only one that composes with `preventDefault()` to keep the menu open. One menu, one activation contract.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects · demo/palettes/browser` · C-13 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `void writeClipboard(userSlug)` discards the discriminated `{ ok } | { ok, reason }` result the glass-ui primitive exists to return, so a denied clipboard write is visually indistinguishable from success — and success is silent too.

**Mechanism.** `void` on a primitive whose entire design point is a nameable failure. The menu closes either way, so the user cannot tell.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteSlugBar.vue:168-170 `function onCopySlug() { if (userSlug) void writeClipboard(userSlug); }`. Contract quoted from node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts: `/** A failed copy always names its channel; a successful copy carries no reason. */ export type CopyResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: CopyFailureReason };` and `/** Stateless one-shot clipboard write — the honest primitive … Returns the discriminated result … rather than a lossy boolean, for identical call ergonomics: const { ok } = await writeClipboard(text) */`. `CopyFailureReason = "clipboard-api" | "no-api"`.
```

**Reproduction.** Structural — the discard is unconditional. Exhibited on any non-secure context or denied permission (Safari private mode).

**Proposed cure.** `const { ok } = await writeClipboard(userSlug); emit("copy", ok)` — which finally gives the dead `copy` emit (C-12) a reason to exist and lets one owner render a single feedback affordance for all copy actions.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects · demo/palettes/browser` · C-22 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The pill's hover-vs-click routing is decided once, non-reactively, at setup: glass-ui reads `matchMedia("(pointer: coarse)").matches` into a plain `let` with no change listener, so a device whose pointer class changes keeps the wrong popover root for the component's lifetime.

**Evidence.**

```

Consumed by PaletteSlugBar.vue:45 `<Popover v-if="userSlug" trigger="hover" :close-delay="0" :open-delay="300">`.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — read from vendor source. The runtime consequence on a pointer-class change is labelled a HYPOTHESIS; the non-reactivity itself is source-proven.

**Proposed cure.** Consumer side: C-8's cure — a focusable trigger makes the routing question moot, because focus works on both pointer classes. Producer side (relay): bind the query with `matchMedia(...).addEventListener("change", …)` so `usesHoverRoot` is genuinely reactive.

**Reproduction.** NONE — hypothesis-free static reading of the six class strings and the token value; no runtime repro attempted because the component never renders. The token arithmetic (50ms gate vs 200ms --duration-fast) is exact.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-25 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Non-concentric corner: the full-bleed colour strip carries the card's OUTER 16px radius while sitting at the border's INNER edge, where 14px is required. Together with three stacked zero-blur casters this is the mechanism behind the owner's own mark, which the prior seat's report never references.

**Mechanism.** Clip responsibility was moved onto the child (to avoid 1-bit rasterization at compositing-layer bounds) without moving the radius arithmetic with it. Three copies of a 16px arc at three offsets diverge maximally at the rounds and converge along the straight edges, so the cast reads clean on the sides and faceted/stepped at the corners.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured live: card `border-top-left-radius: 16px`, `border-top-width: 2px`, strip inset from card left = `2px` (i.e. exactly at the inner edge), strip `border-top-left-radius: 16px`. Concentric requirement = 16 − 2 = **14px**. Owner artifact: `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-2-card-shadow-sharp-corners.png`. Shadow half, computed: `oklab(0.28 …/0.32) -3px 3px 0px 0px, oklab(0.28 …/0.26) -5px 5px 0px 0px, oklab(0.28 …/0.18) -7px 7px 0px 0px` — three hard copies, zero blur, zero spread. Radius applied at PaletteCard.vue:36 (`rounded-t-card`), forced by the deliberate refusal of overflow-hidden at :16-18.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with any populated palette; read `border-top-left-radius`/`border-top-width` on `[role="article"]` and `border-top-left-radius` + `getBoundingClientRect().left` delta on its strip child. Visual: owner-marked/OM-2-card-shadow-sharp-corners.png.

**Proposed cure.** The concentric arithmetic should never be authored by hand. Cure step 1 (`<Card … :shadow="false">`) removes the three casters and therefore the visible artefact; the strip radius then belongs to a producer-side inner-radius token (`calc(var(--radius-card) - var(--card-border-width))`) rather than a repeated `rounded-t-card` literal at the consumer.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-26 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** In dark mode the cel shadow is effectively the same luminance as the surface casting it, and the alpha was raised to compensate rather than the contrast fixed.

**Mechanism.** A hard-edged cel shadow requires luminance headroom beneath the surface; a dark card has none, so the register degrades to a grey smear whose only surviving signal is the offset silhouette. The alpha bump from .32 to .46 is evidence someone noticed the weak read and compensated with opacity instead of contrast.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured on the same element, light vs `.dark`: card `background-color` `oklab(0.913 …)` → `oklab(0.345 …)`; shadow colour `oklab(0.28 …)` → `oklab(0.34 …)`; alphas .32/.26/.18 → **.46/.38/.26**. L(shadow) − L(card) = **−0.633 light** vs **−0.005 dark**. Token: `--shadow-cartoon-md` uses `light-dark(hsl(24 10% 10%), hsl(30 14% 90%))` then `clamp(0.28, l, 0.34)`, so the dark arm takes the LIGHT source colour and clamps it down to 0.34 — landing on the card's own 0.345.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; read `boxShadow` and `backgroundColor` on `[role="article"]`, then `document.documentElement.classList.add('dark')` and read both again.

**Proposed cure.** Not a token patch — the ruled tuple already says `shadow: false` for this species (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1). Cure step 1 removes the caster entirely; a matte specimen slip needs no cast shadow on either scheme. If any producer follow-up is warranted it is a letter to glass-ui that `--shadow-cartoon-md`'s dark arm clamps into its own surface band.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-27 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The identity row has no overflow design in any direction: once the title is starved to 0 (D-2), the remaining `shrink-0` content exits the card box and then the viewport. The prior seat measured a 37px chip↔menu overlap; the mechanism is unbounded.

**Mechanism.** Title absorbs 100% of negative free space (line-clamp's overflow:hidden zeroes its automatic minimum), reaches 0, and the remaining unshrinkable content simply overflows. `REPORT.md`'s `horizontalOverflow: 0` misses it because an ancestor clips before the document scroll width grows — the content is lost, not merely off-screen.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured at 390px viewport, card 324px wide (right edge ≈ 357px), fixture palette with 5 tags: menu button left 307.0 right 343.0; chip 'blue' left 314.9 right 348.7 → **overlapMenuPx: 28.1**; chip 'cool' left 356.7 right 389.9 (outside the card); chip 'ocean' left 397.9 right 441.3 → **84px outside the card, past the 390px viewport**. `metaCluster.scrollWidth − clientWidth = 142`; `row.scrollWidth − clientWidth = 86`. Row structure: PaletteCard.vue:43-79 (`flex items-center justify-between gap-2 min-w-0`) with 9 `shrink-0` siblings, title at :54-59 carrying none.
```

**Reproduction.** Seed a palette with `tier:'featured'`, 5 tags, forkCount/versionCount, and a long name; load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 390×844; read the chip rects against the card's right edge.

**Proposed cure.** Structural, per the ruled anatomy: the identity line gets its own row with `flex-1 min-w-0` and the meta cluster is demoted below it or behind a single count — the chips stop being peers of the title. This is the same move that cures D-2, D-5 and D-18, and it is why `PaletteCardMeta` must not exist as a bare multi-root fragment of `shrink-0` siblings spliced into the parent's flex row. Note the `.slice(0, 3)` tag cap is not conservative truncation — it is the only thing bounding this escape, and three tags already escape.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-28 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The featured badge's gold outline is declared twice by two mechanisms, both per-instance overrides of a glass-ui `Badge`, while glass-ui already ships an unused metal register.

**Mechanism.** The producer's metal register was extended to `Card` but never to `Badge`, so the consumer forked it locally in scoped CSS instead of the fix landing once in the design system.

**Evidence.**

```
PaletteCard.vue:64 applies `border-gold` in the template AND :343-345 re-declares `.featured-badge { border-color: var(--color-gold); }` in scoped CSS. Measured: `border-gold` resolves — computed `border-color: oklch(0.751 0.147 84.2)` = `--color-gold` — so the utility works and the scoped rule is redundant. Producer register that exists and is unused: `dist/styles/utilities/metal.css` exposes `--metal-border-width`, `--metal-stop-{light,base,dark}`, `--metal-glow-{blur,opacity}`; `Card.vue.d.ts` carries `metal?: "gold" | "silver" | "bronze"`; `Badge.vue.d.ts` exposes only `tone?: neutral | destructive | success | warning | info` — no metal arm. ```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with a `tier:'featured'` palette; read `borderColor` on `.featured-badge` (resolves via the utility), then observe the scoped rule at PaletteCard.vue:343-345 declaring the identical value.

**Proposed cure.** A producer change (owner edict 4), not a consumer patch: extend the metal register to `Badge` — `<Badge variant="outline" metal="gold">` — setting border from `--metal-stop-*`, glow from `--metal-glow-*`, and critically owning the `color: transparent` that the Badge's own `text-foreground` currently defeats (the prior seat's D-6 occlusion). That single glass-ui change removes both scoped rules, the redundant `border-gold` utility, the dead `.featured-badge__icon svg` reach, and the invisible infinite shimmer — once, for every consumer.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-16 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** cardRefs is a deep-reactive map of component public instances whose entries are never released, because the ref callback's `el &&` guard skips the unmount null.

**Mechanism.** Local hygiene — imperative child-instance coupling stored in the wrong reactivity primitive with no teardown.

**Mechanism.** An affordance designed for an asynchronous search wired to a synchronous emit. Vue never flushes a render with the flag set. Tranche A's Ad-13 requested this loading state; what landed reads as covered while being structurally impossible — worse than an acknowledged gap.

**Evidence.**

```
SearchFilterBar.vue:213-225 — `async function applyColorSearch()` sets searching=true, emits synchronously, and sets searching=false in `finally`, all within one tick with no `await`. probe.mjs sampled the button across 40 rAF frames with a MutationObserver on childList+subtree+attributes: { sawSpinner: false, sawDisabled: false, finalText: "Search" }. The dead markup is the Loader2 `animate-spin` at :102 and `disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:pointer-events-none` at :99.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe.mjs, read stateProbes.spinner.

**Proposed cure.** Either make the search genuinely asynchronous (which it should be — see D2-m5, the server-side colour-distance filter) and keep the register, or delete `searching`, the Loader2 branch and the disabled classes outright. No third option; a dead state is legacy code by another name.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-16 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The two state transitions this component owns are undesigned — skeleton→rows and pending↔approved are both hard v-if cuts, the latter a full-slab remount of the panel body — while the only motion present transitions width and height (layout-forcing properties) for 440ms.

VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:141 §6: "A scene swap preserves the specimen and changes the surrounding instrument. No full-slab remount hole".
```

**Reproduction.** navigate http://localhost:9000/#/admin/names and read getComputedStyle('.segmented-indicator').transition — width and height appear with 0.44s durations. Switch tabs and observe the body replaced with no transition. Reduced-motion behaviour is UNPROVEN: shots/reduced-motion-desktop/ contains 5 routes and admin-names is not among them.

**Proposed cure.** The list is one field whose membership changes, not two fields that swap: render a single row field keyed by item id and let the tab change its source, so skeleton→rows and pending↔approved become the same TransitionGroup on the same nodes using the tokenized effect curve (--animation-slide-*). **Defect.** The loading region's accessible name is discarded (aria-label on a role-less div), so the loading state announces 'Loading' three times without ever saying what; and the filter's result count — the thing that changes — has no live region, contrary to the navigation/announcement law.

**Mechanism.** ARIA applied to a generic element that cannot carry it; the owning status region never designated

**Evidence.**

```
AdminAuditPanel.vue:36 `<div v-if=… class="grid gap-2" aria-label="Loading audit log">` — no role, so the name is not exposed; AdminListSkeleton.vue:11-12 each carry their own `role="status" aria-label="Loading"`. The sibling does it right: AdminTagsPanel.vue:51-56 puts role=status + a specific label on the wrapper. Count span at line 26 has no aria-live. Measured live: the only live regions on the route are the error plate's role=alert and the COMPANION card's role=status. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5.1: 'in-route filter, tab, selection, or pagination → … announce changed result count/state through the owning status region'. PaginationBar.vue:17 does announce its page, so the grammar exists and the count was left out of it.
```

**Reproduction.** node AAP-probe5.mjs → errD1440light.liveRegions lists exactly two regions, neither of which is the entries count.

**Proposed cure.** role="status" on the loading wrapper with the children mute; aria-live="polite" on the count, which is the natural owning status region for the filter.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-19 · CHALLENGE-D

AdminAuditPanel.vue:30 Refresh has no `:disabled="audit.loading.value"`, and the filters stay live during load and during error — while the sibling does gate its action (AdminTagsPanel.vue:42 `:disabled="… || tagsApi.creating.value"`).
```

**Reproduction.** Source-level: the three guards (onUnmounted, AbortController/sequence token, :disabled) are absent at the coordinates above.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design: visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-02 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The "nothing to save" state is not designed, and the control that would express it is structurally unreachable. `:118 v-if="savedColorStrings.length > 0"` and `:138 :disabled="savedColorStrings.length === 0"` are complementary predicates on the same expression, so the disabled arm can never evaluate true. Worse than the dead branch: when the tray empties, the entire naming-and-commit region vanishes rather than resting, so the two-step grammar the interface teaches (collect → name and commit) deletes its own second step exactly when a new user is looking at it.

**Mechanism.** dead guard + state-by-removal — a defensive predicate was written against a condition its own mounting guard already excludes, and the state it pretended to cover was then expressed by unmounting the surface instead of resting it.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:118 vs :138. Live: with 12 colours the sole well button reports `disabled:false`; with 0 colours the empty-state outerHTML ends `<!--v-if--><!--v-if--><!--v-if-->` and `wellFocusables` is `[]`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 — "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value … are explicit"; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.5; owner edicts 2 (no masking fallbacks) and 3 (KISS).
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with an empty tray → no input, no button, `wellFocusables: []`. Populate the tray → both appear, `disabled:false`. There is no frame in which the button renders disabled.

**Proposed cure.** Delete `:disabled` — it is a lie — and keep the save region mounted and genuinely disabled at zero colours, with the count line reading `0 colors` rather than the header swapping to a different sentence. One region, one identity line, one resting action (PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.2). Falls out for free once D3-04's split lands.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design: visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D4-04 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The palette field has one empty state serving two incompatible meanings — 'you own no palettes' and 'your filter excludes everything' — and this component's commit is what routes users into the wrong one.

**Mechanism.** A predicate and its copy were bound to different quantities. The gate reads the filtered projection while the sentence describes the inventory, so a non-empty library renders as an empty one whenever a query excludes it — and the commit is the moment that converts 'one palette plus a stale filter' into 'the interface says I have none'.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:77-80 — `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` (filtered length) paired with `empty-text="No saved palettes yet."` (owned length). Measured, probe-D11-pass4.json §P2.filtered: with one saved palette and filter 'qqqzzz', cardCount 0, emptyText '· empty plate ·No saved palettes yet.Add colors above, then save the set.', headerBadge '(1 saved)'. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:186 reserves the mark for 'A true empty invitation'; PaletteCardGrid.vue:16 states in its own comment 'TRUE EMPTY is the EmptyState invitation ALONE'; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:114 gives filters their own contract — 'changed result count/state through the owning status region'. Frame: frames-D10/p2b-filter-no-results.png.
```

**Reproduction.** As D4-01 but observable before the save: seed one saved palette, load /#/palettes, type 'qqqzzz' into input[placeholder="Search your palettes..."], read the field. Script: probe-D11-pass4.mjs §P2.filtered.

**Proposed cure.** Two states, two copies, one predicate each. `empty` (nothing owned) keeps the plate mark and the invitation; `no-results` (filter excludes everything) names the query and offers to clear it. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-21 · CHALLENGE-L

```

**Reproduction.** Static: grep shows two uses of cssColor in the component and one consumer of safeFirstColor. The empty-string path (MixSourceSelector.vue:266) would send "" into safeCss(), i.e. into the pass-1 L-1 throw path, for a zero-colour palette.

package.json#exports = ./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize (no "." root). tsconfig.demo.json paths, checked against the filesystem: `@mkbabb/value.js` → ./dist/index.d.ts MISSING; `/parsing` → ./dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts MISSING; `/units` → ./dist/subpaths/units.d.ts MISSING; color/math/easing/transform/quantize EXIST. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-10 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** tsconfig.demo.json's `paths` block advertises a value.js public surface that package.json#exports does not have — three phantom keys pointing at files that do not exist, two real exports omitted — and its own header states the wrong map.

**Mechanism.** A hand-maintained second copy of a generated map — a false public surface advertised by the very config that is meant to be the trust boundary.

**Evidence.**

```
`node -p "Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports).join(' ')"` → `./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize` (7 keys, NO root "."). tsconfig.demo.json paths keys → `@mkbabb/value.js @mkbabb/value.js/color /parsing /math /easing /units /transform /quantize`. Phantoms: bare root (target ./dist/index.d.ts — absent; `ls dist/` shows subpaths/ + 3 chunks), /parsing (dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts — absent), /units (absent). Omitted: /css and /value (both real exports). The header asserts "the bare `.` root + the 7 subpath barrels … a CLOSED 8-key set". vite.config.ts:41-50 GENERATES its alias set from package.json#exports so it "can never drift"; tsconfig hand-maintains a second, drifted copy. Latent break: `import … from "@mkbabb/value.js"` typechecks via paths but has no Vite alias (no `.` export) → falls to node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 → ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. Currently zero such demo imports (grep → one prose mention at demo/shared/utils.ts:12).
```

**Reproduction.** Compare the two key sets above; `ls dist/subpaths/` shows color css easing math quantize transform value — no parsing, no units, and no dist/index.d.ts.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the six @mkbabb/value.js* paths entries. `tsc --traceResolution` proves TypeScript already resolves the whole map through Node self-name resolution honouring `exports` exactly as a real consumer does (measured on /css) — strictly more faithful than the paths shortcut. Removing them makes drift impossible rather than merely discouraged.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure underneath PaletteCard (modu` · L-46 · CHALLENGE-L

```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/mix, expose a palette card via MixSourceSelector, open its ⋯ menu and choose Delete → nothing happens, no diagnostic. MixSourceSelector.vue wires only @click of the 16 emits.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-24 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** demo/palettes and demo/shell are mutually dependent: the palette feature's port CONTRACT is parameterised by the shell's view vocabulary, while five shell/dock modules import the feature's session port. Neither tree can be lifted, tested or reasoned about alone.

**Mechanism.** The shell→feature edge is legitimate composition (a router mounts panes; a dock reads a session port). The feature→shell edge is not: the palette feature cannot state its own port contract without naming the shell's routes. The type-only import erases at runtime so this is not a load-time cycle, but it is a genuine cycle in the dependency lattice.

**Evidence.**

```
Feature→shell: demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:19 `import type { ViewId } from "../shell/useViewManager";` — and PalettePortsDeps (:33-41) declares `currentView: Ref<ViewId>` and `switchView: (id: ViewId) => void`. Shell→feature: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:70,71,76 (lazy panes — legitimate composition) plus demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:18, DockViewSelect.vue:8, layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:5, menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:13, menus/ProfileSection.vue:14 all importing SESSION_PORT_KEY.

**Reproduction.** grep -rn 'shell/' demo/palettes --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' → 1 hit (usePalettePorts.ts:19). grep -rn 'palettes/' demo/shell --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' → 8 hits, 5 of them SESSION_PORT_KEY.

**Proposed cure.** Invert the edge: the ports declare a FEATURE-owned vocabulary — `onNavigate: (intent: "library" | "browse") => void` — and the app root (which already owns both trees) adapts intents to ViewId. The feature stops knowing the shell exists; the shell keeps knowing the feature does. One direction, which is the point of a lattice.

All six operable seats share `focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/40`; the 40% alpha is the whole cause — the same token at full opacity clears the bar comfortably in both schemes.

### `D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-sys` · D-17 · D

**Defect.** NEW. The slug is not LTR-isolated. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6.1 requires 'CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance' to render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose; the pill has no isolation. index.html currently pins dir="ltr" document-wide, which is why nothing is visibly wrong today — but that attribute's own source comment describes it as the RTL seam, deliberately established so dir="rtl" flips the document. The moment it does, an un-isolated hyphen-segmented slug reorders against surrounding prose.

**Mechanism.** bidi isolation — a latent RTL defect held harmless only by a document-level dir pin that the repo explicitly intends to flip.

### `D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-sys` · D-13 · D

### `D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-sys` · D-10/D-11 · D

**Defect.** Motion and type are both declared in channels the system does not read. Six controls declare `active:scale-95`/`active:scale-[0.98]` while their `transition-property` list contains no `transform`, so the press scale snaps instead of animating; a 50ms magic `setTimeout` sequences the component's own state against another component's close animation; and the Login control renders Fira Code at weight 700 where the closed type matrix assigns controls Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold.

**Mechanism.** ad-hoc motion + closed-type-matrix violation — intentions stated in classes the cascade does not act on. (Note: the scale animates `transform`, which is compositor-only, so this is NOT a layout-thrash defect — the defect is that it never animates at all.)

**Evidence.**

```
MOTION — MEASURED (probes/psb-probe.mjs): login `transitionProperty: "color, background-color, border-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color, fill, stroke, --tw-gradient-*"`, `transitionDuration: "0.2s"` — no `transform` in the list, while the class at :73 declares `active:scale-95`. Same shape at :84, :91, :98, :106, :113. Magic delay: :176 `setTimeout(() => { slugEditMode.value = true; … }, 50)` with the comment 'Delay to let the Popover fully close' — an untokenized constant racing a token-driven exit. TYPE — MEASURED: login `{ fontFamily: "Fira Code", fontWeight: "700", fontSize: "16.4px" }`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4 type-jurisdiction table — 'control or label, including dropdown options | text-small | Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold'; Fira Code is reserved for 'value, code, or provenance'. §6 requires spatial continuity to use 'one producer-owned glass-ui spring register'.
```

**Reproduction.** node probes/psb-probe.mjs — `login`/`dots` blocks, fields transitionProperty, fontFamily, fontWeight.

**Proposed cure.** Motion belongs to the producer's spring register, not to per-consumer `active:scale` + `transition-colors` pairs that silently disagree; the 50ms delay is a sequencing bug that disappears once one component owns the open/close state instead of two racing each other. Type: the control consumes the `text-small` rung from the matrix — the mono family is for the slug value, never for the button that opens it.

```

```

Demo-wide split: 5 SAFE_ACCENT_KEY injection sites vs 6 useSafeAccentFn sites.
```

Contrast consequence is a HYPOTHESIS — reproducing the dialog needs an admin token and a non-empty roster, unavailable in this checkout; direction of error is unfavourable (certified against a darker plate, rendered on a lighter one) but magnitude is unmeasured.
