### `CHALLENGE-C — assume the implementation is defective; find t` · D-8 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The coarse-pointer touch-target extension is media-gated on `pointer: coarse` — the PRIMARY input mechanism — rather than `any-pointer: coarse`, so hybrid devices (fine primary + touchscreen) get no 44px hit extension while the JS gate is armed against them.

**Mechanism.** wrong media feature for the question being asked (capability vs primacy) — the CSS gate and the JS gate disagree about which devices are touchable

**Evidence.**

```
ComponentSliders.vue:345 `@media (pointer: coarse)`. Media Queries Level 4 defines `pointer` as reporting the pointing device "that is the primary input mechanism" and `any-pointer` as reporting any available input mechanism. The file's own comment at :342-344 sells the choice as a virtue — "Gated on `pointer: coarse` (the input device), never viewport width" — but the device is not what `pointer` reports; the primary device is. Measured presence of the pseudo (probe.mjs): desktop beforeH "auto"/content "none"; 390x844 coarse beforeH "44px"/content '""'.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE for the hybrid case — labelled HYPOTHESIS. Chromium's touch emulation couples the two features (probe.mjs/probe8.mjs measured pointerCoarse:true AND anyPointerCoarse:true under hasTouch:true), so the divergence could not be isolated in this harness. The spec reading is not a hypothesis; only the device-class consequence is.

**Proposed cure.** Use `@media (any-pointer: coarse)` — one word, and the CSS gate then agrees with the JS gate about which devices are touchable. Under D-1's cure both predicates become per-event and this collapses into a non-question.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/picker/cont` · C-9 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The spectrum drag costs materially more per frame than the L-slider drag that the repo's §6.2 oracle gates, and the spectrum path has no gate at all. `getBoundingClientRect()` is called inside the rAF callback every frame after the previous frame mutated the dot's inline style — a forced synchronous layout per frame.

**Mechanism.** The plate drives the full app-wide colour fan-out per frame (that part is ColorPicker/atmosphere territory) and adds a forced layout of its own. The §6.2 oracle exercises the slider path only, so the more expensive path is unmeasured.

**Evidence.**

```
SpectrumCanvas.vue:114 (rect read inside the rAF callback). Quieter session (probe/probe3.mjs, in-page PointerEvent dispatch at rAF cadence, no protocol RTT): IDLE p50 17.1ms → SPECTRUM-DRAG p50 45.0ms, longTasks [50,52]. Loaded session, both paths back to back at identical cadence (probe/probe9.mjs): IDLE p50 50.4 / longOver50 0; SLIDER-DRAG p50 58.3 / longOver50 30; SPECTRUM-DRAG p50 66.6 / longOver50 44. Marginal over same-session idle: slider +7.9ms, spectrum +16.2ms. The component's own arithmetic is not the cost (probe/probe4.mjs: 0–0.4ms synchronous per pointerdown in the default space).
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/picker-spectrumcanvas/probe/probe9.mjs against http://localhost:9000/. CAVEAT stated plainly: dev-server (unbundled) on a contended host with three other mega-tranche seats running, so the absolute numbers are NOT comparable to the built-bundle §6.2 gate. The within-session slider-vs-spectrum comparison is the controlled result.

**Proposed cure.** Read the plate rect once at pointerdown and invalidate it on resize/scroll (a ResizeObserver already fits the component's lifecycle) instead of per frame; then add a spectrum-drag case to e2e/smoke/perf/drag-frame-budget.spec.ts so the number is defended rather than merely observed.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/picker/cont` · C-12 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The touch gate deactivates mid-gesture on drags longer than 3 s, and two owners write the same inline `touch-action` property.

**Mechanism.** (a) The activation timer measures time since the last pointerdown, not time since the last interaction, so a sustained drag times out under the finger. (b) Vue's patchStyle only re-applies values that changed between binding objects, so an imperative clobber can survive a re-render whose computed value did not change.

**Evidence.**

```
SpectrumCanvas.vue:144-146 calls `spectrumGate.resetTimer()` ONLY on pointerdown, never on move. The gate's deactivate delay defaults to 3000ms (`l(a = 3e3)` in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useTouchGate-B4mzQcHJ.js), whose `x()` flips isActive false and clears the outline. Separately, that module's `y()`/`x()` write `el.style.touchAction` imperatively while useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:41-43 writes touchAction reactively through Vue's :style on the same element.
```

**Reproduction.** (a) By read of the two files — a >3s touch drag drops `touch-gate-active` and re-arms the gate for the next press. (b) NOT REPRODUCED — isTouchDevice is false on the desktop harness. Labelled a HYPOTHESIS.

**Proposed cure.** Call `resetTimer()` from the move path (or `suppressDeactivate(true)` for the drag's duration) so the gate measures interaction, not press age. For the dual writer: give `touch-action` exactly one owner — either the gate owns it imperatively and it leaves `spectrumStyle`, or the computed owns it and the gate is told not to write. Never both.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPic` · C-12 · CHALLENGE-C

```
ColorPicker.vue:227 `/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}$/` — valid CSS hex is 3, 4, 6 or 8 digits. Measured: `"#12345" NOT-OK(result)` and `"#1234567" NOT-OK(result)`. Both reach parseAndSetColor, fail, and trip flashParseError() (useColorParsing.ts:54-57, :84-86).

**Proposed cure.** `/^#([0-9a-fA-F]{3,4}|[0-9a-fA-F]{6}|[0-9a-fA-F]{8})$/`.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-18 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** 12.15% of the product's dominant instrument is a hue-independent black wedge carrying no discriminable chroma, identical in light, dark and forced-colors — and in dark mode that wedge abuts the card at 3.07:1, so it reads as a hole.

**Mechanism.** A direct consequence of the HSV S×V parameterisation (D-01): as v→0 every hue collapses to the same pixels. A perceptual parameterisation spends its area on distinguishable colours. The identical value across schemes is the finding's other half — the plate does nothing at all for dark mode.

**Evidence.**

```
probe/SPCD-pixels.json — 11,470 samples on a 3px grid inside the plate: fraction with max(R,G,B) < 32 is **0.1215**, byte-identical across light, dark and forced-colors. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT §1 — "Every element earns its scale, interval, boundary and material from its job relative to the local protagonist."
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/SPCD-pixels.mjs — decodes the element capture in-page and counts near-black pixels over the plate rect in each scheme.

**Proposed cure.** Subsumed by D-01: a selected-space projection (e.g. OKLCh L×C at fixed H) distributes area over perceptually distinct colours and has no degenerate wedge. If HSV is ever retained deliberately, the wedge must be an argued proportion, not a side effect.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt · demo/scenes/Confi` · D-15 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** NEW in this pass. `fmt()` ignores the declared `SliderDef.step` and formats by a heuristic on the VALUE, so the readout changes shape as the value moves: knobs sitting at exactly 0 render "0" beside neighbours rendering three decimals, and dragging any knob whose domain contains 0 makes the readout jump 5 glyphs → 1 → 5 inside a `truncate` inline row.

**Mechanism.** Precision decided by value shape rather than by the control's declared resolution — the declaration is right there on the SliderDef and is unused.

**Evidence.**

```
ConfigSliderPane.vue:84-86 — `Number.isInteger(v) ? String(v) : v.toFixed(3)`; `def.step` declared at :31 and never read. BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.color.satShift === 0 and .brightnessShift === 0 (verified against the dist), so both render "0" while measured live neighbours render `Body Radius 0.220`, `Sat Radius 0.082`, `Orbit Radius 0.170`, `Eccentricity 0.050`, `Smooth K 0.050`. Same for Warp, Noise Amp, Pulse Amp, Attraction. Conversely a step-100 knob is "2500" only because the value is incidentally integral.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/blob → scroll to Color → Saturation reads "0" while every sibling reads three decimals; drag it one step either way and watch the readout width jump.

**Proposed cure.** `const dp = Math.max(0, -Math.floor(Math.log10(def.step))); v.toFixed(dp)`. Precision then always equals what the control can express and the readout width is constant across the whole domain — one line, and it deletes the heuristic rather than tuning it.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/scenes/abou` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The space-change handler is typed `any`, does a read-modify-write on an uncached `defineModel` computed, and sends a whole-model snapshot into a Partial-merging setter — a second, divergent write path for the same action the picker performs correctly with one field.

**Mechanism.** The pane is wired through the router as a snapshot-passing v-model instead of injecting COLOR_MODEL_KEY, which is already provided app-wide and already injected inside this very subtree (ColorSpaceSelector.vue:142) — so a one-field intent is expressed as a whole-model overwrite of a possibly-stale copy.

**Evidence.**

```
AboutPane.vue:25 `@update:model-value="(colorSpace: any) => { model = { ...model, selectedColorSpace: colorSpace }; }"` with `defineModel<ColorModel>({required:true})` at :72 and NO local shallowRef cache (owner edict 7 names both the hazard and the cure). Prop lands at usePaneRouter.ts:148-151 → useColorPipeline.ts:59-70 whose contract is `Partial<ColorModel>`. The correct sibling: ColorPicker.vue:43 `@update:model-value="(colorSpace: any) => updateModel({ selectedColorSpace: colorSpace })"`.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE for the clobber — labelled a HYPOTHESIS. Probed and NOT reproduced: node scratchpad/about-probe5.mjs → `--- change space via ABOUT dropdown --- after: url …space=oklch… aboutTrigger "OKLCh" pickerTrigger "OKLCh"` vs `--- change space via PICKER dropdown --- after:` identical. Real pointer events land in separate tasks so props always flush between them. The `any`, the missing shallowRef cache, and the dual write path are CONFIRMED by source.

**Proposed cure.** Inject COLOR_MODEL_KEY and call `updateModel({ selectedColorSpace })`. The defineModel and the router's modelValue/onUpdate:modelValue prop pair (usePaneRouter.ts:146-152) both disappear — one write path, no snapshot, no `any`, no stale window to reason about.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/scenes/abou` · C-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `:key="model.selectedColorSpace"` is load-bearing correctness disguised as an optimisation: Markdown.vue loads its doc only in onMounted and never watches its `module` prop, so removing the key freezes the guide on the first space forever.

**Mechanism.** Reactivity implemented as remount — the child's data is a function of a mount event rather than of its input, so the parent must destroy it to update it.

**Evidence.**

```
AboutPane.vue:52 `:key="model.selectedColorSpace"`; Markdown.vue:58-62 `loadDocs` is called only from :69-71 `onMounted`; whole-file read confirms no `watch(() => module, …)` exists. Shipped consequences: every space change discards the rendered doc, flashes the skeleton (Markdown.vue:3-9), re-runs the TreeWalker pass, and loses position in a 7523px scroller (measured: `about-card scroll meta: {"scrollHeight":7523,"clientHeight":830}`).
```

**Reproduction.** NONE at runtime (the failing repro requires deleting AboutPane.vue:52, which this seat may not edit). CONFIRMED by source: no watcher on `module` exists anywhere in Markdown.vue.

**Proposed cure.** Subsumed by C-1's cure: a watchEffect on `module` makes the doc a function of its input, after which the `:key` carries no meaning and can be deleted safely.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/scenes/abou` · K-9 · CHALLENGE-C

**Evidence.**

```

NOTE: this is currently latent — no expression in the 11 documents fails to parse today, so the red ink is not on screen; it is one typo away and K-5 shows nothing would catch it.

**Proposed cure.** Pass `errorColor` from a token (`errorColor: "var(--destructive)"` is accepted by KaTeX since it is written straight into the inline style), or — better, once K-5's dev-throw lands — the error surface stops existing in production entirely and the point is moot.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (pass 4) — demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane` · Q-6 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The pane is not a scroll-confined inspector although canon names it one twice: overscroll-behavior auto (scroll chaining live), scrollbar-gutter auto (no reserved gutter), scroll-padding-top auto (nothing accounts for the 107.4px sticky header), no region role or accessible name — on a port that hides 73.4% of its content.

**Mechanism.** The port was hand-rolled as a class named for a feature it does not implement (`pane-scroll-fade`, maskImage none) instead of composed from the producer's FadingScroll, so three of the four confinement arms were never considered.

**Evidence.**

```
probe2 computed on `.pane-scroll-fade`: {overscrollBehavior: "auto", scrollbarGutter: "auto", scrollPaddingTop: "auto", scrollbarWidth: "thin", maskImage: "none", role: null, ariaLabel: null, hiddenPct: 73.4}. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1 gives both consumer routes 'scroll-confined advanced disclosure' and §7 (line 214) repeats 'a scroll-confined inspector'; docs/tranches/V/megatranche/design/layout-gestalt-worker-o.md:535 spells the owed recipe `min-block-size:0; overflow-block:auto; overscroll-behavior-block:contain; scrollbar-gutter:stable`. The utility already ships: glass-ui components.css `.overscroll-contain{overscroll-behavior:contain}`.
```

**Reproduction.** node probes/pass-4/csp-d4-probe2.mjs "#/blob" 1440 900 light  → the `scroll` block prints all four computed values.

**Proposed cure.** `<FadingScroll axis="y" :aria-label>` under `Configurator scrollMode="auto"`, which brings the feather, the non-supporting-engine fallback and the region naming in one component; the containment arms (overscroll-behavior-block: contain, scrollbar-gutter: stable) belong on the producer's port per worker-O G-2, not as a fourth local CSS block.

Filed MINOR because the home is the shell, not this component — but it is a library-structure finding on this axis: ConfigSliderPane is the only pane whose SOLE routes are right-slot routes, so it is the one component the split renders unreachable at load.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured live at 390×844 (isMobile, hasTouch): hash "#/blob?space=lab&color=lab(92%25+88.8+20+/+82.7%25)", configConsolePresent false, sliderRows 0, bodyTextLen 68, firstHeading null — the Picker pane renders instead. Corroborated by the visual matrix: REPORT.json bodyTextLength 69 mobile vs 713 desktop for the same route; shots/safari-mobile-light/blob.png shows the Picker pane with the tab strip parked on "Picker". Mechanism at demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:178-184 — `mobile` returns `desktopLeft` unless `viewManager.mobilePaneIndex.value === 1`, and navigation sets no pane index.
```

**Reproduction.** Navigate chromium to http://localhost:9000/#/blob at 390×844 with isMobile:true — document.querySelector('.config-console') → null, document.body.innerText.length → 68

**Proposed cure.** Derive `mobilePaneIndex` from the route's slot assignment at navigation: when the entered view declares `cfg.right !== null` and the entry was by URL, the mobile slot IS the right one. One source of truth for "which pane the URL means", in usePaneRouter, not two that must be kept in sync by the user tapping a tab.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-7 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** AboutPane is the last prop-drilled pane in a shell that was deliberately transposed to ambient injection, and the two paths carry different values: the prop cssColor is alpha-bearing while the injected CSS_COLOR_KEY is alpha-stripped, with the default model at 82.7% alpha.

Latent correctness fault, not a current rendering defect.

**Evidence.**

```
usePaneRouter.ts:146-152 hand-builds `{ modelValue: model.value, "onUpdate:modelValue": …, cssColor: deps.cssColor() }` inside an untyped `Record<string, unknown>`. usePaneRouter.ts:135-137 records the picker's opposite treatment: "S.W2 · W2-1: the picker no longer takes the model as a prop — it injects the ONE pipeline (COLOR_MODEL_KEY) App provides." AboutPane's own comment at :7-19 confirms its subtree already reads that ambient pipeline; ColorSpaceSelector.vue:139 injects COLOR_MODEL_KEY, ColorNutritionLabel.vue:188 injects CSS_COLOR_KEY. The divergence: App.vue:340 passes `cssColor: () => cssColor.value` (alpha-bearing) while App.vue:271 does `provide(CSS_COLOR_KEY, cssColorOpaque)` (alpha-stripped). Default model is `lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.70%)` (color-model.ts:43), α=0.827 — confirmed live, REPORT.json safari-desktop-light /#/ records boot URL `?space=lab&color=lab(92%25+88.8+20+/+82.7%25)`. ```

**Reproduction.** NONE for a visible symptom — labelled a latent fault. The value divergence is proven statically by App.vue:271 vs :340 plus the α=0.827 default measured in the live boot URL.

**Proposed cure.** Drop modelValue/cssColor from usePaneRouter.rightProps; let AboutPane inject COLOR_MODEL_KEY and CSS_COLOR_KEY the way the picker already does. rightProps then collapses to the palettes case alone and the shell stops knowing any pane's prop shape — state flows one direction, App provides and panes inject, so no two routes for one value can disagree about alpha.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure: module boundaries, ownershi` · L-7 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The Select handlers are typed against reka-ui's `AcceptableValue` — glass-ui's internal substrate, a devDependency-only package — rather than glass-ui's own emitted `SelectionValue`. The declared domain is strictly wider than the emitter's codomain and the gap is bridged by an unconditional `String(v) as X` coercion.

**Mechanism.** AuroraPane.vue:79 `atoms.harmony = String(v) as AuroraHarmony` is a masking fallback against cases glass-ui cannot emit (String(null)->"null", String({})->"[object Object]"), while the case that CAN occur (SelectionValue includes number) is silently accepted — String(3) as AuroraHarmony writes a garbage atom with no guard. Typing against the true string|number would force that branch into the open.

**Evidence.**

```
AuroraPane.vue:25 `import type { AcceptableValue } from "reka-ui";` — package.json lists reka-ui under devDependencies ("^2.9"); the only runtime dependencies are @mkbabb/glass-ui and @mkbabb/keyframes.js. glass-ui emits its own type: dist/components/select/Select.vue.d.ts `export interface SelectEmits { "update:modelValue": [value: SelectionValue]; … }` with dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts `export type SelectionValue = string | number;`. reka-ui's is wider: dist/index3.d.ts:231 `type AcceptableValue = string | number | bigint | Record<string, any> | null;`. Four demo files do this (AuroraPane.vue:25, GradientVisualizer.vue:28, MixConfigBar.vue:15, GenerateControls.vue:33). `grep -l SelectionValue node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/*.d.ts` returns NOTHING — the correct type is unnameable by a consumer.
```

**Reproduction.** grep -rn 'from "reka-ui"' demo  -> four files; grep -l SelectionValue node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/*.d.ts -> no output.

**Proposed cure.** COORDINATION PACKET P-2 to glass-ui: re-export `SelectionValue` from @mkbabb/glass-ui/select (it is already the declared emit type but is not on the public surface). Then all four handlers type against it and narrow explicitly (`typeof v === "string"`) instead of coercing, and the reka-ui reach disappears.

### `design (visual truth · state coverage · motion · design-syst` · N-6 · design (visual truth · state coverage · motion · design-system boundary · proportion/seat law)

**Defect.** The italic caption face clips its own terminal glyph: the value box is sized to the glyph advance width and carries `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: clip`, so italic ink painting past the advance is sliced. Layout reports no overflow, so no scrollWidth check can detect it.

**Mechanism.** `overflow: hidden` clips PAINT, not just layout. A box sized to the advance width of an italic run cannot contain the run's ink, and `text-overflow: clip` slices rather than ellipsises. An upright control face has no right-side ink overhang, which is why the producer's own `text-dropdown` never exhibits this.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured (pass2/probes/D-aurora-probe2.mjs): value span `overflow: hidden`, `text-overflow: clip`, `font-style: italic`; clientWidth === scrollWidth (74 === 74 for 'Scattered') while getBoundingClientRect().width = 73.67. Reproduced at DPR 2 in pass2/frames/D-probe-zoom200.png ('Scattereᴅ', 'Smootһ', 'Driftin').
```

**Reproduction.** node pass2/probes/D-aurora-probe2.mjs → parts[1] = { text:'Scattered', cw:74, sw:74, overflow:'hidden', textOverflow:'clip', fontStyle:'italic', rect.w:73.67 }. Then open pass2/frames/D-rows-3x.png.

**Proposed cure.** Closed by C-1's cure — deleting `text-caption` removes the italic, and the producer's upright control face fits its own box. No overflow/padding hack should be added.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/shell/PaneSlot.` · PS-9 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** PaneSlot replaces the entire <main> content with no accessible-swap contract: no role, no aria-live, no aria-busy during the 58–109 ms swap, no focus target. AT users get no announcement that the application view changed.

**Mechanism.** The component that owns the swap owns no part of the swap's accessible semantics; a11y was treated as pane-content concern rather than as an implementation property of the mounting mechanism.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:111-129 is the complete template — no wrapper element, no role, no aria-* attribute of any kind; the pane drops straight under `<main aria-label="Color tool panes">` (App.vue:47). MEASURED (PS-probe6.mjs section C, after switchView("gradient")): `{"liveRegionsInMain":1,"mainHasBusy":false,"paneWrapperRoles":["(none)","(none)"],"focusMoved":false,"activeAfter":"BODY/…"}`. Labels for the announcement already exist and are unused for this purpose: viewSchema.ts:72-74 `leftLabel` / `rightLabel`. Honest negative: PaneSlot renders no interactive elements, so it contributes 0 of the visual REPORT's 60 smallTapTargets and 18 namelessButtons rows.
```

**Reproduction.** node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/PS-probe6.mjs, section C. Output pasted above.

**Proposed cure.** Bind the swap semantics at the root level per edict 5 — no new wrapper component and no new shared dir. Bind `aria-busy` on the existing `.pane-wrapper` in App.vue to the predicate "committed key ≠ incoming key" (PaneSlot can expose it alongside PS-1's inversion), and add one shell-owned polite live region announcing the arrived pane from `currentConfig.leftLabel` / `rightLabel`, which viewSchema.ts already carries.

VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4: 'control or label, including dropdown options → text-small → Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold'; 'Fraunces owns display/identity'. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 13 restates it.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-14 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Direction and bidi: every offset is physical, and the field renders a CSS-colour string with no LTR isolation.

**Mechanism.** Physical-axis geometry plus an un-isolated LTR technical value inside a container that may be RTL — under RTL a value beginning with `#` or `/` reorders on screen while the model keeps the original bytes, so what the user reads is not what the parser receives.

**Evidence.**

```
ColorInput.vue physical offsets: `pr-9` (:18), `right-2` (:35), `.send-btn { right: 0.25rem }` (:337), `.error-badge { right: 0.5rem }` (:350), `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, …)` (:300). No `dir` attribute and no `unicode-bidi: isolate` on the value (measured attribute list: data-v-…, contenteditable, role, aria-label, class). Combined with measured `textAlign: center`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1: 'chrome, navigation and layout — logical inline/block direction follows the document' and 'CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance — render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose.'
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — hypothesis for the visual reordering (no RTL locale is currently reachable in-app). The physical-offset inventory and the absence of any dir/unicode-bidi attribute are directly verified from source and from the live attribute enumeration.

**Proposed cure.** Logical properties throughout (`pe-9`, `inset-inline-end`), and `dir="ltr"` on the value element — which glass-ui `Input` makes trivial. Drop `text-align: center` for inline-start alignment; a technical LTR value centred in a possibly-RTL container is the worst of both.

**Defect.** MINOR: `Dock.vue` is a two-root SFC whose second root is unrelated band chrome; that chrome currently renders a red dev-error string in the nav band on every route, clipped at the viewport edge on mobile.

**Evidence.**

```
Dock.vue:128 opens the dock wrapper; Dock.vue:293 mounts `<DockStatusLamp />` as a sibling root — multi-root disables attribute fallthrough. ```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/ at 390 and 1440; query `nav.dock-band` leaf text nodes — one is the lamp string with the colours above. Script: dockprobe2.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Mount DockStatusLamp from the band (App.vue's `<nav class="dock-band">`), which is already its documented positioning context, and let Dock.vue return one root. The lamp's mobile clipping then becomes the band's problem to solve once, at the right altitude.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-12 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** `.dock-layer-grid` is a phantom class with zero CSS rules; because it sets no `position`, the hidden/leaving sub-layer resolves its containing block against the OUTER dock face and covers the dock's live controls for 260ms.

**Mechanism.** A container named "grid" that is a block box; its children carry `grid-area: 1/1` inherited from the producer's `.dock-layer` rule, which is inert in block layout. Absolute positioning then escapes to the nearest positioned ancestor — the outer `.dock-face` — so the leaving face spans the Back control and the toggle, overhanging its own container by 65px left and 53px right, `visibility: visible` at `opacity: 0` for 260ms. glass-ui carves a special `.is-press-keepalive` rule for exactly this hazard on its OWN layers; this consumer gets no such protection.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured computed style: `{display:"block", position:"static", gridTemplateColumns:"none", overflow:"visible"}`. `grep -rn "dock-layer-grid"` across the repo and `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/` returns exactly two hits, both in this file (:91, :101). `offsetParentOfInactive: "DIV.dock-face is-active"`. Rects: container 634.0/184.0; active sub-layer 634.0/184.0; inactive 569.0/302.0; leaving 499.0/443.0 (t=32..246). glass-ui `layers.css`: `.dock-layer:not(.is-active){position:absolute;inset:0}`, `.dock-layer.is-active{position:relative}`, `.dock-layer.is-leaving{opacity:0;visibility:visible}`.
```

**Reproduction.** WebKit 1440×900, open Tools, `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.dock-layer-grid'))` → display block / position static; then read `offsetParent` of the non-`is-active` child → the outer `.dock-face`.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the class. A real `<DockLayer>` inside a real `<DockCrossfade>` gets `position: relative` on its host by construction, so the containing block is correct without a consumer-side container at all.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-15 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** A consumer speaks the producer's private layer vocabulary: `dock-layer` / `is-active` / `is-leaving` are applied to arbitrary child components, silently inheriting glass-ui's entire internal layer contract including its morph stagger rule.

**Mechanism.** Private CSS adopted as a public contract. Because this pseudo-layer nests inside the REAL `.dock-face` layer, the five ActionButtons are staggered as children of this fake layer while the whole run is already staggered above — a nested opacity/scale multiplication no one designed. ```

Measured: the ActionToolbar root carries `flex items-center justify-around flex-1 dock-layer is-active` in the live DOM.
```

**Reproduction.** HYPOTHESIS for the rendered double-stagger — I confirmed the selector applies and the classes are present in the live DOM, but did not capture a frame mid-`[data-morphing]`. To close: sample child `opacity`/`scale` during a dock expand while the action-bar layer is active.

**Proposed cure.** Stop hand-writing producer classes. `<DockLayer>` faces inside `<DockCrossfade>` get the packaging by construction — the API exists precisely so consumers never touch `.dock-layer`.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-16 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The 'certified ink' is certified twice against two different rungs, from a prop whose name asserts it is the raw opaque colour. The D6 rationale both twins quote ('each ink certifies against the surface it actually composites over') is structurally defeated, and in dark mode the live-colour identity renders at 11% of the picked chroma.

**Mechanism.** a pre-certified value passed into a certifier under a name that claims it is raw; monotone walks compose so the second certification can only move further from the pick

**Evidence.**

```
Dock.vue:35 `const safeAccent = inject(SAFE_ACCENT_KEY)!`; Dock.vue:209 `:css-color-opaque="safeAccent"`. keys.ts:9 SAFE_ACCENT_KEY: InjectionKey<ComputedRef<string>>. useContrastSafeColor.ts:301-311 — safeAccentCss = certifyAccentInk(cssColorOpaque, surfaceLightnessNow("resting", …)). MobileMenuDropdown.vue:16-24 declares the prop `cssColorOpaque` and computes safeCss(cssColorOpaque) against surface "floating" (useSafeAccentFn("floating"), :23). So the composition is certifyAccentInk(certifyAccentInk(pick, resting), floating). Measured dark arm: picked accent oklch(0.470927 0.188343 9.834023) C=0.188; rendered pill AND --accent-live oklch(0.958322 0.021053 9.834023) C=0.021 → 11% of the picked chroma. Frame: frames/D-390-dark-loggedin-open.png shows an off-white capsule.
```

**Reproduction.** Mechanism: read Dock.vue:35,209 + useContrastSafeColor.ts:301-311 + MobileMenuDropdown.vue:16-24. Dark-chroma measurement: node frames/mmd-probe.mjs → logged-in-dark.menu.pill.color and .accentLive. The HARM of double-certification is a HYPOTHESIS — measured delta at the boot seed is ZERO (pill.color === --accent-live exactly), and I did not enumerate a pick for which resting requires a walk and floating does not.

**Proposed cure.** Stop passing a certified colour into a certifier: the component should receive the RAW cssColorOpaque (CSS_COLOR_KEY is already injected at Dock.vue:19) and certify once against the floating rung — which is exactly what the comment claims and what D6 requires. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-9 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Quadruple-redundant null defence over a schema that forbids null; the component's own v-if existence guard is unreachable dead code, proven by exhaustive enumeration of all nine VIEW_MAP entries.

**Mechanism.** Masking fallbacks stacked because no layer trusts the one below it — edict 2 (no masking fallbacks) and edict 3 (KISS, no contrivance). The invariant the guards grope for (a right pane implies a right label) is expressible in the type system and was instead encoded four times at runtime, incorrectly.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:73-74 declares `leftLabel: string` (never null) and `rightLabel: string | null`. Four guards over that: (1) Dock.vue:200 `?? ''` on leftLabel — dead, schema is non-null; (2) PaneSegmentedControl.vue:22 `leftLabel: string | null` — fabricated nullability wider than the schema; (3) :31 `leftLabel ?? ""` — dead, Dock already coerced; (4) :3 `v-if="leftLabel && rightLabel"` — dead. Enumeration of VIEW_MAP: picker/palettes/browse/extract/mix/generate/gradient/blob all have right!==null AND rightLabel!==null; atmosphere alone has right=null AND rightLabel=null. So right===null iff rightLabel===null, and the only view that could fire guard 4 is already suppressed one level up by Dock.vue:197 `v-if="…right !== null"`.
```

**Reproduction.** python3 regex walk of demo/shell/viewSchema.ts printing right/rightLabel per entry (pasted in the report §D-9) — nine rows, perfect pairing. Then read Dock.vue:197 and PaneSegmentedControl.vue:3.

**Proposed cure.** Express the invariant structurally: make PaneConfig a discriminated union — `{ right: null } | { right: RightPane; rightLabel: string }` — which deletes all four guards at once and makes the unreachable branch unrepresentable. Note the design gap the dead code was reaching for: were a view ever to have right!==null with rightLabel===null, Dock's wrapper would render, the component's v-if would suppress the control, and the user would face an empty div in the dock aperture with NO way to reach the second pane. Subsumed by D-4.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-10 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Tap target measures 49.09 x 26.25 CSS px at 390w — clearing the WCAG 2.2 AA floor by only 2.25px and failing the 44x44 AAA/HIG floor by 17.75px; the component's own override is what trims it, and it evaded the audit because the sweep's tripwire is <24px.

**Mechanism.** Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation were collapsed into a single shrink. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5 law 7: 'Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities. Accessibility floors do not require bloated visible chrome.' The override commits the same error in the opposite direction — shrinking the target to shrink the glyph.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured tab rect at 390px: 49.09 x 26.25 CSS px. WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 (24x24) — passes by 2.25px on the short axis. WCAG 2.2 AAA SC 2.5.5 / Apple HIG (44x44) — fails by 17.75px. REPORT.json smallTapTargets threshold is <24 (it flags w:160/h:23, 22x22, 12x24), which is exactly why this never surfaced across 60 captures; a python3 filter of all mobile rows for pane labels (Picker/About/Palettes/…) returns zero hits. Contribution of the override: producer default below 640 is padding 0.25rem 0.625rem (4x10px); the override is 0.25rem 0.375rem (4x6px) — 8px narrower per tab — plus a 0.82px font-size cut shrinking the line box.
```

**Reproduction.** node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/psc-probe2.mjs (run A) → tab {w:49.09, h:26.25}. Absence from the sweep: python3 filter over REPORT.json results for matrix startswith 'safari-mobile' and label in the pane-label set → paneHits=[] on all 30 rows.

**Proposed cure.** Separate the quantities: keep the optical rung on the rung ladder and give the seat an invisible target floor (min-block-size 44px via padding-block or a ::before hit area) at the producer level. Also raise the audit tripwire to flag <44 as a warning tier so near-floor targets stop hiding behind a 24px binary. Subsumed by D-4.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-12 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Unchecked numeric cast at the wrapper's translation seam, over a model that is a position rather than a pane identity.

**Mechanism.** The wrapper exists to translate between a string-keyed producer model and a positional consumer model, and the `as` assertion is where the two type systems are forced to agree without validation. The deeper fault is that the model encodes a POSITION (0=left, 1=right) rather than a pane identity — which is also why D-1's RTL failure is possible at all, since position is direction-dependent and identity is not. The inline arrow additionally allocates a new handler each render, purely because the translation exists.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/PaneSegmentedControl.vue:11 — `@update:model-value="(v) => emit('update:modelValue', Number(v) as 0 | 1)"`. The producer's model type is `string` (__VLS_ModelProps = { modelValue: string } in SegmentedTabs.vue.d.ts); the consumer's is `0 | 1` (PaneSegmentedControl.vue:21,27). Options are built as `{ value: "0" }` / `{ value: "1" }` at :31-32. The emitted value flows straight into viewManager.mobilePaneIndex at Dock.vue:202.
```

**Reproduction.** Read demo/shell/PaneSegmentedControl.vue:9-11 and :30-33 against node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/tabs/SegmentedTabs.vue.d.ts (__VLS_ModelProps, SegmentedTabOption.value: string). Static — no runtime out-of-domain emission observed, so the out-of-domain path is a HYPOTHESIS; the type-system hole itself is directly evidenced.

**Proposed cure.** Subsumed by D-4: the route split replaces the positional index with a route identity, dissolving both the cast and the wrapper that requires it. Do not fix by adding a runtime guard — that would add a masking fallback (edict 2) to a seam that is being deleted.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-24 · CHALLENGE-L

**Mechanism.** Mechanism H (generalizes pass 1's L-11 SUB_LAYER_CROSSFADE_MS=260): glass-ui owns the design-token half of timing (--duration-fast/slow/panel) and the demo consumes it correctly in CSS, but the JavaScript half has no home at all, so every site that must coordinate with a CSS duration copies a number and hopes. ```

ColorInput.vue:256 `setTimeout(() => { modeTransition.value = false; }, 300)` gates .color-input-mode-flash (:312-314) whose animation runs `var(--duration-slow)`, measured live off document.documentElement as {"durationSlow":"0.45s","durationPanel":"0.55s","durationFast":"0.2s"} — 300ms JS vs 450ms CSS, the animation is cut short on every mode toggle. ```

The pure-behaviour debounces (parse/URL/slider) are a genuinely demo-owned concern and belong in one named table with a rationale per row. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-7 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** componentFor widens a closed union to `string | null` in its signature, which forces an unreachable `return ColorPicker` masking fallback and destroys the compiler's exhaustiveness check — so adding a pane to viewSchema and forgetting this file silently renders the colour picker instead of failing.

**Mechanism.** A signature that widens a deliberately closed union opts out of the exact compiler guarantee the union exists to provide, and then requires a fallback to satisfy the widened type — the fallback is the SYMPTOM of the widening, not a defensive choice.

```
demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:81 `function componentFor(name: string | null): Component | null` with the fallback at :94 `return ColorPicker;`. Its only callers pass closed-union values: :164 `currentConfig.value.left` (LeftPane) and :171 `currentConfig.value.right` (RightPane). The unions are enumerated at demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:52-63 (LeftPane, 11 members) and :66 (RightPane, 4 members + null). componentFor handles null, color-picker, browse, extract, generate, gradient, atmosphere, about, palettes, mix, blob, admin-* — exhausting both unions, so :94 is unreachable. The same masking shape already shows one layer up: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md reports `safari-desktop-light /#/does-not-exist` at text=859, byte-identical to `/#/` at text=859, via useViewManager.ts:47 `isViewId(name) ? name : "picker"`.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE for a live failure — the fallback is unreachable today, proven by exhausting LeftPane ∪ RightPane against componentFor's branch set. The reproduction is a future one: add a member to LeftPane in viewSchema.ts and do not touch usePaneRouter.ts; the demo compiles clean and silently renders ColorPicker for the new view.

**Proposed cure.** `function componentFor(name: LeftPane | RightPane): Component | null`. TypeScript's exhaustiveness check then makes the fallback impossible to write and makes a schema addition a compile error here — which is the entire point of having the closed union in viewSchema.ts.

**Defect.** The `.pane-segmented-control :deep(.segmented-tab)` block is a per-instance override of a producer internal that buys 8px per tab, changes vertical padding by 0px, and introduces a second breakpoint authority that disagrees with the one governing the control's visibility.

**Mechanism.** A density variant implemented as a consumer-side :deep() patch instead of a producer prop. Violates Edict 5 (never per-instance overrides — the SFC comment's 'ROOT-LEVEL' claim is true only of the consumer's root, which is exactly the per-instance case) and Edict 4 (variants belong in glass-ui).

**Evidence.**

```
MEASURED at 390w: padding "4px 6px", fontSize "12.179px", tab box 57.51x26.27, track 121.02x32.27. Producer base for the same viewport (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/tabs/styles/segmented.css): `.segmented-tab { padding: 0.25rem 0.625rem; font-size: 0.8125rem }` = 4px 10px / 13px → the override changes VERTICAL padding by 0px (0.25rem in both) and horizontal by 4px/side. Token resolved: --type-caption = `clamp( 0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem )` (defined at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/scale.css) → 12.179px at 390w. Breakpoint disagreement: visibility is demo/styles/shell.css:123-125 `[data-layout="desktop"] .dock-mobile-panes { display: none }` where data-layout = width>=1024 AND aspect>=1.1 (shell.css:100-110), while the compact rung is `@media (max-width: 639px)` (PaneSegmentedControl.vue:46) — so in 640-1023px and portrait >=1024 the control is SHOWN in mobile grammar at the producer's >=640px desktop metrics (0.3125rem 0.75rem / 0.875rem).
```

**Reproduction.** Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 390x844, expand the dock, read getComputedStyle on .segmented-tab (pasted above); diff against segmented.css.

**Proposed cure.** Relay to the glass-ui BI/BJ inbox per the standing relay edict: add a `density="compact"` (or `size="sm"`) prop to SegmentedTabs; delete the <style scoped> block; pass the prop at the call site. This is the transposition that makes C-1's inlining lossless and C-9's gate problem disappear.

### `implementation (CHALLENGE-C) — demo/shell/PaneSegmentedContr` · C-6 · implementation (CHALLENGE-C)

**Defect.** `Number(v) as 0 | 1` launders the producer's `string` emit contract through an unchecked cast into a `Ref<0|1>`. Any value outside {"0","1"} yields NaN, which the cast asserts is 0|1 and stores.

**Mechanism.** `as` used as a boundary crossing instead of a narrowing predicate — the repo's banned masking idiom in type clothing.

**Evidence.**

```
Producer emit signature, SegmentedTabs.vue.d.ts: `"update:modelValue": (value: string) => any`. Consumer, PaneSegmentedControl.vue:11: `(v) => emit('update:modelValue', Number(v) as 0 | 1)`. Downstream failure path read in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useTabRovingFocus-YnWh-Ytr.js: with String(NaN)="NaN" no option matches, `if (e < 0) { ...opacity: "0" }` fires and neither button carries aria-pressed="true"; demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:180's `mobilePaneIndex.value === 1` then silently resolves to the left pane.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — HYPOTHESIS. Currently unreachable because tabOptions (PaneSegmentedControl.vue:30-33) hardcodes "0"/"1". The cast is the only thing standing between the producer's string contract and a Ref<0|1>.

**Proposed cure.** `(v) => emit('update:modelValue', v === "1" ? 1 : 0)` — total, no cast. Post-C-1 the whole string↔number seam disappears if the Dock stores the pane as the option value directly.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · D-9 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** devicePixelRatio is ignored — the loupe canvas backing store is a hardcoded 110×110 regardless of DPR, so the deliberately crisp (imageSmoothingEnabled=false) pixel grid is bilinearly upsampled by the compositor. LOUPE_SIZE also has two sources of truth: the constant drives the CSS and the draw math, but the canvas attributes are literals.

**Mechanism.** fixed-pixel backing store on a device-pixel-scaled display; duplicated dimension constant

**Evidence.**

```
ImageEyedropper.vue:85 (`width="110" height="110"` literals); constants.ts:8 (LOUPE_SIZE = 110) used at ImageEyedropper.vue:191-196 and useLoupeCanvas.ts:35-51; useLoupeCanvas.ts:40 (imageSmoothingEnabled = false). `grep -n "devicePixelRatio|dpr"` over the ImageEyedropper directory → no matches. MEASURED at devicePixelRatio 2: loupe canvas {"backing":[110,110],"cssW":106} → 212 device pixels rendered from a 110-pixel backing store, a 1.93× upsample.
```

**Reproduction.** Open the eyedropper on any retina display (probe measured devicePixelRatio: 2) and inspect the loupe canvas: backing 110×110, CSS box 106 px, 212 device px. The magnified pixel edges are smeared by the compositor.

**Proposed cure.** :width="LOUPE_SIZE * dpr" / :height="LOUPE_SIZE * dpr" with ctx.scale(dpr, dpr) in drawLoupe, and no literal dimensions anywhere — one constant, one truth.

**Defect.** WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name failure: `:aria-label="tile.id"` overrides the visible text on every tile, and for the steps tile the accessible name ("steps") does not contain the visible label ("n = 4"). A speech-input user who says the words they can see cannot activate it. The root cause is that all eight family eyebrows are aria-hidden, so the id-as-name override exists to compensate for grouping information deliberately hidden from AT.

**Mechanism.** Semantics authored on the wrong element — grouping hidden from AT, then compensated for by overriding each control's name.

**Evidence.**

```
EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:105 (:aria-label="tile.id"), :116 ({{ tile.label }}), :96 (family eyebrow aria-hidden="true").
Measured: stepsTiles: [{"id":"steps","aria":"steps","text":"n = 4"},{"id":"step-start","aria":"step-start","text":"start"},{"id":"step-end","aria":"step-end","text":"end"}]; familyEyebrows: all eight of css/sine/quad/cubic/expo/circ/back/steps carry hidden:"true".
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; read aria-label vs innerText on [data-specimen='steps'] -> "steps" vs "n = 4".

**Proposed cure.** Make each .strip-family a real group — role="group" with aria-labelledby pointing at its eyebrow, and stop hiding the eyebrow — then DROP :aria-label so the tile is named by its own visible text. "in" inside group "sine" reads correctly and satisfies 2.5.3 by construction. One change kills both this and the hidden-grouping defect.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfig` · R4-7 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The Hue-method quartet — the component's headline preview — interpolates between hues that are pure numerical noise whenever an operand is neutral, so four visibly different arcs are shown for a choice that is meaningless.

**Mechanism.** After the XYZ round trip a neutral color's channel deltas are ~1e-16 rather than exactly 0, so the hue formula divides dust by dust and amplifies it 360×. This is the repo's documented HSV hue-drift hazard living inside the preview feature.

**Evidence.**

```
MixConfigBar.vue:66-74. Measured: `#808080 -> hue 300°`, `#7f7f7f -> hue 340°`, `#c0c0c0 -> 300°`, `#404040 -> 0°`, `#ffffff -> 336°`, every one with saturation ~1e-16; only exactly-black returns `"none"`. src/color/anchors.ts:155-166 `encodedToHsv` yields hue 0 only when delta is exactly 0.
```

**Reproduction.** EXECUTED — `convertColor(parseCssColor("#808080").value, "hsl").value.channels` → `[300, 1.1145939814150194e-16, 0.5019607843137255]`; the same for `#7f7f7f` → `[340, 3.343781944245057e-16, 0.4980392156862746]`.

**Proposed cure.** Carry `none` for a powerless hue the way the library already does for exact black — the channel type has the vocabulary one branch away. The honest predicate is an epsilon threshold on delta relative to max, not exact equality with 0.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (r3: blind third replication + ` · II-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** NEW (r2 carries only a 'wheel momentum double-counted' hypothesis). A plain wheel over a fitted image unconditionally cancels the page default, pans nothing because clampPan re-centres it to a no-op, and still arms an inertia coast that burns ~70 frames each doing a forced layout.

**Mechanism.** An effect armed from an input event without first asking whether the effect is possible — the gesture is inert, expensive, and event-swallowing at the same time.

**Evidence.**

```
ONE wheel tick over a fully fitted image, 1000 ms window: getBoundingClientRect calls: 75, rAF requests: 253, canvas transform unchanged at `translate(0px, 57.8203px) scale(7.9375)`. The route's ambient baseline is `rafPer1500ms: 270` (~180/s) per STATES.json, so ~70 frames are the coast. Code: useInertiaGesture.ts:300 (unconditional preventDefault on a passive:false listener, :333), :311-320 (velocity seeded and startInertia called unconditionally), :80-89 (clampPan re-centres when content fits), :75 and :126 (getBoundingClientRect per call, per frame).
```

**Reproduction.** Open the eyedropper on an image that fits the viewport and scroll the wheel once over it. Nothing moves, the page default is cancelled, and a coast loop spins. `node .../scratchpad/ccED/probe3.mjs` section 2.

**Proposed cure.** Gate on effect: compute the clamped delta first; if it is zero, neither preventDefault nor arm inertia. Cache the viewport rect — the ResizeObserver at :354-360 already exists to invalidate it — instead of measuring inside a per-frame loop.

**Defect.** The loupe's canvas backing store ignores devicePixelRatio, in a component whose whole purpose is per-pixel fidelity and which explicitly disables image smoothing to get crisp nearest-neighbour blocks.

**Mechanism.** A raster surface sized in CSS pixels rather than device pixels — the nearest-neighbour discipline is thrown away by the compositor at the last step.

**Evidence.**

```
{"dpr":2,"loupeBackingW":110,"loupeCssW":110} (Chromium mobile) and {"dpr":3,"backing":110,"cssW":110} (WebKit mobile). Code: ImageEyedropper.vue:85 (`width="110" height="110"` with `class="w-full h-full"`), constants.ts:8 (`LOUPE_SIZE = 110`), useLoupeCanvas.ts:40 (`imageSmoothingEnabled = false`).
```

**Reproduction.** Open the eyedropper on any DPR>1 display and hover; every crisp 10-CSS-px block is resampled 2x/3x. Measured in probe.mjs (matrix A) and probe3.mjs (matrix C).

**Proposed cure.** Size the backing store `LOUPE_SIZE * devicePixelRatio`, `ctx.scale(dpr, dpr)`, keep the CSS box at `LOUPE_SIZE`, and re-size on a `matchMedia('(resolution: …)')` change.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt (round 2) on demo/w` · R2-N3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Unconditional coalescing: sampleCoalescedStops always emits ~32 sub-stops at IEEE-noise precision even when every interval's easing is the IDENTITY cubic-bezier(0,0,1,1) — the seeded default, and the state the parser re-seeds after every successful parse. For identity easing the browser's own interpolation is identical, so all 32 sub-stops are redundant. 2115 bytes where 74 suffice (28.6x), recomputed for the rail AND the tile AND every clipboard copy, with 12 significant decimals per channel.

**Mechanism.** a sampling law applied unconditionally, blind to the case where the sampled function is the identity

**Evidence.**

```
At rest, on load, no user edits: `EDITOR SHOWS (len 74): linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)` vs `CLIPBOARD GOT (len 2115): linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(75% 0.15 145deg) 0.00%, oklch(74.687500147402% 0.150937499558 148.749998231174deg) 3.13%, …`. Sources: useGradientCSS.ts:175-216 (sampler), :53-62 (identity seed), gradientParse.ts:295-298 (re-seed).
```

**Reproduction.** `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-visualizer/probes/challenge-C-r2-clipboard-divergence.mjs`

**Proposed cure.** (a) When every interval is the identity easing, serialize the raw stops — no coalescing (this also cures round-trip fidelity of the default state). (b) Round channels once, in the gradient consumer of colorToCss, to a display-honest 4-6 significant figures instead of presenting floating-point noise as authored CSS.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · C-07 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The keep-in-view watch's SELECTION arm is intermittent: pressing an off-port tile sometimes fails to scroll it into view, while the REVEAL arm (collapse + re-expand) works reliably. The component's docblock promises both.

**Mechanism.** HYPOTHESIS (explicitly labelled): the watch is default flush:'pre', so its callback runs BEFORE the component re-renders and its nextTick promise races the parent's own patch for that tick; when the patch lands in a later flush the measurement reads pre-layout geometry and dx computes to 0, silently skipping the scroll at :71 `if (dx !== 0)`.

**Evidence.**

```
Trial A (fresh load, press [data-specimen="step-end"]): initialScrollLeft 0; after press +1.2 s scrollLeft still 0, tile at x 1673.1-1717.1 against port 237-673, visible false. Then collapse+reopen: scrollLeft 1044, tile at 629.1-673.1, visible true. Trial B (same action, Element.prototype.scrollBy instrumented): exactly one call { fn:'scrollBy', cls:'fading-scroll fading-scrol', args:{left:1044.109375, behavior:'smooth'} } at t=2068, trace 140ms->60.5, 280->645, 420->902, 560->1000, 700->1038, 840->1044, settles 1044. Selection did change in both trials (trial A's later reveal scrolled to step-end's position). Site: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:50-80.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, Easing row 1 open, press the last tile [data-specimen="step-end"] and sample port.scrollLeft for ~1.4 s. Observed failing once and succeeding once across two clean trials — the BEHAVIOUR is reproduced, the MECHANISM is a hypothesis.

**Proposed cure.** Stop racing the scheduler: put { flush: 'post' } on the watch so the callback runs after the DOM patch, and delete the nextTick wrapper (and its void-swallowed promise) outright — the measurement then always reads settled geometry. One line removed, one option added.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · D-6 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Two requestAnimationFrame callbacks are scheduled per authoring event (line 58 eagerly in `onAuthored`, line 65 again from the `value.css` watcher), neither handle is retained, and there is no cleanup on unmount — every frame performs a querySelector that today returns null and is discarded.

**Mechanism.** Hand-rolled frame scheduling with no scope ownership — two independent triggers for one logical event, and callbacks that outlive the component only because an optional-chain accidentally absorbs the torn-down case.

**Evidence.**

```
`grep -n "onUnmounted\|onScopeDispose\|cancelAnimationFrame" demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/*.vue *.ts` → NO MATCHES.
Measured by patching window.requestAnimationFrame and attributing callbacks by source text (EAS-probe6.mjs), one single ArrowRight on a control point with everything else at rest:
```
rAF after ONE ArrowRight: {"syncVbRatio":2, "function sync() { rafId = null; cons":2, "(e) => …":72}
```
`syncVbRatio: 2` — exactly the double predicted from the code read. Under a continuous 20-move pointer drag the page schedules 265 rAF callbacks total (EAS-probe5.mjs).
```

**Reproduction.** Measured (pasted above) for the double-schedule. The unmount-leak half is a LABELLED HYPOTHESIS: no misbehaviour observed, because the `?.` chain in syncVbRatio makes a post-unmount fire harmless by luck rather than by design.

**Proposed cure.** The idiomatic Vue 3.5 answer is not a hand-rolled rAF at all. Use `useMutationObserver` from @vueuse/core (already a dependency, already used two files over in EasingSpecimenStrip.vue via useMediaQuery) with `{ attributes: true, attributeFilter: ["viewBox"] }` on the canvas, and delete `onAuthored`'s rAF, the `value.css` watcher and `onMounted` together: one scope-owned observer replaces three schedulers, is exact rather than one-frame-guessed, and disposes itself. **Mechanism.** Several SR/browser pairings (VoiceOver+Safari, this project's stated matrix) only announce mutations of a live region already present in the accessibility tree; a region inserted pre-populated is commonly missed. WCAG 4.1.3.

**Evidence.**

```
GradientCodeEditor.vue:107-114 — `<p v-if="parseVerdict" role="status">{{ parseVerdict }}</p>`; the verdict value is owned by GradientVisualizer.vue:100/107.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — mechanism/spec-level; not driven with a screen reader in this pass.

**Proposed cure.** Render the status region unconditionally (empty, no visual cost) and write text into it, so every verdict is a mutation of a live region rather than an insertion.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/workbenches/gr` · C-16 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The model is transiently illegal after every stop change: n stops with n-2 intervals until an async watcher flushes.

**Mechanism.** Stops and intervals are updated by two separate writes separated by the scheduler. Vue's pre-flush ordering keeps today's render path safe, so this is luck about scheduler ordering rather than an invariant: any flush:'sync' watcher, watchSyncEffect, or handler that reads a computed in the same tick as an add lands in the illegal window.

**Evidence.**

```
useGradientModel.ts:89-100 (async watch). My run, reading synchronously right after addStop: 'THREW Gradient interval 3 is missing' (useGradientCSS.ts:189).
```

**Reproduction.** npx vite-node .../probes/visualizer-probe.ts → section P6, the 'synchronous read straight after addStop' line.

**Proposed cure.** Stops and intervals change in ONE assignment (the shape `applyCSS` already uses) — or, better, stop having two arrays at all (see C-5).

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/workbenches/mi` · C-7 · CHALLENGE-C

**Reproduction.** Read node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/selection.d.ts (`SelectionValue = string | number`) against MixConfigBar.vue:99. The cast compiles for `null`, which is in AcceptableValue and not in PickerSpace.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C-13 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** In-flight quantizes are neither cancelled nor tokenised. useImageQuantize stores a single pendingResolve/pendingReject pair; a second runQuantize before the first reply overwrites both, so the earlier promise NEVER settles, and the first worker reply then resolves the SECOND caller with the FIRST palette and sets isProcessing=false while run #2 is still in the worker (early skeleton drop + stale render). The worker is also never re-created after onerror, so one worker crash bricks every subsequent extraction for the session.

**Mechanism.** single-slot continuation storage for a multi-request channel; no request identity on the postMessage payload

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useImageQuantize.ts:89-98 (single-slot pending pair), :57-68 (onmessage resolves whatever is currently in the slot), :69-75 (onerror sets error but leaves the dead worker installed), :54-56 (getWorker only constructs when `worker` is null).
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — hypothesis by code path. Forcing the overlap needs a quantize exceeding the 300ms debounce (useExtractSession.ts:159-162); the desktop probe measured the full cycle at 250ms, so I could not force it live. The dropped-promise and dead-worker mechanisms are unconditional and visible in the source.

**Proposed cure.** Attach a per-request id to the postMessage payload and echo it from quantize-worker.ts:20; discard replies whose id is not current. This is the same token that cures C-1, applied one layer down — which is the point: one identity discipline, two layers. Re-create the worker on onerror rather than leaving a corpse installed.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C-14 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `isProcessing` is false during the image-decode window: quantizeFromFile awaits imageFileToPixels BEFORE runQuantize sets isProcessing=true, so nothing renders during the decode — and if the decode throws, nothing ever renders (C-5).

**Mechanism.** loading state raised downstream of the first expensive await instead of at the operation boundary

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useImageQuantize.ts:105-108 (the await) vs :86-87 (where error/isProcessing are actually written). Measured blind window on a 6 MP file: total_mainthread_ms 24.3 (createImageBitmap 8.6 + getImageData 13.8 + slice 1.8), multiples of that on mobile Safari for a 12 MP capture.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/extract — replay imageFileToPixels on a 3000x2000 JPEG and time it (24.3ms here); during that entire window the component is in its resting state with no indication that work has begun.

**Proposed cure.** Raise isProcessing at the TOP of quantizeFromFile inside a try/finally, so the loading state brackets the whole operation rather than only its worker tail. (Cure C-10 alongside it — a loading flag nobody can perceive is only half the fix.)

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C-15 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Camera failures are filed as quantize errors. The component reaches through the session object to write a writable computed whose setter targets the worker's error ref, so a camera fault occupies the quantizer's error channel and the next successful quantize silently erases it. A raw DOMException is template-interpolated, so the user reads 'Camera access denied: NotAllowedError: Permission denied'. There is no dismiss.

**Mechanism.** two unrelated failure domains sharing one channel; a component mutating composable-owned state directly instead of through an action — the encapsulation the session exists to provide, bypassed at the one place it matters

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue:252 (`session.quantizeError.value = \`Camera access denied: ${err}\``); the writable computed at useExtractSession.ts:66-73; the erasure at useImageQuantize.ts:86 (`error.value = null`).
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/extract — deny camera permission: the quantize error line shows the stringified DOMException. Then drop any valid image: the camera message vanishes without the user having acknowledged it.

**Proposed cure.** A separate `cameraError` ref rendered on its own line, written through a `session.setCameraError()` action rather than by reaching into a computed; map the three real getUserMedia rejection names (NotAllowedError / NotFoundError / NotReadableError) to human sentences.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/ext` · C2-12 · CHALLENGE-C

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects of demo/workbenches/gra` · C8 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Rich-HTML paste injects foreign markup with inline styles straight into the editor's DOM, destroying the syntax highlighting and overriding the design system's typography.

**Mechanism.** An unsanitized contenteditable sink. The pasted markup persists until the next render(), which — if the parse is in an error state — never comes, because line 72 gates re-rendering on `!hasError`. NOT XSS: Chromium's paste sanitizer strips scripts and event handlers, so <img onerror> does not execute; this is an integrity and design-system defect, stated precisely rather than inflated.

**Evidence.**

```
GradientCodeEditor.vue:88 `contenteditable="true"` with no `@paste` handler anywhere in the file. LIVE with a real system clipboard (evidence/paste-probe.mjs — clipboard-read/write granted, navigator.clipboard.write of a text/html + text/plain pair, then Cmd+V): {"innerHTML":"<b style=\"color:red;font-size:32px\">linear-gradient</b>(90deg, <i>red</i>, blue)","textContent":"linear-gradient(90deg, red, blue)","foreignTags":["B[style]","I"],"verdict":null}.
```

**Reproduction.** `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-codeeditor/evidence/paste-probe.mjs`. By hand: copy syntax-highlighted CSS from any web page, click the Gradient CSS editor, Cmd+A, Cmd+V — the foreign fonts, sizes and colours land inside the glass panel.

**Proposed cure.** `contenteditable="plaintext-only"` (Chrome/Safari/Firefox 136+, and the demo's baseline is Safari + Chromium) — one attribute that also cures C4's line-break collapse. Failing that, `@paste.prevent` + an explicit plain-text insertion.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects of demo/workbenches/gra` · C9 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `highlight()`'s `catch { return code }` is a masking fallback that, if ever taken, feeds unescaped text into an `innerHTML` sink.

**Mechanism.** A catch whose recovery is 'silently switch to the unescaped path' converts an unknown failure into an injection sink — the masking fallback edict 2 forbids.

**Evidence.**

```
GradientCodeEditor.vue:43-49 (`try { return hljs.highlight(...).value } catch { return code }`) feeding line 52 (`editorRef.value.innerHTML = highlight(code)`). The happy path is safe, measured (evidence/hljs-bench.mjs): `hljs output for an HTML payload: linear-gradient(<span class="hljs-number">90deg</span>, &lt;<span class="hljs-selector-tag">img</span> …` — highlight.js escapes `<` to `&lt;`. The catch branch does not. `modelValue` is not only user-typed: seedFromPalette (GradientVisualizer.vue:110-116) pulls API-fetched saved-palette colour strings into stops[].cssColor, which serialize into simpleCSS, which render() writes.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — reachability is a HYPOTHESIS, explicitly labelled. `css` is registered at module scope (line 8) so 'Unknown language' cannot fire, and hljs v11 handles illegal-lexeme errors internally in safe mode; I could not construct an input that takes the branch. The SHAPE is confirmed by reading lines 43-52.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects of demo/workbenches/gra` · C10 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Every model tick tears down and rebuilds the editor's entire subtree via `innerHTML`, destroying the browser's native undo stack and any selection — including once per pointer frame of an unrelated stop drag, on an editor that may be off-screen.

**Mechanism.** An imperative innerHTML projection instead of a reactive render: Vue cannot patch what it does not own, so every change is a demolition.

**Evidence.**

```
GradientCodeEditor.vue:51-53 (render sets innerHTML) driven by the watcher at lines 76-79 on `modelValue` = `simpleCSS`, which recomputes on every pointermove of a stop drag. MEASURED (evidence/live-probe.mjs R5): {"tag":"R5 editor DOM mutation records during a 40-step stop drag","dragMs":1024,"mutationRecords":40} — one full teardown-and-rebuild per frame. Cost MEASURED over 2000 iterations (evidence/hljs-bench.mjs): 2-stop (74 chars) 0.014 ms/highlight -> 0.8 ms per 60fps second; 4-stop (206 chars) 0.020 ms -> 1.2 ms per 60fps second.
```

**Reproduction.** `node docs/.../evidence/live-probe.mjs` (R5). DOWNGRADED ON THE MEASUREMENT — ~1 ms per second of dragging is not a performance finding and I will not dress it as one. What remains real is the semantic cost: undo stack and selection destroyed on every frame.

**Proposed cure.** The editor is a rendered projection of the model and should re-render when the model changes MEANINGFULLY, not per frame. Render through Vue (a v-html-free token list, or a shallowRef of highlighted tokens) so the update is a patch rather than a demolition, restoring native undo and selection.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (round 4) — demo/workbenches/mix/MixCon` · R4-5 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The dead Button vocabulary r1 found at this one call site is 96 call sites across the demo — glass-ui 7's Button has no `variant` prop at all, so every emphasis declaration in the app is inert and everything renders `emphasis="secondary" tone="neutral"`.

**Mechanism.** Vue attribute fallthrough is silent by design: an undeclared prop lands on the DOM element as a literal attribute and matches no selector. The demo's entire emphasis vocabulary was written against a glass-ui that no longer exists, so the app has no rendered hierarchy — which is the mechanical reason the shipped frames read as one flat register. Note SelectTrigger DOES declare variant?: "default"|"ghost" (SelectTrigger.vue.d.ts:11), so the Select side of this file is unaffected; this is Button-only.

**Evidence.**

```
Producer contract glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts: ButtonProps = { emphasis?: "primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"; tone?; size?: "xs"|"sm"|"md"|"lg"; iconOnly?; loading?; type?; disabled?; class? } — NO `variant`. Producer selectors (components/button/styles.css): .button, [data-emphasis="primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"], [data-tone=…]. `grep -rl audacious node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` hits only typography/scale.css, typography/semantic.css, springPresets.d.ts, dock/styles/density.css — never a button register.
Census: grep -rhn 'variant="[a-z-]*"' demo -r | grep -o 'variant="[a-z-]*"' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn => 29 outline, 28 ghost, 7 spectrum, 7 secondary, 7 error, 5 breath, 3 shimmer, 3 pill, 2 primary-audacious, 2 misconfigured, 2 developing, 1 seated, 1 destructive, 1 default = 96 sites / 14 values, none accepted.
Live (p9.mjs), three components one page: Mix -> data-emphasis=secondary data-size=md + inert variant="primary-audacious"; Dock Login (variant="outline") -> secondary/xs; Dock @mbabb (variant="ghost") -> secondary/xs.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/wbmix/p9.mjs — dumps every attribute of the Mix button and of the other button.button nodes on /#/mix. Plus the two greps above, run against the repo at HEAD c654824e.

**Proposed cure.** 96 local edits is the wrong answer. One `variant -> emphasis|tone` crosswalk relayed to the glass-ui BH inbox under the standing relay edict, plus a vue-tsc gate that rejects unknown props on producer components — the current strictness (verbatimModuleSyntax, strict: true) cannot catch a prop that exists only in the demo's imagination.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (round 4) — demo/workbenches/mix/MixCon` · R4-6 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The canon itself is in conflict about the `.section-label` register and this component sits on the fault line — prior rounds charged the component for a defect the demo's own DESIGN.md explicitly sanctions and names it a consumer of. Separately, and locally chargeable, the verb's type is Fraunces 500 which no document sanctions.

**Mechanism.** Within one component the type jurisdiction is inverted three ways: the LABEL speaks the value family (Fira Code mono-caption), the VALUE speaks the control family (Plus Jakarta Sans 16.4px), and the VERB speaks the display family (Fraunces 500). The caption register is a family across six other demo files (GradientVisualizer x4, GenerateControls x2, MixSourceSelector, SearchFilterBar x4, AdminTagsPanel, TagEditPopover), so its owner is the canon, not this file — fixing it here alone would put this file out of step with six siblings.

**Evidence.**

```
VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 closed matrix: control/label -> text-small, Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold; mono-caption allowed only 'where the content is a caption'. glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/utilities.css: `.section-label { @apply text-mono-caption; color: var(--muted-foreground); }` where text-mono-caption = font-mono + type-caption + tracking-caps + uppercase. demo/DESIGN.md:52-58 blesses exactly this and names the consumers: 'consumed by the gradient / mix / generate control bars'. Measured (p1.mjs): Fira Code, 14.384px, letter-spacing 1.4384px, uppercase, weight 400 — and rendered contrast 5.05:1 (p5.mjs), so it passes AA; the defect is jurisdictional, not contrast. Locally chargeable: MixConfigBar.vue:165 `class="h-10 gap-2 font-medium font-display"` renders the verb in Fraunces weight 500 (measured p1.mjs), against §4 (Fraunces = display/identity) and against demo/DESIGN.md:45-48's own prohibition on blanket font-display.
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/wbmix/p1.mjs (computed font-family/size/letter-spacing/text-transform of label.section-label and of the Mix button); read demo/DESIGN.md:45-58 against docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.

**Proposed cure.** Resolve the canon conflict before any wave closes the row: one of DESIGN.md:58 or VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 must yield, and the decision must land once for all seven consumers. Locally, delete `font-medium font-display` from the verb — the producer's emphasis/size axes own the control's face, and no document sanctions a Fraunces control label.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-18 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The loupe is optically wrong in four independent ways: it is centred under the finger, its backing store ignores devicePixelRatio, its magnification is 9.64x not the intended 10x because LOUPE_SIZE is used as a border-box, and it has no reticle marking which texel is the sample.

**Mechanism.** constants.ts LOUPE_SIZE/LOUPE_PIXELS are treated as CSS px rather than as a model; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 requires 'reticle, loupe and numeric value remain one model'.

The 110->106 delta comes from ImageEyedropper.vue:194-195 setting LOUPE_SIZE as width/height while :265 declares a 2px border, so 110/11=10 px per texel becomes 9.64 and the crisp blocks are resampled by 0.964. probe/shot-forced-colors.png: the loupe shows a red/blue checker while the readout says blue — unverifiable by eye.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/probe.mjs — mobile.loupe backing vs cssRect vs dpr.

**Proposed cure.** Size the backing store to LOUPE_SIZE * devicePixelRatio, make LOUPE_SIZE the content box, offset the loupe from the touch point on coarse pointers, and draw the reticle on the sampled texel — the same model D-1 and D-6 need.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-19 · CHALLENGE-D

useImageSampler.ts:114-115 sampleAt returns null out of bounds and the caller (ImageEyedropper.vue:156-162) does nothing — no message, no cursor change, stale readout retained. loadImage rejects on img.onerror (useImageSampler.ts:72-75) and onMounted(() => { loadAndFit(); ... }) (:237-240) never catches. img.crossOrigin='anonymous' (:70) routes every non-CORS cross-origin URL into that same silent arm; a tainted-canvas getImageData (:116) would throw inside a pointermove handler. The missing catch on loadAndFit is CONFIRMED by reading; its live reachability is a HYPOTHESIS pending a parent that can supply a remote URL — today ExtractWorkbench only passes same-origin data URLs.

**Defect.** Camera failures are routed through the quantizer's error channel with a raw Error object interpolated into user-facing copy, with no dismiss; and the viewfinder renders a black box during the permission prompt with no state.

**Mechanism.** Channel conflation (camera error in the quantize slot) plus optimistic state entry with no pending register.

**Evidence.**

```
ExtractWorkbench.vue:252 — `session.quantizeError.value = `Camera access denied: ${err}`` — surfaces e.g. "Camera access denied: NotAllowedError: The request is not allowed by the user agent…" in the destructive line at ExtractWorkbench.vue:80-85, which sits above the RESULT plate. useImageQuantize.ts:86 clears `error.value` only inside runQuantize, which requires a file the user does not have. ExtractWorkbench.vue:240-247 sets `cameraActive.value = true` BEFORE awaiting getUserMedia, so an empty `bg-stage` rectangle renders during the permission prompt.
```

**Reproduction.** Deny camera permission on /#/extract and observe the destructive line above the result plate; static proof at ExtractWorkbench.vue:252 and useImageQuantize.ts:86.

**Proposed cure.** Separate the camera register from the quantize register (error != error), map exceptions to house copy rather than interpolating `${err}`, give the error a dismiss, and add an explicit 'awaiting camera' state before the stream arrives.

Law: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:72 (§5.7) — 'Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities.' Witness: frames-r3/D3-n4-mobile-390-four-intervals.png; probe frames-r3/probe-rhythm.mjs.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. On the open row's head, read the last span's getBoundingClientRect().width (296.53) and a Range over its contents (60.55). Difference 235.98 against a 460px head. Script: frames-r3/probe-rhythm.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Size the identity run to its own legal width and give the recovered ~236px to the catalogue, which is the element actually starved. This is subsumed by the /easing chassis cure (round 2 D2-02) but is independently correct in the current housing.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D3-11 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The disclosure buys nothing and costs +117% of the route's DOM per three added intervals. Every authoring stage is fully mounted before the user has pressed anything and stays mounted when its row collapses, so the disclosure reduces neither cost nor attention — it only buries the editor two levels deep.

**Mechanism.** a global module constant (the 27-tile catalogue) and a heavyweight editor instantiated once per row instead of once per editor, with v-show rather than v-if, so the composition pays full mount cost for hidden duplicates

**Evidence.**

```
Measured on /#/gradient, same page, before/after adding three stops: specimen rows 1 -> 4; specimen tiles rendered 27 -> 108; EasingPicker plot SVGs mounted 1 -> 4; .fading-scroll ports 1 -> 4; document elements (whole route) 511 -> 1109 (+598, +117%); visible focusables 55 -> 67. At N=3 with nothing disclosed: stagesVisible [false,false,false], stagesMounted (svg) 6. Sites: GradientEasingEditor.vue:161 (strip inside v-for), :204-213 (stage v-show), header comment :16-18 defends always-alive pickers on state-continuity grounds although EasingAuthoringStage is fully controlled. Probes: frames-r3/probe-n2.mjs, probe-tune (scratchpad), probe-n4.json.
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, record document.querySelectorAll('*').length (511) and .specimen-tile count (27). Click .gradient-rail at 25%, 50%, 75%. Re-record: 1109 and 108. Query [id^='easing-authoring-'] svg with nothing disclosed: non-zero. Script: frames-r3/probe-n2.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** One catalogue for the editor, positioned by the open row — the classic single-inspector arrangement — rather than one catalogue per row. And either the disclosure is real (v-if plus one named motion family from demo/styles/animations.css) or it is not a disclosure and the editor is always visible, which is what the /easing chassis of round 2's D2-02 wants.
